note: Raw per-area findings before duplicates were merged. verdict/verified_severity come from the refute-first verifier; see 14-vision-release-review.md for the merged, ranked view.

areas.coverage:
Area: file lifecycle and recovery. I inventoried 12 File-menu commands in scope that have a monetId: new, openf, opensmartobject, clearrecent plus the live Open Recent items, browse (Document Browser), close, closeall, closeothers, save, saveas, savecopy and revert. The 5 disabled placeholders (Browse in Bridge, Close and Go to Bridge, Invite to Edit, Share, Share for Review) are covered in the parity notes.

I also covered 14 flows that are not menu items:
- document tabs: select, close, reorder
- the Home screen: New, Open, Recents
- native OS drops, browser drops and droplet drops
- launch and open-with hand-off (main.rs PendingOpen plus native/openFiles.ts)
- command-line job hand-off (native/cli.ts plus main.rs cli_job)
- the recovery timer and the launch-time recovery prompt (autoRecover.ts plus app.ts)
- atomic write, both halves (monet-react atomic-write.ts and monet-ui atomic_save.rs)
- the quit and window-close guard
- closing a float window
- the MCP commands doc.new, doc.open, doc.saveAs and doc.exportAs

For each one I traced the path App.tsx → state/app.ts → store.ts → engine (save_project, export_png and export_jpeg, layer_count, export_icc). I also read the pinned native dependencies to check platform behaviour: tauri 2.11.2 (IPC ACL gate and JSON body parsing), tao 0.35.3 (macOS app delegate), muda 0.19.2 (the predefined Quit item), wry 0.55.1 and tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1 (the alert and confirm override), plus the Vision capabilities and generated ACL manifests. I grepped the unit tests (unsavedWorkGuard, autoRecover, app.test revert, nativeIoPolicy, bytesForExt) and the e2e specs (home, file-drop, file-manager, desktop-smoke).

I ran no builds or suites. The only thing I executed was a small Node script in my scratch folder, to measure how much memory and time Array.from plus JSON.stringify take on a 50 MB payload.

Not reviewed:
- the decoders for each file format, and the Camera Raw workspace internals (other areas)
- the CLI batch and droplet internals beyond how they hand off
- anything at runtime in the native WKWebView app: findings that depend on platform behaviour cite the pinned dependency source instead

Findings: 2 blocker, 5 major, 13 minor, 1 test gap, 1 polish.
areas.parity_notes:
These disabled placeholders (no monetId) are correct and not bugs: Browse in Bridge, Close and Go to Bridge, Invite to Edit, Share…, Share for Review (Beta).

Other gaps against Photoshop, not reported as bugs:
- The New dialog has no Name field and no bit-depth (8/16/32) choice.
- Save stays enabled for clean documents.
- Revert cannot be recorded in actions.
- Dropping a file onto an open canvas opens a new tab instead of placing it as an embedded layer.
- The close and quit prompts have no Save button (reported as a minor finding).

The menu and MCP surfaces do not match: MCP has doc.new, doc.open, doc.openPhotoshopRaw, doc.saveAs and doc.exportAs, but nothing for File ▸ Save (in place), Close, Close All or Revert. doc.saveAs clears the unsaved state only for project formats, which matches Save As.

In the desktop build, alert() works: tauri-plugin-dialog turns it into a non-blocking native message box, so the Could-not-open and Could-not-save errors do appear. confirm() does not work (see findings).

Two findings go beyond this area and belong to other owners:
- plugin:heic, plugin:c2pa and plugin:models appear to be missing from the ACL for the same reason as atomicsave.
- The same confirm() problem also affects the Convert-to-RGB confirmation for a Photoshop preview (App.tsx:2158) and the paste-profile prompts (store.ts:6645).

findings.title: ⌘Q (Quit menu item, Dock Quit) quits without the unsaved-changes prompt on macOS
findings.feature: Quit / unsaved-work guard
findings.evidence: app.ts:8355-8378 installUnsavedWorkGuard only hooks win.onCloseRequested, and its comment claims 'Tauri fires onCloseRequested for both the red button and ⌘Q'. packages/monet-ui/packages/monet-react/src/mac-menu.ts:187 installs PredefinedMenuItem 'Quit'. In muda-0.19.2, platform_impl/macos/mod.rs:994 maps Quit to sel!(terminate:), and items/predefined.rs:339 gives it the Cmd+Q accelerator. tao-0.35.3 src/platform_impl/macos/app_delegate.rs:60-64 and 131-135 implement only applicationWillTerminate (which calls AppState::exit → LoopDestroyed). There is no applicationShouldTerminate, and no window gets CloseRequested. src-tauri/src/main.rs run_return handles only RunEvent::Opened. No JS shortcut binds ⌘Q (grep psMenuData/psMenus). unsavedWorkGuard.test.ts only exercises a mocked onCloseRequested.
findings.repro: Native macOS build: open an image, paint a stroke (tab shows *), press ⌘Q (or Monet Vision ▸ Quit, or Dock ▸ Quit). The app exits immediately with no prompt.
findings.impact: Unsaved work in every open document is lost on the standard Mac quit gesture. The only safety net is the recovery snapshot, which exists only if the 10-minute timer already ran for that revision (and recovery is disabled in debug builds). Edits made since the last tick, or in documents opened less than one interval ago, are gone.
findings.suggested_fix: Stop using the predefined Quit item. Install a custom MenuItem (Cmd+Q) that emits to the webview, runs the same confirmDiscardAll, then calls app exit. Alternatively, add an applicationShouldTerminate: override in monet-ui that returns NSTerminateCancel and routes through the guard. Add a native test that sends terminate: with a dirty document.
findings.verdict_reason: Followed it end to end. mac-menu.ts:187 installs PredefinedMenuItem 'Quit'. muda-0.19.2 macos/mod.rs:994 maps it to sel!(terminate:). tao-0.35.3 app_delegate.rs registers only applicationWillTerminate (line 131), which calls AppState::exit (app_state.rs:272-282, LoopDestroyed). No applicationShouldTerminate exists in tao, tauri-2.11.2 or tauri-runtime-wry-2.11.2 (grep finds no 'terminate' anywhere), so NSApp gets the default NSTerminateNow, runs exit(), and no window ever receives CloseRequested. main.rs run_return (406-412) handles only RunEvent::Opened, and nothing in the Rust sources handles ExitRequested or prevent_exit. installUnsavedWorkGuard (app.ts:8361-8378) only hooks onCloseRequested, and its comment claiming this covers ⌘Q is wrong. unsavedWorkGuard.test.ts drives a mocked onCloseRequested only. The standard Mac quit gesture loses every dirty document.

findings.title: Every save and every recovery snapshot sends the whole file as a JSON number array (Array.from) over IPC: multi-GB spikes and freezes on ordinary photo projects
findings.feature: Durable save (atomicWriteBytes): Save, Save As, Save a Copy, auto-recovery, MCP doc.saveAs
findings.evidence: atomic-write.ts:53-56 calls invoke('plugin:atomicsave|atomic_write', { destination, bytes: Array.from(bytes) }). tauri-2.11.2 src/ipc/protocol.rs:521-527 parses JSON bodies into serde_json::Value (about 32 B per number) before the ACL gate at webview/mod.rs:1823. The project format stores layer pixels as raw u16 (engine raster/mod.rs:30848, and w_u16vec at 35549-35554), so a 24 MP layer is about 192 MB. Measured in Node: a 50 MB payload becomes a 475 MB JS array plus a 179 MB JSON string and takes about 1 s. Callers: saveDocument app.ts:8067, Save As 8121, writeRecoverySnapshots 8210 (every N minutes, for each dirty document), and MCP doc.saveAs.
findings.repro: Native app: open a 24 MP photo, add two pixel layers, Save As .mvision (or wait for the 10-minute recovery tick). Expect a multi-second main-thread freeze and several GB of extra memory in both WebContent and the app process. Larger documents risk the WebContent process being killed, which loses every open document.
findings.impact: Freezes or crashes during save and during the background recovery tick. The feature meant to prevent data loss becomes the trigger for it. Because the durable command is then rejected by the ACL (next finding), the whole cost is paid before the fallback writes the file a second time.
findings.suggested_fix: Send the bytes as a raw body: invoke('plugin:atomicsave|atomic_write', bytes, { headers: { 'x-destination': encodeURIComponent(destination) } }). Read tauri::ipc::Request::body() in Rust, the way float.rs handles frames. Until then, skip the plugin call and use plugin-fs writeFile, which already sends raw bytes.
findings.verdict_reason: atomic-write.ts:53-56 passes bytes: Array.from(bytes) inside an args object. tauri-2.11.2 process-ipc-message-fn.js JSON.stringifies any non-array payload with a per-value replacer, so even a plain Uint8Array would be Array.from'd. protocol.rs:521-527 then parses the whole body into serde_json::Value before the ACL gate at webview/mod.rs:1823, so the full cost is paid and the call is then rejected (finding 3). The project format is uncompressed raw u16 (raster/mod.rs:30848 w_u16vec, 35549-35554), and there is no compression in projectEnvelope. Callers verified: saveDocument app.ts:8067, Save As 8121, writeRecoverySnapshots 8212. I reproduced the JS half in Node for a 96 MB payload (one 12 MP layer): Array.from took 1.2 s, stringify with Tauri's replacer took 5.0 s, the JSON was 343 MB and RSS reached 5.8 GB. That is before the Rust side builds a Value tree (about 32 B per element, so about 3 GB more). The result is a main-thread hang of several seconds and a multi-GB memory spike on every save and every recovery tick.

findings.title: The durable-save plugin is never allowed: plugin:atomicsave|atomic_write has no ACL permission, so every save silently falls back to write+rename with no fsync
findings.feature: Durable save (docs/durable-save.md)
findings.evidence: The default.json permissions contain no atomicsave entry. build.rs declares only the droplet and float inlined plugins. gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json has no 'atomicsave' key (and none for heic, c2pa or models). monet-ui atomic_save.rs:119-123 Builder::new('atomicsave') ships no permission manifest. tauri-2.11.2 webview/mod.rs:1823-1850 rejects any 'plugin:' command whose resolve_access is None. atomic-write.ts:57-66 turns the rejection into a single console.warn per session. docs/durable-save.md still marks vision ✅.
findings.repro: Native build: press ⌘S and open devtools. The console shows '[monet] durable save unavailable — falling back to write+rename (no fsync)' with 'Command plugin:atomicsave|atomic_write not allowed by ACL'.
findings.impact: The fsync/F_FULLFSYNC guarantee never applies. A power cut or kernel panic just after a save can leave a truncated file where the original was, which is the failure the plugin was built to prevent. The same ACL gap very likely breaks plugin:heic|encode_heic, plugin:c2pa|* and plugin:models|* (outside this area; worth checking by their owners).
findings.suggested_fix: Declare atomicsave (and heic, c2pa, models) as tauri_build InlinedPlugin entries, or ship a permissions manifest in monet-ui. Grant atomicsave:allow-atomic-write in default.json. Before exposing it, make atomic_write enforce the fs scope: it currently accepts any path, which would bypass the fs:scope deny list (~/.ssh, ~/.zshrc and so on). Add a native test that calls the command through the ACL.
findings.verdict_reason: capabilities/default.json has no atomicsave entry. build.rs declares only the droplet and float InlinedPlugins. gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json keys are core*, dialog, drag, droplet, float and fs, with no atomicsave, heic, c2pa or models. atomic_save.rs:119-123 Builder::new("atomicsave") ships no manifest (the monet-ui build.rs only emits cfgs). authority.rs:439-471 resolve_access returns None for a command that is not in allowed_commands, and webview/mod.rs:1818-1850 rejects every plugin: command in that case, with no bypass for plugins that lack a manifest. The team hit the same failure for droplet ('not allowed by ACL', #469, tauriConfig.test.ts:26) and fixed it with an InlinedPlugin. atomic-write.ts:58-67 turns the rejection into a single console.warn. The fallback is still crash-safe write+rename, so the loss is power-cut durability rather than routine data loss, which keeps this at major. The side note checks out: the JS calls plugin:heic|*, plugin:c2pa|* and plugin:models|* (app.ts:4977, 5149, 7146; modelDownload.ts:80), and those plugins have no ACL entries either. Their owners should verify them.

findings.title: Save in place and Save As treat any single-layer document as 'flat', so masks, smart filters, effects, opacity, text, CMYK/Lab and 32-bit are flattened into PNG/JPEG/GIF and the tab is marked saved
findings.feature: File ▸ Save (in place) and Save As retargeting
findings.evidence: app.ts:7702: const docIsFlat = () => E().layer_count() <= 1. nativeIoPolicy.ts:90-94: canSaveInPlace allows png/jpg/jpeg/gif whenever that check passes. saveAsIsCopy (99-103) uses the same flag, so Save As retargets the tab and clears dirty. saveDocument (app.ts:8058-8068) writes the file and calls markDocSavedAtRevision. The engine exports composite (raster/mod.rs:29435-29440). JPEG uses composite_image().to_rgb8(), which drops alpha (29902-29907). The mode is not checked, and 32-bit is written as 16-bit PNG.
findings.repro: Open photo.jpg and convert it for Smart Filters (or add a layer mask, a layer style, set opacity to 50%, erase to transparency, or switch Image ▸ Mode to CMYK, Lab or 32 Bits/Channel). Press ⌘S: the JPEG is overwritten with the composite and the * disappears. Close (no prompt) and reopen: the smart filter, mask, style or mode is gone.
findings.impact: Editable state, colour mode and bit depth are lost silently, and the document is marked saved, so closing gives no warning. This is the exact failure the layer-count guard was written to stop.
findings.suggested_fix: Allow in-place save and Save As retargeting to flat formats only when the format can represent the document: a single pixel layer that is visible, Normal blend at 100% opacity and fill, with no mask, vector mask, effects or smart filters, not a text/SO/adjustment/fill layer, no alpha or spot channels, and a mode and depth the format supports. Otherwise route to Save As, as Photoshop does. Add tests for each disqualifier.
findings.verdict_reason: app.ts:7702 docIsFlat = () => E().layer_count() <= 1, and layer_count is self.layers.len() (raster/mod.rs:9315). nativeIoPolicy.ts:90-94 canSaveInPlace accepts png/jpg/jpeg/gif (IN_PLACE_EXTENSIONS, line 57) whenever that flag is true, and saveAsIsCopy (99-103) uses the same flag. saveDocument (app.ts:8063-8068) writes the composite and calls markDocSavedAtRevision. The exporters write the composite (29435-29440), and JPEG drops alpha with to_rgb8() (29905). Neither the policy nor bytesForExt checks mode, depth, masks, smart filters or effects. A single Smart-Filter layer or a masked layer on a JPEG is therefore overwritten flat and the tab is marked clean.

findings.title: File ▸ Revert cannot be undone: it wipes history, and the bare F12 key triggers it with no confirmation
findings.feature: File ▸ Revert
findings.evidence: revertDocument (app.ts:8014-8043) swaps in a freshly built engine via store.revertActiveDoc. store.ts:6052 sets d.engine = eng, and 6089-6090 and 6119 set history: [], so Undo is dead. There is no confirmation. psMenuData.ts:109-111 gives Revert the F12 shortcut, which collectShortcutCommands binds (keyboardShortcuts.ts:142, 158, 220-244). menuEnablement in App.tsx (~3433-3467) never gates revert, so it stays enabled even for never-saved documents, where it silently does nothing (app.ts:8016). It is not a recordedCall, so actions cannot record it; Photoshop records Revert.
findings.repro: Open a saved file, make several edits, press F12 (or File ▸ Revert). All edits are gone, Edit ▸ Undo is disabled and the History panel is empty.
findings.impact: One keystroke destroys unsaved work irreversibly. Photoshop records Revert as a history state that can be undone.
findings.suggested_fix: Make Revert an undoable history step (keep the pre-revert engine or project bytes as the undo target), or at least confirm when the document is dirty. Disable it when there is no path or the document is clean. Wrap it in recordedCall.
findings.verdict_reason: revertDocument (app.ts:8014-8043) is a plain async function, not a recordedCall, and asks for no confirmation. store.revertActiveDoc swaps in the new engine (store.ts:6052) and sets history: [] twice (6089, 6114), and the fresh engine has an empty undo stack. psMenuData.ts:109-111 binds F12. keyboardShortcuts.ts accepts bare F-keys (the /^F/ test at ~line 158). menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3467) has no revert key, so the command stays enabled for never-saved documents, where it silently returns (app.ts:8016). Its own comment says Photoshop greys the command out in that case. Photoshop records Revert as an undoable history state.

findings.title: Reverting a .mvis document drops its document metadata (guides, notes, layer comps, saved paths, resolution…), and the next save erases them from disk
findings.feature: File ▸ Revert (Monet Vision Document container)
findings.evidence: buildForName (app.ts:8000) returns { engine: engine.buildGraphics(bytes) } with no document. openContainer (6922-6926) instead passes decodeDocumentMetaBytes from the vision-document entry. With document undefined, revertActiveDoc (store.ts:6040-6124) resets guides, notes, layer comps, saved paths (from the engine, which has none here), resolution, pixel aspect, measure scale and Camera Raw provenance to defaults, and marks the document clean. visionContainerBytes (app.ts ~7640-7652) then writes VISION_DOCUMENT_ENTRY from that stripped metadata, and courierContainerSave drops the old entry.
findings.repro: Create guides, a note, a layer comp and a saved path. Save as .mvis, make an edit, then File ▸ Revert: the guides, notes, comps and paths disappear. Press ⌘S and reopen: they are gone from the file.
findings.impact: Permanent loss of document metadata in Vision's own registered document format.
findings.suggested_fix: In buildForName's container branch, read the vision-document entry the same way openContainer does and return it as document. Add a revert round-trip test for .mvis.
findings.verdict_reason: buildForName (app.ts:8000) returns { engine: engine.buildGraphics(bytes) } with no document, while openContainer (6924-6925) decodes the VISION_DOCUMENT_ROLE entry. With document undefined, revertActiveDoc (store.ts:6040-6124) sets guides, notes, layer comps, resolution, pixel aspect and measure scale to defaults. Saved paths come from eng.photoshop_paths_json, and a graphics engine has none. The document is then marked clean. On the next save, visionContainerBytes (app.ts:7634-7644) calls setEntry(VISION_DOCUMENT_ENTRY_PATH, …) with the stripped docDocumentMeta, which overwrites the old entry that courierContainerSave kept. No revert test covers containers (the app.test.ts and pluginFormatsOpen.test.ts revert tests mock revertActiveDoc).

findings.title: Crash recovery deletes the recovery file as soon as the document reopens, so a second crash before the next tick loses the recovered work
findings.feature: Auto-recover (Preferences ▸ File Handling)
findings.evidence: restoreRecoveryFiles (autoRecover.ts:57-76) removes each file right after io.open succeeds. recoverLastSession (app.ts:8256-8275) opens it with store.openProject and markDocDirty. The recovered document gets a new id and no recoverySnapshots entry (app.ts:8159), so writeRecoverySnapshots writes it again only on the next interval tick (startAutoRecover 8283-8288; default 10 minutes).
findings.repro: Crash with a dirty document, relaunch and choose Recover. Crash again within 10 minutes (for example the same out-of-memory condition). On the next launch nothing is offered.
findings.impact: The recovered work is lost, and a repeat crash is likely when the document itself caused the first one.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the file until the recovered document is saved or closed: seed recoverySnapshots with { revision, file } under the new doc id (or rename the file) instead of deleting it, or write a fresh snapshot before removing the old one.
findings.verdict_reason: The mechanism is as described. restoreRecoveryFiles (autoRecover.ts:64-75) removes each file right after io.open. The recovered document gets a new id with no recoverySnapshots entry. startAutoRecover runs only after recoverLastSession resolves and uses setInterval, so the first rewrite happens a full interval later (default 10 minutes, app.ts:8283-8288, 8293). I downgraded it to minor because loss needs a second crash inside that window. The claim that a repeat crash is 'likely' is speculative.

findings.title: Snapshots of documents the user chose to discard survive, and the next launch offers them as 'ended unexpectedly'
findings.feature: Auto-recover / close / quit
findings.evidence: closeDocumentTab (app.ts:8427-8446) calls store.closeDoc (store.ts:6281), which never fires onDocSaved or removes the snapshot. Only the next timer tick's planRecovery drop (app.ts:8185-8196) cleans it up. installUnsavedWorkGuard (8367-8372) calls win.destroy() after 'Quit without saving?' without clearing snapshots.
findings.repro: Keep a document dirty for more than 10 minutes so a snapshot is written. Press ⌘W, answer Yes (close without saving), then quit. Relaunch: 'found 1 unsaved document from a session that ended unexpectedly'.
findings.impact: A misleading recovery prompt resurrects work the user explicitly threw away.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the document's snapshot in closeDocumentTab after a discard, and remove the session's snapshots once confirmDiscardAll is accepted.
findings.verdict_reason: closeDocumentTab (app.ts:8427-8446) and store.closeDoc (store.ts:6281-6331) never touch recoverySnapshots or call onDocSaved. onDocumentEvent('closeDocument') runs only script-event bindings (app.ts:229-235). The only cleanup is the next timer tick's planRecovery drop (app.ts:8190-8196). installUnsavedWorkGuard calls win.destroy() after confirmDiscardAll without clearing snapshots. A discard followed by a quit before the next tick leaves the file on disk, and recoverLastSession offers it at the next launch. The header comment at app.ts:8155 ('a save or close deletes its snapshot') is inaccurate for close.

findings.title: No single-instance guard: a second process's launch recovery scan deletes the running instance's live recovery snapshots
findings.feature: Launch / open-with / auto-recover
findings.evidence: The main.rs builder (321-346) has no single-instance plugin. The comment in setup says plain launches with a path open files on Linux/Windows and by direct exec on macOS, and the Windows/Linux file associations start a new process. app.ts:8293 runs recoverLastSession at every GUI boot against the shared appData recovery folder, and restoreRecoveryFiles removes every file whichever answer the user gives. The first instance's recoverySnapshots map still records them and will not rewrite until the document's revision changes. The second instance also rebinds MCP and rewrites mcp.json.
findings.repro: Windows or Linux: Vision is running with a document dirty for more than 10 minutes. Double-click a .png in the file manager. The second window asks 'Recover Documents?', and either answer deletes the first instance's snapshots.
findings.impact: Crash protection for the running session is silently removed, and there is a confusing duplicate app window.
findings.suggested_fix: Add tauri-plugin-single-instance and forward argv to queue_open. Alternatively, lock the recovery folder or use one subfolder per process and skip folders owned by a live PID.
findings.verdict_reason: The main.rs builder (321-346) registers no single-instance plugin, and Cargo.toml has none. On Windows and Linux, file associations and argv launch a new process (setup's queue_open(file_args(...)) path). macOS Finder opens go through RunEvent::Opened in the same process, so the issue is effectively Windows, Linux and direct exec only. The second process runs recoverLastSession at boot (app.ts:8293) against the same appData/recovery folder, and restoreRecoveryFiles removes every file whichever answer is given. The first instance's recoverySnapshots entry keeps the old revision, so planRecovery will not rewrite until the next edit. Severity stays minor because it needs two instances on non-mac platforms.

findings.title: Synchronous confirm() on the desktop returns a truthy Promise: 'Ask When Opening' profile prompts and the PSD/PSB Save As warning never appear
findings.feature: File ▸ Open colour-profile policy; Save As PSD/PSB
findings.evidence: tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1 src/init-iife.js replaces window.confirm with an async function that invokes plugin:dialog|confirm, a command that is never registered (lib.rs:198-203 registers only open, save and message). The team's own comment at app.ts:575-577 records this. Affected call sites in this area: app.ts:7379 (embedded profile: always preserves), 7398 (missing profile: always assigns working RGB) and 8106 (!confirm(...) is always false, so the PSD warning is skipped). The same pattern appears in App.tsx:2158 and store.ts:6645-6648, outside this area.
findings.repro: Set Color Settings to 'Ask When Opening' and open an Adobe RGB-tagged PNG in the desktop app: no prompt appears and the embedded profile is kept silently. An unhandled promise rejection is logged. Save As .psd: the warning never shows.
findings.impact: User-chosen colour-policy prompts are ignored when opening files, and export warnings are skipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace these calls with await ask(...) from @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog (as confirmPlaybackPause does) or the in-app DialogProvider, and add a lint rule that bans global confirm in src/.
findings.verdict_reason: monet_ui::dialog_plugin() is tauri_plugin_dialog::init(). Its init-iife.js (2.7.1) sets window.confirm = async function invoking plugin:dialog|confirm, while lib.rs registers only open, save and message. app.ts:575-577 already records this (#480). At app.ts:7379 `confirm(...)` yields a Promise, so preserve is always truthy. At 7398 assignWorking is always truthy. In Save As (~8106), `!confirm(...)` is always false, so the PSD warning is skipped. That skip is harmless to data, because saveAsIsCopy keeps the document unsaved. The rejected invoke produces an unhandled rejection.

findings.title: Close, Close All and Quit prompts offer only Discard or Cancel, with no Save option
findings.feature: File ▸ Close / Close All / Close Others / Quit
findings.evidence: confirmDiscard (app.ts:8395-8404) asks 'Close without saving?' and confirmDiscardAll (8381-8393) asks 'Quit without saving?', both through the Yes/No ask(). closeDocumentTab (8427-8446) has no save branch, except for Smart Object edit tabs.
findings.repro: Edit 5 documents and choose Close All. Each prompt only asks whether to discard; to keep work you must cancel, save each document, then close again.
findings.impact: Clumsy workflow, and 'Yes' (discard) is the easy click, unlike Photoshop's Save / Don't Save / Cancel.
findings.suggested_fix: Use plugin-dialog message() with YesNoCancelCustom buttons (Save / Don't Save / Cancel). The Save choice runs saveDocument for that document and aborts the close if the save is cancelled or fails.
findings.verdict_reason: confirmDiscard (app.ts:8395-8404) and confirmDiscardAll (8381-8393) use the Yes/No ask() with 'Close without saving?' and 'Quit without saving?'. closeDocumentTab (8427-8446) has a save branch only for Smart Object edit tabs (confirmSaveEditedContents). This is a UX gap compared with Photoshop's Save / Don't Save / Cancel. It causes no data loss, because cancel is available.

findings.title: Opening a file that is already open creates a second tab bound to the same path; the two tabs overwrite each other on save
findings.feature: File ▸ Open / Open Recent / OS open / Save As
findings.evidence: routeOpen (app.ts:6942-6995) and openPaths (7956-7982) never look for an open document with the same savedPath. adoptDocPath (store.ts:6457-6474) pins both tabs to one path, and renameDoc gives them different names. Save As onto another open document's path is not checked either.
findings.repro: Open photo.png and edit it. Open photo.png again from Open Recent or Finder, edit and save the second tab, then save the first: the second tab's work is overwritten.
findings.impact: Last-writer-wins loss of edits. Photoshop brings the existing document to the front instead.
findings.suggested_fix: In openPaths and routeOpen, activate the existing document when its normalised savedPath matches. Refuse, or warn about, Save As onto another open document's path.
findings.verdict_reason: openPaths (app.ts:7956-7982) and routeOpen (6942+) never look up an existing document by savedPath. The only savedPath lookup in the store is recordRecentFile's thumbnail lookup (store.ts:6758). adoptDocPath (6457-6474) sets savedPath on the new tab and gives it a de-duplicated name through renameDoc, so both tabs save to the same file and the last writer wins. Save As does not check other open documents either.

findings.title: Open as Smart Object converts only the active layer of a layered file, and is disabled on Home
findings.feature: File ▸ Open as Smart Object
findings.evidence: openAsSmartObject (app.ts:7413-7440) calls routeOpen and then smart.convert(store.state.activeLayerId). smart.convert (2450-2464) converts only the selected or active layer. NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS (App.tsx:77) leaves out opensmartobject, so the command is disabled when no document is open.
findings.repro: File ▸ Open as Smart Object on a 3-layer PSD or .mvision: only the top layer becomes a smart object and the other layers stay loose. With no document open, the menu item is greyed out.
findings.impact: Wrong result for layered sources; Photoshop wraps the whole file in one smart object and allows the command from Home.
findings.suggested_fix: After opening, convert every root layer with convert_layers_to_smart_object, and add opensmartobject to NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS.
findings.verdict_reason: openAsSmartObject (app.ts:7413-7440) calls routeOpen and then smart.convert(store.state.activeLayerId). smart.convert (2450-2464) converts the multi-selection only when more than one layer is selected, and otherwise a single layer through convert_to_smart_object. A freshly opened PSD has only its active layer selected, so the other layers stay loose. The NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS regex (App.tsx:77) is ^(new|openf|clearrecent|browse|…)$, which excludes 'opensmartobject' (monetId at psMenuData.ts:40), so the command is disabled on Home.

findings.title: Opening a file silently closes an untouched document the user just made with File ▸ New
findings.feature: File ▸ New / Open (multiple documents)
findings.evidence: newDocument (store.ts:4918-4922) passes pristineBlank=true for every File ▸ New and MCP doc.new document. addDoc (4775-4781) evicts a lone pristine blank on the next open. The comment says this is meant for the boot 'Untitled', but a cold launch now shows Home (main.tsx creates a boot document only for collab).
findings.repro: File ▸ New with 3000×2000 CMYK at 300 ppi, then File ▸ Open photo.jpg: the new document's tab is gone.
findings.impact: The user's configured canvas and its settings are discarded without asking.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark only the collab boot document as pristine, and keep documents created through File ▸ New.
findings.verdict_reason: newDocument calls addDoc(eng, name, true, true, …) with pristineBlank=true as the fourth parameter (store.ts:4919-4924 against the signature at 4751-4755). addDoc (4775-4781) evicts a lone pristine, non-dirty document on the next adoption. The comment says this targets the boot 'Untitled', but main.tsx:34 creates a boot document only for collab. homeStart.test.ts:228 even encodes that a second File ▸ New replaces the first, so the behaviour is partly deliberate, but it still discards a user-configured canvas without asking. The document is untouched, so the loss is limited to its settings, which keeps this minor.

findings.title: Save and Save As never add files to Open Recent or the Home Recent grid, although Home says saved files will appear
findings.feature: File ▸ Open Recent / Home
findings.evidence: The only recordRecentFile callers are store.ts:6445 (setActivePath, used by open and revert), app.ts:6963 and store.ts:5829 (Camera Raw commit). adoptDocPath (6457-6474), used by Save As, never records the file. Home.tsx:55 says 'Files you open or save will appear here.'
findings.repro: New document, then Save As ~/a.mvision, then close: a.mvision is not in File ▸ Open Recent or on Home.
findings.impact: Freshly saved work cannot be reopened from recents.
findings.suggested_fix: Call recordRecentFile(path) in adoptDocPath when the save captured the current revision.
findings.verdict_reason: The only non-test recordRecentFile callers are app.ts:6963, store.ts:5829 and setActivePath (store.ts:6445). Save As goes through setDocPathAfterSave, then adoptDocPath (6457-6474), and neither calls recordRecentFile. Home.tsx:55 says 'Files you open or save will appear here.'

findings.title: .mvision, the default save format, is not a registered file association
findings.feature: Packaging / open-with
findings.evidence: The tauri.conf.json fileAssociations list mvis, psd, the image formats and the raw formats, but not mvision. SAVE_FILTERS (app.ts:7613-7614) and suggestedSaveName (nativeIoPolicy.ts:105-117) default to .mvision, and OPEN_FILTERS includes it.
findings.repro: Save a project (the default is .mvision) and double-click it in Finder: macOS does not offer Monet Vision.
findings.impact: Users' own saved projects do not open from the Finder or Explorer.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an association for 'mvision' (Monet Vision Project, role Editor).
findings.verdict_reason: tauri.conf.json bundle.fileAssociations list mvis, psd/psb/xcf, the image formats, the raw formats and the other Monet containers, but not mvision. SAVE_FILTERS lists 'Monet Vision Project' (mvision) first (app.ts:7613), and suggestedSaveName/withProjectExtension default to .mvision (nativeIoPolicy.ts:105-117). launchOpen.test.ts:83-96 checks the association list without mvision, and I found no recorded rationale for leaving it out.

findings.title: Recovery file names have no length cap: long non-ASCII tab names exceed the 255-byte limit, so that document is never snapshotted
findings.feature: Auto-recover
findings.evidence: recoveryFileName (autoRecover.ts:24-26) percent-encodes the whole tab name, turning each CJK character into 9 bytes. writeRecoverySnapshots (app.ts:8208-8217) only calls console.warn when the write fails.
findings.repro: Open a file whose name has 28 or more Japanese characters, edit it and wait for the recovery tick. The write fails with ENAMETOOLONG and no snapshot exists.
findings.impact: No crash protection for such documents, and nothing tells the user.
findings.suggested_fix: Truncate or hash the encoded name to about 150 bytes, and keep the display name in the file (the project already stores it) or in a small index.
findings.verdict_reason: recoveryFileName (autoRecover.ts:24-26) is `${id}-${encodeURIComponent(name)}.mvision` with no cap, so each CJK character becomes 9 ASCII bytes. 28 CJK characters plus the extension and prefix exceed APFS/ext4 NAME_MAX (255 bytes). writeRecoverySnapshots (app.ts:8214-8218) only console.warns on failure, so the document silently gets no snapshot. The exact threshold depends on the filesystem, but the mechanism is certain.

findings.title: Document Browser says 'Drop … files here to open them', but drops on it do nothing in the desktop app
findings.feature: File ▸ Document Browser
findings.evidence: The Document Browser relies on an HTML5 onDrop (Dialogs.tsx:12572-12576) and shows the hint at 12604. monet-react file-drop.ts:61-63 notes that Tauri swallows HTML5 drops when native drop is enabled. The global handler's isCanvasDrop (App.tsx:2181-2187) accepts only drops over .mv-canvas-viewport or the Home screen.
findings.repro: Desktop app: open File ▸ Document Browser and drag a PNG from Finder onto the grid. Nothing opens.
findings.impact: The UI promises a feature that does not work.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend isCanvasDrop to accept drops over the Document Browser, or hide the hint when running natively.
findings.verdict_reason: The Document Browser relies on HTML5 onDrop (Dialogs.tsx:12572-12576) and shows the hint at 12604. Native drag-drop is not disabled anywhere (no dragDrop or drag_drop setting in tauri.conf.json or the monet-ui crate), so file-drop.ts:61-63 routes desktop drops through onDragDropEvent. The global handler accepts a drop only when elementFromPoint(...).closest('.mv-canvas-viewport, [data-mv-home-screen]') matches (App.tsx:2181-2187). Over the modal dialog it never matches, so the drop is ignored.

findings.title: Revert of a .mvision project skips relative-link resolution and does not restore smart links or smart-edit sources
findings.feature: File ▸ Revert (linked Smart Objects)
findings.evidence: revertDocument (app.ts:8021-8033) reads the bytes without resolveNativeProjectBytes, which openPaths applies at 7962 through resolveProjectLinks in packageDocument.ts:80-96. buildForName (8001-8004) plus revertActiveDoc never calls restoreSmartLinksForDoc or restoreSmartEditSources, which store.openProject does (store.ts:5018-5026).
findings.repro: Open a .mvision containing a linked Smart Object stored with a relative path, relink it during the session, then File ▸ Revert: the link keeps the in-session target instead of the saved one.
findings.impact: Links after Revert can differ from the file on disk; later saves then persist the wrong link.
findings.suggested_fix: Route .mvision revert through resolveNativeProjectBytes and apply the envelope's smart links and edit sources, as openProject does.
findings.verdict_reason: revertDocument (app.ts:8021-8032) reads the bytes without resolveNativeProjectBytes, which openPaths applies at 7962. buildForName's .mvision branch (8003-8006) returns only engine and document. revertActiveDoc never calls restoreSmartLinksForDoc or restoreSmartEditSources, which openProject calls (store.ts:5024-5025). restoreSmartLinksForDoc (smartLinks.ts:66-82) is what clears and replaces a document's links, so after a revert the in-session link map survives unchanged.

findings.title: Closed, reverted and evicted documents' WASM engines are freed only by GC, which can exhaust wasm32 memory when working with several large documents
findings.feature: Multiple documents / memory
findings.evidence: closeDoc (store.ts:6281-6345) says 'dropped engine is GC-reclaimed (no eager free)'. revertActiveDoc (6052) and addDoc eviction (4777-4781) also drop engines without freeing them. Reclaiming depends on wasm-bindgen's FinalizationRegistry (engine/pkg/monet_render_engine.js:8020-8022), and JS GC is not driven by WASM heap pressure. Linear memory never shrinks and is capped at 4 GB.
findings.repro: Unconfirmed. Native build: open and close five 50 MP layered documents one after another while logging the WASM memory.buffer.byteLength, and watch for engine allocation failures.
findings.impact: Possible engine out-of-memory after a long session with large files.
findings.suggested_fix: Free engines eagerly in closeDoc and revert once no pinned reference remains (count pins held by in-flight saves), or at least nudge a GC or compaction after closing.
findings.verdict_reason: The code facts hold. closeDoc (store.ts:6294) says 'dropped engine is GC-reclaimed (no eager free)', and revertActiveDoc (6052) and addDoc eviction (4777-4781) also drop engines without .free(). The impact is not shown: FinalizationRegistry timing is up to the engine, and once finalizers run, freed memory is reusable inside linear memory. Settling it needs the reviewer's own repro: log memory.buffer.byteLength while opening and closing several 50 MP layered documents in a native build and watch for allocation failures.

findings.title: Recovery I/O and the ⌘Q path have no behavioural tests
findings.feature: Auto-recover / quit guard
findings.evidence: autoRecover.test.ts:79-110 checks app.ts source strings. documentRecoveryEnabled (app.ts:8161-8163) is false in dev and test builds, so writeRecoverySnapshots and recoverLastSession never actually run. unsavedWorkGuard.test.ts drives a mocked onCloseRequested, and nothing covers terminate or ⌘Q.
findings.repro: Look for a test that writes and restores a snapshot through the real functions, or that quits the native app with a dirty document: there is none.
findings.impact: The blocker and major recovery bugs above were not caught.
findings.suggested_fix: Make documentRecoveryEnabled injectable and test the write → restore → keep-until-saved cycle with a mocked plugin-fs. Add a native smoke test that sends terminate: with a dirty document.
findings.verdict_reason: Mostly accurate, with one nuance. autoRecover.test.ts:79-110 asserts app.ts and store.ts source strings. There is one real-disk behavioural test of the pure restoreRecoveryFiles (from line 110), but writeRecoverySnapshots and recoverLastSession never execute under test, because documentRecoveryEnabled (app.ts:8161-8163) is false outside release Tauri. unsavedWorkGuard.test.ts mocks onCloseRequested only, and nothing exercises terminate: or ⌘Q, which is how the blocker in finding 1 slipped through.

findings.title: The MCP doc.new description says it replaces the current document, but it opens a new tab
findings.feature: MCP doc.new
findings.evidence: commands.ts:52 says 'Create a new blank document, replacing the current one'. store.newDocument then calls addDoc, which appends a tab (store.ts:4918).
findings.repro: Call doc.new over MCP with a document open: a second tab appears.
findings.impact: Agents misread what the tool does.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the JSDoc to say it opens a new tab, then run mcp:codegen.
findings.verdict_reason: commands.ts:51 says 'Create a new blank document, replacing the current one'. store.newDocument calls addDoc, which appends a tab. It replaces only when the current document is a lone pristine blank (the store.ts:4775 eviction), so the description is wrong in the common case.

areas.coverage:
What I inventoried: the File ▸ Export submenu has 39 items. 28 come from the psMenuData.ts blueprint and are all wired, with "Layer Comps to Files…" wired by label. psMenus.ts:288-310 injects 11 more: Preserved Photoshop Original, Layer Comps to PDF, TGA, PPM, PCX, SVG (Document), WebP Lossy, HEIC, DNG, PDF/X-1a and PDF/X-4. File ▸ Import has 5 blueprint items: 4 are wired (Open GIF as Animation, Variable Data Sets, Video Frames to Layers, Notes); WIA Support is a placeholder, and 3D LUT is injected on top. I also covered Place Embedded, Place Linked, Package, Open, Open as Smart Object, Open Recent, Save, Save As, Save a Copy, Revert, File Info, Generate ▸ Image Assets, Layer ▸ Quick Export and Export As, Smart Object ▸ Export Contents, and the MCP doc.open / saveAs / exportAs / exportPngBase64 / openPhotoshopRaw commands. Formats: about 30 read-format families (OPEN_FILTERS, app.ts:7596), 14 Save As families (SAVE_FILTERS, app.ts:7613), and the extra export-only encoders.

How I traced it: from each menu entry in App.tsx (menuActions 2562-2690, 2950-2980) through the handler in state/app.ts (saveBytes/downloadBytes, the export functions, bytesForExt, routeOpen, open/save/revert/recovery/package) and on into the engine in packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs (encoders, export_icc, encode_image_tagged, the PSD/CMYK writers, place_smart_object, save_project/MVSN, the metadata scope). I also read the native side: src-tauri main.rs, the c2pa_sign and heic plugins, capabilities, and tauri.conf.json. For download handling I checked the vendored tauri-2.11.2 and wry-0.55.1 sources in ~/.cargo. Other code read: projectEnvelope, nativeIoPolicy, photoshopFilePolicy, nativeBoundedRead, pdfExport and pdfImport, the Dialogs.tsx ExportPrefs, SaveForWeb and FileInfo dialogs, and the relevant e2e and unit tests.

What I did not do or could not confirm: I ran no builds, tests or runtime checks, so every finding comes from reading code. I did not verify byte-level PSD/PSB round-trip fidelity for text, styles and smart objects (the engine has extensive round-trip tests for it). I did not audit XCF, JPEG 2000, Cineon/DPX, IFF or DICOM decoder internals, and I did not check the video encoders on real hardware.
areas.parity_notes:
Photoshop items in this area that correctly show as disabled placeholders: Browse in Bridge, Close and Go to Bridge, Invite to Edit, Share, Share for Review (Beta), Import ▸ WIA Support. Every other File ▸ Export and Import blueprint item is wired.

Parity gaps (not bugs):
- Export As offers only PNG/JPEG/GIF: no SVG/WebP/AVIF, and no canvas size or resample options.
- Export Layers to Files has no options dialog (file type, prefix, visible layers only). It writes a full-canvas PNG of every layer, hidden ones included.
- Save As cannot write AVIF, HEIC, DNG, SVG, PCX, PPM or CMYK PSD; these are export-only.
- TIFF is written uncompressed RGBA and never CMYK or Gray.
- PSD/PSB/TIFF opens are capped at 256 MiB, so large Photoshop files, and PSB files in general, will not open.
- ⌘S on a TIFF/WebP/HEIC/PSD always goes to Save As; saving in place is limited to .mvision/.mvis/.png/.jpg/.gif. This is by design.
- Place cannot bring in vector formats (SVG/PDF/AI) as vector smart objects.
- Paths to Illustrator writes SVG, not .ai.
- Color Lookup Tables exports only .cube.
- Smart Object ▸ Export Contents writes a PNG of the source, not the original embedded file.

MCP compared with the menus:
- doc.exportAs and doc.saveAs cover the Save As formats and, unlike the menu exports, do write natively (atomicWriteBytes).
- MCP has no AVIF/HEIC/DNG/SVG/CMYK PSD/video export and no Export As scale or metadata options.

Content Credentials:
- The Signed export uses a bundled self-signed dev key until the user imports a certificate (documented as untrusted in docs/c2pa-signing.md).
- The unsigned JSON sidecar always declares format image/png.

findings.title: Every File ▸ Export command saves nothing in the macOS desktop app: the download it relies on is silently cancelled
findings.feature: File ▸ Export (all download-based exports: Quick Export, Export As, Export at Sizes, JPEG/PSD/PSB/CMYK PSD/GIF/TIFF/WebP/HDR/EXR/AVIF/PDF/PDF-X/HEIC/DNG/TGA/PPM/PCX/SVG, Save for Web, Layers/Artboards/Layer Comps to Files and PDF, Color Lookup Tables, Data Sets, Paths to Illustrator, Render Video, Content Credentials JSON), Layer ▸ Quick Export/Export As, Smart Object ▸ Export Contents
findings.evidence: app.ts:3605-3632: saveBytes → downloadBytes always writes by clicking a hidden `<a download href=blob:>` link; there is no isTauri() branch (unchanged since 89d53207). Vision registers no download handler: src-tauri/src/main.rs:321-400 and MonetWindowBuilder (packages/monet-ui/crates/monet-ui/src/lib.rs:315ff) never call on_download. Tauri only attaches a handler when one is given (tauri-2.11.2 src/webview/mod.rs:357,740). With no handler, wry-0.55.1 src/wkwebview/navigation.rs:68-74 answers a download request with WKNavigationActionPolicy::Cancel. By contrast, Save, Save As and Save a Copy (app.ts:8067,8121), Zoomify (5584-5602), signed Content Credentials (4988), Package, Image Assets watch mode (6740) and MCP doc.exportAs (mcp/commands.ts:317) all write with atomicWriteBytes. The e2e suite runs in Chromium, where link downloads work, so nothing tests the native path. e2e/heic-export.spec.ts even says the HEIC path is 'exercised on real hardware'. Yet exportHEIC (app.ts:5129-5155) only runs natively and ends in saveBytes, so HEIC export can never produce a file on any platform.
findings.repro: pnpm dev:vision (native macOS). Open any image. Choose File ▸ Export ▸ Export JPEG…, or Export As… ▸ Export, or Save for Web ▸ Save. No save panel appears, nothing lands in ~/Downloads or anywhere else, and no error is shown. The Export As / Save for Web dialogs close as if the export worked.
findings.impact: On the primary platform, roughly 40 advertised export commands do nothing. The only ways to get a file out are Save As / Save a Copy for the formats they support, or MCP. Preset, swatch and ACT exports that go through saveBytes are affected the same way.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix it once in saveBytes. When isTauri(), show the plugin-dialog save() panel defaulting to `filename`, then call atomicWriteBytes; treat Cancel as a no-op. Artisan's io/files.ts:57 saveBytesFile already does this. Multi-file exporters (layers, artboards, comps, sizes, slices, data sets) should ask for a folder once, as zoomifyWriter does. A stopgap is to register on_download in MonetWindowBuilder so that link downloads land in ~/Downloads. Add a vitest that mocks isTauri=true and asserts that saveBytes writes through atomicWriteBytes.
findings.verdict_reason: saveBytes (app.ts:3605-3609) always calls downloadBytes (3614-3628), which only clicks a hidden <a download href=blob:>. Neither function has an isTauri() branch. No on_download or DownloadEvent handler exists in apps/vision/src-tauri/src or packages/monet-ui/crates (grep finds only model_dl.rs's own unrelated enum). tauri.conf.json has windows: [], so the only webview is the MonetWindow built in main.rs:393-404, with no download handler. Cargo.lock pins wry 0.55.1. Its navigation.rs:68-74 answers WKNavigationActionPolicy::Cancel when shouldPerformDownload is set and has_download_handler is false, and has_download_handler is set only when a handler is attached (wkwebview/mod.rs:570). exportPNG/exportJPEG (4633, 4673), exportTIFF (5055), Save for Web (saveCanvasRegion 5240), exportSizes, layer/artboard/comp exports and dataVars.exportAll all end in saveBytes. exportHEIC (5129-5155) returns early when !isTauri() and ends in saveBytes when native, so it can never produce a file. No menu wrapper swaps in a native path (App.tsx:2586, 2622, 2628 call these functions directly).

findings.title: Save in place strips the original file's EXIF/XMP/IPTC, and File Info never loads metadata from opened files
findings.feature: File ▸ Save (in-place JPEG/PNG), all flat exports, PSD/PSB export, File ▸ File Info
findings.evidence: The engine's doc_meta is only ever set by set_document_metadata (mod.rs:8412-8416) or when a project loads. from_image (mod.rs:7094-7103) decodes pixels only. encode_image_tagged (mod.rs:35338-35393) writes the ICC profile plus doc_meta alone, so the source file's EXIF, XMP and IPTC are never carried over. saveDocument's in-place path (app.ts:8062-8068) re-encodes through bytesForExt into these encoders. The File Info dialog reads engine.document_metadata() (Dialogs.tsx:2571-2579), so it opens blank for a photo that has copyright/author/keywords. The PSD/PSB writer's image resources (mod.rs:30421-30452) contain no XMP (resource 1060) or IPTC, so even File Info typed into Vision is lost in PSD exports. No test round-trips metadata through open → save.
findings.repro: Open a camera JPEG that has EXIF (make, model, date, GPS) and an XMP copyright. Crop it and press ⌘S. Run exiftool on the file: the camera EXIF, GPS, capture date and copyright are gone. File ▸ File Info also showed empty fields before the save.
findings.impact: Pressing ⌘S destroys irreplaceable photo metadata in the user's original file, silently. Photoshop keeps it. Copyright and credit fields are lost on every PSD export.
findings.suggested_fix: When opening, parse the source XMP/IPTC/EXIF into doc_meta (at least the File Info fields). Keep the raw EXIF/XMP blocks from the opened file and re-embed them in same-format saves, via set_exif_metadata on the jpeg/webp encoders and iTXt/eXIf in PNG. Write XMP resource 1060 in the PSD writer.
findings.verdict_reason: from_image (mod.rs:7094-7103) only decodes pixels. doc_meta starts as the default (3615) and is set only by set_document_metadata (8412), whose single app caller is the File Info dialog (Dialogs.tsx:2623). The project loader also restores it. No TS code parses EXIF/XMP from a source file (the only exif/xmp hits in app.ts, store.ts and projectEnvelope.ts are Camera Raw sidecars and a HEIC comment). encode_image_tagged (35338-35393) embeds only the ICC plus doc_meta, and TIFF/WebP get ICC only. In-place ⌘S is allowed for png/jpg/jpeg/gif (nativeIoPolicy.ts:57), and saveDocument (app.ts:8063-8066) re-encodes through bytesForExt. meta.xmp() is called only at 35139 and 35164 (PNG and JPEG), so the PSD writer's resource assembly (30421-30452) carries no XMP or IPTC. readFileInfo (Dialogs.tsx:2571) reads only the engine, so File Info opens blank.

findings.title: Vision saves project files it later refuses to open: .mvis open is capped at 256 MiB and raw .mvision at 512 MiB, but neither write is capped
findings.feature: File ▸ Save / Save As (.mvis, .mvision), auto-recovery, Revert; also PSD/PSB/TIFF exports above 256 MiB
findings.evidence: openFileReadLimit (app.ts:6809-6815) sends .mvis and every other Monet container, TIFF, PSD and PSB through imageReadLimit, which is MAX_OPEN_IMAGE_SOURCE_BYTES = 256 MiB (photoshopFilePolicy.ts:12-16, 100-115). A plain .mvision gets 512 MiB (projectEnvelope.ts:34). The .mvis writer (visionContainerBytes, app.ts:7631-7643) has no size check; the container format allows up to 4 GB (monet-format container/mod.rs:429). store.saveProjectForDoc (store.ts:5071-5085) returns the raw MVSN engine bytes, with no cap, when a document has no extra metadata. MVSN stores every layer uncompressed as u16 RGBA (mod.rs:35549-35554; pixels plus smart_src at 30844-30848), which is 8 bytes per pixel per layer and 16 for Smart Objects. When the document does need the envelope, the encoder refuses anything over 384 MiB with the internal message 'Monet Vision project engine exceeds the decoded size limit' (projectEnvelope.ts:37,226-227,570). Recovery snapshots use the same bytes and only console.warn on failure (app.ts:8210-8216).
findings.repro: Create a 6000×4000 document at 72 ppi and add 3-4 pixel layers. Save as .mvision: the file is over 512 MiB, the tab is marked clean, and reopening it says 'Monet Vision project exceeds the 512 MiB size limit.' Or save a large layered photo as .mvis: once the compressed file passes 256 MiB, reopening says 'Image document exceeds the 256 MiB size limit.' When the document has guides, EXIF or a non-72 ppi resolution, ⌘S fails outright with the internal message, and no auto-recovery snapshot is taken.
findings.impact: Work the app reported as saved cannot be reopened in this build, and Revert fails for the same reason. Large documents also silently lose crash recovery.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one limit per format for both read and write: have .mvis/containers use a container limit at least as large as anything the writer produces, and make the writers refuse (before writing or marking the tab clean) any size the reader will reject, with a plain message that points to an alternative format. Consider compressing MVSN pixel planes. Show recovery-snapshot failures to the user.
findings.verdict_reason: openFileReadLimit (app.ts:6809-6816) sends .mvis to imageReadLimit(name, 'open'), which returns MAX_OPEN_IMAGE_SOURCE_BYTES = 256 MiB (photoshopFilePolicy.ts:12-16, 115). .mvision gets MAX_PROJECT_ENVELOPE_BYTES = 512 MiB. Native open (6416, 7092), Revert (8026) and recovery (8264) all use this limit. The write side has no size check: bytesForExt (7654+) → visionContainerBytes (7634-7644) or projectBytesForDoc. saveProjectForDoc (store.ts:5071-5085) returns the raw engine bytes when no metadata is present, and EngineClient.projectBytes (411-417) does not compress. save_project writes every layer through w_u16vec (mod.rs:35548-35554, 30844-30848), i.e. uncompressed u16 RGBA. A 24 MP layer is about 192 MB, so three layers pass 512 MiB. encodeProjectEnvelope refuses engine bytes over 384 MiB with 'Monet Vision project engine exceeds the decoded size limit' (projectEnvelope.ts:226-227, 570). The recovery snapshot only console.warns (app.ts:8215). The work is not destroyed, since a later build could raise the limit, so this stays major.

findings.title: PDF export ignores the built-in working profile: PDF/X-4 rejects nearly every document, and standard PDFs of P3/Adobe RGB documents are untagged
findings.feature: File ▸ Export ▸ PDF, PDF/X-4, Artboards/Layer Comps to PDF, PDF Presentation, Save As PDF
findings.evidence: exportIccBytes (app.ts:4626-4629) returns ICC bytes only for a loaded custom profile, and store.assignProfile leaves iccProfileBytes null for the built-in sRGB/P3/Adobe RGB/Rec.2020 profiles (store.ts:8070-8100). The engine encoders fall back to psd_icc_profile(self.profile), but pdfDocument has no such fallback: when X-4 gets an empty icc it shows 'PDF/X-4 needs a colour profile. Assign one with Edit ▸ Assign Profile' (app.ts:5704-5707), and otherwise passes icc null (5718), which pdfExport.ts:176 writes as /DeviceRGB. The page samples are decoded unmanaged in document space (pdfPageFromPng / pngToJpegPage, #34). No engine method exposes the built-in ICC bytes. pdfExport.test.ts:124 tests the builder only; no test drives exportPDFX4 on a document with a built-in profile.
findings.repro: Open any sRGB or Display P3 JPEG, or create a new document. Choose File ▸ Export ▸ Export PDF/X-4…: an alert asks you to assign a profile, and doing so does not help. Export a plain PDF from a Display P3 document and open it in Preview or Acrobat: the colours are desaturated because P3 values are read as DeviceRGB.
findings.impact: An advertised prepress preset effectively only works for documents with a hand-loaded ICC file. Ordinary PDFs of wide-gamut documents show wrong colours.
findings.suggested_fix: Expose the built-in profile's ICC bytes from the engine (a wrapper around psd_icc_profile(self.profile, false, true)). In pdfDocument, use it whenever exportIccBytes returns empty. Add a unit test for X-4 and for standard PDF on a P3 document.
findings.verdict_reason: exportIccBytes (app.ts:4625-4628) returns bytes only when iccProfileBytes is set. Open-time profile handling (7365-7386) sets bytes only for embedded profiles that 'match no built-in', and assignProfile (store.ts:8070-8088) stores rawIcc = null for built-ins. pdfDocument (5697-5719) shows the X-4 alert when icc is empty and otherwise passes icc: null, which buildPdf writes as /DeviceRGB (pdfExport.ts:176). Pages are decoded unmanaged, in document space (pngToJpegPage 5353-5358 and the lossless path at 5632), so P3 samples are labelled DeviceRGB. pngToJpegPage's own comment assumes 'the page is tagged with the document's ICC profile by pdfDocument', which is false for built-ins. No wasm method exposes the built-in ICC: export_icc (mod.rs:29388) is private, and mode_profile_icc covers CMYK/Gray only. The only X-4 test (pdfExport.test.ts:124) exercises the builder, not exportPDFX4.

findings.title: Transparent areas turn black in JPEG, PDF, Save for Web JPEG and CMYK PSD exports
findings.feature: File ▸ Export ▸ JPEG / Export As JPEG / Save for Web JPEG / Layer Export As JPEG / PDF / PDF-X / CMYK PSD; ⌘S to .jpg
findings.evidence: Engine export_jpeg_with_icc (mod.rs:29905), export_scaled_jpeg_with_icc (29590) and export_layer_jpeg_trimmed (29700) all call to_rgb8() on the RGBA composite. That drops alpha without applying a matte, and new transparent layers are zero-filled (Layer::transparent). PDF pages use pngToJpegPage (app.ts:5353-5366): putImageData followed by canvas.toBlob('image/jpeg') with no white fill, and the HTML spec composites transparent pixels onto opaque black. The lossless/X-4 path strips alpha with rgbFromRgba. export_psd_cmyk_with_icc (mod.rs:9169-9200) separates RGB and ignores alpha. Save for Web's default matte is 'transparent' (webExportPrefs.ts:47-53).
findings.repro: File ▸ New with a Transparent background. Paint a shape, then choose File ▸ Export ▸ Export JPEG… or Export PDF…. The empty area comes out black. Photoshop flattens it to white.
findings.impact: Logos and cut-outs exported for print or web get black backgrounds, and the CMYK press file gets rich-black ink where there should be none.
findings.suggested_fix: In the engine's JPEG/CMYK flatten paths, composite onto white (or the Save for Web matte) before dropping alpha. In pngToJpegPage and the lossless PDF path, fill the canvas with white (or the matte) before drawing.
findings.verdict_reason: The composite accumulator starts at Rgba::new(0,0,0,0) (mod.rs:6864), and Layer::transparent is zero-filled (384-388), so uncovered pixels are RGB 0. export_jpeg_with_icc (29905), export_scaled_jpeg (29591) and the layer JPEG trims (29700, 29740) call to_rgb8() with no matte. pngToJpegPage (app.ts:5353-5365) calls putImageData and then toBlob('image/jpeg') with no fill. The lossless PDF path uses rgbFromRgba (5634). Save for Web's default matte 'transparent' maps to null (webExportPrefs.ts:50, 120-121), and canvasRegionBytes (5231-5233) then encodes JPEG straight from the canvas. export_psd_cmyk_with_icc (9176-9203) separates the rgba16 composite and ignores alpha, so empty areas become rich black ink. This is only reached for documents with transparent regions, but opening a transparent PNG and exporting a JPEG is a common path.

findings.title: Layer, artboard, layer-comp and Image Assets exports drop the document's colour profile
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Quick Export as PNG / Export As; File ▸ Export ▸ Export Layers to Files, Artboards to Files, Layer Comps to Files; File ▸ Generate ▸ Image Assets
findings.evidence: export_layer_png_trimmed, export_layer_jpeg_trimmed and the scaled variants (mod.rs:29683-29740) tag the file with engine.export_icc(&[]), which is the built-in profile only. export_icc (mod.rs:~29389-29394) never consults the engine's own custom document ICC (document_icc, mod.rs:15758), and a custom profile's id is clamped to sRGB. exportLayersToFiles (app.ts:6085-6090) and generateImageAssets (6715-6722) use export_layer_png → export_png() with no custom ICC. renderLayerCompPngs (6096-6111) uses clone.export_png(). export_artboard_png (mod.rs:13810-13849) encodes with write_to and embeds no ICC at all, even for built-in P3/Adobe RGB. The same bug was fixed for Export at Sizes in #35 (app.ts:4904-4913), and colorExportWiring.test.ts covers only document-level exports.
findings.repro: Open a ProPhoto RGB TIFF (or Assign Profile ▸ Load Profile… with any .icc). Choose Layer ▸ Quick Export as PNG: the PNG is untagged, so its ProPhoto values display as sRGB and colours are badly off. In a Display P3 document with artboards, File ▸ Export ▸ Artboards to Files writes untagged PNGs.
findings.impact: Asset and handoff exports come out in the wrong colours whenever the document is not plain sRGB (artboards) or uses a custom ICC profile (everything else).
findings.suggested_fix: Fix it once in the engine: have export_icc(&[]) fall back to the stored custom document ICC before the built-in profile, and route export_artboard_png through encode_image_tagged. That covers every caller.
findings.verdict_reason: The trimmed and scaled layer encoders (mod.rs:29682-29745) call engine.export_icc(&[]). export_icc (29388-29393) falls back only to psd_icc_profile(self.profile), and a custom profile's id is clamped to sRGB (comment at app.ts:7371-7373), so the result is untagged. The engine does hold the custom ICC via set_document_icc/document_icc (15739, 15758), which store.syncDocumentIcc pushes, but export_icc never reads it. exportLayersToFiles (app.ts:6085-6090) and generateImageAssets (6715-6722) use export_layer_png/jpeg with no ICC, and renderLayerCompPngs uses clone.export_png(). export_artboard_png (13810-13849) encodes with write_to and embeds no ICC at all, even for built-in P3 or Adobe RGB. The severity depends on how many documents use a custom or wide-gamut profile, but when it happens the colours are silently wrong, so it stays major.

findings.title: Open as Smart Object on a layered file converts only the active layer, not the whole file
findings.feature: File ▸ Open as Smart Object
findings.evidence: openAsSmartObject (app.ts:7413-7440) calls routeOpen, which opens the layered PSD/PSB/TIFF/.mvision/.mvis as a normal document, and then smart.convert(store.state.activeLayerId) (7436). smart.convert (app.ts:2450-2460) converts only the selected layers, or just the one id when nothing is multi-selected (a newly opened document has no multi-selection). Photoshop wraps the entire file in a single embedded Smart Object.
findings.repro: File ▸ Open as Smart Object…, then pick a layered PSD. The resulting document still has all the separate layers, and only the top/active one is a Smart Object.
findings.impact: The advertised command gives the wrong document structure for layered inputs. Only flat inputs (JPEG/PNG/raw) work as expected.
findings.suggested_fix: After opening, convert every root layer: call convert_layers_to_smart_object with all layer ids, or flatten the file into a single place_smart_object on a new document of the file's size.
findings.verdict_reason: openAsSmartObject (app.ts:7413-7440) calls routeOpen and then smart.convert(store.state.activeLayerId). smart.convert (2450-2462) converts the multi-selection only when it has more than one entry, and otherwise converts the single id. A freshly opened document resets selectedLayerIds to [] (store.ts:1371, 6311), so a layered PSD, TIFF or .mvision keeps its separate layers and only the active one becomes a Smart Object. Flat and raw inputs behave correctly.

findings.title: Place Embedded/Linked does no colour conversion and accepts formats the place decoder cannot read
findings.feature: File ▸ Place Embedded / Place Linked; File ▸ Scripts ▸ Load Files into Stack
findings.evidence: place_smart_object → decoded_placed_smart_source (mod.rs:5373-5402) → decode_oriented (1347-1370) copies the raw numbers and never looks at the file's embedded profile, whereas pasting between documents follows the paste profile policy (store.ts:6636-6648). The Place Embedded input accepts 'image/*,.psd,.psb' (App.tsx:3752), which admits SVG/AVIF/HEIC/TGA/PNM/PCX. The engine is built with only png/jpeg/webp/bmp/tiff/gif/hdr/exr (+JP2/DPX/IFF/DICOM) decoders (engine Cargo.toml:40, codecs.rs:17-28), and placeImageFile (app.ts:7520-7532) sends everything to the engine, so those formats fail with 'decode failed'. Place Linked's native filter omits PSD/PSB (app.ts:330-333). Load Files into Stack offers every OPEN_FILTERS type but imports files 2 through n with E().importImage (app.ts:7739), so AVIF/HEIC/SVG/TGA/PDF layers fail there as well.
findings.repro: Place Embedded an Adobe RGB JPEG into an sRGB document: the colours shift. Place Embedded a .svg or .avif: the alert says 'decode failed'. Load Files into Stack with a PNG followed by an AVIF: the AVIF layer is rejected.
findings.impact: Colours are wrong when placing non-sRGB images. File types that File ▸ Open supports fail in Place and in stacking.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the paste/embedded profile policy on place. Run placed bytes through the same TS transcoders routeOpen uses (avifToPng, svgToPng, decodeTga and so on) before calling the engine, or narrow the accept lists to what the engine can decode.
findings.verdict_reason: place_smart_object (mod.rs:14475-14494) → decoded_placed_smart_source (5373-5402) → decode_oriented (1347-1370) uses image::load_from_memory, with no ICC or profile policy. The TS side (placeImageFile 7520-7532, placeEmbeddedFromBytes 7491) does no transcoding or conversion. The place input accepts 'image/*,.psd,.psb' (App.tsx:3752). The engine's image crate has only png/jpeg/webp/bmp/tiff/gif/hdr/exr (engine Cargo.toml:39), plus the JP2/Cineon/DPX/IFF/DICOM codecs (codecs.rs:17-28), so SVG, AVIF, HEIC and TGA fail with 'decode failed'. SMART_LINK_FILTERS (app.ts:330-333) leaves out PSD/PSB. stackImages (7739) imports files 2..n with E().importImage while the native picker offers OPEN_FILTERS (7592-7600), which include avif/heic/svg/tga/pdf.

findings.title: The Export As ▸ Metadata choice persists in the engine and silently changes later saves and exports
findings.feature: File ▸ Export ▸ Export As… Metadata; File ▸ Save; all flat exports
findings.evidence: The Export As commit (Dialogs.tsx:4151) calls set_export_metadata_scope on the document engine. The scope is engine state (mod.rs:8423-8441), and export_png/jpeg/tiff/webp_with_icc read it on every encode (29437, 29904, 29918, 29984), including the in-place ⌘S path (app.ts:8066 → bytesForExt). Photoshop applies that choice only to the one Export As.
findings.repro: Fill in File ▸ File Info ▸ Copyright. Run Export As… with Metadata set to None. Then press ⌘S on the opened JPEG: the saved file has no copyright or XMP.
findings.impact: One export silently strips File Info from every later save and export of that document.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the scope into the export call (or restore the previous scope after exportAs / exportSelectedLayersAs runs) instead of changing persistent engine state.
findings.verdict_reason: Dialogs.tsx:4151 is the only caller of set_export_metadata_scope, and nothing restores the scope afterwards. The scope is persistent engine state (mod.rs:8423-8441, default META_SCOPE_ALL at 3616), and export_metadata() scopes every tagged encode, including in-place ⌘S through bytesForExt (app.ts:8066). The dialog re-seeds from the engine's scope (Dialogs.tsx:4114), so the stickiness looks partly intentional. Only File Info typed in Vision is affected, because source metadata is never loaded (see the metadata finding).

findings.title: Flat exports and in-place saves of CMYK/Gray/Lab documents silently write RGB(A)
findings.feature: File ▸ Export ▸ TIFF / JPEG / PNG / WebP; ⌘S of a flat .png/.jpg after Image ▸ Mode
findings.evidence: composite_image_deep and composite_image (mod.rs:~29395-29425) always produce RGBA. export_tiff_with_icc (29916-29921) writes an RGBA TIFF with an alpha channel even for an opaque CMYK or Gray document, and exportTIFF (app.ts:5055-5065) shows no notice. canSaveInPlace (nativeIoPolicy.ts:90-94) allows ⌘S of a flat CMYK document to .png/.jpg and marks it clean. Only the PSD writers keep the document's mode.
findings.repro: Choose Image ▸ Mode ▸ CMYK, then File ▸ Export ▸ Export TIFF…: the TIFF is RGBA and tagged with the RGB working profile. Or open a PNG, convert it to CMYK and press ⌘S: the file is written as RGB, the tab is clean, and after reopening the CMYK plates are gone.
findings.impact: Press-bound TIFF/JPEG deliverables come out as RGB with no warning. The CMYK plates are lost after an in-place save.
findings.suggested_fix: Write CMYK/Gray TIFF and JPEG from the document's plates, as the CMYK PSD path already does, or at least warn. Route ⌘S for a non-RGB document to Save As when the target format cannot hold the mode.
findings.verdict_reason: composite_image_deep (mod.rs:29407-29425) and composite_image always build RGBA DynamicImages. export_tiff_with_icc (29916-29921) encodes that with the RGB export_icc, and exportTIFF (app.ts:5055-5065) shows no notice. canSaveInPlace (nativeIoPolicy.ts:90-94) checks only the extension and flatness, and docIsFlat is just layer_count() <= 1 (app.ts:7702), with no mode check. ⌘S of a flat CMYK document to .png or .jpg therefore writes RGB and marks the document saved.

findings.title: Synchronous exporters have no error reporting, so failures disappear
findings.feature: Export PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/HDR/EXR, Export at Sizes, Export Layers to Files, Layer Comps to Files, Color Lookup Tables, Paths/SVG, Export As dialog
findings.evidence: The menu dispatch (App.tsx:3333-3336) has no try/catch, and there is no global error handler. exportPNG (app.ts:4633), exportJPEG (4673), exportGIF (1921), exportWebP (5067), exportHDR/EXR (5089-5095), exportSizes (4904; unlike exportAs at 4815 it has no exportScaleFits pre-check), exportLayersToFiles (6085), exportLayerCompsToFiles (6113), exportColorLUT (5809) and exportPathsSVG/DocumentSVG (6070-6082) call engine encoders that return Err: for a rejected imported-Photoshop edit, for scaled dimensions over MAX_PIXELS, and when saveBytes' assertHistorySettled fails. ExportPrefs.commit (Dialogs.tsx:4146-4155) calls exportAs without a catch, so on a throw the dialog stays open with no message. #384 fixed only the async exporters.
findings.repro: On a very large document, choose File ▸ Export ▸ Export at Sizes: 1× and 2× are saved, the 3× row goes over the pixel limit, and nothing tells the user a file is missing.
findings.impact: Some or all of an export is silently missing. The user sees no feedback.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the synchronous exporters in the existing reportSave, or catch once in the stableMenuActions wrapper and in ExportPrefs.commit. Add the exportScaleFits check to exportSizes.
findings.verdict_reason: stableMenuActions (App.tsx:3333-3336) calls the action with no try/catch, and there is no window error or unhandledrejection handler in src. Neither recordedCall (app.ts:877-893) nor rec (501-509) catches. exportPNG/JPEG (4633, 4673), exportWebP (5066), exportSizes (4904-4912, with no exportScaleFits check), exportLayersToFiles (6085), exportLayerCompsToFiles (6113) and the others call engine encoders that return Err, which surfaces in JS as a throw. ExportPrefs.commit (Dialogs.tsx:4146-4154) runs exportAs before close(), so a throw leaves the dialog open with no message. That dialog does pre-block oversized rows, but menu-driven exportSizes does not.

findings.title: File ▸ Import ▸ 3D LUT drops the active selection and converts colour twice on non-sRGB documents
findings.feature: File ▸ Import ▸ 3D LUT (.cube/.3dl)
findings.evidence: bakeColorLut (app.ts:5828-5843) decodes the composite with a colour-managed (loadImg), which converts P3/Adobe RGB to sRGB, applies the LUT, and stamps the sRGB result back into document space. Save for Web avoids this same #33 double-conversion by decoding unmanaged. It also calls E().select_none() (5838) to clear the user's selection and never restores it. 16-bit documents get an 8-bit baked layer.
findings.repro: Take a Display P3 document with an active selection and choose File ▸ Import ▸ 3D LUT… with an identity .cube. The new layer is visibly desaturated compared with the original, and the selection is gone.
findings.impact: An identity LUT changes the image's colours, and the user's selection is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Decode with pngToImageData(png, false). Save the selection mask and restore it (removeStroke does exactly this at app.ts:2031-2047), or mask the stamped layer to the selection.
findings.verdict_reason: bakeColorLut (app.ts:5828-5843) decodes E().export_png(), which embeds the built-in P3 or Adobe RGB iCCP, through loadImg and drawImage. That decode is colour-managed, and pngToImageData's own #33 comment (5368-5375) says so. The sRGB-converted numbers are then stamped back into document space with no reverse conversion. Line 5838 calls E().select_none() on purpose ('stamp_image clips to any active selection') and never restores the mask. The result is also 8-bit on 16-bit documents.

findings.title: Export commands with nothing to export stay enabled and silently do nothing
findings.feature: Artboards to Files/PDF, Layer Comps to Files/PDF, Data Sets as Files, Revert
findings.evidence: menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3470) disables these only when no document is open. exportArtboardsToFiles loops zero times (app.ts:6053-6066). exportArtboardsToPDF returns early (5740-5742). exportLayerCompsToFiles/PDF iterate an empty list (6113-6125). dataVars.exportAll returns true with no data sets (5485-5492). revertDocument returns when there is no path (8014-8017), and its own comment notes that Photoshop greys the command out.
findings.repro: In a document with no artboards, choose File ▸ Export ▸ Artboards to Files…. Nothing happens and there is no message.
findings.impact: The commands look broken. Photoshop disables them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add enablement flags: artboard count > 0, layerComps.length > 0, dataSets.length > 0, activePath for Revert.
findings.verdict_reason: menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3469) has no flags for artboards, layer comps, data sets or revert. Only the no-document case disables them. exportArtboardsToFiles loops zero times (app.ts:6053-6060). exportArtboardsToPDF returns when count is 0 (5740-5741). renderLayerCompPngs iterates an empty list. dataVars.exportAll loops over an empty sets list and returns true (5494-5502). revertDocument returns early when there is no path (8014-8015), and its own comment notes that Photoshop greys the command out.

findings.title: Most file operations are not recorded in actions
findings.feature: Actions recording of Place, Export TIFF/WebP/GIF/PDF/…, Save for Web, Revert, Open
findings.evidence: Only exportPNG, exportJPEG, exportPSD, exportPSB, exportAs and saveDocument/As/Copy are wrapped with recordedCall (app.ts:4633-4798, 8050-8151). placeEmbeddedFromBytes/placeLinkedFromBytes (7491-7516), exportTIFF (5055), exportWebP, exportGIF, exportPDF, saveForWeb, revertDocument and routeOpen are not wrapped. Photoshop records Place, Save for Web, Revert and Open as action steps.
findings.repro: Start recording in the Actions panel, choose File ▸ Place Embedded… and then File ▸ Export ▸ Export TIFF…, and stop. The action has no steps for either command.
findings.impact: Common batch recipes (watermark via Place, export TIFF) cannot be recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the place, export, revert and save-for-web entry points in recordedCall, as the PNG/JPEG exports already are.
findings.verdict_reason: The only recordedCall-wrapped file operations are exportPNG, exportJPEG, exportPSD, exportPSB, exportAs, saveDocument, saveDocumentAs and saveDocumentAsCopy (app.ts:4633, 4673, 4756, 4787, 4798, 8050, 8149, 8151). visionOps registers only those same file operations (2319-2327). placeEmbeddedFromBytes and placeLinkedFromBytes (7491-7516), exportTIFF (5055), exportWebP (5066), revertDocument (8014) and the Save for Web/PDF/GIF paths are plain functions that call the engine directly, with no rec(). Insert Menu Item (759) exists, but that is a manual insertion, not automatic recording.

areas.coverage:
Read-only code review; I ran no builds or tests. Everything below comes from reading the code.

What I covered, with counts:
- **MCP (all 90 tools).** I read every tool in src/mcp/commands.ts and checked the list against mcp.manifest.json and mcp.generated.ts. I also read the index.ts wrapper that blocks tools while a history transaction is open. I read the whole Rust host (packages/monet-ui/crates/monet-mcp/src/lib.rs): 127.0.0.1 binding, bearer/query token, body limits, CORS, the 60 s bridge timeout and the mcp.json write. I read the TS bridge and protocol (bridge.ts, protocol.ts), the handlers.test/commands.test mocks, and the Vision main.rs wiring (MCP is off for CLI jobs; the fallback port range is 6).
- **Actions engine (app.ts:430-1000).** I traced about 35 actions.* methods, the rec/withOpCapture/recordedCall recorder, 120+ recordable store ops, the 6 proxied namespaces and the visionOps allowlist.
- **Actions panel.** About 22 controls: Rec, Play, Tool, Playback options, Load, Save, .atn, Export, Import, per-action play/delete/favorite/set, Insert Stop / Menu Item / Conditional, and per-step enable/modal/play-from/move/delete.
- **ATN.** Reader and writer in actionSets.ts: 13 mapped events, bounds checks and the round trip.
