- **File ▸ Automate (11 items).** Batch, Create Droplet (.json and .app, including droplet.rs), Crop and Straighten, Contact Sheet, Conditional Mode Change, Fit Image, Lens Correction (only the entry point), Merge to HDR Pro, Photomerge, Picture Package, PDF Presentation.
- **File ▸ Scripts (11 items).** Scripting Console, Image Processor, the 4 cleanup scripts, Script Events Manager, Load Files into Stack, Load DICOM, Statistics, Browse.
- **Variables (5 entries).** Define, Data Sets, Apply, Import, Export as Files.
- **Command line.** All 3 job kinds (--run-script, --play-action with --batch, droplet), both the main.rs parser and the webview side.
- **Script sandbox.** I read scriptWorker.ts and runScript in full. I found no escape: constructors are removed, fetch/XHR/WebSocket/Worker/importScripts/eval/Function/postMessage are masked, `import` is refused, and op and read paths are re-checked on the main thread.
- **Menu wiring.** I checked enablement and dispatch in App.tsx and psMenus.ts.
- **Tests.** I grepped the unit and e2e tests for each area: batch, droplet, script sandbox, scripting-actions, command-line, actionInserts, actionRecording, handlers.test.

Not reviewed:
- Runtime behaviour in the Tauri WKWebView: native dialogs, the ACL at runtime, downloads. The ACL and hang findings come from reading the Tauri 2.11.2 source, the wry 0.55.1 source and the generated acl-manifests.json. They are not observed; each finding says how to confirm it.
- The ML job tools and the Camera Raw / lens MCP tools only as far as their wrappers.
- Photoshop-side loading of exported .atn files.
- The internals of the Contact Sheet / Picture Package / PDF Presentation renderers.
areas.parity_notes:
In this area there are no disabled placeholders: every File ▸ Automate item (11), every File ▸ Scripts item (11) and every Variables item (5) is wired. Create Droplet…, Script Events Manager…, Load Multiple DICOM Files… and Photomerge… are wired by label in psMenus.ts LABEL_WIRING. Several of them run a Vision-specific form rather than Photoshop's:
- Photomerge, Merge to HDR Pro and Statistics work on the current document's layers instead of picking files.
- Merge to HDR Pro has no dialog (EVs are estimated).
- Contact Sheet tiles the open documents' thumbnails.
- Fit Image has no 'Don't Enlarge' option.

Photoshop Actions-panel features that are absent (not bugs):
- New Set / New Action naming dialog. The missing rename is reported above as a finding.
- Duplicate action, Record Again, Insert Path, Button Mode, function-key assignment.
- Clear, Reset and Replace Actions, and the 'Pause For N seconds' playback option (intentionally omitted).
- Insert steps are append-only, reordered with the ↑/↓ buttons.
- Conditionals branch by action name.
- Tool recording covers brush, eraser, lasso and marquee only.

MCP (90 tools) has no tools for:
- Insert Stop / Menu Item / Conditional, sets, favorites, playback options, Allow Tool Recording, or .mvactions/.atn export (only import).
- Script Events Manager, Variables/Data Sets, Image Processor, Fit Image, Conditional Mode Change, Load Files into Stack, Contact Sheet.
- Undo/redo, history, selections, layer listing/selection, document switching and closing.

The script API reaches most of the recordable command surface, but it cannot open files, save to a path, or undo. Menu, MCP and script use the same action layer, except that the MCP numeric scaling is inconsistent (finding above).

findings.title: Plugin commands for atomicsave, heic, models and c2pa are refused by Tauri's permission system (no capability grants them)
findings.feature: Native plugins used by Save/Batch/MCP writes (atomicsave), File ▸ Open/Export HEIC, Model Manager, Content Credentials
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json:6-40 grants only core/dialog/drag/droplet/fs/float permissions. apps/vision/src-tauri/build.rs declares only the droplet and float inline plugins. src-tauri/gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json has manifests only for core*, dialog, drag, droplet, float and fs. tauri-2.11.2 src/webview/mod.rs:1823-1850 rejects any 'plugin:' command that has no resolved permission ('Command … not allowed by ACL'). The team hit this before: src/native/tauriConfig.test.ts:26 records that Save Droplet App failed 'not allowed by ACL' until droplet:default was added (#469). Affected callers: packages/monet-ui/packages/monet-react/src/atomic-write.ts:53 (plugin:atomicsave|atomic_write; on rejection it silently falls back to a write+rename with no fsync and logs one console warning); apps/vision/src/state/app.ts:7146 and 5149 (plugin:heic|decode_heic / encode_heic); app.ts:4977-5050 and state/contentCredentials.ts:116 (plugin:c2pa|…); src/ml/modelSource.ts:57 and src/ml/modelDownload.ts:77-136 (plugin:models|…).
findings.repro: Desktop build: open an iPhone .heic file, or run Model Manager ▸ download/import, or export signed Content Credentials. The call is rejected with 'not allowed by ACL'. On every Batch output, MCP doc.saveAs or document save, the webview console shows '[monet] durable save unavailable' once and the write is not fsynced.
findings.impact: HEIC open/export, C2PA signing/reading and model provisioning fail in the shipped app. The 'durable save' guarantee in AGENTS.md does not hold for any write, including every Batch, droplet and MCP output. Automated tests cannot catch this: e2e runs in Chromium and test:native does not drive IPC. This is outside my assigned area, but Batch and MCP writes depend on it.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare atomicsave, heic, models and c2pa as tauri_build InlinedPlugins with a default permission (or ship permission files with monet-ui), and add 'atomicsave:default', 'heic:default', 'models:default', 'c2pa:default' to default.json. Add a tauriConfig test that every invoke("plugin:x|y") in src/ has a matching capability grant.
findings.verdict_reason: Traced end to end. The shipped lockfile pins tauri 2.11.2. In webview/mod.rs:1818-1850 every 'plugin:' command is rejected when resolve_access returns None, and authority.rs:439-471 returns None for any command missing from allowed_commands. build.rs declares only the droplet and float inlined plugins, and monet-ui's build.rs is plain std with no tauri-build manifest. The generated acl-manifests.json lists only core, dialog, drag, droplet, float and fs, and default.json grants nothing for atomicsave, heic, models or c2pa. main.rs:340-345 does register those plugins, and the webview calls them at app.ts:4977/5012/5040/5050 (c2pa), 5149/7146 (heic), contentCredentials.ts:116, modelDownload.ts:77-153, modelSource.ts:57 and monet-react atomic-write.ts:53. Galerie's capability, by contrast, grants its own inline plugins (catalog:default, raw-decode:default and others), so the omission is specific to Vision. Result: HEIC open and export, C2PA and model provisioning are refused in both dev and release builds, and every atomicWriteBytes quietly takes the plugin-fs write+rename path with no fsync after a single console.warn. tauriConfig.test.ts:26-27 checks only droplet.

findings.title: Four MCP adjustment/filter tools send UI-scale numbers to actions that expect 0..1 fractions
findings.feature: MCP adj.threshold / adj.brightnessContrast / adj.vibrance / fil.unsharp (+ fil.sharpen's range)
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/mcp/commands.ts:785-790 advertises level (0..255) and calls adj.threshold(level) unchanged. :613-619 brightness (-150..150) and contrast (-100..100) go straight to adj.brightnessContrast. :702-708 vibrance/saturation (-100..100) are passed raw. :827-835 unsharp amount (1..500) and threshold (0..255) are passed raw. :817-822 sharpen advertises 0..500, but the engine treats it as a multiplier. The dialogs normalise the same values: state/threshold.ts:41-42 (/255), state/brightnessContrast.ts:38-39 (/100), state/vibrance.ts:86-87 (/100), ui/Dialogs.tsx:3189 fil.unsharp(r, a/100, t/255); App.tsx:3128-3130 uses sharpen(1) and sharpen(3). The engine confirms the fraction domain: packages/engine/src/raster/adjust.rs:46-47 ('brightness/contrast in -1..1') and adjust.rs:522-526 (threshold compares 0..1 luminance). actionSets.ts:630-647 documents the same bug already fixed for .atn import (#138-#140). The tests pin the wrong behaviour: src/mcp/handlers.test.ts:196-220 and 287-301 assert raw pass-through.
findings.repro: MCP tools/call adj.threshold {level:128} turns the whole layer black. adj.brightnessContrast {brightness:20, contrast:10} blows out to white at about 11× contrast. adj.vibrance {vibrance:30, saturation:0} fully saturates. fil.unsharp {radius:1, amount:100, threshold:5} sharpens at 100× and ignores the threshold.
findings.impact: An agent's common calls destroy the image, and actions recorded through MCP replay the same wrong values. Any value an agent reads from the dialogs or the Photoshop docs gives a wrong result.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise in commands.ts with the same helpers the dialogs use (brightnessContrastArgs, vibranceArgs, thresholdFraction, a/100, t/255). Describe fil.sharpen's amount as a multiplier with a sensible range. Replace the pass-through tests with a test that MCP and dialog calls with the same UI values produce the same engine arguments.
findings.verdict_reason: commands.ts:616-618, 706-708, 788-790 and 832-834 pass raw values to adj.brightnessContrast, adj.vibrance, adj.threshold and fil.unsharp. app.ts:1008/1018/1027/1194 forward those values to the engine unchanged. The dialogs normalise first (Dialogs.tsx:708 brightnessContrastArgs /100, :1172 vibranceArgs /100, :3132 thresholdFraction /255, :3189 a/100 and t/255). The engine works in fractions: adjust.rs:46 contrast is 1+c, :432 vibrance adds vib*(1-s)+sat, and :522-526 threshold does 'l >= level' on 0..1 luminance, so level 128 turns everything black. The same MCP file does normalise hueSaturation and blackWhite, so these four are inconsistent within it. The .atn importer fixed exactly this bug (actionSets.ts:617-647, #138-#140), and handlers.test.ts:210/219/301 pins the raw pass-through.

findings.title: Recorded action steps store absolute layer ids, so playback hits the wrong layer or does nothing
findings.feature: Actions record/play, Batch, droplets, --play-action
findings.evidence: state/app.ts:877-894 (recordedCall) stores [path, args] verbatim. The recorded store ops take a layer id first: store.ts:6494 deleteLayer(id), 6498 duplicateLayer(id), 6674 selectLayer(id), 7702 setLayerOpacity(id,…), 7706 setLayerBlend(id,…), 7843 mergeDown(id), 8178 addLayerMask(id), 8480 setEffect(id,…). Callers pass the active id (ui/Panels.tsx:587, 612). Engine ids are per-document counters starting at 1 (packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:3501, 3661-3662). An unknown id is a silent no-op (mod.rs:10727-10728 set_layer_opacity, 10440-10441 merge_down). No test replays a recorded layer op against a different layer or document (actionRecording.test.ts only checks the recorded surface and serialization).
findings.repro: Record: with layer A active, Duplicate Layer, set Blend Mode to Screen, set Opacity to 50%. Stop and Save. Make layer B active and press Play: layer A is duplicated again and A's earlier copy is restyled; B is untouched. Or Batch the action over a folder of layered PSDs, or files opened after other layers were created: steps silently no-op or edit whichever layer has that id.
findings.impact: The core Photoshop pattern of recording on one layer and playing on another, or batching over other files, gives wrong results with no error.
findings.suggested_fix: Record layer-targeted commands against the active layer: variants without an id, or a sentinel resolved at play time. Record Select Layer by name or relative position, as Photoshop does. Add an e2e test that plays a recorded Duplicate/Opacity action on a second layer and on a second document.
findings.verdict_reason: recordedCall (app.ts:877-894) stores [path, args] verbatim. Its in-session thunk also closes over the original args. deleteLayer, duplicateLayer, selectLayer, setLayerOpacity, setLayerBlend, mergeDown, addLayerMask and setEffect all take the layer id as their first argument (store.ts:6494-6500, 7702-7708, 7843). The Layers panel passes the active id (Panels.tsx:584/587/612). decodeOpArgs (actionSets.ts:369) only rebuilds typed arrays, and nothing remaps ids at play time. The engine's merge_down, set_layer_opacity and duplicate_layer all begin with 'if let Some(i) = self.layer_index(id)', so an unknown id is a silent no-op, and ids restart at next_id 1 for each document (mod.rs:3501).

findings.title: Command-line and headless runs hang on modal steps and continuable Stops, because desktop prompts bypass runUnattended
findings.feature: monet-vision --play-action … --batch / droplet CLI jobs (and Script Events inside them)
findings.evidence: state/app.ts:578-586: confirmPlaybackPause calls @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog ask() first whenever isTauri(). runUnattended (app.ts:6578-6586) only swaps globalThis.alert/confirm, so ask() is not intercepted. runActionSteps awaits the prompt for Stop-with-Continue (app.ts:610), per-step modal toggles (623-624) and Step By Step (602-603). A CLI job runs in a hidden window as an Accessory app (src-tauri/src/main.rs:386, 399 .visible(job.is_none())). The dialog command parents the prompt to that invisible window (tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1 commands.rs message → builder.parent(&window).blocking_show_with_result()). No job timeout exists. Save and Close takes the same path: saveDocument → native save() picker (app.ts:8095-8100) and closeDocumentTab → confirmDiscard ask() (app.ts:8395-8401). The e2e test command-line.spec.ts:155-197 runs in Chromium (isTauri false), so the desktop branch is untested.
findings.repro: Save an action with a step's modal toggle on, or import an .atn containing a Stop with Continue. Run `monet-vision --play-action "Default Actions/Action 1" --batch ~/in`. The process never exits, and nothing visible asks for input.
findings.impact: Scheduled or scripted batch jobs hang forever instead of taking the 'every confirm answers OK' behaviour that runUnattended's comment promises.
findings.suggested_fix: Have runUnattended set a module flag that confirmPlaybackPause, confirmDiscard and the save-picker fallback check before calling ask() or save(): answer OK, or fail the job. Add a native-path unit test that stubs isTauri() to true.
findings.verdict_reason: runUnattended (app.ts:6578-6586) swaps only globalThis.alert and confirm. confirmPlaybackPause (app.ts:578-585) goes straight to @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog confirm whenever isTauri() is true. runCliJob (6620-6636) does not override the playback mode or modal steps. main.rs:385-399 makes a CLI job an Accessory app with an invisible window. plugin-dialog 2.7.1 commands.rs:280-289 parents the prompt to that window and calls blocking_show_with_result, which in rfd 0.16 macOS (message_dialog.rs:88-101) is beginSheetModalForWindow on the hidden window followed by runModal. The job therefore blocks on a prompt that nobody can see, or at best on one that is not expected, and no job timeout exists. The Save and Close sub-claim is weaker: folder inputs have paths, so saveDocument does not open a picker. The Stop/modal/Step By Step path alone is enough to confirm the finding. Whether the sheet is invisible was not observed at runtime.

findings.title: MCP action.saveDroplet can delete any .app bundle and overwrite any file without confirmation
findings.feature: MCP action.saveDroplet (and the overwrite policy of doc.saveAs / doc.exportAs)
findings.evidence: src/mcp/commands.ts:388-392 → state/app.ts:6505-6509 saveDropletFile. A path ending in .app goes to src-tauri/src/droplet.rs:92-128 build_app → replace(), which RENAME_SWAPs with whatever already exists at dest (droplet.rs:148-163). build_app's cleanup then remove_dir_all's the old bundle (droplet.rs:127). Nothing checks that the existing target is a droplet. Any other path goes to atomicWriteBytes(path, json) with any extension. In the GUI the save panel's replace confirmation guards this path; MCP has no guard. The protocol exposes no destructive-tool annotations (packages/monet-ui/packages/monet-mcp/src/protocol.ts:211-212 returns only name, description and schema).
findings.repro: tools/call action.saveDroplet {path:"/Applications/Monet Vision.app", actionId:1} replaces Vision's own bundle with an AppleScript applet and deletes the original. tools/call action.saveDroplet {path:"/Users/me/Documents/report.docx", actionId:1} overwrites the document with droplet JSON.
findings.impact: An LLM agent driving MCP, possibly under prompt injection, can destroy user apps or documents in one call without any prompt.
findings.suggested_fix: In the MCP wrapper, require a .json or .app extension. Refuse to replace an existing target unless it is itself a droplet (for example, Contents/Resources/droplet.json exists) or the caller passes an explicit overwrite:true. Apply the same no-overwrite default to doc.saveAs and doc.exportAs, and emit MCP tool annotations (destructiveHint) for write tools.
findings.verdict_reason: The code path holds. commands.ts:388-392 calls saveDropletFile (app.ts:6505-6509), which sends .app paths to build_app → replace(), a RENAME_SWAP with no check that the old bundle is a droplet, and staging cleanup then remove_dir_all's the old bundle (droplet.rs:118-163). Every other extension goes to atomicWriteBytes with no extension check, whereas doc.saveAs and doc.exportAs are limited to image or project extensions (commands.ts:296-327). Downgraded to minor: the endpoint needs the bearer token and serves the user's own agent, which can already overwrite any image-extension file silently through doc.saveAs. The '/Applications/Monet Vision.app' repro is also likely blocked by macOS App Management protection for signed bundles; I did not verify this. What this tool genuinely adds is overwriting arbitrary non-image files, such as .docx, with droplet JSON.

findings.title: Actions ▸ ＋ Stop does nothing in the desktop app (it relies on window.prompt)
findings.feature: Actions panel ▸ Insert Stop
findings.evidence: ui/Panels.tsx:2557-2561 calls prompt("Stop message…") and returns when the result is null. wry 0.55.1's WKWebView UI delegate implements only the file-open panel and the media permission handler (wry_web_view_ui_delegate.rs:99-141), so prompt() returns null. The team documented this for another control: ui/panelInventory.test.ts:281-283 (#480). The follow-up confirm() is also broken in Tauri: plugin-dialog's init script makes window.confirm async (it returns a Promise, which is always truthy). The same root cause, outside my area, breaks Window ▸ Workspace ▸ New Workspace… and Delete Workspace… (App.tsx:2664-2687) and History ▸ New Snapshot naming (Panels.tsx:2647).
findings.repro: Desktop app: expand an action and click ＋ Stop. Nothing happens and no step is added.
findings.impact: An enabled, advertised action-authoring command is a no-op on the shipped platform. Stops can only arrive through .atn/.mvactions import.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace prompt/confirm with a Monet Dialog (message field plus an 'Allow Continue' checkbox). Fix the workspace and snapshot prompts the same way, and add a unit test asserting no prompt( remains in src/ui or App.tsx.
findings.verdict_reason: Panels.tsx:2557-2562 calls prompt() and returns on null. wry 0.55.1's WKUIDelegate (wry_web_view_ui_delegate.rs) implements only windowWillClose, runOpenPanel and media-capture permission, with no runJavaScriptTextInputPanel. tauri-plugin-dialog's init script (guest-js/init.ts) overrides only alert and confirm, not prompt, so prompt() returns null in WKWebView and the handler exits without adding a step. panelInventory.test.ts:281-285 records the same fact for the Channels flyout (#480). In the plugin, window.confirm is async and returns a truthy Promise, so allowContinue would always be true even if prompt worked.

findings.title: Insert Menu Item inserts commands that need arguments with no arguments, so playback no-ops, errors or blackens the layer
findings.feature: Actions panel ▸ Insert Menu Item
findings.evidence: ui/Panels.tsx:2572-2576 calls actions.insertMenuItem(a.id, path) with no arguments; state/app.ts:759-763 defaults args to []. The picker lists every visionOps path (app.ts:766), and most need arguments. opRunner (app.ts:512-514) calls fn() with nothing. Engine results: filter_gaussian_blur(NaN) is refused with an error (mod.rs:23477-23480); duplicate_layer(0) and set_layer_opacity(0, …) silently no-op (mod.rs:9371-9372, 10727-10728); adjust_brightness_contrast(NaN, NaN) has no finite check (mod.rs:22801-22805), so NaN pixels are written back as 0 (adjust.rs:40-42) and the layer turns black. actionInserts.test.ts:31-37 only checks that every path is accepted.
findings.repro: Insert Menu Item 'adj.brightnessContrast' or 'fil.gaussian' into an action and play it. Brightness/Contrast turns the active layer black; Gaussian Blur shows an 'invalid parameters' error; 'store.duplicateLayer' does nothing.
findings.impact: The feature works only for commands that take no arguments, yet the picker offers every command. Photoshop instead opens the command's dialog at playback.
findings.suggested_fix: Limit the picker to commands that take no arguments, or insert a modal step that opens the command's dialog at playback and captures its arguments at insert time.
findings.verdict_reason: Panels.tsx:2574-2576 calls actions.insertMenuItem(a.id, path) with no args. app.ts:759-763 defaults args to [] and opRunner (512-514) calls fn() with nothing. The picker lists every visionOps path (menuItemPaths, app.ts:766), and store ops take a layer id first. adjust_brightness_contrast (mod.rs:22801-22805) has no finite check, and a NaN value propagates through clamp and lerp and then to16, so the layer turns black. duplicate_layer and merge_down(0) find no layer and return. actionInserts.test.ts:31-37 only checks that every path is accepted.

findings.title: Conditional Mode Change records an unconditional mode change, and Fit Image records fixed pixel dimensions
findings.feature: File ▸ Automate ▸ Conditional Mode Change / Fit Image inside actions and Batch
findings.evidence: store.ts:8054-8058: conditionalModeChange is not in RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:904-952). It calls this.convertGrayscale() / this.setColorMode(), which are wrapped instance methods (app.ts:971-974), so the recording is a plain setColorMode/convertGrayscale step with the condition lost. When the recording document does not match, nothing is recorded at all. Fit Image (ui/Dialogs.tsx:6779-6786) computes width and height from the current document and calls xform.resizeImage(w, h); withOpCapture records those fixed numbers (app.ts:462-486).
findings.repro: (1) While recording, run Conditional Mode Change (source RGB, target Grayscale) on an RGB file, then Batch the action over a folder containing CMYK and Lab files: every file is converted. (2) Record Fit Image 1920×1920 on a 4000×3000 landscape, then Batch over portrait images: each becomes 1920×1440, distorted.
findings.impact: Both commands exist mainly to be recorded for Batch, and that is exactly the case that gives wrong output.
findings.suggested_fix: Add recordable ops such as store.conditionalModeChange(sources, target) and fitImage(maxW, maxH) that evaluate at play time, and call them from the dialogs.
findings.verdict_reason: conditionalModeChange (store.ts:8054-8058) is not in RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:904-952). It calls this.convertGrayscale() and this.setColorMode(), which the loop at app.ts:971-974 replaces with recordedCall wrappers on the store instance. The recording therefore holds an unconditional convertGrayscale or setColorMode step, and when the source mode does not match it holds nothing. Its only caller is Dialogs.tsx:5160. FitImage (Dialogs.tsx:6779-6786) computes w and h from the current document and calls xform.resizeImage, and withOpCapture (app.ts:462-486) records those literal numbers.

findings.title: Actions cannot be named or renamed in the UI; every saved action is 'Action N'
findings.feature: Actions panel (New Action / rename)
findings.evidence: ui/Panels.tsx:2485: Save calls actions.save() with no name, so app.ts:660-662 uses defaultActionName. The action row (Panels.tsx:2527-2545) has no rename control, and actions.rename is reachable only from MCP (mcp/commands.ts:460-465). The name is the durable handle for droplets and Script Events (app.ts:688-706 resolve), Insert Conditional branches (app.ts:615-619) and CLI --play-action "Set/Name" (actionSets.ts:53-57, Dialogs.tsx:10423).
findings.repro: Record, then Save: the action is 'Action 1'. No double-click or menu entry renames it. Copy as Command Line yields --play-action 'Default Actions/Action 1'.
findings.impact: Conditionals, droplets and CLI jobs have to name meaningless, order-dependent labels; editing the list later makes them easy to confuse.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask for a name in a Monet dialog on Save (Photoshop's New Action…), add in-place rename, and de-duplicate names.
findings.verdict_reason: The facts check out. The only UI Save is Panels.tsx:2485 actions.save() with no name, the action row has no rename control, and actions.rename/save(name) are reachable only from MCP (commands.ts:449, 460-463); a grep found no other caller. Downgraded to minor: this is a missing capability, not a broken feature. Nothing gives a wrong result, conditionals and droplets still work with the default names, and naming is possible through MCP or by editing the exported .mvactions.

findings.title: Photoshop Merge Down ('Mrg2') from an .atn import replays as a silent no-op
findings.feature: Actions ▸ .atn import / export round trip
findings.evidence: state/actionSets.ts:637 maps "Mrg2" to store.mergeDown with no arguments. store.ts:7843-7845 mergeDown(id) calls engine merge_down(undefined), which becomes 0 across wasm, and packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:10440-10441 finds no layer 0 and returns silently. A Vision-recorded mergeDown(id) exports as Mrg2 (ATN_WRITERS, actionSets.ts:729-736) and re-imports broken.
findings.repro: Load a Photoshop .atn containing Merge Down, or export a Vision action with Merge Down to .atn and re-import it. Playing it leaves the layers unmerged, with no message.
findings.impact: Imported actions silently skip one of the most common Photoshop steps.
findings.suggested_fix: Map Mrg2 to an operation that resolves store.state.activeLayerId at play time, and add an ATN import-then-play test.
findings.verdict_reason: actionSets.ts:637 maps Mrg2 to store.mergeDown with no args function, so atnStep produces []. store.mergeDown(id) (store.ts:7843-7845) calls merge_down(undefined), which wasm coerces to 0, and mod.rs:10440-10441 finds no layer with id 0 because ids start at 1, so nothing happens. ATN_WRITERS (actionSets.ts:729-736) writes a Vision mergeDown(id) back out as a parameterless Mrg2, so the round trip loses it the same way.

findings.title: Image Processor never closes the documents it opens, overwrites same-named files, and reports nothing
findings.feature: File ▸ Scripts ▸ Image Processor…
findings.evidence: state/app.ts:6237 opens each file as a new tab through openAutomationInput and never closes it. Batch does close its inputs (app.ts:6361, #469). app.ts:6252 writes `${base}.${ext}` straight into destDir, overwriting any existing file, including the source when the destination is the source folder; Photoshop writes into JPEG/PSD/TIFF subfolders. ui/Dialogs.tsx:5089-5098 runs `void imageProcessor(...)` and closes the dialog, so the result, progress and cancel are ignored. Write failures are reported as open errors (app.ts:6256 reportOpen). No test runs imageProcessor (imageProcessorIo.test.ts:93 only inspects source text).
findings.repro: Run Image Processor on 200 photos: 200 documents stay open, the wasm heap grows until opens fail, and the app is sluggish. Choose the photos' own folder as the destination with JPEG output: the originals are replaced by resized copies.
findings.impact: Memory exhaustion on real-size runs and silent loss of the source images.
findings.suggested_fix: Close each input after its saves, as runBatchInputs does. Write into per-format subfolders or refuse to overwrite, and show progress, cancel and a summary like the Batch dialog.
findings.verdict_reason: imageProcessor (app.ts:6224-6258) opens each file through openAutomationInput and never calls closeDocumentTab. runBatchInputs does close its inputs (app.ts:6358). writeBatchOutput (6384-6388) writes straight to `${destDir}/${base}.ext` through atomicWriteBytes, with no subfolders and no existence check. The dialog (Dialogs.tsx:5089-5098) runs `void imageProcessor(...)` and closes, ignoring the returned count, and write failures go to reportOpen. Overwriting originals needs the user to choose the source folder and the same format, which is plausible because the browser-file picker does not expose the source path. The memory exhaustion is inferred from engine size, not observed.

findings.title: --run-script cannot reliably write output: script save/export ops are fire-and-forget and the process exits immediately
findings.feature: monet-vision --run-script (Scripting Console ▸ Copy as Command Line)
findings.evidence: visionOps saveDocument/saveDocumentAs are `void saveDocument()` (state/app.ts:2321-2322). exportPNG/JPEG/… go through saveBytes → downloadBytes, an anchor-click download that finishes asynchronously (app.ts:3605-3627). runScript resolves right after the synchronous replay (app.ts:2440-2446), and runCliScript reports done (app.ts:6588-6593). main.rs:371-382 then calls handle.exit on CLI_DONE. The script API has no open or path-taking save. For a new document, saveDocument falls back to a native Save panel on the hidden window.
findings.repro: Put `vision.newDoc(800,600); vision.fill(255,0,0); vision.exportPNG("out.png");` in s.js and run `monet-vision --run-script s.js`. It exits 0, but out.png may never appear in Downloads, and saveDocument never saves. To confirm, run it in a packaged build and check ~/Downloads.
findings.impact: A headless script job reports success but may leave no output, so the advertised command-line scripting mode is effectively unusable.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the ops async: have the worker await an op 'thenable' or add a flush, and have runScript await the promises that save/export return. Add a path-taking export op for CLI jobs, restricted to the job's working folder.
findings.verdict_reason: visionOps saveDocument and saveDocumentAs are `void saveDocument()` (app.ts:2321-2322). runScript resolves as soon as the synchronous replay ends (2436-2441), runCliScript reports done, and main.rs:372-382 calls handle.exit on CLI_DONE. exportPNG (app.ts:4633-4636) goes through saveBytes → downloadBytes, an anchor with download=, and the problem is worse than the finding says. Neither Vision nor monet-ui registers on_download (grep found nothing), so tauri-runtime-wry never installs a download handler, and wry 0.55.1 navigation.rs:68-74 cancels any navigation with shouldPerformDownload when no handler exists. The export therefore never writes anything in the desktop app, rather than racing the exit. The script API has no path-taking save, so a CLI script has no working output channel.

findings.title: Batch, droplets and the CLI count refused steps and halting Stops as successful files; MCP action.play always says 'Played'
findings.feature: Batch / droplet / --play-action result and Stop For Errors; MCP action.play
findings.evidence: runBatchInputs (state/app.ts:6350-6366) awaits playNamed and then writes the output and counts it processed. Engine refusals on locked, text, smart or group layers only reach onEditError as a toast (engine/EngineClient.ts:823-824). mcp/commands.ts:580-589 admits the adj/fil/xform wrappers drop the refusal. A Stop without Continue just breaks out of the loop (app.ts:609), and playNamed still returns true (app.ts:710-722). runUnattended collects alerts only (app.ts:6578-6583), so the CLI exits 0 for refused steps. MCP playAction (commands.ts:356-360) ignores the outcome and can block on a modal ask() until the 60 s bridge timeout (monet-mcp lib.rs:56).
findings.repro: Batch an Invert action over files whose only layer is a text layer: every file is written unchanged and the batch reports processed = N with Stop For Errors ignored. In the GUI, a Stop (no Continue) in the action still writes the partial result.
findings.impact: Unattended runs report success while producing unedited or partial outputs.
findings.suggested_fix: Have playNamed return {halted, refused} by watching engine.onEditError and undo_pushes, as MCP's applied() does. Turn a refusal into a BatchError that honours Stop For Errors, treat a halting Stop as cancelling the batch, and surface the same status from action.play.
findings.verdict_reason: A Stop without Continue does alert-then-break (app.ts:609), and playNamed still returns true (710-722). runBatchInputs (6350-6366) then writes the output and increments processed. Engine refusals only reach App.tsx:2086-2097's onEditError toast, which is not an alert, so runUnattended does not collect them and the CLI exits 0. The CLI does exit 1 for a halting Stop, because that alert is collected. commands.ts:356-360 playAction ignores the outcome, while commands.ts:580-605 applies the refusal detection only to its direct adj/fil/xform wrappers.

findings.title: Automate/Scripts file-based commands are disabled when no document is open
findings.feature: File ▸ Automate ▸ Batch / Create Droplet; File ▸ Scripts ▸ Scripting Console, Image Processor, Script Events Manager, Load Files into Stack, Load Multiple DICOM Files, Browse…
findings.evidence: App.tsx:77 NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS covers only new/openf/clearrecent/browse/search/colorsettings/pref*/exportprefs/customizetoolbar. App.tsx:3440-3442 disables every other command on Home, and App.tsx:3335 blocks dispatch. The handlers (App.tsx:2579-2580, 2690, 2979-2984) pick files or create documents and do not need an open one. Photoshop enables all of them with no document.
findings.repro: Start Vision, stay on Home, open File ▸ Automate: Batch… and Create Droplet… are greyed out, as are Scripts ▸ Image Processor…, Load Files into Stack…, and the other commands listed.
findings.impact: Users must create a throwaway document before running a batch or loading a stack.
findings.suggested_fix: Add batch, createdroplet, imageprocessor, loadfilesstack, loaddicom, scripteventsmanager, script and scriptbrowse to NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS.
findings.verdict_reason: NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS (App.tsx:77) matches only new, openf, clearrecent, browse, search, colorsettings, pref*, exportprefs and customizetoolbar. menuEnablement (3435-3442) disables everything else on Home, and the dispatcher wrapper (3335) refuses them. batch, createdroplet, scripteventsmanager, scriptbrowse, imageprocessor, script, loadfilesstack and loaddicom (App.tsx:2579-2580, 2690, 2979-2984) open dialogs or pickers and do not need a document, but all are greyed out.

findings.title: Duplicate action names are allowed, and name-first resolution can run the wrong action
findings.feature: Actions resolve() for droplets / Script Events / Batch; MCP action.save and action.rename
findings.evidence: state/actionSets.ts:36-40 renameActionMeta does no de-duplication; app.ts:662 save() keeps an explicit name as given. resolve() (app.ts:698-706) matches by name first even when the stored id is still valid, and runBatchInputs uses it (app.ts:6322-6324).
findings.repro: MCP action.save {name:'Web'}, then save or rename a second action to 'Web'. Create a droplet for the second one: dropping files runs the first.
findings.impact: A droplet or Script Event can silently run a different action.
findings.suggested_fix: De-duplicate on save and rename. In resolve(), prefer the stored id when its name still matches, and fall back to the name only when the id is stale.
findings.verdict_reason: renameActionMeta (actionSets.ts:36-40) and save(name) (app.ts:660-662) do not de-duplicate. resolve() (app.ts:698-706) returns the first case-insensitive name match before it even checks a still-valid id, and it ignores the set, so identically named actions from different imported .atn sets collide as well. Droplets carry both actionName and actionId (commands.ts:390) and resolve by name in runBatchInputs (6321-6323). The CLI --play-action path is safe, because it passes the id only.

findings.title: MCP and the script API cannot undo, redo, or list/switch/close documents
findings.feature: MCP surface parity
findings.evidence: None of the 90 manifest tools undoes, reads history or lists/switches/closes documents (src/mcp/mcp.manifest.json). visionOps (state/app.ts:2279-2340) exposes no undo either. Every destructive tool (adj.*, fil.*, xform.*, script.run, action.play) is therefore irreversible for an agent.
findings.repro: After a wrong MCP edit (for example the threshold bug above), no MCP tool can revert it; the user has to press ⌘Z.
findings.impact: Agents cannot recover from their own mistakes or target a specific open document.
findings.suggested_fix: Add edit.undo, edit.redo, history.list, doc.list, doc.activate and doc.close tools that wrap the existing store methods.
findings.verdict_reason: The generated manifest lists 90 tools, and none of them undoes, redoes, reads history or lists/activates/closes documents (checked the full name list). visionOps (app.ts:2279-2340) and the namespaces it flattens (adj, fil, xform, neural, anim, distort, the RECORDED_STORE_OPS store.* and the text.* ops) expose no undo either.

findings.title: MCP server is always on in release builds, with no opt-out or indicator
findings.feature: Local MCP server (127.0.0.1:48211)
findings.evidence: src-tauri/src/main.rs:331-338 registers monet_mcp for every GUI launch, and I found no preference or UI control that mentions MCP. packages/monet-ui/crates/monet-mcp/src/lib.rs:415-432 writes the bearer token to <app config>/mcp.json with default permissions. With that token, script.run, doc.saveAs (any path) and action.saveDroplet are reachable by any same-user process that can read the file.
findings.repro: Launch Vision; any local process that reads ~/Library/Application Support/<id>/mcp.json can drive the app and write files, and the user is never told.
findings.impact: There is no privilege escalation across users, but a write-capable automation endpoint is on by default and invisible to the user.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Preferences toggle (off by default, or with first-run consent) and a visible indicator while a client is connected. Write mcp.json with 0600.
findings.verdict_reason: main.rs:330-338 registers monet_mcp on every GUI launch, and the UI has no MCP preference: a grep of Dialogs and Panels found only comments. monet-mcp lib.rs:415-432 writes mcp.json with std::fs::write, so it gets umask-default permissions. That matters little in practice: ~/Library is per-user 0700, and any same-user process can read the user's files anyway. What remains is a design and consent issue, which is correctly graded minor.

findings.title: The script op budget counts calls, not cost; its timeouts don't cover main-thread replay
findings.feature: Scripting Console / script.run / Script Events / --run-script
findings.evidence: state/app.ts:2410-2418: replay runs up to SCRIPT_MAX_OPS=256 operations synchronously on the main thread (scriptLimits.ts). SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_MS and SCRIPT_MAX_RUNTIME_MS only bound the worker (app.ts:2393-2408). newDoc (app.ts:2281) opens a new document tab on every call.
findings.repro: Run `for (let i=0;i<250;i++) vision.newDoc(30000,30000)` from the console, a Script Events binding or MCP script.run: 250 max-budget documents are created synchronously, freezing the UI and exhausting wasm memory.
findings.impact: A shared or downloaded script, or an agent, can freeze or crash the app despite the advertised op budget and timeouts.
findings.suggested_fix: Also budget new documents, pixel volume or cumulative main-thread time per run, and yield between ops so a cancel can land.
findings.verdict_reason: replay (app.ts:2410-2418) counts only ops, capped at SCRIPT_MAX_OPS=256, and runs them synchronously. The idle and total timers (2393-2408) cannot interrupt it. newDoc goes to store.newDocument → Engine::new, which clamp_dims to 80M pixels (mod.rs:7071-7073, MAX_PIXELS=80_000_000). That is about 640 MB of u16 layer plus 320 MB of output buffer per document, so roughly four or five newDoc calls exhaust wasm32's 4 GB. The op budget offers no protection, which is exactly the finding's point.

findings.title: MCP view.setProof accepts any string as a proof mode
findings.feature: MCP view.setProof
findings.evidence: src/mcp/commands.ts:960-967 forwards mode:string unchecked; store.ts:3605-3617 stores proofMode and sets proofOn=true without validating it.
findings.repro: tools/call view.setProof {mode:'banana'} returns 'Proof mode set to banana' and turns Proof Colors on with an unknown mode.
findings.impact: The agent is told it succeeded while the view is in an undefined proof state.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare mode as a string-literal union so the codegen emits an enum, or validate it against the proof-mode list and throw on unknown values.
findings.verdict_reason: commands.ts:960-967 forwards mode:string unchecked. store.setProof (store.ts:3605-3617) sets proofMode=mode and proofOn=true without validating it. The manifest schema is a plain string with no enum (mcp.manifest.json:1981-1984), and the tool answers 'Proof mode set to banana'.

findings.title: No automated test exercises the automation paths under Tauri (native dialogs, permissions, hidden CLI window)
findings.feature: Actions / Batch / CLI / droplets / MCP on desktop
findings.evidence: apps/vision/AGENTS.md: e2e runs in Chromium with isTauri() false, and test:native does not drive IPC. The only unattended test (e2e/command-line.spec.ts:155-197) runs in the browser branch. The permission grants (tauriConfig.test.ts:21-30) are checked only for dialog, fs, droplet and drag. The native-only branches behind the Insert Stop, CLI hang and permission findings above therefore went unnoticed.
findings.repro: No test reaches the isTauri() branches of confirmPlaybackPause, atomicWriteBytes, the heic/models/c2pa invokes or the Actions panel prompts.
findings.impact: Desktop-only regressions in these features ship undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Add unit tests that stub isTauri() to true (as atomic-write-native.test.ts does), plus a static test mapping every invoke('plugin:x|…') to a capability grant.
findings.verdict_reason: The core gap is real. No test maps each invoke('plugin:x|y') to a capability grant (tauriConfig.test.ts:21-30 checks only dialog, fs and droplet, which is how finding 1 slipped through), and no test runs runUnattended or runCliJob with isTauri() true. The evidence overstates the gap, though. playbackOptions.test.ts:20-34/91 stubs isTauri and plugin-dialog confirm, so the native branch of confirmPlaybackPause is unit-tested. batchRun.test.ts stubs isTauri, and monet-react has atomic-write-native.test.ts. Only the ACL, CLI-under-Tauri and window.prompt paths are untested.

findings.title: Vision's MCP fallback ports overlap the documented ports of the other Monet apps
findings.feature: MCP port assignment
findings.evidence: src-tauri/src/main.rs:333-337 uses port_range(6), which covers 48211-48216. docs/mcp.md assigns 48212-48216 to Artisan, Cinema, Jouer, Rythme and Anime. The code comment only considers Galerie's 48217.
findings.repro: With 48211 busy (for example a second Vision launched with `open -n`), Vision binds 48212. An MCP client configured from the docs for Artisan then reaches Vision and gets 401, and Artisan falls back to Cinema's port.
findings.impact: MCP connections between apps get confused. mcp.json stays correct, but the documented fixed ports do not.
findings.suggested_fix: Use port_range(1) and fall back straight to an ephemeral port (or a range above 48217), and say so in docs/mcp.md.
findings.verdict_reason: main.rs:337 uses port(48211).port_range(6), and bind_server (monet-mcp lib.rs:197) walks consecutive ports, so a busy 48211 makes Vision take 48212-48216. docs/mcp.md:96-104 assigns those ports to artisan, cinema, jouer, rythme and anime. The docs do say 'the host tries the next few', and mcp.json always carries the real URL, so the effect is limited to clients configured from the fixed table.

findings.title: Scripts ▸ Browse… offers .jsx files, but Photoshop ExtendScript cannot run
findings.feature: File ▸ Scripts ▸ Browse…
findings.evidence: state/app.ts:6189 filters for js, jsx and txt. Scripts only get the `vision` API (app.ts:2279-2340), so an ExtendScript .jsx (app.activeDocument…) fails with a ReferenceError.
findings.repro: Browse to a Photoshop .jsx script: it errors with 'app is not defined'.
findings.impact: Photoshop users are misled into thinking ExtendScript is supported.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop jsx from the filter, or detect ExtendScript and show a clear 'Vision runs its own vision.* API' message.
findings.verdict_reason: browseAndRunScript (app.ts:6187-6190, 6203) filters for js, jsx and txt. runScript exposes only the vision.* op and read allowlist (visionOps, app.ts:2279-2340), so an ExtendScript file referencing app.activeDocument fails inside the worker.

findings.title: Deleting an action or re-arming Rec discards work with no confirmation or undo
findings.feature: Actions panel
findings.evidence: ui/Panels.tsx:2543: × calls actions.delete immediately and persists it (app.ts:674-678). Panels.tsx:2465: Rec calls actions.start(), which clears an unsaved recording (app.ts:630).
findings.repro: Click × on an action: it is gone with no prompt or undo. Record steps, forget to Save, press Rec again: the recording is lost.
findings.impact: Easy accidental loss of authored actions.
findings.suggested_fix: Ask for confirmation, as Photoshop's 'Delete the action?' does, or offer an undo toast. Warn before Rec discards an unsaved recording.
findings.verdict_reason: Panels.tsx:2543 × calls actions.delete(a.id) directly, and that filters and persists at once (app.ts:674-678). Rec (Panels.tsx:2465) calls actions.start(), which sets _recorded.length = 0 (app.ts:630) with no check for an unsaved recording. Neither path offers undo.

areas.coverage:
Code review only. I built no builds and ran no test suites. The one exception was a node script on a copy of psMenus.ts and psMenuData.ts in the scratchpad, with App.tsx's registered action ids passed in. It confirmed that Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective renders disabled. No repository files were modified.

Inventory: the Edit menu has 82 leaf items after psMenus wiring. 79 are wired and 3 are disabled: Adobe PDF Presets…, Remote Connections…, and Transform ▸ Perspective (a wiring bug, finding 13).
- In scope, about 52 leaves: Undo, Redo, Toggle Last State, Fade, Cut, Copy, Copy Merged, Paste, Paste in Place, Paste Into, Paste Outside, Clear, Search, Check Spelling (wired through LABEL_WIRING), Find and Replace, Fill, Fill with Foreground, Fill with Background, Stroke, Content-Aware Fill workspace, Content-Aware Scale, Puppet Warp, Perspective Warp, Free Transform, the Transform submenu (12 items plus the injected Perspective Crop), Auto-Align, Auto-Blend, Define Brush/Pattern/Custom Shape, Purge, the Presets submenu (3 doors into Preset Manager), Color Settings, Assign Profile, Convert to Profile, Keyboard Shortcuts, Menus, and Toolbar.
- Also reviewed: the History panel (states, per-state Delete, New Document, snapshots, Set Source, History Options).
- Not reviewed: the 18 Preferences pages and the 10 generative/AI/Patch/Sky items (other areas).

Traced from the menu through App.tsx menuActions and menuEnablement, the dialogs (Dialogs.tsx), state/app.ts and state/store.ts, down to the Rust engine for: undo, redo, history_seek, fade_last, clear_selection, fill_blend_inner, fill_pattern, stroke_selection, capture_clip, copy, copy_merged, cut, paste, paste_in_place, paste_into, purge, transform_layer, skew_layer, flip and rotate layer, perspective_transform, mesh_warp, content_aware_scale and carve_seam, content_aware_fill (plus the workspace variant), auto_align_layers, auto_blend_layers, define_pattern, define_brush_from_selection, and store-level assign and convert profile.

Also checked:
- The native menu's transaction block and the keyboard dispatch guard.
- Macro recording: rec() and RECORDED_STORE_OPS.
- The MCP manifest (97 tools).
- Unit, e2e and engine test references for each feature.

Could not verify:
- Whether WKWebView returns the same PNG bytes from navigator.clipboard on a round trip (this decides which branch of finding 2 users hit).
- Real timings for Content-Aware Scale.
- Photoshop behaviour, which I judged from domain knowledge (pivot and selection semantics, snapshot semantics).
areas.parity_notes:
Photoshop Edit items that are correctly disabled (no monetId): Adobe PDF Presets… and Remote Connections…. Transform ▸ Perspective is disabled only because of the id-collision bug above (finding 13).

Partial-parity implementations. These are behaviour notes, not bugs:
- Presets: a single Preset Manager behind three menu doors (Preset Manager, Migrate, Export/Import).
- Purge: one all-or-nothing command, not Photoshop's submenu.
- Content-Aware Scale: shrinks the whole canvas by seam carving from the composite; it cannot enlarge and has no Protect or skin-tone options; Photoshop scales the active layer.
- Auto-Align: translation only, with a ±32 px search.
- Auto-Blend: focus-stack only, output to a new layer; no Panorama mode and no masks.
- Free Transform (⌘T): a numeric dialog. On-canvas handles exist only through the Move tool's Show Transform Controls.
- Perspective Warp: numeric corner offsets as a percentage of the canvas.
- Warp: preset envelopes only, no custom grid.
- Puppet Warp: a hard-coded demo (finding 10).
- Edit ▸ Transform rasterizes type layers (one undo step restores them); Photoshop keeps type live.
- Stroke: foreground colour only, needs a selection, hard-edged band.
- Define Brush and Define Pattern: auto-named with no name prompt, and they take the selection's bounding box, ignoring non-rectangular coverage.
- Check Spelling: the webview's native spellcheck in a textarea.
- Search (⌘F): searches commands only.
- Toggle Last State (⌥⌘Z) is implemented. Step Forward and Step Backward are not in this blueprint (CC 2022 layout).
- History: there is no Allow Non-Linear History.
- Keyboard Shortcuts: offers Application Menus and Tools scopes only, with no panel menus.

findings.title: Clicking a History snapshot row irreversibly wipes all undo history and the current unsaved state
findings.feature: History panel ▸ Snapshots (restoreSnapshot)
findings.evidence: Panels.tsx:2718 calls store.restoreSnapshot(s.id) on a single row click, with no confirmation. store.ts:7302-7309 then runs revertActiveDoc(buildProject(snap.bytes)). revertActiveDoc swaps in a new engine and sets history: [] (store.ts:6040, 6090). e2e/history-snapshots.spec.ts shows an auto-created first snapshot is present by default (s0 === 1).
findings.repro: 1. Open an image. The auto first snapshot row appears. 2. Make ten edits. 3. Click the snapshot row, for example to compare. 4. Try Undo or clicking a history state.
findings.impact: The document goes back to the snapshot and history is empty, so every edit made since then is gone unless it was saved or snapshotted. In Photoshop, clicking a snapshot is non-destructive: history states stay clickable until the next edit. The top row is always present, so one stray click loses work.
findings.suggested_fix: Make restore itself an undoable step, for example by pushing a stack snapshot before swapping or by recording 'Restore Snapshot' as a history state. Or keep the previous engine so it can be restored. At minimum, snapshot the current state automatically or confirm before discarding unsaved history.
findings.verdict_reason: Panels.tsx:2718 calls store.restoreSnapshot(s.id) straight from the row's onClick, with no confirmation. store.ts:7302-7309 then calls revertActiveDoc(this.engine.buildProject(snap.bytes), ..., {dirty:true}). revertActiveDoc (store.ts:6040-6125) swaps d.engine for the freshly built engine, whose undo stack is empty, and sets history: [] twice. Nothing captures the pre-restore state: there is no auto-snapshot and the old engine is not kept. The comment at 7300 ('Like Revert, this resets the linear history') shows this is deliberate, but it differs from Photoshop, where clicking a snapshot is non-destructive until the next edit. The e2e test confirms the auto-first snapshot row is always there (s0 === 1). Only the dirty flag survives (#27 fix), so the file on disk is safe but every edit since the snapshot is gone.

findings.title: Copy in one document then Paste in another pastes nothing, or pastes that document's own older clip
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Paste / Paste in Place / Paste Into (cross-document)
findings.evidence: Each document has its own engine clipboard (engine mod.rs:9563 self.clip). store.ts:2533 keeps Paste enabled after a document switch through `hasClipboard: e.has_clipboard() || !!this.publishedPng?.length`. But adoptPasteboardImage (store.ts:6561) returns early in two cases without giving the target engine any pixels: when the system pasteboard read fails or returns null (`!found`), and when it returns our own PNG byte-for-byte (`sameBytes(this.publishedPng, found.bytes)`). Then pasteFromClipboard (6663-6665) calls e.paste() on the target engine, which returns 0 with no clip (mod.rs:9789) or pastes that engine's stale clip. There are no tests for pasting across documents: pasteboard.test.ts and the color-management e2e both paste into the same engine.
findings.repro: 1. Open documents A and B. 2. In A, select an area and press ⌘C. 3. Switch to B and press ⌘V. This fails whenever the platform returns the published PNG unchanged, or when clipboard.read() is denied (for example when Paste is triggered from the native menu with no DOM user gesture).
findings.impact: The most common clipboard workflow, copying between two images, silently does nothing even though Paste is enabled. If B had its own earlier Copy, the wrong pixels are pasted.
findings.suggested_fix: In adoptPasteboardImage, when the target engine is not the one that produced publishedPng, or has no clip, adopt the pixels anyway. Better: keep the last Clip (u16 pixels, anchor, profile) at store level and push it into the target engine before pasting, so cross-document paste keeps 16-bit precision and the Paste in Place anchor. Add a two-document copy/paste test.
findings.verdict_reason: The engine clipboard is per engine (mod.rs:3468 `clip: Option<Clip>`). The only cross-engine transfer is set_clipboard_from_image in adoptPasteboardImage (store.ts:6567). That function returns true without adopting anything at store.ts:6561 when `!found || sameBytes(this.publishedPng, found.bytes)`. The byte-identical round-trip is exactly the case the ponytail comment (6553-6557) says to expect. pasteFromClipboard (6663-6665) then runs e.paste() on document B's engine: paste() returns 0 with no clip (mod.rs:9789-9792), or pastes B's stale clip. store.ts:2531-2533 even claims 'A published PNG remains pasteable after switching documents', and the sameBytes shortcut defeats that. No test copies in one document and pastes in another; pasteAcrossProfiles in color-management-profiles.spec.ts:655 uses a single engine.

findings.title: Paste crops the clipboard to the canvas, so a large pasted image cannot be scaled down afterwards
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Paste / Paste in Place / Paste Into / Paste Outside
findings.evidence: paste_layer (mod.rs:9758) builds Layer::transparent(self.w, self.h), a canvas-sized plane. It skips every clip pixel outside the canvas: `if dx < 0 || dy < 0 || dx >= docw || dy >= doch { continue; }`. The engine does support planes larger than the canvas (crop keeps them for Reveal All), so this is a choice, not a limitation.
findings.repro: Copy a 4000×3000 photo, paste it into a 1000×1000 document, then Free Transform it to 25%.
findings.impact: Photoshop keeps the whole pasted layer, including the parts off-canvas. Here only the centred 1000×1000 crop survives, so scaling it down produces a small cropped fragment. The pixels outside the canvas are lost at paste time.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the pasted layer with pixel_bounds equal to the clip rect at (ax, ay), the same oversized-plane representation crop already uses, instead of a canvas-sized plane.
findings.verdict_reason: paste_layer (mod.rs:9756-9784) always builds Layer::transparent(self.next_id, 'Layer', self.w, self.h) and skips every clip pixel with `dx < 0 || dy < 0 || dx >= docw || dy >= doch`. A foreign clip adopted through set_clipboard_from_image keeps its full size, so pasting a 4000x3000 image into a 1000x1000 document keeps only the centred crop. The engine already supports planes larger than the canvas: remap_active_layer and transform_layer comment that crop keeps them for Reveal All, and pixel_bounds is used throughout. So this is avoidable loss of the off-canvas pixels at paste time.

findings.title: The clipboard does not preserve bit depth: Copy Merged quantizes to 8 bits and Copy clamps 32-bit HDR
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Copy Merged / Copy (16/32-bit documents)
findings.evidence: capture_clip(merged=true) reads the RGBA8 display buffer: `let out = &self.output; // composited RGBA8` then `pixels[di] = out[o] as u16 * 257` (mod.rs:9546-9550). A precise 16-bit composite already exists as export_composite_rgba16 (mod.rs:7941). Non-merged Copy reads the u16 proxy `layers[active].pixels` (mod.rs:9555), not pixels_f32, so in 32-bit documents values above 1.0 are clamped. Cut refuses 32-bit edits; Copy does not.
findings.repro: 1. Create a 16-bit document with a smooth gradient over two layers. 2. Select All, Copy Merged, Paste. 3. Compare the pasted layer with the composite in Levels or Info. Similarly, in a 32-bit HDR document, Copy and then Paste a bright area.
findings.impact: On high-bit documents, Copy Merged and Paste silently posterize to 256 levels per channel (banding), and Copy/Paste in 32-bit loses highlight data. The rubric treats corruption on 16/32-bit documents as major.
findings.suggested_fix: For merged capture, composite into a u16 (or f32) buffer with composite_region_into(..., Some(out16)...) instead of self.output. For 32-bit documents, carry f32 clip pixels (or refuse with a message the way Cut does).
findings.verdict_reason: In capture_clip (mod.rs:9544-9550), the merged branch reads `let out = &self.output; // composited RGBA8` and widens with `* 257`, so Copy Merged is 8-bit precision on 16-bit documents. The non-merged branch reads `self.layers[self.active].pixels` (the u16 proxy), never pixels_f32. copy() and copy_merged() have no reject_legacy_float_edit guard; cut() does (mod.rs:9717). paste_layer builds a plain u16 Layer::transparent with no float authority, so HDR values above 1.0 do not survive Copy and Paste in a 32-bit document. export_composite_rgba16 exists at mod.rs:7941 as the precise alternative for the merged case.

findings.title: Fill, Fill with FG/BG, Clear, Cut and Stroke write layer pixels when the layer mask or Quick Mask is the target
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Fill / Fill FG (⌥⌫) / Fill BG (⌘⌫) / Clear (⌫) / Cut / Stroke
findings.evidence:
Relevant code:
- fill_blend_inner (mod.rs:19514), clear_selection (mod.rs:19945), cut (mod.rs:9713) and stroke_selection (mod.rs:21673) always write `self.layers[self.active].pixels`. None of them consults painting_mask() or mask_edit (mod.rs:17506), although the store sets it (store.ts:2962 `e.set_mask_edit(this.snap.maskEdit)`).
- Adjustment and fill layers, whose mask is the only thing Photoshop edits, are refused instead: refuse_destructive_edit (mod.rs:3890) says 'adjustment layers hold no pixels'.
- In Quick Mask, enter_quick_mask sets `self.sel.active = false` (mod.rs:22763), so Fill with FG fills the whole layer.
- For comparison, adjustments route to the mask through apply16 (mask_edit_tests.rs), and content_aware_fill refuses a mask target (mod.rs:20283).
findings.repro: Case 1: 1. Add a layer mask to a photo layer and click the mask thumbnail. 2. Make a selection. 3. Press ⌥⌫ with black as the foreground colour. Case 2: press Q to enter Quick Mask, then press ⌥⌫. Case 3: select a Levels adjustment layer and press ⌥⌫.
findings.impact: Case 1: the photo pixels are painted black and the mask is untouched. Case 2: the whole layer is filled with the foreground colour. Case 3: the edit is refused. Filling or clearing a mask is one of the most common Photoshop masking gestures. It silently damages artwork (undoable) or does nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Branch on painting_mask() and quick-mask state at the top of fill_blend_inner, clear_selection, cut and stroke_selection. Write the colour's grey value (or the background grey for Clear) into the mask, filter mask or quick_mask plane with the selection coverage, under a LayerPx or quick-mask undo. Stop refusing kind 1 and kind 4 when they have a mask.
findings.verdict_reason: fill_blend_inner (mod.rs:19514-19552), clear_selection (19945-19974), cut (9713-9752) and stroke_selection (21673-21710) only write `self.layers[self.active].pixels`. None consults painting_mask() (17506) or mask_edit, which the store sets through set_mask_edit (17483). The JS paths do not reroute either: App.tsx:2117-2122 fillWith calls engine fill_selection directly, store.fillContents/applyFill (store.ts:9789-9813) calls fill_blend, and App.tsx:2734 clear calls clear_selection. None of them checks maskEdit or quickMask. enter_quick_mask sets `self.sel.active = false` (mod.rs:22763), so a Fill in Quick Mask sees no selection and fills the whole layer. For adjustment and fill layers, refuse_destructive_edit (3890) rejects kinds 1 and 4 ('adjustment layers hold no pixels'), even though their mask is the only editable target.

findings.title: Cut skips the guards Clear has: it ignores Lock Image Pixels and cuts type, smart, vector and fill layers
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Cut (⌘X)
findings.evidence: cut() only checks `self.active_layer().locked` (mod.rs:9714), then zeroes alpha in `layers[active].pixels`. It never calls refuse_destructive_edit (mod.rs:3890), which Clear uses and which is pinned by clear_selection_refuses_layers_that_cannot_be_destructively_edited (mod.rs:~60062). A plain locked layer also returns false without setting last_edit_error, so the user gets no message. There is no engine test of Cut on protected layer kinds.
findings.repro: 1. Turn on Lock Image Pixels on a pixel layer, select an area, press ⌘X. 2. Or: on a type layer, select an area, press ⌘X, then edit the text.
findings.impact: Case 1: pixels are removed despite the lock. Case 2: the cut pixels come back, because the type layer re-renders from its spec. The same happens later on smart objects, fill and vector layers. A locked layer silently refuses Cut with no message.
findings.suggested_fix: Put `if self.refuse_destructive_edit() { return false; }` at the top of cut(), and set last_edit_error on the locked path. Mirror the clear_selection guard test for cut().
findings.verdict_reason: cut() (mod.rs:9713-9752) checks only `self.active_layer().locked`, which returns false without setting last_edit_error, then reject_legacy_float_edit and reject_imported_photoshop_edit. It never calls refuse_destructive_edit, which is what refuses lock_image and kinds 2, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 1 for Clear (19950) and Fill (19516). The alpha reduction then runs on the pixels of type and smart layers, which re-render from their spec or source (see the refuse_destructive_edit comment at 3905-3907), so the cut region comes back later. store.cut (store.ts:6531) adds no guard of its own.

findings.title: Lock Transparent Pixels is bypassed by Clear, Cut and Stroke; Lock Position is bypassed by every Edit ▸ Transform command
findings.feature: Layer locks × Edit ▸ Clear / Cut / Stroke / Free Transform / Transform ▸ * / Perspective Warp / Warp / Puppet Warp
findings.evidence: Lock Transparent Pixels: Fill honours it through preserve_for_active (mod.rs:19482). clear_selection (19945), cut (9713) and stroke_selection (21673) never consult lock_transparent, so they rewrite alpha freely. Lock Position: the Layer field is documented as `lock_position: bool, // no moves or transforms` (mod.rs:193), and move_layer_offset refuses it (mod.rs:16628). But refuse_locked_transform (mod.rs:3847), used by transform_layer, skew_layer, flip/rotate layer, perspective_transform and mesh_warp, only checks `locked`.
findings.repro: 1. Turn on Lock Transparent Pixels on a layer with a shape. 2. Select a region and press ⌫, or run Stroke with Location Outside. 3. Separately, turn on Lock Position on a layer and use Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Flip Horizontal, or ⌘T and scale to 50%.
findings.impact: Clear and Cut punch holes in a transparency-locked layer, Stroke paints outside its opaque area, and position-locked layers flip, scale and warp. All of these silently ignore a lock the user set.
findings.suggested_fix: OR lock_transparent into clear, cut and stroke the same way fill_blend_inner does (preserve alpha, or refuse Clear with a message). Make refuse_locked_transform also refuse `lock_position`, with a message like move_layer_offset's.
findings.verdict_reason: Only fill_blend_inner, through preserve_for_active (mod.rs:19481), and content_aware_fill honour lock_transparent. clear_selection, cut and stroke_selection never read it: they scale alpha or composite over it. lock_position is read only by move_layer_offset (16628) and the lock-flag plumbing (grep shows no other use). refuse_locked_transform (3847-3853) checks only `locked`, and transform_layer, skew_layer, flip_layer_h/v, rotate_layer_180/90, perspective_transform and mesh_warp all rely on it. The JS side has no lockPosition guard either (grep for lockPosition in src returns nothing).

findings.title: Free Transform, Skew, Perspective Warp, Warp and Puppet Warp leave the linked layer mask in place
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Free Transform (numeric dialog and the Move tool's on-canvas frame) / Transform ▸ Scale, Rotate, Skew, Distort / Perspective Warp / Warp / Puppet Warp
findings.evidence: transform_layer only replaces `self.layers[self.active].pixels` (mod.rs:26857-26863). skew_layer (26870-26960), perspective_transform (27505+) and mesh_warp (28327-28340) likewise rewrite only pixels. By contrast, remap_active_layer, used by flip and rotate 180°, remaps `l.mask` when mask_linked (mod.rs:26978+), and rotate_layer_90 does the same. CanvasView.tsx:3825 routes the on-canvas frame through the same xform.transformLayer. No engine test covers a transform on a masked layer.
findings.repro: 1. Give a photo layer a mask that reveals a circle, with the mask linked (the default). 2. Press ⌘T and scale to 50%, or apply Transform ▸ Warp.
findings.impact: The image shrinks but the mask keeps its old position and size, so the reveal no longer matches the content. Photoshop transforms a linked mask with its layer. Every masked composite breaks on the most common transform.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same inverse map to `layer.mask` (and to smart_mask and the psd_mask invalidation) when mask_linked, as remap_active_layer does: transform_plane_with_inverse on the 1-channel mask for transform_layer, skew_layer and perspective_transform, and mesh_warp_pixels on the mask for mesh_warp. Add a masked-layer transform test.
findings.verdict_reason: transform_layer (mod.rs:26849-26863) replaces only `.pixels`. skew_layer (26870-26960), perspective_transform (27547-27604) and mesh_warp (28327-28340) likewise touch only pixels; there is no mask reference in any of their bodies. By contrast, remap_active_layer (27025-27039) and rotate_layer_90 (27104-27108) remap `l.mask` when mask_linked. The JS wrapper bakeTransform (app.ts:3526) is just run plus commit, and the on-canvas frame (CanvasView.tsx:3825) goes through the same xform.transformLayer. A linked mask therefore stays put while the content scales, rotates or warps.

findings.title: Edit ▸ Transform pivots on the canvas centre and ignores the active selection
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Flip H/V, Rotate 180°/90°, Scale/Rotate (numeric Free Transform), Skew
findings.evidence:
Relevant code:
- flip_layer_h mirrors about the canvas: `remap_active_layer(move |x, y| (w - 1 - x, y))` (mod.rs:~27053).
- rotate_layer_90 rotates about the canvas centre, `let (cx, cy) = ((w - 1)/2, (h - 1)/2)` (mod.rs:27106). Its own comment says content rotating off-canvas 'is clipped to transparent'.
- transform_layer says 'pivot = doc center' (mod.rs:26815).
- skew_layer's comment says 'pivoting at the layer centre' but uses `cx = w/2` (mod.rs:26898).
- None of these reads `self.sel`. App.tsx:2753-2766 passes no selection context.
- The on-canvas frame compensates for the pivot (CanvasView.tsx:3797 layerTransformArgs); the menu and dialog paths do not.
findings.repro: 1. Place a small logo in the top-left corner of a 1920×1080 document. 2. Apply Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Flip Horizontal, or Rotate 90° CW, or ⌘T with Width 50%. 3. Separately, marquee half of a photo layer and choose Flip Horizontal.
findings.impact: The logo jumps to the opposite corner, or moves toward the centre when scaled, instead of transforming in place. Rotate 90° on a non-square canvas destroys content that leaves the canvas. With a selection, the whole layer flips instead of only the selected pixels. In Photoshop, Transform works around the content bounds' reference point, and with a selection it acts on the selection.
findings.suggested_fix: Pivot the menu and dialog transforms on the active layer's content bbox centre (the same conversion layerTransformArgs already does for the frame). Keep off-canvas pixels in an oversized plane instead of clipping. When a selection is active, float the selected pixels (as Layer via Cut does), transform them, and merge them back.
findings.verdict_reason: The flips map `(w - 1 - x, y)` in canvas coordinates (mod.rs:27053), and remap_active_layer moves the plane origin accordingly, so a top-left logo ends up top-right. rotate_layer_90 rotates about ((w-1)/2, (h-1)/2) and says content off-canvas is clipped (27091-27093). transform_layer is documented 'pivot = doc center' (26815). skew_layer uses cx = w/2 in canvas space (26899-26900) despite its 'layer centre' comment. None of these reads self.sel. The FreeTransform dialog (Dialogs.tsx:8280) passes raw tx/ty with no pivot compensation, unlike CanvasView's layerTransformArgs. The App.tsx:2753-2766 actions pass no selection context. Photoshop transforms around the content bounds and acts on the selected pixels.

findings.title: Edit ▸ Puppet Warp applies a fixed demo bulge; there are no pins, no workspace and no cancel
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Puppet Warp
findings.evidence: app.ts:1854 says `// Puppet warp demo: a 4×4 control mesh bulged outward from the center.` puppetWarp() computes fixed displacement vectors and immediately calls E().mesh_warp. App.tsx:2767 wires `puppet: () => puppetWarp()` directly to the enabled menu item. The only test (e2e/transforms.spec.ts:50) checks that the composite changed.
findings.repro: Choose Edit ▸ Puppet Warp on any layer.
findings.impact: An advertised, enabled command immediately distorts the active layer with a hard-coded outward bulge, with no user control. It is a stub presented as a working feature (the step is undoable).
findings.suggested_fix: Disable the item (drop the monetId wiring) until a pin workspace exists, or build a minimal pin-drag workspace on top of mesh_warp. Rename the demo so it is not reachable from the menu or the scripting ops.
findings.verdict_reason: app.ts:1854 says '// Puppet warp demo: a 4x4 control mesh bulged outward from the center.' puppetWarp() computes fixed radial displacements and immediately calls E().mesh_warp inside rec(). App.tsx:2767 wires `puppet: () => puppetWarp()`, and psMenuData.ts:694-695 gives Edit ▸ Puppet Warp monetId 'puppet', so the item is enabled. A grep shows no Puppet Warp tool, workspace or pin UI anywhere in src. The only test (e2e/transforms.spec.ts:50) asserts that the composite changed. The same demo is also exposed as the puppetWarp scripting op (app.ts:2315).

findings.title: Warp and Puppet Warp (mesh_warp) do not rasterize type and do not refuse non-pixel layers, so the warp is lost later
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Warp / Puppet Warp on type, vector and fill layers
findings.evidence: mesh_warp (mod.rs:28290-28340) calls push_layer_undo and writes the warped pixels. Unlike transform_layer, skew, flip, rotate and perspective, it never calls push_transform_undo or rasterize_active_text_metadata, and it has no refuse_destructive_edit. A type layer stays kind 2 while holding baked warp pixels. The bakeTransform comment in app.ts (around 3555) explains that type re-renders from its spec, so an unrasterized bake 'silently vanishes'. The undo label is also 'Puppet Warp' even for Transform ▸ Warp.
findings.repro: 1. Create a type layer. 2. Apply Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Warp (Arc). 3. Edit the text.
findings.impact: The warp disappears on the next text edit. Vector and fill layers lose the warp on their next re-render. Group and adjustment layers get a no-op step. The History panel shows 'Puppet Warp' for a Warp.
findings.suggested_fix: Give mesh_warp the same prologue as the other transforms: push_transform_undo, then rasterize_active_text_metadata, and refuse kinds 1, 3, 4 and 6 through refuse_destructive_edit (smart objects keep their smart path). Pass the undo label in from the caller.
findings.verdict_reason: mesh_warp (mod.rs:28290-28340) calls refuse_locked_transform and reject_legacy_float_edit and has a smart-object branch. For everything else it calls push_layer_undo('Puppet Warp') and writes the pixels. It never calls push_transform_undo or rasterize_active_text_metadata, which every sibling transform does (26848-26849, 26894-26895, 27049-27052, 27545-27546), and it has no refuse_destructive_edit. On the JS side, warpLayer (app.ts:1877-1881) and the WarpDialog (Dialogs.tsx:8504) do not rasterize first, and bakeTransform now only commits. A kind-2 type layer therefore keeps its spec, and the next text edit re-renders over the warp. The undo label is hard-coded 'Puppet Warp' for Transform ▸ Warp too. Major is kept because the team fixed this same bug on flip, rotate and perspective (app.ts:3555-3560), although it only affects type, vector and fill layers.

findings.title: Pressing OK in Color Settings strips the active document's custom ICC profile or tags an untagged document
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Color Settings…
findings.evidence: ColorSettings.ok always calls `store.assignProfile(choice.profile, choice.custom?.bytes, choice.custom?.name)` (Dialogs.tsx:2853). useProfileChoice starts with `custom = null` (Dialogs.tsx:2704), so the document's own custom ICC is never pre-selected. In store.assignProfile (store.ts:8078-8086), the early return needs sameBytes(snap.iccProfileBytes, null). For a document with custom ICC bytes, or an untagged one (colorProfileAssigned false), the code falls through to markDirty() and `set({ colorProfileAssigned: true, iccProfileBytes: null, iccProfileName: null })`. The existing e2e tests only change the working RGB on built-in profiles.
findings.repro: 1. Open a PSD carrying a custom ICC payload, or open an untagged PNG with Missing Profile set to Leave Untagged. 2. Open Edit ▸ Color Settings, change only the Paste profile policy, and press OK. 3. Save.
findings.impact: The embedded custom profile is silently replaced by the nearest built-in one, or the untagged document becomes tagged, and the document is marked dirty. Colours are interpreted differently after saving. Photoshop's Color Settings never retags open documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Only call assignProfile when the user actually changed the working RGB choice. Better: keep a separate working-RGB preference for new and untagged documents instead of retagging the active one. Seed useProfileChoice with the document's custom ICC when present.
findings.verdict_reason: ColorSettings.ok (Dialogs.tsx:2851-2853) always calls store.assignProfile(choice.profile, choice.custom?.bytes, choice.custom?.name). useProfileChoice starts with custom = null (2704) and is seeded only with store.state.colorProfile (2815), so the document's own ICC is never pre-selected. In assignProfile (store.ts:8070-8089), the early return needs `colorProfileAssigned && sameBytes(this.snap.iccProfileBytes, rawIcc)`. For a document with custom ICC bytes, or an untagged one, that fails. With the same built-in id the code reaches `this.markDirty()` and then sets `colorProfileAssigned: true, iccProfileBytes: null, iccProfileName: null`, then syncDocumentIcc(null). So OK with only a policy change retags the document and marks it dirty.

findings.title: Undo of Convert to Profile or Assign Profile does not restore the document's custom ICC tag
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Convert to Profile / Assign Profile + Undo
findings.evidence: convertToProfile sets JS-only state after commit: `set({ colorProfile: p, colorProfileAssigned: true, iccProfileBytes: destinationIcc, iccProfileName: destinationName })` (store.ts:8166-8172). assignProfile does the same (8086). syncFromEngine restores colorProfile from `e.doc_profile()` and mode, but never reads iccProfileBytes, iccProfileName or colorProfileAssigned back from the engine; the store has no engine ICC getter (only setDocumentIcc at 8094). When only the ICC bytes differ (same built-in id), assignProfile just calls markDirty (8084) and records no history step. The e2e undo test (color-management-profiles.spec.ts:67) covers only built-in to built-in.
findings.repro: 1. Open a PSD with a custom ICC. 2. Convert to Profile ▸ sRGB. 3. Press ⌘Z. 4. Inspect the status bar profile, or save.
findings.impact: The pixels go back to the source space, but the document stays tagged with the destination (or no custom ICC), so the saved file carries the wrong profile. Assigning a different custom ICC with the same built-in id cannot be undone at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the document ICC bytes, name and assigned flag in the engine's undo snapshot (the engine already holds them through setDocumentIcc), and read them back in syncFromEngine. Or push a JS-side history companion for profile metadata.
findings.verdict_reason: convertToProfile (store.ts:8165-8172) and assignProfile (8086) write iccProfileBytes, iccProfileName and colorProfileAssigned into JS state and push them into the engine only through setDocumentIcc. undo(), redo() and seekHistory() (store.ts:9932-9955) only call the engine and commit. syncFromEngine reads colorProfile from e.doc_profile() (2516), but a grep finds no read-back of ICC bytes, name or assigned flag anywhere. After undoing a conversion from a custom-ICC source, the pixels revert but the store still holds the destination's (null) ICC, so saves and exports carry the wrong tag. A same-id custom-to-custom assign takes the markDirty branch (8084) with no history step, so it cannot be undone. This only affects documents with a custom ICC; built-in-to-built-in undo is covered by e2e.

findings.title: Content-Aware Scale re-composites the whole document for every seam on the UI thread and freezes the app on real photos
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Content-Aware Scale (⌥⇧⌘C)
findings.evidence: content_aware_scale loops `while self.w > target_w { self.carve_seam(true) }` (mod.rs:25773-25805).
