Each carve_seam first calls self.composite() over the full document, then builds a full-frame energy map and a full DP table, then removes the seam from every layer (mod.rs:25808+). The wasm engine runs on the main thread (EngineClient creates no Worker), and store.contentAwareScale (store.ts:7914) runs synchronously with no progress or cancel. There is no e2e test or timing check.
findings.repro: 1. Open a 24 MP photo. 2. Choose Content-Aware Scale and reduce the width by 25%, about 1500 seams.
findings.impact: The work is O(seams × layers × pixels): roughly 1500 full composites plus energy and DP passes over 24 M pixels each. The window stops responding (spinning cursor) for a long time with no way to cancel, which looks like a hang.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute energy on a composite taken once, then update it locally along the removed seam, or carve on a downscaled proxy. Run it off the UI thread (worker or chunked with yields) with progress and Esc to cancel. Add a size-bounded timing test.
findings.verdict_reason: content_aware_scale (mod.rs:25773-25805) loops carve_seam once per removed column or row. Each carve_seam (25808+) calls self.composite() (a full composite_region over the document), builds a full w×h energy map and a full DP table, then allocates a new carved buffer for every layer's pixels, mask and smart source. store.contentAwareScale (store.ts:7914-7916) calls it synchronously, and the only Worker in src is scriptWorker (app.ts:2385), so the wasm engine runs on the UI thread with no progress or cancel. Removing about 1500 seams from a 24 MP image is therefore about 1500 full-resolution composites plus allocations. The wall-clock time was not measured, but the complexity makes a multi-minute freeze near-certain.

findings.title: Auto-Align Layers shifts every visible pixel layer, including unselected and locked ones
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Auto-Align Layers…
findings.evidence: auto_align_layers takes as targets every layer with `kind == 0 && visible` (mod.rs:11473-11475), not the selected layers, and calls shift_layer (mod.rs ~10020), which has no locked or lock_position check. App.tsx:2609 wires it with no enablement and no dialog. There are no unit or e2e tests (only engine tests).
findings.repro: 1. Open a document with two exposure layers plus a visible logo pixel layer (locked or position-locked). 2. Select the two exposures. 3. Choose Edit ▸ Auto-Align Layers.
findings.impact: The logo layer is also shifted to match the reference layer, destroying the layout, and locks are ignored. Photoshop aligns only the selected layers and needs at least two.
findings.suggested_fix: Use selectedLayerIds as the target set (pass them in from the store) and skip or refuse locked and position-locked layers. Disable the command when fewer than two pixel layers are selected. The same targeting applies to Auto-Blend.
findings.verdict_reason: auto_align_layers (mod.rs:11446-11520) picks the reference as the first `kind == 0 && visible` layer and the targets as every other visible kind-0 layer (11473-11475). It takes no layer-id argument and checks neither locked nor lock_position before calling shift_layer (10021), which has no lock check either. store.autoAlignLayers (store.ts:7426-7427) passes no selection, and App.tsx:2609 wires it unconditionally. A visible locked or unrelated pixel layer is therefore shifted too.

findings.title: Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective is permanently disabled by a menu-id collision
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective
findings.evidence: In the blueprint, both 'Perspective Warp' (psMenuData.ts:699) and 'Transform ▸ Perspective' (psMenuData.ts:743) carry monetId 'persp'. psMenus.ts:376 wires only the first occurrence unless the path is in SHARED_ACTION_PATHS (psMenus.ts:57), and 'Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective' is not in it. A scratch run of buildPhotoshopMenus with all of App.tsx's action ids printed 'Edit > Transform > Perspective' as disabled.
findings.repro: Open Edit ▸ Transform with a document open.
findings.impact: The Perspective item is greyed out even though its action exists (Distort, beside it, opens the same dialog).
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective' to SHARED_ACTION_PATHS, or give it its own PATH_WIRING row. Add a psMenus test that asserts it is enabled.
findings.verdict_reason: psMenuData.ts:699-700 (Edit ▸ Perspective Warp) and 743-745 (Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective) both carry monetId 'persp'. In psMenus.ts:372-380, `mid && (!wired.has(mid) || SHARED_ACTION_PATHS.has(path))` wires only the first occurrence. The depth-first walk reaches Perspective Warp first. 'Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective' is not in SHARED_ACTION_PATHS (57-66) or PATH_WIRING, and LABEL_WIRING has no 'Perspective' entry, so the Transform item gets `disabled = true`. psMenus.test.ts covers only the injected 'Perspective Crop…'.

findings.title: Refused Cut/Paste errors are not shown until the next command, whose commit is then treated as refused
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Cut / Paste on 32-bit or read-only Photoshop documents
findings.evidence: store.cut only commits when e.cut() returns true (store.ts:6531-6537), and pasteFromClipboard only commits when paste() is non-zero (6665). The engine sets last_edit_error on these refusals: reject_legacy_float_edit('Cut') and reject_imported_photoshop_edit in push_stack_undo. It is never cleared per operation, only by consumeEditError. The next unrelated EngineClient.commit() calls consumeEditError first and returns false (EngineClient.ts:823-825), which skips onCommit (the dirty flag). Callers like assignProfile (`if (!this.engine.commit()) return;`) or contentAwareScale then skip their bookkeeping.
findings.repro: 1. In a 32-bit document, press ⌘X: nothing happens and no message appears. 2. Add a layer or assign a profile. A toast 'Cut is not 32-bit-float safe…' appears for the wrong action, and that action's dirty or state update is skipped.
findings.impact: The user sees an error for the wrong command. The following successful edit may not mark the document dirty, so a close could skip the unsaved-changes prompt, and JS profile state can desync from the engine.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `this.engine.consumeEditError()` on the false/0 paths of store.cut and pasteFromClipboard. Consider clearing last_edit_error at the start of each engine entry point.
findings.verdict_reason: store.cut (store.ts:6531-6537) commits only when e.cut() is true, and pasteFromClipboard (6663-6665) only when paste() is non-zero. Neither false path calls consumeEditError. The engine sets last_edit_error on these refusals (reject_legacy_float_edit at 3778-3780 via reject_float_edit_for_layer, and reject_imported_photoshop_edit at 4052-4064). It is cleared only by clear_last_edit_error, set_depth, a PSD export and a few other paths (grep 7540, 8218, 30136). The next EngineClient.commit() (EngineClient.ts:823-824) returns false from consumeEditError before calling onCommit, which is `this.markDirty()` (store.ts:2256). So the stale toast appears on the wrong action and that action skips the dirty mark and its caller's follow-up (for example assignProfile's `if (!this.engine.commit()) return;`).

findings.title: Find and Replace Text drops character formatting between the first and last match
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Find and Replace Text…
findings.evidence: findReplace runs the regex replacement over fullText(s), then applyTextSpec(id, setText(s, after)) (app.ts:3442-3456). setText (text/spec.ts:576) assumes one contiguous splice: it diffs the common prefix and suffix and restyles the whole middle with the run at the caret. With two or more matches, everything between the first and last match is treated as inserted text.
findings.repro: 1. Create a type layer 'Hello **bold** world Hello' with one word bold. 2. Find 'Hello', change to 'Hi', Replace All.
findings.impact: The bold (or colour, size) run between the matches is reset to the first run's style. Formatting is silently lost across whole paragraphs. Each changed layer is also a separate undo step.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply each match as its own range splice from the end of the string backwards, using the existing range helpers (applyRangeFormat/mergeRuns), instead of one setText over the whole string.
findings.verdict_reason: findReplace (app.ts:3442-3456) replaces across fullText(s) and applies setText(s, after) once. setText (text/spec.ts:576-616) computes a single longest-common-prefix/suffix splice and restyles the whole inserted middle with `inherit = styleAt(p - 1)`. With two or more matches, everything between the first and last match falls inside that one splice and takes the first run's style. The docstring at 3438-3441 admits that formatting on the replaced spans is not preserved, but the actual loss is wider: it also covers the unmatched text between matches.

findings.title: Clear and Fill with Foreground/Background are not macro-recordable, and the Content-Aware Fill workspace records a session-only step
findings.feature: Actions recording × Edit ▸ Clear / Fill FG / Fill BG / Content-Aware Fill…
findings.evidence: App.tsx:2734 `clear: () => { engine.e.clear_selection(); engine.commit(); }` and fillWith (App.tsx:2117-2122) call the engine directly and bypass rec() and RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:905-950). contentAwareFillWith (app.ts:1680) calls rec() without an explicit op, so the step is not serializable and does not persist or replay across sessions.
findings.repro: 1. Start recording an action. 2. Make a selection, press ⌫, then press ⌥⌫. 3. Stop recording and inspect the steps.
findings.impact: Photoshop records Delete and Fill steps. Here the recorded action silently misses them, so the replayed macro produces a different result.
findings.suggested_fix: Route clear and fillWith through store methods (for example store.clearSelectionPixels and store.fillContents('fg'/'bg', 1, 'normal')) listed in RECORDED_STORE_OPS. Give contentAwareFillWith an explicit op.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:2734 `clear: () => { engine.e.clear_selection(); engine.commit(); }` and fillWith (App.tsx:2117-2122) call the engine directly. Neither is a store method in RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:903-950) or goes through rec(), so a recording captures neither step. The Content-Aware Fill part is deliberate: contentAwareFillWith (app.ts:1678-1681) is documented as recording 'as volatile, like the other preview dialogs' because its sampling mask is document-sized. rec() then stores op undefined (506), so the step replays within the session but does not persist. That is a known design trade-off rather than a defect; the Clear and Fill FG/BG gap is the real issue.

findings.title: Purge irreversibly clears all history with no confirmation, and only in the active document
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Purge
findings.evidence: store.purge calls engine.purge() with no confirm (store.ts:7796-7800). engine.purge clears undo and redo, the clipboard, the pattern slot, the brush tip and last_sel (mod.rs:9897-9913) for the active engine only. store.activeBrushTip and activePattern are left pointing at presets until the next pushBrush repairs the engine slot. Photoshop shows a Purge submenu (Undo, Clipboard, Histories, All) and warns that it cannot be undone.
findings.repro: Make edits, then choose Edit ▸ Purge.
findings.impact: One click permanently removes the ability to undo, and the other open documents keep their histories. Until the next brush or colour change, a selected custom tip paints as the round brush and Fill ▸ Pattern silently does nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm before purging, offer the Photoshop sub-items, apply it to all documents for Histories and All, and re-push the active tip and pattern (call pushBrush) afterwards.
findings.verdict_reason: store.purge (store.ts:7796-7800) calls engine.e.purge() with no confirm and leaves the other documents' engines untouched. Engine purge (mod.rs:9897-9913) clears undo and redo, the clip, the pattern slot, the brush tip (brush_tip_active = false) and last_sel. store.purge does not re-run pushBrush and does not reset activePattern or activeBrushTip, so the store's selection points at slots the engine no longer holds. publishedPng is also left set, so hasClipboard (2533) stays true. The blueprint has Purge as a single item (psMenuData.ts:819-820) rather than Photoshop's submenu.

findings.title: Content-Aware Fill is enabled without a selection, and Fill ▸ Content-Aware and Define Custom Shape then do nothing silently
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Content-Aware Fill… / Edit ▸ Fill ▸ Content-Aware / Edit ▸ Define Custom Shape…
findings.evidence: menuEnablement (App.tsx:3440-3468) gates clear and stroke on selectionActive but not caf. Engine content_aware_fill returns silently when `!self.sel.active` (mod.rs:20278). The Fill dialog routes Content-Aware there and closes (Dialogs.tsx:5930), ignoring its Opacity, Mode and Preserve options. store.defineCustomShape returns -1 with no feedback when there is no path (store.ts:4191), and the menu is always enabled.
findings.repro: With no selection, choose Edit ▸ Fill, set Contents to Content-Aware, and press OK. Or, with no path, choose Define Custom Shape.
findings.impact: The dialog closes and nothing happens, with no message.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable caf and Fill's Content-Aware option without a selection, and Define Custom Shape without a work path. Or surface a toast from each no-op path.
findings.verdict_reason: menuEnablement (App.tsx:3444-3466) gates clear and stroke on selectionActive but has no caf entry, and definecustomshape is always enabled. The Fill dialog's Content-Aware option (Dialogs.tsx:5930) calls contentAwareFill(). The engine's content_aware_fill returns immediately when `!self.sel.active` (mod.rs:20278) and sets no error, then the dialog closes; the Opacity, Mode and Preserve options are ignored, as the inline comment admits. defineCustomShape returns -1 with no feedback (store.ts:4191-4193). One nuance: the Edit ▸ Content-Aware Fill… workspace itself is not silent, because content_aware_fill_workspace sets 'Content-Aware Fill needs a selection…' (20327-20329) when applied. For that entry point the problem is only the enablement.

findings.title: Paste Into / Paste Outside create a linked mask, so the pasted image cannot be repositioned inside the frame
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Paste Special ▸ Paste Into / Paste Outside
findings.evidence: paste_into passes the selection mask to paste_layer, which sets `layer.mask = m` on a Layer::transparent whose default is `mask_linked: true` (Layer::with_pixels, mod.rs:~409). shift_layer remaps a linked mask together with the pixels (mod.rs ~10032).
findings.repro: 1. Select a rectangle and Paste Into. 2. Drag the pasted content with the Move tool.
findings.impact: The mask moves with the image, so the 'frame' travels instead of the image sliding inside it. Photoshop creates this mask unlinked.
findings.suggested_fix: Set mask_linked = false on the layer created by paste_into.
findings.verdict_reason: paste_into (mod.rs:9809-9836) hands the selection mask to paste_layer, which sets `layer.mask = m` on Layer::transparent → with_pixels, whose default is `mask_linked: true` (around mod.rs:409). The Move tool commits through commit_offset → apply_linked_move → bake_offset, which remaps the mask when mask_linked (16864-16881), so the mask travels with the pasted pixels. Photoshop creates the Paste Into mask unlinked.

findings.title: MCP exposes almost none of the Edit menu, not even undo/redo
findings.feature: MCP surface (src/mcp/commands.ts)
findings.evidence: The manifest (mcp.manifest.json, 97 tools) contains only doc.setColorSettings, doc.convertToProfile and shortcuts.* from the Edit menu. There is no undo, redo, history seek, fill, stroke, clear, cut/copy/paste, layer transform, fade, define-pattern or purge tool. The xform.flip* and rotate* tools (commands.ts:1222-1255) flip the canvas (Image menu), not the layer (Edit ▸ Transform).
findings.repro: From an MCP client, apply a filter by mistake and try to undo it, or try to flip the active layer.
findings.impact: An agent driving the app cannot recover from its own edits or reach core Edit functionality. MCP names suggest parity with Edit ▸ Transform but act on the canvas.
findings.suggested_fix: Add @mcp wrappers for history.undo, history.redo and history.seek, edit.fill, edit.stroke, edit.clear, clipboard.copy and paste, and layer transforms (xform.transformLayer, flipLayer, rotateLayer). Then run mcp:codegen.
findings.verdict_reason: Narrower than stated. mcp.manifest.json has 90 tools, not 97, with no undo, redo, history, fill, stroke, clear, cut/copy/paste or layer-transform tool, and xform.flip* and rotate* are documented as canvas ops (commands.ts:1220-1255). However, script.run (commands.ts:565) exposes visionOps (app.ts:2279-2334), which includes store.fillContents, strokeSelection, cut, copy, copyMerged, paste, pasteInPlace, pasteInto, fadeLast and contentAwareScale plus every xform.* op such as flipLayerH and transformLayer. So much of Edit is reachable through scripting. What an agent truly cannot do via MCP is undo, redo, seek history, Clear or Purge, and missing undo is the part that matters.

findings.title: Edit ▸ Menus… opens on the Keyboard Shortcuts tab, and both Shortcuts doors are disabled with no document open
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Menus… / Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… / Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…
findings.evidence: PATH_WIRING maps both Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… and Edit ▸ Menus… to 'keyboardshortcuts' (psMenus.ts:79-81). That action is `open("keyboardShortcuts")` with no arg (App.tsx:2708), while the dialog only starts on the Menus tab when `arg === "menus"` (Dialogs.tsx:2184). NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS (App.tsx:77) omits keyboardshortcuts and presetmanager, so they are disabled on Home.
findings.repro: Choose Edit ▸ Menus…. Or, with no documents open, try ⌥⇧⌘K.
findings.impact: Menus… lands on the wrong tab. Customizing shortcuts or presets requires opening a document first.
findings.suggested_fix: Give Menus… its own id that calls open('keyboardShortcuts', 'menus'), and add keyboardshortcuts and presetmanager to NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS.
findings.verdict_reason: PATH_WIRING maps both 'Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…' and 'Edit ▸ Menus…' to 'keyboardshortcuts' (psMenus.ts:79-85). That action is `open("keyboardShortcuts")` with no arg (App.tsx:2708), and the dialog opens on the Menus tab only when `arg === "menus"` (Dialogs.tsx:2184). No caller passes 'menus'. NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS (App.tsx:77) does not match keyboardshortcuts or presetmanager, so both are disabled on Home.

findings.title: Free Transform, Skew, Warp, Fade and Stroke dialogs have no preview; Fade stays available after a Fade; Undo lacks the step name
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Free Transform (⌘T), Transform ▸ Skew/Warp, Fade, Stroke, Undo/Redo labels
findings.evidence: FreeTransform, Skew and WarpDialog (Dialogs.tsx:8258, 8288, 8487), Fade (5971) and StrokeSelection (6684) are plain Dialogs that apply only on OK. PerspectiveWarp uses PreviewDialog. can_fade is true whenever the top undo entry is any LayerPx on the active layer, including a 'Fade' itself (mod.rs:19935-19939), so a Fade can be faded again and compounds. The Stroke dialog only uses the foreground colour, with no blend mode, opacity or Preserve Transparency. App.tsx never uses the undoLabel or redoLabel snapshot fields for the Edit ▸ Undo item.
findings.repro: Press ⌘T, type Width 50, and watch the canvas. Apply a filter, then Fade twice.
findings.impact: Parameters are applied blind, which differs from Photoshop's on-canvas ⌘T and its previewing Fade. Edit ▸ Undo does not say what it will undo.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap these dialogs in PreviewDialog. Make can_fade false after a Fade. Relabel Undo/Redo from undoLabel and redoLabel. Consider making ⌘T start the Move-tool transform frame.
findings.verdict_reason: FreeTransform (Dialogs.tsx:8258), Skew, WarpDialog (8487), Fade (5971) and StrokeSelection (6684) are plain Dialogs that act only on OK. can_fade (mod.rs:19938-19941) is true for any LayerPx on the active layer, and fade_last pushes its own LayerPx 'Fade' (19918), so Fade stays enabled after a Fade and re-fades between the full-strength and faded results. undoLabel and redoLabel are only read as cache-bust keys in Panels.tsx and are never used for the Edit ▸ Undo label; App.tsx and psMenus.ts do not reference them.

areas.coverage:
Code review only. I ran no builds, suites or single tests. Inventory:
(1) Edit ▸ Preferences: 18 enabled menu items (psMenuData.ts:880-897, App.tsx:2710-2727) open a dialog with 20 sections (Dialogs.tsx:1552). Content Credentials and AI Models can only be reached from inside the dialog. 16 sections have real controls, about 37 settings in all. 4 sections are deliberate "no options" placeholders.
(2) Persistence: I traced every preference loader and setter across the roughly 30 `mv.*` localStorage keys in store.ts (loadStorePreferences, loadPreferencePanes, loadWebAndFilePrefs, loadExportPrefs, loadColorPolicyPrefs, loadAutoRecoverMinutes, font, shift-key, spring-loaded tools, history options/log/states, grid), plus interfacePrefs.ts, docPresets.ts (ruler unit), EngineClient.ts (gamut paint), keyboardShortcuts.ts, shortcutSets.ts and psMenus.ts (hidden menus). I also traced the boot order in app.ts:271-293.
(3) Keyboard Shortcuts and Menus dialog: set save, save-as, delete, import, export, reset; the Menus tab; 6 MCP shortcut-set commands.
(4) Window ▸ Workspace: 6 built-ins, save, delete, reset, last-layout and toolbar persistence, and DockableWorkspace normLayout.
(5) Edit ▸ Color Settings: dialog, .csf, policy persistence and MCP doc.setColorSettings.
(6) Consumers of each preference: App.tsx (workspace/tools/general), CanvasView (cursors, rulers), Camera Raw session queue, history log sync, float window entry.
(7) Native side: tauri.conf identifier and plugins, wry 0.55.1 WKUIDelegate methods, tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1 init script, c2pa signer storage.
Tests I checked by grep: e2e/preference-panes.spec.ts, storePreferences/historyLog/historyOptions/interfacePrefs/preferencePanes/shortcutSets unit tests, color-management e2e, workspace e2e.
Not reviewed in depth: the Content Credentials import flow in Rust beyond storage, .csf file parsing, the model manager internals, and whether WKWebView anchor downloads (used by History Log ▸ Save Log…) land anywhere.
areas.parity_notes:
Photoshop preferences that are absent or deliberately empty. None is reported as a bug, since these are correctly absent or disclosed:
- General: Reset Preferences On Quit, image interpolation, HUD color picker, export clipboard.
- Interface: UI scaling, per-screen-mode canvas colors.
- Workspace: floating document windows, narrow options bar.
- Tools: most options beyond spring-loaded keys.
- History Log: "Save Log Items To" Metadata (text export only; ponytail at Dialogs.tsx:1889).
- File Handling: save options, image previews, Maximize PSD Compatibility, recent-list length, and the recovery interval (backend exists, no UI; reported above).
- Performance: memory, GPU, cache levels.
- Scratch Disks, Plug-Ins, Technology Previews, Product Improvement: placeholder panes.
- Transparency & Gamut: transparency grid size/colors (gamut warning only).
- Units & Rulers: column size, point size.
- Guides, Grid & Slices: guide/smart-guide/slice colors and styles, grid subdivisions and units.
- Type: only font preview size.
- Camera Raw: JPEG/HEIC/TIFF handling (raw-only by design).
Workspaces capture panel layout, toolbar placement, tool configuration and shortcuts, but not Edit ▸ Menus visibility. The comment at App.tsx:285-286 says Vision has no menu-hiding feature, which is now stale.
MCP covers Color Settings (doc.setColorSettings), shortcut sets (shortcuts.listSets/saveSet/selectSet/deleteSet/importSet/exportSet), panel options, dock collapse and Camera Raw import options. It has no commands for Preferences panes (theme, History States, cursors, grid, units, history log) or for saving/applying workspaces.
Every preference is stored in WebView localStorage under the bundle id dev.monet.vision. This survives app updates as long as the identifier does not change. Dev (localhost:1420) and release (tauri://localhost) have separate stores. The Content Credentials signer is the only native-side setting (app data c2pa/, key written then chmod 0600).
Well-covered areas: cursor/workspace/Camera Raw prefs (e2e/preference-panes.spec.ts), History States and grid (storePreferences.test.ts), history options/log normalization, interface prefs, shortcut sets (unit + e2e), Color Settings policies (e2e). Gaps: Color Settings OK on custom-ICC or untagged documents, History Log across document switches, and workspace save in the native webview (e2e runs in Chromium, where prompt works).

findings.title: Window ▸ Workspace ▸ Save Workspace… and Delete Workspace… do nothing in the desktop app (window.prompt returns null)
findings.feature: Window ▸ Workspace ▸ Save Workspace… / Delete Workspace…; History panel ▸ New Snapshot when History Options ▸ Show New Snapshot Dialog is on
findings.evidence: App.tsx:2665 `const name = (typeof prompt === "function" ? prompt("Save workspace as:") : null)?.trim(); if (!name || !dockRef.current) return;` and App.tsx:2683 (delws) use the same pattern. wry 0.55.1's WKUIDelegate (wkwebview/class/wry_web_view_ui_delegate.rs) implements only runOpenPanel, requestMediaCapturePermission and createWebView. It has no runJavaScriptTextInputPanel. tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1's init-iife.js overrides only window.alert and window.confirm. So WebKit resolves prompt() as Cancel, which returns null. The repo already records this limit: Panels.tsx:1802 says "No prompt(): the desktop webview has none", and panelInventory.test.ts:281 says "wry implements no text-input panel". The same null return turns Panels.tsx:2647 (New Snapshot with showNewSnapshotDialog) into a silent cancel. The e2e specs pass only because Playwright's Chromium implements prompt (panel-views.spec.ts:142, shortcut-sets.spec.ts:184, customize-toolbar.spec.ts:173 all use page.once('dialog')).
findings.repro: In the native app, arrange panels, then choose Window ▸ Workspace ▸ Save Workspace…. No name field appears, nothing is saved and no new workspace shows in the menu. Delete Workspace… only appears once a custom workspace exists, so it cannot be reached either. Separately, turn on History ▸ History Options ▸ Show New Snapshot Dialog, then click New Snapshot: nothing happens.
findings.impact: On the shipped build, users cannot create named workspaces: the panel layout, toolbar placement and shortcut capture described at App.tsx:280-292 are unreachable. The History Options preference turns New Snapshot into a no-op. No error is shown.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace prompt() with the app's own naming dialog, the same approach Select ▸ Save Selection… already uses (e.g. a small `nameInput` dialog in the DialogsProvider). Give Delete Workspace… a picker listing the saved names. Add a unit or source guard banning `prompt(` in src, like panelInventory.test.ts does for the Channels flyout.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:2665 and 2683 get the name only from prompt(), and Panels.tsx:2647 (New Snapshot with showNewSnapshotDialog on) does the same. Nothing in src or monet-ui overrides window.prompt (grepped). Locked wry is 0.55.1 (src-tauri/Cargo.lock). Its wkwebview/class/wry_web_view_ui_delegate.rs registers only windowWillClose, runOpenPanel, requestMediaCapturePermission and createWebView; there is no runJavaScriptTextInputPanel. Without that delegate method, WKWebView behaves as if the user pressed Cancel. tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1's init-iife.js overrides only alert and confirm. The repo already states the limit at Panels.tsx:1802 and panelInventory.test.ts:281. All three e2e specs pass only because Chromium implements prompt (page.once('dialog') at panel-views:142, shortcut-sets:184, customize-toolbar:172). Scope is the macOS build: Windows WebView2 and WebKitGTK do show a prompt. macOS is the primary target, so this stays major.

findings.title: Color Settings OK re-assigns the active document's profile even when Working RGB is unchanged: it strips an embedded custom ICC, tags an untagged document and dirties it, with no undo
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Color Settings… ▸ OK
findings.evidence: Dialogs.tsx:2851-2853: `ok` always calls `store.assignProfile(choice.profile, choice.custom?.bytes, choice.custom?.name)`. useProfileChoice (Dialogs.tsx:2702-2704) starts with `custom = null`, even when the document carries custom ICC bytes. store.ts:8078 early-returns only if `colorProfileAssigned && sameBytes(this.snap.iccProfileBytes, rawIcc)`. For a document with iccProfileBytes, or an untagged one (assigned=false), that guard fails. The profile id is unchanged, so line 8084 calls `this.markDirty()` with no engine commit and no history step. Line 8086 then sets `colorProfileAssigned: true, iccProfileBytes: null, iccProfileName: null`, and syncDocumentIcc(null) clears the container ICC.
findings.repro: (a) Open a JPEG that has an embedded non-built-in ICC profile, such as a camera or custom display profile. Open Edit ▸ Color Settings, change only Paste profile policy, click OK. The document's embedded profile is gone (status shows the built-in fallback), the tab shows `*`, and Edit ▸ Undo does not restore it. (b) Open a PNG with Missing profile policy = Leave Untagged. Open Color Settings, click OK with no changes. The document is now tagged and dirty.
findings.impact: An app-level settings dialog silently rewrites the active document's color identity. Saves and exports then embed the fallback built-in profile instead of the original ICC, which shifts colors for wide-gamut content. The change cannot be undone. Existing e2e tests only cover changing the RGB choice on sRGB documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Only call assignProfile when the user actually changed the Working RGB control (`choice.value !== String(initial) || choice.custom`). Better still, stop Color Settings from touching open documents, as Photoshop does, and keep Working RGB as an app preference (see the Working RGB finding). Add an e2e test that opens a custom-ICC document and an untagged one, clicks Color Settings OK unchanged, and asserts profile, bytes and dirty state are unchanged.
findings.verdict_reason: ColorSettings (Dialogs.tsx:2813) seeds useProfileChoice with store.state.colorProfile only, and custom starts null (2703), so choice.custom?.bytes is undefined. ok() (2851-2853) always calls assignProfile. In store.ts:8078 the early return needs colorProfileAssigned && sameBytes(iccProfileBytes, null) && iccProfileName === null. That fails for a document opened through applyOpenedImageProfilePolicy with embedded custom bytes (app.ts:7380-7385), and for an untagged document (markProfileUntagged sets assigned=false). With the profile id unchanged it takes the markDirty() branch (8084): no engine commit and no history step. Then 8086-8087 clear iccProfileBytes/name, set assigned=true and call syncDocumentIcc(null), which clears the container ICC. sameBytes (1318) treats null/null as equal, so a plain built-in sRGB document is unaffected; only the custom-ICC and untagged cases trigger. No e2e test reopens Color Settings on such a document (color-management-profiles.spec.ts:549 stops after the open).

findings.title: Working RGB is not a saved setting: it is whichever profile the active document has, so it is lost on relaunch and changes with the active tab
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Color Settings ▸ Working Spaces ▸ RGB; Missing/Embedded profile policies
findings.evidence: monet-color colorManagement.ts:115-142: ColorPolicyPrefs persists working CMYK, Gray and Spot, but not RGB ("RGB stays on the document"). app.ts:6950 and siblings (7070, 7115, 7143…) take `const workingProfile = store.state.colorProfile`, the active document's profile, and pass it to Assign Working RGB and Convert to Working RGB. On a cold launch the snapshot default is `colorProfile: 0` (store.ts:1388), and nothing restores it.
findings.repro: Set Color Settings ▸ RGB to Adobe RGB (1998) and Missing profile = Assign Working RGB, then quit and relaunch. Open an untagged PNG: it gets sRGB. Or, with a ProPhoto document active, open an untagged PNG: it is assigned ProPhoto. With Embedded = Convert to Working RGB, its pixels are converted into ProPhoto.
findings.impact: Color-management presets such as North America Prepress 2 do not survive a restart; the dialog then reads Custom. Newly opened files get tagged or converted into an unrelated document's profile depending on which tab was active.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `workingRgb` to ColorPolicyPrefs, persisted and normalized like workingCmyk. Use it in the open and paste policy paths instead of `store.state.colorProfile`, and have Color Settings stop assigning to the active document.
findings.verdict_reason: ColorPolicyPrefs (monet-color colorManagement.ts:116-142) has workingCmyk, workingGray and workingSpot, with the comment "RGB stays on the document". No persisted workingRgb exists in src; the only uses are the .csf save/load and presets in Dialogs.tsx. routeOpen (app.ts:6950) and the sibling open paths (7070, 7115, 7143, 7171, 7234, 7250, 7289, 7325, 8025) read workingProfile = store.state.colorProfile before the new document replaces the active one, then pass it to applyOpened*ProfilePolicy / convertToWorkingRgb. The snapshot default is colorProfile: 0 (store.ts:1388), and only mv.colorPolicyPrefs is persisted (6882/6898). The design is intentional but has the stated side effects.

findings.title: History Log writes a phantom edit entry every time you switch or close a document tab
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ History Log (Concise/Detailed)
findings.evidence: store.ts:2523-2526 logs `historyLogDelta(this.snap.historyLog, this.snap.history, history, …)` on every syncFromEngine. activateDoc (store.ts:6177-6226) calls `this.engine.activate(target.engine)`, which runs afterDocChange → sync() → onSync → syncFromEngine (EngineClient.ts:472-486, app.ts:236), while `this.snap.history` still holds the previous document's labels. `this.set({ history: target.historyLabels })` only runs after that, at 6226. historyLogDelta (store.ts:776-792) treats any label difference as a new state and logs `history[historyIndex-1]` of the newly active document. historyLog.test.ts has no document-switch case.
findings.repro: Turn on Preferences ▸ History Log. Open two documents with different histories (e.g. paint one stroke in A). Click between the tabs. Each switch adds a line such as "Brush Tool" (Concise) or "B.psd: Open (state 1 of 1)" (Detailed), with no edit made.
findings.impact: The audit trail, which is the purpose of the feature, records edits that never happened, and the saved log is unreliable.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip logging when the sync follows a document change: compare the active doc id captured at the last sync, or set `history` before `engine.activate` and on close. Add a unit test that switches between two stores/docs and asserts no entries.
findings.verdict_reason: activateDoc (store.ts:6172-6230) sets doc.name to the target first, then calls engine.activate(target.engine). activate → afterDocChange → sync() → onSync (EngineClient.ts:439-486, 804-808; app.ts:236) runs syncFromEngine synchronously while this.snap.history still holds the previous document's labels. history: target.historyLabels is set only afterwards, at 6226. At store.ts:2523-2526, historyLogDelta(this.snap.historyLog, this.snap.history, history, …) finds the labels changed (776-792) and logs the new document's current label under its name. It stays silent only when both timelines are identical. Closing a tab reaches the same path through the next activation. historyLog.test.ts has no document-switch case.

findings.title: The auto-recovery interval preference has no UI or MCP control, so recovery saving cannot be changed or turned off
findings.feature: Preferences ▸ File Handling ▸ Automatically Save Recovery Information
findings.evidence: store.ts:6860-6876 defines setAutoRecoverMinutes/loadAutoRecoverMinutes and the comment "Preferences ▸ File Handling ▸ Automatically Save Recovery Information". autoRecover.ts:6-8 has the menu `[0, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60]`. Grepping src finds no caller of setAutoRecoverMinutes outside tests. FileHandlingPrefs (Dialogs.tsx:1772-1802) has only the JPEG-as-layer, new-doc background, 32-bit PSD and Clear Recent controls. `git log -S setAutoRecoverMinutes` shows it arrived in ce409900 with no UI.
findings.repro: Open Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ File Handling: there is no recovery interval. Recovery snapshots are written every 10 minutes (DEFAULT_AUTO_RECOVER_MINUTES) for every dirty document, and nothing turns this off.
findings.impact: Users with very large documents cannot reduce or disable the periodic full-project snapshot writes. The persistence path (mv.autoRecoverMinutes, startAutoRecover restart hook) is dead code in production.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Select to FileHandlingPrefs bound to AUTO_RECOVER_MINUTES (0 = Off) that calls store.setAutoRecoverMinutes. Optionally expose it via MCP.
findings.verdict_reason: The only reference to setAutoRecoverMinutes in src (non-test) is its definition at store.ts:6864. Grepping src/ui, src/mcp and App.tsx for autoRecover or Recovery finds nothing. startAutoRecover (app.ts:8283-8288) runs a fixed DEFAULT 10-minute interval after recoverLastSession, and only mv.autoRecoverMinutes, which no UI writes, can change it. The feature works at its default; the control is simply missing, so minor fits.

findings.title: Edit ▸ Menus… (⌥⇧⌘M) opens the dialog on the Keyboard Shortcuts tab, not the Menus tab
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Menus…
findings.evidence: psMenus.ts:80 maps `"Edit ▸ Menus…": "keyboardshortcuts"`, the same action as Keyboard Shortcuts…. App.tsx:2708 `keyboardshortcuts: () => open("keyboardShortcuts")` passes no arg. Dialogs.tsx:2184 opens on the Menus tab only when `arg === "menus"`, and no caller passes "menus" (grep). The comment at Dialogs.tsx:2181 claims "`arg === \"menus\"` opens straight on the Menus tab". psMenusCustomize.test.ts:112 only string-matches the source.
findings.repro: Choose Edit ▸ Menus… or press ⌥⇧⌘M. The dialog opens on Keyboard Shortcuts.
findings.impact: The command does something other than its label says. Users have to find the tab themselves.
findings.suggested_fix: Wire the path to its own id, e.g. `"Edit ▸ Menus…": "menuscustomize"` with `menuscustomize: () => open("keyboardShortcuts", "menus")`, add it to NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS, and replace the string-match test with a behavior test.
findings.verdict_reason: psMenus.ts:80 maps "Edit ▸ Menus…" to "keyboardshortcuts", and App.tsx:2708 is open("keyboardShortcuts") with no arg. Dialogs.tsx:2184 selects the Menus tab only when arg === "menus", and no caller passes it (grep). psMenusCustomize.test.ts:110-118 only string-matches the source. Downgraded to polish: the correct dialog opens and the Menus tab is one click away.

findings.title: The Menus tab can hide every way back into the Menus dialog, locking the user out (shortcuts dispatch only from the pruned menu)
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Menus… (hidden menu commands)
findings.evidence: App.tsx:3526-3534 builds `shortcutCommands` (dispatch and Edit ▸ Search) from `baseMenus = buildMenus(hiddenMenuCommands, …)`. psMenus.ts:531-540 prunes hidden paths from every menu, Help included. listMenuCommands (psMenus.ts:171) lists Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…, Edit ▸ Menus… and Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… as hideable, with no protection. No MCP command resets mv.hiddenMenuCommands.
findings.repro: In Edit ▸ Menus…, uncheck Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…, Edit ▸ Menus… and Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…, then click OK. ⌥⇧⌘K and ⌥⇧⌘M stop working and Edit ▸ Search cannot find the command. There is no way to reopen the dialog.
findings.impact: Recovery requires deleting the app's WebKit website data, which also wipes every other preference and library.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the dialog's own entry points as non-hideable (disable their checkboxes), or keep shortcut dispatch on the unpruned catalog so hidden commands keep their chords, as Photoshop does.
findings.verdict_reason: shortcutCommands comes from baseMenus = buildMenus(hiddenMenuCommands, …) (App.tsx:3526-3535). Both keydown paths (2306 and 2375) dispatch from shortcutCommandsRef built from it, and Edit ▸ Search uses commandPalette.items = shortcutCommands (3653). pruneHidden (psMenus.ts:147-165) removes hidden paths from every menu, Help included; Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… is at psMenus.ts:526. listMenuCommands lists every item with no protection. The only other open("keyboardShortcuts") is App.tsx:2708. There is no native menubar in src-tauri, no "Show All Menu Items", resetWorkspace (3376) does not touch mv.hiddenMenuCommands, and no MCP command does. The only reset is the dialog's own Reset All (Dialogs.tsx:2322), which is unreachable once locked out. It takes a deliberate three-step self-inflicted action, so minor stands.

findings.title: Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… is disabled on the Home screen with no document open
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… / Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… / ⌥⇧⌘K
findings.evidence: App.tsx:77 `NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS = /^(new|openf|clearrecent|browse|search|colorsettings|pref[a-z]*|exportprefs|customizetoolbar)$/` does not include `keyboardshortcuts`. App.tsx:3440-3442 disables every other registered action when `doc.width`/`doc.height` is 0. The KeyboardShortcuts dialog (Dialogs.tsx:2182+) never touches the engine.
findings.repro: Launch the app, which lands on Home. Open Edit: Keyboard Shortcuts… and Menus… are greyed out, and ⌥⇧⌘K does nothing. Preferences and Toolbar… remain enabled.
findings.impact: This is inconsistent with the other preference commands. Users cannot customize shortcuts until they create or open a document.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `keyboardshortcuts` (and the Menus… id if it is split out) to NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS, and cover it in menuEnablement.test.ts.
findings.verdict_reason: NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS (App.tsx:77) is /^(new|openf|clearrecent|browse|search|colorsettings|pref[a-z]*|exportprefs|customizetoolbar)$/, and "keyboardshortcuts" does not match. menuEnablement (3434-3441) sets every non-matching stableMenuActions id to false when there is no document, and nothing re-enables keyboardshortcuts (its only other mention is 2708). The Home keydown path (2304-2308) dispatches from the same disabled map, so ⌥⇧⌘K is dead too. Edit ▸ Menus… and Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… share the id and are disabled as well.

findings.title: Corrupt stored settings can crash the UI, sometimes on every launch, and there is no Reset Preferences
findings.feature: Settings persistence / invalid stored settings recovery
findings.evidence: store.ts:6830-6834 `loadExportPrefs`: `this.set({ exportPrefs: JSON.parse(s) as AppSnapshot["exportPrefs"] })` is the only preference loader with no normalization. A stored `null` or `{}` reaches Dialogs.tsx:1815 (`exportPrefs.format`) and 4109-4110 (`prefs.format`, `prefs.quality`), and exportAs gets quality NaN (app.ts:4805). App.tsx:294-309 `loadLS` casts mv.workspaces, mv.workspaceLast and mv.toolbarLast without shape checks. A non-array mv.workspaces throws in `workspaces.map` (App.tsx:3350) during App render on every launch. normGroup (dockable-core.ts:196) assumes `g.tabs` is an array. The only ErrorBoundary is at the root (main.tsx:95), and the app has no Reset Preferences or Reset-on-quit path (grep).
findings.repro: Set localStorage mv.exportPrefs to `null` (or mv.workspaces to `{}`) and relaunch. Opening Preferences ▸ Export or File ▸ Export As… replaces the whole app with "Monet Vision hit an unexpected error". With the corrupted workspaces key, this happens at every launch.
findings.impact: Only corruption or a hand edit triggers this, since the schemas have been stable since 89d53207. When it happens the user has no in-app way to recover, and any open documents' UI is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize exportPrefs like normalizeWebExportPrefs. Validate the workspace keys (Array.isArray plus per-entry shape; drop bad entries). Add a General ▸ Reset Preferences On Quit, or a startup key such as holding ⌥⌘⇧, that clears the `mv.*` preference keys.
findings.verdict_reason: loadExportPrefs (store.ts:6830-6834) assigns JSON.parse(s) unchecked; a stored "null" makes exportPrefs null, and Dialogs.tsx:1815 (exportPrefs.format) and 4109 (prefs.format) then throw during render. loadLS (App.tsx:294-296) casts mv.workspaces with no shape check. useState(loadWorkspacesLS) (2020) followed by workspaces.map in the menuWorkspaces useMemo (3350) throws on every App render when the value is a non-array. The only boundary is the root ErrorBoundary (main.tsx; ErrorBoundary.tsx), which shows BootError with no reset action, and grep finds no Reset Preferences path. Only corruption or a hand edit triggers it, since every writer stores arrays or objects, so minor is right.

findings.title: Preferences ▸ Units & Rulers ▸ "Rulers" does not change the rulers or the Info panel
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ Units & Rulers
findings.evidence: Dialogs.tsx:1751-1766: the select is labeled "Rulers" (aria-label "Ruler units"). Its only consumers are ImageSize (5848), CanvasSize (10279) and PrintDialog (5369). CanvasView.tsx:3252-3275 always draws pixel ticks every 50 px. docPresets.ts:153-155 has a ponytail note saying rulers and the Info panel don't react.
findings.repro: Set Units & Rulers ▸ Rulers to Inches. The on-canvas rulers still read 0, 100, 200… pixels, and the Info panel still reports pixels.
findings.impact: The setting's label promises something it doesn't deliver; only the pane's help text discloses the limit.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel the control "Size dialog units" until the rulers follow it, or lift the unit into the store and convert the ruler/Info labels through resolutionPpi.
findings.verdict_reason: loadRulerUnit's only consumers are the pane itself and Dialogs.tsx:5369 (Print), 5848 (Image Size) and 10279 (Canvas Size). CanvasView.tsx:3252-3275 draws pixel ticks every 50 px, unconditionally. The source comment (Dialogs.tsx:1748-1750) and the docPresets.ts:153-155 ponytail note both admit it. Downgraded to polish: the pane's help text says the setting applies to Image Size and Canvas Size, so the only issue is the misleading "Rulers" label.

findings.title: Preference changes can silently fail to save once authored libraries fill the shared localStorage quota
findings.feature: Settings storage (what survives restart/update)
findings.evidence: All preferences live in the WebView's localStorage (no native settings file; the tauri.conf identifier dev.monet.vision keys the WebKit store). Preference setters swallow write errors: store.ts:3501, 3506, 3511, 4354, 4364, 4386, 6827, 6840, 6845, 6882; keyboardShortcuts.ts saveShortcutOverrides; interfacePrefs.ts saveInterfacePrefs; App.tsx saveLS. The same origin also stores multi-MB libraries: patterns as 16-bit base64 (patternPresets.ts:119), brush tips with a 64 MB library cap (brushTips.ts:22), and recent-file PNG thumbnails (store.ts:6766, whose ponytail comment already anticipates quota trouble). WebKit's per-origin localStorage quota is about 5 MB. I did not verify that figure for this WKWebView configuration in-session.
findings.repro: Import or define patterns and brush tips until mv.patternPresets and mv.brushTips approach the quota. Then change any preference (theme, cursors, History States): it applies for the session and reverts on relaunch, with no message.
findings.impact: Settings quietly stop persisting. Users may think preferences are broken or random.
findings.suggested_fix: Route preference writes through persistAuthoredContent (or at least surface a one-time warning), and move pixel libraries out of localStorage to app-data files or IndexedDB, as was already done for Camera Raw profiles (store.ts:5435-5446).
findings.verdict_reason: The mechanism is real. Preference setters swallow write errors (e.g. store.ts:3501, 3506, 3511, 4354, 6840, 6868, 6882). mv.patternPresets (9908) and mv.brushTips (4086) are stored in the same origin's localStorage. But library writes go through persistAuthoredContent (store.ts:2339-2343), which does surface "storage is full". So a user who reaches the quota through libraries gets a warning, and only later preference writes fail silently. Whether the narrow window before that is reachable depends on the WKWebView per-origin localStorage quota for this configuration, which was not verified. Measuring the quota in the native build (write increasing strings until it throws) would settle it.

findings.title: The Light theme and density are not applied to float windows, the canvas rulers stay dark, and boot flashes the dark theme
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ Interface
findings.evidence: float.tsx:220-223 renders `<MonetProvider>` with no applyInterfacePrefs/loadInterfacePrefs call. Grepping float.tsx for theme/density finds nothing, although the page shares the origin's localStorage. CanvasView.tsx:3254 and 3267 hard-code the ruler background `rgba(20,22,28,0.92)` and white ticks. The main window applies prefs only in a DialogsProvider useEffect (Dialogs.tsx:251), after first paint, and main.tsx has no early stamp. The pane's copy says it "Applies immediately to the whole window".
findings.repro: Choose Light in Preferences ▸ Interface. Use Window ▸ Arrange ▸ Float in Window: the float window is dark. Turn on rulers: they are a dark strip over the light chrome. Relaunch: the app briefly paints dark before switching.
findings.impact: The light theme looks inconsistent across windows and chrome.
findings.suggested_fix: Call `applyInterfacePrefs(loadInterfacePrefs(), document.documentElement)` at module top in both main.tsx and float.tsx, before render. Use theme tokens (var(--surface-*)/var(--text-*)) for the ruler SVGs.
findings.verdict_reason: float.html is a separate document (vite.config.ts:132), and float.tsx:220-223 renders MonetProvider with no applyInterfacePrefs call. applyInterfacePrefs is called only at Dialogs.tsx:251 (a useEffect, so after first paint) and 1723. The interfacePrefs.ts header comment says the attributes "cascade to every window", which is not true for a separate webview document. CanvasView.tsx:3254/3267 hard-code a dark ruler background and white ticks.

findings.title: Four enabled Preferences menu items open empty panes
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ Scratch Disks… / Plug-Ins… / Technology Previews… / Product Improvement…
findings.evidence: psMenuData.ts:888, 893, 895 and 896 carry monetIds wired in App.tsx:2718, 2723, 2725 and 2726. Dialogs.tsx:2141-2143 then shows "No configurable options for this pane in this build." e2e/preference-panes.spec.ts:171-183 pins this as intended.
findings.repro: Choose Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ Plug-Ins…. The pane says it has no options.
findings.impact: Enabled commands that do nothing. The menu should show these the way it shows other unimplemented Photoshop items.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the monetIds so these render as disabled placeholders, as other unimplemented items do. Keep the sections in the dialog list if parity of the list matters.
findings.verdict_reason: psMenuData.ts:888, 893, 895 and 896 carry monetIds that App.tsx:2718/2723/2725/2726 route to open("preferences", …). Those panes have no Pane and are not inline, so Dialogs.tsx:2141-2143 shows "No configurable options for this pane in this build." This is deliberate and pinned by e2e/preference-panes.spec.ts:171-183. Polish is the right grade.

findings.title: The Preferences section list can't be used from the keyboard, and some numeric fields have no accessible name
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Preferences dialog
findings.evidence: Dialogs.tsx:2082-2088: the section navigator is plain `<div onClick>` with no role, tabIndex or key handler. History States (2121-2124) and Gridline Every (2127-2130) NumberFields have no id or aria-label; their visible text is a `<span>`, not a `<label>`.
findings.repro: Open Preferences and press Tab: focus skips the section list, so keyboard-only users can't switch panes. A screen reader announces the History States field as an unlabeled spinbutton.
findings.impact: Accessibility gap in a core dialog.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the sections as a `role="tablist"`/listbox of buttons with arrow-key navigation. Add `aria-label`/`id` + `<label htmlFor>` to the two NumberFields.
findings.verdict_reason: The section list (Dialogs.tsx:2082-2088) is plain <div onClick> with no role, tabIndex or key handler. The History States (2121-2124) and Gridline Every (2127-2130) NumberFields have no id or aria-label, and their captions are <span>s. monet-react's NumberField only passes through aria props and adds no label outside <Field>.

areas.coverage:
Read-only code review; I ran no builds or tests. Inventory, from psMenuData.ts lines 903-1318 and App.tsx menuActions lines 2771-2836, 2974-2976 and 3280-3294: the Image menu has 64 items with a monetId, and every one has a handler. Breakdown: Mode 12 (Bitmap, Grayscale, Duotone, Indexed, RGB, CMYK, Lab, Multichannel, 8/16/32 bits, Color Table); Adjustments 22; Auto Tone/Contrast/Color 3; Image Size and Canvas Size 2; Image Rotation 6; Crop, Trim and Reveal All 3; Duplicate, Apply Image, Calculations and Merge to HDR (Exposure Fusion) 4; Variables Define, Data Sets and Apply Data Set 3; Trap 1; Analysis 8 (Set Measurement Scale, Select Data Points, Record Measurements, Place Scale Marker, plus four tool switches). I also reviewed the Histogram panel for each colour mode.

For each item I traced menu entry → App.tsx → the dialog in Dialogs.tsx or dialogs/common.tsx (PreviewDialog) → state/app.ts (adjImpl, xformImpl, dataVars, placeScaleMarker, rec/recordedCall and RECORDED_STORE_OPS) → state/store.ts (mode and depth conversions, Duotone, Indexed, Bitmap, Apply Image, Calculations, Trap, analysis state, activateDoc) → the engine (packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs: apply16/apply32 guards, set_mode, set_depth, convert_grayscale/bitmap/indexed, auto_stretch/auto_color, hdr_toning_pro, match_color, apply_image_channel, calculations, trap, resample_document/reframe_document/remap_document/rotate_arbitrary, render_vector/ensure_vector; adjust.rs kernels). I also checked the MCP surface (commands.ts, mcp.manifest.json, commands.test.ts, handlers.test.ts), the shared histogram helpers in monet-photo, EngineClient edit-error handling, and test coverage by grepping e2e/ (358 specs), the unit tests and the engine tests.

Not reviewed in depth: every adjustment formula against Photoshop numerically (unit tests cover most of them), the Levels/Curves eyedropper and preset codecs, the internals of the PSD Gray writer, the CSV path handling in Data Sets, and native Tauri behaviour. Two findings (vector snap-back, Grayscale export) are confirmed by static reasoning only; no existing test covers them, and adding one would mean editing the repo, which this review was not allowed to do.
areas.parity_notes:
Every item in Vision's Image menu has a monetId, so the menu has no disabled placeholders. The Photoshop gaps are inside features.

- **Image Size:** no Resample-off / Resolution field, no resampling-method choice, no Scale Styles option.
- **Apply Image:** no Merged or other-document source, the active layer can't be its own source, and there is no Mask option.
- **Calculations:** New Channel is not independent of the selection.
- **Replace Color:** a plain dialog targeting the foreground colour, with no eyedropper, selection preview or live preview.
- **Gradient Map:** the destructive dialog offers presets only, with no gradient editor.
- **Brightness/Contrast:** only the legacy linear model; no 'Use Legacy' toggle.
- **Adjustments in CMYK and Lab:** they operate on RGB pixels, not per plate (for example, Invert in Lab is not L→100−L), and there is no CMYK or Lab channel choice in Curves or Levels.
- **Multichannel:** maps to four CMYK plates rather than Photoshop's spot-channel conversion.
- **CMYK Color conversion:** uses the built-in UCR model, while CMYK PSD export uses the working CMYK ICC.
- **Indexed and Bitmap:** stored as RGB pixel states (the menu keeps RGB checked), and later edits aren't constrained to the palette.
- **32-bit:** most destructive adjustments refuse (loudly, with a Convert to 16-bit toast); Levels, Curves, Exposure, Hue/Sat and HDR Toning have float paths.
- **HDR Toning:** runs on the active layer rather than flattening.
- **Analysis:** Record Measurements captures only ruler length/angle and count, not selection area or perimeter data points.
- **MCP:** covers few Image-menu commands directly (no mode, depth, canvas, auto, levels/curves, trim or arbitrary-rotation tools). They are reachable through script.run. xform.resizeImage documents 1..16384 while the engine allows 32767.

findings.title: Image Size, Canvas Size, Crop, Trim, Reveal All, Image Rotation and Flip Canvas leave type specs and vector scenes untransformed: vector layers snap back at once, type layers on their next edit
findings.feature: Image ▸ Image Size / Canvas Size / Crop / Trim / Reveal All / Image Rotation (all 6)
findings.evidence: reframe_document (mod.rs:25410), remap_document (25627), resample_document (25177) and rotate_arbitrary only remap or resample `layer.pixels` for layers whose kind is not 0. They never touch `text_spec` (ax, ay, size) or `vector_scene`/`vector_view`, and they reset ox/oy to 0. A vector layer's pixels are a cache: render_vector (5423) keys it on the canvas width and height plus the view, and ensure_vector runs on every composite (7803). So when w or h changes, the scene re-rasterises at its old geometry and the remapped pixels are thrown away. For type, set_text_layer_spec places glyphs at the spec's canvas coordinates. The Move tool already re-anchors the spec for exactly this reason (CanvasView.tsx:2211-2219, comment: 'commit_offset would leave the spec's ax/ay stale, snapping the text back'). The canvas-geometry commands have no equivalent. No engine or e2e test combines type or vector layers with these commands.
findings.repro: 1) Add a vector shape layer. Image ▸ Image Rotation ▸ 90° CW: the shape renders unrotated in the new portrait canvas. Image Size 50%: the shape stays full size. Crop from a non-zero origin: the shape is not shifted. 2) Add a type layer, then crop, rotate or resize. It looks right until you change its font, bold or text (or run Type ▸ Update All Text Layers). Then it snaps back to its pre-transform position, size or orientation.
findings.impact: Any layered document with live type or shapes is visibly corrupted by core Image-menu geometry commands. Undo works, but the damage appears later, on an unrelated edit, so users won't connect it to the cause.
findings.suggested_fix: In the shared geometry helpers, transform the source of truth, not just the cache. Map a type spec's ax/ay (plus size, and angle for rotate/flip) through the same transform; this touches the JSON the engine already rewrites for colour conversions. Update vector_view (translate, scale, rotate) the way map_smart_link is updated for smart objects. Alternatively, rasterise type and vector layers first, as rasterize_active_text_metadata does for layer transforms. Add an engine test per command and an e2e test (type layer + crop + text.apply shows no jump).
findings.verdict_reason: I found no mention of text_spec, vector_scene or vector_view anywhere in the geometry region of mod.rs (lines 24860-26800). resample_document (25177) and reframe_document (25410) remap or resample only the pixels. Reframe sets ox/oy to 0 for non-raster layers, and resample scales them. Only kind 7 gets map_smart_link. render_vector (5423) keys its cache on (self.w, self.h, view), and composite calls ensure_vector on every layer (7803). When the canvas size changes, the scene is re-rasterised with the unchanged vector_view (5406: rotation about the new centre, no scale). Type: applyTextSpec (app.ts:2920) re-rasterises from the spec's ax/ay, and set_text_layer_spec zeroes the plane first. Neither runGeometryEdit (app.ts:3496) nor EngineClient.afterDocChange re-anchors the spec. text.updateAll (app.ts:3170) therefore snaps every type layer back. No engine or e2e test combines type or vector layers with these commands. One correction: flip, rotate 180°, and rotate 90° on a square canvas keep w and h, so the cache still hits. There the vector reverts only on the next invalidation, not 'at once'.

findings.title: MCP adj.brightnessContrast, adj.vibrance and adj.threshold pass Photoshop-scale values straight to kernels that expect 0..1 fractions, so results blow out to white, full saturation or black
findings.feature: MCP adj.brightnessContrast / adj.vibrance / adj.threshold
findings.evidence: commands.ts:617 `applied(() => adj.brightnessContrast(brightness, contrast))`, documented as -150..150 / -100..100 (the manifest schema enforces those ranges). The engine adds the brightness to a 0..1 channel (adjust.rs:47-56), and the dialog divides by 100 first (brightnessContrast.ts:38 brightnessContrastArgs). vibrance (commands.ts:706) is documented -100..100, while adjust.rs:429 computes `s + vib*(1-s) + sat` (the dialog uses vibranceArgs /100). threshold (commands.ts:788) is documented 0..255, while adjust.rs:522 compares 0..1 luma with `level` (the dialog uses thresholdFraction /255). hueSaturation in the same file does normalise, so the MCP surface is inconsistent with itself. commands.test.ts:197 and handlers.test.ts:210 assert the raw pass-through, and e2e/adjustments.spec.ts only checks that the composite changed.
findings.repro: From an MCP client: adj.brightnessContrast {brightness: 20, contrast: 10} turns the layer solid white. adj.threshold {level: 128} turns it solid black. adj.vibrance {vibrance: 30, saturation: 0} saturates every pixel fully.
findings.impact: An agent driving Vision gets destroyed images from in-schema values and reports 'Applied …'. This silently breaks the MCP adjustment workflow.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise in the wrappers with the existing helpers: brightnessContrastArgs({brightness, contrast}), vibranceArgs({vibrance, saturation}), thresholdFraction(level). Update commands.test.ts and handlers.test.ts to expect the normalised arguments, and add a pixel-level assertion (for example, B/C 20 leaves mid-gray below 0.8).
findings.verdict_reason: commands.ts:617, 706 and 788 pass their raw arguments to adj.* (app.ts:1008, 1018, 1027). Those call E().adjust_* directly, and the adjust_* entry points (mod.rs:22801, 22890, 22913) pass them unchanged to adjust.rs. brightness_contrast adds brightness to 0..1 channels (adjust.rs:47-55), vibrance computes s + vib*(1-s) + sat (adjust.rs:429), and threshold compares 0..1 luma with level (adjust.rs:522). The dialogs normalise instead: brightnessContrastArgs and vibranceArgs divide by 100 (brightnessContrast.ts:38, vibrance.ts:86), and thresholdFraction divides by 255. Dialogs.tsx:708, 1172 and 3132 use them. hueSaturation in the same file does normalise, through packHueSaturation. handlers.test.ts:210-220 and commands.test.ts:197 assert the raw pass-through.

findings.title: Auto Tone, Auto Contrast and Auto Color ignore the selection, Lock Image Pixels, the targeted mask and the layer kind, and cut 16-bit layers down to 8-bit precision
findings.feature: Image ▸ Auto Tone / Auto Contrast / Auto Color
findings.evidence: auto_stretch (mod.rs:23214) and auto_color (22952) bypass apply16. Their only guards are refuse_locked_transform (Lock All only) and reject_legacy_float_edit. They loop over every pixel of the plane with no selection coverage; auto_color even computes plane_local_selection and discards it (`let Some(_) = ...`). They never check painting_mask(), lock_image or refuse_destructive_edit (text, smart object, vector, adjustment or fill layers). Every sample is quantised through `(px >> 8)` … `nv * 257`, which snaps a 16-bit layer onto the 8-bit grid. Tests cover only the whole-layer stretch, undo and oversized planes (mod.rs:48404-48701, 77206, 75315); none uses a selection, a 16-bit document or a mask.
findings.repro: 1) Marquee part of a photo, then press ⇧⌘L: the whole layer changes. 2) Image ▸ Mode ▸ 16 Bits/Channel on a smooth gradient, then Auto Tone: the gradient bands to 256 levels. 3) Click a layer-mask thumbnail, then Auto Color: the artwork changes, not the mask. 4) On a type or smart-object layer, Auto Tone bakes into pixels that the next re-render discards.
findings.impact: A one-keystroke command edits outside the selection, destroys 16-bit precision, and edits locked or non-pixel layers. Photoshop honours all of these.
findings.suggested_fix: Route the per-pixel remap through apply16 (which already handles the mask target, locks, layer kinds, float refusal and selection coverage). Compute the histogram from selected, opaque pixels. Build a 65536-entry (or float) stretch instead of shifting to 8 bits. Add engine tests for selection clipping and 16-bit precision.
findings.verdict_reason: auto_stretch (mod.rs:23214) and auto_color (22952) guard only with refuse_locked_transform, which checks .locked alone (3847), and reject_legacy_float_edit. Neither calls painting_mask(), checks lock_image, or calls refuse_destructive_edit (3890). auto_color discards the result of plane_local_selection() (`let Some(_)`), and both loops run over every pixel with no coverage. Every channel is binned through `>>8` and written back as `nv*257`, which puts 16-bit data on the 8-bit grid. app.ts:1022-1024 call the engine directly, and menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434) doesn't gate autotone, autocontrast or autocolor. apply16 (4694) has every guard these functions are missing.

findings.title: In a Grayscale (or CMYK) document, colour can still be painted and displayed, but Gray/CMYK exports drop it
findings.feature: Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale / CMYK Color
findings.evidence: convert_grayscale (mod.rs:9084) greys the pixels, smart sources and fill colours once and sets mode = 1. Nothing enforces gray afterwards: set_brush (17063) and store.pushBrush pass RGB colours through; layer-effect colours and adjustment-layer parameters (Color Balance, Photo Filter, Gradient Map, Hue/Sat colorize) are neither converted nor clamped; active_blend_space (7762) is the only mode-aware composite code. psd_color_mode (30300) writes a Gray PSD, and Photoshop Raw / JPEG 2000 write one channel for mode 1 (mod.rs:29996, 30005; app.ts:8117). set_mode(2) likewise re-separates pixels only once.
findings.repro: Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale, pick red, paint a stroke (or add a red Drop Shadow, or a Photo Filter adjustment layer). The canvas shows red while the title/menu says Grayscale and Channels/Histogram show one Gray plate. Save as PSD: the red is gone.
findings.impact: The document looks different on screen than in the exported file. Colour work in a Gray document is silently lost on export. Photoshop never lets a Gray document hold colour.
findings.suggested_fix: While mode is 1, convert the foreground and background colours (and fills, pastes, placed images) to luma when they are pushed to the engine. On conversion, either convert or rasterise colour effects and adjustment layers, or prompt to flatten like Photoshop. At minimum, composite through the mode's plates (for example, map output to luma for mode 1) so the screen matches the export.
findings.verdict_reason: The Grayscale half holds. convert_grayscale (mod.rs:9084) greys the pixels once and sets mode = 1. set_brush (17063) stores the RGB colour as given. store.setForeground and pushBrush (store.ts:2878, 2898) never coerce colour by mode, and EngineClient has no mode-aware display path. The only mode-dependent composite code is active_blend_space (7762). psd_color_mode (30301) writes a Gray PSD, and the JPEG 2000 and Photoshop Raw encoders take a single channel when mode == 1 (29996, 30005). So colour painted after the conversion shows on screen but exports as gray. The CMYK half is overstated: CMYK pixels are kept as RGB and separated at export, so painted colour is not dropped. It only drifts when it is out of gamut, which is a soft-proof concern, not loss.

findings.title: Image ▸ Trap erodes every dark region by the trap width
findings.feature: Image ▸ Trap…
findings.evidence: trap (mod.rs:27205-27252) replaces every pixel with the brightest-luma pixel within `radius`. That is a luminance Maximum filter over the whole layer. Photoshop's Trap spreads inks under adjacent inks and leaves black type on white paper untouched (no ink spreads from white). The engine test trap_spreads_light_into_dark (67981) asserts the erosion. Trap also ignores the selection, Lock Image Pixels and the layer kind (it checks `locked` only). It pushes a whole-stack undo before the plane check, is enabled in RGB documents, and is not in RECORDED_STORE_OPS.
findings.repro: New white document, 3 px black type (or a 3 px black line). Image ▸ Trap… with the default 2 px: the black strokes shrink by 2 px per side and mostly vanish.
findings.impact: A prepress command visibly destroys fine dark detail. It is undoable, but the result is simply wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Model it on plates: in CMYK, spread each lighter ink plate under the neighbouring darker ink, and leave RGB composite pixels where one side has no ink. Or restrict Trap to CMYK documents and disable it otherwise. Honour the selection and use refuse_destructive_edit. Fix the test's expectation.
findings.verdict_reason: trap (mod.rs:27205-27252) replaces each pixel with the highest-luma pixel within a square of the given radius, which is a luminance dilation. A black stroke 3 px wide therefore disappears at radius 2, and the engine test trap_spreads_light_into_dark (67981) asserts exactly this erosion. The only guard is `.locked`: there is no selection, lock_image or layer-kind check. The stack undo is pushed before the active_plane_dims check. Nothing gates the command in RGB documents: the menu opens the dialog (App.tsx:3290), which calls store.trap (store.ts:7473), and store.trap is not in RECORDED_STORE_OPS. The code comment admits it is an 'RGB approximation', but the approximation is visually destructive, unlike ink trapping.

findings.title: Apply Image, Match Color, HDR Toning and Trap skip apply16's guards: Lock Image Pixels and the targeted mask are ignored, some refusals are silent, and Apply Image bakes into type layers
findings.feature: Image ▸ Apply Image / Adjustments ▸ Match Color / HDR Toning / Trap
findings.evidence: apply_image_channel (12916) returns silently for locked, smart-object (7) or vector (3) layers, with no last_edit_error. It accepts type layers (kind 2; the next re-type erases the result), ignores lock_image and never checks painting_mask. match_color (23143) and hdr_toning_pro (23058) return silently when `locked || kind != 0` and ignore lock_image and the mask target. hdr_toning_pro also ignores the selection. trap (27206) checks `locked` only. apply16 (4694) and refuse_destructive_edit (3895) already implement the correct, loud refusal.
findings.repro: Lock Image Pixels on a layer, then Image ▸ Apply Image or Adjustments ▸ HDR Toning: the pixels change. Target a type layer and run Match Color: the preview does nothing, OK closes the dialog, and no message is shown.
findings.impact: Locks are not honoured. Mask-targeted edits land on the artwork. Refused dialogs look broken, and MCP applied() cannot report the reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Call refuse_destructive_edit(), and branch on painting_mask() like apply16 does, at the top of each op. Set last_edit_error on every refusal.
findings.verdict_reason: apply_image_channel (mod.rs:12916-12933) returns silently for locked layers and layers of kind 7 or 3, without setting last_edit_error. It accepts kind 2 and checks neither lock_image nor painting_mask. match_color (23143) and hdr_toning_pro (around 23058) return silently on `locked || kind != 0` and check neither lock_image nor the mask target. hdr_toning_pro processes the whole plane with no selection coverage. trap checks `.locked` only. refuse_destructive_edit (3890) and apply16 (4694) implement the loud refusal and the mask branch these functions lack.

findings.title: Guides, notes and colour samplers are not remapped after Rotate, Flip Canvas, Trim or Reveal All; count markers and the ruler line are never remapped
findings.feature: Image ▸ Image Rotation / Trim / Reveal All (document annotations)
findings.evidence: xformImpl only passes `annotations` to runGeometryEdit for resizeImage, resizeCanvas and crop (app.ts:3532-3541). rotate90, rotate180, rotateArbitrary, revealAll and trim pass none, and flipH/flipV bypass runGeometryEdit (3546-3551). remapDocSpaceAnnotations (store.ts:3560) handles guides, notes and colorSamplers, but not countPoints or rulerLine (store.ts:1115-1116), so even Image Size and Crop leave count markers and the ruler line behind.
findings.repro: Add a vertical guide at x=100 and a note. Image ▸ Image Rotation ▸ 90° CW: the guide stays vertical at x=100 and the note stays put, while the pixels rotate. Trim away a top border: guides and notes are off by the trimmed amount.
findings.impact: Layout aids and annotations end up detached from the content they marked.
findings.suggested_fix: Give remapDocSpaceAnnotations a general affine map (translate, scale, 90/180 rotation, flip) and call it from every canvas-geometry command, including countPoints and rulerLine. For Trim and Reveal All, return the origin shift from the engine.
findings.verdict_reason: In xformImpl (app.ts:3532-3553), only resizeImage, resizeCanvas, resizeCanvasFilled, crop and cropToSelection pass an `annotations` argument to runGeometryEdit. revealAll, trim, rotate90, rotate180 and rotateArbitrary pass none. flipH and flipV call the engine directly. remapDocSpaceAnnotations (store.ts:3560-3574) remaps only guides, notes and colorSamplers, never countPoints or rulerLine.

findings.title: Count markers, the ruler line, colour samplers and the Measurement Log are app-global, not per document
findings.feature: Image ▸ Analysis (Count / Ruler / Color Sampler / Record Measurements)
findings.evidence: countPoints, rulerLine, colorSamplers and measurements live in AppSnapshot (store.ts:1115-1133). activateDoc (6177-6216) swaps notes, guides and measureScale per document but not these, and nothing resets them on New/Open/Close (they are only cleared at store.ts:3704 and 4250 by explicit Clear).
findings.repro: Put 5 count markers on document A, switch to document B, then Image ▸ Analysis ▸ Record Measurements. The log records count 5 for B, and A's markers and samplers are drawn and read on B.
findings.impact: Measurements and Info readouts are wrong across tabs, which defeats the analysis workflow.
findings.suggested_fix: Move these four fields into the per-document entry, alongside notes and guides, and swap them in activateDoc/addDoc.
findings.verdict_reason: activateDoc (store.ts:6177-6220) swaps notes, guides and measureScale per document, but not rulerLine, countPoints, colorSamplers or measurements. The only writes to these fields are the initial state (1582-1594) and explicit add or clear calls (3692-3725, 4250, 4294-4297), so they carry across tabs. One caveat: Photoshop's own Measurement Log is also app-wide (it has a Document column), so the real defect is count markers, the ruler line and colour samplers leaking between documents.

findings.title: The Image Size and Canvas Size fields are capped at 8192 px even though documents can be 32767 px, and Image Size neither scales layer styles nor offers resolution-only resizing
findings.feature: Image ▸ Image Size… / Canvas Size…
findings.evidence: ImageSize: `max = ... imageSizeFromPixels(8192, ...)` (Dialogs.tsx:5868). CanvasSize: `fieldMax = convertDocumentLength(8192, ...)` (10289). NumberField clamps on commit (monet-react controls.tsx `commit(round(clamp(n)))`), while canvasSizeFits and the engine allow 32767 px / 80 MP (docPresets.ts:11-12). resample_document (mod.rs:25177) never scales effects (Photoshop defaults 'Scale Styles' on), and the dialog has no Resample checkbox or Resolution field.
findings.repro: Open a 9504×6336 photo. Image Size ▸ Width 9000: it commits as 8192. Pressing ArrowUp from 9504 also jumps to 8192. Canvas Size absolute width 10000 on a 9000 px image: it becomes 8192 and crops the image. Downsizing to 50% leaves drop shadows at their old pixel size, so they look twice as large.
findings.impact: High-resolution camera files can't be sized precisely, a Canvas Size edit can crop unexpectedly, and layer styles look wrong after resampling.
findings.suggested_fix: Use MAX_DOCUMENT_DIMENSION_PX for the field caps. Scale effect parameters in resample_document (reuse store.scaleEffects' math) or add a Scale Styles option. Add Resample off (change ppi only) to the dialog.
findings.verdict_reason: Dialogs.tsx:5868 sets `max = imageSizeFromPixels(8192, ...)` and 10289 sets `fieldMax = convertDocumentLength(8192, ...)`, and both are passed as max to NumberField (5881/5885, 10328/10335). NumberField clamps every commit to [min, max] (monet-react controls.tsx:398-403). Meanwhile MAX_DOCUMENT_DIMENSION_PX is 32_767 (docPresets.ts:11). resample_document (mod.rs:25177-25300) never touches layer effects, and the dialog has no Resample or resolution-only option.

findings.title: Histogram CMYK and Lab channels come out combed (only 101 of 256 bins used) and differ from the engine's plates; the histogram also ignores the selection
findings.feature: Histogram panel (per mode)
findings.evidence: channelCounts uses rgbToCmyk (which rounds to integer 0-100%) and rgbToLab (which rounds L to an integer), then scales ×2.55, so only about 101 bins are ever populated. The engine's plates use the ink-limited model or the document's Convert-to-Profile ICC (plates_of / doc_plates_of, mod.rs:4320-4424); the Channels panel and Info use those, the histogram does not. EngineClient.channelHistogram reads the whole composite regardless of selection.
findings.repro: Image ▸ Mode ▸ CMYK Color, then look at Histogram ▸ Cyan (or Lab ▸ Lightness) on a smooth gradient: a comb with regular gaps. A saturated dark colour shows C/M/Y values different from the Channels panel's plates.
findings.impact: The histogram suggests posterisation that isn't there, and its statistics don't match the plates.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute CMYK and Lab histograms from the engine's plate separation (a separate_plates readback) at full precision, or at least stop rounding before binning. Respect the active selection, as Photoshop does.
findings.verdict_reason: The data claims hold, but the visible comb is refuted. channelCounts (channelHistogram.ts:63-83) bins rgbToCmyk and rgbToLab output after rounding to integer percent or integer L*, so only about 101 of the 256 levels are populated. rgbToCmyk (rgbCmyk.ts) is the naive k = 1 - max model, not the engine's ink-limited or ICC plates. EngineClient.channelHistogram (862) reads the whole output buffer, ignoring the selection. However, the panel draws downsampleBins(counts, 48) (Panels.tsx:1477, 1483), so each drawn bar covers about 5 levels and the curve shows no comb. The gaps appear only in the per-level hover readout and slightly in the statistics. The Levels and Curves histograms use only the luma and R/G/B channels.

findings.title: Converting 32-bit to 16 or 8 bits clips HDR values silently, with no tone mapping or warning
findings.feature: Image ▸ Mode ▸ 16/8 Bits/Channel (from 32-bit)
