findings.evidence: set_depth (8159) maps pixels_f32 through float_preview_u16, which is `value.clamp(0.0, 1.0)` (mod.rs:2704), or through clamp×255 for 8-bit. has_hdr_samples exists, but only the import path uses it (EngineClient.ts:370). App.tsx:2803 claims 'Image ▸ Mode do the tone mapping Photoshop offers', but set_depth does not; the View ▸ 32-bit Preview exposure the user is looking at is display-only and is not baked in.
findings.repro: File ▸ Automate ▸ Merge to HDR Pro (32-bit radiance), then Image ▸ Mode ▸ 16 Bits/Channel. Every highlight above 1.0 is clipped flat, and the image no longer matches the 32-bit preview.
findings.impact: HDR highlight detail is lost silently (undoable). Photoshop opens its HDR Toning dialog for this conversion.
findings.suggested_fix: When has_hdr_samples() is true, prompt with HDR Toning (or the current 32-bit Preview exposure/gamma), or at least warn and offer Cancel before clipping.
findings.verdict_reason: set_depth (mod.rs:8159-8215) maps pixels_f32 and smart_src_f32 through float_preview_u16 (which is value.clamp(0, 1), line 2704) or through clamp × 255 for 8-bit, with no tone map. store.setDepth (store.ts:8174) and the d8/d16 menu actions (App.tsx:2779-2780) call it directly. has_hdr_samples is used only at EngineClient.ts:370 on import. The App.tsx:2803-2806 comment claiming 'Image ▸ Mode do the tone mapping' does not match the code. The change is undoable.

findings.title: Color Table is enabled in RGB documents, where Apply re-indexes the image to the first 256 colours in scan order
findings.feature: Image ▸ Mode ▸ Color Table…
findings.evidence: colorTableHexes (app.ts:4053) falls back to EngineClient.colorTable(256) (EngineClient.ts:844-856), which takes the first 256 distinct colours scanning from the top-left, i.e. mostly the image's top rows. ColorTable Apply (Dialogs.tsx:3828) calls convertIndexed(..., palette 7 Custom, table, original), which flattens and quantises every pixel to that arbitrary table. menuEnablement doesn't gate 'colortable', and there is no Indexed checkmark (psMenus.ts:201-203 only knows modes 0-4 and duotone).
findings.repro: Open a photo with a blue sky, Image ▸ Mode ▸ Color Table…, Apply: the whole photo is quantised mostly to sky colours.
findings.impact: A one-click destructive result with poor quality (undoable). Photoshop only enables Color Table for Indexed images.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable colortable unless indexed_palette_rgb() is non-empty (or the document is Duotone), or build an Adaptive palette when it isn't. Also show an Indexed/Bitmap checkmark in Image ▸ Mode.
findings.verdict_reason: When indexed_palette_rgb() is empty, colorTableHexes (app.ts:4053) falls back to engine.colorTable(256). That function (EngineClient.ts:844-856) collects the first 256 distinct opaque colours in raster order. The ColorTable Apply button (Dialogs.tsx:3828) calls store.convertIndexed(..., 7, ..., table, original), which quantises the whole flattened image to that table. menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3468) doesn't gate colortable, and imageModeCheckedIds (psMenus.ts:201-203) has no Indexed entry. The dialog does label the list as 'distinct colors in the image' and shows a flatten notice, which softens but doesn't fix the problem.

findings.title: Place Scale Marker clears the user's selection and makes several history steps, and a recorded action replays it incompletely
findings.feature: Image ▸ Analysis ▸ Place Scale Marker…
findings.evidence: placeScaleMarker calls store.addLayer() (recorded), then E().set_layer_name, E().select_rect, E().fill_selection and E().select_none (not recorded, and they discard the existing selection), then text.create (recorded).
findings.repro: Make a selection, then Place Scale Marker…, OK: the selection is gone and the History panel shows about 5 steps. Record it in an action and play it back: you get an empty layer plus the caption, with no bar.
findings.impact: Selection lost, a cluttered history, and a broken action.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the command in begin/commit_history_transaction. Save and restore the selection mask (or fill the bar without using the selection). Record it as a single op, placeScaleMarker(len, caption).
findings.verdict_reason: placeScaleMarker (app.ts:7886-7901) calls store.addLayer (recorded) and then, directly on the engine, set_layer_name, select_rect, fill_selection and select_none. That replaces and then clears the user's selection, and nothing wraps it in a transaction. The caption goes through text.create, which is createTextLayer (3058): another recorded store.addLayer plus an unrecorded applyTextSpec. One correction to the repro: replay yields two empty layers (the caption is not recorded either), not 'an empty layer plus the caption'.

findings.title: Calculations ▸ Result ▸ New Channel overwrites the current selection
findings.feature: Image ▸ Calculations…
findings.evidence: The Calculations dialog's apply runs store.calculations (which writes the selection) and then saveSelection(chanName). The ponytail comment admits the selection is replaced. calculations_mask already returns the plane without touching the selection.
findings.repro: Make a selection, then Image ▸ Calculations… with Result: New Channel. The channel is created, but the original selection has been replaced by the blend.
findings.impact: The user's selection is lost (Undo gets it back).
findings.suggested_fix: For 'channel', call calculations_mask and store the result directly as a saved alpha channel (there is already a saved-selection store). Don't call calculations().
findings.verdict_reason: For Result: New Channel, apply (Dialogs.tsx:6615-6628) calls store.calculations, which writes the result into the engine selection (store.ts:9756-9759), and then calls saveSelection. The in-code ponytail comment (6623-6625) admits the selection is replaced. calculations_mask already exists and is used for the New Document path (store.ts:9764) without touching the selection. Undo recovers the selection.

findings.title: Duotone, Trap, Duplicate Image and Merge to HDR don't record as single action steps
findings.feature: Actions recording for Image menu
findings.evidence: RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:904-950) lists convertGrayscale, convertIndexed, convertBitmap, setColorMode and setDepth, but not convertDuotone, trap or duplicateDocument. store.convertDuotone therefore records its nested convertGrayscale plus addAdjustmentLayer / setAdjustmentParams(layerId) as separate top-level steps, and the layerId is document-specific. exposureFusion (app.ts:1791) is a plain function with no rec().
findings.repro: Start recording, Image ▸ Mode ▸ Duotone… (re-ink an existing duotone), Trap…, Duplicate…. The action has no Trap or Duplicate step, and its Duotone step targets a stale layer id.
findings.impact: Macros miss steps that Photoshop records.
findings.suggested_fix: Add convertDuotone, trap and duplicateDocument to RECORDED_STORE_OPS. Wrap exposureFusion with rec(), or move it into a proxied namespace.
findings.verdict_reason: RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:903-950) contains none of convertDuotone, trap or duplicateDocument. Because the list wraps the live instance methods, store.convertDuotone (store.ts:7957-7987) records its inner calls as separate steps. The first conversion records convertGrayscale and addAdjustmentLayer; a re-ink records setAdjustmentParams with the document-specific layer id. The Duplicate dialog calls store.duplicateDocument (Dialogs.tsx:5736), and nothing records it. exposureFusion (app.ts:1791) is a plain function with no rec().

findings.title: Measurement Log heading shows the current unit, but older rows were computed with the scale in effect when recorded
findings.feature: Image ▸ Analysis ▸ Record Measurements / Measurement Log
findings.evidence: MeasurementRows labels the column `Length ({unit})` from the live measureScale, but each entry's lengthUnits was frozen at record time (store.ts:4283-4294).
findings.repro: Record with the scale in mm, change Set Measurement Scale to inches: the old mm values now appear under 'Length (in)'.
findings.impact: Mislabelled data.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the unit (or the scale) on each entry and show it per row, or recompute from lengthPx.
findings.verdict_reason: MeasurementRows (Dialogs.tsx:4932-4952) labels the column `Length ({unit})` from the live measureScale.unit. recordMeasurement (store.ts:4283-4294) freezes lengthUnits using the scale at record time and stores no unit on the entry.

findings.title: Posterize dialog caps Levels at 32 (Photoshop and the engine allow 2-255); Apply Data Set is enabled with no data sets and does nothing
findings.feature: Image ▸ Adjustments ▸ Posterize / Image ▸ Apply Data Set
findings.evidence: `<Row label="Levels" ... max={32}>` while POSTERIZE_MAX = 255 (posterize.ts:17). applydataset (App.tsx:2976) calls dataVars.apply(activeDataSet), which returns false silently when `sets[index]` is undefined (app.ts:5421), and the menu is not gated.
findings.repro: Try to posterize to 64 levels: it isn't possible. Choose Image ▸ Apply Data Set… in a document with no variables: nothing happens and there is no message.
findings.impact: Minor parity/UX gaps.
findings.suggested_fix: Use POSTERIZE_MAX for the slider. Disable applydataset when store.state.dataSets is empty, or show a notice.
findings.verdict_reason: The Posterize dialog uses `<Row ... min={POSTERIZE_MIN} max={32}>` (Dialogs.tsx:3125), while POSTERIZE_MAX = 255 (posterize.ts:17). The applydataset menu action (App.tsx:2976) calls dataVars.apply(activeDataSet), which returns false silently when `sets[index]` is undefined (app.ts:5421). menuEnablement doesn't gate the command.

areas.coverage:
I reviewed the code only. I did not run any builds, test suites or the app, and I did not edit the repo.

Inventory, taken from psMenuData.ts, psMenus.ts and the App.tsx menuActions:
- The in-scope Layer menu items total 69. 56 are wired and 13 are disabled.
- The 56 wired items: New 10/10, Duplicate/Delete/Rename/Auto-Name/Layer Cleanup 5, Group/Ungroup/Hide 3, Arrange 5/5, Align 6/6, Distribute 8/8, Lock Layers/Link/Select Linked 3, Merge Down/Merge Visible/Flatten 3, Rasterize 8/9 (Fill Content is wired through LABEL_WIRING), New Layer Based Slice 1, Matting 4/4.
- The 13 disabled items are the 12 Video Layers entries and Rasterize ▸ Video.
- Layers panel: 9 footer buttons, 11 context-menu entries plus Panel Options, 4 lock toggles, and the filter bar (Kind 6, Attribute 8, Mode, Effect, 7 color swatches, name search).
- Layers panel gestures: drag reorder and reparent, inline rename, dragging a thumbnail out as PNG, ⌘-clicking a thumbnail, mask-thumbnail modifier clicks, and ⌥-clicking the boundary between two rows to toggle a clipping mask.
- Layer Comps panel: New, previous/next, Restore Last Document State, apply, options, update, delete, plus the Layer Comps to Files and to PDF exports.
- Dialogs: NewLayer, NewGroup, DuplicateLayer, RenameLayer, LockLayers, NewArtboard, Defringe.
- MCP surface: only doc.addLayer and layer.cleanup are direct commands. The other structure operations can be reached only through script.run, which exposes the RECORDED_STORE_OPS allowlist.

Tracing:
- Each wired item was traced through App.tsx to store.ts (plus the app.ts text/smart namespaces) to the engine functions in packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs.
- Engine functions covered: add/delete/duplicate_layer, layer_via_copy/cut, group_layers, create_group, ungroup, arrange_layer, move_layer_in_tree, reverse_layers, align_layer(s), distribute_layers, shift_layer, bake_offset, link/unlink/linked_layers, set_layer_locked/locks, merge_down, merge_visible, flatten, rasterize_*, new_artboard, artboard_from_*, new_frame, defringe, remove_matte, apply_layer_comp, the push_*_undo snapshot family, render_vector, and composite plan building.
- For each I checked undo, locks, the selection, 16/32-bit handling, and the no-document state.

Tests: I grepped the unit and e2e tests for each feature. No tests at all exist for Reverse, Rasterize ▸ Layer / All Layers, Select Linked Layers, Artboard from Group, or New Layer Based Slice.

Not reviewed:
- Runtime memory ceilings. The out-of-memory threshold in finding 1 is calculated, not measured.
- WKWebView and native macOS menu behaviour.
- Compositor pixel correctness beyond the functions listed above.
- Smart Object and Layer Style internals, and the Move tool, which belong to other areas. I only noted where the Move tool shares a root cause with a finding here.
areas.parity_notes:
These items are shown disabled, which is correct, so they are not reported as bugs: Layer ▸ Video Layers (0 of 12 implemented) and Rasterize ▸ Video.

Photoshop parity gaps noticed in this area that are not filed as findings:
- There is no Layer Properties… dialog; inline rename plus the Color Label submenu cover it.
- There is no Merge Layers or Merge Group. Finding 6 covers this.
- There is no 'Delete Group and Contents / Group Only' prompt.
- There is no Align Layers to Selection: the single-layer align always aligns to the canvas.
- ⌥-clicking the eye does not solo a layer, and dragging across eye icons does not toggle several layers.
- Dragging in the Layers panel moves only the dragged row, not the whole multi-selection.
- Opacity, Fill and blend-mode changes apply only to the active layer, not to all selected layers.
- Locking a group does not lock its children: engine lock checks look only at the active layer.
- The Duplicate Layer dialog has no Destination document option.
- The New Layer dialog has no 'Use Previous Layer to Create Clipping Mask' option.
- Hide Layers never relabels itself to 'Show Layers'.
- The Layers attribute filter's 'Locked' option matches only Lock All, not partial locks.
- Indexed and Bitmap documents allow extra layers (Photoshop does not), and nothing enforces the palette.

MCP versus menu:
- The only direct MCP tools for layer structure are doc.addLayer and layer.cleanup.
- Delete, duplicate, merge, group, reorder, rename, visibility, lock, align and distribute can be reached only through script.run, which accepts the RECORDED_STORE_OPS allowlist.
- setLayerLocks, the artboard and rasterize operations, and slices are not on that allowlist, so MCP cannot reach them at all.

Shortcut versus menu:
- Two items carry ⌘G: Layer ▸ New ▸ Group… and Group Layers. shortcutCommandMap deliberately lets the later one (Group Layers) win, so this is intended.
- The Distribute ▸ Horizontal/Vertical menu items do not match the options-bar Spacing buttons. Finding 11 covers this.

For another reviewer:
- The Move tool's commit_offset calls bake_offset, which for kind-3 shape layers remaps only the cached pixels, not vector_view or the scene (mod.rs:16896-16908).
- So Move-tool drags of shape layers probably snap back after a reload or scene edit. This is the same root cause as finding 2 and belongs to whoever reviews the Move tool and shapes. I did not trace that path end to end, so confidence is medium.
- Engine MAX_LAYERS (4096) is enforced only when loading a project, not when creating layers (mod.rs:1051, 31249). This matters only for tiny canvases, so I did not file it.

findings.title: Structural edits snapshot every layer's full pixel plane into history; pixel-less layers also allocate full planes, so memory can run out on real-size photos
findings.feature: Layer structure undo / layer limits (New, Delete, Duplicate, Rename, Lock, Visibility, Opacity, Blend, Group, Reorder, Link, Merge)
findings.evidence: push_stack_undo (mod.rs:5692) builds Snap::Stack(doc_snap()). doc_snap (mod.rs:5505) deep-clones every Layer, including its Vec<u16> pixels (Layer.pixels at mod.rs:179). The history cap is 50 states (UNDO_CAP mod.rs:989, store.ts:1403) and there is no byte budget (push_undo mod.rs:5737 trims by count only). set_layer_name (16551), set_layer_locked (11038), set_layer_locks (11058), set_layer_visible (10710), set_layer_blend (10745) and set_layer_opacity (through push_prop_undo, 5771) all push a full-document snapshot even though they change metadata only. Visibility with undo turned off still clones and then drops (store.ts withoutHistoryStep). Layer::transparent (mod.rs:384) allocates w*h*4 u16 for group headers (create_group 13481, group_layers 13505), artboards and adjustment layers (14975). The App.tsx loops push one snapshot per layer: del (App.tsx:2850), Hide Layers (App.tsx:2897), and the Lock Layers dialog (Dialogs.tsx:6519-6521, two snapshots per layer). All documents share one wasm32 heap (EngineClient.ts:342).
findings.repro: Open a 6000x4000 photo (192 MB per layer at 16-bit RGBA). Add three layers, then rename, lock or reorder layers about 8–10 times. Alternatively, Select ▸ All Layers on a 20-layer document and press Delete. Watch the growth of the engine's wasm memory.buffer.byteLength.
findings.impact: Each metadata-only change costs a full copy of the document, so a 24 MP document with a few layers passes the 4 GB wasm32 address space within a handful of edits. When allocation fails the engine traps (default allocator, no try_reserve), the document stops working and unsaved work is at risk. Even when it does not trap, every eye/lock/rename click memcpys hundreds of MB.
findings.suggested_fix: Make structural snapshots copy-on-write: store layer planes as Arc<Vec<u16>> (or Arc<[u16]>) so DocSnap shares untouched planes and rename/lock/visibility/reorder cost O(layers), not O(pixels). Give groups, adjustment layers and artboard headers zero-length planes. Add an undo byte budget that evicts the oldest states. Wrap the multi-layer loops in a single beginHistory/commitHistory transaction.
findings.verdict_reason: Every step checks out. push_stack_undo (mod.rs:5692) wraps doc_snap (mod.rs:5505), which clones each Layer including `pixels: Vec<u16>` (mod.rs:179; it only drops mask_soft). push_undo (5737) trims by count only (UNDO_CAP 50 at mod.rs:989, default 50 at store.ts:1403). No byte budget, try_reserve or custom allocator exists anywhere in packages/engine. These metadata-only setters all call push_stack_undo: set_layer_visible 10710, set_layer_blend 10745, set_layer_locked 11038, set_layer_locks 11058 and set_layer_name 16551; set_layer_opacity 10727 goes through push_prop_undo. Group headers (13481/13505) and adjustment layers (14975) use Layer::transparent (mod.rs:384), which allocates w*h*4 u16. withoutHistoryStep (store.ts:7673) still clones the whole document before dropping the step. The loops App.tsx:2850 and 2897 and Dialogs.tsx:6519-6521 push one snapshot per layer. All engines share one wasm heap (EngineClient.ts:342). Example: a 24 MP document with 3 layers costs about 576 MB per snapshot, so a handful of renames or lock toggles passes 4 GB. The problem is broader than structural edits: LayerPx snapshots also clone a full layer on every paint stroke, so the missing byte budget is the root cause. An OOM abort traps the wasm call and leaves that document unusable. I kept it at blocker.

findings.title: Align and Distribute move only the cached raster of type, shape and Smart Object layers; the layer snaps back on the next re-render or reload
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Align / Distribute, and the Move tool options-bar align buttons
findings.evidence: shift_layer (mod.rs:10021) updates pixel_bounds only for kind 0. Every other kind goes to shift_layer_plane_contents (10047), which remaps `pixels` alone. It does not update the text spec (the next text.apply re-rasterizes at spec.x/y, app.ts:2920), the vector scene or vector_view (render_vector 5423 re-rasterizes from the scene whenever vector_cache_key is reset, and it is None after project load, mod.rs:31393, and after undo, 5588), or the smart transform (render_smart 5005). align_layer (9843), align_layers (10183) and distribute_layers (10088) all use shift_layer. CanvasView.tsx:2211-2220 documents this exact snap-back for text and works around it for the Move tool only. bake_offset (16896-16908) has the same pixels-only branch for kind 3, so Move-tool drags of shape layers look affected as well (outside this area, confidence medium).
findings.repro: Create a type layer or a Rectangle shape layer. Choose Layer ▸ Align ▸ Right Edges. Then edit the text, change the shape's fill, or save and reopen.
findings.impact: The layout work is silently lost: the layer returns to its pre-align position after a later edit or a reload.
findings.suggested_fix: In shift_layer, update the authoritative source for each kind: the text spec anchor (as CanvasView does), vector_view tx/ty (or translate the scene) with the cache invalidated, and append_smart_matrix for kind 7, as bake_offset already does for smart objects. Add engine tests that align a kind 2/3/7 layer, then re-render and reload.
findings.verdict_reason: shift_layer (mod.rs:10021) updates pixel_bounds only for kind 0. Every other kind goes to shift_layer_plane_contents (10047), which remaps `pixels` and the mask only. The text spec, vector_scene/vector_view and the smart transform are not touched. Vector: render_vector (5423) rebuilds pixels from the scene whenever vector_cache_key is None. That happens on any scene edit (15148-15693), on font registration (invalidate_vector_layers, 5478) and on load (the default is None, mod.rs:457). Text: applyTextSpec (app.ts:2918) re-rasterizes at spec ax/ay, and CanvasView.tsx:2211-2220 works around this for Move drags only. align_layer (9843), align_layers (10183) and distribute_layers/distribute_spacing (10088) all route through shift_layer. One nuance: type layers keep their stored pixels on reload, so they snap back on the next text edit rather than on reload.

findings.title: Multi-layer Align and Distribute move locked layers; Lock Position is enforced only by Move-tool drags
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Align / Distribute, Lock Layers (Position, All)
findings.evidence: align_layers (10183) and distribute_layers (10088) never check locked or lock_position before shift_layer. The single-layer align_layer (9843) calls refuse_locked_transform (3847), which checks only `.locked`, so Lock Position is ignored. The only lock_position check in the engine is move_layer_offset (16628). The flips, rotates and free transforms go through refuse_locked_transform too.
findings.repro: Select three layers, choose Lock All on the middle one, then choose Layer ▸ Align ▸ Left Edges or Distribute ▸ Horizontal Centers. Separately, set Lock Position on a layer and choose Layer ▸ Align ▸ Top Edges with only that layer selected.
findings.impact: Locked layers get moved, even though the lock is supposed to protect them; Photoshop skips locked layers here.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter out locked and lock_position layers in align_layers and distribute_layers (with an edit error when all are filtered). Make refuse_locked_transform also refuse on lock_position.
findings.verdict_reason: align_layers (10183), distribute_layers (10088) and distribute_spacing check only reject_document_float_edit, with no locked or lock_position test. refuse_locked_transform (3847) checks only `.locked`. The only engine lock_position checks are the setter/getter and move_layer_offset (16628). The app side has none either: store.alignLayer and store.distributeLayers call the engine directly (store.ts:7691, 2653), and a grep finds no position-lock check in apps/vision/src.

findings.title: Layer ▸ Arrange ▸ Reverse reverses the whole document and breaks clipping groups
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Arrange ▸ Reverse
findings.evidence: reverse_layers (mod.rs:9992) calls self.layers.reverse() on the entire stack. App.tsx:2902 calls store.reverseLayers() (store.ts:7791) with no selection and no enablement check. Clip bases are positional (clip_base_index 4109 searches below the layer), so after reversal each clipped layer sits below its base and renders unclipped or against the wrong base. No test covers Reverse.
findings.repro: Take a document with Background, a photo layer, and a Curves layer clipped to the photo. Select two layers and choose Layer ▸ Arrange ▸ Reverse.
findings.impact: The opaque Background ends up on top and hides everything, and clipped adjustments hit the wrong layers. Photoshop reverses only the selected layers (2 or more) and disables the command otherwise.
findings.suggested_fix: Take the selected ids, reverse only their slots among siblings of the same parent (keep each clip group together), and disable the command with fewer than 2 selected. Add an engine test and an e2e test.
findings.verdict_reason: reverse_layers (mod.rs:9992) calls self.layers.reverse() on the entire vec. App.tsx:2902 calls store.reverseLayers (store.ts:7791) without the selection, and menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3470) has no entry for it. clip_base_index (4109) searches only below the layer, so a clipped layer ends up above nothing, or clipped to a different base. Group headers, stored at the bottom of their span, also move to the top. One correction: an engine test does exist (reverse_layers_flips_the_stack, mod.rs:64552), but it asserts the whole-stack flip, which is the wrong behavior.

findings.title: Merge Down onto a hidden (or 0% opacity) layer replaces that layer's pixels with the upper layer's
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Merge Down (⌘E), Layers panel Merge Down
findings.evidence: merge_down (10440) composites [lower, upper] through composite_stack_px. composite_plan_item_px (6670) returns early for `!layer.visible || layer.opacity <= 0.0`, so a hidden lower layer adds nothing. The merged layer then takes lower.id and name with pixels = upper only, and `merged.visible = lower.visible || upper.visible` (10580) makes it visible. No visibility check exists before push_stack_undo. The panel enablement (Panels.tsx:614) checks only the stack position.
findings.repro: Paint on Layer 1, hide it, add Layer 2 above it with other content, select Layer 2 and press ⌘E.
findings.impact: Layer 1's content is gone and the merged layer shows only Layer 2's pixels. It can be undone, but it is silent. Photoshop refuses to merge into a hidden layer.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse with an edit error when the lower layer is hidden or at 0% opacity. Also decide how a hidden upper layer should be handled (refuse or discard explicitly). Add an engine test.
findings.verdict_reason: merge_down (10440-10600) has no visibility or opacity guard before push_stack_undo. composite_plan_item_px (6670-6672) returns acc for `!layer.visible || layer.opacity <= 0.0`, so a hidden lower layer contributes nothing. The merged layer takes lower.id and name with the composite (upper only) as its pixels and `visible = lower.visible || upper.visible` (10580). Panel and menu enablement check only the stack position (Panels.tsx:619/657). None of the merge_down tests (78132-78342) covers a hidden layer. It can be undone, but the loss is silent.

findings.title: ⌘E ignores the multi-layer selection and has no Merge Group; the error message points to a command that does not exist
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Merge Down (⌘E) with several layers or a group selected
findings.evidence: `merge: () => store.mergeDown(store.state.activeLayerId)` (App.tsx:3009). No Merge Layers or Merge Group exists anywhere (a grep of apps/vision/src and packages/engine/src finds nothing). merge_down on a group header sets 'Could not merge down a group header; merge the group first.' (mod.rs:10453), but nothing in the app can merge a group.
findings.repro: Shift-select layers A and C (not adjacent) and press ⌘E. Separately, select a group and press ⌘E.
findings.impact: With a multi-selection, the active layer is merged into whatever is below it, which may not be selected. With a group, the user gets an error telling them to use a command that isn't there. Photoshop's ⌘E becomes Merge Layers or Merge Group in these cases.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an engine merge_layers(ids) (composite the selected subtree into the bottom-most selected slot) and a merge_group(id). Have the `merge` handler dispatch on the selection count and the active layer's kind, and relabel the menu item the way Create/Release Clipping Mask already is.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:3009 is `merge: () => store.mergeDown(store.state.activeLayerId)`. A grep for merge_layers, mergeLayers, merge_group, mergeGroup, 'Merge Layers' and 'Merge Group' across apps/vision/src and packages/engine/src finds nothing. With a group header active, merge_down (mod.rs:10451-10455) sets 'Could not merge down a group header; merge the group first.', and commit() surfaces it as a toast. With a multi-selection, the active layer merges into whatever is directly below it.

findings.title: Merge Down refuses any non-Normal or adjustment upper layer unless the lower layer is the bottom of the document
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Merge Down
findings.evidence: `let mut has_backdrop = lower_i > 0;` (10484). Then `if has_backdrop && (lower.blend != Normal || upper.blend != Normal || … || upper.kind == 1 …)`, which sets 'Could not merge down because a layer depends on the backdrop.' (10498-10511). The engine test merge_down_refuses_a_backdrop_dependent_blend_before_undo shows the refusal is deliberate.
findings.repro: Background, then Layer 1 (paint), then Layer 2 set to Multiply (or a Curves adjustment layer). Select the top layer and press ⌘E.
findings.impact: Two common Photoshop workflows fail: merging shading or texture layers and merging adjustment layers into the layer below. They only work directly above the bottom layer.
findings.suggested_fix: Follow Photoshop: bake the upper layer onto the lower layer's pixels in isolation (lower keeps its mode). Or ask 'Merging will change the appearance — continue?' instead of refusing outright.
findings.verdict_reason: mod.rs:10474 sets `has_backdrop = lower_i > 0`. mod.rs:10498-10511 refuses when there is a backdrop and any of these hold: a non-Normal blend on either layer, blend_if, upper.kind == 1, or knockout. merge_down_refuses_a_backdrop_dependent_blend_before_undo (78240) shows the refusal is deliberate. The refusal is visible, not silent, but merging an adjustment layer or a Multiply or Overlay layer into the layer below fails everywhere except directly above the bottom layer.

findings.title: Rasterize ▸ Layer and Rasterize ▸ All Layers silently skip shape (vector) layers
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Rasterize ▸ Layer / All Layers
findings.evidence: rasterizelayer calls text.rasterizeLayer(id), smart.rasterize(id) and store.rasterizeFillLayer(id) (App.tsx:3019-3020). These handle kind 2 (rasterize_text_layer mod.rs:16060), kind 7 (16076) and kind 4 (store.ts:7904) only. Kind-3 vector layers, which the shape tools create (store.ts:7101), go only through store.rasterizeShape (7417), which these handlers never call. Each handler also issues three commits per layer. No tests cover either command.
findings.repro: Draw a Rectangle shape layer and choose Layer ▸ Rasterize ▸ Layer (or All Layers).
findings.impact: Nothing happens and no message is shown, so the most common rasterize target stays a vector layer.
findings.suggested_fix: Dispatch on layer_kind: 3 goes to rasterize_vector_layer, 2 to text, 7 to smart, 4 to fill (and rasterize any vector mask). For All Layers, wrap it in one history transaction. Add an e2e test.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:3019-3020 calls only text.rasterizeLayer (app.ts:3146 → rasterize_text_layer, kind 2 only, mod.rs:16060), smart.rasterize (app.ts:2494 → rasterize_smart_object, kind 7 only, 16076) and store.rasterizeFillLayer (kind 4 only, store.ts:7904). rasterize_vector_layer (mod.rs:15163) is reachable only through store.rasterizeShape (store.ts:7417), which neither handler calls. Each handler also runs three engine.commit() calls per layer. No unit or e2e test references rasterizelayer or rasterizealllayers.

findings.title: Group Layers with a group and its descendants selected (e.g. after Select ▸ All Layers) flattens the hierarchy and changes the composite
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Group Layers (⌘G) / New ▸ Group from Layers
findings.evidence: group_layers (13505) removes every selected index and sets `l.group = id` (13534-13541), including layers whose own ancestor group is also selected. selectAllLayers (store.ts:7635) selects every header and child. The engine test group_layers_and_create_group_nest_inside_an_existing_group asserts that a selected child is pulled out of its selected group.
findings.repro: Make a group at 50% opacity (or with a mask or blend mode). Choose Select ▸ All Layers, then ⌘G.
findings.impact: Every existing group becomes an empty sibling in the new group and its children lose the group's opacity, blend mode, mask and effects. The image visibly changes and the nesting is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Before retagging, drop selected ids whose ancestor chain contains another selected id, so descendants stay under their selected group.
findings.verdict_reason: group_layers (13505-13552) removes every selected index and sets `l.group = id` on each one, including children whose ancestor group is also selected. selectAllLayers (store.ts:7635) selects every id, and groupSelectedLayers (7864) passes them unfiltered. The engine test at mod.rs:46832 asserts `layer_group(a) == both` when [inner, a] are selected, which pins the flattening. The composite plan (7808-7850) would then render the old group as an empty header, so its opacity, blend mode, mask and effects no longer apply to its former children.

findings.title: Layer Via Cut on type, shape or Smart Object layers cuts only the derived raster; the source content comes back later, duplicating it
findings.feature: Layer ▸ New ▸ Layer Via Cut (⇧⌘J)
findings.evidence: layer_via_cut (9459) guards only on the selection, locked, float and plane_rect, with no refuse_destructive_edit and no kind check. It zeroes alpha in `self.layers[self.active].pixels` (9486-9489). For kind 3 that buffer is a cache that render_vector (5423) rebuilds from the scene after a reload or undo. Kind 2 re-renders from its spec on the next edit, and kind 7 from smart_src (render_smart 5005).
findings.repro: Draw a shape or type layer, marquee part of it, press ⇧⌘J, then save and reopen (or edit the text).
findings.impact: The 'cut' region reappears on the source while the new layer also holds a copy, so the content is duplicated after reload. Photoshop disables Via Cut until the layer is rasterized.
findings.suggested_fix: Call refuse_destructive_edit (or a kind 0/4 check) at the top of layer_via_cut, and disable ⇧⌘J when there is no selection.
findings.verdict_reason: layer_via_cut (9459-9496) guards only on sel.active, locked, the float check and plane_rect. It has no refuse_destructive_edit (3890, which names kinds 2, 3 and 7) and no kind check, and store.layerViaCut (store.ts:6508) adds none. It zeroes alpha in `pixels` only. For kind 3 the vector_cache_key stays set, so the next invalidation (a scene edit, font registration, or load, where the key defaults to None at mod.rs:457) re-rasterizes the full scene. Kind 2 re-renders from its spec on the next text apply, and kind 7 on the next render_smart. After that, the cut content exists in both layers.

findings.title: Distribute ▸ Horizontal and Vertical are wired to centers instead of equal spacing
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Distribute ▸ Horizontal / Vertical
findings.evidence: `disth: () => store.distributeLayers(0, 1)` and `distv: () => store.distributeLayers(1, 1)` (App.tsx:2914-2915) are the same calls as disthc and distvc. The engine supports key 3 = equal spacing (distribute_spacing, mod.rs:10088-10092), and the Move options bar already uses it (App.tsx:268-269).
findings.repro: Select three layers of different widths and choose Layer ▸ Distribute ▸ Horizontal.
findings.impact: The centers are spaced evenly but the gaps are not, and the menu disagrees with the options-bar Spacing buttons.
findings.suggested_fix: Change them to `distributeLayers(0, 3)` and `distributeLayers(1, 3)`, and add a test that compares the menu with the options bar.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:2914-2915 maps disth to distributeLayers(0, 1) and distv to distributeLayers(1, 1), the same calls as disthc and distvc (2911, 2908). The engine's key 3 gives equal spacing (mod.rs:10092), and the options-bar Spacing buttons use it (App.tsx:268-269). psMenuData.ts:2227-2235 labels the two items 'Horizontal' and 'Vertical', which match Photoshop's spacing commands.

findings.title: Duplicate Layer… on a group made with ⌘G renames a child's copy instead of the group copy
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Duplicate Layer…
findings.evidence: The dialog finds the copy with `store.state.layers.find((l) => !before.has(l.id))` (Dialogs.tsx:3625). That list is ordered top-first. group_layers puts the header at the bottom of its span (mod.rs:13545-13549), and duplicate_layer splices [header', members'] above the original (9395-9401), so the first new id found top-first is the top member's copy. renameLayer then gives that child the group's '<name> copy' name.
findings.repro: Select two layers, press ⌘G, then choose Layer ▸ Duplicate Layer… and click OK.
findings.impact: A child layer copy loses its name and two layers end up named 'Group N copy'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the id returned by duplicate_layer (or the engine's active layer after the call) instead of diffing ids, and do the duplicate and rename in one history step.
findings.verdict_reason: group_layers inserts the header at the bottom-most slot, with the members above it at higher vec indices (mod.rs:13545-13549). duplicate_layer (9371-9408) copies [header, members] in vec order and splices them in above, and it already names the header copy '<name> copy'. layer_id_at (9319) lists layers top-first, so the dialog's `store.state.layers.find((l) => !before.has(l.id))` (Dialogs.tsx:3625) finds the top member's copy first and renames it. The panel's New Group uses create_group, which places the header above its child, so only ⌘G groups are affected, as the finding says.

findings.title: Deleting a group deletes only its header and leaves members with a dangling parent id, so later Merge Down is refused
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Delete / Layers panel Delete on a group
findings.evidence: delete_layer (9347) calls `self.layers.remove(i)` only and does not reparent descendants. The members keep `group == <deleted id>`. The panel treats them as root (validParent in layerTree.ts), but merge_down compares raw ids (`upper.group != lower.group` → 'Could not merge down layers from different groups.', mod.rs:10456), and clip_base_index (4115) does too. Artboards, by contrast, delete their contents (store.ts deleteSelectedArtboard).
findings.repro: Group two layers, delete the group, then Merge Down the former member onto a root layer below it.
findings.impact: The group's contents are not deleted, which is not what Photoshop does (it prompts group and contents / group only). Later merges and clipping behave inconsistently.
findings.suggested_fix: In delete_layer for kind 6, either delete the subtree or reparent members to the header's parent (as ungroup does). Offer Photoshop's 'Group and Contents / Group Only' prompt from the UI.
findings.verdict_reason: delete_layer (9347-9368) calls layers.remove(i) only, with no reparenting or subtree removal, and store.deleteLayer and the panel Delete (Panels.tsx:626) add nothing. The compositor treats dangling ids as root (7815-7820), but merge_down compares raw ids (`upper.group != lower.group`, 10456), and clip_base_index (4115) does too. So a former member cannot merge down onto a root layer.

findings.title: Layer Comps to Files and to PDF ignore each comp's Apply To Layers options
findings.feature: File ▸ Export ▸ Layer Comps to Files / PDF
findings.evidence: renderLayerCompPngs calls `store.applyLayerCompToEngine(clone, comp)` with the raw comp (app.ts:6101). The panel narrows the comp first with compForApply (Panels.tsx:3084). applyLayerCompToEngine (store.ts:7204) always writes visibility, opacity, blend, offset and style.
findings.repro: Save a comp, open Layer Comp Options, uncheck Position, move a layer, then Export Layer Comps to Files.
findings.impact: The exported comp puts layers back at their captured positions and appearance, so it does not match what applying the comp in the panel shows.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply compForApply(comp, liveLayersOf(clone)) inside renderLayerCompPngs (and store.applyLayerComp), or move the narrowing into applyLayerCompToEngine.
findings.verdict_reason: renderLayerCompPngs (app.ts:6093-6107) calls store.applyLayerCompToEngine(clone, comp) with the raw comp. The panel narrows the comp first with compForApply (Panels.tsx:3084; layerComps.ts:124-142 honours applyVisibility, applyPosition and applyAppearance). applyLayerCompToEngine (store.ts:7204-7224) always writes visibility, opacity, blend, offset, fill and style. store.applyLayerComp (7226) skips the narrowing too.

findings.title: Every engine commit re-encodes a PNG thumbnail for every layer, making multi-layer commands O(N²)
findings.feature: Layers panel thumbnails / performance with many layers
findings.evidence: syncFromEngine runs synchronously on every commit (app.ts:236). For every layer it calls this.engine.layerThumbUrl(id), which creates a canvas and calls toDataURL (EngineClient.ts:952-963), plus maskThumbUrl (store.ts:2372) and an effect scan. The App.tsx loops (del 2850, hidelayers 2897, rasterizealllayers 3020 with three commits per layer) and the LockLayers dialog commit once per layer.
findings.repro: Take a document with 200 layers and drag the Opacity slider, or Select All Layers and choose Hide Layers or Delete.
findings.impact: Opacity drags get sluggish and bulk layer commands can freeze for seconds.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache thumbnails per layer, keyed by an engine revision or dirty flag, and regenerate only changed layers (or regenerate lazily for visible rows). Batch the loops into one engine call or history transaction with one sync.
findings.verdict_reason: engine.onSync runs store.syncFromEngine synchronously (app.ts:236, EngineClient.ts:804-808). The loop at store.ts:2397-2440 calls layerThumbUrl for every layer (a new canvas plus toDataURL each time, EngineClient.ts:952-963), maskThumbUrl for masked layers, and an effect scan. Nothing is cached. The per-layer loops (App.tsx:2850, 2897, 3020, Dialogs.tsx:6519) commit once per layer. How slow this gets was not measured, so the perf impact rests on medium confidence.

findings.title: Applying a Layer Comp runs about two full-canvas composites per layer
findings.feature: Layer Comps panel apply / Layer Comps export
findings.evidence: captureCompLayers stores a style for every layer (store.ts:7190). For each live layer, applyLayerCompToEngine calls e.clear_layer_effects, then set_layer_effect_at once per effect, then set_layer_blend_if (store.ts:7215-7222). Each of those runs self.composite() over the whole canvas (mod.rs:11006, 10962, 10914).
findings.repro: On a 24 MP document with 50 layers, click a comp, or run Layer Comps to Files with several comps.
findings.impact: The UI freezes for several seconds per comp, multiplied by the number of comps on export.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an engine batch (apply_layer_comp_styles) or a composite-suspend flag, and composite once at the end. Skip layers whose style has not changed.
findings.verdict_reason: captureCompLayers (store.ts:7186-7191) always stores a style object, so the `if (!layer.style) continue` at 7217 never skips a layer. For each layer, clear_layer_effects (mod.rs:11006-11014) and set_layer_blend_if (10914-10921) each run self.composite() unconditionally, and set_layer_effect_at composites once per effect (10962). composite() covers the full canvas (7726). The magnitude was not measured.

findings.title: Slices are app-global: they leak between documents and are not saved or undoable
findings.feature: Layer ▸ New Layer Based Slice (and Save for Web slices)
findings.evidence: newLayerBasedSlice only calls this.set({ slices: … }) (store.ts:4305-4309). captureActiveView and activateDoc (store.ts:4617, 6177) swap many per-document fields but not slices, selectedSlice or slicesLocked. Slices are not in the project data (app.ts reads them only for export, 5322). The slice is a static rectangle, not tied to the layer.
findings.repro: Make a layer-based slice in document A, switch to document B, and run Save for Web.
findings.impact: B shows A's slices and exports with them. Slices are lost when the document is reopened, and Undo does not remove one.
findings.suggested_fix: Store slices per document (in captureActiveView/activateDoc) and persist them with the project. Record them in history or in the action recorder.
findings.verdict_reason: newLayerBasedSlice (store.ts:4305-4309) and addSliceRect only call this.set({ slices }). captureActiveView (4617-4654) swaps many per-document fields but not slices, selectedSlice or slicesLocked, and nothing resets slices when documents switch. Outside store.ts, the only slice reads in app.ts are for export (5322). No persistence module references slices, and the engine history never sees them.

findings.title: Layer from Background… only unlocks the active layer
findings.feature: Layer ▸ New ▸ Layer from Background…
findings.evidence: `layerfrombg: () => store.setLayerLocked(store.state.activeLayerId, false)` (App.tsx:2917). The engine has no Background concept: layers are not locked by default (Engine::new mod.rs:7077), so in a normal document this does nothing.
findings.repro: Open an image and choose Layer ▸ New ▸ Layer from Background….
findings.impact: The menu item with an ellipsis promises a dialog and a conversion. Instead it does nothing, or silently unlocks whatever layer the user had locked.
findings.suggested_fix: Open the New Layer dialog prefilled 'Layer 0' and rename or unlock the bottom layer only when it is the Background. Otherwise disable the item until a Background concept exists.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:2917 is `layerfrombg: () => store.setLayerLocked(store.state.activeLayerId, false)`. Engine::new (mod.rs:7071-7090) creates 'Background' unlocked; the other `locked = true` sites (57268+) are tests. So in a new document the command does nothing, and on any other locked layer it silently unlocks it, with no dialog and no rename, although the label ends in an ellipsis (psMenuData.ts:1328).

findings.title: Matting ▸ Color Decontaminate opens the Defringe dialog
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Matting ▸ Color Decontaminate
findings.evidence: `colordecontaminate: () => open("defringe")` (App.tsx:2769). The dialog is titled 'Defringe' and calls store.defringe (Dialogs.tsx:6668-6676).
findings.repro: Choose Layer ▸ Matting ▸ Color Decontaminate.
findings.impact: The command is a second way into Defringe, not color decontamination.
findings.suggested_fix: Wire it to the decontaminate path that Select and Mask already has (store.selectAndMask with decontaminate), or leave it as a disabled placeholder.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:2769 has `colordecontaminate: () => open("defringe")`, the same target as `defringe` (App.tsx:3006). The Defringe dialog (Dialogs.tsx:6669-6682) calls store.defringe(width). A decontaminate path does exist (store.ts:8957-8974, e.decontaminate_colors) but this command does not use it.

findings.title: New ▸ Group… and the panel's New Group button wrap the active layer instead of making an empty group
findings.feature: Layer ▸ New ▸ Group…, Layers panel New group
findings.evidence: create_group (13481-13503) sets the active layer's group to the new header. NewGroup dialog comment: 'store.createGroup(); // empty group' (Dialogs.tsx:3572). The panel button is Panels.tsx:611. Default names use layer_count ('Group ${e.layer_count()}', store.ts:7858).
findings.repro: With only the Background layer, click New group or choose Layer ▸ New ▸ Group….
findings.impact: The Background, or whatever layer is active, is moved into the group, and the default name is misnumbered (for example 'Group 3' for the first group).
findings.suggested_fix: Add an engine create_empty_group, or pass a flag so these entry points insert an empty header above the active layer. Name it with defaultGroupName.
findings.verdict_reason: create_group (mod.rs:13481-13501) sets the active layer's group to the new header. store.createGroup (store.ts:7856-7861) calls it; so do the panel button (Panels.tsx:611) and the NewGroup dialog (Dialogs.tsx:3572), whose comment says 'empty group'. The default name is `Group ${e.layer_count()}`. The dialog renames the group afterwards; the panel button does not.

findings.title: Several layer commands ignore the multi-selection and stay enabled when they cannot run
findings.feature: Duplicate, Arrange, Ungroup, Rasterize, Artboard from Layers, Link/Distribute, panel Delete
findings.evidence: These act only on activeLayerId: dup (2840), arrFwd/arrBwd (2854-2855), ungrp (2930), which silently does nothing when the active layer is inside a group rather than being the header (engine ungroup mod.rs:14063), rasterize* (3017-3020), and artboardfromlayers (store.ts:7543 → engine uses active_layer_bounds only, mod.rs:13946). The panel Delete button deletes only the active layer (Panels.tsx:622), while the menu deletes the whole selection (App.tsx:2850). menuEnablement (App.tsx:3440-3470) does not gate Merge Down on the bottom layer, Ungroup without a group, Via Cut without a selection, Link with fewer than 2, or Distribute with fewer than 3. The engine returns silently in each case.
findings.repro: Select three layers and choose Duplicate Layer…, Bring Forward, or Artboard from Layers. Or, with a child layer active, press ⇧⌘G.
findings.impact: Only one layer is affected, or nothing happens, with no feedback.
findings.suggested_fix: Route these through targetLayerIds(), or disable them via menuEnablement with state-derived flags, and surface an edit error when the engine refuses.
findings.verdict_reason: These handlers read only activeLayerId: dup (App.tsx:2840 → dialog), arrFwd/arrBwd (2854-2855 → store.arrangeLayer uses activeLayerId, store.ts:7786), ungrp (2930; engine ungroup returns silently for a non-kind-6 id, mod.rs:14063) and rasterize* (3017-3020). artboard_from_layers uses active_layer_bounds only (mod.rs:13946). The panel Delete removes only activeId (Panels.tsx:626). menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3470) has no layer-structure entries. link_layers and distribute return silently below 2 or 3 layers (16755, 10116).

findings.title: Rename and lock changes skip commit(), so refusals surface on the next unrelated edit and the document is marked dirty anyway
findings.feature: Rename Layer, Lock Layers, lock toggles
findings.evidence: renameLayer, setLayerLocked and setLayerLocks call the engine, then `this.markDirty(); this.engine.sync();` (store.ts:7710-7725, 7769-7773). When the engine refuses (reject_imported_photoshop_edit sets last_edit_error, mod.rs:4061), nothing consumes the error until the next commit(). consumeEditError then reports it and makes that unrelated commit return false (EngineClient.ts:823-825).
findings.repro: Open a non-RGB PSD in preserved read-only mode, rename a layer, then run any other edit.
findings.impact: The rename silently reverts, the tab shows unsaved changes, and the 'read-only' toast appears on a later, unrelated action, which is then treated as failed.
findings.suggested_fix: Use engine.commit() (or consumeEditError) in these setters, and call markDirty only when commit reports success.
findings.verdict_reason: renameLayer (store.ts:7769-7773), setLayerLocked (7710-7714) and setLayerLocks (7718-7725) call markDirty() and engine.sync(), never commit() or consumeEditError(). reject_imported_photoshop_edit sets last_edit_error (mod.rs:4061), and sync() does not consume it (EngineClient.ts:804). The next commit() consumes it and returns false (EngineClient.ts:457-468, 823). This matters only in the read-only imported-PSD mode, where the following edit would usually be refused anyway. The spurious dirty mark and the late toast are the real effects.

findings.title: Flatten, Merge Down/Visible, multi-layer Align/Distribute and Via Copy/Cut refuse on 32-bit documents
findings.feature: Merge / Flatten / Align / Distribute on 32 bits/channel
findings.evidence: reject_document_float_edit (3932) is called by flatten (10601), merge_visible (10675), merge_down (10513), distribute_layers (10089) and align_layers (10184). layer_via_copy and layer_via_cut call reject_legacy_float_edit (9425, 9467). The message is 'not 32-bit-float safe; convert … first'.
findings.repro: Run File ▸ Automate ▸ Merge to HDR Pro (which produces a 32-bit document), add a layer, then choose Flatten Image or press ⌘E.
findings.impact: Core stack operations are unavailable in HDR workflows. The refusal is visible, not silent.
findings.suggested_fix: Composite into RGBA32 (try_export_composite_rgba32 already exists) for flatten and merge, and give shift_layer a float-plane path. Until then, disable these menu items for 32-bit documents.
findings.verdict_reason: reject_document_float_edit (mod.rs:3932) is called by flatten (10602), merge_visible (about 10685), merge_down (10513), distribute_layers (10089) and align_layers (10184). layer_via_copy and layer_via_cut call reject_legacy_float_edit (9425, 9467). All of them report the 'not 32-bit-float safe' error, and the menu items stay enabled. The refusal is visible, so minor is right.

findings.title: Linked layers have no indicator in the panel and a single linked layer cannot be unlinked
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Link Layers / Select Linked Layers
findings.evidence: linkLayers unlinks only when `ids.length >= 2 && every linked`; otherwise it calls link_layers, which returns early with fewer than 2 ids (store.ts:7643-7650, mod.rs:16755). LayerInfo carries no link state and Panels.tsx renders no chain icon. The menu label never changes to 'Unlink Layers'.
findings.repro: Link A, B and C, then select only B and choose Link Layers to unlink it.
findings.impact: Nothing happens and the user cannot see which layers are linked.
findings.suggested_fix: When any selected layer is linked, unlink the selection (Photoshop's toggle). Expose is_linked in LayerInfo, draw a link glyph on the row, and relabel the menu item.
findings.verdict_reason: linkLayers (store.ts:7643-7650) unlinks only when `ids.length >= 2 && every is_linked`. Otherwise it calls link_layers, which returns early with fewer than 2 ids (mod.rs:16755). The LayerInfo built in syncFromEngine (store.ts:2413-2439) has no link field. In Panels.tsx, 'linked' appears only for smart-object source links, never for layer links.

findings.title: Several layer-structure commands are not macro-recorded, and the dialogs record several steps each
findings.feature: Actions recording of layer structure
findings.evidence: RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:904-952) leaves out setLayerLocks (Lock Layers dialog and panel lock toggles), toggleLayerInSelection, selectAllLayers, deselectLayers, selectLinkedLayers, newArtboard, artboardFromLayers, artboardFromGroup, newFrame, rasterizeShape, rasterizeFillLayer, rasterizeVectorMask, smart.rasterize, autoNameLayers, cleanupLayers and newLayerBasedSlice. The New Layer, New Group and Duplicate dialogs run 2–4 separate recorded and undoable operations (Dialogs.tsx:3518-3526, 3570-3579, 3622-3627).
findings.repro: Record an action: Select All Layers, Lock Position, Artboard from Layers. Then play it on another document.
findings.impact: The replayed action misses steps or targets the wrong layers, and one dialog OK needs several Undos.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the missing ops to RECORDED_STORE_OPS, and wrap each dialog's compound operation in beginHistory/commitHistory with a single recorded step.
findings.verdict_reason: RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:903-952) does not include setLayerLocks, selectAllLayers, deselectLayers, selectLinkedLayers, newArtboard, artboardFromLayers, artboardFromGroup, rasterizeShape, rasterizeFillLayer, autoNameLayers or newLayerBasedSlice. A grep finds them in no other recorded list. smart.rasterize has no recorded list at all; only text has RECORDED_TEXT_OPS (3462). The NewLayer, NewGroup and Duplicate dialogs (Dialogs.tsx:3518-3526, 3570-3579, 3622-3627) each call 2 to 4 recorded store ops with no beginHistory wrapper.

findings.title: Layer thumbnails are stretched on non-square documents and always 44 px regardless of the thumbnail-size option
findings.feature: Layers panel thumbnails
findings.evidence: layer_thumb samples `sx = tx*w/tw`, `sy = ty*h/th` independently (mod.rs:17051-17052), which distorts the aspect ratio. layerThumbUrl defaults to 44x44 (EngineClient.ts:952) while the Panel Options offer 24/40/64 (commands.ts:1003).
findings.repro: Open a 4000x1000 panorama, or set Layers Panel Options to the 64 px thumbnail.
findings.impact: Panoramas show squashed thumbnails, and the 64 px size is a blurry upscale.
findings.suggested_fix: Fit the document aspect into the thumbnail box (letterbox), and request the thumbnail at the configured size times devicePixelRatio.
findings.verdict_reason: layer_thumb (mod.rs:17044-17059) samples sx = tx*w/tw and sy = ty*h/th independently into a tw×th box, so the aspect ratio is not kept. store.ts:2421 calls layerThumbUrl(id) with the default 44×44 (EngineClient.ts:952). The row shows it with objectFit cover (Panels.tsx:511) in a square var(--mv-layer-thumbnail-size) box (styles.css:37-39), which can be 64 px, so that size is an upscale.

findings.title: No or weak automated tests for Rasterize ▸ Layer/All Layers, Reverse, Merge Down visibility, Align/Distribute on non-pixel layers, and lock enforcement
findings.feature: Layer structure tests
findings.evidence: A grep of the unit and e2e tests finds nothing for rasterizelayer, rasterizealllayers, reverse_layers, reverseLayers, selectLinkedLayers, artboardFromGroup or newLayerBasedSlice. 'locked layer rejects painting' (layers.spec.ts:176-189) only asserts `layer_locked(id)` is true and never checks that the pixels were unchanged. The engine align/distribute tests (mod.rs:64462-64579) use pixel layers only, and no merge_down test covers hidden layers.
findings.repro: Not applicable; this is a coverage gap.
findings.impact: The regressions in the findings above would not be caught.
findings.suggested_fix: Add engine tests for reverse (selection and clipping), merge_down onto hidden layers, align/distribute on kind 2/3/7 followed by re-render or reload, and locks honoured by align/distribute. Add an e2e test for Rasterize ▸ Layer on a shape layer, and make the lock e2e compare the composite before and after.
findings.verdict_reason: The gap is real, with two corrections. First, an engine test for Reverse exists (reverse_layers_flips_the_stack, mod.rs:64552), but it pins the whole-stack behavior. Second, the lock e2e test is at e2e/layers.spec.ts:123-135, not 176-189; it still asserts only `layer_locked(id)` and never compares pixels. Confirmed: nothing under src or e2e references rasterizelayer, rasterizealllayers, reverseLayers, selectLinkedLayers, artboardFromGroup or newLayerBasedSlice. The engine align/distribute tests (64449-64600) use plain add_layer pixel layers, and no merge_down test (78132-78342) hides a layer.

areas.area: Layers: styles, masks, fill/adjustment layers, smart objects
areas.coverage:
Scope inventory taken from psMenuData.ts, psMenus.ts and App.tsx menuActions: Layer Style 18 (Blending Options, 10 effects, Copy/Paste/Clear, Global Light, Create Layer, Hide All Effects, Scale Effects), Smart Filter 5, New Fill Layer 3, New Adjustment Layer 17, Layer Mask 10, Vector Mask 6, Create/Release Clipping Mask 1, Smart Objects 14 implemented out of 15 rows (Relink to Library Graphic has no monetId), plus Rasterize ▸ Vector Mask, Layer Style and Smart Object (one of them shared with Smart Objects ▸ Rasterize) and Layer Content Options, which is wired by label. That is about 78 commands.

For each command I followed the path from the menu or panel to its handler, then to state/app.ts (smart.*) or state/store.ts, then to the Rust engine in packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs and effects.rs. I also read the PSD writer (format_import.rs, monet-format psd_semantics.rs), the LayerStyle, GlobalLight, ScaleEffects, SmartStackMode, VectorMaskPathOp, fill-layer and adjustment-layer dialogs, the useScratch* hooks, the Properties, Adjustments and Layers panel sub-rows, RECORDED_STORE_OPS, the MCP commands in scope, and the unit/e2e test coverage (grep).

Per the instructions I ran no builds or suites. To confirm the key findings I ran small node scripts from my scratchpad against the existing, already-built apps/vision/engine/pkg WASM, which was built today and matches the clean HEAD source. No repository files were changed.

Not reviewed in depth: the rendering accuracy of each effect, the correctness of every adjustment formula, the ASL/Styles-panel preset import, linked-file watcher internals, and smart-filter re-edit dialogs for individual filters.
areas.parity_notes:
Photoshop items in scope that are correctly shown disabled (no monetId): Smart Objects ▸ Relink to Library Graphic…, the whole Video Layers submenu, and Rasterize ▸ Video. Rasterize ▸ Fill Content and Layer Content Options… are wired by label in psMenus.ts.

Partial parity (worth tracking, not reported as bugs):
- **Fill and adjustment layers:** Gradient Fill is top-to-bottom only, with no angle, style, scale or offset. Levels and Curves adjustment layers are composite-channel only (no per-channel R/G/B). Converting a type or fill layer to a Smart Object flattens it, so Edit Contents cannot re-edit the type or fill.
- **Blending Options:** Blend If authors only hard thresholds (outer = inner), so there are no split sliders. Editing an imported split range collapses it. The Channels row always shows R/G/B, even in CMYK or Lab documents.
- **Masks:** layer masks are 8-bit even in 16- and 32-bit documents. Pixel and vector masks share one plane and one Density/Feather setting.
- **Layers panel:** effect sub-rows are read-only, with no per-effect eye and no double-click to edit.
- **Background and locked layers:** they can receive layer styles and masks; Photoshop greys these out.
- **Stack Mode:** it is a destructive merge, not a re-editable smart-object stack.
- **Convert to Linked:** Vision's semantics differ from Photoshop's.
- **MCP:** only layer.vectorMaskFromPath, layer.editSmartObjectContents and layer.updateSmartObjectContents exist in this area. Layer styles, layer masks, clipping, fill and adjustment layers, and smart-object convert, rasterize and filters are reachable over MCP only through script.run and the recorded store ops, and vector-mask and smart ops are not reachable there.
- **Shortcuts:** ⌥⌘G, Create/Release Clipping Mask, matches Photoshop and is relabelled correctly.

findings.title: PSD/PSB/layered-TIFF save refuses the whole document when any layer has a layer style or advanced-blending option set in Vision
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Layer Style (all effects, Blending Options) → File ▸ Save / Save As PSD, PSB, layered TIFF
findings.evidence: unmap_effects (format_import.rs:2181-2230) requires EXACT param counts (0|1|5=>10, 2|9=>8, 3=>9, 4=>17, 7=>13) and errors on disabled effects (:2216). Vision's own defaults are longer: Drop Shadow def has 13 floats (effects.ts:121), Inner Shadow 12, Outer Glow 17, Inner Glow 18, Bevel 28, Satin 11, Gradient Overlay 18, Stroke 15 (effects.ts:283). The 'Use Global Light' toggle writes slot def.length (Dialogs.tsx:12119), which pads the array further. psd_semantics.rs:1707 refuses stacked instances ('multiple layer effects of the same type'). format_import.rs:1743-1760 refuses Transparency Shapes off, Blend Interior as Group and Blend Clipped as Group. prepare_psd_export_record (mod.rs:34318) propagates the Err, so the whole file fails. Confirmed with the built WASM: set_layer_effect(id,0,<13-float Drop Shadow default>) makes export_psd() fail with 'Photoshop semantic export cannot represent layer 2 ("L"): Drop Shadow payload has 13 values; expected 10'. Stroke default fails with 'expected 8'. A disabled Color Overlay, two Color Overlays, set_layer_blend_interior_group(true), transparency_shapes(false) and blend_clipped_group(true) each fail. export_psb and export_tiff_layered_with_icc fail the same way. Only a 6-float Color Overlay or a 10-float shadow exports.
findings.repro: New document → Layer ▸ New Layer, paint something → Layer ▸ Layer Style ▸ Drop Shadow… → OK → File ▸ Save As… → Photoshop (.psd). An error appears and no file is written. The same happens with ⌘S on a document opened from a PSD after adding a stroke or shadow, and when unticking an imported effect in Blending Options and saving.
findings.impact: PSD interop, the main exchange format, fails for almost every styled document. Users cannot save back to a PSD they opened once they touch its layer styles. Image Processor PSD output and MCP doc.saveAs psd fail the same way.
findings.suggested_fix: In unmap_effects, accept params.len() >= expected. Map the Vision-only tail (contour, knockout, noise, technique, gradient stops, global-light flag) into the lfx2 descriptor or drop it. Write disabled effects with enab=false. Write stacked instances as Photoshop's *Multi lists. Write tsly/infx/clbl blocks instead of refusing. Where something truly cannot be represented, rasterize that one layer's style with a photoshop_export_notice instead of failing the file. Add an engine test that exports every FX_DEFS default from effects.ts.
findings.verdict_reason: Traced end to end. The Layer Style dialog seeds a new effect from fxDef(eid).def (Dialogs.tsx:12299), and those defaults are longer than the export accepts: Drop Shadow is 13 floats (effects.ts:121), Satin 11, Gradient Overlay 18 and Stroke 15. set_layer_effect stores the array unchanged (mod.rs:10931-10938). On export, to_import_layer_for_photoshop_with_id_status calls unmap_effects unconditionally (format_import.rs:1803). exact_params requires len == expected (format_import.rs:1917-1931), and a disabled effect errors (format_import.rs:2213-2217). The same function refuses transparency_shapes=false, blend_interior_group and blend_clipped_group (1743-1760). encode_effects refuses duplicate effect types (psd_semantics.rs:1707). prepare_psd_export_record propagates the Err (mod.rs:34318). psdExportBytes has no fallback, and exportPSD only reports the error (app.ts:4733-4761). Imported RGB PSD effects are 10 floats (map_effects, format_import.rs:1222+), so they export while unchanged. A newly added effect, or toggling Use Global Light (which writes slot def.length, Dialogs.tsx:12119), breaks the export. The document stays open and can be saved natively, so nothing is lost. Still, Save As PSD fails for nearly every styled document, a core interchange workflow, so this stays a blocker. I did not re-run the WASM probes; the code path alone is conclusive.

findings.title: PSD/PSB/layered-TIFF save refuses documents containing common Vision-created adjustment layers (Curves, Gradient Map, Channel Mixer, Selective Color, Color Lookup, Desaturate, Color Balance, Photo Filter)
findings.feature: Layer ▸ New Adjustment Layer ▸ * → File ▸ Save As PSD/PSB/TIFF (layers)
findings.evidence: unmap_adjustment (format_import.rs:2002-2137) handles only kinds 0-13 and requires exact lengths. Color Balance requires 9 values (:2107), but ADJ_SPECS.alColorBalance.defaults has 10 because Preserve Luminosity is slot 9. Photo Filter requires 4, but the UI writes 5. Kinds 14/15/16 hit 'unsupported adjustment kind' (:2132). encode_adjustment in psd_semantics.rs:1685-1695 returns unsupported for Photo Filter, Desaturate, Curves and Gradient Map. Confirmed with the built WASM: add_adjustment_layer + export_psd() fails for Desaturate, ColorBalance(10), PhotoFilter(5), Curves(256), GradientMap(768), Mixer, SelectiveColor and ColorLookup. Brightness, Levels, Hue/Sat, Vibrance, Invert, B&W, Posterize, Threshold and Exposure export OK. The engine test at format_import.rs:5088 asserts this refusal on purpose.
findings.repro: Open any image → Layer ▸ New Adjustment Layer ▸ Curves… → OK → File ▸ Save As… PSD. The save fails with '… Curves LUTs need a PSD curve-point encoder'. Same for Color Balance or Photo Filter left at their defaults.
findings.impact: Adding Curves, arguably the most common adjustment layer, makes the document unsaveable as PSD/PSB/layered TIFF. An imported PSD Curves layer that is re-edited in Vision also becomes unsaveable.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement the missing encoders: curv (fit points from the LUT; Dialogs.tsx already has sparseSampleIndices), grdm, mixr, selc, phfl, clrL, and accept Color Balance's Preserve Luminosity slot. Until then, degrade per layer (for example, bake the adjustment into a merged pixel layer and add a photoshop_export_notice) instead of failing the whole file. Add a test that exports every ADJ_SPECS default.
findings.verdict_reason: ADJ_SPECS.alColorBalance.defaults has 10 values and alPhotoFilter has 5 (Dialogs.tsx:343, 350). unmap_adjustment requires exactly 9 and 4 (format_import.rs:2106-2119). Kinds 14, 15 and 16 are created by Dialogs.tsx:608/629/682 and hit 'unsupported adjustment kind' (format_import.rs:2132). Curves (Dialogs.tsx:507, 256 values) and Gradient Map pass unmap_adjustment. encode_adjustment then returns unsupported for Curves, Gradient Map, Photo Filter and Desaturate (psd_semantics.rs:1683-1695). reconcile only keeps an unchanged imported block, so a Vision-created layer always reaches the encoder. add_adjustment_layer stores the params unchanged (mod.rs:14978). One detail in the evidence is wrong: the engine test near format_import.rs:5085 asserts the refusal for adj_kind 99, not for Curves or kinds 14-16. The core claim holds. Curves is the most common adjustment layer, so this is a blocker for the same reason as the layer-style refusal.

findings.title: Blending Options OK throws away a change made only to Advanced Blending ▸ Channels (R/G/B)
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Layer Style ▸ Blending Options… ▸ Channels
findings.evidence: The no-change snapshot (Dialogs.tsx:12287) records fillOp, knock, txShapes, blendGroup, blendClipped, bif and fx but not blendChans. The `same` check at 12410-12413 also omits it. When `same` is true, ok() calls rollback(), which runs cancel_history_transaction and restores the pre-dialog layer stack, including blend_channels. blendChannels.test.ts only tests the store plumbing and applyLayerStyleState, not the dialog OK path.
findings.repro: Select a pixel layer → Layer ▸ Layer Style ▸ Blending Options… → untick R → the preview changes → OK. The canvas reverts and reopening the dialog shows R ticked again.
findings.impact: This advertised control does nothing unless some other option changes in the same session. The user sees the preview, clicks OK, and the result is silently discarded.
findings.suggested_fix: Add blendChans to snap.current and to the `same` comparison. Add a dialog test that changes only a channel bit and asserts it persists after OK.
findings.verdict_reason: snap.current (Dialogs.tsx:12287) and the `same` comparison (12410-12413) both omit blendChans. A channel checkbox mutates the engine inside the transaction via store.setLayerBlendChannels (12460-12463). With no other change, `same` is true and rollback() runs cancel_history_transaction (12265-12272). reset_history_transaction then pops the undo entries and apply_snap restores the pre-dialog layer stack (mod.rs:16464-16502), which reverts blend_channels. The only dialog test is a source-string check (levelsCurvesDialogs.test.ts:109-113), which does not exercise the OK path.

findings.title: Rasterize ▸ Layer Style (and Flatten All Layer Effects) applies layer Opacity and Fill twice and truncates 16-bit layers to 8-bit
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Rasterize ▸ Layer Style; File ▸ Scripts ▸ Flatten All Layer Effects
findings.evidence: bake_layer_style (mod.rs:16335-16385) composites the isolated layer through the normal compositor, which applies the layer's opacity, fill_opacity and blend_if, into the 8-bit self.output. It writes `px[p + c] = out[k + c] as u16 * 257` (16372) and then clears only `effects`: opacity, fill_opacity and blend_if stay on the layer. Built-WASM probe, blue square with a red 2px stroke over white: at opacity 0.5 the center goes 8080ff→bfbfff and the stroke ff8080→ffbfbf. At Fill 0.5 the center goes 8080ff→bfbfff and the stroke ff0000→ff8080. In a 16-bit doc with a Color Overlay, composite R goes 5316→5397 (8-bit step).
findings.repro: Layer at 50% opacity with a Stroke → Layer ▸ Rasterize ▸ Layer Style. The layer visibly fades to about 25%. Same with Fill 50%. In a 16-bit document, fine gradients band after rasterizing.
findings.impact: The result looks different from before the command, even though the command exists to keep the look while dropping the style. It also permanently loses 16-bit precision. Undo recovers.
findings.suggested_fix: Bake with opacity forced to 1 and blend Normal, bake Fill, then reset fill_opacity to 1 (Photoshop behavior). Read the 16-bit composite (export_composite_rgba16 path) instead of self.output. Refuse or handle float docs as today. Add engine tests for opacity, fill and 16-bit.
findings.verdict_reason: bake_layer_style (mod.rs:16335-16385) isolates the layer and calls composite(). The compositor multiplies content by layer.opacity * fill_opacity and effects by layer.opacity (base_extra/fx_extra at about mod.rs:6479-6483, fill_extra at 6554). It writes self.output, which is a Vec<u8> (mod.rs:3164), back as `out as u16 * 257` (16372). It then clears only `effects`, leaving opacity, fill_opacity and blend_if on the layer, so they apply a second time. The TS wrappers do nothing else (store.ts:7747-7750, 7833-7836). reject_float_edit_for_layer blocks only 32-bit float layers, so 16-bit layers lose precision. Existing tests (mod.rs:64300, group_effects_tests.rs) do not cover opacity, fill or 16-bit.

findings.title: Layer mask and vector mask share one mask plane: adding a vector mask overwrites a painted layer mask, and Layer Mask commands no-op or leave orphans on vector-masked layers
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Vector Mask ▸ Reveal All / Hide All / Current Path; Layer ▸ Layer Mask ▸ Reveal All / Hide All / From Transparency / Delete / Apply
findings.evidence: add_full_vector_mask (mod.rs:11424-11441) and set_vector_mask_impl (11302-11340) assign `self.layers[i].mask = …` without checking for an existing pixel mask. add_layer_mask/add_layer_mask_hidden (11178-11220) and layer_mask_from_transparency (13153) return silently when `mask` is non-empty. delete_layer_mask (12548) and apply_layer_mask (12571) clear `mask` but not vector_path/vector_is_mask. Built-WASM probe: a painted mask revealing only the right half, then add_vector_mask_reveal_all, leaves the left half visible (painted mask gone). A vector mask then add_layer_mask pushes 0 history steps and gives no error. A vector mask then delete_layer_mask leaves the layer unmasked while has_vector_mask()==true, and this survives save/load.
findings.repro: Paint a layer mask → Layer ▸ Vector Mask ▸ Reveal All: the painted mask is replaced. Or: Vector Mask ▸ Hide All → Layer ▸ Layer Mask ▸ Reveal All does nothing. Or: Layer ▸ Layer Mask ▸ Delete removes the clip, yet Vector Mask ▸ Enable/Link/Delete still see a vector mask.
findings.impact: A painted mask is silently destroyed (only Undo recovers it). Photoshop's standard pixel-mask-plus-vector-mask setup cannot be built. The UI state becomes inconsistent.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the vector-mask raster separately and compose it with the pixel mask in the compositor and exports. As a minimum for release: refuse with last_edit_error when the other mask kind exists, and clear vector_path/vector_is_mask in delete_layer_mask/apply_layer_mask.
findings.verdict_reason: add_full_vector_mask (mod.rs:11424-11441) and set_vector_mask_impl (11302-11339) assign layers[i].mask unconditionally. add_layer_mask and add_layer_mask_hidden return early when a mask exists, with no undo step and no error (11180-11182, 11203-11205). delete_layer_mask (12548-12560) clears `mask` but leaves vector_path and vector_is_mask set, so has_vector_mask (11410-11413) still returns true. The store wrappers (store.ts:7612-7619, 8178-8190, 8264-8271) add no guard, and menuEnablement (App.tsx:3440-3470) has no rules for these items. A painted mask is silently replaced; only Undo recovers it.

findings.title: Smart Object Edit Contents → Update round-trips through an 8-bit PNG in 16- and 32-bit documents
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Smart Objects ▸ Edit Contents / Update Edited Contents / Export Contents
findings.evidence: editContents (app.ts:2783-2811) opens a project only when smart_object_document returns bytes. For any Convert to Smart Object result smart_doc is empty, so it falls back to export_smart_object_png, which writes `(v >> 8) as u8` 8-bit RGBA (mod.rs:16186-16205). updateEditedContents (app.ts:2813-2845) writes E().export_png() of that 8-bit tab back through replace_smart_object_preserve_placement. Built-WASM probe: in 16- and 32-bit docs after convert_to_smart_object, smart_object_document is 0 bytes and the export PNG bit depth is 8.
findings.repro: New 16-bit (or 32-bit HDR) document → Layer ▸ Smart Objects ▸ Convert to Smart Object → Edit Contents. The contents tab is 8-bit. Make any edit → Update Edited Contents. The smart object source is now 8-bit, and HDR values above 1.0 are clipped.
findings.impact: This silently lowers the precision of 16- and 32-bit smart objects, the main reason to use high bit depth. Export Contents is 8-bit too.
findings.suggested_fix: For a flat smart object, open the contents as a sub-document at the parent's depth (build a one-layer project from smart_src/smart_src_f32) and update back via replace_smart_object_document. Or export a 16-bit PNG / float TIFF. Add a 16-bit round-trip test.
findings.verdict_reason: convert_to_smart_object (mod.rs:14427-14459) sets smart_src and smart_src_f32 but not smart_doc. smart_object_document therefore returns the empty smart_doc when there is no link (mod.rs:14286-14287), and editContents falls back to export_smart_object_png (app.ts:2803). That function encodes smart_src as `(v >> 8) as u8` RGBA8 and ignores smart_src_f32 (mod.rs:16195-16201). updateEditedContents writes E().export_png() of that tab back through replace_smart_object_preserve_placement (app.ts:2819, 2839). The result is a silent precision loss in 16-bit documents and clipping in 32-bit documents.

findings.title: Smart Objects ▸ Stack Mode ignores the smart object and merges the document's visible layers
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Smart Objects ▸ Stack Mode
findings.evidence: SmartStackMode (Dialogs.tsx:3742-3765) calls store.stackStatistic(mode) and then renameLayer. That is two history steps, and the rename is not recorded as part of the same step. engine stack_statistic (mod.rs:28737-28750) collects all visible non-adjustment, non-group layers of the DOCUMENT and returns silently when fewer than 2 exist. The active smart object and its smart_doc are never consulted.
findings.repro: Convert several layers into one Smart Object (Convert with multiple selected) → Layer ▸ Smart Objects ▸ Stack Mode → Median → OK. Nothing happens, because only one visible layer exists. In a document with other visible layers, those unrelated layers are merged into a new flat layer instead.
findings.impact: The command reached from the Smart Objects menu gives the wrong result in its normal use and silently no-ops otherwise. The dialog note partly admits it is a merge.
