findings.suggested_fix: Operate on the active smart object's inner document layers (smart_doc) and replace its source, storing the mode for re-editing. Disable the item unless the active layer is a layered smart object. Make it one history step.
findings.verdict_reason: SmartStackMode (Dialogs.tsx:3742-3765) calls store.stackStatistic and then renameLayer as a separate step. stack_statistic (mod.rs:28737-28752) gathers the document's visible non-adjustment, non-group layers, returns silently when there are fewer than 2, and never reads the active smart object or its smart_doc. The dialog does disclose that it 'Combines the visible layers into a new stack-mode layer… merged rather than re-editable', which softens the charge of misleading users. Even so, in the normal Photoshop workflow (layers already converted into one smart object) the command silently does nothing. Otherwise it merges unrelated layers.

findings.title: 'Blend Clipped Layers as Group' defaults off and PSD import ignores clbl/infx/tsly, so clipping groups on a blend-moded base render differently from Photoshop
findings.feature: Clipping masks + Blending Options advanced flags, PSD round-trip
findings.evidence: The Layer default is blend_clipped_group: false (mod.rs:450), and the compositor comments say 'Default off' (mod.rs:7891-7897). The engine test at mod.rs:42010-42035 shows the two settings render differently for a Multiply base. The monet-format PSD reader parses only knko among the advanced-blending blocks (psd.rs:1081), with no clbl/infx/tsly. Export refuses blend_clipped_group=true (format_import.rs:1755). Photoshop's default for this option is ON.
findings.repro: In Photoshop, make a Multiply base with a clipped red layer and save a PSD. Open it in Vision: the red is painted Normal instead of multiplied. In Vision, tick Blend Clipped Layers as Group to match: PSD export now fails.
findings.impact: Common Photoshop clip-group setups look different after import, and fixing it in Vision blocks saving. Round-trip fidelity is broken in both directions.
findings.suggested_fix: Default blend_clipped_group to true for new layers, which is Photoshop's default. Read clbl/infx/tsly on import and write them on export. Update tests that assume the old default.
findings.verdict_reason: The Layer default is blend_clipped_group: false (mod.rs:450), and the compositor documents 'Default off' (mod.rs:7891-7897). The engine test at mod.rs:42005-42031 shows a Multiply base renders differently with the flag on and off. Among the advanced-blending blocks, psd.rs matches only knko (psd.rs:1081), and nothing in monet-format or format_import maps clbl onto blend_clipped_group. Export refuses the flag when true (format_import.rs:1755-1759). The claim that Photoshop defaults this option to ON is external knowledge, but it is well established. The difference only appears for clip groups whose base has a non-Normal mode (or similar), which is a real but partial subset of documents.

findings.title: Convert to Linked… opens an Open dialog and replaces the layer's contents with the picked file
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Smart Objects ▸ Convert to Linked…
findings.evidence: convertToLinked (app.ts:2695-2725) opens pickSmartLinkedSourceFile, an Open dialog (app.ts:348-363). convertToLinkedFromBytes (app.ts:2512-2535) then runs convert_to_smart_object and replace_smart_object(picked bytes), which is two history steps. It also accepts plain pixel layers. The e2e test masks-adjlayers-text-smart.spec.ts:653 asserts that a gray layer becomes the picked blue file.
findings.repro: Select a smart object (or a pixel layer) with artwork → Layer ▸ Smart Objects ▸ Convert to Linked… → pick any image. The layer's artwork is replaced by that image.
findings.impact: Photoshop's command writes the embedded contents OUT to a new linked file. Vision's version discards the user's current contents (recoverable only with two Undo steps) and links to an unrelated file.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a Save dialog. Write the current contents (the project or a PNG at document depth) to the chosen path, then setSmartLink without touching pixels. Restrict the command to embedded smart objects.
findings.verdict_reason: convertToLinked (app.ts:2690-2718) accepts both smart and pixel layers and calls pickSmartLinkedSourceFile, which uses plugin-dialog `open` (app.ts:347-359), or a file input in the browser. convertToLinkedFromBytes (app.ts:2512-2535) runs convert_to_smart_object if needed and then replace_smart_object(picked bytes), overwriting the user's artwork. The e2e test (masks-adjlayers-text-smart.spec.ts:649-656) exercises exactly this replace behavior. Photoshop's command exports the embedded contents out to a new file instead. Undo recovers the artwork in two steps.

findings.title: Layer Mask ▸ Reveal All / Hide All use the active selection
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Layer Mask ▸ Reveal All / Hide All (+ Reveal/Hide Selection enablement)
findings.evidence: The addmask and hidemask menu items (App.tsx:2996-2997) call engine add_layer_mask/add_layer_mask_hidden. Those seed the mask from sel.mask whenever a selection is active (mod.rs:11178-11220), which is Reveal Selection / Hide Selection behavior. Built-WASM probe: with a 3×3 selection, Reveal All hides pixel (8,8). Reveal/Hide Selection with no selection, and every add-mask command on a layer that already has a mask, return silently. All of these stay enabled (menuEnablement at App.tsx:3440-3470 has no rules for them).
findings.repro: Make a selection → Layer ▸ Layer Mask ▸ Reveal All. Everything outside the selection disappears.
findings.impact: The result is wrong whenever a selection is active. Other commands silently do nothing when the preconditions are not met.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the menu items selection-independent engine entry points and keep the selection-seeded path for the Layers-panel button. Add enablement rules (needs a selection; needs no existing mask).
findings.verdict_reason: The addmask and hidemask menu actions (App.tsx:2996-2997) call store.addLayerMask and addLayerMaskHidden (store.ts:8178-8190). Those call engine add_layer_mask and add_layer_mask_hidden, which seed the mask from sel.mask whenever sel.active (mod.rs:11187-11191, 11210-11214), so they behave as Reveal/Hide Selection. Reveal and Hide Selection return silently without a selection (e.g. 12486-12488). menuEnablement (App.tsx:3440-3470) has no entries for addmask, hidemask, revealsel or hidesel.

findings.title: Toggle commands keep static labels, so clicking 'Enable' disables; Hide All Effects is also not undoable or saved
findings.feature: Layer Mask ▸ Unlink; Vector Mask ▸ Enable / Link; Smart Filter ▸ Disable Filter Mask; Layer Style ▸ Hide All Effects
findings.evidence: vectormaskenable/vectormasklink → toggleVectorMaskEnabled/Linked (store.ts:7621-7633). unlinkmask → toggleLayerMaskLinked (store.ts:8225). disablefiltermask toggles (App.tsx:2943-2946). hidealleffects → toggleEffectsVisible (store.ts:7752). Only Create/Release Clipping Mask is relabelled (App.tsx buildMenus activeClipped). engine set_effects_visible (mod.rs:12646) pushes no undo, the state is not in MVSN, yet engine.commit() marks the doc dirty. psMenuData.ts:1714 labels Hide All 'Hide Layer Mask'.
findings.repro: Add a vector mask → Layer ▸ Vector Mask ▸ Enable. The mask turns OFF. Layer Style ▸ Hide All Effects → ⌘Z does not bring the effects back, and reopening the saved file shows them again.
findings.impact: Commands do the opposite of their label. Hide All Effects state is lost on save and cannot be undone.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel these items the way Release Clipping Mask is relabelled (Link/Unlink, Enable/Disable, Show/Hide All Effects, Enable/Disable Filter Mask), or use explicit set-true/false handlers. Push an undo step and persist effects_visible. Rename 'Hide Layer Mask' to 'Hide All'.
findings.verdict_reason: The Vector Mask 'Enable' and 'Link' items and the Layer Mask 'Unlink' item are single static rows (psMenuData.ts:1762-1807) wired to toggles (App.tsx:2990-2991, 3000; store.ts:7621-7633, 8225). A new vector mask has mask_enabled=true (mod.rs:11437), so 'Enable' turns it off. Only Create/Release Clipping Mask is relabelled (App.tsx:3515-3522), and the checkedIds set does not cover these items. set_effects_visible (mod.rs:12646-12653) pushes no undo. effects_visible appears only at construction and in the setter/getter, so it is never serialized. psMenuData.ts:1714 labels hidemask 'Hide Layer Mask' instead of 'Hide All'.

findings.title: Global Light only changes the active layer; 'Use Global Light' has no effect across layers; Satin wrongly follows Global Light
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Layer Style ▸ Global Light…, effect 'Use Global Light'
findings.evidence: setGlobalLight (store.ts:8589-8606) iterates only this.state.activeLayerId. There is no document-level angle (the GlobalLight dialog at Dialogs.tsx:1518-1545 says 'active layer'). Changing an effect's angle with Use Global Light ticked does not propagate. Satin's angle field is kind 'angle' (effects.ts, SATIN i:6), so FxFieldRow shows Use Global Light (Dialogs.tsx:12112-12120) and Global Light rotates it. Photoshop's Satin has no global light.
findings.repro: Two layers with drop shadows, both with Use Global Light → Layer ▸ Layer Style ▸ Global Light… 45°. Only the active layer's shadow moves.
findings.impact: Photoshop's document-wide lighting workflow does not work, and the checkbox misleads users.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a document global angle (persisted, and written as PSD resource 1037/gblA). Apply it to every effect with the flag on across all layers when it changes. Make Satin's angle a plain 'num' field.
findings.verdict_reason: setGlobalLight (store.ts:8589-8606) iterates only activeLayerId, and the dialog says 'active layer' (Dialogs.tsx:1548). No document-level angle exists, so editing one effect's angle with Use Global Light on does not propagate. Satin's Angle field is k:'angle' (effects.ts:224), so FxFieldRow shows Use Global Light and setGlobalLight rotates it. Gradient Overlay and Stroke were deliberately made 'num' for this reason (effects.ts:251-253, 279-281); Satin was missed.

findings.title: Copy/Paste Layer Style drops most Blending Options and pastes to one layer only
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Layer Style ▸ Copy / Paste Layer Style
findings.evidence: captureStyle (store.ts:8738-8748) stores only effects, blendIf and fillOpacity. pasteLayerStyle (8711-8725) applies them to activeLayerId only. Knockout, Transparency Shapes, Blend Interior/Clipped as Group, Channels, blend mode and opacity are not transferred. Paste stays enabled with an empty clipboard and silently does nothing.
findings.repro: Set Knockout Deep and untick R on layer A → Copy Layer Style → select layers B and C → Paste Layer Style. Only the active layer gets the effects, and neither knockout nor channels are pasted.
findings.impact: Pasted styles do not look like the source.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the full LayerStyleState that applyLayerStyleState already accepts, apply it to selectedLayerIds in one history step, and disable Paste when there is no clipboard.
findings.verdict_reason: captureStyle (store.ts:8738-8748) returns only effects, blendIf and fillOpacity, although the comment claims 'full advanced-blending state'. pasteLayerStyle (8711-8725) writes only to activeLayerId. Knockout, transparency shapes, the interior/clipped group flags and blend channels are not transferred, even though applyLayerStyleState can set them (store.ts:8560-8567). There is no fxpaste rule in menuEnablement (App.tsx:3440-3470), and pasteLayerStyle returns silently when styleClip is null.

findings.title: Scale Effects leaves pattern and gradient scale unscaled
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Layer Style ▸ Scale Effects…
findings.evidence: scaleEffects (store.ts:8571-8587) scales only fields with k === 'px'. Pattern Overlay Scale, Stroke Pattern Scale, Bevel Texture Scale and Gradient Overlay Scale are 'num' fields (effects.ts) and are skipped.
findings.repro: Layer with a Pattern Overlay → Scale Effects 200%. The pattern tile size is unchanged.
findings.impact: The scaled style no longer matches the proportions of the original when a document is resized.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the scale fields as scalable (for example a `scales: true` flag in FxDef) and multiply them as well.
findings.verdict_reason: scaleEffects (store.ts:8571-8587) multiplies only fields with k === 'px'. Pattern Overlay Scale (effects.ts:277), Stroke Pattern Scale (292), Bevel Texture Scale (212) and Gradient Overlay Scale (255) are 'num' and are skipped. Pattern scale is the clear parity gap. Whether Photoshop also scales Gradient Overlay's layer-relative Scale is less certain.

findings.title: Rasterize ▸ Vector Mask deletes a work-path or shape outline that is not a vector mask
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Rasterize ▸ Vector Mask
findings.evidence: rasterize_vector_mask (mod.rs:12467-12480) gates on vector_path.is_empty() and not on has_vector_mask. delete_vector_mask (12443-12451) was fixed for this exact confusion. Outlines with vector_is_mask=false come from Create Work Path / Convert to Shape (mod.rs:12027-12062). The menu item is always enabled (App.tsx:2987).
findings.repro: Type ▸ Convert to Shape on a type layer whose font has no outline data (the pixel-trace fallback) → Layer ▸ Rasterize ▸ Vector Mask. The shape outline is cleared and a 'Rasterize Vector Mask' step is recorded.
findings.impact: Silently drops the layer's path data. Undo recovers it.
findings.suggested_fix: Gate on has_vector_mask(id) and set last_edit_error otherwise, mirroring delete_vector_mask.
findings.verdict_reason: rasterize_vector_mask (mod.rs:12467-12482) checks only vector_path.is_empty(), not has_vector_mask. It then clears vector_path and anchors under a 'Rasterize Vector Mask' undo step. store.rasterizeVectorMask (store.ts:7363-7366) adds no guard. Outlines with vector_is_mask=false are written by both the glyph-outline branch (mod.rs:12031) and the pixel-trace fallback (12062). delete_vector_mask was already fixed for the same confusion (12445-12451).

findings.title: Clear Smart Filters ignores the layer lock that every other smart-filter command respects
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Smart Filter ▸ Clear Smart Filters
findings.evidence: smart_clear_filters (mod.rs:14774-14790) has no refuse_locked_smart. set_smart_filters_enabled, add/delete/enable filter mask and smart_add_filter all refuse on locked layers (14813+, 14548 comment: 'lock is the user's only protection').
findings.repro: Lock All on a smart object with filters → Layer ▸ Smart Filter ▸ Clear Smart Filters. The filters are removed.
findings.impact: Lock protection is inconsistent, and locked content can be destroyed.
findings.suggested_fix: Call refuse_locked_smart(id) before the undo push.
findings.verdict_reason: smart_clear_filters (mod.rs:14774-14790) checks kind, empty filters and float, then pushes undo and clears, with no refuse_locked_smart call. set_smart_filters_enabled calls refuse_locked_smart (14820-14822), as do the other filter commands. The TS wrapper smart.clearFilters (app.ts:2477) adds no lock check either.

findings.title: New Smart Object via Copy on a non-smart layer silently becomes a plain Duplicate (two history steps, only one recorded)
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Smart Objects ▸ New Smart Object via Copy
findings.evidence: smartviacopy runs store.duplicateLayer and then smart.detach. detach_smart_object returns false for kind != 7 (mod.rs:14204-14212). The item is always enabled. duplicateLayer is a recorded op but detach is not, so a macro replays this as a linked-instance duplicate.
findings.repro: Select a pixel layer → New Smart Object via Copy. You get a pixel copy and no smart object. Recording the command on a smart object and replaying it produces a linked instance.
findings.impact: The menu says one thing and does another. Undo takes two steps, and recorded actions diverge.
findings.suggested_fix: Enable only for smart objects and implement it as one engine op (duplicate + detach) with one history step, and make it recordable.
findings.verdict_reason: smartviacopy runs store.duplicateLayer and then smart.detach (App.tsx:2936). detach_smart_object returns false for kind != 7 or an unshared source (mod.rs:14208-14215). smart.detach still calls engine.commit (app.ts:2467-2471). There is no enablement rule. duplicateLayer is in RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:906), but the smart namespace is not recorded (see the next finding), so a macro replays only the duplicate.

findings.title: Vector-mask and smart-object commands are not macro-recordable
findings.feature: Actions recording for Vector Mask ▸ *, Smart Objects ▸ *, Smart Filter ▸ *
findings.evidence: RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:904-958) contains the layer-mask ops but none of addVectorMaskRevealAll/HideAll, addVectorMaskFromPath, deleteVectorMask, toggleVectorMaskEnabled/Linked or rasterizeVectorMask. The `smart` namespace (convert, rasterize, clearFilters, setFiltersEnabled, filter mask, resetTransform, replace) is neither proxied nor in visionOps' ns list (app.ts:2334).
findings.repro: Record an action: Convert to Smart Object → Vector Mask ▸ Hide All. Stop. The action has no steps for either.
findings.impact: Photoshop records these steps. Batch and droplet workflows built on them replay incompletely.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the vector-mask store methods to RECORDED_STORE_OPS, and wrap the smart.* mutators with recordedCall. The linked-file pickers need their paths as arguments.
findings.verdict_reason: RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:904-958) lists the layer-mask ops but no addVectorMask*, deleteVectorMask, toggleVectorMask* or rasterizeVectorMask. `smart` is a plain object (app.ts:2449) with no recordedCall wrappers, and visionOps' ns list is { adj, fil, xform, neural, anim, distort } (app.ts:2334), so smart.* ops are neither recorded nor replayable. No menu-level recorder exists either: the only other paths are actions.recordTool for canvas tools and insertMenuItem for manual insertion.

findings.title: PSD export silently turns Vision-created smart objects (and their smart filters) and vector masks into pixels
findings.feature: Smart Objects / Smart Filters / Vector Mask PSD round-trip
findings.evidence: Kind 7 without SoLd/SoLE/PlLd is written as Raster (format_import.rs:1722-1735). synthesized_photoshop_vector_blocks emits vmsk only for kind-3 shapes (format_import.rs:252-330), so a vector mask on any other layer leaves only as its rasterized user mask. Built-WASM probe: convert_to_smart_object + Gaussian smart filter → export_psd → fromFormat gives layer kind 0, 0 filters, and photoshop_export_notice() is ''. A vector mask → PSD → reopen gives has_vector_mask false and has_mask true.
findings.repro: Convert a layer to a smart object, add Filter ▸ Blur ▸ Gaussian Blur (smart), add Vector Mask ▸ Current Path → Save As PSD → reopen in Vision or Photoshop. You get a flattened pixel layer with a pixel mask, and nothing warns you.
findings.impact: Editability is lost with no warning, although the appearance is kept. The notice infrastructure already exists and is used for nested smart objects.
findings.suggested_fix: Push photoshop_export_notice entries for each smart object or vector mask that is downgraded. Write vmsk for vector masks on any layer kind (encode_vector_mask already exists).
findings.verdict_reason: A kind-7 layer without a SoLd, SoLE or PlLd block maps to Raster (format_import.rs:1722-1733). fresh_photoshop_smart_objects skips layers with no smart_link or empty smart_doc, and descriptor-less layers with filters, without pushing a notice (mod.rs:30189-30214). Its own doc comment says these keep exporting rendered pixels. synthesized_photoshop_vector_blocks emits vmsk only for kind 3 (format_import.rs:261-287), so a vector mask on any other layer leaves only as its rasterized user mask, with no photoshop_export_notice. Appearance is preserved; editability is lost silently.

findings.title: No test exports a PSD from the layer styles and adjustment layers Vision's own UI creates
findings.feature: PSD export of layer styles / adjustment layers
findings.evidence: The only PSD export fixtures with a Vision effect use a hand-built 6-float Color Overlay (format_import.rs:6068) or map_effects output (4648). No e2e test exports a PSD after using Layer Style or New Adjustment Layer (grep over e2e/ for export_psd with effects or adjustment layers finds nothing). That is why the two blocker refusals shipped.
findings.repro: n/a
findings.impact: Regressions in the most common PSD save path go unnoticed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an engine test that builds layers from the TS FX_DEFS and ADJ_SPECS defaults (mirrored as constants or through engineContracts) and asserts export_psd/export_psb succeed and reopen equivalently. Add one e2e that goes through the dialogs and then Save As PSD.
findings.verdict_reason: None of the e2e specs that export PSD (io, psd-*, batch-dialog, paths-panel, color-management, float-32bit) set layer effects or add adjustment layers (grep for set_layer_effect, setEffect and addAdjustmentLayer in those files found none). The engine refusal tests (format_import.rs:5077-5098) use hand-built or broken payloads, not FX_DEFS or ADJ_SPECS defaults. Both blocker refusals above are consistent with no success-path coverage.

findings.title: Update Edited Contents from the menu fails silently when the parent document or layer is gone
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Smart Objects ▸ Update Edited Contents
findings.evidence: updateEditedContents returns false without notify() when the parent doc cannot be activated or the layer is no longer a smart object (app.ts:2818-2829). The soupdate handler (App.tsx:2950) ignores the return value. The MCP wrapper, by contrast, throws a clear message (commands.ts:942-952).
findings.repro: Edit Contents → close the parent document → in the contents tab choose Update Edited Contents. Nothing happens.
findings.impact: The user gets no feedback about why the update did not happen.
findings.suggested_fix: notify() on each false branch, as the layered-contents path already does.
findings.verdict_reason: updateEditedContents (app.ts:2813-2829) returns false without notify() when there is no binding, when activateDoc cannot reach the parent, or when the layer is no longer a smart object. Only the layered replace refusal notifies (2833-2836). The soupdate handler (App.tsx:2950) discards the return value.

areas.coverage:
This was a read-only code review. I ran no builds, suites or single test files.

What I inventoried:
- Type menu: 81 enabled leaf commands, taken from psMenuData.ts plus the psMenus.ts LABEL_WIRING and PATH_WIRING tables:
  - New Text Layer and Edit Text
  - 5 Panels
  - 7 Anti-Alias
  - 2 Orientation
  - 30 of 30 OpenType. Only 4 carry a monetId, but PATH_WIRING wires calt, swsh, onum, salt, titl, jalt and ss01–ss20.
  - Create Work Path and Convert to Shape
  - Rasterize Type Layer and Convert to Paragraph Text
  - Text on Path submenu (Create, Bind, Options)
  - Warp Text, Match Font and Match Font (Image AI)
  - 6 Font Preview Size
  - 13 of 16 Language Options leaves
  - Update All Text Layers, Replace All Missing Fonts and Resolve Missing Fonts
  - Paste Lorem Ipsum and Load/Save Default Type Styles
- Commands outside the Type menu: Edit ▸ Find and Replace Text, Edit ▸ Check Spelling, Preferences ▸ Type, and Layer ▸ Rasterize ▸ Type / Layer / All Layers.
- 4 type tools: text, verticaltype, horizontaltypemask, verticaltypemask.
- UI surfaces: the Character and Paragraph dock panels, the TypeToolbar options bar, the on-canvas TextEditOverlay, and 7 dialogs (Type, Glyphs, Character/Paragraph Styles, Match Font, Type on a Path Options, Find/Replace, Check Spelling).

How I traced it: each command from UI to App.tsx menuActions, then the `text` namespace in state/app.ts (29 recorded ops), then store.ts (text-edit session, Type Mask, applyTypeOutline), then src/text/* (spec, raster, warp, outline). On the engine side I followed set_text_layer_spec, text_edit_session, rasterize_text_layer, set_type_outline and outline_text_scene, the vector font registry (fonts.rs with_font_for_style) and host font provisioning (vectorFonts.ts). I also checked how Crop, Image Size, rotate, flip and Align/Distribute (reframe_document, resample_document, remap_document, shift_layer) and layer transforms (rasterize_active_text_metadata) interact with type layers.

Test coverage: I grepped every in-scope action against unit tests and e2e specs:
- Unit: text/*.test.ts, typeStyleLinks, typeOutlines, glyphCaretInsert.
- e2e: text, text-inplace, type-toolbar, type-mask, vertical-type, type-outlines, opentype-toggles, east-asian-features, match-font, text-on-path-options, system-font-faces, and the Check Spelling case in feature-regressions.

MCP: there are no dedicated type tools. Type is reachable only through script.run or action playback of the `text.*` recorded ops.

Not reviewed or not confirmable by reading:
- How the native WKWebView renders canvas text. Font-feature-settings and platform shaping are only exercised in Chromium e2e.
- PSD type import/export fidelity.
- Collaboration.
- Real performance numbers.

Confidence notes:
- Finding 7 depends on Inter not being installed. It is not bundled, and to my knowledge macOS does not ship it.
- Finding 16 is based on reading the code path, not on profiling.
areas.parity_notes:
Photoshop items shown disabled, which are placeholders and not bugs:
- Type ▸ Language Options ▸ Default
- Type ▸ Language Options ▸ Middle Eastern Features. The individual Middle Eastern commands (direction, digits, kashidas, composers) are implemented.
- Type ▸ Language Options ▸ Indic Features. The label is wired to `langindic` but has no handler, deliberately, per the ponytail comment in psMenus.ts.

Counts in scope:

- Language Options: 13 of 16 leaves are live.

Behaviour that differs from Photoshop but is disclosed in code or tests rather than silently wrong:
- Glyphs and Character/Paragraph Styles open as modal dialogs, not dockable panels.
- Find and Replace offers only Replace All; there is no Find Next, Change or Change/Find.
- One paragraph style applies per layer; Next Style advances between layers, not at Enter.
- Style definitions are stored per app (localStorage), not per document.
- Leading is per layer, not per run.
- Warp/perspective/distort on type rasterizes it.
- The on-canvas editor lays out with the first run's style only and does not warp.
- Vertical and on-path type have no in-place editor.

MCP:
- There are no dedicated type MCP tools. Type is reachable only through script.run and action playback of the recorded `text.*` ops.

Not verified by reading:
- Whether WKWebView's canvas honours font-feature-settings and variation settings. Every e2e runs in Chromium only.

findings.title: Crop, Canvas Size, Image Size, Image Rotation, Flip Canvas, Trim and Align/Distribute move or resample type pixels but leave the type spec stale, so the next text edit snaps the text back
findings.feature: Type layers across document geometry and Layer ▸ Align/Distribute
findings.evidence: packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:25423-25467: reframe_document (Crop, Canvas Size) remaps the pixels of every non-kind-0 layer, including kind 2 type, but leaves layer.text_spec alone. mod.rs:25177-25265: resample_document (Image Size) resamples type pixels and keeps kind 2 with the unscaled spec. mod.rs:26441 and 26492: flip_horizontal and rotate_90 remap_document the pixels only. mod.rs:10021-10044: shift_layer, used by align_layers at mod.rs (align) and distribute, shifts the plane contents only. On the host side, apps/vision/src/state/app.ts:3496-3521 runGeometryEdit and store.ts:3560-3574 remapDocSpaceAnnotations remap only guides, notes and color samplers. Every later edit goes through app.ts:2920 applyTextSpec, then rasterizeSpec, which places the text from spec.ax/ay/size (text/raster.ts:1517-1519). The Move tool is the only path that re-anchors the spec (canvas/CanvasView.tsx:2213-2219). No unit, e2e or engine test combines a type layer with crop, resize, rotate or align.
findings.repro:
1. Create a type layer at about (400,300).
2. Image ▸ Crop to a selection at (200,200), or Image ▸ Image Size to 50%, or Image Rotation 90°.
3. Change the font size in the Character panel, or run Type ▸ Update All Text Layers.
The text re-renders at its old coordinates and size, un-rotated. It is often offset or pushed off the canvas.
findings.impact: Silent layout corruption. Text looks right after the geometry edit, then jumps the next time anything touches the type. Update All Text Layers does this to every type layer at once. Can reach exported files unnoticed.
findings.suggested_fix:
Transform the type spec whenever the engine moves type pixels:
- Offset: shift ax/ay (and path points) by dx/dy.
- Image Size: scale size, leading, tracking, box and indents.
- Rotate/flip: rasterize, the way layer transforms already do.
The spec is JSON the engine already parses (mod.rs:11832), so this can be done in reframe_document, resample_document, remap_document and shift_layer, or on the host after runGeometryEdit and align. Add an e2e test: crop, then edit the text, and assert the ink position.
findings.verdict_reason: The engine never maps text_spec during a geometry edit. Its only writes are the color transform (mod.rs:7007), set_text_layer_spec (16027) and the rasterize paths. reframe_document (mod.rs:25423-25467) remaps the pixels of every non-kind-0 layer and leaves text_spec and text_x/text_y alone. resample_document (25177-25265) resamples the pixels and scales ox/oy only. align_layers (10183-10229) calls shift_layer (10021), which moves the plane contents only. On the host, runGeometryEdit (app.ts:3496-3521) and remapDocSpaceAnnotations (store.ts:3560-3574) remap only guides, notes and samplers. flipH/flipV (app.ts:3549-3550) and alignLayer/distributeLayers (store.ts:7690-7700, 2653-2656) just commit. The next applyTextSpec (app.ts:2920) re-rasterizes from spec.ax/ay (raster.ts:1517-1519) into a zeroed plane (mod.rs:16012). Only the Move tool re-anchors the spec (CanvasView.tsx:2214-2219). The team fixed exactly this failure for layer transforms by baking the type (transformBakesType.test.ts header), but not for canvas geometry. No test combines type with crop, resize, rotate or align; ps-fidelity.spec.ts:275 covers crop and resize without type.

findings.title: Free Transform, Scale, Rotate, Flip or Skew on a type layer rasterizes the type silently, so it is no longer editable
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Free Transform / Transform on type layers
findings.evidence: packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:3855-3865: rasterize_active_text_metadata sets kind to 0 and clears text_spec. It is called from every layer transform (mod.rs:26849, 26896, 27052, 27068, 27084, 27104, 27547). apps/vision/src/state/app.ts:3523-3529: bakeTransform just runs and commits, and app.ts:3566 routes transform_layer through it. There is no toast, confirm dialog or warning anywhere on the path. transformBakesType.test.ts pins this as intended.
findings.repro:
1. Create a type layer.
2. Edit ▸ Free Transform, scale it 150% and commit.
3. Double-click it, or look at the Character panel.
It is now a pixel layer. The typo can only be fixed by undoing the scale.
findings.impact: In Photoshop, scale, rotate, flip and skew keep type editable. Only perspective, distort and warp ask before rasterizing. Here a very common step silently destroys editability. It can be undone, but nothing tells the user it happened.
findings.suggested_fix:
Short term: warn or confirm before a transform rasterizes a type layer, as Photoshop does for distort and perspective.
Proper fix: add an affine transform matrix to TextSpec, applied in rasterizeSpec and typeOutlineScene, so scale, rotate, flip and skew stay live.
findings.verdict_reason: rasterize_active_text_metadata (mod.rs:3859-3865) sets kind 0 and clears text_spec. It is called from all 7 layer-transform paths (26849, 26896, 27052, 27068, 27084, 27104, 27547). bakeTransform (app.ts:3527-3530) only runs the transform and commits. Nowhere in app.ts, CanvasView or Dialogs does a warning, confirm or toast mention the rasterization; my grep for rasterize plus warn/toast/confirm found nothing on this path. The behavior is deliberate and pinned by transformBakesType.test.ts, and one Undo restores editable type. So this is silent loss of editability, not pixel loss. Scaling a headline is a very common step, and Photoshop keeps type live for it, so major stands for a Photoshop-class release. The data-loss category overstates it; ux or parity fits better.

findings.title: Lock All is ignored by type editing: text, font and Character/Paragraph edits and Rasterize Type all apply to a locked type layer
findings.feature: Type editing on locked layers (on-canvas editor, TypeToolbar, Character/Paragraph panels, Type menu, Rasterize Type)
findings.evidence: packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:15965-16038: set_text_layer_spec checks only the layer kind (0 or 2) and the imported-PSD guard, never .locked. mod.rs:16060-16072: rasterize_text_layer has no lock check. On the host, app.ts:2920-2925 applyTextSpec, store.ts:2759 beginTextEdit and CanvasView.tsx:2558-2565 editText do not consult layer_locked either. Convert to Shape does refuse (mod.rs:11952 refuse_locked_vector), and Check Spelling excludes locked layers (Dialogs.tsx:3682). Find and Replace does not (app.ts:3442-3455).
findings.repro:
1. Create a type layer.
2. In the Layers panel, turn on Lock All.
3. With the Move tool, double-click the canvas and type. Or change the font in the Character panel or the options bar. Or run Type ▸ Anti-Alias ▸ None, Edit ▸ Find and Replace, or Type ▸ Rasterize Type Layer.
Every one of these edits the locked layer.
findings.impact: The lock does not protect type, and behavior is inconsistent across type commands.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse in set_text_layer_spec and rasterize_text_layer when layers[i].locked is set, with last_edit_error, as refuse_locked_vector does. Have editText and beginTextEdit decline to open the editor on a locked layer, and skip locked layers in findReplace, updateAll and replaceMissingFonts.
findings.verdict_reason: set_text_layer_spec (mod.rs:15965-16038) checks only reject_imported_photoshop_edit and kind 0|2, never layers[i].locked. rasterize_text_layer (16060-16072) has no lock check either. By contrast, refuse_locked_transform (3847) and refuse_locked_vector (11952) exist. On the host, applyTextSpec (app.ts:2920-2925), every text.* action (app.ts:3146-3455), beginTextEdit (store.ts:2759-2770), editText (CanvasView.tsx:2558-2565) and the double-click handler (2773) never read layer.locked. SpellCheck is the only type command that filters locked layers (Dialogs.tsx:3681-3684); FindReplace (Dialogs.tsx:3651) and findReplace (app.ts:3442-3455) do not. The release lens explicitly calls silently ignoring a locked layer major.

findings.title: Character Styles and Save/Load Default Type Styles read and write layer-level defaults, while every formatting UI writes per-run attributes, so styles capture stale values and applying them has no effect
findings.feature: Type ▸ Panels ▸ Character Styles; Type ▸ Save/Load Default Type Styles; Redefine, overrides badge and Clear Override
findings.evidence:
The style code works on layer-level fields:
- state/app.ts:2937-2951: styleFields and charStyleFields read spec.font, size, color, bold, italic, tracking and so on.
- app.ts:3257-3278: addTypeStyle and applyTypeStyle, and app.ts:3236-3251: save/loadDefaultStyles, also read and write these layer-level fields.

Every formatting UI writes run-level fields with applyRangeFormat over the whole range:
- ui/Panels.tsx:3888 (Character panel charPatch)
- ui/Dialogs.tsx:11977-11980 (TypeToolbar charAll)
- ui/Dialogs.tsx:11687 (Type dialog charPatch)

Rendering prefers the run: text/spec.ts:196-201 resolveStyle uses run.font ?? spec.font and run.size ?? spec.size. typeStyleLinks.test.ts only patches layer-level fields (line 50), so the real UI path is untested.
findings.repro:
1. Create type.
2. In the options bar or Character panel, set the font to Georgia, size 120 and color red.
3. Character Styles ▸ New from Selection, named "Headline".
4. Select another type layer that has also been formatted in the panel, and click Apply.
Nothing changes visibly. On a fresh layer, Apply gives the original creation defaults, not Georgia/120/red. Type ▸ Save Default Type Styles after the same formatting saves the untouched defaults. The "+" override badge never appears after panel edits.
findings.impact: Character Styles, Redefine, Clear Override and Default Type Styles effectively do not work in normal use.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture from the resolved style of the selection or first run (resolveStyle over the runs), not from the spec root. When applying a style, write it onto the runs in the range: applyRangeFormat with the style fields, clearing conflicting run overrides. Compute overrides from resolved run styles. Add a unit test that formats through applyRangeFormat before addTypeStyle.
findings.verdict_reason: charStyleFields and styleFields (app.ts:2937-2951) read spec.font, size, color and the other root fields. addTypeStyle, applyTypeStyle, redefineTypeStyle and clearTypeStyleOverride (app.ts:3257-3350) spread those fields onto the spec root. Every character control writes run fields instead. The Character panel's font, size, tracking, color, bold and italic call charPatch, which is applyRangeFormat over the runs (Panels.tsx:3888, 3913-3975). The TypeToolbar uses charAll over the whole range (Dialogs.tsx:11977-11980, 12013). The Type dialog uses charPatch (11687). resolveStyle (spec.ts:196-201) prefers run.font/size/color over the spec, so a root-level apply is hidden by any run override, and a capture made after panel formatting records the stale root values. The UI calls these actions directly (Dialogs.tsx:4514, 4548-4549; App.tsx:3064). typeStyleLinks.test.ts patches root fields only (line 50), so the real UI path is untested. Paragraph styles are unaffected, because paragraph controls do write the root.

findings.title: Clicking over an existing type layer with the Type tool creates a new layer instead of editing the existing one
findings.feature: Horizontal/Vertical Type tools: re-editing existing type
findings.evidence: canvas/CanvasView.tsx:1529-1538: pointerdown for the type tools only starts a drag preview. CanvasView.tsx:2255-2264: pointerup always calls doText. CanvasView.tsx:2544-2553: doText always calls text.createAt, which always creates a layer (app.ts:3116-3143, createTextLayer at 3058). There is no hit test against existing type bounds. The only in-place re-edit is onDoubleClick calling editText(activeLayerId) (CanvasView.tsx:2773). It needs the layer to be active already, fires wherever you double-click, and with the Type tool the first click has already created a new layer. The e2e test for re-editing (text-inplace.spec.ts:77-96) deliberately switches to the Move tool.
findings.repro:
1. With the Type tool (T), click on the canvas, type "Hello" and press Esc.
2. Still with the Type tool, click on the word "Hello" to fix a typo.
A second "Text Layer 2" with a selected "Type" placeholder appears on top instead of a caret in "Hello".
findings.impact: Photoshop's main way to edit type is broken. It produces stray layers, and users have to discover the Move-tool double-click.
findings.suggested_fix: In the type-tool pointerdown/up handler, hit-test the topmost visible kind-2 layer whose rendered bounds contain the point. If found, select it and beginTextEdit(id), placing the caret at the click (textarea selectionStart from caretPositionFromPoint). Only create a new layer when nothing is hit.
findings.verdict_reason: The type-tool pointerdown only sets a rect preview (CanvasView.tsx:1529-1538). pointerup always calls doText (2255-2264), and doText always calls text.createAt (2544-2551), which always goes through createTextLayer and store.addLayer (app.ts:3058-3070, 3116-3143). There is no hit test against existing type. If the editor is open, the first click only commits it (CanvasView.tsx:1139); after Esc, the next click creates a new layer. A double-click with the Type tool therefore creates a layer on the first click and re-opens the editor on that new layer. The only in-place re-edit is editText(activeLayerId) on double-click (2773), and the e2e test for it switches to the Move tool first (text-inplace.spec.ts:77-84).

findings.title: The Glyphs panel always appends the glyph to the end of the layer, ignoring the caret and the font chosen in the panel
findings.feature: Type ▸ Panels ▸ Glyphs
findings.evidence: ui/Dialogs.tsx:4019-4034: insert() calls text.apply(activeId, appendGlyph(base, ch, ...)). appendGlyph is insertGlyph(spec, ch, null) (text/spec.ts:334-356), and null means append. The caret-aware text.insertGlyph (state/app.ts:3221-3233), which reads the on-canvas editor selection and advances the caret, is never called from the UI. glyphCaretInsert.test.ts and glyphCaretAdvance.test.ts only test the unused action. The panel's Font select (Dialogs.tsx:4061-4062) only changes the preview grid; the inserted run keeps the caret run's font. Macro recording logs text.apply instead of Insert Glyph.
findings.repro:
1. Type "Hello World" on canvas.
2. Put the caret after "Hello".
3. Type ▸ Panels ▸ Glyphs, click ©.
Result: "Hello World©", not "Hello© World". Picking a symbol font in the panel and inserting still renders in the layer's font.
findings.impact: Common glyph insertion lands in the wrong place, and the fix that exists in the action layer never reaches users.
findings.suggested_fix: Call text.insertGlyph(ch, tag ? { [tag]: true } : undefined) from the dialog, and drop appendGlyph there. Pass the panel's family as a run patch, for example { font: family }, when it differs from the run at the caret. Add a Glyphs-dialog e2e test with the caret in mid-text.
findings.verdict_reason: Glyphs insert() (Dialogs.tsx:4019-4034) calls text.apply(activeId, appendGlyph(...)). appendGlyph is insertGlyph(spec, ch, null) (spec.ts:355-356), and a null range means append at prev.length (spec.ts:341-342). The caret-aware text.insertGlyph (app.ts:3221-3233, which reads typeEditorSelection) has no UI caller; a grep finds only its definition and the recording list. The panel's Font select (4061-4062) only feeds the preview grid and fontCoverage; insert passes no font, so setText gives the new glyph the caret run's style. The action is recorded as text.apply, not text.insertGlyph (app.ts:3462-3471). Major is fair for a wrong result in the panel's main path.

findings.title: Create Work Path and Convert to Shape fail with the default type font, because generic families (system-ui/sans-serif) are never provisioned and Inter is not bundled
findings.feature: Type ▸ Create Work Path / Convert to Shape
findings.evidence: text/spec.ts:358-359: new type defaults to FONTS[0] = "Inter, system-ui, sans-serif". engine/vectorFonts.ts:89-93 and 131-136: fontFamilyNames drops system-ui and sans-serif, so the only provisioning target is "Inter". Inter is not bundled anywhere (monet-core CSS only names it in a stack; there is no @font-face). packages/engine/src/vector/fonts.rs:142-185: with_font_for_style matches exact family keys only (inter, system-ui, sans-serif), so no face resolves, and outline_text_scene returns "" (raster/mod.rs:11916-11918). state/store.ts:7367-7381: applyTypeOutline then reports "needs outline data for this layer's font… Choose an installed font". The e2e test (type-outlines.spec.ts:62-70) always registers a fixture font first, so the default-font case is untested.
findings.repro:
1. On a Mac without Inter installed, pick the Type tool, click and type "Hi", and commit.
2. Type ▸ Convert to Shape, or Type ▸ Create Work Path.
You get the error toast and nothing is converted, although the canvas shows the text in the system UI font.
findings.impact: The standard type-to-shape workflow fails on stock systems unless the user first switches the font by hand.
findings.suggested_fix: Map generic families to concrete registered faces during provisioning. For example, alias system-ui and sans-serif to the platform UI face (SF Pro / Helvetica), serif to Times, monospace to Menlo. Or fall back to the first registered face that covers the text. Alternatively, change the default font to a family that is actually provisioned. Add an e2e test with the default spec.
findings.verdict_reason: defaultSpec uses FONTS[0] = "Inter, system-ui, sans-serif" (spec.ts:359, 475). createAt passes no font (app.ts:3121-3126). Provisioning drops generic families (vectorFonts.ts:89-93, 131-136), so the only target is "inter". The only Inter file in the repo is test-assets/fixtures/Inter-Regular.woff2, and there are no bundled engine fonts; every include_bytes font is testdata. typeOutlineScene passes fontFamily = renderFontFamily(st) (outline.ts:24, raster.ts:592). build_registered_font_text_path and its family fallback (render.rs:1011-1034, 1386) resolve only through with_font_for_style (fonts.rs:142-185), which matches exact family keys. So outline_text_scene returns "" (mod.rs:11916-11918), and applyTypeOutline raises the 'needs outline data' error (store.ts:7376-7381). The e2e test always registers a fixture font first (type-outlines.spec.ts:67-68). Two things remain unverified: whether the target macOS ships or commonly has Inter, and that the refusal has a clear message and an easy workaround. Both keep confidence at medium.

findings.title: Match Font does not identify a font from the image: the dialog ranks fonts by name against the layer's own font, and the Image AI variant reads the whole unselected composite and offers no way to apply its result
findings.feature: Type ▸ Match Font… / Match Font (Image AI)…
findings.evidence:
ui/Dialogs.tsx:6401-6418: MatchFontDialog calls rankFontMatches(current, FONTS), a name, token and class heuristic in state/matchFont.ts:61-98. The current font scores +1000 against itself, so the preselected result is always the layer's own font and OK does nothing. The dialog also needs an existing type layer; it never looks at pixels.

The OK path at Dialogs.tsx:6417 sets run.font but keeps run.face. renderFontFamily (text/spec.ts:240-244) puts the face alias first, so a run styled with the Style picker keeps rendering the old face even after the font changes.

Match Font (Image AI), App.tsx:3212-3216 calling ml/onnx.ts:935-953 matchFontML: classifies export_png() of the whole document, squashed to 224×224 (onnx.ts:938-940), ignoring the selection, and only shows a toast with the top 3 names. It cannot be applied, and runMl then pushes a second "Done." toast (App.tsx:2134).
findings.repro:
Case 1:
1. Open a photo containing a sign.
2. Draw a marquee around the lettering.
3. Type ▸ Match Font….
The dialog says "Select an editable type layer"; the pixels are never read.

Case 2:
1. On a type layer, pick a font style in the Character panel.
2. Match Font, choose another font, OK.
The canvas keeps the old face.

Case 3: Match Font (Image AI) with a selection returns a ranking for the whole image and offers nothing to apply.
findings.impact: Two menu entries are presented as Photoshop's Match Font, but neither matches the selected text in the image.
findings.suggested_fix:
Relabel or disable the name-based dialog as "Similar Fonts", or feed it the ML ranking. For the AI path:
- Crop the composite to the selection bounds, with padding and aspect-preserving letterbox, before the classifier.
- Map the class names to installed FONTS.
- Open the dialog with those candidates so OK applies one.
When applying a font, clear `face` (as applyRangeFormat does for font patches).
findings.verdict_reason: MatchFontDialog (Dialogs.tsx:6401-6418) calls rankFontMatches(current, text.FONTS, ...). This is a name, token and class heuristic (matchFont.ts:61-98), and an exact match scores +1000, so the preselected result is the layer's own font and OK changes nothing. Without a type layer the dialog shows only 'Select an editable type layer.' OK spreads {...r, font} and so keeps r.face (6417), while renderFontFamily (spec.ts:240-244) puts the face alias first, so the old face keeps rendering. matchfontai (App.tsx:3212-3216) calls matchFontML (onnx.ts:935-953), whose composite() (onnx.ts:76-86) runs export_png over the whole document, resized to 224×224 without looking at the selection. The result only goes to a toast, and runMl then pushes a second 'Done.' toast (App.tsx:2134). The menu advertises both items (psMenuData.ts:2610-2618).

findings.title: Vertical type is edited only in the options-bar text field, where every keystroke is a separate full-document undo step
findings.feature: Vertical Type / Vertical Type Mask tools; TypeToolbar text field
findings.evidence: state/app.ts:3129-3137: createAt closes the text_edit_session for vertical type and opens no on-canvas editor. ui/Dialogs.tsx:12002-12003: the TypeToolbar Textarea calls apply(text.setText(...)) on every change with no session. packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:16004-16011: with text_session false, each set_text_layer_spec calls push_stack_undo("Type"), a full doc_snap clone of every layer (mod.rs:5505-5517). Horizontal edits made in the same field are affected too when the canvas editor is closed.
findings.repro:
1. Pick the Vertical Type tool, click, and type a 40-character phrase in the options-bar field.
2. Open History.
There are 40 "Type" states. Earlier states beyond the History States cap are evicted.
findings.impact: The history panel fills up, earlier undo history is lost, and memory churns on large documents.
findings.suggested_fix: Open text_edit_session(true) while the TypeToolbar field has focus (onFocus) and close it on blur, mirroring beginTextEdit and endTextEdit.
findings.verdict_reason: createAt closes the session for vertical type (app.ts:3133-3136), and editText also defers vertical type to the toolbar (CanvasView.tsx:2563). The TypeToolbar Textarea onChange calls apply, then text.apply(setText) (Dialogs.tsx:12002-12003), and it never opens text_edit_session. The only session callers are app.ts:3120/3134, store.ts:2455/2769/2780 and the Type dialog (Dialogs.tsx:11600-11709). With text_session false, each set_text_layer_spec calls push_stack_undo('Type') (mod.rs:16004-16011), which takes doc_snap, a clone of every layer (mod.rs:5505-5517, 5692-5697).

findings.title: Find and Replace and Check Spelling restyle everything between the first and last change, and Find and Replace also edits locked and hidden layers in several undo steps
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Find and Replace Text…; Edit ▸ Check Spelling…
findings.evidence:
state/app.ts:3442-3455: findReplace rebuilds the whole string and calls setText(s, after). text/spec.ts:572-622: setText diffs one common prefix and suffix and styles the whole middle splice like the run before it. With two replacements far apart, every run between them, including untouched bold or colored spans, loses its formatting. The doc comment (app.ts:3438-3441) claims only the replaced spans are affected. Check Spelling applies the same way (Dialogs.tsx:3690-3693).

findReplace with allLayers, the dialog default (Dialogs.tsx:3649), walks every layer with no locked or visible filter. Each changed layer is its own applyTextSpec undo step, with no transaction.
findings.repro:
1. Create type "cat **big dog** cat" with the middle words bold and red.
2. Find and Replace "cat" with "cow".
The middle words lose bold and red.

Also: lock a second type layer that contains "cat"; it is changed too. Undo takes one step per layer.
findings.impact: Rich formatting is lost silently, locks are bypassed, and undo is fragmented.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace match by match with a range splice: for each match, apply setText for that span only, or add a spliceText(spec, start, end, str) helper that keeps the runs outside [start,end). Skip locked and hidden layers as SpellCheck does. Wrap multi-layer runs in begin/commit_history_transaction.
findings.verdict_reason: findReplace (app.ts:3442-3455) rebuilds the whole string and calls setText. setText (spec.ts:576-622) diffs a single common prefix and suffix and injects the whole middle with the style of the run before it (styleAt(p-1)). For 'cat big dog cat' to 'cow big dog cow', p=1 and s=0, so 'big dog' takes the plain style of the 'c' run. SpellCheck applies the same way (Dialogs.tsx:3690-3692). findReplace takes all layer ids with no visible or locked filter when allLayers is on, which is the dialog default (Dialogs.tsx:3649). Each changed layer is a separate applyTextSpec call, pushing a 'Type' undo step outside any session or transaction.

findings.title: Most Type menu commands stay enabled with no type layer and silently do nothing; Edit Text… and Warp Text… on a non-type layer create a new type layer
findings.feature: Type menu enablement
findings.evidence: App.tsx:3460-3470: menuEnablement gates only langeastasian on activeIsText (with a comment saying it greys out "as in Photoshop"). The other text.* handlers return silently when getTextSpec is null: setAntialias, setOrientation, toggleFeature, setDigits, setKashida, setDirection, setComposer, pasteLorem, toggleParagraph, save/loadDefaultStyles, rasterizeLayer (app.ts:3146-3170, 3207-3251, 3368-3423). textOnPath and bindToPath (app.ts:3174-3193) no-op silently without a work path, and on success they clear the user's work path (store.setPenPath([])). tedit and twarp (App.tsx:3014-3015) set a pending edit, but TypeDialog (Dialogs.tsx:11626-11646) falls through to text.create at pend.ax/ay = 0,0 when the active layer is not type.
findings.repro:
1. Select a pixel layer.
2. Run Type ▸ Anti-Alias ▸ Sharp, Type ▸ OpenType ▸ Swash, or Type ▸ Text on Path ▸ Create from Work Path with no path: nothing happens and no message appears.
3. Type ▸ Warp Text…: a new "Type" layer appears at the top-left corner.
findings.impact: Commands look available but do nothing, and there are surprising side effects.
findings.suggested_fix: Add activeIsText to menuEnablement for every type-layer command. Gate textonpath and bindtoworkpath on penPath.length >= 4. Have tedit and twarp disabled, or no-op, when the active layer is not type. Keep the work path after Text on Path, as Photoshop does.
findings.verdict_reason: menuEnablement (App.tsx:3436-3470) gates only langeastasian on activeIsText. The aa*, orient*, digits*, kashida*, textdir*, composer*, pastelorem, converttoparagraph and ot* handlers (App.tsx:3018-3070) call text.* methods that return early when getTextSpec is null (app.ts:3146-3423). textOnPath and bindToPath return early without a 4-point path, and on success they clear it with store.setPenPath([]) (app.ts:3174-3193). tedit and twarp (App.tsx:3014-3015) set pending {mode:'edit', ax:0, ay:0}. When text.get fails, TypeDialog falls through to text.create at pend.ax/ay = 0,0 (Dialogs.tsx:11630-11650).

findings.title: Creating type takes two undo steps (New Layer + Type), and untouched or emptied type layers are never discarded
findings.feature: Type tool create/commit
findings.evidence: state/app.ts:3058-3070: createTextLayer calls store.addLayer(), which pushes "New Layer", then applyTextSpec, whose first set_text_layer_spec in a session pushes "Type" (packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:16004-16011). e2e/text-inplace.spec.ts:162 asserts that one undo leaves "the blank pre-text layer". store.ts:2774-2790: endTextEdit has no empty or placeholder check, so clicking with the Type tool and committing without typing keeps a "Type" layer.
findings.repro:
Case 1:
1. With the Type tool, click the canvas, type "Hi", and click elsewhere.
2. Press ⌘Z once.
An empty pixel layer named "Text Layer 1" remains.

Case 2: With the Type tool, click the canvas and press Esc without typing. A "Type" text layer remains.
findings.impact: Stray layers pile up, and history does not match Photoshop's single type step.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the layer inside the same coalesced snapshot (open the session, add the layer and apply under one push_stack_undo), or drop the New Layer push on the first Type apply. In endTextEdit, if the layer is still fresh or its fullText is empty, delete the layer and drop its undo steps.
findings.verdict_reason: createTextLayer calls store.addLayer, whose add_layer pushes 'New Layer' (mod.rs:9336-9337). It then renames the layer untracked and runs applyTextSpec, which pushes 'Type' (mod.rs:16004-16011) (app.ts:3064-3069). The e2e test pins that one undo leaves the blank pre-text layer (text-inplace.spec.ts:153-162); that layer is already named 'Text Layer n', because the rename happens before the Type snapshot. endTextEdit (store.ts:2774-2790) has no empty-text or placeholder check, so committing a fresh 'Type' placeholder keeps the layer.

findings.title: Replace All Missing Fonts checks the picker registry, not actual availability, and Resolve Missing Fonts is the same command with no UI
findings.feature: Type ▸ Replace All Missing Fonts / Resolve Missing Fonts
findings.evidence: App.tsx:3049-3050: both ids map to text.replaceMissingFonts. state/app.ts:3427-3437: "known" is FONTS (text/spec.ts:358). The built-in list always contains Inter, Impact and others whether or not they are installed, and the web build or a pre-scan launch has no discovered families. Missing fonts are replaced with FONTS[0] (Inter), which may itself be missing. The replacement keeps run.face, and there is no count or toast feedback.
findings.repro:
Case 1: Open a project whose type uses "Inter" on a Mac without Inter and run Replace All Missing Fonts. Nothing is reported or changed; it renders in the system fallback.

Case 2: In the browser build, use Helvetica and run it. The text is changed to Inter even though Helvetica exists.
findings.impact: Missing fonts go undetected, or fonts that are present get replaced. Resolve Missing Fonts looks implemented but duplicates Replace.
findings.suggested_fix: Check availability with document.fonts.check(`12px ${family}`) and the native scan, not membership in FONTS. Replace with a concrete installed default. Clear `face` on replaced runs. Report the count. Give Resolve Missing Fonts a dialog that maps each missing family to a chosen replacement.
findings.verdict_reason: Both ids map to text.replaceMissingFonts (App.tsx:3049-3050). The known set is FONTS keyed by first family (app.ts:3427-3437, spec.ts:377-378), and the replacement is FONTS[0] (Inter), itself possibly not installed. The run replacement {...run, font} keeps run.face. There is no count or feedback. Case 2 of the repro is wrong as written: 'Helvetica' keys to 'helvetica', which matches the built-in 'Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif' entry, so Helvetica is not replaced. The claim still holds for any installed family that is not in the built-in list and not discovered, such as Futura in the browser build.

findings.title: Turning Type ▸ OpenType ▸ Standard Ligatures off does not remove ligatures
findings.feature: Type ▸ OpenType ▸ Standard Ligatures
findings.evidence: text/spec.ts:275-285: mergedFeatures emits the legacy tags (liga, dlig, frac, ordn) only when true. An unchecked liga leaves font-feature-settings at "normal", where fonts apply liga by default. Plain runs are drawn as whole platform-shaped strings (text/raster.ts:1141-1150 canPlatformShape and 1188-1206 platformRunLength), so fi/fl ligatures still appear. When checked, applyOpenType (raster.ts:330-336) substitutes presentation-form codepoints (ﬁ) that many fonts lack.
findings.repro:
1. Create type "office fish" in Georgia or Times, where default ligatures show.
2. Look at Type ▸ OpenType ▸ Standard Ligatures: it is unchecked, but the fi/ff ligatures still render.
findings.impact: The toggle state does not match what is rendered, and there is no way to get discrete letters.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit liga as an explicit tag when off ("liga" 0), either by defaulting spec.liga to true (Photoshop's default) or by writing the tag when it is false. Prefer font-feature-settings over codepoint substitution.
findings.verdict_reason: mergedFeatures (spec.ts:275-285) adds liga only when spec.liga is truthy, so an unchecked liga yields "". applyCanvasFeatures then sets font-feature-settings to 'normal' (raster.ts:132), which leaves the platform's default liga on. Runs of cells that pass canPlatformShape (raster.ts:1141-1150) are drawn as one joined string (platformRunLength, 1188-1206), so the shaper can form fi/ff ligatures. When checked, applyOpenType swaps in presentation-form codepoints (raster.ts:330-331). What still needs checking is what the WKWebView canvas actually renders, since that depends on the platform. I followed the code path end to end.

findings.title: Paste Lorem Ipsum replaces the layer's whole text instead of inserting at the caret
findings.feature: Type ▸ Paste Lorem Ipsum
findings.evidence: state/app.ts:3160-3164: pasteLorem calls applyTextSpec(id, setText(s, "Lorem ipsum…")), which replaces the full string. It ignores typeEditorSelection(), which the same file already uses for glyph insertion (app.ts:3084-3090).
findings.repro:
1. Type "Headline" on canvas.
2. With the caret at the end, run Type ▸ Paste Lorem Ipsum.
"Headline" is gone.
findings.impact: Unexpected destructive replacement. It can be undone.
findings.suggested_fix: Splice the placeholder at typeEditorSelection(), like insertGlyph, or only fill when the layer is fresh or empty.
findings.verdict_reason: pasteLorem (app.ts:3160-3164) calls applyTextSpec(id, setText(s, 'Lorem ipsum…')), which replaces the whole string. It never consults typeEditorSelection (app.ts:3084-3090), which insertGlyph in the same object does use (3221-3233). It is undoable, and inside an open editor session it coalesces into the typing step.

findings.title: Each keystroke clears and rewrites the full-canvas type plane, recomposites the whole document and re-syncs the UI
findings.feature: On-canvas type editing, Character panel and toolbar live edits
findings.evidence: packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:16012-16036: set_text_layer_spec zeroes every u16 in the layer plane, which is full-canvas for kind 2, writes the raster, and calls composite(). composite() is composite_region(0,0,w,h) (mod.rs:7726-7728). state/app.ts:2920-2925: applyTextSpec then calls engine.commit(), which does a full blit and sync (engine/EngineClient.ts:823-840). The overlay calls text.apply on every onChange (CanvasView.tsx:4033).
findings.repro: On an 8000×6000 document, click with the Type tool and type quickly. I expect typing to lag noticeably behind input; this has not been profiled.
findings.impact: Typing latency grows with document size.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear only the previous text bounds, and composite only the union of the old and new raster rects (composite_region). Batch the per-keystroke apply with requestAnimationFrame.
findings.verdict_reason: The mechanism is as described. set_text_layer_spec zeroes every element of the layer plane and calls composite() (mod.rs:16012-16036). composite is composite_region(0,0,w,h) (mod.rs:7726-7728). applyTextSpec re-runs rasterizeSpec and then engine.commit(), which does blit and sync (app.ts:2920-2925; EngineClient.ts:823-840). The overlay applies on every onChange (CanvasView.tsx:4033). The latency impact is not profiled, so the severity is an estimate.

findings.title: Type menu shows no radio check for Anti-Alias, Orientation, direction, composer, digits or kashida, and Convert to Paragraph Text never changes to Convert to Point Text
findings.feature: Type menu state indicators
findings.evidence: App.tsx:1907-1916: openTypeCheckedIds returns only the OpenType tags and langeastasian, so the aa*, orienth/orientv, textdirltr/rtl, composer*, digits* and kashida* ids are never checked. App.tsx:3032: converttoparagraph toggles via text.toggleParagraph (app.ts:3404-3414), but the label comes from the blueprint and is never relabelled, unlike the clipping-mask relabel at App.tsx:3522-3530.
findings.repro:
1. Select a paragraph type layer set to Sharp anti-alias and RTL.
2. Open the Type menu.
There are no checkmarks, and it still reads "Convert to Paragraph Text".
findings.impact: The user cannot see the current mode from the menu.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend openTypeCheckedIds with the active spec's antialias, vertical, direction, composer, digits and kashida ids. Relabel converttoparagraph when spec.kind is "paragraph".
findings.verdict_reason: openTypeCheckedIds (App.tsx:1907-1916) emits only langeastasian, otliga, otdlig, otfrac, otordn and the enabled feature tags. The checked set passed to the menu builder (App.tsx:3506-3510) adds only imageassets and the image-mode ids, so the aa*, orient*, textdir*, composer*, digits* and kashida* items never get a check. The only relabel is the clipping-mask one (App.tsx:3515-3523). converttoparagraph toggles both ways (app.ts:3404-3414), but its blueprint label is never changed (psMenuData.ts:2594).

areas.coverage:
This was a code review only. I ran no builds or test suites. The only things I ran were two small JS copies of engine loops, in the scratchpad only, to estimate how slow they are. What I reviewed:

- Select menu: 25 items, all wired. 24 carry a monetId; "Sky" has none in the blueprint but is wired by label in psMenus.ts. Items: All, Deselect, Reselect, Inverse, All Layers, Deselect Layers, Find Layers, Isolate Layers, Color Range, Focus Area, Subject, Sky, Remove Background (AI), Select and Mask, Modify (Border, Smooth, Expand, Contract, Feather), Grow, Similar, Transform Selection, Edit in Quick Mask Mode, Load Selection, Save Selection.
- Tools: 10 selection tools (marquee, ellipse, single row, single column, lasso, polygonal lasso, magnetic lasso, wand, quick selection, object selection). I traced pointer-down, move and up in CanvasView.tsx.
- Options bars: Mode, Anti-alias, Feather, Style (Normal/Fixed Ratio/Fixed Size), Tolerance, Contiguous, Sample All Layers, Auto-Enhance, and the Object Selection hint.
- Dialogs: 10 (Expand/Contract, Feather, Border, Smooth, Transform Selection plus its on-canvas frame, Color Range, Save Selection, Load Selection, Focus Area, Select and Mask).
- Store and app code: selection mutations in store.ts, which actions get recorded in app.ts, and the script/VisionOps allowlist.
- Engine: raster/selection.rs (all 1285 lines) and the selection API in raster/mod.rs (select_*, modify operations, color range, tonal, localized, sky, focus area, quick mask, save/load, decontaminate).
- MCP surface: the only selection command is ml.selectSubject. Everything else is reachable only through script.run's store.* ops.
- Tests: I grepped the ~37 selection-related e2e specs and the relevant unit and engine tests.

Not reviewed in depth: how good the refine_edge guided-filter matte is, how accurately the magnetic lasso snaps, object-selection and U²-Net output quality, and native src-tauri code (it has no selection-specific logic).

Main result: 10 major issues and no blockers. The biggest are that Select ▸ All is invisible and blocks the selection commands that follow it, that Modify and Select and Mask freeze the app for seconds to minutes with larger values on camera-size photos, and that the options-bar Feather re-feathers the whole selection. Full list in the findings.
areas.parity_notes:
Every Select-menu item in the blueprint is wired; "Sky" has no monetId in psMenuData.ts but is wired through LABEL_WIRING. So there are no disabled placeholders in this menu.

Photoshop behaviours that are missing (not bugs in advertised items):
- Selection tools:
  - Dragging inside an active selection does not move the selection outline, and arrow keys do not nudge it.
  - The Polygonal Lasso has no Backspace to remove the last point and no Enter to close. Alt does not toggle between freehand and polygonal lasso.
  - A plain click with the Lasso does not deselect.
- Select and Mask:
  - No Object Aware refine mode.
  - No New Layer or New Document outputs.
  - Cannot load and edit an existing layer mask.
  - No Select and Mask button in the tool options bars.
- Modify dialogs lack "Apply effect at canvas bounds", and Feather's minimum is 1 px (Photoshop allows 0.1).
- Color Range:
  - No Detect Faces.
  - No Sample: Current Layer (allLayers is always true).
  - The Reds/Yellows/… presets are RGB clusters scaled by Fuzziness, not hue ranges.
- Select ▸ All Layers includes the Background layer, and Deselect Layers keeps the active layer (Photoshop deselects all).
- Quick Mask: the menu item shows no checkmark, and resizing the canvas while in Quick Mask resets the buffer to all-selected (documented shortcut).
- MCP: there are no dedicated selection tools. Selections are reachable only through script.run (store.selectAll, selectRect, invertSelection, colorRangeSelect, …) and ml.selectSubject. ml.generativeFill ("requires an active selection") therefore depends on script.run to create one.
- Remove Background (AI) sits in the Select menu, which Photoshop does not do (it is a Properties quick action there).

findings.title: Select ▸ All (⌘A) leaves no selection the app can see: no marching ants, and Clear, Stroke, Crop, Modify and Transform Selection are all disabled or do nothing
findings.feature: Select ▸ All / Deselect / Reselect; Edit ▸ Clear, Stroke; Image ▸ Crop; Select ▸ Modify, Transform Selection, Select and Mask
findings.evidence: packages/engine/src/raster/selection.rs:65-70 (select_all sets active=false with the mask at 255); packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:22738 (has_selection returns sel.active); apps/vision/src/state/store.ts:2498 (selectionActive = e.has_selection()); apps/vision/src/canvas/CanvasView.tsx:604 and 659 (no ants when inactive); apps/vision/src/App.tsx:3460-3462 (clear/stroke/cropsel need selectionActive); mod.rs:21144-21148 and 21240-21290 (transform and modify return early when !sel.active); mod.rs:21097-21103 (select_none is a no-op after Select All, so Reselect restores an older selection); store.ts:4905 (a comment admits select_all is an 'inactive whole-canvas marker')
findings.repro: Open an image, press ⌘A. No marching ants appear. Press ⌫: nothing, because Edit ▸ Clear is disabled. Edit ▸ Stroke… and Image ▸ Crop are disabled. Select ▸ Modify ▸ Border 20 or Contract 10: nothing. Transform Selection ▸ On Canvas does nothing. Select and Mask says 'No active selection'.
findings.impact: Several everyday Photoshop workflows fail silently: ⌘A then ⌫ to clear a layer, ⌘A then Border/Contract to make a frame, ⌘A then Stroke, and ⌘A then Paste Into. The user gets no feedback.
findings.suggested_fix: Have select_all set active=true with a mask of 255 (sel_dirty already treats an empty mask as a deselect, so a full mask is safe). Keep 'inactive means everything is selected' only for the no-selection state. Adjust the engine tests that rely on select_all being inactive.

findings.title: Modify Expand/Contract/Border/Smooth, Feather and Select and Mask Smooth/Shift Edge freeze the UI for seconds to minutes at valid dialog values
findings.feature: Select ▸ Modify ▸ Expand/Contract/Border/Smooth/Feather; options-bar Feather; Select and Mask live preview
findings.evidence: packages/engine/src/raster/selection.rs:743-783 (morph scans a full disc for every pixel far from an edge), 834-872 (border scans a full disc for every pixel in a flat region), 874-906 (smooth always scans a full disc per pixel), 785-832 (feather uses a direct Gaussian kernel of 2·ceil(2.5r)+1 taps per pass). Dialog limits: apps/vision/src/ui/Dialogs.tsx:5916 (Expand/Contract up to 500), 9813 (Smooth up to 100), 9827 (Border up to 200), 9842 (Feather up to 250). App.tsx options-bar Feather allows up to 1000. state/selectAndMask.ts:185-188 (Select and Mask Smooth up to 100, Shift Edge ±100 px), recomputed on every setting change (Dialogs.tsx:9985-10018). All of this runs synchronously in WASM on the main thread. A JS copy of the smooth loop took 2.5 s for 1 MP at r=20, which extrapolates to roughly 25 min for 24 MP at r=100.
findings.repro: Open a 6000×4000 photo, draw a large marquee, then Select ▸ Modify ▸ Smooth 60 (or Border 150, or Expand 200). The app stops responding for minutes. In Select and Mask, set Smooth to 50; because the setting is remembered, the workspace freezes again every time it opens.
findings.impact: The app appears hung with no progress or cancel. The user may force-quit and lose unsaved work.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the brute-force disc scans with a Euclidean distance transform, which is O(n) and gives Expand, Contract, Border and Shift Edge as thresholds of the distance. Implement Smooth as a box/integral-image majority filter. Implement Feather as three stacked box blurs, or with an integral image. Until then, lower the input limits and run on a worker with progress.
findings.verdict_reason: selection.rs:743-783 morph: exterior pixels (expand) or interior pixels (contract) scan the full pi·r² disc before they can break. :834-872 border scans a full disc in flat regions. :874-906 smooth always scans the full disc with no early exit. :785-832 feather runs a direct 2·ceil(2.5r)+1-tap kernel twice. The dialog limits match the finding: Dialogs.tsx:5916 (500), 9818 (100), 9832 (200), 9847 (250). Magnetic Lasso's options-bar feather input allows max=1000 (App.tsx:859). mod.rs:21312-21325 sam_refine calls sel.smooth, sel.feather and sel.morph(shift), and the Select and Mask live preview recomputes after a debounce on every setting change (Dialogs.tsx:~9996). store.ts:8875-8898 calls the engine synchronously on the main thread (engine.e.*), with no worker. Example: Smooth 60 on a 24 MP image is about 24e6 × 11,300 disc taps, which is minutes.

findings.title: Options-bar Feather re-feathers the whole selection on every Add/Subtract gesture and adds a separate undo step
findings.feature: Marquee / Ellipse / Lasso / Polygonal / Magnetic Lasso / Magic Wand / Quick Selection / Object Selection ▸ Feather
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/canvas/CanvasView.tsx:987-990 (applyFeather calls engine.e.feather_selection after the selection op), called at 1344, 2153, 2169, 2248, 2294, 2306 and 2639; apps/vision/src/state/store.ts:9001 and 9013 (Object Selection does the same); packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:21262-21272 (feather_selection pushes its own 'Feather Selection' undo and blurs the entire mask). The recorded replay ops at apps/vision/src/state/app.ts:2284-2289 never apply a feather, although the comment there says they replay 'with the options bar as it stands'.
findings.repro: Set Marquee Feather to 10. Drag rectangle A, then Shift-drag rectangle B elsewhere: A's edge is now feathered twice. With Quick Selection and Feather 5, each additional stroke softens every earlier part of the selection again. Press ⌘Z once after a feathered marquee: the unfeathered marquee is still there.
findings.impact: Edges come out wrong whenever an options-bar feather is combined with Add/Subtract, and blurrier on every stroke with Quick Selection. History fills with extra steps, and recorded actions play back without the feather.
findings.suggested_fix: Feather only the newly created shape before combining it: build the shape into a scratch Selection, feather that, then combine by mode inside one push_sel_undo. For example, pass the feather radius into select_rect, select_ellipse, select_polygon, magic_wand and the other selection calls.
findings.verdict_reason: The code is as described. CanvasView.tsx:987-990 applyFeather calls engine.e.feather_selection(f) after the op. It is called after the wand (1344), magnetic lasso (2153), lasso (2169), quick selection end (2248), marquee (2294), ellipse (2306) and polygonal lasso (2639). mod.rs:21262-21272 feather_selection pushes its own 'Feather Selection' Sel undo and blurs the entire mask, so earlier parts of an Add/Subtract result are feathered again, and one Cmd+Z leaves the unfeathered shape. The replay ops at app.ts:2283-2289 (selectRect, selectEllipse, selectPolygon) never feather, which contradicts the comment 'they replay with the options bar as it stands'. Downgraded to minor because the common path (one feathered shape) gives the correct edge. Only the Add/Subtract combination and the undo granularity are wrong.

findings.title: Color Range with Shadows/Midtones/Highlights or Localized Color Clusters combines wrongly with Add/Subtract/Intersect, and Invert flips the whole combined selection
findings.feature: Select ▸ Color Range (tonal presets, Localized Color Clusters, Invert, Combine With Selection)
findings.evidence: packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:22152-22178 (select_tonal_range calls sel.tonal_range(..., mode) and then sel.invert() on the combined mask); mod.rs:22180-22223 (select_color_range_localized combines the first sample with `mode` and every later sample with SelMode::Add, then inverts the combined mask). Compare select_color_range_batch at mod.rs:22225-22290, which builds the cluster first, inverts it, then combines. Engine tests at mod.rs:41400-41452 only cover mode 0.
findings.repro: Make a marquee on the left half. Color Range ▸ Highlights, Invert on, Combine = Add, OK. The left half becomes deselected, because the result is NOT(previous ∪ highlights). Or: Localized Color Clusters with 2 samples, Combine = Subtract: the second sample is added to the selection instead of subtracted.
findings.impact: Wrong selections that are easy to miss, followed by edits applied to the wrong pixels.
findings.suggested_fix: Match the batch path. Build the tonal or localized coverage into a scratch Selection with Replace (union for extra samples), apply invert to that scratch, then combine it into the live selection with apply_saved(mode). Add engine tests for modes 1, 2 and 3 with and without invert.
findings.verdict_reason: mod.rs:22152-22178 select_tonal_range calls sel.tonal_range(..., mode) and then sel.invert() on the combined mask, so Add+Invert gives NOT(prev ∪ band). mod.rs:22180-22223 select_color_range_localized uses `mode` for the first sample and SelMode::Add for every later one, then inverts the combined mask. With Subtract, sample 2 is added back. By contrast, select_color_range_batch (22225-22290) builds the cluster with Replace, inverts it, and then combines it with apply_saved. The dialog passes the user's mode and invert straight through (Dialogs.tsx:6180-6185, store.ts:9047-9056 and 9102-9110). Out of Gamut does this correctly: it inverts before combining (store.ts:9116-9121). Downgraded to minor because only non-default combinations are affected (Invert with a non-New mode, or 2+ localized samples with Subtract/Intersect). The default New mode is correct.

findings.title: Select and Mask / Focus Area 'Output To: Layer Mask' on a layer that already has a mask throws away the refined selection and outputs nothing
findings.feature: Select ▸ Select and Mask… / Focus Area… ▸ Output To: Layer Mask
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/state/store.ts:8964-8967 (routeSelectionOutput calls add_layer_mask_reveal_selection, then select_none); packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:11225-11232 (add_layer_mask_reveal_selection returns early when the layer's mask is not empty). The transaction is then committed. Output is remembered across sessions (state/selectAndMask.ts:179-190).
findings.repro: Add a layer mask to a layer. Make a selection, open Select and Mask, refine it, choose Output To: Layer Mask, and click OK. The layer mask is unchanged and the selection is gone.
