findings.impact: The user's refinement work is discarded silently, recoverable only by Undo. Because the output setting is remembered, it happens again on later uses.
findings.suggested_fix: When the layer already has a mask, replace its pixels with the refined coverage (as Photoshop does), or refuse with a message before select_none. Add a test with a pre-existing mask.
findings.verdict_reason: store.ts:8964-8967 routeSelectionOutput calls add_layer_mask_reveal_selection and then select_none unconditionally. mod.rs:11229-11231 returns early when the layer's mask is not empty. commitSelectionOutput (store.ts:8940-8951) then commits the transaction, and Dialogs.tsx:10144-10158 records it as done. Neither the dialog (Output select at 10267 with all SAM_OUTPUTS) nor the store guards against an existing mask, and no test covers this. The output choice persists through normalizeSamSettings (selectAndMask.ts:190). Undo returns only to the pre-refine selection, so brush and refine work is lost.

findings.title: In Quick Mask mode only brush strokes edit the mask; Gradient, Fill, filters and adjustments change the layer's pixels across the whole canvas
findings.feature: Select ▸ Edit in Quick Mask Mode (Q)
findings.evidence: packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:22753-22766 (enter_quick_mask sets sel.active=false, so every masked edit sees 'everything selected'); mod.rs:17520-17531 and 19085-19091 (only the brush paths check qm_on); mod.rs:20904-20934 (gradient_fill has no qm_on branch and writes layers[active].pixels); apps/vision/src/state/store.ts:8283-8288. The comment at store.ts:8316-8318 admits filters and adjustments still hit layer pixels. e2e/quick-mask.spec.ts has no gradient/fill/filter case.
findings.repro: Press Q, pick the Gradient tool and drag across the canvas. The gradient is painted onto the image layer over the full canvas, not into the quick mask. Or press Q, then Filter ▸ Gaussian Blur: the whole layer is blurred instead of the mask.
findings.impact: Common Quick Mask techniques (a gradient for a graduated selection, blurring the mask) destroy image pixels without any restriction instead of shaping the selection. Undo recovers them.
findings.suggested_fix: While qm_on, send gradient_fill, fill_selection, clear and the filter/adjustment paths to the quick_mask buffer (as painting_mask does for layer masks), or refuse them with a message while Quick Mask is on.
findings.verdict_reason: mod.rs:22753-22766 enter_quick_mask sets sel.active=false. The only qm_on checks in the engine are in the stroke/brush paths (17526, 17956, 18032, 18058, 19091), plus bucket's bg_flood (18909). gradient_fill (20904-20934) has no qm_on branch, and it writes the active layer with coverage 1 everywhere. The CanvasView gradient case (2459-2467) does not check quickMask either. menuEnablement (App.tsx:3442-3467) does not gate filters or adjustments on quick mask. The ponytail comment at store.ts:8313-8315 admits that 'filters and adjustments still hit the layer's pixels'. e2e/quick-mask.spec.ts has no gradient, fill or filter case.

findings.title: Quick Selection: each new stroke replaces the selection by default, and Shift-drag does not add
findings.feature: Quick Selection tool
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/canvas/CanvasView.tsx:1348-1353 (the first dab passes `e.altKey ? 2 : 0` and ignores Shift); apps/vision/src/state/store.ts:1480 (quickSelectionMode defaults to 0 = New) and 2739-2745 (a fresh stroke re-reads New and nothing switches it to Add). src/state/quickSelectionOptions.test.ts:35 locks this behaviour in. Photoshop switches to Add after the first stroke and treats Shift as Add.
findings.repro: Pick Quick Selection with default options. Paint over part of an object, release, then paint over another part (or Shift-paint). The first part is deselected.
findings.impact: Building a selection over several strokes, which is how the tool is normally used, keeps losing earlier work unless the user finds the Mode control and sets it to Add.
findings.suggested_fix: After the first committed stroke, switch quickSelectionMode to Add (as Photoshop does). Also treat Shift at pointer-down as Add, matching the other selection tools.
findings.verdict_reason: CanvasView.tsx:1348-1353 sends the first dab as `e.altKey ? 2 : 0` and ignores Shift. store.ts:2741 sets quickStrokeMode from snap.quickSelectionMode, which defaults to 0/New (store.ts:1480). Nothing switches it to Add after a stroke. quickSelectionOptions.test.ts:35-40 locks in 'defaults to New: the first dab replaces'. In Photoshop the option flips to Add after the first stroke, and Shift adds. The e2e (quick-selection.spec.ts) covers only Alt-subtract and single strokes. Building a selection over several strokes is the tool's primary use, so major stands.

findings.title: Select ▸ Sky never selects sky below 56% of the image height, and silently does nothing when it finds no sky
findings.feature: Select ▸ Sky
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/state/store.ts:8871-8873 (select_sky(0.45, 0.35) with fixed values and no feedback on false); packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:21866-21885 (limit_y = horizon_y + h·(0.08+0.08·tol), about 0.558·h) and 37630-37632 (sky_candidate rejects y > limit_y). Engine tests (mod.rs:39858-39895) only cover skies ending above that line. Edit ▸ Sky Replacement passes its own horizon (state/app.ts:7911-7913); the menu command cannot.
findings.repro: Open a landscape with the horizon at about 2/3 of the height (sky covering the top 65%) and choose Select ▸ Sky. The bottom ~10% of the sky above the horizon stays unselected. On an image with no top-edge sky, nothing happens and no message appears.
findings.impact: Wrong selection in a common photo composition, so later sky edits leave a visible band. A no-op with no explanation otherwise.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the hard y cutoff for Select ▸ Sky (let the flood follow sky-like pixels and stop at the colour boundary), or estimate the horizon from the image. Show a toast when select_sky returns false.

findings.title: Select ▸ Remove Background (AI) leaves the canvas visually unchanged: it stacks a cut-out copy over the untouched original
findings.feature: Select ▸ Remove Background (AI)
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ml/onnx.ts:678-696: select_none(), then store.addLayer(), then stamp_image(composite RGB + subject alpha). The original layers stay visible underneath, so the composite is identical. It also takes three undo steps (Deselect, New Layer, 'Paste'). e2e/ml.spec.ts:54-62 only checks that the layer count went up.
findings.repro: Open a photo of a subject on a background and choose Select ▸ Remove Background (AI). The toast says 'Done.' but the canvas looks the same until the user hides the original layer.
findings.impact: The feature looks broken. The user's existing selection is also discarded, and history gets three unclear steps.
findings.suggested_fix: Match Photoshop: apply the matte as a layer mask on the active layer (converting Background to a layer), or hide the source layer. Wrap the operation in one beginHistory/commitHistory labelled 'Remove Background', and stop discarding the user's selection.

findings.title: Quick Selection does full-document work on every pointer move, so drags lag badly on camera-size images
findings.feature: Quick Selection tool (and the Select and Mask Quick Selection brush)
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/canvas/CanvasView.tsx:1928-1931 (every pointermove calls store.quickSelectionAt, with no rAF coalescing); packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:21964-21990 (every dab copies the full sample buffer); selection.rs:302-380 (allocates full-document matched/seen arrays and runs a 3×3 anti-alias pass over the whole document per dab); selection.rs:~395-420 (Auto-Enhance runs the guided filter over the whole document per dab; the ponytail note admits this). A JS copy of one dab took about 330 ms on 24 MP.
findings.repro: Open a 6000×4000 photo, pick Quick Selection (Anti-alias on) and drag across it. The selection trails the pointer by seconds, at a few frames per second.
findings.impact: A core interactive tool becomes very sluggish on typical photos.
findings.suggested_fix: Limit each dab's flood, anti-alias pass and Auto-Enhance to the dab's bounding box plus one pixel. Keep a cached sample buffer for the whole stroke instead of re-copying it per dab. Coalesce moves with rAF.
findings.verdict_reason: CanvasView.tsx:1928-1931 calls store.quickSelectionAt on every pointermove with no rAF batching. store.ts:2745 calls engine.sync() per dab. Per dab, mod.rs:21964-21990 runs selection_sample_buffer (mod.rs:4658-4680), which converts the whole 16-bit layer plane into a new w·h·4 buffer. selection.rs:329-330 allocates two full-document bool arrays, and :352-370 runs a 3×3 anti-alias pass over every pixel in the document (antiAlias defaults on). auto_enhance_dab (:397-420) runs refine_edge over the whole document, but Auto-Enhance is off by default (store.ts:1497). The 'trails by seconds' wording is probably overstated, because browsers coalesce pointermove while the thread is busy, so the symptom is a low update rate rather than a backlog. The O(W·H) per-dab cost is real.

findings.title: Save Selection's default channel name 'Selection 1' silently overwrites an existing channel with that name
findings.feature: Select ▸ Save Selection…
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ui/Dialogs.tsx:6303 (the name always defaults to 'Selection 1') and 6312 (OK calls saveSelection(target, 0)); packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:22329-22334 (write_saved_selection_mask replaces a slot with the same name). The Channels panel (ui/Panels.tsx:1686-1690) and Calculations (Dialogs.tsx:6609-6613) already pick a unique 'Alpha N' name.
findings.repro: Make selection A and Save Selection with defaults. Make selection B and Save Selection with defaults. Only one channel, 'Selection 1', exists, and it now holds B.
findings.impact: A saved alpha channel is lost without a warning. It can only be recovered through History, and not at all after the history is gone.
findings.suggested_fix: Default to the next unused name (reuse the 'Alpha N' loop). If a typed name already exists, warn or switch to the channel's Operation mode.
findings.verdict_reason: Dialogs.tsx:6303 always defaults the name to 'Selection 1', and OK calls store.saveSelection(target, 0, docId) (6312). With mode 0 on the active doc, store.ts:9131-9135 calls e.save_selection(name). mod.rs:22329-22334 write_saved_selection_mask replaces the slot with the same name. Nothing warns or picks a unique name. Photoshop defaults to 'Alpha N' and never overwrites by name. push_stack_undo means Undo can recover it, but the loss is silent.

findings.title: Transform Selection drops flips (negative width/height or dragging a handle past the opposite edge) and uses nearest-neighbour for plain scaling
findings.feature: Select ▸ Transform Selection (dialog and on-canvas frame)
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/state/store.ts:8815-8829: pure scale and move go to e.transform_selection. packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:21148-21151 uses scale_x.abs() and scale_y.abs(), and 21158-21169 samples nearest-neighbour. store.ts:2112-2113 (scaleSelectionFrame) produces negative sx/sy when a handle crosses the anchor. The affine path (mod.rs:21185) handles both correctly.
findings.repro: Lasso an asymmetric shape. Transform Selection with Width -100% and OK: nothing changes. Or drag the right handle past the left edge in the on-canvas frame: the frame shows a mirrored shape, but the commit is not mirrored. Scale an elliptical selection by 300%: the edge is stair-stepped.
findings.impact: The preview and the result disagree, and scaled selections get jagged edges.
findings.suggested_fix: Send every non-identity transform through transform_selection_affine (bilinear sampling, keeps the sign), or at least do so whenever sx or sy is negative.
findings.verdict_reason: In store.ts:8814-8829, scale() keeps negative values, and pure scale/move goes to e.transform_selection. mod.rs:21150-21151 takes scale_x.abs() and scale_y.abs(), so -100% becomes the identity and returns at 21152. mod.rs:21162-21168 samples with floor, i.e. nearest-neighbour. scaleSelectionFrame (store.ts:2112-2113, g.x/(2·vx)) produces a negative sx when a handle crosses the anchor, and anchorOpposite computes tx for that signed scale, so the commit is also mis-translated. The dialog's Width field is an unbounded number input (Dialogs.tsx:8381). The affine path (mod.rs:21185+) is bilinear and keeps the sign.

findings.title: Commands that need a selection stay enabled with nothing selected and silently do nothing
findings.feature: Select ▸ Inverse, Modify ▸ *, Grow, Similar, Transform Selection, Save Selection
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/App.tsx:3440-3466: menuEnablement gates clear/stroke/cropsel/pasteinto on selectionActive, but not inv, feather, border, smooth, expand, contract, grow, similar, xfsel or savesel. The engine then returns early (mod.rs:21240-21290, 21646-21668, 21144-21148). Inverse with no selection still pushes an 'Inverse' undo step (mod.rs:21133-21139). Save Selection with no selection saves a full-canvas channel (mod.rs:22321-22327).
findings.repro: With no selection, choose Select ▸ Modify ▸ Feather…, enter 10 and click OK. Nothing happens and no message appears. Select ▸ Inverse adds a history step that does nothing.
findings.impact: Confusing no-ops and wasted history steps.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `inv, feather, border, smooth, expand, contract, grow, similar, xfsel, savesel: hasDocument && selectionActive` to menuEnablement (once Select All sets an active selection).
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:3442-3467 menuEnablement gates only pasteinto, pasteoutside, clear, stroke and cropsel on selectionActive. inv, feather, border, smooth, expand, contract, grow, similar, xfsel and savesel stay enabled. The engine then returns early (mod.rs:21240-21290 and 21646-21668). select_invert (21133-21139) pushes an 'Inverse' undo, then invert() makes the mask active with all zeros, and sel_dirty resets it, leaving an empty history step. write_saved_selection (22321-22327) saves a full-canvas mask when nothing is selected.

findings.title: Color Range previews do not match what OK selects for Shadows/Midtones/Highlights, Out of Gamut and Localized Color Clusters
findings.feature: Select ▸ Color Range preview (dialog thumbnail and on-canvas Selection Preview)
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ui/Dialogs.tsx:6092-6096: previewMask always uses colorRangePreviewMask(samples…), even when a tonal or gamut preset is chosen. Dialogs.tsx:6131-6136: the canvas preview ignores `localized`, `points` and `clusterRange`, although the comment says 'what the canvas shows is what OK will select'.
findings.repro: Open Color Range and choose Highlights: the dialog thumbnail still shows the old sampled-colour mask. Or turn on Localized Color Clusters with a small Range: the preview shows every matching pixel in the image, but OK selects only those near the sample.
findings.impact: Users tune settings against a preview that does not match the result.
findings.suggested_fix: Use tonalPreviewMask or outOfGamutMask for the thumbnail too, and add a TS version of the localized spatial falloff (or call the engine's preview) for both preview surfaces.
findings.verdict_reason: Dialogs.tsx:6092-6097: the thumbnail previewMask always uses colorRangePreviewMask(samples...), with no tonal or gamut branch. Dialogs.tsx:6131-6139: the canvas preview does handle tonal and gamut, but ignores localized, points and clusterRange, even though the comment claims 'what the canvas shows is what OK will select'. It also ignores `invert` for Out of Gamut, while OK honours it (store.ts:9119).

findings.title: Channels panel ⌘-click always replaces the selection; ⌘⇧/⌘⌥/⌘⌥⇧ (add/subtract/intersect) are ignored
findings.feature: Channels panel ▸ load channel as selection
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ui/Panels.tsx:1785 (loadChannelAsSelection(channel) uses the default mode 0) and 1864 (loadSelection(name, 0)). The Layers panel honours modifiers through loadSelectionMode (Panels.tsx:1586, 939 and 964), and store.loadChannelAsSelection already accepts a mode (store.ts:8364).
findings.repro: Make a marquee, then ⌘⇧-click an alpha channel row. The selection is replaced instead of added to.
findings.impact: The same gesture behaves differently in the Channels and Layers panels, and a common channel-combining workflow does not work.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass loadSelectionMode({ shift: e.shiftKey, alt: e.altKey }) in both Channels onClick handlers.

findings.title: Magic Wand and Magnetic Lasso use a hidden combine Mode left over from the Marquee options bar
findings.feature: Magic Wand / Magnetic Lasso options bar
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/App.tsx:850-866 (Magnetic Lasso options have no Mode control) and 917-958 (the Wand shares the Bucket bar, also without Mode). CanvasView.tsx:982-983: with no modifier, modeFromKeys falls back to store.state.selMode, the value last set in the Marquee/Lasso or Object Selection bar.
findings.repro: With the Marquee tool, set Mode to Subtract. Switch to the Magic Wand and click: it subtracts, and the options bar shows no mode.
findings.impact: Selections behave in a way the visible UI does not explain.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same New/Add/Subtract/Intersect control to the Wand and Magnetic Lasso options bars.
findings.verdict_reason: The magneticlasso options bar (App.tsx:850-866) and the shared bucket/wand bar (936-962) have no selMode control. The only selMode SegmentedControls are at App.tsx:873 (object selection) and 987 (marquee/lasso). CanvasView.tsx:982-983 modeFromKeys falls back to store.state.selMode, and the wand (1343) and magnetic lasso (2152) use it.

findings.title: Marquee: holding Shift or Alt from pointer-down to add or subtract also forces a square or centred shape, and a click with no drag deselects even in Add mode
findings.feature: Rectangular / Elliptical Marquee, Object Selection
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/canvas/CanvasView.tsx:1966-1977 and 2288-2290: styledSelectionRect/marqueeRect use the live e.shiftKey/e.altKey, so the key that picked Add/Subtract at pointer-down also constrains the shape. CanvasView.tsx:2296 and 2282: a click without a drag calls E.select_none() whatever the mode.
findings.repro: With a selection active, hold Shift and drag a wide rectangle to add it: the added area is forced to a square. Shift-click without dragging: the whole selection is deselected.
findings.impact: Shift-add, the most common add gesture, cannot make non-square rectangles unless the user releases and re-presses Shift. An accidental Shift-click wipes the selection.
findings.suggested_fix: Constrain only when Shift/Alt is newly pressed during the drag (track the keys held at pointer-down and ignore them for geometry until released). In Add/Subtract/Intersect mode, make a click without drag a no-op.
findings.verdict_reason: CanvasView.tsx:2288-2290 and 2302: styledSelectionRect is given the live e.shiftKey/e.altKey at pointer-up, while the combine mode comes from d.shift/d.alt sampled at pointer-down, so a held Shift both adds and constrains. Photoshop requires a release and re-press of Shift to constrain while adding. CanvasView.tsx:2296 `else E.select_none()` runs regardless of mode, and objectselection (2282) does the same. The ellipse path does not deselect. Behaviour matches the finding.

findings.title: Many selection steps are never recorded into Actions
findings.feature: Actions recording of selection tools and Select commands
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/canvas/CanvasView.tsx:1341-1346 (Magic Wand), 1543-1550 (single row/column), 2632-2641 (Polygonal Lasso) and 1928-1931/2246-2250 (Quick Selection) never call actions.recordTool. Marquee, Ellipse and Lasso record only with Allow Tool Recording on (state/app.ts:776-790). Photoshop records 'Set Selection' regardless. state/app.ts:931-932: RECORDED_STORE_OPS lacks selectObjectLasso, tonalRangeSelect, outOfGamutSelect, selectAllLayers and deselectLayers. ml.selectSubject is not wrapped (app.ts:2075-2080).
findings.repro: Record an action: Magic Wand click, Select Subject, then Color Range ▸ Highlights, then Fill. Play it back on another image: only the Fill step exists.
findings.impact: Macros built around selections replay against the wrong region.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the Wand, Polygonal Lasso, Row/Column and Quick Selection results (the resulting mask, or the op with its parameters) as Set Selection steps. Add the missing store ops to RECORDED_STORE_OPS, and wrap ml.selectSubject with recordedCall.
findings.verdict_reason: recordTool is called only for lasso (2171), marquee (2295) and ellipse (2307) in CanvasView. The wand (1341-1346), single row/column (1543-1550), polygonal lasso (closePolyLasso at ~2632-2641) and quick selection record nothing. recordTool is gated on _allowToolRecording (app.ts:787). The RECORDED_STORE_OPS list (app.ts:931-934) lacks tonalRangeSelect, outOfGamutSelect and selectObjectLasso, and the Color Range OK (Dialogs.tsx:6180-6181) calls those directly. ml.selectSubject (app.ts:2080) is a plain import wrapper with no recordedCall.

findings.title: A faint selection (all coverage under 50%) stays active but shows no marching ants, and later edits are silently weakened
findings.feature: Marching ants / Feather / Color Range
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/canvas/CanvasView.tsx:628: an edge pixel needs mask ≥ 128. packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:21035-21047: sel_dirty only turns an all-zero mask into a deselect (#53). Photoshop warns 'No pixels are more than 50% selected'.
findings.repro: Draw a 10×10 marquee with options-bar Feather 20, or run Color Range with a low Fuzziness. No ants appear, but fills and brush strokes now land at a few percent opacity.
findings.impact: This is the same kind of invisible selection that #53 fixed for the all-zero case.
findings.suggested_fix: When the maximum coverage is below 128 after an operation, show a warning toast (as Photoshop does), or draw the ants at the maximum coverage's contour.
findings.verdict_reason: The CanvasView.tsx:628 boundary scan skips every pixel with mask < 128, so a mask whose maximum is under 128 yields no edge points. sel_dirty (mod.rs:21035-21047) deactivates only an all-zero mask. There is no max-coverage warning anywhere on the feather or Color Range paths. A small marquee with a large feather produces this state.

findings.title: Select and Mask: Decontaminate Colors is silently ignored for Layer Mask output, adds an unrequested layer for Selection output, and New Layer with Layer Mask copies the merged image instead of the active layer
findings.feature: Select and Mask ▸ Output Settings
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/state/store.ts:8964-8975: the layermask branch never uses `amount`, and for 'selection' with amount > 0 it calls decontaminate_colors, which inserts a new layer. packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:21420-21424 and 21484-21494: decontaminate_colors builds the new layer from the merged 8-bit composite (self.output) with alpha 1.0, not from the active layer. Dialogs.tsx:10262-10267 lets Decontaminate be combined with any output.
findings.repro: With a multi-layer document, check Decontaminate Colors with Output To: Selection and click OK: a new 'Decontaminated' layer appears as well. With Output To: Layer Mask, the fringe is not decontaminated.
findings.impact: Surprise layers, a setting that does nothing, and 16-bit detail flattened to 8-bit in the new layer.
findings.suggested_fix: As in Photoshop, when Decontaminate is on, allow only the New Layer with Layer Mask (or New Document) output. Build that layer from the active layer's pixels at document depth.
findings.verdict_reason: store.ts:8964-8975: the layermask branch never reads `amount`, and the selection branch with amount > 0 calls decontaminate_colors. mod.rs:21423-21494 builds a new 'Decontaminated' layer from self.output, the merged RGBA8 composite, with alpha 1.0, inserts it and keeps the selection. The Output select (Dialogs.tsx:10267) is not restricted when Decontaminate is on. Photoshop restricts it to the new-layer and new-document outputs and duplicates the active layer.

findings.title: Modify ▸ Contract… opens a combined 'Expand / Contract' dialog whose primary button is Expand
findings.feature: Select ▸ Modify ▸ Expand… / Contract…
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/App.tsx:3090-3091 (both menu ids open 'expandContract'); apps/vision/src/ui/Dialogs.tsx:5906-5919 (Expand is the primary variant whichever menu item opened it).
findings.repro: Choose Select ▸ Modify ▸ Contract…. The dialog title and highlighted button point to Expand.
findings.impact: Easy to apply the wrong operation.
findings.suggested_fix: Open the dialog with a mode argument (open('expandContract', 'contract')) and show one titled action, as Photoshop does.

areas.coverage:
This was a code review only. I ran no builds, suites or single test files; the checks were reading code and grep.

Inventory (from psMenuData.ts plus the psMenus.ts injections):
- 115 blueprint Filter-menu leaf items are in scope, and every one has a monetId wired to a handler in App.tsx:3101-3240. There are no disabled placeholders in scope.
  - Top level: 8 (Last Filter, Convert for Smart Filters, Filter Gallery, Adaptive Wide Angle, Camera Raw Filter, Lens Correction, Liquify, Vanishing Point).
  - Submenus: Blur 11, Blur Gallery 5, Distort 12, Noise 5, Pixelate 7, Render 7, Sharpen 6, Stylize 45, Video 2, Other 7.
  - Pinch is re-wired by path to `dpinch` (psMenus.ts:86).
- 9 more items are injected by psMenus.ts:309-323: Lighting Effects and 8 Artistic filters.
- Frequency Separation and Browse Filters Online are also in the Filter menu.

What I traced:
- Every menu id through to its handler.
- The whole app.ts filter layer: applyFilter/smart routing (1083), filImpl (1186-1488), the Last Filter proxy (1493-1506), distortImpl (1826-1853), neural.oilPaint (2050), the Filter Gallery and Blur Gallery preview/commit transactions (1098-1184, 1531-1673), frequencySeparation (1704), adaptiveWideAngle (1885), and the smart.* actions (2449).
- About 60 filter dialog components in Dialogs.tsx, plus PreviewDialog in dialogs/common.tsx.
- Liquify, Vanishing Point and Camera Raw entry/commit in store.ts.
- The MCP filter wrappers in mcp/commands.ts.
- In the engine (packages/engine/src/raster): apply16, apply16_mask, apply32, the refuse guards, painting_mask, Quick Mask; all 70+ filter WASM entry points, sorted by which guard they use; the whole-buffer ops at mod.rs:27167-28280; the distort kernels; the smart-filter fid table (mod.rs:36323-36790); smart_add_filter; and the median, smart_blur, unsharp, gaussian_kernel, tiles and wave kernels.
- Test coverage: I grepped e2e/ (about 30 filter-related specs) and the unit/engine tests.

Not reviewed in depth: Camera Raw workspace internals, the Liquify mesh engine, Vanishing Point engine maths, the lens-profile database, and the visual correctness of each Artistic/Sketch/Texture kernel. Neural Filters are out of scope.

Timing claims are not measured. The perf finding rests on counting operations in the loops.
areas.parity_notes:
Every in-scope Filter-menu item is wired (no disabled placeholders). Several are simplified compared with Photoshop:

- **Displace** uses the layer's own R/G channels as the map. There is no map file, and no Stretch/Tile or Undefined Areas options.
- **Shape Blur** offers only Square or Circle, which become Box Blur or Lens Blur, radius up to 20.
- **Lens Blur** has only Radius (up to 20) and Brightness: no depth map, iris shape, specular highlights or noise.
- **Picture Frame** draws a bevelled solid frame only.
- **Flame** rises from the bottom of the selection instead of following a path.
- **Wave** has no Randomize; it is deterministic.
- **Add Noise** tops out at 100% (Photoshop 400%).
- **Other dialog ranges** are narrower: Median ≤8 (Photoshop 500), High Pass ≤50 (Photoshop 1000), Lens Blur ≤20.
- **Color Halftone** always uses 3 channels, even in CMYK.
- **Smart Sharpen** has no Shadow/Highlight tonal width or radius.
- **Reduce Noise** has no per-channel mode.
- **Filter Gallery** stores each effect as a separate smart filter.
- **No live preview** in Shear, Wave, Glass, Ocean Ripple, Diffuse Glow, Displace, Lens Correction, Smart Sharpen, Reduce Noise, Surface/Smart/Lens/Shape Blur, Dust & Scratches, Maximum/Minimum, Offset and Custom (Photoshop previews most of these).
- **Last Filter** never takes the filter's name, and Photoshop's ⌃⌘F "Last Filter with dialog" variant is missing.
- **32-bit documents**: only Gaussian Blur, Sharpen and Unsharp Mask have float kernels.

Menu, shortcut and MCP stay consistent: the blueprint shortcuts do not collide, and the MCP filter surface is small (gaussian, box, sharpen, unsharp, median, sponge, removeDistractions/Reflections, adaptiveWideAngle, lens profile), with everything else reachable through script.run. The one inconsistency is the unsharp/sharpen unit mismatch reported above.

Engineered carefully:
- Blur Gallery and Filter Gallery preview transactions, including the undo_pushes-based collapse.
- PreviewDialog target pinning and cancel-on-unmount.
- Pinned retargeting for Lens Correction and Camera Raw.
- Liquify and Vanishing Point session commit/cancel.
- Smart-object routing for every fil/distort op.
- Selection clipping for the whole-buffer ops.

Test coverage: about 30 e2e filter specs plus engine tests. The notable gaps, beyond those in the findings: nothing tests Last Filter, filters in Quick Mask or on a targeted channel, filter results in non-RGB modes, 8/16-bit filters with Lock Transparent Pixels, or the mask target for the whole-buffer ops.

findings.title: Filters in Quick Mask / targeted alpha or spot channel hit the whole layer's artwork instead of the mask
findings.feature: Filter menu (all) × Quick Mask / Channels panel targeting
findings.evidence: enter_quick_mask (mod.rs:22753-22766) moves the selection into `quick_mask` and sets `self.sel.active = false`. apply16 (4694-4735) and apply32 only divert to a mask through painting_mask() (17506), which checks mask_edit, adjustment/fill masks and the filter mask, never qm_on. No filter path reads qm_on. Channels-panel targeting (store.ts:8305-8323) is built on Quick Mask. Its own comment admits the gap: 'ponytail: … filters and adjustments still hit the layer's pixels'. Menu enablement (App.tsx:3434-3469) does not grey filters out in Quick Mask.
findings.repro: 1. Make a marquee and press Q (Quick Mask). 2. Filter ▸ Blur ▸ Gaussian Blur, 10 px, OK. 3. Press Q again. Photoshop feathers the mask. Vision blurs the entire layer (the selection is suspended, so nothing clips the edit) and the mask stays hard-edged. The same happens with an alpha or spot channel targeted in the Channels panel.
findings.impact: A core Photoshop workflow (refine a selection by filtering the Quick Mask or an alpha channel: Gaussian Blur, Crystallize, Maximum/Minimum) silently damages the artwork across the whole layer. The rubylith overlay can hide that the image changed. No test covers filters in Quick Mask (e2e/quick-mask.spec.ts has none).
findings.suggested_fix: When qm_on, run the filter closure on the quick_mask buffer through the same grey-plane widening that apply16_mask uses (a mask_of variant for quick_mask), with one Sel undo step. Until then, refuse with last_edit_error or disable filter commands in Quick Mask and channel-target mode. Add an engine test: enter_quick_mask, then filter_gaussian_blur changes quick_mask and leaves the pixels untouched.
findings.verdict_reason: enter_quick_mask (mod.rs:22753-22766) sets sel.active=false. The filter path is apply16 (4694), which diverts only on painting_mask() (17506-17510). painting_mask checks the filter mask, mask_edit and adjustment/fill kinds, never qm_on. project_selection_to_bounds (1131-1136) returns full coverage when the selection is inactive, so filter_gaussian_blur (23477) blurs the whole layer. qm_on is only read by the stroke, fill and selection paths. store.ts:8305-8310 admits in a ponytail comment that filters still hit the layer's pixels. menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3469) has no quickMask or channelTarget gating. The only UI guard is on data sets (app.ts:5427). e2e/quick-mask.spec.ts never mentions a filter. The edit can be undone, so major, not blocker.

findings.title: Offset, Maximum/Minimum, Dust & Scratches, Surface Blur, Custom, Diffuse, Clouds, Difference Clouds and Lens Flare ignore the layer-mask target
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Other (Offset/Maximum/Minimum/Custom), Noise ▸ Dust & Scratches, Blur ▸ Surface Blur, Stylize ▸ Diffuse, Render ▸ Clouds/Difference Clouds/Lens Flare
findings.evidence: These ops skip apply16 and never check painting_mask(): offset 27167, morph (Maximum/Minimum) 27262, lens_flare 27777, clouds 27846, difference_clouds 27874, diffuse 27903, custom_filter 27930, dust_and_scratches 27960, surface_blur 28254. Each calls refuse_destructive_edit and then writes `layers[active].pixels`. apply16 (4694-4707) sends mask targets to apply16_mask, so Gaussian Blur and the other apply16 filters do edit the mask. The mask tests (mask_edit_tests.rs) cover only the apply16 path.
findings.repro: 1. Add a layer mask to a pixel layer and click the mask thumbnail. 2. Filter ▸ Other ▸ Minimum, radius 5. The layer's image is eroded and the mask is unchanged. 3. On an adjustment layer (whose mask is always the target), Maximum/Minimum/Dust & Scratches refuse with 'adjustment layers hold no pixels', although Gaussian Blur on the same mask works.
findings.impact: Choking or spreading a mask with Maximum/Minimum, and cleaning masks with Dust & Scratches, are standard Photoshop mask workflows. Here they damage the artwork instead. Filters behave inconsistently depending on which engine path they use.
findings.suggested_fix: Route each op through apply16 with a closure that runs the *_buf kernel on a clone and blends it back by `sel` (the spherize pattern at 27609). The mask target, locks, float refusal and history then come for free. Alternatively, add `if self.painting_mask() { return self.apply16_mask(label, …) }` at the top of each. Add mask-target tests for these ops.
findings.verdict_reason: offset (27167), morph (27262), lens_flare (27777), clouds (27846), difference_clouds (27874), diffuse (27903), custom_filter (27930), dust_and_scratches (27960) and surface_blur (28254) all call refuse_destructive_edit and then write layers[active].pixels. None calls painting_mask(). A pixel layer with mask_edit on passes refuse_destructive_edit (kind 0) and has its image edited. An adjustment layer (kind 1) is refused with 'adjustment layers hold no pixels', while apply16 filters route it to apply16_mask. The fil wrappers (app.ts:1449-1481) have no maskEdit guard. mask_edit_tests.rs tests only apply16 ops.

findings.title: Lock Transparent Pixels is ignored by every filter in 8/16-bit documents (32-bit honours it)
findings.feature: All filters × Layers panel ▸ Lock Transparent Pixels
findings.evidence: apply16 (4694-4735) passes only `(pixels, selection)` to the kernel and never reads `lock_transparent`. apply32 (4769-4780) restores alpha and keeps transparent pixels. A restore_locked_transparency helper exists (19489) but only brush/fill paths use it (19515, 20300, 20372, 20682). Kernels change alpha: gaussian_blur writes to16(p[3]) (filters.rs gaussian_blur). The whole-buffer ops (Clouds, Offset, Lens Flare…) also ignore the lock. The only lock-transparent filter test is float-only (mod.rs:58670).
findings.repro: 1. On an 8-bit document, draw a hard-edged opaque shape on a transparent layer. 2. Lock Transparent Pixels. 3. Filter ▸ Blur ▸ Gaussian Blur 10 px. The shape's alpha edge softens and colour bleeds into the transparent area. Convert the same document to 32-bit and the alpha stays locked. Filter ▸ Render ▸ Clouds fills the transparent area too.
findings.impact: This silently ignores a layer lock. Photoshop users rely on it to blur or texture only the painted pixels. The same command gives different results at different bit depths.
findings.suggested_fix: In apply16 (and the whole-buffer ops), when `lock_transparent` is set, snapshot the plane before `f` and call restore_locked_transparency(&before) afterwards. Add an 8-bit engine test mirroring the float test at 58670.
findings.verdict_reason: apply16 (4694-4735) never reads lock_transparent. apply32 (4769-4780) restores alpha and transparent pixels. restore_locked_transparency (19489) is called only at 20304, 20373 and 20683 (fill and brush paths). filters::gaussian_blur (filters.rs:304-314) writes to16(p[3]), so alpha changes. The whole-buffer ops (clouds, offset, lens flare and the rest) only call restore_outside_selection. The app.ts fil path has no lock_transparent handling.

findings.title: Smart filters ignore the active selection, and the filter mask cannot be targeted from the UI
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Convert for Smart Filters → any filter on a Smart Object
findings.evidence: applyFilter (app.ts:1083-1093) calls smart_add_filter for kind 7 and passes no selection. smart_add_filter (mod.rs:14557-14594) creates an all-255 smart_mask whatever `self.sel` holds. apply_smart_filter renders every fid with a `full` selection (36333-36339). set_filter_mask_edit (mod.rs:14936) has no caller in apps/vision/src, so painting or filtering the filter mask is unreachable. The engine's painting_filter_mask branch in apply16 is dead from the UI.
findings.repro: 1. Filter ▸ Convert for Smart Filters. 2. Marquee the left half. 3. Filter ▸ Blur ▸ Gaussian Blur 20. The whole Smart Object blurs. Photoshop seeds the new filter mask from the selection, so only the left half would blur. There is also no way to click or paint the filter mask afterwards to fix it.
findings.impact: Selections are silently ignored on the non-destructive path, which is the path Photoshop steers users to for filters. The only workaround is rasterizing.
findings.suggested_fix: In smart_add_filter, when the mask is being created and `self.sel.active`, initialize smart_mask from the selection coverage. Expose filter-mask targeting (a filter-mask thumbnail row in the Layers panel that calls set_filter_mask_edit), and make applyFilter take the destructive/mask route when the filter mask is targeted.
findings.verdict_reason: applyFilter (app.ts:1083-1093) calls smart_add_filter with no selection. smart_add_filter (mod.rs:14586-14589) seeds smart_mask with all-255 whatever self.sel holds. apply_smart_filter (36323-36339) renders with a 'full' Selection. set_filter_mask_edit (14936) is called only from engine tests (smart_filter_mask_tests.rs:109, mask_edit_tests.rs:249) and the wasm export list. A grep of apps/vision/src finds no caller and no filter-mask row or thumbnail in Panels.tsx. Only Delete and Disable Filter Mask are wired (App.tsx:2940-2945).

findings.title: Spherize, Pinch, Twirl, ZigZag and Polar Coordinates centre on the layer plane, not the selection
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Distort ▸ Spherize/Pinch/Twirl/ZigZag/Polar Coordinates
findings.evidence: spherize_buf (36805-36813), twirl_buf (36868-36874), zigzag_buf (37597-37602) and polar_buf (37298-37305) take cx=w/2, cy=h/2 and a radius from the whole plane. The wrappers (27609-27660) run the kernel on the full plane and then `filters::blend_back(px, &filtered, sel)`, so the selection only masks the result.
findings.repro: 1. Draw an elliptical marquee around a small object in the upper-left corner. 2. Filter ▸ Distort ▸ Spherize, 100%. Photoshop bulges the object inside the ellipse. Vision reveals a slice of a whole-image bulge centred on the canvas, a shifted and stretched fragment. Twirl and Pinch on a selection behave the same way.
findings.impact: These distort filters are almost always used on a selection (e.g. spherize an eye or a lens), and there the common path gives the wrong result.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the plane-local selection bounds and run the *_buf kernel on that sub-rectangle (copy out, remap with the centre and radius of the bounds, copy back), then blend_back by selection. Do the same in the smart path if smart filters gain selection masks.
findings.verdict_reason: spherize_buf (36805-36810), twirl_buf (36868-36872), polar_buf (37298-37303) and zigzag_buf (37597-37601) take cx=w/2, cy=h/2 of the full plane. The wrappers spherize, pinch, twirl, polar_coordinates (27609-27650) and zigzag (27761-27767) run the kernel on a full-plane clone and then blend_back by sel, so the selection only clips the result. distortImpl (app.ts:1827-1839) passes no bounds. Nothing crops to the selection bounds.

findings.title: Last Filter (⌥⌘F) repeats cancelled filters, skips Distort, Oil Paint and gallery filters, and has no tests
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Last Filter
findings.evidence: The `fil` proxy (app.ts:1493-1506) sets `lastFilter` on every call, including the suspended preview calls PreviewDialog makes each frame (dialogs/common.tsx:283-298). Cancel (common.tsx:366) never restores it. `distort` (app.ts:1853) and `neural` (2069) are wrapped only in withOpCapture, not the lastFilter proxy, so all 11 Distort dialogs, Radial Blur and Oil Paint never become the Last Filter. The pixel-layer Blur Gallery (runBlurSteps 1126), Liquify, Vanishing Point and Camera Raw never set it either. Filter Gallery dispatches through fil.* (1531-1583), so only its last effect is remembered, and a cancelled gallery preview sets it too. The menu entry is always enabled (App.tsx:3117; nothing in menuEnablement). No test references lastfilter or repeatLastFilter.
findings.repro: (a) Apply Gaussian Blur 2. Open Motion Blur, drag Distance to 200, press Cancel, then ⌥⌘F: Motion Blur 200 is applied. (b) Apply Gaussian Blur 2, then Filter ▸ Distort ▸ Twirl OK, then ⌥⌘F: Gaussian Blur 2 is applied again, not Twirl. (c) Filter Gallery with Cutout + Grain, OK, then ⌥⌘F: only Grain is re-applied, as a standalone filter.
findings.impact: The most-used Filter shortcut applies filters the user just cancelled or never chose, with a visible pixel change that has to be undone.
findings.suggested_fix: Stop assigning lastFilter while `_suspended` is set. Set it explicitly on commit: in PreviewDialog.ok (when the committed op is in the fil/distort/neural namespace), in the non-preview OK handlers, in commitGalleryStack (the whole-stack thunk), in commitBlurSteps, and in the Liquify/VP/Camera Raw commits. Wrap `distort` and `neural.oilPaint` with the same proxy. Disable the menu item until a filter has run. Add a unit test covering cancel, then repeat.
findings.verdict_reason: The fil proxy (app.ts:1498-1506) assigns lastFilter on every call. PreviewDialog.applyFrame (common.tsx:283-304) calls applyRef.current(), e.g. fil.motion for Motion Blur (Dialogs.tsx:3221), on every preview frame, and cancel (366-372) never resets it. distort (app.ts:1853) and neural (2069, oilPaint at 2050) are withOpCapture only, not the proxy. Radial Blur is in distortImpl (1851). runBlurSteps and applyGalleryBlurPins/applySpinBlurPins bypass fil for pixel layers. runGalleryStack dispatches each effect through fil.*, so only the last fil effect sticks. lastfilter is absent from menuEnablement. The only references are App.tsx:3117 and app.ts, with no tests. The OK path does work: the last preview frame holds the final values. So the bug hits cancel and the Distort, Oil Paint and gallery routes, all undoable. Major is defensible.

findings.title: Brute-force O(r²) kernels freeze the app at in-range radii, with no cancel or progress, and filters process the whole plane even for tiny selections
findings.feature: Noise ▸ Dust & Scratches / Median, Blur ▸ Surface Blur / Smart Blur, Other ▸ Maximum/Minimum; heavy live previews (Motion Blur, Unsharp Mask)
findings.evidence: dust_scratches_buf (36939-36970) sorts a (2r+1)² window per pixel per channel, and the UI allows r up to 100 (Dialogs.tsx:8237). surface_blur_buf (36903) is (2r+1)² per pixel per channel, r up to 100 (Dialogs.tsx:8525). morph_buf (37008) is (2r+1)² per pixel, r up to 250 (Dialogs.tsx:6899). smart_blur (filters.rs:175) doubles the window at High quality, r up to 100. filters::median (filters.rs:6259) sorts (2r+1)², and MCP fil.median advertises radius 1..100 (commands.ts:840). The engine runs on the UI thread (no Worker in EngineClient). Every kernel processes the full plane and applies the selection only afterwards (blend_back / restore_outside_selection). PreviewDialog re-runs full-resolution Motion Blur (distance up to 999) and Unsharp (radius up to 250 → 501-tap kernel) on every settled slider change.
findings.repro: On a 12 MP photo: Filter ▸ Other ▸ Maximum, radius 250 → about 251k samples × 4 channels per pixel, around 1e13 operations. Or Dust & Scratches radius 100 inside a 50×50 px marquee: the whole image is processed. The window stops responding with no progress and no way to cancel.
findings.impact: The app looks hung for minutes to hours. Users may force-quit and lose unsaved work.
findings.suggested_fix: Use O(1)-per-pixel algorithms: van Herk/Gil-Werman or separable passes for square Max/Min, histogram medians (Huang or constant-time) for Median and Dust & Scratches, a separable/box approximation or downsampled pass for Surface/Smart Blur. Crop processing to the selection bounds plus the radius. Preview at proxy resolution. Clamp MCP ranges. Longer term, run long filters in a worker with a cancel control.
findings.verdict_reason: surface_blur_buf (36903) scans (2r+1)² per pixel per channel. dust_scratches_buf (36939) collects and sorts (2r+1)² per pixel per channel. morph_buf (37008) scans (2r+1)² per pixel. filters::median (filters.rs:6259) sorts (2r+1)². Dialog ranges: Dust & Scratches 1-100 (Dialogs.tsx:8235), Surface Blur 1-100 (8525), Max/Min 1-250 (6899). MCP fil.median advertises 1..100 (commands.ts:840). Each kernel runs over the full plane and only then applies restore_outside_selection or blend_back. EngineClient has no Worker, so these run on the UI thread. Even realistic settings (Surface Blur r≈30-40 on 24 MP) come to around 1e11-1e12 inner iterations: minutes of frozen UI with no cancel. Small radii are fine, but a hang with a force-quit risk at in-range values holds major.

findings.title: MCP fil.unsharp and fil.sharpen document Photoshop units but pass raw values the engine reads as fractions
findings.feature: MCP fil.unsharp / fil.sharpen
findings.evidence: commands.ts:826-834 documents `amount Amount percent (1..500)` and `threshold Threshold levels (0..255)` and calls fil.unsharp(radius, amount, threshold) unchanged. sharpen (815-822) documents 0..500. The engine (filters.rs:432-462) uses `th = threshold * 65535` and `o + diff * amount`, so amount 1.0 means 100% and threshold is 0..1. The Unsharp dialog converts with a/100 and t/255 (Dialogs.tsx:3189), and e2e/filters.spec.ts:31 notes 'threshold is 0..1'. handlers.test.ts:287-301 locks in the raw forwarding.
findings.repro: MCP call fil.unsharp {radius:2, amount:150, threshold:4}: no pixel passes a threshold of 4×65535, the image does not change, a history step is still pushed, and the tool reports 'Unsharp mask applied'. With threshold 0, amount 150 means 15000%, which blows the image out. fil.sharpen {amount:100} gives 10000%.
findings.impact: MCP agents following the documented ranges get no visible effect or a destroyed image, and are told the call succeeded.
findings.suggested_fix: Convert in the wrappers (amount/100, threshold/255, and sharpen amount/100), or change the docs to engine units. Update handlers.test.ts and regenerate the manifest (pnpm mcp:codegen).
findings.verdict_reason: commands.ts:815-835 documents amount 0..500 / 1..500 (percent) and threshold 0..255 levels, then forwards the values unchanged. fil.unsharp and fil.sharpen (app.ts:1191-1194) and filter_unsharp_mask (mod.rs:23508) do not convert either. filters::unsharp_mask (filters.rs:432-462) uses th = threshold*65535 and o + diff*amount. The dialog divides by 100 and 255 (Dialogs.tsx:3189). threshold 4 means th=262140 > 65535, so no pixel changes. apply16 still pushes undo, so applied() (commands.ts:589-607) sees undo_pushes move and reports success. handlers.test.ts:286/298 locks in the raw forwarding.

findings.title: Filters are enabled and run unchanged in Grayscale, Indexed and CMYK documents, writing pixels the mode cannot hold
findings.feature: All filters × Image ▸ Mode (Grayscale/Indexed/CMYK/Multichannel)
findings.evidence: menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3469) has no colour-mode gating. apply16 and the whole-buffer ops never read `self.mode` or `indexed_palette`. convert_grayscale (mod.rs:9084-9111) desaturates only once, at conversion. set_mode's CMYK/Multichannel separation (8088-8135) also runs only at conversion. Nothing re-indexes to indexed_palette after an edit. Chromatic filters bake in fg/bg or fixed colours: Lens Flare ghosts, Clouds, Fibers, Neon Glow, Stained Glass, Tree, Flame, Picture Frame.
findings.repro: 1. Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale. 2. Filter ▸ Render ▸ Lens Flare, OK: coloured flare pixels appear in a document that still reports Grayscale. Or: Image ▸ Mode ▸ Indexed Color, then Gaussian Blur: the result has off-palette colours while the mode stays Indexed. Photoshop greys out all filters in Indexed and Bitmap, and Lens Flare, Lighting Effects and the Filter Gallery in CMYK/Lab/Grayscale.
findings.impact: The document's mode no longer matches its pixels, so the canvas, Info readouts and mode-specific exports disagree (e.g. a gray or indexed writer quietly re-quantizes).
findings.suggested_fix: Gate filter enablement by doc mode and depth the way Photoshop does, at least Indexed/Bitmap (all filters) and colour-generating filters in Grayscale/CMYK. Or re-conform after each edit: desaturate in mode 1, re-separate in modes 2 and 4, re-index when a palette is present.
findings.verdict_reason: The core claim holds. menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3469) has no mode gating. set_mode (8088-8135) separates and convert_grayscale (9084-9111) desaturates only at conversion. Nothing re-indexes after an edit, so Gaussian Blur on an Indexed document gives off-palette colours. The Lens Flare example is refuted: lens_flare_buf (~37099-37115) adds the same scalar to R, G and B, so it stays grey on a grey image. Clouds uses fg/bg, which default to black and white. So Grayscale contamination needs coloured swatches or a chromatic filter. Brushes can also paint off-mode colours, so this is a document-wide mode-fidelity gap, not a filter defect. Downgraded to minor: the results are wrong for the mode but undoable, and no data is corrupted.

findings.title: Frequency Separation hard-codes radius 8 and leaves a broken Linear Light copy when High Pass is refused or only partly applied
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Frequency Separation…
findings.evidence: App.tsx:2933 calls frequencySeparation(8), with no dialog even though the label ends in '…'. app.ts:1704-1721 duplicates the layer, calls e.filter_high_pass and sets Linear Light without checking whether the engine refused. filter_high_pass is apply16-only (mod.rs:24639), so it refuses on 32-bit float layers, type/vector/smart layers and locked layers, and with an active selection it only filters inside it. Gaussian Blur does have a 32-bit path, so the Low layer still blurs.
findings.repro: On a 32-bit document (or with a marquee active), run Filter ▸ Frequency Separation. The 'High Frequency' layer is an unfiltered copy in Linear Light (outside the marquee, or everywhere in 32-bit), and the composite is blown out. Several undo steps are needed to recover.
findings.impact: The document is visibly corrupted until undone. Users cannot choose the separation radius, which Photoshop users always set.
findings.suggested_fix: Open a radius dialog. Check refusals (undo_pushes or last_edit_error) after each engine call and roll the whole rec() back if either filter refused. Run with the selection suspended, or refuse when a selection is active.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:2933 calls frequencySeparation(8) directly, and the menu label is 'Frequency Separation…' (psMenuData.ts:2981). app.ts:1704-1721 duplicates the layer, runs filter_high_pass and sets Linear Light, all without checking refusal. filter_high_pass (24639) is apply16-only. apply16 calls reject_legacy_float_edit, which refuses 32-bit float layers, while filter_gaussian_blur has an apply32 path. Locked, smart and type duplicates are refused by both filters. With a selection, both filters only edit inside it. rec() (501-509) runs the thunk with no rollback.

findings.title: Several filter dialogs use unbounded raw number inputs (Tiles count can hang the engine)
findings.feature: Stylize ▸ Tiles, Pixelate ▸ Color Halftone / Stained Glass, Distort ▸ Wave / Shear, Other ▸ Custom
findings.evidence: Tiles (Dialogs.tsx:8124-8147), Color Halftone (8148), Stained Glass (8187), Wave (3421-3458), Shear (3371) and Custom (9777) use `<input type=number>` with `Number(v) || 0` and no min/max, unlike the NumberField-based dialogs. filters::tiles (filters.rs:3991) loops nt × nt tiles with i32 `ti * wi / nt` maths. Photoshop limits Number of Tiles to 1..99 and Maximum Offset to 1..99%.
findings.repro: Filter ▸ Stylize ▸ Tiles, type 100000 in Number Of Tiles, OK. The engine iterates 1e10 empty tiles and the UI freezes. Maximum Offset 1000% also gives nonsensical offsets.
findings.impact: Easy to freeze the app or get garbage from a typo. Other dialogs silently accept out-of-range values.
findings.suggested_fix: Use NumberField with Photoshop's ranges (Tiles 1-99 / 1-99%, Color Halftone radius 4-127, Wave generators 1-999, Custom scale 1-9999), or clamp in the fil wrappers.
findings.verdict_reason: Tiles (Dialogs.tsx:8123-8147), Color Halftone, Stained Glass, Shear (3371-3380) and Wave (~3436) use <input type=number> with Number(v)||0 and no min/max. Tiles clamps only to Math.max(1, …). filters::tiles (filters.rs:3991-4036) loops nt×nt, so 100000 gives 1e10 iterations on the UI thread. ti*wi/nt is i32 maths, so very large values can also overflow. The offset percentage is passed as /100 with no clamp (app.ts:1419-1422).

findings.title: Gaussian-based radii are roughly half as strong as Photoshop's (σ = radius/2, kernel cut at 2σ)
findings.feature: Blur ▸ Gaussian Blur, Sharpen ▸ Unsharp Mask/Sharpen, Other ▸ High Pass
findings.evidence: gaussian_kernel (filters.rs:285-301) sets r = ceil(radius) and sigma = radius/2, so the kernel is truncated at 2σ. Photoshop's Gaussian Blur Radius behaves as roughly the standard deviation, so an R px blur in Vision matches about R/2 in Photoshop. Unsharp and High Pass reuse the kernel.
findings.repro: Gaussian Blur 10 px in Vision vs Photoshop on the same image: Vision's blur is visibly narrower. Recipes and presets (e.g. High Pass sharpening, Unsharp 'radius 1.0') ported from Photoshop come out under-strength.
findings.impact: Parameters in tutorials, actions and PSD workflows don't carry over. The 2σ truncation also adds slight ringing and banding.
findings.suggested_fix: Use sigma = radius with a 3σ kernel, or calibrate against Photoshop. Version the smart-filter fids so stored stacks keep rendering as before.
findings.verdict_reason: gaussian_kernel (filters.rs:284-301) sets r = ceil(radius) and sigma = radius/2, so the kernel is truncated at 2σ. It has been unchanged since the initial scaffold (89d53207). gaussian_blur, unsharp_mask (filters.rs:448) and high_pass reuse it. The Photoshop comparison (PS radius ≈ σ) is widely documented, e.g. in ImageMagick's blur notes, but it was not measured here, so the parity magnitude is medium confidence. Changing it would also change how stored smart-filter stacks render.

findings.title: Liquify, Vanishing Point and Convert for Smart Filters are not recorded by Actions
findings.feature: Actions recording × Filter ▸ Liquify / Vanishing Point / Convert for Smart Filters
findings.evidence: finishLiquify (store.ts:3200-3218) and applyVanishingPoint (store.ts:3260-3275) commit without rec() or actions.record. smart.convert (app.ts:2450-2464) is a plain object method, not wrapped in withOpCapture or rec(), unlike AWA (app.ts:1885, rec-wrapped) and every fil/distort action.
findings.repro: Start recording an action, run Filter ▸ Convert for Smart Filters and then Filter ▸ Liquify (warp, OK), stop. Only the steps after them are recorded, so playback skips the conversion and the warp.
findings.impact: Photoshop records Convert to Smart Object and Liquify (with its mesh). Batch and droplet workflows built on them silently do less.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap smart.convert in rec() with an op descriptor. Record the Liquify commit with the saved mesh (the mesh import/export code already exists) and the VP commit as volatile steps.
findings.verdict_reason: finishLiquify (store.ts:3212-3228) and applyVanishingPoint (3259-3274) commit with no rec() or recording. Their callers (App.tsx:705, 1680, 2109, 2328) call store.endLiquify and applyVanishingPoint directly. Neither appears in RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:904+). smart.convert (app.ts:2450-2464) is a plain object method, not wrapped in withOpCapture. The visionOps namespaces (2333) cover only adj, fil, xform, neural, anim and distort, so recording skips all three.

findings.title: All filters stay enabled in 32-bit documents though only Gaussian Blur, Sharpen and Unsharp Mask have float kernels
findings.feature: Filter menu × Image ▸ Mode ▸ 32 Bits/Channel
findings.evidence: Only Gaussian Blur, Sharpen and Unsharp Mask call apply32 (grep of `apply32("`). Every other filter reaches reject_legacy_float_edit (3778), which sets '… is not 32-bit-float safe'. menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434) does not consider depth.
findings.repro: Convert to 32 Bits/Channel. Open Filter ▸ Distort ▸ Wave, set values, OK. A toast says Wave is not 32-bit-float safe. The same happens with PreviewDialog filters on each preview frame.
findings.impact: Users set up dialogs only to be refused. Photoshop greys out filters unavailable in 32-bit, and supports more of them there (Motion/Radial/Box Blur, Add Noise, High Pass, Max/Min, Offset…).
findings.suggested_fix: Grey out filters without a float kernel when doc depth is 32 (a static allow-list next to the fid table), and grow the apply32 coverage over time.
findings.verdict_reason: Among filters, apply32 is called only for Gaussian Blur, Sharpen and Unsharp Mask (mod.rs:23481, 23502, 23512). The other apply32 users are adjustments (Levels, Curves, Hue/Sat, Exposure). Every other filter reaches reject_legacy_float_edit, which becomes reject_float_edit_for_layer (3914-3925) and sets 'X is not 32-bit-float safe…'. menuEnablement has no depth gating. PreviewDialog filters are refused on each preview frame.

findings.title: The smart filter parameter editor shows 'Value n' for Oil Paint and for most Tree and Flame parameters
findings.feature: Layers panel ▸ Smart Filters rows (re-edit)
findings.evidence: SMART_FILTER_PARAMS (Panels.tsx:299-341) has no fid 12 (Oil Paint, 6 params). Fid 28 (Tree) labels only 5 of its 10 params (app.ts:1246-1247), and fid 29 (Flame) only 4 of 8 (app.ts:1251-1253). The rest fall back to `Value ${i+1}` (Panels.tsx:1259).
findings.repro: Convert for Smart Filters, apply Oil Paint, Tree or Flame, then expand the smart filter row: fields read 'Value 1…6', or 'Value 6…10' for Leaves Amount, Branch Height and so on.
findings.impact: Re-editing these smart filters is guesswork.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the missing fid entries with labels and ranges matching the dialogs.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed with one correction: fid 12 is not missing. SMART_FILTER_PARAMS has 12: [{label:'Radius'}] (Panels.tsx:311), the legacy layout. Oil Paint now stores six params under fid 12 (app.ts:2048-2051), so Stylization is labelled 'Radius' and the other five fall back to 'Value 2'..'Value 6' (Panels.tsx:1258-1259). Tree (fid 28) stores 10 params (app.ts:1246-1247) against 5 labels (angle, Depth, Color R/G/B). Flame (fid 29) stores 8 (app.ts:1251-1253) against 4 labels (SEED, Color R/G/B).

areas.coverage:
Reviewed by reading code only. I ran no builds and no tests.

**Entry points inventoried: 23**
- Filter ▸ Neural Filters submenu, 10 items: nai, njpeg, nsr, ndenoise, ncol, ndepthblur, nharmonize, nrestore, nfaceliquify, nskinsmooth.
- Edit menu, 8 items: genfill, genfillml, genimage, genexpand, genbg, the injected gensimilar, removedistractions, removereflections.
- Select menu, 2 items: subj, rembg. The same two actions also appear on the contextual task bar and the tool options bar.
- Type menu, 1 item: matchfontai.
- Remove tool, ML tier: removeStroke using LaMa or MI-GAN.
- Camera Raw Subject mask: subjectOutline.

**Other surfaces**
- MCP: 14 ml.* tools.
- Model registry: 13 units. Only 3 are bundled (styles, u2netp, super-res), which is 7 checksum-pinned files.
- Native plugin: the commands and path validation in src-tauri/src/model_dl.rs.

**Files read in full or traced**
- src/ml: onnx.ts, diffusion.ts, modelSource.ts, modelRegistry.ts, modelDownload.ts, mlJob.ts, ortEnv.ts, tiling.ts, styleBlend.ts, editStamp.ts.
- Dialogs.tsx: NeuralAI, AiDenoise, ModelManager, FaceAwareLiquifySection, RemoveDistractions/RemoveReflections, Deblock, and the AI Models preferences pane.
- state/app.ts: the ml, models and neural objects, and removeStroke. Also state/skinSmoothing.ts.
- App.tsx: runMl, menu handlers, enablement, the first-run model toast.
- mcp/commands.ts: the ML section.
- Model files and gates: public/models/MODELS.md, checksums.txt, .gitignore, scripts/check-model-licenses.mjs, the vite selectivePublicAssets plugin, tauri.conf.json (CSP and asset scope).
- Engine functions in packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs: stamp_image, export_png/export_icc, select_none, set_selection_mask, select_polygon, select_color_range_batch, add_layer, generative_fill, remove_distractions, remove_reflections, split_reflections, super_resolution/can_super_resolution, refuse_destructive_edit, the history-transaction API, mark_ai_generated/c2pa_action_list, MAX_PIXELS/MAX_DIM, filters::deblock.
- Tests checked by grep: e2e/ml.spec.ts, ml-menu, neural-filters-tier2, ai-denoise-dialog; unit tests faceLiquify, neuralFilters, onnxPipeline, diffusion.

**Not reviewed or not confirmed**
- How the real models behave at runtime.
- The contract of the OpenSeeFace landmark model. No copy exists on this machine to inspect its tensor shapes.
- The internals of model_dl.rs import_model_at.
- genMeta.ts.
- Sky Replacement (outside this area).
- How a stamped RGB layer renders in CMYK, Lab, Indexed, Bitmap or Multichannel documents.
- The geometry of the Camera Raw subject outline against smart-object sources.
areas.parity_notes:
- **Neural Filters submenu:** all 10 items have a monetId. What works in a release build differs by item:
  - **Work out of the box:** Style Transfer (5 fixed styles, 224² network then upscaled, so soft on large photos), JPEG Artifacts Removal (classic engine deblock), Super Resolution (ESPCN 3×, see the size finding), and Skin Smoothing (skin-tone color-range gate plus Smart Blur).
  - **Fall back to a heuristic:** Colorize and Photo Restoration.
  - **Need user-imported weights:** AI Denoise, Depth Blur, Harmonize and Face-Aware Liquify.
- **Photoshop Neural Filters with no Vision equivalent anywhere in the menu:** Smart Portrait (only partly covered by Face-Aware Liquify), Makeup Transfer, Landscape Mixer, Color Transfer, Super Zoom.
- **Generative items:** Generative Fill (prompted), Generate Image, Generate Background, Restyle and Generative Expand need user-built SD-1.5 (WebGPU) or bring-your-own MI-GAN weights. None ship, so in a release build they are gated or fail. The Edit ▸ Generative Fill (Synthesis) command is a classical fill algorithm, not ML.
- **Non-ML stand-ins:**
  - Remove Distractions is a median outlier filter.
  - Remove Reflections and Split Reflections use a deterministic detector.
  - Select ▸ Sky is a heuristic.
  - The Remove tool falls back to spot heal unless LaMa or MI-GAN has been imported.
- **Model downloads:** the app deliberately never downloads models; they install only through Model Manager ▸ Install from Disk with SHA-256 pins. The native download command refuses before reading any input. Import validates paths and ids.
- **Licensing:**
  - The shipped set is 7 files: 5 fast-neural-style (BSD-3-Clause), u2netp (Apache-2.0) and super-res (BSD-3-Clause / Apache-2.0). It is enforced by check:models against checksums.txt and THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md.
  - The unlicensed SD test placeholder and MI-GAN are correctly excluded.
  - The CreativeML OpenRAIL-M text ships and is shown for acceptance before SD-1.5 import.
- **Content Credentials:** Style Transfer, Colorize, Super-Resolution and Face-Aware Liquify outputs are not tagged as AI-modified. Only the fill paths and Generate Background call mark_ai_generated. Generate Image is also untagged; that one is reported as a finding.

findings.title: Every ML filter reads the composite through a color-managed decode, so results are color-shifted on Display P3 / Adobe RGB / Rec.2020 documents
findings.feature: All ML filters (Style, AI Denoise, Colorize, Depth Blur, Harmonize, Restore, Remove Background, Generate Background, Generative Fill/Expand, Remove tool ML tier)
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ml/onnx.ts:76-87 composite() does engine.e.export_png() -> new Image() -> drawImage -> getImageData. export_png embeds the working profile (packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:29388-29393 export_icc, and psd_icc_profile at 34434 embeds P3/AdobeRGB/Rec2020). The app already knows this decode path converts: apps/vision/src/state/app.ts:5376-5381 pngToImageData says "`colorSpaceConversion: \"none\"` is the only decode path that ignores iCCP", and bugs #33/#34 (app.ts:5189-5191, 5354-5358) fixed the same root cause for export. The ML results are then written back as raw document values (stamp_image, onnx.ts:157, 419).
findings.repro: 1) Open an iPhone photo with an embedded Display P3 profile, using the default preserve-embedded-profile policy (app.ts:7365-7386). 2) Run Filter > Neural Filters > AI Neural Filters > Apply 'candy' at Strength 0, or Select > Remove Background and hide the original. 3) Compare the new layer with the original.
findings.impact: The new full-canvas layer is the browser's sRGB-converted values reinterpreted as P3 or Adobe RGB, so it visibly shifts saturation and hue compared with the layer beneath. Generative Fill and Remove-tool patches do not match the colors around them.
findings.suggested_fix: Decode in composite() with createImageBitmap(blob, { colorSpaceConversion: "none" }), or reuse pngToImageData(png, false). A cheaper option is to read the engine's RGBA output buffer directly.
findings.verdict_reason: onnx.ts:76-87 composite() decodes engine.e.export_png() with new Image() and drawImage. export_png_with_icc (mod.rs:29427-29438) embeds export_icc(), which is psd_icc_profile(self.profile, false, true), so any built-in non-sRGB working profile gets an iCCP chunk. The app's own pngToImageData comment (app.ts:5368-5381) says an /drawImage decode is colour-managed in both WebKit and Chromium, and that colorSpaceConversion:'none' is the only path that ignores iCCP. Bugs #33/#34 fixed exactly this for export. The browser-converted sRGB values are then blended (blendAmount/blendStyle) and stamped back as raw document values (stampResult; compositeFillOntoNewLayer). applyOpenedImageProfilePolicy (app.ts:7365-7386) assigns the embedded P3 profile on preserve. No test covers this: the unit tests mock export_png with 3 bytes. Documents with an sRGB or custom profile are untagged and unaffected.

findings.title: Colorize and Photo Restoration buttons apply a destructive, Amount-ignoring fallback to the active layer, and Cancel or any error also triggers that fallback
findings.feature: Filter > Neural Filters > Colorize / Photo Restoration (Neural Filters dialog; ml.colorize/ml.restore facade)
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ui/Dialogs.tsx:11489-11492 and 11508-11511: `try { colorizeML(p, colAmount) } catch { p(...); neural.colorize(); }` and `catch { ...; engine.e.filter_deblock(3); engine.commit(); }`. The buttons are labelled "→ New Layer". The catch-all also swallows the AbortError that throwIfCancelled raises (onnx.ts:152 stampResult; tiling.ts:69). filter_deblock(3) is clamped to maximum strength (packages/engine/src/raster/filters.rs:5707), and neural.colorize is a fixed gradient map applied to the active layer (app.ts:2051-2067). The "not installed" notice is then overwritten by run()'s "✓ Done." (Dialogs.tsx:11343). The facade duplicates the same logic (app.ts:2100-2125).
findings.repro: Release build (colorizer.onnx and fbcnn.onnx are never shipped): Filter > Neural Filters > Colorize, set Amount to 20%, click 'Colorize → New Layer'. With the models imported instead: start Restore on a large image and press 'Cancel Job'.
findings.impact: In release, which is the common path, a color photo's active layer is recolored in place through a blue-to-cream gradient map at full strength. No new layer is created and the status reads '✓ Done.'. With the models installed, pressing Cancel applies a different destructive filter instead of cancelling. The edit can still be undone, but the result is not what the user asked for.
findings.suggested_fix: Fall back only when the model is actually missing: check models status first, or catch the specific not-installed error and rethrow isMlCancel errors. Route the fallback through a new layer and apply Amount, or disable the button and say the model is missing. Keep the fallback notice visible after the job ends.
findings.verdict_reason: Dialogs.tsx:11489-11492 and 11508-11511 wrap colorizeML/restoreML in a bare catch{}. That catch also swallows the AbortError from throwIfCancelled (stampResult onnx.ts:152; tileFilter tiling.ts:69), so 'Cancel Job' (Dialogs.tsx:11198) applies the fallback instead of cancelling. colorizer.onnx and fbcnn.onnx are in public/models/.gitignore, so they are never bundled, and requireModel throws, which makes the fallback the common release path. neural.colorize (app.ts:2051-2067) is a fixed 4-stop gradient map written onto the active layer through rec(adjust_gradient_map), with no new layer and no Amount. filter_deblock(3) clamps strength to 1 (filters.rs:5707). run() then overwrites the notice with '✓ Done.' (Dialogs.tsx:11343). The facade (app.ts:2100-2125) duplicates this. The menu items open this dialog. The edit can be undone.

findings.title: Neural Filters dialog reports '✓ Done.' when a job returned ok:false, so Generate Image, Restyle and Replace Background silently do nothing in release
findings.feature: Edit > Generate Image / Generate Background (Neural Filters dialog), plus doc-changed, Expand-blocked and WebGPU-gated paths
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ui/Dialogs.tsx:11343 `try { await fn((m) => setStatus(m)); setStatus("✓ Done."); }` ignores the returned {ok}. generateRGBA reports a missing model or the WebGPU gate only through onProgress and returns ok:false (diffusion.ts:240-259). The same pattern applies to generateBackgroundML (onnx.ts:598-599), stampResult's doc-changed branch (onnx.ts:154), generativeExpandML's 'Expansion blocked' (onnx.ts:573-575), and generativeFillDiffusion's silent MI-GAN downgrade (onnx.ts:541-543). The Generate buttons are enabled even when sdGen === 'missing' (Dialogs.tsx:11467-11471).
findings.repro: Release build (no SD weights are shipped): Edit > Generate Image (AI · Diffusion)…, click 'Generate → New Document'.
findings.impact: No document is produced and the status line says '✓ Done.'. The error text ('No Stable Diffusion models at /models/sd…') flashes and is immediately replaced. The same false success appears for 'Replace Background' (after a U²-Net pass), for Restyle, and when real SD is installed but WebGPU is missing (prompted fill silently ignores the prompt).
findings.suggested_fix: In run(), inspect the result: if it is an object with ok === false, keep the last progress message or show an error. Disable the Generate, Restyle and Replace buttons when sdGen === 'missing'.
findings.verdict_reason: The code matches: run() at Dialogs.tsx:11343 ignores the resolved value. generateRGBA returns ok:false after only an onProgress message (diffusion.ts:240-259), and so do the Expand-blocked path (onnx.ts:573-575), the stampResult doc-changed branch and the MI-GAN downgrade (onnx.ts:541-543). The Generate/Restyle/Replace buttons are gated only on busy and prompt (Dialogs.tsx:11467-11471). Downgraded to minor because the dialog already shows a persistent role=alert 'Stable Diffusion weights are not installed' when sdGen !== 'real' (Dialogs.tsx:11472-11476), and a WebGPU warning (11367). The user is told up front, so the defect is the misleading success status rather than a feature that silently misleads.

findings.title: Super Resolution menu item runs an unguarded 3× upscale into a new document, which fails on any photo above ~8.9 MP; the menu says '2×, fast'
findings.feature: Filter > Neural Filters > Super Resolution (2×, fast) / Neural dialog 'Super-Resolution 3×' / MCP ml.superResolution
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ml/onnx.ts:231-284 allocates outW=w*3 × outH=h*3 Float32 plus three RGBA buffers and a canvas, then store.openImage. There is no dimension or budget check. The engine limit is MAX_PIXELS 80,000,000 and MAX_DIM 32,767 (packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:1049-1050), and fromImageLayers rejects 'document dimensions out of range' (mod.rs:7193). The menu label is 'Super Resolution (2×, fast)' (src/ui/psMenuData.ts:3003) but the handler is `nsr: () => runMl("Super-Resolution", ml.superResolution)` (App.tsx:3201), which is the 3× ESPCN. The engine's actual 2× path (neural.superResolution, app.ts:2037, guarded by can_super_resolution) is unused by the menu. The menu runMl path has no progress and no cancel.
findings.repro: Open a 12 MP photo (4000×3000) and choose Filter > Neural Filters > Super Resolution (2×, fast).
findings.impact: About 250 tile inferences plus roughly 2 GB of JS buffers, running for minutes with no progress and no cancel, then an error toast ('document dimensions out of range') or a failed canvas allocation. It cannot succeed on typical camera images, and the label promises something different.
findings.suggested_fix: Pre-check (w*3)*(h*3) <= 80e6 and each side <= 32767, and refuse up front with a clear message. Either wire the menu item to the 2× engine path its label describes or relabel it '3×'. Run it through beginMlJob so it gets progress and Cancel.
findings.verdict_reason: psMenuData.ts:3003 labels nsr 'Super Resolution (2×, fast)', but App.tsx:3201 routes it to ml.superResolution, which is the 3× ESPCN (onnx.ts:231-284). There is no size pre-check. The 12 MP example tiles 18×14 = 252 inferences, allocates a 108M-element Float32Array plus three 432 MB RGBA buffers and canvases, then calls store.openImage → Engine.fromImageLayers → from_decoded. That refuses above MAX_PIXELS=80,000,000 (mod.rs:1049-1050, 7145-7146) with 'image dimensions out of range' (the wording differs slightly from the finding). runMl passes a no-op progress callback and never calls beginMlJob, so there is no progress or cancel. The engine's 2× path (neural.superResolution / can_super_resolution) is not used by any menu item.

findings.title: Remove Background leaves the background visible: it stacks a cutout copy over the untouched original
findings.feature: Select > Remove Background (AI) / contextual task bar / Neural dialog / MCP ml.removeBackground
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ml/onnx.ts:678-696 builds RGBA = composite with alpha = saliency, calls store.addLayer() and stamp_image on the new layer, and never masks or hides the source layers. The e2e test (e2e/ml.spec.ts:54-62) asserts only that the layer count grew by 1, not the composite.
findings.repro: Open a photo of a subject on a background and choose Select > Remove Background (AI).
findings.impact: The canvas looks identical before and after, because the subject sits over the original subject and the original background still shows around it. Photoshop hides the background with a layer mask. Users will read this as the command doing nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the matte as a layer mask on the active (source) layer, or hide the layers beneath the cutout. Add an e2e assertion that background pixels become transparent.
findings.verdict_reason: onnx.ts:678-696 builds the composite with alpha set to saliency, then calls store.addLayer() and stamp_image on the new layer, and never masks or hides the source. The subject is stamped over identical pixels, so the composite is visually unchanged. e2e/ml.spec.ts:54-62 asserts only the layer count and ret.ok. The MCP tool reports success ('Removed background onto a new layer'). Nothing elsewhere hides the original.

findings.title: Neural filters ignore the active selection and silently discard it
findings.feature: Style Transfer, AI Denoise, Colorize, Depth Blur, Photo Restoration (stampResult path)
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ml/onnx.ts:151-160 stampResult calls `engine.e.select_none(); // whole-document result` before stamping a full-canvas opaque layer. Only Harmonize reads the selection (onnx.ts:869). Fill jobs already capture the mask at job start and apply it once (compositeFillOntoNewLayer, onnx.ts:405-426), so the same approach is available here.
findings.repro: Make an elliptical selection on a portrait, then run AI Denoise or Colorize from Filter > Neural Filters.
findings.impact: The whole image is processed and covered by the new layer, and the user's selection is deselected. Photoshop confines filters to the selection. The user has to undo twice and redo the selection work.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the selection mask with the edit stamp at job start and write it into the stamped layer's alpha, as compositeFillOntoNewLayer does. Restore the selection afterwards.
findings.verdict_reason: stampResult (onnx.ts:151-160) calls engine.e.select_none() before stamping a full-canvas layer with alpha 255. select_none pushes a 'Deselect' undo (mod.rs:21097-21108). Style, Denoise, Colorize, Depth Blur and Restore never read the selection. Only harmonizeML uses selectionMaskAt. The comment shows the intent was to avoid clipping to a selection that changed mid-job, but the selection captured at job start is not applied either, although compositeFillOntoNewLayer already implements that pattern.

findings.title: Generate Image, Restyle and Generate Similar documents are not marked AI-generated, so Content Credentials under-disclose
findings.feature: Edit > Generate Image / Generate Similar / Restyle Current Image (img2img); File > Export > Content Credentials
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ml/diffusion.ts:331-342 (generateImage) and 662-674 (generateImageFromReference) open the result with store.openImage(), and store.stampGenMeta() only records settings (store.ts:4422-4425). Neither calls mark_ai_generated. Only compositeFillOntoNewLayer (onnx.ts:424) and generateBackgroundML (onnx.ts:607) do. c2pa_action_list adds the trainedAlgorithmicMedia token only when ai_generated is set (packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:29521-29546). The engine comment at mod.rs:3484-3489 calls under-disclosure 'the failure that matters'.
findings.repro: With SD weights installed, choose Edit > Generate Image > Generate → New Document, then File > Export > Content Credentials.
findings.impact: A fully diffusion-generated image is exported with a manifest that makes no AI disclosure, which is a provenance and compliance problem.
