findings.suggested_fix: Call engine.e.mark_ai_generated() right after store.openImage in generateImage and generateImageFromReference. Add a diffusion.test assertion for it.
findings.verdict_reason: The only mark_ai_generated calls in apps/vision/src are onnx.ts:424 (compositeFillOntoNewLayer) and onnx.ts:607 (generateBackgroundML). generateImage (diffusion.ts:331-342) and generateImageFromReference (diffusion.ts:662-674) call store.openImage plus stampGenMeta (which only stores settings, store.ts:4422-4425) and upscaleToTarget. None of these sets ai_generated. c2pa_action_list appends the AI token only when ai_generated is true (mod.rs:29534-29546), and the native signer emits c2pa.created for a parentless document (c2pa_sign.rs:130). No test asserts this: diffusion.test.ts has no mark_ai_generated check. This only matters once the user has imported SD weights.

findings.title: Face-Aware Liquify assumes a 68-point [x,y] regression model on the whole image, but the pinned OpenSeeFace model probably emits heatmaps for 66 points on 224² face crops
findings.feature: Filter > Neural Filters > Face-Aware Liquify (AI); face gating in Skin Smoothing
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ml/onnx.ts:964-1001 feeds the whole composite at 192², reads the output as normalized [x,y]×68, and counts faces as lm.length/136. The registry and MODELS.md pin OpenSeeFace lm_model3_opt.onnx (modelRegistry.ts face-landmarks; MODELS.md 'Getting models' table). As far as I know, OpenSeeFace's tracker feeds 224×224 face crops from a separate detector and decodes a [198,28,28] heatmap/offset tensor for 66 landmarks. Both unit tests mock a synthetic 68×2 output (faceLiquify.test.ts:30-40; neuralFilters.test.ts:36), and unlike LaMa, DDColor and FBCNN, no contract verification is recorded for this model (commit d8363925 only pinned license, hash and URL).
findings.repro: Import face_landmarks.onnx per MODELS.md, then choose Filter > Neural Filters > Face-Aware Liquify > Detect Faces, or Apply with Eye Size +0.5.
findings.impact: With the only model the docs point to, this likely fails with an ORT input-dimension error (192 vs 224). If the dims are dynamic, it reports about 1141 'faces' and warps at garbage coordinates. Skin Smoothing then falls back and reports 'Face model not installed' although it is installed.
findings.suggested_fix: To confirm, load lm_model3_opt.onnx in onnxruntime and print the input and output shapes. Then implement the real contract (a face detector crop, 224² input, heatmap argmax plus offsets for 66 points, and a 66-point index map) or pin a model that really outputs 68-point coordinates. Add an ORT-web fixture test with the real I/O shapes.
findings.verdict_reason: Checked directly. I downloaded the exact pinned file (OpenSeeFace@85aa70f lm_model3_opt.onnx; its sha256 5aa0ab25…49d1 matches the registry pin) to the scratchpad and loaded it with the repo's onnxruntime-web in node. Input is float32 [batch,3,224,224] and output is [batch,198,28,28]. Running it at 192² as faceLandmarks does (onnx.ts:982) fails: 'Got invalid dimensions for input: input … index: 2 Got: 192 Expected: 224'. With the only documented model, Detect Faces and Face-Aware Liquify always throw a raw ORT error (requireModel wraps only session creation, not run). Skin Smoothing's catch-all (app.ts:2140-2144) then reports 'Face model not installed' although the model is installed. Even at 224² the decode would be wrong: 198×28×28 read as [x,y]×68 would give about 570 'faces'. The unit tests mock a synthetic 68×2 output (faceLiquify.test.ts:30-40).

findings.title: MCP ml.generativeFill and ml.generativeExpand (and the ml.models report) probe only /models/*, so they always fail after a Model Manager import
findings.feature: MCP ml.generativeFill / ml.generativeExpand / ml.models
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/mcp/commands.ts:1394-1417 hard-code `filePresent("/models/migan.onnx")`, and mlModels (commands.ts:1513-1531, with ML_FEATURES at 1336-1344) probes static /models paths only and omits the Tier-2 and LaMa units. In release, migan.onnx is gitignored and stripped (public/models/.gitignore), and the only supported install is Import into appData/models, which the UI resolves through resolveModelUrl/convertFileSrc (modelSource.ts:103-107). No native route maps /models to appData (src-tauri/src/main.rs plugin list).
findings.repro: In a release build, import migan.onnx through Neural Filters > Manage AI Models > Install from Disk. The UI's Generative Fill now works. Then call MCP ml.generativeFill with a selection.
findings.impact: The MCP tool always throws 'MI-GAN is not installed', and ml.models reports installed models as missing, so the MCP surface disagrees with the menu for the same feature.
findings.suggested_fix: Use models.miganInstalled() / modelStatus() from modelSource, and resolve feature readiness through MODEL_REGISTRY in ml.models.
findings.verdict_reason:
commands.ts:1397-1398 and 1414-1415 hard-code filePresent('/models/migan.onnx'). migan.onnx is in the release exclusion list (public/models/.gitignore). The only release install path is appData via Import, which resolveModelUrl maps through convertFileSrc (modelSource.ts:103-107), and nothing maps /models to appData. Both MCP tools can therefore never succeed in a release build, while the UI path (models.miganInstalled / resolveModelUrl) works. mlModels (commands.ts:1513-1531) probes /models/

for everything except SD, which goes through resolveSdBase. Imported drunet and migan are reported missing, and the Tier-2 and LaMa units are absent from ML_FEATURES.

findings.title: Remove Distractions / Remove Reflections / Split Reflections bypass the destructive-edit guard: they write through 'Lock image pixels', smart objects and type layers, and silently no-op on locked layers
findings.feature: Edit > Remove Distractions… / Remove Reflections…
findings.evidence: packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:27988-27992 (remove_distractions), 28069-28072 (remove_reflections) and split_reflections check only `self.active_layer().locked` and return silently. They never call refuse_destructive_edit (mod.rs lock_image / kind 1,2,3,4,6,7 checks), which apply16 uses for every other filter, and they ignore painting_mask. The engine's own rule is 'Refuse LOUDLY via the edit-error bridge: a silent no-op reads as a broken filter'.
findings.repro: Enable Lock Image Pixels on a layer and choose Edit > Remove Distractions… > OK: the pixels change. Or run it on a type layer or smart object: the edit is erased on the next re-render or retype. Or run it on a fully locked layer: nothing happens and no message appears.
findings.impact: Pixel locks are violated, edits to type and smart layers are silently lost later, and a locked layer gives no feedback.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `.locked` early return with `if self.refuse_destructive_edit() { return; }` (and handle painting_mask) in all three functions.
findings.verdict_reason: remove_distractions (mod.rs:27988-27992), remove_reflections (28069-28072) and split_reflections (28154-28157) check only active_layer().locked and return silently, with no last_edit_error. The later guards are reject_legacy_float_edit (32-bit float only) and push_layer_undo (mod.rs:5673), and push_layer_undo checks only reject_imported_photoshop_edit. None checks lock_image or layer kind, unlike refuse_destructive_edit (mod.rs:3890-3912). There is no JS-side guard: app.ts:1683-1695 calls the engine inside rec(), and no menuEnablement entry exists for these items. Lock Image Pixels is violated, type and smart-object bakes are later erased on re-render, and a fully locked layer gets no feedback. Note these are deterministic filters, not ML.

findings.title: Menu-triggered ML jobs (runMl) bypass the single-flight/cancel gate, discard progress, and toast 'Done.' for ok:false results
findings.feature: Select > Subject, Remove Background, Super Resolution, Generative Fill (MI-GAN), Generate Similar, Match Font (Image AI)
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/App.tsx:2129-2137. runMl uses its own mlBusy flag instead of beginMlJob, passes `() => {}` as progress, shows a persistent toast with no Cancel, and treats any resolved promise as success. generateSimilar resolves ok:false with 'No generation settings on this document' (diffusion.ts:349-356), and gensimilar is wired at App.tsx:2749. A menu job running during a dialog preview hits the module-global _preview (onnx.ts:133, 165-167), and the dialog's 'Cancel Job' aborts it too (mlJob.ts:16-35).
findings.repro: Open a normal (non-generated) document and choose Edit > Generate Similar.
findings.impact: A green 'Done.' toast appears although nothing happened. Long Super-Resolution runs cannot be cancelled and show no progress. Menu and dialog jobs can interfere with each other.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap runMl in beginMlJob/cancel, surface the last progress message, and treat `{ok:false}` as an error toast.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:2129-2137 uses a local mlBusy ref, passes () => {} as progress, and its .then shows a success 'Done.' toast for any resolved value. generateSimilar resolves {ok:false} with only a progress message on non-generated documents (diffusion.ts:349-356), and gensimilar is wired at App.tsx:2749. Because runMl never calls beginMlJob, a menu job can run alongside a dialog job and shares the module-global ctrl (mlJob.ts:16-35) and _preview. Super-Resolution runs through runMl with no progress and no cancel.

findings.title: Missing-model messages point release users to source-tree paths and to a menu item that doesn't exist; AI Denoise surfaces a raw ORT error
findings.feature: AI Denoise, Depth Blur, Harmonize, Face-Aware Liquify, Match Font (AI), Generative Fill, first-run notice
findings.evidence: requireModel says 'place its weights at /models/… (see public/models/MODELS.md)' (onnx.ts:707-714). generativeFillML says 'see public/models/MODELS.md' (onnx.ts:431-432). aiDenoise uses bestSession with no wrapper (onnx.ts:638-642), and the AiDenoise dialog has no drunetInstalled pre-check (Dialogs.tsx:11077-11091). The first-run toast (App.tsx:2235) and WEBGPU_GATE_MSG (diffusion.ts:21) direct users to 'Filter ▸ Neural Filters ▸ Manage AI Models', but no such menu item exists; the Model Manager is reachable only from buttons inside dialogs (Dialogs.tsx:11363, 1580).
findings.repro: Release build: choose Filter > Neural Filters > AI Denoise… and click Apply.
findings.impact: The user gets an opaque onnxruntime fetch error, or instructions to edit files inside the app bundle, instead of 'Install from Disk…'.
findings.suggested_fix: Word the missing-model error around the Model Manager, wrap bestSession like requireModel, and add a Filter > Neural Filters > Manage AI Models… menu item (or fix the copy).
findings.verdict_reason: requireModel's message (onnx.ts:707-714) embeds resolveModelUrl's fallback '/models/<rel>' and 'see public/models/MODELS.md'. aiDenoise uses bestSession with no wrapper (onnx.ts:638-642), and the AiDenoise dialog (Dialogs.tsx:11077-11091) just prints String(e). psMenuData.ts, psMenus.ts and App.tsx have no 'Manage AI Models' menu item. The Model Manager opens only from buttons in the Neural Filters dialog (Dialogs.tsx:11363, 11389) and Preferences (1580), yet the first-run toast (App.tsx:2235) and WEBGPU_GATE_MSG (diffusion.ts:21) name a Filter ▸ Neural Filters ▸ Manage AI Models path.

findings.title: ML results create several history steps labelled 'New Layer'/'Deselect'/'Paste'; Skin Smoothing's 'one undo step' claim is false
findings.feature: All stamp-style neural filters, Generative Fill, Skin Smoothing, Remove tool ML tier
findings.evidence: stampResult/compositeFillOntoNewLayer call select_none (a 'Deselect' undo), store.addLayer (a 'New Layer' commit, store.ts:6489-6493), then stamp_image, which pushes a layer undo labelled 'Paste' (packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:18605). applySkinSmoothing issues select_polygon ('Lasso'), select_color_range_batch ('Color Range'), smart_blur, then select_none or set_selection_mask ('Select Subject' label, mod.rs:21712-21717). Each pushes its own entry, but Dialogs.tsx:11518 says 'One commit inside the facade, so the whole pass is one undo step'.
findings.repro: Run AI Denoise and press ⌘Z once. Or run Skin Smoothing and press ⌘Z once.
findings.impact: The first undo leaves an empty 'Layer N' behind, or only changes the selection. History shows 'Paste' instead of the filter name, and a single user action takes 2-6 undos.
findings.suggested_fix: Group each ML apply into one named history step (collapse the entries or use a compound snapshot). Pass a label to stamp_image or add a stamp_new_layer engine call.
findings.verdict_reason: Each call pushes its own undo entry, and EngineClient.commit (EngineClient.ts:823-840) does no grouping. The stamp path records up to three entries: select_none pushes 'Deselect' when a selection exists (mod.rs:21102), store.addLayer → add_layer pushes 'New Layer' and commits (store.ts:6489-6493, mod.rs:9337), and stamp_image pushes 'Paste' (mod.rs:18605). applySkinSmoothing calls select_polygon ('Lasso', mod.rs:21084), select_color_range_batch ('Color Range'), smart_blur, and set_selection_mask ('Select Subject', mod.rs:21716) or select_none. The comment at Dialogs.tsx:11518 claiming one undo step is wrong.

findings.title: Neural filters flatten transparency: formerly transparent areas become opaque black on the result layer
findings.feature: Style, AI Denoise, Colorize, Depth Blur, Harmonize, Restore, Super-Resolution
findings.evidence: tiling.ts:100-107, blendAmount (onnx.ts:669-673), colorizeML (onnx.ts:779), variableBlur (onnx.ts:796, 807) and superResolution (onnx.ts:277) all force alpha = 255. styleBlend.ts leaves alpha as the styled 255 ('the stylized stamp covers the canvas'). The composite of transparent pixels decodes as RGB 0.
findings.repro: Open a PNG logo on a transparent background (or use a Remove Background cutout with the original hidden), then run AI Denoise.
findings.impact: A full-canvas layer with a black background covers the document.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the composite's alpha through to the stamped result (and to the Super-Resolution output).
findings.verdict_reason: tileFilter writes alpha 255 (tiling.ts:100-107), as do blendAmount (onnx.ts:669-673), colorizeML (779), variableBlur (796, 807) and superResolution (277). The styled buffer is built with alpha 255 (onnx.ts:215), and blendStyle leaves alpha untouched. A canvas getImageData read of fully transparent pixels returns RGB 0, so transparent regions become opaque black on a full-canvas layer.

findings.title: On 16-bit and 32-bit documents, ML results are 8-bit (and HDR is clipped) on a full-canvas opaque layer
findings.feature: All stamp-style ML filters on 16/32-bit documents
findings.evidence: composite() decodes export_png through an 8-bit canvas (onnx.ts:76-87). export_png writes 16-bit for 16/32-bit documents, but float HDR values are clamped to a 16-bit PNG (mod.rs:29432-29437, 29416-29418). stamp_image converts u8/255 into the u16 plane (mod.rs:18619-18628). The new layer has no float authority in 32-bit documents.
findings.repro: Open a 16-bit gradient image, run Photo Restoration or Style at Strength 0.3, and inspect for banding. On a 32-bit HDR document, run AI Denoise.
findings.impact: Precision drops to 8 bits across the whole visible image, causing banding. Highlights above 1.0 in 32-bit documents are clipped under an opaque layer.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the 16-bit composite (export_composite_rgba16) and a 16-bit stamp path, or refuse or warn on 32-bit documents.
findings.verdict_reason: composite() decodes the PNG into an 8-bit 2D canvas. export_png writes 16-bit for 16/32-bit documents, so precision is lost on decode. stamp_image scales u8 into the u16 plane. add_layer creates Layer::transparent with no pixels_f32, and layer_has_float_authority (mod.rs:3709) is false, so stamp_image is not refused in 32-bit documents. The new layer carries only clamped u16 values, so HDR above 1.0 is clipped under an opaque layer. I did not measure banding, but the 8-bit bottleneck is certain from the code.

findings.title: Remove tool ML tier has no in-flight lock: overlapping strokes race on the selection and the first stroke is silently dropped
findings.feature: Remove tool (LaMa / MI-GAN tier)
findings.evidence: CanvasView.tsx:2119 `void removeStroke(...)` runs on every pointer-up. removeStroke (app.ts:2003-2031) saves the selection, adds dab ellipses, awaits a multi-second inference, then restores. It is not gated by beginMlJob or any busy flag. A second stroke's select_ellipse moves undo_pushes, so the first job hits docChanged and returns ok:false without falling back. The second stroke then 'restores' the first stroke's dab selection.
findings.repro: Import LaMa or MI-GAN, then make two quick Remove strokes about 1 s apart.
findings.impact: The first stroke vanishes with no heal applied, and a stray selection of dab ellipses is left behind that clips subsequent edits.
findings.suggested_fix: Serialize removeStroke with a promise queue (or beginMlJob), and fall back to spotHeal when the ML result is ok:false.
findings.verdict_reason: CanvasView.tsx:2119 calls `void removeStroke(...)` on every pointer-up with no busy gate. removeStroke (app.ts:2003-2031) saves the selection, adds dab ellipses (each a sel undo push), awaits lamaFillML/generativeFillML, then restores in finally. When a second stroke starts mid-job, its undo pushes change undo_pushes, so job 1's docChanged returns {ok:false}. That is not a throw, so there is no spotHeal fallback. Stroke 2 has saved stroke 1's dab selection and restores it at the end. The problem is likely worse than reported: job 1's finally set_selection_mask also pushes an undo, which likely invalidates stroke 2 as well. Timing-dependent; the mechanism was followed in code.

findings.title: Depth Blur's naive per-pixel box gather runs on the UI thread with no cancel checks
findings.feature: Filter > Neural Filters > Depth Blur (AI)
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ml/onnx.ts:789-811. variableBlur is O(n·r²) with r up to 16 (a window of up to 33²), runs synchronously on the main thread after inference (onnx.ts:846-850), and has no throwIfCancelled inside. The ponytail comment acknowledges the O(n·r²) ceiling. Only inference runs on the ORT proxy worker (ortEnv.ts).
findings.repro: With MiDaS imported, choose Depth Blur with Blur Strength 2 on a 24 MP photo.
findings.impact: The webview freezes for tens of seconds or more: the Cancel Job button and canvas do not respond, and macOS may show a beachball.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a summed-area table (O(n)), or chunk the work with yields and throwIfCancelled per row band.
findings.verdict_reason: variableBlur (onnx.ts:789-811) is a synchronous O(n·r²) gather with r ≤ DEPTH_MAX_RADIUS=16, which means up to 1089 samples per pixel per channel group. It runs on the main thread after inference (onnx.ts:846-850) with no throwIfCancelled inside, so the Cancel Job button cannot be serviced until it finishes. The ponytail comment acknowledges the ceiling. I did not measure the actual stall duration.

findings.title: No ML action is macro-recordable
findings.feature: Actions panel recording of Select Subject, Remove Background, Neural Filters, Generative Fill
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/state/app.ts:2076-2155. The `ml` object's methods are not wrapped in rec() (compare generativeFill at app.ts:1992-1994 and removeDistractions at app.ts:1683-1684). AGENTS.md says only rec()-wrapped actions are recordable.
findings.repro: Start recording an Action, choose Select > Subject, then stop recording.
findings.impact: The step is not recorded. Photoshop records Select Subject, Remove Background and Neural Filters.
findings.suggested_fix: rec()-wrap the deterministic ML entry points (selectSubject, removeBackground, styleTransfer, aiDenoise with params) as async-aware recorded steps.
findings.verdict_reason: The ml facade (app.ts:2076-2155) is not rec()-wrapped or withOpCapture'd. visionOps namespaces are {adj, fil, xform, neural, anim, distort}, and neural holds only the heuristic colorize. It is slightly worse than reported: store.addLayer and setLayerOpacity are recordedCall-wrapped (RECORDED_STORE_OPS, app.ts:906), so recording during Remove Background or a Neural Filter records a stray 'addLayer' step. The ML step itself is not recorded, so playback adds an empty layer.

findings.title: ORT sessions are never released; clearing the cache on import/delete leaks them and diffusion caches aren't reset
findings.feature: ML runtime memory (onnx.ts / diffusion.ts session caches)
findings.evidence: onnx.ts:34-49 and diffusion.ts:34-47 cache InferenceSession promises for the whole app session and never call release(). clearSessionCache (onnx.ts:35) just clears the Map, and modelDownload.resetModelCaches (modelDownload.ts:38-44) calls only that one, never diffusion's _sessions or _tokenizers. All sessions share one wasm32 heap in the ORT proxy worker (ortEnv.ts).
findings.repro: With the Tier-2 models imported, run Colorize (224 MB), Restore (288 MB), Denoise (130 MB), Harmonize and Depth Blur in one session, then Generate Image.
findings.impact: Memory grows with every model used and never drops. The wasm heap can hit an OOM that breaks all later ML until restart. After a delete or re-import, stale sessions stay resident.
findings.suggested_fix: Release sessions (await s.release()) on cache clear, keep an LRU of one or two large models, and reset diffusion caches in resetModelCaches.
findings.verdict_reason: clearSessionCache (onnx.ts:35) only clears the Map, and nothing in src/ml calls session.release(). resetModelCaches (modelDownload.ts:38-44) resets modelSource and the onnx session cache but not diffusion.ts's _sessions or its tokenizer cache. The code facts are confirmed. The OOM impact depends on ORT-web freeing memory on GC and was not measured, so it stays minor.

findings.title: Match Font (Image AI) classifies the entire composite instead of the selected text region, and results are only a toast
findings.feature: Type > Match Font (Image AI)…
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/ml/onnx.ts:935-954 matchFontML squashes the whole composite to 224² and has no selection crop. App.tsx:3212-3216 shows only 'Closest: …' in a toast, although the label has an ellipsis.
findings.repro: With the font classifier imported, marquee a line of text in a photo and choose Type > Match Font (Image AI)….
findings.impact: The ranking reflects the whole photo, so results are meaningless unless the document is only text. Photoshop requires a text selection and lets you apply the match.
findings.suggested_fix: Crop to selection_bounds (require a selection) before resizing. Show the candidates in a dialog that can apply one to a type layer.
findings.verdict_reason: matchFontML (onnx.ts:935-954) resizes the whole composite to 224² with no selection crop. App.tsx:3212-3216 shows only a 'Closest: …' toast, although the menu label 'Match Font (Image AI)…' (psMenuData.ts:2616) implies a dialog. There is no way to apply the match.

findings.title: MCP surface lacks the Tier-2 neural filters, Generate Similar, Restyle (img2img) and Match Font (AI)
findings.feature: MCP ml.* tool set vs Neural Filters menu
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/mcp/commands.ts:1353-1531 lists 14 ml.* tools. There are none for ml.colorize, depthBlur, harmonize, restore, faceAwareLiquify, detectFaces, matchFontImage, generateSimilar or generateImageReference, although all are wired in app.ts:2076-2155 and the menu. AGENTS.md says new features get MCP support.
findings.repro: Ask an MCP client to colorize or depth-blur the document.
findings.impact: Agents cannot drive half the Neural Filters menu, which is a menu/MCP inconsistency.
findings.suggested_fix: Add @mcp wrappers (job-style for the tiled ones) and run mcp:codegen.
findings.verdict_reason: The only @mcp ml.* tools are selectSubject, removeBackground, styleTransfer, superResolution, generativeFill, generativeExpand, skinSmoothing, aiDenoise, generativeFillPrompt, generateImage, generateBackground, jobStatus, jobCancel and models (commands.ts:1353-1531). script.run exposes visionOps, which includes only neural.colorize (the heuristic), so there is no MCP path to ML colorize, depthBlur, harmonize, restore, faceAwareLiquify, detectFaces, matchFontImage, generateSimilar or generateImageReference.

findings.title: lama_fp32.onnx is missing from public/models/.gitignore (the release exclusion list)
findings.feature: Model packaging / check:models
findings.evidence: apps/vision/public/models/.gitignore lists migan, drunet, sd, sd15 and the six Tier-2 files but not lama_fp32.onnx. modelStatus probes /models/<rel> for local installs (modelSource.ts:153-156), so developers are invited to drop it there. check-model-licenses.mjs then fails the release build ('absent from checksums.txt'), and git shows a 208 MB untracked file that could be committed.
findings.repro: Place lama_fp32.onnx in public/models for local testing, then run pnpm build:release or git status.
findings.impact: The release build is blocked by a local-only optional model, and there is a risk of committing a 208 MB weight file.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `lama_fp32.onnx` to public/models/.gitignore next to migan.onnx.
findings.verdict_reason: public/models/.gitignore lists drunet_color, sd15/, sd/, migan and the six Tier-2 files but not lama_fp32.onnx. `git check-ignore` confirms it is not ignored. check-model-licenses.mjs treats non-excluded .onnx files as release files and would fail with 'absent from checksums.txt' and a missing license entry. modelStatus and resolveModelUrl fall back to /models/lama_fp32.onnx, so a local drop is a supported dev path. The impact is limited to developers who place it locally.

findings.title: Generative Fill (Synthesis) is enabled with no selection and silently does nothing
findings.feature: Edit > Generative Fill (Synthesis)
findings.evidence: App.tsx:2746 `genfill: () => generativeFill()` has no selection gate in menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3468). The engine returns early and silently when there is no selection, the layer is locked, or it is a fill layer (packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:19982-19985).
findings.repro: With no selection, choose Edit > Generative Fill (Synthesis).
findings.impact: Nothing happens and no message appears.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `genfill: hasDocument && selectionActive` (and genfillml) to menuEnablement, and set last_edit_error on the locked/fill-layer early returns.
findings.verdict_reason: menuEnablement (App.tsx:3434-3468) has no genfill entry, so the item is enabled whenever a document exists. generative_fill (mod.rs:19982-19985) returns silently when there is no selection, the layer is locked, or it is a fill layer, and sets no last_edit_error. By contrast, genfillml throws 'Make a selection to fill first.', which runMl shows as an error toast.

findings.title: Key ML behaviors have no meaningful automated test
findings.feature: Remove Background, Neural Filters dialog outcomes, fallbacks, Super-Resolution limits, color management, AI disclosure
findings.evidence: The Remove Background e2e test asserts only the layer count (e2e/ml.spec.ts:54-62). No test covers the NeuralAI run() status for ok:false (Dialogs.tsx:11337-11346), Cancel during Colorize/Restore, the SR output-size limit, P3-tagged composite decoding in onnx.ts, or mark_ai_generated for generateImage (diffusion.test.ts has none). The face-landmark tests use synthetic 68×2 outputs (faceLiquify.test.ts:30-40).
findings.repro: n/a
findings.impact: The major regressions above can ship silently.
findings.suggested_fix: Add targeted unit tests (mocked ORT) for each of these behaviors, plus a composite-pixel assertion in the Remove Background e2e.
findings.verdict_reason: e2e/ml.spec.ts:54-62 asserts only ret.ok and the layer count. Unit tests mock export_png with 3-byte stubs, so there is no colour-management coverage. diffusion.test.ts has no mark_ai_generated assertion (only onnx.test.ts and onnxPipeline.test.ts check it, for fill and background). faceLiquify.test.ts mocks a synthetic 68×2 output, which hid the real [1,198,28,28] contract I measured. I found no test for run() handling ok:false or for Cancel during Colorize/Restore.

findings.title: Stale or overstated copy in ML docs and UI
findings.feature: diffusion.ts header, Vision AGENTS.md, Generate Image output size, Preferences AI Models count
findings.evidence: diffusion.ts:7-10 says it 'Ships wired to a tiny placeholder model so the feature runs out of the box', but the placeholder is release-excluded. onnx.ts:589-591 makes the same claim. apps/vision/AGENTS.md says optional weights 'must be installed manually under public/models', but in release they go through Model Manager Import. The Generate Image 'Output' options '1024 px (SR ×2)' and '2048 px (2K · SR ×4)' (Dialogs.tsx:11455-11458) are an engine 2× bilinear upscale plus unsharp mask (mod.rs:29169). The Preferences AI Models count (Dialogs.tsx:1567-1576) ignores imported Tier-2 and LaMa units.
findings.repro: n/a
findings.impact: The docs and labels mislead contributors and users.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the comments and AGENTS.md. Relabel the output sizes as 'upscaled'. Compute the preferences count from models.status over MODEL_REGISTRY.
findings.verdict_reason: The diffusion.ts:7-10 header claims it 'Ships wired to a tiny placeholder model', but sd/ is release-excluded; onnx.ts:589-591 makes the same claim. apps/vision/AGENTS.md:113-114 says Tier-2 weights 'must be installed manually under public/models', while release installs go through Model Manager Import. upscaleToTarget uses engine super_resolution, which is a '2× bilinear upscale of the document + crisp unsharp' (mod.rs comment), yet the options are labelled 'SR ×2' and 'SR ×4'. AiModelsPrefs (Dialogs.tsx:1567-1569) counts only bundled units plus drunet, migan and sd, so it ignores imported LaMa and Tier-2 units.

areas.coverage:
Area: Camera Raw and develop. I worked by reading code only. The one command I ran was a 6-line node script in the scratchpad, to confirm the microtask ordering behind finding 5. I ran no builds or test suites.

What I inventoried:
- Menu entries (4 monetIds): Filter ▸ Camera Raw Filter (cameraraw, ⇧⌘A); Filter ▸ Lens Correction and File ▸ Automate ▸ Lens Correction, which share the one id lenscorrection; Preferences ▸ Camera Raw (prefcameraraw).
- File paths that route a RAW: Open (native openPaths and browser openImageFiles), Open as Smart Object, drag-drop, Revert, Export DNG, Batch, droplet and CLI inputs.
- MCP commands (7): adj.cameraRawRecipe, cameraRaw.sessions, cameraRaw.selectSession, cameraRaw.setImportOptions, cameraRaw.profiles, cameraRaw.loadProfile, and the RAW route of doc.open.
- Workspace: 17 sections and about 45 controls, all traced in CameraRawWorkspace.tsx (2013 lines). Sections: Presets (apply, save, import/export .xmp), Snapshots, Profile & Calibration (DCP menu, Load Profile, Amount, shadow tint, 3 primaries), Basic (9 white-balance modes, WB tool, Auto WB, Auto Tone, 13 sliders), Tone Curve (4 channels plus parametric), Detail (10), Effects (5), Optics (lens profile controls, 5 sliders, 2 defringe ranges), HSL (3×8), Color Grading (3 wheels), Point Color, Crop & Straighten (tool, aspect presets, flip, Generative Expand), Healing (place, stroke, detect, visualize), Masking (8 kinds, gradient handles, 16 local sliders), Enhance (Denoise, Raw Details, Super Resolution), Geometry (Upright including Guided, 7 sliders). Also the preview tools (zoom, before/after, split view, clipping overlays, histogram), Demosaic and Depth, the filmstrip with Sync Settings, and the footer buttons (Save Settings, Done, Cancel, Open, Open Object, OK).

Traced end to end:
- store.ts session handling: openRaw, presentNext, complete/cancel/done, activate/select, demosaic, the profile library, prepareProfile, requestCameraRawEdit, cameraRawDevelopTarget, revertActiveCameraRawSource, duplicate and revert provenance.
- app.ts: sidecar read/write/import, preset import/export, profile storage, findAdobeCameraProfiles, openPaths, openImageFiles, openAutomationInput, openAsSmartObject, runBatchInputs, runDroplet, runCliJob, exportDNG, save/Save As/Revert policy.
- Also: cameraRawSidecar.ts, cameraRawPresets.ts, cameraRawProfiles.ts, visionDevelopRecipe.ts, monet-photo xmp.ts (the WB, crop and local-adjustment rules), and the engine's camera_raw_develop, camera_raw_commit, apply16, proxy_engine and develop.rs (crop map, heal and mask order, local tint).

Tests checked by grep: 49 e2e tests in camera-raw-workspace.spec.ts, 4 in lens-profiles.spec.ts, the RAW case in batch-dialog.spec.ts, about 20 unit files (cameraRaw*.test.ts, dialogs/cameraRaw*.test.ts, preferencePanes, visionDevelopRecipe, lensProfiles, dng, and the MCP command/handler tests).

Not reviewed in depth:
- Numeric correctness of each develop stage in develop.rs, DCP parsing (dcp.rs), and the RAW decoders.
- How a develop behaves on Grayscale, CMYK, Lab, Indexed or Multichannel documents. That goes through the shared apply16 path, which I did not verify per mode.
- The full monet-photo XMP mapping table.
- The native Rust side.

Items marked medium or low confidence are ones where a single runtime check would settle it (the check is named in each finding).
areas.parity_notes:
No Photoshop menu items in this area are disabled placeholders. Every Camera Raw related blueprint entry has a monetId (Camera Raw Filter, both Lens Correction entries, Preferences ▸ Camera Raw).

Adobe Camera Raw features that are missing or reduced compared with ACR (by design, not bugs):
- No undo/history inside the workspace. Cmd+Z reaches the document underneath, because the global keydown handler does not stop at modal dialogs.
- Color Grading has only hue and saturation per region. It lacks the Global wheel and the Luminance, Blending and Balance controls.
- Vignette Roundness, Feather, Style and Highlights, and ConvertToGrayscale, are skipped on XMP import with a reason.
- No targeted-adjustment tool for Tone Curve or HSL.
- The Sky mask is a heuristic, not a model.
- No People or Object masks, and no mask add/subtract/intersect combine in Vision's engine masks.
- No AI Remove or Generative Remove. Healing is heal or clone spots only.
- No Adaptive profiles or ACR process versions.
- Presets are whole-recipe snapshots, not partial presets with amounts.
- Preview zoom tops out at the proxy resolution (no true 1:1).
- Guided Upright guides are session-only.
- Cancel with several staged images cancels only the current one.
- The Adobe CameraProfiles folder scan is macOS-only.
- Lens Correction (Filter) has no live preview.

MCP compared with the UI: no MCP equivalent for Open, Open Object, Cancel or Done of a session, the sidecar and preset I/O, or snapshots. adj.cameraRawRecipe is the scriptable counterpart of Camera Raw Filter OK.

findings.title: Done / Save Settings / Export XMP… overwrite a Lightroom/ACR sidecar .xmp beside the RAW
findings.feature: Camera Raw workspace ▸ Done, Save Settings, Presets ▸ Export XMP… (sidecar)
findings.evidence: saveCameraRawSidecar (app.ts:3686-3703) builds the target as <raw>.xmp from source.originalPath and calls atomicWriteBytes(target, packet) with no existence or ownership check. The open-time writer saveCameraRawSidecarOnOpen (app.ts:3655-3665) refuses when !isOwnCameraRawXmp(existing), because a Lightroom, ACR or Galerie sidecar would lose fields (see cameraRawSidecar.ts:172-185). The workspace routes Done (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1389-1396), the footer Save Settings (1465) and Export XMP… (1588) through saveSettings → saveCameraRawSidecar. The Preferences pane text (Dialogs.tsx:2037-2040) promises it never writes 'over one another app wrote'.
findings.repro: Desktop app. Have IMG_1.CR2 with an IMG_1.xmp written by Lightroom/ACR (with keywords, rating, local adjustments). File ▸ Open IMG_1.CR2 (Camera Raw shows with the LR look) → click Done (or Save Settings / Export XMP…).
findings.impact: The Lightroom/ACR sidecar is silently replaced by Vision's packet. Every field Vision does not map is lost: keywords, ratings, labels, LR masks and profiles, absolute white balance. For ACR/Bridge users that file is the only copy of their edits.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply the same guard as saveCameraRawSidecarOnOpen inside saveCameraRawSidecar. When the existing file is not isOwnCameraRawXmp, either refuse with a message or ask for a different path through the save dialog. Add a unit test for Done over a foreign sidecar.
findings.verdict_reason: saveCameraRawSidecar (app.ts:3686-3703) builds the target as <originalPath>.xmp and calls atomicWriteBytes with no exists or isOwnCameraRawXmp check. The only guard is in saveCameraRawSidecarOnOpen (app.ts:3655-3665). The workspace sends Done (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1389-1396), the Save Settings footer button (1465) and Export XMP… (1588) through saveSettings → saveCameraRawSidecar (1357-1362). For native opens, sourceRef comes from the session source, which carries originalPath (app.ts:7967, store.ts:5274). Unit tests cover only the on-open writer (cameraRawSidecarOnOpen.test.ts). The result is a silent, wholesale replacement of third-party user data by the default Done button, which the code itself guards against on the open path. I kept blocker; major is defensible because the write is user-initiated.

findings.title: Crop & Straighten stretches the crop into the original frame, distorting any crop whose aspect differs from the image
findings.feature: Camera Raw ▸ Crop & Straighten (Crop Aspect presets 1:1, 4:5, 16:9…, crop tool); XMP crs:Crop* import
findings.evidence: develop_crop_to_fill (develop.rs:839-857) resamples in place into the same w×h buffer. DevelopCropMap::output_to_source (782-797) maps output x across crop_px_w and output y across crop_px_h independently, so the scale is non-uniform whenever crop_px_w/crop_px_h ≠ w/h. The engine test advanced_crop_angle_and_flip_resample_without_changing_dimensions (mod.rs:71490) pins 'without changing dimensions' using a 0.6×0.8 crop on a 24×24 document. Nothing in completeCameraRawOpen (store.ts:5759+) resizes the canvas to the crop. The workspace offers 1:1, 4:5, 16:9 and similar presets (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:156-164). The preview also draws the crop rectangle in source coordinates over the already-cropped output (renderCopy 664-686; applyFrame 744 develops with the crop applied), so the rectangle no longer matches what is shown. LR sidecar crops (xmp.ts:872-876) go through the same path.
findings.repro: Open a 3:2 RAW → Crop & Straighten → Crop Aspect 1:1 (or drag a free crop) → Open.
findings.impact: The document keeps its 3:2 pixel size, and the square crop is stretched 1.5× horizontally and upsampled. Any LR-cropped RAW opens distorted. While the crop tool is active the user sees the stretched result under a rectangle that does not line up with it.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the develop crop change the output dimensions (crop the canvas or the Smart Object content to crop_px_w×crop_px_h after developing). Show the uncropped image while the crop tool is active, as the upright-guides preview already does with unwarped(). Add an e2e test that checks the dimensions and aspect after a 1:1 crop.
findings.verdict_reason: DevelopCropMap::output_to_source (develop.rs:779-795) scales output x by crop_px_w and output y by crop_px_h independently. develop_crop_to_fill (839-857) writes back into the same w×h buffer, so any crop where crop_px_w/crop_px_h ≠ w/h is resampled non-uniformly. completeCameraRawOpen (store.ts:5759-5810) never resizes the canvas, and camera_raw_develop and camera_raw_commit (mod.rs:23403-23470) keep the dimensions. The engine test at mod.rs:71490 asserts that 24×24 stays 24×24 for a 0.6×0.8 crop. The preview strokes crop.rect in source-normalized coordinates over the already-cropped output (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:664-686), so the rectangle does not match what is shown.

findings.title: Applying a preset (built-in or imported .xmp) wipes the image's crop, heal spots, masks, point colours and every other slider
findings.feature: Camera Raw ▸ Presets ▸ Apply a preset / Import Preset…
findings.evidence: The Apply select calls applyRecipe(applyWorkingPreset(normalizeWorkingRecipe(p.recipe), recipe)) (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1571-1573, and 1058 for imports). applyWorkingPreset (visionDevelopRecipe.ts:144-152) copies the whole preset recipe and keeps only the target's lens capture overrides. Built-in presets are full default recipes plus a few changes (cameraRawPresets.ts:30-36), and an imported LR preset is parsed onto defaults. syncWorkingRecipe (133-141) deliberately keeps crop, heal, masks and enhance, which shows these are image-local, but preset apply does not. The workspace has no undo.
findings.repro: In Camera Raw, set Exposure +1, add heal spots, a radial mask and a crop → Presets ▸ Apply ‘Punchy’ (or Import Preset… with an LR preset that only sets B&W).
findings.impact: All local work and every setting the preset does not mention is reset to defaults: exposure, WB, profile, crop, spots, masks. Cmd+Z inside the workspace cannot recover it.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply presets as partial overrides. Store and apply only the panels a preset sets, and never replace crop, heal, engineMasks, pointColor or enhance unless the preset explicitly carries them (at least reuse the syncWorkingRecipe carve-out). Add a unit test for applyWorkingPreset that preserves image-local fields.
findings.verdict_reason: applyWorkingPreset (visionDevelopRecipe.ts:144-152) returns the whole source recipe and keeps only the target's lens capture overrides. Built-in presets are full default recipes plus a few changes (cameraRawPresets.ts:23-36). Apply (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1572) and Import (1058) pass the result to applyRecipe, which calls setCrop, setHealSpots, setMasks and setPointColors from it (994-1016). syncWorkingRecipe (133-141) keeps the image-local fields; preset apply does not. The workspace has no recipe undo: its only keydown handler is Y for Before (957-970).

findings.title: Masking ▸ Subject segments the active document's composite, not the RAW being edited
findings.feature: Camera Raw ▸ Masking ▸ Subject
findings.evidence: addSubjectMask (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1336-1346) calls subjectOutline() with no image argument. subjectOutline → segMask → composite() (onnx.ts:76-87, 290-300) reads engine.e.export_png(), which is the active document tab. In a RAW session the image lives in a separate session engine that is not yet a document. u2netp.onnx is one of the shipped models (public/models/MODELS.md:35).
findings.repro: Open any document (or leave the launch Untitled) → File ▸ Open a RAW → Masking ▸ Subject.
findings.impact: The mask outline is computed from a different image, whichever tab was active, and saved into the recipe, so local adjustments land in unrelated regions. In filter or re-edit mode it segments the full composite, not the target layer or the RAW source.
findings.suggested_fix: Give subjectOutline the pixels to segment. Pass the workspace's pristine proxy copy (pristineRef.current plus proxy width/height) instead of reading engine.e.
findings.verdict_reason: addSubjectMask calls subjectOutline() with no image (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1336-1346). subjectOutline → segMask → composite() reads engine.e.export_png() (onnx.ts:76-87, 290-300). engine.e is the active document engine (EngineClient.ts:186). openRaw builds the session engine with engine.buildRaw (store.ts:5268, EngineClient.ts:378), which does not activate it; activation happens only in addDoc or a tab switch. With another tab open, the outline comes from that tab's composite and is persisted as an 'outline' mask. With no document, engine.e throws and the code silently falls back to the heuristic.

findings.title: Batch/droplet/CLI silently skip every RAW when Preferences ▸ Camera Raw ▸ ‘Show Camera Raw’ is off
findings.feature: File ▸ Automate ▸ Batch, droplets, --batch CLI with RAW inputs
findings.evidence: With the preference off, presentNextCameraRawSession queues a microtask that completes and retires the session (store.ts:5319-5336). openAutomationInput does `const sessionId = await openCameraRaw(...)` (app.ts:7017). That await continuation is queued after the microtask, so the session is already retired when it runs. The suppressed branch then finds no recipe (7027), and waitForCameraRawSession returns Promise.resolve(null) for an unknown id (store.ts:5711-5713), so the function returns false. runBatchInputs treats false as not opened (`if (!opened) continue;`, app.ts:6345). I confirmed the ordering with a 6-line node script.
findings.repro: Preferences ▸ Camera Raw: untick ‘Show Camera Raw when opening raw files’. Run File ▸ Automate ▸ Batch (any action, Destination Folder) over a folder of .NEF/.DNG, with or without Suppress File Open Options Dialogs.
findings.impact: Each RAW opens as a tab, but the action never plays, nothing is exported, the tab is left open, and no error is logged. The report reads ‘Processed 0 of N’; CLI and droplets exit with code 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the completion promise synchronously, before any await, when openCameraRaw returns a session id (for example, call waitForCameraRawSession immediately), or keep the final disposition of retired sessions. Add a batch unit or e2e test with openInCameraRaw=false.
findings.verdict_reason: I traced the ordering myself. store.openRaw → presentNextCameraRawSession queues a microtask (store.ts:5324-5336) that runs completeCameraRawOpen, which resolves and retires the session (5820-5823). openAutomationInput then does `await openCameraRaw(...)` (app.ts:7017). The call returns a plain string synchronously, and the await continuation is queued after that microtask. The suppress branch then finds no session recipe (7027), and waitForCameraRawSession returns Promise.resolve(null) for an unknown id (store.ts:5711-5713), so the function returns false. runBatchInputs then skips the file with `if (!opened) continue` (app.ts:6345), leaving the adopted tab open. The existing batch unit test mocks openRaw and completeCameraRawOpen (cameraRawSidecarOnOpen.test.ts:114-126), so it never exercises this ordering. No test sets openInCameraRaw=false for batch.

findings.title: Known issue root cause: a suppressed Batch still mounts Camera Raw because React drains pendingDialog before openAutomationInput clears it
findings.feature: Batch ▸ Suppress File Open Options Dialogs (batch-dialog.spec.ts:244)
findings.evidence: store.openRaw → presentNextCameraRawSession → requestDialog('cameraRaw') runs synchronously (store.ts:5318-5319), and store.set schedules React 18's useSyncExternalStore SyncLane flush as a microtask (createRoot, main.tsx:1,24). openAutomationInput then does `await openCameraRaw(...)` (app.ts:7017), so its continuation is queued after React's flush. React renders App, flushes the pendingDialog effect synchronously (App.tsx:2036-2041), calls open('cameraRaw') and clears the request. The code at app.ts:7024-7031 then finds pending=null and still completes the session. The dialog open lands in a later render: the workspace replaces Batch in the single slot, renders data-mv-cr-open, then closes itself because its session is gone (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:819-825). The MutationObserver in the spec sees it.
findings.repro: Run e2e batch-dialog.spec.ts:244, or run Batch with Suppress File Open Options Dialogs over a DNG.
findings.impact: The Camera Raw dialog flashes for every RAW and takes over the Batch dialog slot. The advertised ‘suppress’ is not honoured, and the release e2e fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not yield between openRaw and the suppress handling: `const r = openCameraRaw(...); const sessionId = typeof r === 'string' ? r : await r;`. Alternatively, add an OpenCameraRawOptions flag (for example present:false) so presentNextCameraRawSession never calls requestDialog for a suppressed automation open. The second option also covers finding 5 when combined with a synchronous completion capture.
findings.verdict_reason: The pieces all line up in code. requestDialog runs synchronously inside openRaw (store.ts:5318-5319). useStore is useSyncExternalStore (store.ts:10097), store.set notifies listeners synchronously (2330-2334), and React 18 createRoot (main.tsx) flushes SyncLane work, including passive effects, in a microtask. That microtask is queued before the `await openCameraRaw(...)` continuation (app.ts:7017). The App effect (App.tsx:2036-2041) calls open('cameraRaw') and clearPendingDialog, so pending is null by the time app.ts:7024-7031 runs. The session is still completed, but the DialogProvider's single slot (Dialogs.tsx:238-247) has already been handed to the workspace, and the footer renders data-mv-cr-open. One correction to the finding's aftermath: by this ordering the workspace probably mounts while the session is still alive, so its mount-time close (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:824) does not fire. After completion, Cancel calls cancelCameraRawSession, which returns false (store.ts:5728-5730). finishTerminal then shows 'Could not finish' and never closes (1423-1426), so the modal may get stuck rather than flash. I did not run the e2e to confirm.

findings.title: Open at Depth 32 with Profile Corrections silently discards the whole Camera Raw session (the engine's error is swallowed)
findings.feature: Camera Raw ▸ Depth 32 bits + Optics ▸ Enable Profile Corrections ▸ Open
findings.evidence: camera_raw_commit refuses a float document when the RAW has highlight headroom and the recipe has lens correction. It sets 'Could not open this RAW at 32 bits without losing highlight detail. Disable Profile Corrections or choose 16 Bits/Channel.' (mod.rs:23425-23436), and the comment there says 'so a retry can keep the recorded detail'. completeCameraRawOpen throws on that (store.ts:5788-5790). Its catch cancels and retires the session and frees the engine (5812-5818). finishTerminal's catch sees no session and just calls freeProxy(); close() (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1427-1433), without showing the message.
findings.repro: Open a RAW that has clipped highlights (for example a sky) → set Depth to 32 → Optics ▸ Enable Profile Corrections (or open one whose LR sidecar has LensProfileEnable=1 with Depth 32) → Open.
findings.impact: The workspace disappears with no document and no message, and all develop edits are lost. The user is never told to switch to 16-bit or disable corrections.
findings.suggested_fix: Check this condition before mutating anything, via a pure check or can_* probe, and keep the workspace open with the engine's message. At minimum, surface the thrown message through engine.onEditError in finishTerminal's catch.
findings.verdict_reason: camera_raw_commit refuses a float document when headroom exists and has_lens_correction is set, and sets last_edit_error (mod.rs:23425-23436). completeCameraRawOpen throws that message (store.ts:5788-5790). Its catch marks the session cancelled, retires it and frees the engine, because no document owns it (5812-5818). finishTerminal's catch sees no session, then calls freeProxy() and close() without surfacing the error (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1427-1433). The workspace has no pre-check that combines depth with Profile Corrections (1532-1535). No test drives camera_raw_commit returning false. The trigger combination is narrow, but the loss is total and silent.

findings.title: Filter ▸ Camera Raw Filter and the smart-filter row re-edit ignore the chosen layer
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Camera Raw Filter (⇧⌘A); Layers panel ▸ double-click a Camera Raw smart-filter row
findings.evidence: In requestCameraRawEdit (store.ts:5881-5895), `layerId = canReopen ? d.cameraRawLayerId : activeLayerId`. Any document that holds a RAW Smart Object always reopens that layer, whatever layer is active. SmartFilterRows receives layerId but its Camera Raw row calls store.requestCameraRawEdit() without it (Panels.tsx:1175). Every layer row renders its filter rows (Panels.tsx:1002-1006), so double-clicking the Camera Raw row of a non-active Smart Object targets the active layer instead.
findings.repro: (a) Open a RAW with Open Object, add a pixel layer (or Stamp Visible), select it → Filter ▸ Camera Raw Filter: the RAW Smart Object recipe opens instead. (b) Two Smart Objects A and B, where B has a Camera Raw smart filter. Select A (or a pixel layer) → double-click B's ‘Camera Raw Filter’ row: the workspace targets A with default settings, and OK applies there.
findings.impact: The Camera Raw Filter cannot be applied to any other layer in a RAW-object document. Re-editing a filter row can destructively develop, or stack a new fid-17 on, the wrong layer.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit target to requestCameraRawEdit(layerId?). The menu passes the active layer (reopen only when that is the RAW Smart Object). The smart-filter row passes its own layerId and index.
findings.verdict_reason: requestCameraRawEdit takes no target. For any document where d.cameraRaw and cameraRawLayerId exist, it picks `canReopen ? d.cameraRawLayerId : activeLayerId` (store.ts:5881-5895), so the menu cannot target another layer. The SmartFilterRows reedit for CAMERA_RAW_FID calls store.requestCameraRawEdit() and ignores its own layerId prop (Panels.tsx:1160-1176). Neither the row's double-click nor the ⇅ button selects the layer first (1187-1212). A non-active Smart Object's Camera Raw row therefore opens the workspace on the active layer.

findings.title: Native File ▸ Open / drag-drop of several RAWs opens them one at a time; the filmstrip and Sync Settings never appear
findings.feature: Camera Raw filmstrip / Sync Settings (desktop app)
findings.evidence: openPaths, used by the native Open dialog and OS drops through openFileNative and openDroppedPaths, awaits store.waitForCameraRawSession(sessionId) for each RAW before reading the next path (app.ts:7956-7978). Only the browser path openImageFiles stages every RAW first 'so multiple appear in the filmstrip at once' (7463-7483). The workspace shows the filmstrip only when filmstrip.length > 1 (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1543). The e2e filmstrip coverage (camera-raw-workspace.spec.ts:702-727) runs only the browser path.
findings.repro: In the Tauri app, File ▸ Open, multi-select 3 RAW files.
findings.impact: Each image opens in its own workspace after the previous one finishes. The advertised multi-image filmstrip, thumbnails and Sync Settings cannot be reached from the shipping desktop app.
findings.suggested_fix: In openPaths, stage every RAW first (like openImageFiles) and then await all sessions, or wait only for interactive=false callers.
findings.verdict_reason: openFiles uses openFileNative → openPaths under Tauri (app.ts:7709-7710, 7940-7946), and OS drops go through openDroppedPaths → openPaths (6562-6566). openPaths awaits store.waitForCameraRawSession for each RAW before reading the next path (7959-7971). Only the browser openImageFiles stages every RAW first (7463-7483). The filmstrip renders only when filmstrip.length > 1 (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1543).

findings.title: MCP doc.open of a RAW blocks until a human finishes the workspace, and MCP has no command to finish it
findings.feature: MCP doc.open (RAW), cameraRaw.* tools
findings.evidence: doc.open → openPath → openPaths([path], false) (commands.ts:213-218; app.ts:7988-7992). For a RAW it stages a session, which presents the modal workspace when openInCameraRaw is on (the default), and then awaits waitForCameraRawSession (7966-7971). The interactive flag only affects the .raw layout picker. The cameraRaw.* commands (sessions, selectSession, setImportOptions, profiles, loadProfile) provide no Open, Open Object or Cancel, and no way to set a session recipe. The MCP bridge times out after 60 s with ‘MCP bridge timeout — is the app window open?’ (monet-mcp lib.rs:56,311).
findings.repro: MCP: doc.open {path: '/…/shot.NEF'} with default preferences.
findings.impact: An agent cannot open RAW files. The call hangs, then fails with a misleading timeout, while a modal workspace waits in the app. A document may appear later if a person clicks Open.
findings.suggested_fix: For non-interactive opens, develop with the sidecar or default recipe (the openInCameraRaw=false path), or add cameraRaw.open / cameraRaw.cancel / cameraRaw.setRecipe tools and return the session id at once.
findings.verdict_reason: doc.open → openPath → openPaths([path], false) (commands.ts:213-218; app.ts:7988-7992). For a RAW, openPaths stages a session and awaits waitForCameraRawSession (7966-7971). The interactive flag only reaches askLayout; with openInCameraRaw on, presentNextCameraRawSession calls requestDialog (store.ts:5318-5319). The cameraRaw.* MCP tools (commands.ts:1052-1115) cover sessions, selectSession, setImportOptions, profiles and loadProfile, with no complete or cancel. BRIDGE_TIMEOUT is 60 s with the 'is the app window open?' message (monet-mcp lib.rs:56, 311).

findings.title: Auto White Balance, Auto Tone and the WB eyedropper give wrong values when re-editing a Camera Raw Smart Object or smart filter
findings.feature: Camera Raw ▸ Basic ▸ Auto White Balance / Auto Tone / White Balance Tool (reopen)
findings.evidence: On a re-edit, pristineRef is set to the last committed develop (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:860-867: ‘Before means the last committed Camera Raw result’). autoWB measures pristineRef (1076), the eyedropper samples pristineRef (1250), and autoTone reads pristineRef (1090). All three write absolute values: autoWhiteBalance returns absolute temp/tint (cameraRaw.ts:1160-1170), and autoDevelopBasic returns absolute exposure and tone (autoDevelopBasic.ts). The measurement already includes the current WB and exposure, so the result cancels the existing correction. Upright already avoids this by re-rendering unwarped (1105-1120).
findings.repro: Open a RAW with a strong cast using Open Object, click Auto White Balance (or set Exposure +1 and Auto Tone), OK. Then Filter ▸ Camera Raw Filter again and click Auto White Balance / Auto Tone, or click the same neutral with the WB tool.
findings.impact: Temperature and Tint return to about 0 (and exposure to about 0), so the cast or the dark exposure comes back. ‘Auto’ is not idempotent, and the eyedropper un-neutralises a neutral.
findings.suggested_fix: For the measurement, render the stack with basic.temp/tint and the tone sliders at neutral (the same way unwarped() does for Upright), or measure the smart source. Add an e2e test for re-edit followed by Auto WB.
findings.verdict_reason: On a re-edit, pristineRef is the stack developed with the seeded (committed) recipe (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:856-867). autoWB measures pristineRef (1075-1077). autoWhiteBalance returns absolute temp and tint from the channel means (cameraRaw.ts:1160-1170). autoTone reads pristineRef (1088-1093), and the WB tool samples pristineRef (1250). Each writes absolute values measured on an image that already includes the current correction, so they collapse back toward 0. uprightImage explicitly re-renders unwarped for re-edits (1101-1120), which shows the authors knew about the issue for geometry but not for WB or tone. This is a secondary path, but it affects every re-edit of an Open Object, so I kept major.

findings.title: Export DNG of a RAW-derived document embeds the crs: develop settings next to already-developed pixels
findings.feature: File ▸ Export ▸ Export DNG… (RAW-sourced documents)
findings.evidence: exportDNG writes the developed 16-bit composite as a LinearRaw DNG (dng.ts:1-10, 219) and passes xmp: rawExport.xmp (app.ts:5109-5117). That value is serializeCameraRawXmp(source) (store.ts cameraRawExportSnapshotForDoc), which emits the full crs: block (cameraRawSidecar.ts:157-161) with exposure, contrast, HSL, WB increments, crop and so on. ACR and Lightroom read develop settings from a DNG's embedded XMP.
findings.repro: Open a RAW with Exposure +1 and Saturation +30 → Open → File ▸ Export ▸ Export DNG… → open the .dng in Lightroom or ACR.
findings.impact: Other apps apply the develop a second time on top of baked pixels (double exposure, saturation and crop), so the exported DNG does not look like the Vision document.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not embed the develop crs: block in the rendered DNG. Keep identity metadata only, or write crs settings reset to neutral with HasSettings=False.
findings.verdict_reason: exportDNG passes rawExport.xmp into buildDNG16 (app.ts:5099-5117). cameraRawExportSnapshotForDoc sets xmp: serializeCameraRawXmp(source) (store.ts:5862-5876), which writes the full crs: block alongside mvcr:Payload (cameraRawSidecar.ts:157-161; xmp.ts crsAttrs writes exposure, WB, crop and more). dng.ts:231 stores it as tag 700 (XMP) in a DNG whose pixels are the developed 16-bit composite. Adobe readers apply embedded crs: settings from a DNG's XMP, so the develop and crop are applied twice. This is a wrong result on an interchange export; major is reasonable.

findings.title: Snapshots added or deleted while re-editing a RAW Smart Object are lost on OK
findings.feature: Camera Raw ▸ Snapshots (reopen invocation)
findings.evidence: updateSnapshots updates local state and sourceRef, and persists only through store.setCameraRawSnapshots when request.sessionId exists (1022-1026). The Snapshots section is shown on reopen (1591: rawOnly && sourceRef.current). ok() calls cameraRawDevelopTarget with the recipe only (1413-1418), and store.ts has no path that writes snapshots onto d.cameraRaw. No unit or e2e test touches data-mv-cr-add-snapshot or setCameraRawSnapshots.
findings.repro: Open a RAW with Open Object → Filter ▸ Camera Raw Filter → + New Snapshot → OK → reopen Camera Raw.
findings.impact: New snapshots, or deletions, disappear, although the panel showed them as saved.
findings.suggested_fix: When the target owns the RAW source, persist the snapshots to d.cameraRaw in cameraRawDevelopTarget (as part of the same history step), or hide Snapshots on reopen. Add a test.
findings.verdict_reason: updateSnapshots persists only when request.sessionId exists (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1022-1026). On a reopen, sourceRef is a copy (cameraRawTarget returns cameraRawSidecarSourceSnapshot, store.ts:5846-5851), and updateSnapshots replaces the ref with a new object, so d.cameraRaw is never mutated. ok() passes only the recipe (1413-1418). cameraRawDevelopTarget (store.ts:5899-5937) and setCameraRawSnapshots (5754-5757, sessions only) never write snapshots to d.cameraRaw. The Snapshots section is shown whenever rawOnly && sourceRef.current (1591), and a reopen counts as rawOnly.

findings.title: MCP cameraRaw.selectSession throws away the current image's unsaved workspace edits
findings.feature: MCP cameraRaw.selectSession vs filmstrip click
findings.evidence: The UI's switchTo saves the live recipe first: store.setCameraRawSessionWorkingRecipe(request.sessionId, recipe) (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1444-1450). selectCameraRawSession (store.ts:5701-5706; commands.ts:1064-1067) activates the target and remounts the workspace without saving. The workspace keeps its edits only in React state; its cleanup calls only cancelStagedSession, which does nothing for a non-active session.
findings.repro: Stage 2 RAWs (browser build), move sliders on image 1, call MCP cameraRaw.selectSession(image 2), then switch back.
findings.impact: Image 1's edits are gone. The MCP tool behaves differently from the filmstrip it mirrors.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the workspace push its recipe to the store on change (debounced) or on unmount, or make selectCameraRawSession ask the workspace to flush first.
findings.verdict_reason: selectCameraRawSession activates the target and requests the dialog without saving (store.ts:5701-5706; commands.ts:1064-1067). The UI's switchTo first calls setCameraRawSessionWorkingRecipe (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1444-1450). The unmount cleanup calls only cancelStagedSession, and cancelCameraRawSession returns false for a non-active session (store.ts:5728-5730), so runtime.working and source.recipe keep the pre-edit recipe (5402-5407).

findings.title: Camera Raw Filter local adjustments, heal spots and vignette land in different places than previewed on moved or non-canvas-sized layers
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Camera Raw Filter on a pixel layer (masks, healing, effects, geometry)
findings.evidence: The preview proxy_engine remaps the active layer into canvas space (mod.rs:25102-25124), so normalized mask, spot and vignette coordinates are relative to the canvas. On OK, camera_raw_develop runs develop_buf_with_headroom over active_pixel_plane_dimensions(), the layer's own pixel_bounds (mod.rs:4443-4449, 23403-23414), so the same normalized coordinates are relative to the layer plane.
findings.repro: Move a pixel layer with the Move tool (or use a layer larger or smaller than the canvas) → Camera Raw Filter → add a Radial mask centred on a face → OK.
findings.impact: The committed mask, spot or vignette is offset or scaled compared with the preview.
findings.suggested_fix: Develop the preview in plane space, or pass plane-to-canvas offsets and scale into the develop so both paths use the same coordinate frame. Confirm with an e2e test on an offset layer.
findings.verdict_reason: stageProxy calls eng.proxy_engine(0,0,width,height,…) (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:785-791). proxy_engine remaps the active layer's plane into canvas bounds (mod.rs:25102-25124). camera_raw_develop develops over active_pixel_plane_dimensions(), which is the layer's pixel_bounds w×h (mod.rs:4443-4449, 23403-23414). A Move bakes into pixel_bounds via checked_translate_bounds (bake_offset, mod.rs:~16850-16865). The normalized mask, spot and vignette coordinates are therefore canvas-relative in the preview and plane-relative on commit, offset by the move or scaled for planes that differ in size from the canvas.

findings.title: Local mask Tint slider runs opposite to the Basic Tint slider and to ACR
findings.feature: Camera Raw ▸ Masking ▸ Tint
findings.evidence: BASIC_ROWS Tint has invert:true because the recipe stores positive = green (lines 113-119, 240, fix #108). LOCAL_MASK_ROWS Tint has no invert (310). The engine applies the mask tint with the same adjust::wb_tint (develop.rs:1771), where positive tint means g_gain = 1+0.3·tint, that is greener.
findings.repro: Add a Brush or Radial mask and drag its Tint slider to +50.
findings.impact: Positive mask Tint makes the area greener, while Basic Tint +50 makes the image magenta (as in ACR).
findings.suggested_fix: Add invert: true to the LOCAL_MASK_ROWS tint spec, and check the XMP LocalTint mapping for the same axis.
findings.verdict_reason: BASIC_ROWS tint has invert:true (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:240, documented at 113-119 for #108), and LOCAL_MASK_ROWS tint does not (310). pushEngineMaskBlock emits mask adjustments verbatim (developParams.ts:184-199). The engine applies adjustments[1] through adjust::wb_tint (develop.rs:1771), where positive means g_gain = 1+0.3·tint, that is greener (adjust.rs:793-799). The global XMP write negates tint (xmp.ts:286), but LocalTint maps unnegated (xmp.ts:197).

findings.title: Camera Raw Filter stays enabled on layers it will refuse, and OK on a stale target does nothing with no message
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Camera Raw Filter enablement / OK
findings.evidence: menuEnablement leaves cameraraw on whenever a document exists (App.tsx:3440-3468). The workspace opens and lets the user build a full recipe for locked, type, adjustment, group, vector or fill layers and 32-bit documents. Only at OK does apply16 refuse (refuse_destructive_edit / reject_float_edit_for_layer, mod.rs:3890-3925). When the pinned target is gone, ok() returns silently (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1414-1415). The e2e test at camera-raw-workspace.spec.ts:1585 asserts the dialog just stays open.
findings.repro: Select a type layer (or lock a layer, or use a 32-bit document) → ⇧⌘A → adjust → OK. Or delete the target layer with a shortcut while the dialog is open → OK.
findings.impact: Work spent in the dialog is refused only at the end. In the stale case, OK looks broken.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable cameraraw for layer kinds or depths develop cannot target (or refuse when the dialog opens), and show an alert in the dialog when cameraRawDevelopTarget returns false.
findings.verdict_reason: menuEnablement has no cameraraw entry, so the command is enabled whenever a document exists (App.tsx:3434-3470; action at 2825). ok() returns silently when cameraRawDevelopTarget returns false (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1413-1415), and a stale layer makes it return false (store.ts:5913-5914). Refusals for locked, type and similar layers happen only in apply16, at commit.

findings.title: Camera Raw Filter / workspace develops are not recorded into actions; the recordable adj.cameraRawDevelop is unused
findings.feature: Actions recording of Camera Raw Filter
findings.evidence: The workspace's OK calls store.cameraRawDevelopTarget directly (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1415), and that function is not rec()-wrapped. The rec()-wrapped adj.cameraRawDevelop (app.ts:1062-1073) is called only from tests, e2e and nothing in the UI. Photoshop records Camera Raw Filter.
findings.repro: Actions ▸ Record → Filter ▸ Camera Raw Filter → OK → Stop. The action has no Camera Raw step.
findings.impact: Batch and droplets cannot replay a Camera Raw look.
findings.suggested_fix: Route OK through a rec()-wrapped action that carries docId, layerId, params and smartIndex (or adapt adj.cameraRawDevelop).
findings.verdict_reason: The rec()-wrapped adj.cameraRawDevelop (app.ts:1062-1073) has no non-test caller. The only production callers of the develop path use the unwrapped store.cameraRawDevelopTarget: workspace OK (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1415) and MCP (commands.ts:758). The Camera Raw Filter apply is therefore never captured by the action recorder.

findings.title: File ▸ Automate ▸ Lens Correction opens the single-layer Filter ▸ Lens Correction dialog
findings.feature: File ▸ Automate ▸ Lens Correction…
findings.evidence: The Automate submenu item has monetId 'lenscorrection' (psMenuData.ts:355-358), the same id as Filter ▸ Lens Correction (3062-3064). It maps to open('lensCorrection') (App.tsx:3118), a one-layer filter dialog with no preview (Dialogs.tsx LensCorrection).
findings.repro: File ▸ Automate ▸ Lens Correction…
findings.impact: The Photoshop batch lens-correction command (source files → destination) is advertised but not provided.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the monetId from the Automate entry so it shows disabled, or implement a batch over files that reuses applyLensProfileCorrection.
findings.verdict_reason: The facts hold: the Automate item uses monetId 'lenscorrection' (psMenuData.ts:355-358), the same as the Filter item (3060-3064), and it maps to open('lensCorrection') (App.tsx:3118). However, the aliasing is deliberate: psMenus.ts:57-59 lists both paths in SHARED_ACTION_PATHS as 'intentionally expose the same Monet command'. It works, applying lens correction to the current document, so this is a scope and labeling parity gap rather than a broken feature. I re-graded it to polish.

findings.title: Lightroom/ACR RAW white balance is dropped on import, and the WB menu shows a preset the render does not apply
findings.feature: XMP sidecar / preset import (white balance)
findings.evidence: RULES skips crs:Temperature and crs:Tint, the absolute values ACR and LR write for raw files (xmp.ts:771-772). readWhiteBalance still sets wbMode from crs:WhiteBalance, for example 'Daylight' (1214-1224), while temp and tint stay 0. Vision writes WB only as Incremental* (xmp.ts:281-286), which ACR uses for non-raw files. readNativeRawSidecar discards the skipped-field report (app.ts:3637-3653).
findings.repro: Open a RAW whose LR sidecar has WhiteBalance=Custom, Temperature=4300.
findings.impact: The image opens at as-shot WB with no notice, and the menu may read ‘Daylight’ or ‘Custom’. WB does not survive a round trip to ACR for raws.
findings.suggested_fix: Convert absolute Kelvin and tint to Vision offsets using the source's asShotKelvin (already recorded in profile.asShotKelvin), write absolute Temperature/Tint for raw sources, and report skipped fields when importing.
findings.verdict_reason: RULES skip crs:Temperature and crs:Tint (xmp.ts:771-772). readWhiteBalance sets wbMode from the crs:WhiteBalance name only (1212-1224), so temp and tint stay 0 while the label reads, for example, Daylight. Vision writes only Incremental* for WB (xmp.ts:281-292). readNativeRawSidecar keeps only look.recipe and drops the skipped report (app.ts:3637-3653).

findings.title: File ▸ Revert on a RAW-developed document marks it clean, so closing no longer protects the develop
findings.feature: File ▸ Revert (RAW-sourced documents)
findings.evidence: completeCameraRawOpen deliberately calls dirtyEntry so that 'closing it cannot silently discard the recipe' (store.ts ~5803-5808). revertDocument → revertActiveCameraRawSource → revertActiveDoc(eng, document) uses the default dirty=false (6055, 6169), even though the ‘file’ is a camera original with no saved project. For Open Object documents, revert re-develops d.cameraRaw.recipe, which cameraRawDevelopTarget has kept in sync with later edits, so it does not return to the state at open.
findings.repro: Open a RAW (adjust in the workspace) → File ▸ Revert → close the tab.
findings.impact: The tab closes without a save prompt, and the develop settings (and any later Smart Object recipe edits) are gone unless a sidecar was written.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass { dirty: true } for RAW-source reverts (no project path), or grey out Revert for RAW-pathed documents, as Photoshop does for unsaved ACR opens.
findings.verdict_reason: completeCameraRawOpen dirties the entry deliberately (store.ts:5804-5808). revertDocument → revertActiveCameraRawSource (app.ts:8023; store.ts:6133-6173) → revertActiveDoc(eng, document) without opts, so d.dirty = opts?.dirty ?? false (6055). Other synthetic reverts pass {dirty:true} (7307). For Open Object documents, the reverted recipe is the synced current recipe, not the one at open.

findings.title: Open as Smart Object uses a browser file input even on desktop, so RAW sidecars, originalPath and Revert are lost
findings.feature: File ▸ Open as Smart Object (RAW)
findings.evidence: openAsSmartObject always builds an <input type=file> (7413-7422), including in Tauri, and calls openCameraRaw without originalPath or readNativeRawSidecar (7426-7431), unlike openPaths (7966-7970).
findings.repro: Desktop: File ▸ Open as Smart Object a RAW that has an .xmp beside it.
findings.impact: The sidecar settings are ignored. Done prompts a save dialog instead of writing beside the RAW. The document has no path for Revert or Open Recent.
findings.suggested_fix: In Tauri, use the native open dialog and share the openPaths RAW branch with invocation 'open-as-smart-object'.
findings.verdict_reason: openAsSmartObject always creates an <input type=file>, with no isTauri branch (app.ts:7413-7422). It calls openCameraRaw with only invocation, sha256 and lastModified (7426-7431): no originalPath and no readNativeRawSidecar, unlike openPaths (7966-7970). Without originalPath, saveCameraRawSidecar falls back to a save dialog (3689-3695), and completeCameraRawOpen sets savedPath to null (store.ts:5807).

findings.title: No aggregate limit on decoded memory for staged RAW sessions (up to 8 full-resolution 16-bit engines in one WASM heap)
findings.feature: Camera Raw multi-image staging
findings.evidence: openRaw caps the number of sessions (8) and the aggregate SOURCE bytes (256 MB) (store.ts:5247-5260; cameraRaw.ts:56-63), but each session decodes a full 16-bit RGBA engine (about 8 B/px, so roughly 360 MB for a 45 MP file) in the shared WASM memory, and no decoded-size budget exists.
findings.repro: Browser build: select 5-8 45-60 MP RAWs at once.
findings.impact: Could exhaust WASM linear memory, and an allocation abort would take every open document with it. Not reproduced; confirm by staging several 45 MP RAWs and watching memory.
findings.suggested_fix: Budget staged sessions by decoded w×h×8, or decode lazily and keep only the active session's engine plus thumbnails.
findings.verdict_reason: The code facts hold. openRaw caps the session count at 8 and aggregate source bytes at 256 MB (store.ts:5247-5260; cameraRaw.ts:55-62), and each session holds a full engine from buildRaw with no decoded-size budget. The claimed consequence, a WASM OOM abort, is not demonstrated. Exposure is also limited to the browser build, because native multi-open is serial (see the openPaths finding). Staging 5-8 files of 45-60 MP in the browser build and watching wasm memory would settle it.

findings.title: Preset library: no way to delete a user preset, and a user preset named like a built-in cannot be applied
findings.feature: Camera Raw ▸ Presets
findings.evidence: removeCameraRawPresetAt exists (cameraRawPresets.ts:60-63) but no UI calls it. Apply finds a preset by name across [...DEFAULT, ...user] (990, 1572), so the built-in always wins a name clash, and the option values are duplicated.
findings.repro: Save a preset named ‘Punchy’, then apply ‘Punchy’.
findings.impact: Presets pile up with no way to remove them, and a same-named user preset cannot be reached.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Delete action per user preset, and key options by source plus name (or reject names that match built-ins).
findings.verdict_reason: removeCameraRawPresetAt (cameraRawPresets.ts:58-61) has no caller outside tests. Apply uses allPresets.find by name over [...DEFAULT, ...user] (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:990, 1572), so a built-in wins a name clash. savePreset does not reject built-in names (1031-1033). The storage-full message tells the user to 'Remove an existing preset' (1035), which the UI does not allow.

findings.title: Workspace accessibility and labels: pointer-only controls and a mislabeled Effects slider
findings.feature: Camera Raw preview toolbar / Effects
findings.evidence: The shadow and highlight clipping toggles are <span onClick> with no role, tabIndex or keyboard handler (1510-1521). The Before button works only on pointer-down/up (1504-1505); keyboard users have only the Y key. EFFECTS_ROWS labels the grainRoughness key ‘Grain Highlights’ (269); ACR calls it Roughness.
findings.repro: Tab through the preview toolbar; open the Effects section.
findings.impact: The clipping overlays cannot be reached by keyboard or screen reader, and the slider name is misleading.
findings.suggested_fix: Use Button or ToggleButton with aria-pressed for the clip toggles, add a keyboard toggle for Before, and relabel the slider ‘Grain Roughness’.
findings.verdict_reason: The clip toggles are <span onClick> with no role, tabIndex or key handler (CameraRawWorkspace.tsx:1510-1521). The Before button responds only to onPointerDown, onPointerUp and onPointerLeave (1504-1505); keyboard users have only the Y shortcut (966). EFFECTS_ROWS labels grainRoughness as 'Grain Highlights' (269).

areas.coverage: Inventory: 25 in-scope tools from src/state/toolRail.ts (brush, pencil, colorreplace, mixerbrush, adjustmentbrush, historybrush, erase, backgrounderaser, magiceraser, clone, patternstamp, heal, spothealing, remove, redeye, patch, contentawaremove, dodge, burn, sponge, smudge, blur, sharpen, gradient, bucket).
