I also covered their options bars (App.tsx 531-703, 924-981, 1025-1069, 1177-1231), the Brushes/Brush Settings panel (11 symmetry presets, 5 Shape Dynamics, 4 Scattering and 4 Transfer controls, presets, tips), the Clone Source store actions, and the 2 painting-related MCP commands (brush.setSymmetry, brush.transformSymmetry). Traced each one from the CanvasView pointer handlers (down 1124-1694, move 1699-2048, up/cancel 2050-2525), through store.pushBrush/beginBrushStroke/spotHeal/patchSelectionBy and app.removeStroke/contentAwareMoveBy, into EngineClient (commit, paintRegion, collab and tool-recording stroke replay), and on into packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs: stroke_begin, stroke_to, stamp, stroke_end, bucket_fill(_pattern), gradient_fill, magic_eraser, remove_red_eye, spot_heal_selection, patch_selection, content_aware_move, push_layer_undo/push_undo, the lock helpers and color-mode conversion. Test coverage was checked by grep: every tool is referenced by at least one e2e or unit test, but nothing tests lock-transparent painting, spot-heal undo step counts, replayed stroke fidelity, or painting on masks with the retouch tools. Nothing was built or run; all findings come from reading the code. Not reviewed in depth: Liquify, the Vanishing Point workspace (only its clone path was touched), the Clone Source panel's rendering, brush-preset import/export UI, and what the e2e specs assert beyond grep hits.
areas.parity_notes:
None of the in-scope tools is a disabled placeholder; all 25 are wired. These are Photoshop behaviours Vision does not implement, and they are not reported as bugs:
- Painting in 32-bit documents is refused, with a clear message, for every stroke tool, fill and retouch op (reject_legacy_float_edit).
- Brushes cannot target a single colour channel (R/G/B); only alpha channels, through Quick Mask.
- No pen tilt, rotation or stylus-wheel dynamics. There are no Texture, Dual Brush, Color Dynamics, Wet Edges or Noise brush settings.
- Brush presets store only BrushState, not dynamics. Custom brush tips apply only to Brush, Pencil and Eraser (stamp_geometry `matches!(mode, 0 | 1)`).
- The options-bar Size slider tops out at 400 px (Photoshop allows 5000), and [ / ] step a fixed ±2 px.
- Missing Alt modifiers: Dodge↔Burn, Blur↔Sharpen, Eraser → Erase to History, and the temporary eyedropper for Bucket, Gradient, Color Replacement and Mixer.
- Missing tool options: Color Replacement has no Tolerance, Sampling or Limits (it recolours everything under the brush); Paint Bucket and Magic Eraser have no Anti-alias; the Remove tool has no options.
- Patch cannot draw its own selection, and Red Eye needs a drag rather than a click.
- On empty layers, the Mixer Brush only deposits paint with Sample All Layers.
- The Remove tool's ML tier writes a new layer on each stroke, where Photoshop heals in place.
- Spot Healing is not constrained by an active selection: it replaces the selection with its own dabs.
- The Adjustment Brush is a Vision-specific tool. Its first stroke creates two history steps (layer plus stroke).
- The MCP surface has no painting commands (stroke, fill, gradient, heal, set tool/brush/colours); it only offers brush.setSymmetry and brush.transformSymmetry, so agents cannot drive any painting tool.

findings.title: Lock Transparent Pixels is ignored by every brush-stroke tool, Paint Bucket, Gradient, Magic Eraser, Red Eye and Spot Healing
findings.feature: Layers ▸ Lock Transparent Pixels × painting tools
findings.evidence: lock_transparent is only honoured through preserve_for_active/restore_locked_transparency (mod.rs:19482-19501). Its only callers are fills, the content-aware ops and patch (19515, 19849, 20300, 20372, 20682, 27333). stamp() (18683-19458), bucket_fill (20778), bucket_fill_pattern (20844), gradient_fill (20904), magic_eraser (22041), remove_red_eye (19622) and spot_heal_selection (20214) never read it. The paint path composite_overs straight onto base alpha (19405-19429), and erase lowers alpha (19316-19323). The Layers panel advertises the toggle (Panels.tsx:112), and layer_locks_transparency's doc comment says 'Read by the paint and fill paths' (mod.rs:11170-11176), which is not true.
findings.repro: 1) Paint a shape on an empty layer. 2) Click Lock Transparent Pixels in the Layers panel. 3) Brush with a new color across the shape and past its edge. The paint also lands on the transparent area. The Eraser/Magic Eraser make pixels transparent; Gradient and Paint Bucket fill the transparent area.
findings.impact: Recoloring 'inside the existing pixels', the main purpose of this lock, does not work. Users get paint outside their artwork, and holes from the eraser, on a layer they locked.
findings.suggested_fix: In stroke_begin, record preserve_for_active(false). In stamp's per-pixel write, skip pixels whose stroke_base alpha is 0 and keep base.a for the others. For mode 1 (erase) on a locked-transparency layer, paint the background colour at base alpha instead (Photoshop behaviour). Wrap bucket_fill(_pattern), gradient_fill, magic_eraser, remove_red_eye and spot_heal_selection with the existing restore_locked_transparency(before) pattern. Add an engine test per op, like the_content_aware_siblings_honour_lock_transparent_and_refuse_a_mask_target.
findings.verdict_reason: lock_transparent is read only in apply32 (mod.rs:4769-4779), preserve_for_active/restore_locked_transparency (19482-19501) and their callers (fill 19515/19849, content-aware 20300/20372/20682, patch 27333). stroke_begin (17512-17633), stamp (18683-19458), stroke_end (18057-18083), bucket_fill (20778), bucket_fill_pattern (20844), gradient_fill (20904) and magic_eraser (22041) never read it. The paint path composite_overs onto stroke_base alpha (19405-19429), and erase lowers alpha (19316-19323). No TS guard exists: grep finds no lock-transparency read in apps/vision/src outside Panels.tsx:112. The engine test at 41094-41100 covers only fill_blend. The doc comment at 11170-11176 ('Read by the paint and fill paths') is wrong. One caveat: Red Eye keeps alpha and only rewrites RGB (19664), so on alpha-0 pixels its violation is invisible. The brush, eraser, bucket, gradient and magic-eraser cases stand.

findings.title: Spot Healing/Remove, Red Eye and Magic Eraser skip the destructive-edit guards: they edit Lock-Image-Pixels layers, type/vector/smart layers and the pixels behind a targeted mask
findings.feature: Spot Healing Brush, Remove (classic fallback), Red Eye, Magic Eraser
findings.evidence: spot_heal_selection only checks `self.active_layer().locked || kind == 4` (20215). remove_red_eye does the same (19623). magic_eraser checks locked and kinds 1/3/4/7 only (22057-22059). None calls refuse_destructive_edit (3890-3912: lock_image, type, vector, smart, group) or refuse_mask_target (19506). The sibling ops do call both: content_aware_fill (20283), content_aware_move (20560), patch_selection (27319-27330). A Lock All layer returns silently with no last_edit_error, so CanvasView's engine.commit() (1358, 2407) and store.spotHeal (7022) show no message.
findings.repro: Case 1: on a pixel layer, turn on Lock Image Pixels, then Spot-Heal, Red-Eye-drag or Magic-Erase: the pixels change. Case 2: select a type layer and Spot-Heal it: the heal shows, then disappears the next time the text is edited. Case 3: target a layer mask (mask thumbnail) and Red-Eye or Spot-Heal: the colour pixels change, not the mask.
findings.impact: The locks are bypassed without any notice. Edits made to type or smart-object layers are silently lost on re-render, and mask-targeted edits land on the wrong target.
findings.suggested_fix: At the top of spot_heal_selection, remove_red_eye and magic_eraser, use the same guard as content_aware_fill: `if self.refuse_destructive_edit() || self.refuse_mask_target(label) { return; }` (a Lock All layer then reports its reason). Add these three ops to the lock/mask refusal test.
findings.verdict_reason: spot_heal_selection guards only `!sel.active || locked || kind == 4` (mod.rs:20215). remove_red_eye guards only `locked || kind == 4` (19623). magic_eraser refuses only locked and kinds 1/3/4/7 (22057-22059), so type layers (2) get through. None of them calls refuse_destructive_edit (3890-3912) or refuse_mask_target (19506), and none checks lock_image or painting_mask(). content_aware_fill does call both (20283). A Lock All layer returns without setting last_edit_error, so commit() shows nothing. There is no TS-side guard: CanvasView pointerup 2124-2126/2406 and pointerdown 1355-1357 call straight into the engine. The engine refusal test (43808) covers Content-Aware Fill/Move/workspace only, not these three ops. Small nit: magic_eraser does refuse vector and smart layers; its gaps are type layers, Lock Image and mask targets.

findings.title: A Spot Healing/Remove stroke pushes one 'Ellipse Marquee' history step per dab, which can evict the entire undo history
findings.feature: Spot Healing Brush / Remove tool undo
findings.evidence: store.spotHeal calls e.select_ellipse once per dab (7018). Each call runs push_sel_undo('Ellipse Marquee') (mod.rs:21071-21077). The heal pushes one more step, and the restore pushes a third: set_selection_mask pushes 'Select Subject' (mod.rs:21712-21716) or select_none pushes 'Deselect'. Dabs are added every >2 doc px (CanvasView.tsx:1853). push_undo trims to history_states, default 50 (store.ts:1403; mod.rs:5751-5752). fillPath already uses the scaffolding pattern this needs, withoutHistoryStep (store.ts:7035, 7043), but spotHeal and the ML path of app.removeStroke (app.ts:2021, 2029-2030) do not. Each selection snapshot also clones a canvas-sized mask (mod.rs:5705-5708).
findings.repro: 1) Make a few edits. 2) With the Spot Healing Brush, drag about 150 px across a blemish. 3) Open the History panel: dozens of 'Ellipse Marquee' rows plus a 'Select Subject' row. The earlier edits are gone. 4) Press Undo once: the canvas gains a circular marquee and the heal is not undone.
findings.impact: Users lose the ability to undo earlier work, and one Undo does not revert a heal. On a 24 MP image, one long drag retains roughly 1 GB of selection snapshots.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the dab selection and the restore in withoutHistoryStep, or build the dab mask in JS and apply it inside a single history transaction, so each stroke leaves exactly one 'Spot Healing Brush' step. Do the same in app.removeStroke. Add a unit test that asserts undo_pushes grows by 1 per stroke.
findings.verdict_reason: spotHealDabs emits one rect per accumulated point (spotHeal.ts:20-32). Points are added every >2 px (CanvasView.tsx:1853). store.spotHeal calls e.select_ellipse per dab (store.ts:7018), and each call runs push_sel_undo('Ellipse Marquee') (mod.rs:21071-21073), which clones the canvas-sized mask (5705-5708). The heal then pushes 'Spot Healing Brush' (20227). The restore pushes 'Select Subject' (set_selection_mask 21716) or 'Deselect' (21103). push_undo trims to history_states outside a transaction (5751-5752), with a default of 50 (store.ts:1403). Neither the recordedCall/rec wrapper (app.ts:877-894, 501-509) nor engine.commit opens a transaction. fillPath shows the intended pattern (withoutHistoryStep, store.ts:7035/7043). app.removeStroke's ML path does the same thing (app.ts:2021, 2029-2030). The first Undo restores the dab-union selection instead of undoing the heal.

findings.title: Collaboration and Allow Tool Recording replay every captured stroke as a plain Normal-mode Brush or Eraser stroke
findings.feature: Collab stroke sync; Actions ▸ Allow Tool Recording (paintStroke)
findings.evidence: strokeCaptureBegin runs for every tool in the brush-family case (CanvasView.tsx:1262-1299: dodge, burn, smudge, blur, sharpen, sponge, mixer, colour replace, background eraser, history brush, pattern stamp, adjustment brush). It captures only lastBrush: size, hardness, flow, opacity, spacing, rgba and the erase flag (store.ts:2920; EngineClient.ts:216-221). applyStroke replays with e.set_brush(...) (EngineClient.ts:275-276), which sets `brush.mode = if erase {1} else {0}` (mod.rs:17083). The recorded action step replays the same way (app.ts:781-783, 2291-2294). The replay also inherits the receiving engine's clone, pattern_stamp, mask_edit, brush tip and blend state.
findings.repro: Case 1: in a collab session, peer A dodges an area; on peer B the stroke appears as a solid stroke in A's foreground colour. Case 2: turn on Allow Tool Recording, record a Burn or Smudge stroke, then play the action: it paints the recorded foreground colour. An Erase-to-History stroke replays as paint.
findings.impact: Collaborators' documents silently diverge and get corrupted, and recorded actions produce wrong pixels.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the full stroke config in the StrokeOp: brush mode, blend/paint mode, clone/pattern flags, dodge/sponge/blur/sharpen/mixer options and tip id. On replay, set all of it, clear clone and mask_edit unless captured, and afterwards restore via store.pushBrush(). Alternatively, refuse to capture tools that cannot be replayed faithfully.
findings.verdict_reason: strokeCaptureBegin runs for the whole brush-family case, which includes dodge, burn, smudge, blur, sharpen, sponge, mixer, colour replace, background eraser, history brush, pattern stamp and adjustment brush (CanvasView.tsx:1256-1297). It copies only lastBrush, which has 10 fields: size, hardness, flow, opacity, spacing, rgba and an erase flag (store.ts:2920; EngineClient.ts:216-221). applyStroke replays through e.set_brush(...) (EngineClient.ts:275-276), and engine set_brush sets `brush.mode = if erase {1} else {0}` (mod.rs:17083) without touching blend, clone, pattern or mask state. Erase to History sets erase=false (store.ts:2907-2908), so it replays as paint in the foreground colour. The action op paintStroke goes through the same replayStroke path (app.ts:781-783, 2291-2294).

findings.title: Gradient and Paint Bucket ignore a targeted layer mask (they write the colour pixels) and refuse adjustment/fill layers
findings.feature: Gradient tool / Paint Bucket on layer masks
findings.evidence: gradient_fill (20904-21032), bucket_fill (20778-20838) and bucket_fill_pattern (20844-20898) never check painting_mask(). They call refuse_destructive_edit and then write layers[active].pixels. For an adjustment layer (kind 1), whose mask Photoshop targets by default, refuse_destructive_edit fails with 'adjustment layers hold no pixels' (3905). CanvasView calls them directly (1329-1339, 2458-2467). The brush path and patch_selection route to the mask through painting_mask() (17506-17510, 27316-27321).
findings.repro: Case 1: add a layer mask, click the mask thumbnail (mask edit on), then drag a black-to-white Gradient: the layer's pixels get the gradient and the mask is unchanged. Case 2: select a Curves adjustment layer and drag a Gradient: toast 'Could not apply the edit because adjustment layers hold no pixels'.
findings.impact: The standard Photoshop gradient-mask / graduated-adjustment workflow is impossible. With a mask targeted, the tools silently damage the pixels instead.
findings.suggested_fix: When painting_mask() is true, render the gradient ramp's (or flood's) luminance × coverage into the mask (or smart_mask) under push_stack_undo, the same way stamp's masking branch does. Do not refuse kinds 1/4 in that case. Edit ▸ Fill (fill_blend_inner, 19514) has the same gap.
findings.verdict_reason: bucket_fill (mod.rs:20778-20838), bucket_fill_pattern (20844-20898) and gradient_fill (20904-21032) never call painting_mask(). They run refuse_destructive_edit and then write layers[active].pixels. For kind 1 that call fails with 'adjustment layers hold no pixels' (3905), and engine.commit→consumeEditError turns that into a toast. CanvasView calls the engine directly, with no maskEdit routing (1329-1339, 2458-2467), and CanvasView has no maskEdit reference at all. The brush path, by contrast, routes to the mask through painting_mask() (17506-17510).

findings.title: With a mask targeted, Smudge/Blur/Sharpen/Sponge/Mixer edit the layer's colour pixels, and Dodge/Burn/Clone/Heal/Eraser just paint foreground luminance
findings.feature: Retouch brushes on layer masks / Quick Mask
findings.evidence: In stamp's per-pixel loop, modes 4 (smudge, 19104-19123), 8/9/10 (sponge/blur/sharpen, 19128-19204) and 11 (mixer, 19212-19240) write layers[active].pixels and `continue` BEFORE the `if masking` branch (19250-19269). stroke_begin's masking branch pushes a stack snapshot but never checks the tool (17599-17607). Every other mode reaching the masking branch writes the FG luminance: dodge/burn, clone and heal (clone_src is not captured when masking, 17612-17618), history brush, colour replacement and eraser. The eraser writes FG, not BG as in Photoshop.
findings.repro: Case 1: target a layer mask and drag the Blur tool along the mask edge: the image pixels blur and the mask edge stays hard. Case 2: with default colours on a mask (FG white / BG black), drag the Eraser: the mask is revealed (white), not hidden.
findings.impact: Softening, blending or erasing a mask edge with the retouch tools, a common masking task, edits the wrong target or does the opposite of what Photoshop users expect.
findings.suggested_fix: Branch on masking before the retouch modes and run smudge/blur/sharpen/dodge/burn/clone against the mask buffer (stroke_base_mask) as a single-channel plane. If that is out of scope for release, refuse those modes on a mask with a clear message. Make the eraser on a mask/Quick Mask use the background colour's luminance.
findings.verdict_reason: In stamp's per-pixel loop, mode 4 (19104-19123), modes 8/9/10 (19128-19204) and mode 11 (19212-19240) write layers[active].pixels and `continue` before the `if masking` branch (19250-19269). stroke_begin's masking branch only pushes a stack snapshot and copies the mask (17599-17607). It does not capture clone_src, and it has no per-tool check. Every other mode, including erase (mode 1), reaches the masking branch and writes pv = FG luma (or 1.0 for mask_reveal). So the eraser on a mask paints the foreground value, where Photoshop uses the background colour.

findings.title: Magic Eraser ignores the active selection
findings.feature: Magic Eraser
findings.evidence: The erase loop uses only the wand mask: `let cov = mask.coverage(i); ... *a = (*a as f32 * (1.0 - op * cov))` (22106-22114). self.sel is never consulted. In contrast, bucket_fill multiplies by self.sel.coverage (20824), and stamp does too (19065). CanvasView calls it with no selection handling (1355-1361).
findings.repro: 1) Select the left half of the image. 2) Magic-Eraser-click a colour region that extends into the right half: the right half is erased too.
findings.impact: Pixels outside the user's protective selection are destroyed, and the user may not notice until later.
findings.suggested_fix: Multiply cov by the plane-local selection coverage (plane_local_selection().coverage(i)) when a selection is active, and add a test next to each_op_matches_its_native_result.
findings.verdict_reason: magic_eraser's erase loop multiplies only by the wand mask's coverage (mod.rs:22106-22114). self.sel is never read in the function (22041-22117). bucket_fill (20824) and stamp (19065) do apply sel.coverage. CanvasView.tsx:1355-1361 passes no selection information, so pixels outside a protective selection get erased.

findings.title: Brush Settings ▸ Shape Dynamics / Scattering / Transfer only reach the engine that was active when the slider moved
findings.feature: Brushes panel dynamics
findings.evidence: setBrushTransfer/setBrushShapeDynamics/setBrushScatter push to `engine.engine` once, and keep the values in module-level `current` (brushDynamics.ts:41-56, 105-115, 160-170). A ponytail note already admits 'a New/Open engine swap resets the engine's copy back to zero while these values stay on screen'. store.pushBrush (store.ts:2898-2973), which activateDoc and every stroke call (store.ts:6227, 2705), never re-pushes them. Each document has its own engine (store.ts:6224).
findings.repro: 1) Open doc A and set Scatter 200% / Size Jitter 100%. 2) Open or switch to doc B and paint: no scatter or jitter, while the panel still shows 200% / 100%.
findings.impact: An advertised panel silently stops applying in the ordinary multi-document path, with no visible indication.
findings.suggested_fix: Call set_brush_transfer, set_brush_shape_dynamics and set_brush_scatter from pushBrush using brushTransfer(), brushShapeDynamics() and brushScatter(), or move the values into BrushState. Add a unit test that swaps the engine and asserts the dynamics are re-pushed.
findings.verdict_reason: setBrushTransfer, setBrushShapeDynamics and setBrushScatter push once to the engine passed in (brushDynamics.ts:53-57, 105-115, 160-166; Panels.tsx:3433/3441/3496/3502) and keep the values in module state. pushBrush (store.ts:2898-2973) never re-pushes them, and activateDoc switches to the target engine and calls pushBrush (6225-6227), so the other document's engine keeps its own, usually zero, values. The file's own ponytail note admits the New/Open case. Re-graded to minor: the single-document path works, and nothing is lost or corrupted; only the jitter/scatter is missing in other documents while the panel still shows it.

findings.title: Painting a targeted mask skips the Lock All check
findings.feature: Brush tools on locked layers' masks / adjustment layers
findings.evidence: stroke_begin runs `if !masking && self.refuse_destructive_edit() { return false; }` (17543-17547), so when painting_mask() is true (mask targeted, or any adjustment/fill layer, 17506-17510) the locked flag is never checked. The masking branch then writes layer.mask (19264-19266). Mask-targeted filters do refuse a locked layer (test float_edits_project_selection_honor_locks_and_target_masks, mod.rs:58689-58693), so the lock is enforced inconsistently.
findings.repro: 1) Lock All on an adjustment layer (or a masked pixel layer with the mask targeted). 2) Paint with the Brush: the mask changes.
findings.impact: 'Lock All' does not protect the mask from brushes, even though filters respect it.
findings.suggested_fix: In the masking branch of stroke_begin, refuse when layers[active].locked, with the same message refuse_destructive_edit uses.
findings.verdict_reason: stroke_begin runs `if !masking && self.refuse_destructive_edit() { return false; }` (mod.rs:17545-17547), so when painting_mask() is true (mask_edit, or a kind 1/4 layer that has a mask), `locked` is never checked. The masking branch then writes layer.mask (19264-19266). beginBrushStroke/pushBrush (store.ts:2701-2706) add no lock check. Filters do refuse a locked layer's mask (test at 58687-58691), so the lock is enforced inconsistently. Re-graded to minor: the path is narrow (Lock All on an adjustment layer or a mask-targeted layer), and the stroke is undoable.

findings.title: Each stroke keeps a full-layer u16 copy in undo with no memory budget, so large documents can exhaust WASM memory and poison the engine
findings.feature: Brush-stroke undo / stroke performance
findings.evidence: stroke_begin calls push_layer_undo, which clones the whole plane: px, px_f32, mask and more (5673-5689). It then clones the plane again into stroke_base (17627) and allocates a canvas-sized f32 accumulator (17629), synchronously on every pointerdown. Undo is trimmed only by count (trim_undo_to_history_states, 5729-5734; default 50, store.ts:1403); no byte budget exists anywhere. For 6000×4000, one snapshot is 192 MB, so about 15-20 strokes approach the wasm32 4 GiB ceiling. MAX_PIXELS is 80 MP (1050), where a single snapshot is 640 MB. The engine's own comment (17500-17505) notes that a wasm panic leaves the wasm-bindgen borrow flag set, so 'the unsaved document cannot even be saved'. An allocation failure traps the same way.
findings.repro: 1) Open a 24 MP single-layer photo. 2) Paint 20-30 short strokes with History States at 50, watching WebAssembly memory. Expected: memory climbs about 190 MB per stroke until allocation fails and the engine throws on every later call. There is also a visible hitch at each pointerdown from the ~290 MB clone and allocation.
findings.impact: Painting in a crash-then-can't-save state, which is likely on camera-sized images. I did not observe this at runtime.
findings.suggested_fix: Store only the stroke's dirty-rect region in the undo snapshot: snapshot lazily per tile, or union the dirty rects and crop at stroke_end. Add a total undo byte budget that evicts the oldest entries. Reuse stroke_base and stroke_acc buffers across strokes. Confirm with an e2e that paints N strokes on a 6000×4000 document and asserts memory stays bounded.
findings.verdict_reason: The code facts check out. push_layer_undo clones the whole plane: pixels (u16×4), px_f32, mask and more (mod.rs:5673-5689). stroke_begin then clones it again into stroke_base (17627) and allocates a canvas-sized f32 stroke_acc (17629). pixels is always u16, so an 8-bit 24 MP document costs about 192 MB per snapshot. Undo is limited only by count (trim_undo_to_history_states, 5729-5734; default 50). The engine has no byte budget, and EngineClient/store have no memory-pressure purge (purge is called only on convert/import paths). 50 × 192 MB is far past the wasm32 4 GiB address space, which all open documents share. The OOM-trap-then-poisoned-engine outcome is inferred from standard wasm-bindgen behaviour and the engine's own note (17500-17505), not observed; a large-document stroke loop that watches WebAssembly.Memory would settle it.

findings.title: The Healing Brush can panic the engine on an empty imported layer whose pixel plane is 0×0
findings.feature: Healing Brush (mode 5) on zero-bounds layers
findings.evidence: The heal membrane probe clamps `((cx + ox).round() as i32).clamp(plane.x, plane.x + plane.w as i32 - 1)` (18810-18811). With plane.w == 0 or plane.h == 0 that is clamp(min, min-1), and i32::clamp panics when min > max. Imported raster layers keep their PSD bounds and clear their pixels (format_import.rs:732-733), so an empty PSD layer is a valid 0×0 plane (pixel_plane_is_valid, mod.rs:482-485). The plane grows only for non-mask, non-Quick-Mask dabs that hit selected pixels (17956-18022). So heal on such a layer with a selection that excludes the first dab, or with Quick Mask on, or with a mask targeted, reaches stamp with a 0-width plane.
findings.repro: 1) Open a PSD containing an empty layer and select it. 2) Make a selection elsewhere. 3) Alt-click a Healing Brush source. 4) Start a heal stroke outside the selection. Expected: an engine panic, after which every engine call throws.
findings.impact: The document can no longer be saved. Healing on an empty layer is the standard non-destructive retouch workflow.
findings.suggested_fix: Return early from stamp when plane.w == 0 || plane.h == 0 (nothing can be written). Guard the heal probe's clamp. Add an engine test that heals on a 0×0-plane layer.
findings.verdict_reason: An imported raster layer keeps its PSD bounds and clears its pixels (format_import.rs:731-743), and a 0×0 plane passes checked_plane_len/pixel_plane_is_valid (mod.rs:1082-1093, 482-485), so plane_rect returns Some(w=0,h=0) (4478-4484). stamp builds heal_membrane whenever mode == 5 && clone (18803-18829), before the masking and Quick Mask branches. HealMembrane::from_boundary calls the probe unconditionally (develop.rs:1028-1043), and the probe does `.clamp(plane.x, plane.x + plane.w - 1)` (18810-18811), where i32::clamp panics if min > max. Plane growth runs only when not Quick Mask, not masking, and some selected pixel is outside the plane (17949-18022). So Quick Mask on, a targeted mask, or a selection that excludes the dab each reach stamp with a 0-width plane.

findings.title: Painting ignores the document colour mode: Grayscale, Indexed and CMYK documents receive arbitrary RGB
findings.feature: Painting tools in non-RGB documents
findings.evidence: The mode is applied only at conversion time: convert_grayscale rewrites pixels once and sets self.mode = 1 (9084-9111), and set_mode separates CMYK once (8088-8130). stamp's paint path deposits brush.color unchanged (19405-19429). gradient_fill and bucket_fill do the same (20834, 21026-21028), as does pushBrush's hsvToRgba(fg) (store.ts:2904). composite() does not project to the mode. self.mode is otherwise read only by blend-space selection and a few encoders (7762, 29996, 30005).
findings.repro: 1) Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale. 2) Pick a red foreground and paint: a red stroke appears in a 'Grayscale' document. The same happens with off-palette colours in an Indexed document and out-of-gamut colours in CMYK.
findings.impact: What the user sees is not what gets saved: some exporters gray-convert while others write colour, and the Channels panel disagrees with the canvas.
findings.suggested_fix: Map the effective paint colour through the document mode before depositing: luma for Grayscale, nearest palette entry for Indexed, reseparate() for CMYK/Multichannel. The simplest place is in pushBrush and in the gradient/bucket colour sources. Or re-apply the mode's projection to the dirty rect at stroke_end.
findings.verdict_reason: The colour mode is applied only at conversion (convert_grayscale at 9109; the set_mode separation at 8088-8130). The self.mode reads in mod.rs are limited to blend-space selection (7762), plates, conversion and encoders (29996/30005); composite has none. pushBrush sends hsvToRgba(fg) unchanged (store.ts:2904), setForeground does no mode projection (store.ts setForeground), and no TS display path reads doc_mode for the canvas. stamp's paint path deposits brush.color as is (19405-19429), and bucket_fill and gradient_fill do the same. A red stroke in a Grayscale document therefore stays red in the layer data.

findings.title: Quick Mask, targeted alpha-channel and layer-mask strokes are clipped to the active layer's pixel plane
findings.feature: Quick Mask / alpha channel painting / mask painting
findings.evidence: stamp requires the point to lie inside the active layer's plane (`let Some(pi) = checked_plane_index(plane, x, y, 4) else { continue; }`, 19069-19071) before the Quick Mask branch (19091-19101) and the mask branch (19250). Plane growth is disabled for Quick Mask and mask strokes (17956-17957). Moving a pixel layer bakes the offset into pixel_bounds (bake_offset, 16858-16863), and imported layers keep compact bounds, so parts of the canvas lie outside the plane. Channels-panel alpha targeting paints through the Quick Mask buffer (store.ts:8305-8321).
findings.repro: 1) Move the active pixel layer 200 px right. 2) Press Q (Quick Mask) and paint across the left 200 px: nothing is painted there. Targeting an alpha channel behaves the same way.
findings.impact: Parts of the document cannot be painted into the selection or alpha channel, with no explanation.
findings.suggested_fix: Evaluate the Quick Mask and mask branches before the plane lookup; they index canvas-sized buffers by `i`. Only require `pi` for the pixel-writing branches.
findings.verdict_reason: In stamp, `let Some(pi) = checked_plane_index(plane, x, y, 4) else { continue; }` (mod.rs:19069-19071) comes before both the Quick Mask branch (19091-19101) and the mask branch (19250). Both of those index canvas-sized buffers by `i`. Plane growth is skipped when qm_on or painting_mask() (17955-17957). bake_offset moves pixel_bounds on a layer Move (16858-16863), and imported layers keep compact bounds (format_import.rs:732), so canvas areas outside the plane cannot be painted in Quick Mask or on a mask.

findings.title: Clone Stamp and Healing Brush sample an 8-bit source in 16-bit documents
findings.feature: Clone Stamp / Healing Brush in 16-bit
findings.evidence: capture_clone_src fills clone_src from selection_sample_buffer(false), which takes `(src[p + k] >> 8) as u8` (4674), or from 8-bit composites (17414-17420). A cross-document source is RGBA8 too (set_clone_source, 17356-17365; clone_source_rgba8, 17371-17377). The pattern source stays 16-bit, so only clone and heal quantize.
findings.repro: 1) In a 16-bit smooth gradient (sky), clone one area over another at 100%. 2) Apply strong Curves: the cloned patch bands relative to its surroundings.
findings.impact: Retouched areas silently lose 16-bit precision.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep clone_src as u16 (or f32), sample it at full depth, and extend set_clone_source to accept u16.
findings.verdict_reason: clone_src is a Vec<u8> (mod.rs:3212). capture_clone_src fills it from selection_sample_buffer(false), which does `(src >> 8) as u8` (4674), or from the 8-bit composite (17414-17420). set_clone_source and clone_source_rgba8 are RGBA8 too (17356-17377). One sub-claim is wrong: the pattern source is quantized as well, because fill_clone_from_pattern writes `(pattern >> 8) as u8` into clone_src (fill_clone_from_pattern), so Pattern Stamp and Heal ▸ Pattern also lose 16-bit precision. The finding therefore understates the scope.

findings.title: Color Replacement deposits the foreground onto transparent pixels and raises edge alpha
findings.feature: Color Replacement tool
findings.evidence: Mode 6 does `composite_over(base, Rgba::new(cr,cg,cb, ca*cov), cr_blend, 1.0)` (19374-19376). composite_over mixes the source by backdrop alpha `(1-αb)*Cs + αb*B(Cb,Cs)` and raises alpha to `αs + αb(1-αs)` (blend.rs:301-313). With αb = 0, the raw foreground is painted. The tool's own description promises recolor-only behaviour: 'Recolor with the foreground while preserving each pixel's brightness/shading' (toolRail.ts:28).
findings.repro: 1) On a cut-out subject layer, drag the Color Replacement tool across the edge into the transparent area: solid foreground paint appears where there were no pixels.
findings.impact: The tool paints instead of recolouring on any layer with transparency.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep base.a (write the result with a = base.a) and skip pixels with base.a == 0. Photoshop's Color Replacement never adds coverage.
findings.verdict_reason: Mode 6 runs composite_over(base, Rgba(cr,cg,cb, ca*cov), cr_blend, 1.0) (mod.rs:19370-19376). composite_over mixes Cs' = (1-αb)·Cs + αb·B(Cb,Cs) and outputs alpha αs + αb(1-αs) (blend.rs:297-313). At αb = 0 that gives the raw foreground with new coverage, which contradicts the tool's recolor-only description (toolRail.ts:28). There is no base.a preservation or skip for transparent pixels.

findings.title: Options-bar controls that do nothing: Opacity/number keys on Smudge/Blur/Sharpen/Sponge/Mixer, Airbrush on Clone/Heal, and a duplicate 'Flow' on Sponge
findings.feature: Painting options bar
findings.evidence: The Opacity slider and the digit shortcuts are shown and applied for all OPACITY_TOOLS (App.tsx:572-575, 2459-2460; opacityShortcuts.ts:10). stamp reads `opacity` only for the accumulator cap (mod.rs:19243) and Quick Mask (19093); modes 4/8/9/10/11 `continue` before that. The Airbrush checkbox is shown for clone/heal/vanishing point (App.tsx:586-599), but those pointerdown paths never call startAirbrushTimer (CanvasView.tsx:1362-1474). Sponge shows the shared 'Flow' slider (b.flow) and a second slider also labelled 'Flow' (b.spongeRate) (App.tsx:573, 646).
findings.repro: 1) Pick Blur, set Opacity to 10%, and blur: the result is the same as at 100%. 2) Pick Clone Stamp, tick Airbrush, and hold still: nothing builds up. 3) Pick Sponge: two sliders both named Flow.
findings.impact: Users get misleading controls, and accessible names are duplicated.
findings.suggested_fix: Hide Opacity for modes that ignore it, or map it to Strength like Photoshop does. Start the airbrush timer on the clone/heal path, or hide the checkbox. Rename the sponge slider (or drop one of the two).
findings.verdict_reason: OPACITY_TOOLS includes smudge, blur, sharpen, sponge and mixerbrush (opacityShortcuts.ts:10). The Opacity slider (App.tsx:574) and the digit keys (App.tsx:2459-2460) target brush.opacity. In stamp, modes 4/8/9/10/11 `continue` before `cap = opacity * sel_cov` (19243), so opacity has no effect there. The Airbrush checkbox is shown for every opacity tool (App.tsx:590), but only the brush-family pointerdown calls startAirbrushTimer (CanvasView.tsx:1317); the clone/heal/vanishing-point paths (1362-1474) do not. Sponge shows the shared Flow slider (573) and a second slider also labelled 'Flow' for spongeRate (646).

findings.title: A Gradient click without a drag fills the whole layer or selection with one colour
findings.feature: Gradient tool
findings.evidence: onPointerUp calls E.gradient_fill for any release, with no minimum drag distance (2458-2467). The engine clamps `len2 = (dx*dx + dy*dy).max(1e-4)`, so ux = uy = 0 and the linear t is 0 everywhere, while radial t clamps to 1 (mod.rs:20937-21001). It then pushes an undo step.
findings.repro: Select the Gradient tool and click once on the canvas: the entire layer becomes the first stop colour.
findings.impact: A stray click destroys the layer's content. It is undoable, but surprising; Photoshop does nothing.
findings.suggested_fix: Ignore releases shorter than about 2 screen px (as typeBoxFromDrag does), both in CanvasView and in the engine (return when len2 < 1).
findings.verdict_reason: The pointerup gradient case (CanvasView.tsx:2458-2467) calls gradient_fill with no minimum drag distance. In gradient_fill, len2 = max(1e-4) gives len = 0.01 and ux = uy = 0, so a linear gradient gets t = 0 everywhere and a radial one clamps t to 1 (mod.rs:20933-21001). It then writes every selected pixel and pushes an undo step ('Gradient', 20925). Other drag tools do reject a click (crop w>2, frameIsValid, artboardDragIsValid).

findings.title: Painting on a hidden layer is silently allowed
findings.feature: Brush tools / fills on hidden layers
findings.evidence: Neither stroke_begin (17512-17633) nor refuse_destructive_edit (3890-3912) checks layers[active].visible. Bucket and gradient only call refuse_destructive_edit too (20792, 20919).
findings.repro: 1) Hide the active layer. 2) Paint a stroke: nothing appears on screen, but an undo step is added and the hidden layer is modified.
findings.impact: Users paint 'blind' and then wonder why nothing happens. Photoshop refuses with 'the target layer is hidden'.
findings.suggested_fix: Refuse in stroke_begin, bucket_fill and gradient_fill when the active layer is invisible, with a message.
findings.verdict_reason: stroke_begin (mod.rs:17512-17633) and refuse_destructive_edit (3890-3912) never read layers[active].visible. bucket_fill and gradient_fill guard only through refuse_destructive_edit. Neither CanvasView nor the store has a hidden-layer check, and no 'layer is hidden' message exists anywhere in the engine or the store.

findings.title: Gradient, Paint Bucket and Magic Eraser are never recorded into actions
findings.feature: Actions recording of fill tools
findings.evidence: The bucket (1329-1339), magic eraser (1355-1361) and gradient (2458-2467) commits call the engine plus engine.commit(), with no rec() and no actions.recordTool. Lasso and marquee do record (2171, 2295). Photoshop records Gradient, Paint Bucket and Magic Eraser steps.
findings.repro: 1) Start recording an action. 2) Drag a Gradient and click the Paint Bucket. 3) Stop: the action has no steps for them.
findings.impact: Macros replay without their fills.
findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the three commits in an app.ts rec() action (e.g. gradientFill(args), bucketFill(args), magicErase(args)) and register them in visionOps.
findings.verdict_reason: The bucket (CanvasView.tsx:1329-1339), magic eraser (1355-1361) and gradient (2458-2467) commits call E.* and engine.commit() directly. They are not store methods, so the RECORDED_STORE_OPS wrapping (app.ts:903-975) cannot catch them, and actions.recordTool is called only for selectPolygon, selectRect and selectEllipse (CanvasView.tsx:2171/2295/2307). visionOps has no gradient, bucket or magic-eraser op (app.ts:2280-2300).

findings.title: The Remove tool's ML path can overwrite a newer selection and can drop the stroke silently
findings.feature: Remove tool (MI-GAN / LaMa)
findings.evidence: removeStroke builds a temporary dab selection, then awaits the model import, session load and inference (2021-2025). Its `finally` always restores savedCopy (2029-2030), even when the user changed the selection meanwhile. When docChanged() is hit, lamaFillML/generativeFillML return {ok:false} without throwing (onnx.ts:458, 509), so the classic fallback at 2027 never runs and the stroke has no effect. There is no busy indicator or concurrency guard, so a second stroke during inference replaces the first stroke's selection before it is read (onnx.ts:437, 487).
findings.repro: 1) With the LaMa or MI-GAN model installed, make a Remove stroke. 2) While it infers, drag a new marquee: the marquee is replaced by the old selection when inference ends. 3) Making another edit during inference leaves the first stroke with no effect.
findings.impact: Selections get clobbered and strokes are lost without feedback.
findings.suggested_fix: Serialize Remove strokes and show progress. Restore the selection only if the selection generation is unchanged. Fall back to the classic heal (or toast) when ok is false.
findings.verdict_reason: removeStroke selects the dab union (app.ts:2021) and awaits the import, session and inference. Its `finally` unconditionally restores savedCopy or runs select_none (2029-2030). lamaFillML and generativeFillML read get_selection_mask only after `await session()` and `await composite()` (onnx.ts:437, 487), so a selection change made meanwhile is what gets inpainted. When docChanged(gen) is hit, they return {ok:false} without throwing (onnx.ts:458, 509), so the catch fallback at app.ts:2027 never runs. There is no concurrency guard in removeStroke.

findings.title: Clone Stamp / Healing Brush with no source silently do nothing
findings.feature: Clone Stamp / Healing Brush
findings.evidence: `if (!src && !fromPattern) { dragRef.current = null; break; }` (1376-1378) shows no message. prepareCloneSource returning false, when the source document was closed, is also silent (1393-1395). Only the Clone Stamp options bar has an 'Alt-click to set source' hint (App.tsx:618); the Healing Brush has none.
findings.repro: Select the Healing Brush and drag without Alt-clicking first: nothing happens.
findings.impact: The tool looks broken. Photoshop shows 'the area to clone has not been defined'.
findings.suggested_fix: Call engine.onEditError with an 'Alt-click to define a source' message, and show the hint for the Healing Brush too.
findings.verdict_reason: `if (!src && !fromPattern) { dragRef.current = null; break; }` (CanvasView.tsx:1378) shows no message, and `if (!armed) { ...break; }` (1392) stays silent when prepareCloneSource returns false (store prepareCloneSource). The options-bar hint exists only for clone (App.tsx:618). The Healing Brush's tool-rail description (toolRail.ts heal) does say 'Alt-click to set the source', which partly offsets this.

findings.title: Pattern Stamp and Color Replacement show no brush-size cursor
findings.feature: Brush tip cursor
findings.evidence: PAINTING_TOOLS omits 'patternstamp' and 'colorreplace' (75). brushTipDiameter returns 0 for tools outside that set (86), and cursorCss falls back to the tool icon (2746-2756).
findings.repro: Select the Pattern Stamp: the pointer is an icon, and no brush outline shows its size.
findings.impact: Users cannot see the footprint of two brush tools.
findings.suggested_fix: Add both ids to PAINTING_TOOLS.
findings.verdict_reason: PAINTING_TOOLS (CanvasView.tsx:75) omits 'patternstamp' and 'colorreplace'. For those tools brushTipDiameter returns 0 (86), and cursorCss falls through to crosshair or toolIconCursor (2746-2756).

findings.title: The Healing Brush with Source: Pattern and no pattern reports a 'Pattern Stamp' error
findings.feature: Healing Brush ▸ Source: Pattern
findings.evidence: stroke_begin always says 'Could not use the Pattern Stamp because no pattern is defined…' when pattern_stamp is set (17552-17556). pushBrush sets that flag for the heal pattern source too (store.ts:2952-2954).
findings.repro: Healing Brush ▸ Source: Pattern with no defined pattern, then stroke: the toast names the Pattern Stamp.
findings.impact: The error names the wrong tool.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose the label by brush.mode (5 → Healing Brush).
findings.verdict_reason: pushBrush sets set_pattern_stamp(true) for heal with healSource === 'pattern' (store.ts:2952-2954). stroke_begin then emits the fixed message 'Could not use the Pattern Stamp because no pattern is defined…' (mod.rs:17552-17556), and consumeEditError shows it as a toast (EngineClient consumeEditError → onEditError).

findings.title: The Eraser tooltip promises 'transparency or the background color', but there is no erase-to-background path
findings.feature: Eraser tool description
findings.evidence: The description reads 'Erase pixels to transparency or the background color.' pushBrush maps the eraser only to alpha removal (mode 1, store.ts:2908, 2924), stamp mode 1 only lowers alpha (mod.rs:19316-19323), and the engine has no Background-layer concept.
findings.repro: Hover the Eraser in the tool rail, then erase: pixels always become transparent.
findings.impact: The tooltip is misleading.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the copy, or implement erase-to-BG on transparency-locked layers together with the lock fix above.
findings.verdict_reason: toolRail.ts erase description: 'Erase pixels to transparency or the background color.' pushBrush maps the Eraser only to erase mode 1 or Erase to History (store.ts:2907-2908, 2924). Stamp mode 1 only lowers alpha (mod.rs:19316-19323). The only background-colour paint path is the Pencil's Auto Erase (strokePaintsBackground, store.ts:2703-2704), and the engine has no background-layer concept.

areas.coverage: Read-only code review; no builds or test suites were run. Inventory: 23 in-scope tools from toolRail.ts: move, crop, frame, artboard, slice, sliceselect, shape (6 kinds: rect, roundrect, ellipse, polygon, line, custom; 3 modes: shape, path, pixels), pen, freeformpen, curvaturepen, addanchor, deleteanchor, convertpoint, pathselect, directselect, dropper, colorsampler, ruler, count, note, hand, rotateview, zoom. 84 in-scope menu rows: 82 blueprint rows with a monetId plus 2 injected (Perspective Crop…, Fit Layer(s) on Screen). They cover Transform, Crop, Trim, Reveal All, Crop and Straighten, Analysis/measurement, Artboard and Frame, Vector Mask, Rasterize Shape, Combine Shapes, Align ×6, Distribute ×8, Create Work Path, Convert to Shape, Define Custom Shape, Paths to Illustrator, zoom and fit, Show toggles, Rulers, Slices. 8 Paths-panel actions: Make Selection, Make Work Path, Fill, Stroke, Save, Delete, Load, Clipping Path. About 6 in-scope MCP commands: xform.crop/flip/rotate/resize and layer.vectorMaskFromPath. I followed every tool's pointer down/move/up/cancel path in CanvasView.tsx into store.ts, app.ts and the engine (raster/mod.rs, format_import.rs), including lock and refusal handling, undo pushes, per-document state and persistence. I grep'd unit and e2e coverage for each tool. I did not review in depth: Artboards to Files/PDF export, the Combine Shapes pathfinder internals, PSD vmsk encoding details, the Smart Guides snap maths, rotated-view hit testing, and how the compositor treats a group header's offset. For that last one I could not confirm whether moving a group with the Move tool moves its members, so it is not reported.
areas.parity_notes:
These are unimplemented or simplified compared with Photoshop. They are not reported as bugs where disabled or documented:
- **Move tool:** no Auto-Select (layer/group), no arrow-key nudge, and no Apply/Don't Apply prompt when a pending Transform Controls frame is dropped on a tool switch.
- **Rulers:** a static 50-px tick strip that ignores zoom and the Units & Rulers preference. You cannot drag guides out of them.
- **Crop tool:** commits on release, with no adjustable crop box, no rotate or Straighten in the tool, and no Classic/Shield options.
- **Perspective Crop:** only a numeric-percent dialog (Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective Crop…), not an on-canvas tool.
- **Pen:** no Path mode (see findings), no closing by clicking the first anchor, no Auto Add/Delete, no Rubber Band. A double-click close also adds two duplicate end anchors.
- **Shape tool:**
  - No Path Operations dropdown; a new Shape-mode shape is appended into the active vector layer rather than getting its own layer.
  - Stroke uses the background colour, and only for rect/ellipse.
  - Transform Controls have no distort/skew and no flip past the anchor (documented ponytail).
- **Zoom:** no scrubby or marquee zoom. Double-clicking Hand or Zoom does nothing special.
- **Count tool:** no count groups, colours or label sizes.
- **Slices:** layer-based slices are static snapshots, and slices are not undoable.
- **Crop and Straighten:** no deskew.
- **MCP:** the in-scope surface is only xform.crop/flip/rotate/resize and layer.vectorMaskFromPath. There is no MCP for the Shape, Pen or Paths panel, slices, artboards, frames, measurement, zoom or align/distribute.
- **Duplicate-id menu rows:** Fit Artboard on Screen, Canvas Guides, Artboard Guides, Clear Selected Artboard Guides and Clear Canvas Guides render correctly disabled (first-wins in psMenus.ts). File ▸ Import ▸ Notes… is wired by label (importnotes).
- **Vision-authored vector layers exported to PSD:** these carry live vmsk+SoCo only when the scene reduces to one solid fill with no stroke; otherwise they export as pixels (documented). A PSD shape layer imports as an editable kind-3 layer (covered by psd-shape-layer.spec.ts).

findings.title: Moving or transforming a vector (shape) layer only shifts its cached pixels; the scene stays put and the edit is lost on save/reopen or the next re-render
findings.feature: Move tool / Show Transform Controls / Edit ▸ Transform / Align-Distribute on kind-3 vector layers
findings.evidence: CanvasView.tsx:2222 commits a Move drag via E.commit_offset. mod.rs:16912 commit_offset → apply_linked_move → bake_offset. bake_offset (mod.rs:16850-16909) only special-cases kind 0 (moves the plane bounds) and kind 7 (appends a smart matrix). Every other kind, including 3, hits the else-branch at 16896, which remaps `layer.pixels` and never touches `vector_scene` or `vector_cache_key`. transform_layer (26816-26862), flip_layer_h/v (27042-27071) and shift_layer → shift_layer_plane_contents (10021-10080, used by align_layer/align_layers/distribute_layers) are also pixel-only for kind 3. render_vector (5423-5436) re-rasterizes from the scene on any cache miss. That happens on invalidate_vector_layers after font registration (5474), after any vector edit, and on load: format_import.rs:3647 rebuilds kind 3 from the scene with no cache key. Export also reads the stale scene: the PSD vmsk path (format_import.rs:256-283) and export_paths_svg (mod.rs:12094-12121). The team already fixed this class of bug for type (rasterize_active_text_metadata; see transformBakesType.test.ts header) and for smart objects, but not for vectors. No test moves or transforms a kind-3 layer.
findings.repro: 1) Shape tool, Mode = Shape, draw a rectangle (creates a vector layer). 2) Move tool, drag the layer 100 px right. 3) Switch to Direct Selection: the anchors are still drawn at the old spot. 4) Drag any anchor, or save as .monetgfx/.psd and reopen: the rectangle is back at its original position. Free Transform, Show Transform Controls, Flip Layer and Align behave the same way.
findings.impact: A core shape-layer workflow silently loses the user's positioning and transforms on save or reopen and in PSD/SVG export. The overlay and hit-testing also disagree with the pixels.
findings.suggested_fix: In bake_offset (and the align/distribute shift paths), handle kind 3 by translating the scene: prepend (dx, dy) to each top-level item, as vector_translate_item does, then clear vector_cache_key and re-render. For transform_layer, flips, skew and warp on kind 3, either apply the matrix to the scene's items or rasterize the layer first (kind=0, drop the scene) inside the same undo step, mirroring rasterize_active_text_metadata. Add an engine test: move a vector layer, then invalidate_vector_layers, and the pixels stay moved.
findings.verdict_reason: I traced it end to end. CanvasView.tsx:2208-2223 has a special branch only for text (LAYER_KIND.text); a vector layer falls through to E.commit_offset. commit_offset (mod.rs:16912) → apply_linked_move (16716) → bake_offset (16850). bake_offset special-cases only kind 0 and kind 7; kind 3 lands in the else branch (16896-16908), which remaps layer.pixels and never touches vector_scene or vector_cache_key. render_vector (5423-5472) keys its cache only on w, h and view, so the moved pixels survive only until something invalidates the cache: invalidate_vector_layers (5474), any vector_* edit (15358, 15416 …), or load. On load, format_import.rs:3647-3656 rebuilds kind 3 from the scene with vector_cache_key None, and the next composite re-rasterizes at the old position. transform_layer (26816-26862: refuse, push, rasterize_active_text_metadata, which only handles kind 2, then a pixel remap) and shift_layer → shift_layer_plane_contents (10021-10080), used by align_layers and distribute_layers, are also pixel-only for kind 3. No engine test or e2e moves or transforms a kind-3 layer. Moving a shape layer is a core workflow and the position is silently lost on save, so blocker stands.

findings.title: Move tool relocates a locked (Lock All / Lock Position) type layer on release while reporting that the move was refused
findings.feature: Move tool on type layers
findings.evidence: flushMove (CanvasView.tsx:1012-1013) sets appliedMoveRef.current = p even when move_layer_offset refused. The engine refuses at mod.rs:16628 for lock_position || locked and sets last_edit_error. On pointerup (2208-2220), `applied` is non-zero, so the text branch calls text.apply(id, {...spec, ax+fdx, ay+fdy}). text.apply is applyTextSpec (app.ts:2920-2925), which calls set_text_layer_spec (mod.rs:15965-15988) with no lock check, pushes a 'Type' undo and re-renders at the new anchor. engine.commit() then consumes the stale move refusal (EngineClient.ts:823-824): it shows 'Could not move the layer because its position is locked.' and returns false, so onCommit never marks the document dirty.
findings.repro: Create a type layer, lock it (Lock All or Lock Position), select the Move tool and drag it. Nothing moves during the drag. On release the text jumps to the drop point and a 'position is locked' toast appears. Close the tab: no unsaved-changes prompt.
findings.impact: Locks are bypassed. The user gets a false error message, and the document is left un-dirtied, so the edit can be lost without a save prompt.
findings.suggested_fix: Only take the text re-anchor branch when the engine accepted the offset (the flush returned a non-zero rect / no pending edit error), and reset appliedMoveRef when move_layer_offset refuses. Also make set_text_layer_spec refuse lock_position changes of ax/ay or locked layers (or check E.layer_locks in the branch).
findings.verdict_reason: There is no lock guard in CanvasView (grep 'lock' finds nothing on the move path). flushMove (CanvasView.tsx:1008-1019) sets appliedMoveRef = p even when move_layer_offset refuses; the refusal is at mod.rs:16626-16631 for lock_position || locked. At pointerup (2197-2219) `applied` is non-zero, so the text branch runs text.apply → applyTextSpec (app.ts:2920-2924) → set_text_layer_spec (mod.rs:15965-16039). That function checks only the kind; it pushes a 'Type' stack undo and re-places the pixels at the new anchor. engine.commit() (EngineClient.ts:823-824) then consumes the stale refusal, shows the toast and returns false before onCommit, blit and sync. Nuance: because commit bails before blit, the visual jump may only appear on the next repaint. The engine state really is changed, though, the lock is bypassed and the document is not marked dirty.

findings.title: Move tool with an active selection ignores Lock All and Lock Image Pixels, and bakes into type, vector and smart-object layers
findings.feature: Move tool (selection float)
findings.evidence: CanvasView.tsx:1156 makes any Move drag with has_selection() a selMove, and pointerup (2185-2190) calls E.move_selection unconditionally. move_selection (mod.rs:16940-16964) checks only float depth. It never calls refuse_destructive_edit (3890-3912), which every other pixel op uses to refuse locked, lock_image, kind 2/3/4/7 layers. It treats `locked` as a 'Background-style layer' and fills the hole with the background colour (16964-16986; engine test at 57047). In Vision, `locked` is only ever set by the Layers panel Lock All toggle (store.ts:7711); the Background layer is not locked.
findings.repro: Lock a pixel layer (Lock All), make a marquee selection, and drag with the Move tool: the pixels move and the hole is filled with the background colour. Do the same on a type or shape layer: the rendered pixels move but vanish on the next re-type or re-render.
findings.impact: Locked content is edited. Edits to type and vector layers are silently discarded later.
findings.suggested_fix: Call refuse_destructive_edit() at the top of move_selection (or refuse in CanvasView and drain the error). Drop the 'locked = Background' branch, or key it off a real background flag.
findings.verdict_reason: CanvasView.tsx:1156 sets selMove whenever has_selection(), and pointerup (2185-2191) calls E.move_selection unconditionally. move_selection (mod.rs:16940-16990) checks only sel.active, reject_legacy_float_edit, an empty mask and plane_rect; it never calls refuse_destructive_edit (3890-3912), which is what refuses locked, lock_image and kinds 1/2/3/4/6/7. It reads `locked` as 'Background' and fills the hole with the bg colour. In Vision, `locked` is set by set_layer_locked, which the UI calls only from setLayerLocked (store.ts:7710-7711, the Lock All toggle and layerfrombg). So locked content is edited, and the pixels baked into type and vector layers are discarded on the next re-render or re-type.

findings.title: Lock Position is ignored by Free Transform, Show Transform Controls and single-layer Align; multi-layer Align/Distribute ignore every lock
findings.feature: Move tool options (Align/Distribute), Edit ▸ Transform, Layer ▸ Align/Distribute
findings.evidence: refuse_locked_transform (mod.rs:3847-3853) checks only `locked`. transform_layer (26827), the flips and skew use it, so lock_position is never consulted. align_layer (9843-9848) likewise checks only `locked`. align_layers (10183-10230) and distribute_layers (10088-10130) check no lock at all and call shift_layer, which also has no lock check (10021). The only lock_position check is in move_layer_offset (16628).
findings.repro: Set Lock Position on a layer and press ⌘T, or drag a Transform Controls handle: it transforms. Multi-select three layers including a Lock All layer and click Align Left: the locked layer moves too.
findings.impact: The per-attribute locks (#418) do not protect position against the most common repositioning commands.
findings.suggested_fix: Have refuse_locked_transform also refuse lock_position. In align_layers/distribute_layers, skip or refuse layers with locked || lock_position and set last_edit_error.
findings.verdict_reason: refuse_locked_transform (mod.rs:3847-3853) checks only `locked`. transform_layer (26827) and align_layer (9843) rely on it, so lock_position is never consulted. align_layers (10183-10230) and distribute_layers (10088-10130) have no lock check at all and call shift_layer (10021), which has none either. The TS wrappers (store.alignLayer 7691-7701, distributeLayers 2653-2656, xform.transformLayer via bakeTransform app.ts:3526-3566) add no guard, and no UI code reads layer_locks for these commands (the only reads are store.ts:2433 and 7728, for display). The only lock_position check is move_layer_offset (16628).

findings.title: An unfinished Pen path survives tool and document switches, corrupting the next Freeform/Curvature commit and overwriting Direct Selection edits; the advertised Enter/Esc do nothing
findings.feature: Pen tool
findings.evidence: penAnchorRef (CanvasView.tsx:310) is cleared only inside closePen (2602). No effect resets it on a tool or activeDocId change, unlike the curvature pen (2680-2692). The main CanvasView is not keyed per document (App.tsx:3746). closePen prefers penAnchorRef over penRef (2583-2584). commitCurvePen (2610-2618) and the freeform release (2129-2138) both call closePen, so a stale Pen path is what gets filled or turned into a shape. Every Pen click runs syncPen → store.setPenAnchors(penAnchorRef) (2571-2577), which overwrites the store work path, including edits Direct Selection just made through moveWorkPathAnchors (store.ts:9446-9456) and the work path of the document you switched to. Only the curvature pen binds Enter/Esc (2680-2692). PEN_HINT (App.tsx:275) promises 'double-click or Enter to close the path'. The in-progress overlay (2978-3010) also stays drawn under other tools.
findings.repro: 1) Pen: click 3 points, don't close. 2) Switch to Freeform Pen and drag a loop: on release the earlier Pen triangle is filled, not the loop. Or: Pen, click 3 points; Direct Selection, drag an anchor; back to Pen and click: the anchor snaps back. Or: Pen in doc A, switch tab, click in doc B: doc A's anchors appear in doc B's work path.
findings.impact: The wrong geometry is filled or committed, and in-progress path edits are silently reverted. Enter/Esc don't work, contrary to the hint.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset penAnchorRef, penPts and penAnchorPath when tool or activeDocId changes (keep the work path in the store). Re-seed penAnchorRef from store.state.penAnchors before appending, so Direct Selection edits survive. Add Enter (close) and Esc (end or cancel) handlers for the Pen like the curvature pen's.
findings.verdict_reason: penAnchorRef (CanvasView.tsx:310) is reset only in closePen (2602). No effect clears it on a tool or doc change; only the curvature pen (2680-2692) and poly lasso have such effects. The main CanvasView is not keyed per doc (App.tsx:3746). closePen (2580-2607) prefers penAnchorRef when it has anchor form, so the freeform release (2129-2138), which only fills penRef and setPenAnchors, and commitCurvePen (2610-2618) both fill the stale Pen path. syncPen (2570-2577) writes penAnchorRef to store.setPenAnchors on every Pen click, overwriting moveWorkPathAnchors edits (store.ts:9446-9456) and, after activateDoc swaps penAnchors per doc (store.ts:6211-6213), doc B's work path. PEN_HINT (App.tsx:275) promises Enter, but only the curvature pen binds Enter/Esc, and the only Pen close path is onDoubleClick (2773).

findings.title: Pen has no Path mode; closing a path always fills pixels (the default) or creates a shape layer, and throws away the work path
findings.feature: Pen / Freeform / Curvature Pen → Paths panel, Define Custom Shape, Vector Mask ▸ Current Path
findings.evidence: penMode is typed 'pixels' | 'shape' with default 'pixels' (store.ts:1164, 1611; options bar App.tsx:826). closePen fills with FG in pixels mode (2590-2598) and then clears the work path in every branch (store.setPenPath([]) at 2606). The work path therefore exists only while the path is left open. Yet the Paths panel's empty state says 'No paths — draw one with the Pen tool' (Panels.tsx:2900), the Custom shape hint says 'Draw a Pen path, then Edit ▸ Define Custom Shape…' (App.tsx:1090), and the layer.vectorMaskFromPath MCP error says 'draw a path with the Pen tool first'. After the natural double-click close, all of these find no path: defineCustomShape returns -1 silently (store.ts:4191-4193).
findings.repro: Draw a closed path with the Pen (double-click) and open the Paths panel: no Work Path, and the active layer was painted. Edit ▸ Define Custom Shape does nothing.
findings.impact: Photoshop's default Pen workflow (draw a path, then Make Selection, Save Path, Stroke Path, or Define Custom Shape) is broken, and the default mode destructively paints instead.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'path' penMode (make it the default) in which closing keeps the anchors as the work path (setPenAnchors with a closed flag) and paints nothing. Keep Pixels/Shape as explicit choices. Disable Define Custom Shape when there is no work path, or explain why.
findings.verdict_reason: The facts hold. penMode is 'pixels' | 'shape' with default 'pixels' (store.ts:1164, 1611; App.tsx:826). closePen fills in pixels mode and always calls store.setPenPath([]) (2606). defineCustomShape returns -1 silently when there is no path (store.ts:4191-4193). I downgraded it: both advertised modes do what their labels say, the fill is undoable, and a work path is still available by leaving the Pen path open or by using the Shape tool's 'path' mode (App.tsx:1093). This is a Photoshop-parity and UX gap, not a broken feature. The misleading hints (Panels.tsx:2900, App.tsx:1090) are the actionable part.

findings.title: Pixels-mode Shape, Line and Pen fills destroy the user's selection and write 3–9 undo steps per shape
findings.feature: Shape tool (Pixels, the default) / Line / Pen, Freeform and Curvature in Pixels mode
findings.evidence: The Pixels branch (2354-2398) runs E.select_rect/ellipse/polygon(...,0), then fill_selection, then select_none, plus a second select/subtract/fill/deselect pass for the stroke ring. The line branch (2327-2339) runs select/fill/deselect up to 3 times for the arrowheads, and closePen (2590-2598) does the same. Each select_* pushes its own history state (push_sel_undo, mod.rs:21064-21108), fill_blend_inner pushes 'Fill' (19521ff) and select_none pushes 'Deselect' and overwrites last_sel (Reselect). store.withoutHistoryStep (store.ts:7673) exists for exactly this and is used by fillPath, but not here. e2e/curvature-pen.spec.ts:96-99 accepts 'each its own history step'. Both shapeMode and penMode default to 'pixels' (store.ts:1417, 1611). If the fill is refused (locked or non-pixel layer), the selection is still lost and 2 empty steps remain.
findings.repro: Make a marquee selection, then draw a rectangle with Stroke > 0 using the Shape tool (default Pixels). The selection is gone, the History panel shows about 7 rows (Marquee, Fill, Deselect, …), one ⌘Z does not undo the shape, and Select ▸ Reselect gives the rectangle outline, not your selection.
findings.impact: Every default shape wipes the active selection and floods History. Near the History States cap this evicts real older states.
findings.suggested_fix: Save the selection mask, run select/fill/deselect with the selection steps wrapped in withoutHistoryStep (or one history transaction), restore the saved mask with set_selection_mask (as spotHeal does, store.ts:7015-7025), then commit once. Move the logic into a store method shared by the shape, line and pen code.
findings.verdict_reason: The shape branch (CanvasView.tsx:2353-2396), the line fillPoly (2329-2334) and closePen (2590-2598) all call E.select_* (mode 0 = replace), then fill_selection, then select_none, with no withoutHistoryStep and no save/restore of the mask. Each select_* calls push_sel_undo (mod.rs:5701-5710, 21064-21089), fill pushes a layer 'Fill' (19522), and select_none pushes 'Deselect' and overwrites last_sel (21097-21109). shapeMode defaults to 'pixels' (store.ts:1417). e2e/curvature-pen.spec.ts:96-100 explicitly loops up to 4 undos to take back one pen fill. The contrast with store.fillPath (7035, 7043, withoutHistoryStep) and spotHeal (7015-7022, mask save/restore) shows the pattern exists but is not used here.

findings.title: Slices, count markers, color samplers and the ruler line are app-global rather than per document, are not saved, and are not remapped by crop
findings.feature: Slice / Slice Select, Count, Color Sampler, Ruler, File ▸ Save for Web
findings.evidence: The fields slices/selectedSlice/slicesLocked, countPoints, colorSamplers and rulerLine (store.ts:1115-1141, defaults 1582-1599) are absent from DocEntry (347-407) and from activateDoc's per-document swap (6192-6224). They are never reset on New or Open, and ProjectDocumentMeta (projectEnvelope.ts:57-86) has no field for them. saveForWeb reads store.state.slices for whichever document is active (app.ts:5322-5342). remapDocSpaceAnnotations (store.ts:3559-3574) remaps guides, notes and samplers but not slices, count points or the ruler line after a crop. This contradicts the stated rule in perDocumentTools.test.ts: 'Tool state that names pixels belongs to the document that owns them'.
findings.repro: Doc A: draw 3 slices and place 2 color samplers. Switch to doc B: they show on B, the Info panel reads B's pixels at A's coordinates, and File ▸ Save for Web on B exports three slice files cut at A's rectangles instead of one image. Save A and reopen it: the slices and samplers are gone.
findings.impact: Export produces wrong output across documents, measurements are wrong, and slice work is lost on save.
findings.suggested_fix: Move these fields into DocEntry and swap them in activateDoc (and reset on New/Open). Persist slices, samplers and count in ProjectDocumentMeta, and in PSD resources where supported. Include slices and count in remapDocSpaceAnnotations.
findings.verdict_reason: These fields exist only in AppSnapshot (store.ts:1115-1141, defaults 1582-1599). activateDoc's per-doc set (6192-6224) swaps notes, guides, penPath and so on, but not slices, countPoints, colorSamplers or rulerLine. A grep finds no reset anywhere outside the store's own mutators, and none in projectEnvelope.ts. saveForWeb reads store.state.slices for the active doc (app.ts:5322-5342). remapDocSpaceAnnotations (store.ts:3560-3574) remaps guides, notes and colorSamplers but not slices, count points or the ruler line.

findings.title: Frame tool does not scale the placed image to fit, and images larger than the canvas are cropped at the canvas's top-left before centring
findings.feature: Frame tool (K) → drop/place image
findings.evidence: fillFrame (store.ts:7596-7611) calls E.importImage, then only offsets the layer with frameFillOffset (frameTool.ts), which is centring only with no scale. import_image (mod.rs:29355-29381) copies min(iw,w)×min(ih,h) from the image's top-left into a canvas-sized plane. Anything past the canvas is discarded before centring. The tool text says 'drop or place an image to fill it'; Photoshop's frames scale content to fit.
findings.repro: In a 1000×1000 document, drag a 200×200 frame and place a 4000×3000 photo into it. The frame shows a 1:1 200-px window of the photo's top-left 1000×1000 region, not the photo fitted to the frame.
findings.impact: The Frame tool's main purpose, placing a photo into a frame, gives a useless crop in the common case of photos larger than the frame or canvas.
findings.suggested_fix: Decode at full size (or place as a smart object), compute a fill or fit scale for the frame bounds, and transform the member (e.g. transform_layer or a smart matrix) before clipping. Add an e2e test with an image larger than the canvas.
findings.verdict_reason: fillFrame (store.ts:7596-7610) calls E.importImage and then only set_layer_offset, using frameFillOffset (frameTool.ts:67-77), which does centring arithmetic with no scale. import_image (mod.rs:29355-29381) copies only min(iw,w)×min(ih,h) from the image's top-left into a canvas-sized plane, so anything beyond the canvas is gone before centring, and nothing scales to the frame. Placing a typical photo into a frame, the tool's main use case, gives a 1:1 crop.

findings.title: Layer ▸ Distribute ▸ Horizontal and Vertical do centre distribution instead of spacing
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Distribute
findings.evidence: App.tsx:2914-2915: disth → distributeLayers(0, 1) and distv → distributeLayers(1, 1), the same as disthc and distvc (2912, 2909). The engine supports equal spacing as key 3 (mod.rs:10088-10095, distribute_spacing), and the options bar uses it (App.tsx:268-269). In Photoshop the Horizontal/Vertical items distribute spacing.
findings.repro: Select 3 layers of unequal widths and choose Layer ▸ Distribute ▸ Horizontal: the gaps are unequal, exactly as with Horizontal Centers.
findings.impact: Two menu items duplicate other items and never give the spacing result.
findings.suggested_fix: Wire disth to distributeLayers(0, 3) and distv to distributeLayers(1, 3).
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:2914-2915 wires disth → distributeLayers(0, 1) and distv → distributeLayers(1, 1), the same as disthc (2912) and distvc (2909). The menu labels are 'Horizontal' and 'Vertical' under a separator (psMenuData.ts:2226-2235). The engine's key 3 = distribute_spacing (mod.rs:10091-10093) is used only by the options bar (App.tsx:268-269). No test references disth or distv.

findings.title: Paths panel Fill Path permanently discards the user's active selection
findings.feature: Paths panel ▸ Fill Path
findings.evidence: fillPath replaces the selection with the path through withoutHistoryStep(select_polygon(...,0)) (7035), fills, then withoutHistoryStep(select_none) (7043). Both selection changes are dropped from history, so Undo restores only the pixels and the prior selection is unrecoverable. select_none also stores the path as last_sel, so Reselect does not bring it back either. spotHeal (7015-7025) shows the save-and-restore pattern.
findings.repro: Make a marquee selection, then Paths ▸ Fill Path. The selection is gone, and neither ⌘Z nor ⇧⌘D restores it.
findings.impact: Loses selection work; this differs from Photoshop, where Fill Path leaves the selection alone.
findings.suggested_fix: Copy engine.selectionMask() before the fill and restore it with set_selection_mask afterwards (or select_none if there was none), as spotHeal does.
findings.verdict_reason: store.fillPath (store.ts:7027-7045) replaces the selection through withoutHistoryStep(select_polygon(...,0)), which drops the Sel snapshot (7673-7687). The fill itself pushes only a layer 'Fill' snapshot (mod.rs:19522), so Undo restores pixels but not the selection. withoutHistoryStep(select_none) runs select_none, which sets last_sel to the path mask (21106), so Reselect restores the path, not the user's selection. There is no save/restore like spotHeal's (7015-7022).

findings.title: Stroke Path on a locked, type or vector layer does nothing and leaves its refusal message to pop up on the next unrelated commit
findings.feature: Paths panel ▸ Stroke Path
findings.evidence: strokePath: `const began = e.stroke_begin(); if (began) {...}`, then `if (began) this.engine.commit();` (7071-7090). When stroke_begin refuses, it sets last_edit_error through refuse_destructive_edit (mod.rs:17550-17552), and nothing drains it. CanvasView drains this exact case for brush strokes (1289-1296: 'an undrained message would surface on the next unrelated commit').
findings.repro: Lock the active layer, then Paths ▸ Stroke Path: nothing happens. Your next edit shows 'Could not apply the edit because the layer is locked.'
findings.impact: A silent failure, followed by an error that blames the wrong action.
findings.suggested_fix: When began is false, call this.engine.consumeEditError().
findings.verdict_reason: store.strokePath (7052-7090) calls engine.commit() only `if (began)`, and nothing drains the error when stroke_begin returns false. stroke_begin sets last_edit_error on refusal (the lock/kind gate after mod.rs:17537). Callers (Panels.tsx:2852, 2890, 2957) do not drain either. The brush path does drain in this exact case (CanvasView.tsx:1289-1296), so the next commit's consumeEditError (EngineClient.ts:823-824) would surface the stale message and swallow that commit's own sync.

findings.title: Crop tool runs Delete Cropped Pixels even when the crop itself was refused, destroying off-canvas pixels without an undo step
findings.feature: Crop tool (Delete Cropped Pixels + Content-Aware)
findings.evidence: CanvasView.tsx:2417-2421 calls crop_content_aware/crop, then E.delete_cropped_pixels() unconditionally. delete_cropped_pixels is raw and pushes no undo (mod.rs:25354-25404). crop_content_aware refuses on 32-bit documents when the box extends past the canvas (reject_document_float_edit, 26228-26232), and can return silently when plan_document_remap fails. After a refusal, delete_cropped_pixels still clips every raster plane to the unchanged canvas.
findings.repro: 32-bit document: drag a layer partly off-canvas with the Move tool. Crop tool with Content-Aware on and Delete Cropped Pixels on (the default): drag a box past the canvas edge. You get a 'not 32-bit-float safe' toast, but the layer's off-canvas part is now gone, and ⌘Z does not restore it.
findings.impact: Narrow trigger, but unrecoverable pixel loss.
findings.suggested_fix: Record E.undo_pushes() before the crop and call delete_cropped_pixels only if the crop pushed a step (or move the delete into the engine's crop functions behind a flag).
findings.verdict_reason: CanvasView.tsx:2417-2421 runs crop or crop_content_aware, then E.delete_cropped_pixels() unconditionally when cropDeletePixels is on (the default, store.ts:1436). crop_content_aware refuses on 32-bit documents for border-exposing boxes (mod.rs:26228-26230) and returns silently on plan_document_remap failure (26237-26239). delete_cropped_pixels (25354ff) pushes no undo and clips every oversized kind-0 plane to the unchanged canvas. Nuance: ⌘Z still steps back to the snapshot before the prior edit (for example the Move), so the loss is 'the post-move off-canvas content', not strictly unrecoverable. The trigger is narrow.

findings.title: Path Selection and Direct Selection push an 'Edit Path' undo step on every click, even without a drag
findings.feature: Path Selection / Direct Selection on shape layers
findings.evidence: pathSelectAt (store.ts:9503-9523), directSelectAt (9366) and directSelectHandleAt (9412) call e.vector_begin_edit on every hit. vector_begin_edit (mod.rs:15367-15378) immediately calls push_layer_undo('Edit Path'), and push_undo clears the redo branch (5757).
findings.repro: Undo an edit, then click a shape component with Path Selection just to select it for Properties or Align. History gains an 'Edit Path' row and Redo is gone.
findings.impact: Selecting destroys the redo chain and pads History with no-op entries.
findings.suggested_fix: Defer vector_begin_edit to the first actual pointermove delta (a lazy snapshot), or drop the step on release with drop_last_undo when nothing moved.
findings.verdict_reason: pathSelectAt (store.ts:9510-9523), directSelectAt (9371) and directSelectHandleAt (9412) call e.vector_begin_edit on every layer hit. vector_begin_edit (mod.rs:15367-15378) calls push_layer_undo('Edit Path') unconditionally for kind 3, and push_undo moves redo into redo_before_last_push (5761), so the redo branch is cleared. On release, CanvasView (around 2505-2508) calls only endPathDrag or endAnchorDrag, and no drop_last_undo runs when nothing moved.

findings.title: Dragging a rubber-band anchor set that spans the work path and a shape layer, by one of the work-path anchors, edits the layer with no undo snapshot
findings.feature: Direct Selection
findings.evidence: directSelectAt returns early for a work-path hit without calling vector_begin_edit (store.ts:9356-9360). The drag loop then calls engine.e.vector_move_anchor for every non-primary layer anchor (CanvasView.tsx:1768-1775). vector_move_anchor pushes no undo (mod.rs:15296-15365).
