findings.repro: With a visible work path and an active shape layer, marquee-select anchors from both, then drag by a work-path anchor. ⌘Z does not revert the shape-layer anchors; it reverts an earlier edit instead.
findings.impact: A non-undoable vector edit (edge case).
findings.suggested_fix: Call vector_begin_edit(activeLayer) at drag start whenever anchorOrigins contains a non-work-path anchor.
findings.verdict_reason: vectorPaths (CanvasView.tsx:419-428) merges work-path overlays with the active vector layer's paths under Direct Selection, so a rubber band can select both. Clicking a work-path anchor makes directSelectAt return early (store.ts:9356-9360) without vector_begin_edit. The drag loop (CanvasView.tsx:1762-1775) then calls engine.e.vector_move_anchor for the layer anchors, and that function contains no push_* or undo call (mod.rs:15296-15362). Because the primary anchor is the work-path one, only markDirty and refreshFromEngine run, and no snapshot is taken.

findings.title: The Add, Delete and Convert Anchor Point tools ignore the work path
findings.feature: Add / Delete / Convert Anchor Point tools
findings.evidence: addAnchorAt, deleteAnchorAt and convertPointAt (store.ts:9458-9500) call only the engine vector_* functions on the active layer. Direct Selection targets the work path first (9353-9360). A Pen, Shape-Path or Create Work Path path is therefore not editable with the three point tools.
findings.repro: Shape tool in Path mode: draw a rectangle (work path). Add Anchor Point: click a segment. Nothing happens.
findings.impact: The point tools work only on shape layers, which is inconsistent with Direct Selection and with Photoshop.
findings.suggested_fix: When the hit is on workPathTargets(), apply the insert, delete or convert to penAnchors (the path helpers already exist in state/paths.ts) before falling back to the engine.
findings.verdict_reason: addAnchorAt, deleteAnchorAt and convertPointAt (store.ts:9458-9500) call only the engine vector_* functions on the active layer, while directSelectAt and directSelectHandleAt target workPathTargets() first (9356, 9397). Nuance: the finding's repro (Shape tool in Path mode) goes through setPenPath, which clears penAnchors (6936-6939), so Direct Selection can't edit that path either. The gap is real for Pen-authored paths and Type ▸ Create Work Path paths (which have anchor form).

findings.title: View ▸ Zoom In/Out, 100%, 200% and Print Size (and the Navigator and zoom field) zoom about the document's top-left corner, not the view centre
findings.feature: View zoom commands
findings.evidence: zoomBy (store.ts:10089-10091) and setZoom (2818-2821) change the zoom but leave the pan untouched. They are called with no pan from App.tsx:3242-3243 (zi/zo), 3300 (zoom200), 3305 (printsize), 3330 (actual), 1517 (zoom field) and Panels.tsx:2086 (Navigator). The Zoom tool's own 100% button centres (CanvasView.tsx:594-597), and panes zoom about the centre (setPaneZoom, 2847-2851).
findings.repro: Fit on Screen, then press ⌘+ several times: the image slides toward the bottom-right and out of view instead of enlarging about the middle.
findings.impact: Menu, keyboard and tool zoom behave inconsistently, and zooming in pushes content off-screen.
findings.suggested_fix: Route these through a zoom-about-viewport-centre helper (reuse matchedView or the zoomAt maths with the viewport centre).
findings.verdict_reason: Pan is the screen position of the document origin: zoomAt (CanvasView.tsx:2714-2724) computes docx = (clientX - panX) / zoom. zoomBy (store.ts:10089-10091) and setZoom without pan (2818-2821) keep the pan, so the doc origin stays fixed and the image grows toward the bottom-right. Callers that pass no pan: App.tsx:3242-3243, 3300, 3305, 3330, 1517 and Panels.tsx:2086. In contrast, setPaneZoom (store.ts:2847-2851) and the Zoom tool presets (CanvasView.tsx:591-598) centre.

findings.title: Trim, Reveal All, Image Rotation, Ruler ▸ Straighten and Perspective Crop leave guides, notes and color samplers at stale coordinates
findings.feature: Image ▸ Trim / Reveal All / Rotation, Ruler Straighten, Perspective Crop
findings.evidence: Crop passes an annotations remap (app.ts:3541, and the crop tool at CanvasView.tsx:2423). trim (3547-3549), revealAll (3544), rotate90/180/rotateArbitrary (3551-3553; the Ruler 'Straighten Layer' button calls rotateArbitrary at App.tsx:1431) run runGeometryEdit without annotations. perspectiveCrop (1815-1823) skips runGeometryEdit entirely: no remap and no requestFit.
findings.repro: Add a guide at x=100 and a note, then Image ▸ Reveal All with content left of the canvas (or Trim the top-left border). The guide and note no longer sit on the same pixels.
findings.impact: Measurement and annotation positions become wrong after common geometry edits.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the origin shift for Trim and Reveal All (derive it from the engine or compare the canvas before and after), rotate annotation points for the rotations, and route perspectiveCrop through runGeometryEdit.
findings.verdict_reason: runGeometryEdit remaps only when `annotations` is passed (app.ts:3511-3518). trim (3546-3548), revealAll (3538), rotate90, rotate180 and rotateArbitrary (3551-3553) pass none. The Ruler 'Straighten Layer' button calls xform.rotateArbitrary (App.tsx:1431). perspectiveCrop (app.ts:1815-1823) calls e.perspective_crop and then engine.commit() directly: no annotation remap, no markDirty via runGeometryEdit and no requestFit.

findings.title: File ▸ Automate ▸ Crop and Straighten Photos does not straighten
findings.feature: Crop and Straighten Photos
findings.evidence: cropAndStraightenPhotos (app.ts:6653-6660) exports axis-aligned bounding boxes from detect_photo_regions. The engine comment says '(The crop / split is modelled; rotation deskew is not.)' (mod.rs:29750-29753). With no regions found it returns silently, and the regions are exported as 8-bit PNG only (export_region_png).
findings.repro: Scan with two tilted photos: the command opens two tilted crops that include background corners.
findings.impact: The menu item promises something it only half does, and gives no feedback when nothing is detected.
findings.suggested_fix: Relabel or disable it until deskew exists (min-area-rect angle per component, then rotate), and show a toast when no photos are detected.
findings.verdict_reason: cropAndStraightenPhotos (app.ts:6653-6660) exports axis-aligned boxes from detect_photo_regions through export_region_png, and returns silently when fewer than 4 values come back. Both the TS doc comment (6651-6652) and the engine comment (mod.rs:29750-29753) state that rotation deskew is not modelled.

findings.title: Move-tool drags, the Crop tool and Shape/Pen/Frame/Artboard commits are never recorded into Actions
findings.feature: Actions recording for canvas tools
findings.evidence: Only marquee, ellipse, lasso and brush strokes call actions.recordTool (CanvasView.tsx:2171, 2295, 2307; app.ts:782). RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:904-951) contains none of addShapeLayerItems, addShapeLayerFromPath, createFrame, createArtboardRect, setArtboardBounds or addSliceRect. The crop tool calls E.crop directly (CanvasView.tsx:2417-2418) instead of the recorded xform.crop, and the Move drag commits through E.commit_offset (2222).
findings.repro: Start recording an action, then crop with the Crop tool, move a layer, and draw a shape. Stop: the action has no steps for these.
findings.impact: Macros miss the most common layout steps that Photoshop records (Crop, Move, Make shape layer).
findings.suggested_fix: Emit recordTool ops (or call recorded wrappers such as xform.crop and a recorded moveLayerBy) from these commit paths, and add the shape, frame and artboard store methods to RECORDED_STORE_OPS.
findings.verdict_reason: RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:904-951) has no addShapeLayerItems, addShapeLayerFromPath, createFrame, fillFrame, createArtboardRect or addSliceRect. The only actions.recordTool calls are CanvasView.tsx:2171, 2295 and 2307 (lasso and marquees) and app.ts:782 (brush). The Crop tool calls E.crop or E.crop_content_aware directly (CanvasView.tsx:2417-2418) instead of the op-captured xform.crop (app.ts:3536), and the Move drag commits through E.commit_offset (2222) with no recording.

findings.title: Paths to Illustrator omits the Paths panel work path and saved paths
findings.feature: File ▸ Export ▸ Paths to Illustrator
findings.evidence: exportPathsSVG (app.ts:6070-6073) calls E().export_paths_svg(). paths_svg (mod.rs:12084-12160) walks only kind-3 scenes and layer vector_path (vector masks). The work path (store.penPath/penAnchors) and savedPaths live only in the TS store and are never passed in.
findings.repro: Save two named paths in the Paths panel, with no shape layers or vector masks, then Export ▸ Paths to Illustrator. The SVG contains an empty document frame.
findings.impact: The export named after exactly those paths does not include them.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the SVG in TS from savedPaths and the work path (anchors → C segments), merged with the engine's shape and mask output, or pass them into the engine.
findings.verdict_reason: pathstoai (App.tsx:2963) → exportPathsSVG (app.ts:6070-6073) → E().export_paths_svg() → paths_svg (mod.rs:12084-12165), which walks only kind-3 scenes and per-layer vector_path/vector_anchors (vector masks). savedPaths and penPath/penAnchors live only in the TS store, and a grep finds no engine setter for them. With only saved or work paths, the SVG contains no paths.

findings.title: Move tool moves only the active layer when several layers are selected, and its tooltip promises movable guides that cannot be dragged
findings.feature: Move tool
findings.evidence: The drag moves d.layerId = store.state.activeLayerId only (CanvasView.tsx:1166, 1012). commit_offset follows linked siblings only (mod.rs:16720-16741), even though Align/Distribute already use selectedLayerIds. The tool description reads 'Move layers, selections, and guides around the canvas', but there is no guide hit-testing in CanvasView, and the rulers are pointer-events:none (3254, 3267), so guides can be neither dragged out nor moved.
findings.repro: Shift-select two layers in the Layers panel and drag with Move: only one moves. Try dragging a guide: the layer moves instead.
findings.impact: Contradicts the tool's own description and a basic Photoshop workflow.
findings.suggested_fix: Move all selectedLayerIds together (a temporary link set, or one stack-undo move), and implement guide grab/drag on the Move tool, or drop 'guides' from the description.
findings.verdict_reason: The drag uses layerId: store.state.activeLayerId (CanvasView.tsx:1166), and commit_offset follows only linked siblings (mod.rs:16720-16741). The description reads 'Move layers, selections, and guides around the canvas.' (toolRail.ts:11). Guides render as plain SVG lines (CanvasView.tsx:2951-2953), the rulers are pointerEvents:none (around 3254 and 3267), and a grep finds no moveGuide or dragGuide anywhere in src.

findings.title: Count tool Alt-click removes the last marker rather than the one clicked; Eyedropper Alt-click sets the foreground instead of the background
findings.feature: Count tool / Eyedropper
findings.evidence: Count: `if (e.altKey) store.removeLastCountPoint()` (1558-1561; store.ts:3698-3701), even though the comment says 'nearest/last'. Dropper: pointerdown always calls pickColor → setForeground (1539-1542, 2527-2538) and ignores Alt; Photoshop samples the background colour on Alt. The eyedropper also doesn't sample continuously while dragging (no pointermove case).
findings.repro: Place 5 count markers and Alt-click marker #2: #5 disappears. Alt-click with the Eyedropper: the foreground changes.
findings.impact: Small parity surprises in the measure tools.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the nearest marker within the hit radius (as the color sampler does). On Alt, route pickColor to setBackground and add drag sampling.
findings.verdict_reason: Count: `if (e.altKey) store.removeLastCountPoint()` (CanvasView.tsx:1558-1560), which slices off the last marker (store.ts:3699-3701) regardless of position. Dropper: `pickColor(ix, iy)` ignores Alt (1539-1541), and pickColor always calls setForeground (2527-2538). 'dropper' appears only once in CanvasView, so there is no drag sampling.

findings.title: No end-to-end test for the Pen tool's click, drag, close and Shape-mode flow, or for moving and transforming vector or locked type layers
findings.feature: Pen tool; Move/transform on kind-3 and locked layers
findings.evidence: Freeform and curvature pens have specs (freeform-pen.spec.ts, curvature-pen.spec.ts), but no e2e drives the Pen tool itself: its anchor clicks, handle drags, double-click close, Pixels vs Shape commit and tool-switch behaviour. penHandles.test.ts only replays helper maths ('a jsdom pointer-event harness for CanvasView is the upgrade path'). No test moves, aligns or transforms a kind-3 layer and then re-renders or saves it, and none moves a locked type layer. Those gaps are where the blocker and major findings above live.
findings.repro: Use grep: e2e has no setTool("pen"), no penMode, and no vector-layer move or transform assertions.
findings.impact: Regressions in core vector workflows ship undetected.
findings.suggested_fix: Add e2e specs: Pen click/drag/close in each mode plus a tool-switch; Move and Free Transform a Shape-mode rectangle, then invalidate or save-and-reopen and assert the position holds; drag a Lock Position type layer and assert it stays put.
findings.verdict_reason: A grep of e2e finds no selection of the Pen tool: the only '"pen"' hit is pointerType in misc.spec.ts:96, and no spec references penMode. The curvature and freeform pens have specs. No e2e or engine test pairs commit_offset, transform_layer or align with a kind-3 layer; the engine vector tests (mod.rs:40338-40523) cover only vector_translate_item and the anchor tools. No test drags a lock_position type layer.

areas.coverage:
Reviewed by reading code only. No builds or suites were run. The one command I ran was a scratch micro-benchmark under the scratchpad, which imported monet-color's built dist to time the display-LUT pass.

Inventory (in scope):
- **View menu, 71 enabled items with a monetId:**
  - Proof Setup: 16 (14 with a monetId, plus sRGB and Monitor RGB wired by label)
  - Proof Colors, Gamut Warning
  - Pixel Aspect Ratio: 11 (3 management items, 8 presets injected as a checked list, plus Correction)
  - 32-bit Preview Options
  - Zoom: 7 (Zoom In, Zoom Out, Fit, the injected Fit Layer(s), 100%, 200%, Print Size)
  - Screen Mode: 3
  - Extras
  - Show: 15
  - Rulers
  - Snap plus Snap To: 6
  - Lock/Clear/New Guide, New Guide Layout, Guides From Shape, Lock/Clear Slices, Pattern Preview: 8
  - Five duplicate blueprint rows (Fit Artboard, Canvas/Artboard Guides, Clear Selected Artboard/Canvas Guides) are correctly disabled as first-wins duplicates.
- **Color management:** Color Settings (including Working CMYK/Gray/Spot, policies, Advanced), Assign Profile, Convert to Profile, display LUT, ICC soft-proof LUT, gamut overlay, Color Range ▸ Out of Gamut, embedded, missing and paste profile policies across all open paths, Info/Color panel readouts.
- **Print:** File ▸ Print dialog, Print One Copy, src/print.ts, printSettings.ts, engine print_pixels.
- **MCP:** doc.setColorSettings, doc.convertToProfile, print.setSettings, print.oneCopy, view.setProof.

Traced UI → App.tsx menuActions → store.ts → EngineClient.ts → packages/engine (display_lut, proof_lut, assign_profile, convert_to_profile, convert_profile_with_icc_inner, doc_snap, set_document_icc, print_pixels). Also checked the Tauri 2.11.2, wry 0.55.1 and tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1 sources in ~/.cargo for native print and confirm() behaviour.

Tests checked: the e2e specs color-management-profiles, print-settings, pixel-aspect, new-guide, snap-targets, screen-mode, zoom-field, zoom-presets, navigator; the unit tests print, printJob, printSettings, proofProfile, gamutWarningPaint, EngineClient, screenMode, newGuide, snapTargets, zoomPresets, viewTransform, convertToProfileBpcWiring.

Not verified at runtime:
- Native WKWebView print (finding 5).
- The JavaScriptCore cost of the display-LUT pass (finding 6). In Node/V8 it measured about 0.93 s per 24 MP frame.

Areas left to other auditors: Image ▸ Mode conversions themselves, and the Slice tool / Save for Web internals.
areas.parity_notes:
Photoshop items in scope that are correctly shown disabled (no monetId): View ▸ Show ▸ Mesh and Edit Pins. Five duplicate rows (Fit Artboard on Screen, Canvas Guides, Artboard Guides, Clear Selected Artboard Guides, Clear Canvas Guides) are intentionally disabled as duplicates of wired commands.

Photoshop behaviours absent here (not counted as bugs):
- Guides and rulers: no drag-out guides from rulers, no ruler origin reset, no Snap To ▸ Layers/Slices/Artboards, grid has no subdivisions, New Guide Layout has no margins or gutters.
- Zoom: maximum is 3200% (Photoshop allows 12800%).
- Per-window state: Proof Colors, Gamut Warning and 32-bit Preview are app-wide, not per document window.
- Proof Setup: 'Internet Standard RGB' and 'Monitor RGB' are identity even for non-sRGB documents, so they show no simulation there.
- CMYK profiles: only one CMYK ICC profile is bundled (ISO Coated v2).
- Print: printer choice, copies and marks are left to the OS print dialog. Print One Copy still opens the OS dialog.
- MCP: no zoom, guide, gamut-warning or screen-mode commands. doc.setColorSettings cannot set working spaces, policies or intent.

Tests: color management has good coverage for the built-in-profile paths. Gaps: custom-ICC undo, the working CMYK press reaching the display, the native print path (every test stubs print()), and snapping during Move-tool drags.

findings.title: Color Settings ▸ OK silently strips a document's custom embedded ICC profile (e.g. ProPhoto), with no undo
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Color Settings / Assign Profile
findings.evidence: The profile picker's initial value only knows the built-in profiles: useProfileChoice(initial) seeds String(colorProfile) with custom=null (Dialogs.tsx:2702-2733). ColorSettings.ok() calls store.assignProfile(choice.profile, choice.custom?.bytes, choice.custom?.name) unconditionally (Dialogs.tsx:2849-2853). A custom ICC maps to index 0 (monet-color colorManagement.ts:557). In store.assignProfile (store.ts:8078-8087), colorProfile===p but sameBytes(iccBytes, null) is false, so it only calls markDirty() and then sets iccProfileBytes:null and iccProfileName:null. No engine undo step is pushed. syncDocumentIcc(null) also clears the .monetgfx envelope. The Assign Profile dialog (Dialogs.tsx:2929-2933) has the same default.
findings.repro: 1) Open a 16-bit TIFF or PNG with an embedded ProPhoto RGB profile (any non-built-in ICC; for example a Lightroom 'Edit in' export) and keep the embedded profile. 2) Edit ▸ Color Settings (⇧⌘K), change only Intent or nothing, press OK. 3) The canvas colours shift; the status bar profile reads sRGB; ⌘Z does not restore it; Save/Export embeds no ProPhoto profile.
findings.impact: Every file with a non-built-in profile (ProPhoto, camera and scanner profiles) is re-tagged as sRGB by an unrelated dialog. Colours are then wrong on screen and in every saved or exported file, and the change cannot be undone. An untagged document is also silently tagged the same way.
findings.suggested_fix: Seed useProfileChoice with the document's current custom ICC (value CUSTOM_ICC, custom={bytes,name}) when iccProfileBytes is set. In ColorSettings.ok, only call assignProfile when the working-RGB choice actually changed. Make metadata-only profile changes push a history step.
findings.verdict_reason: Traced end to end. A custom ICC opens as profile 0 with bytes (colorManagement.ts:639-642 embeddedFromIccBytes → {profile:0, iccProfileBytes}; profileFromEmbeddedName only knows sRGB/P3/AdobeRGB/Rec.2020). ColorSettings seeds useProfileChoice(store.state.colorProfile) (Dialogs.tsx:2815) with custom=null (2703-2704), so choice.profile=0 and choice.custom=null. ok() calls store.assignProfile(0, undefined, undefined) unconditionally (2849-2850). In assignProfile (store.ts:8070-8089) the early return fails because sameBytes(prophoto, null) is false (store.ts:1318-1322), colorProfile===p, so it takes the markDirty() branch (no engine push, markDirty at 6389 only dirties), then sets iccProfileBytes/iccProfileName null, clears the envelope through syncDocumentIcc, and rebakes the display LUT as plain sRGB. AssignProfile has the same seed (2929-2933). No e2e test covers Color Settings OK on a custom-ICC document.

findings.title: Undoing Convert/Assign Profile with a custom ICC leaves the document tagged with the wrong profile
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Convert to Profile / Assign Profile; open-time 'Convert to Working RGB' policy
findings.evidence: convertToProfile/assignProfile write iccProfileBytes, iccProfileName and colorProfileAssigned into JS state (store.ts:8086, 8166-8170) and into the engine envelope via setDocumentIcc. Undo/redo (store.ts:9932-9945) re-reads only e.doc_profile() in the sync (store.ts:2516), never the ICC bytes. The engine DocSnap (packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:5505-5540) does not snapshot gfx_envelope.icc_profile. Exports embed store.state.iccProfileBytes (app.ts:4626-4629, 4746, 4777). Assign of a custom ICC keeps index 0, so it pushes no undo step at all (store.ts:8080-8085). The e2e test covers undo only for built-in indices (e2e/color-management-profiles.spec.ts:67-81).
findings.repro: A) sRGB document ▸ Convert to Profile ▸ Load Profile… (ProPhoto.icc) ▸ OK ▸ ⌘Z. The pixels are back in sRGB but the document still claims ProPhoto: the canvas looks oversaturated, and Save/Export embeds ProPhoto. B) Open a ProPhoto TIFF with the embedded policy set to 'Convert to Working RGB', then ⌘Z the 'Convert to Profile' state: the ProPhoto numbers are now tagged sRGB. C) Assign a loaded ICC profile, then ⌘Z: an earlier edit is undone and the assignment stays.
findings.impact: Normal undo produces files whose pixel values and embedded profile disagree, so colours are wrong in every other application. Assigning a custom profile cannot be undone at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Make document profile metadata part of history. Either snapshot envelope ICC bytes, name and the assigned flag in DocSnap and read them back in the store sync (documentIcc()/documentIccName()), or record the previous ICC state alongside the engine undo label and restore it on undo/redo. Push an 'Assign Profile' history entry even when only the ICC bytes change.
findings.verdict_reason: DocSnap (engine raster/mod.rs:5504-5540) snapshots profile and mode_profile but not gfx_envelope.icc_profile. Undo/redo/seekHistory (store.ts:9932-9954) re-sync only colorProfile via clampProfile(e.doc_profile()) (2516) and never touch iccProfileBytes/iccProfileName/colorProfileAssigned; no other store path reads them back (grep of store.ts shows only doc-switch, paste and set sites). convertToProfile writes the ICC into JS state after commit (8166-8171). Repro A holds: sRGB→custom-RGB converts with p=0, so undo restores the pixels while the JS ICC stays ProPhoto. Repro B holds: the open policy calls assignProfile(0, prophoto) (no undo step because p is unchanged) and then convertToProfile(0), which pushes an undo and nulls the ICC, so ⌘Z brings back the ProPhoto numbers tagged sRGB. Repro C holds via the markDirty branch (8083-8085). Exports read store.state.iccProfileBytes.

findings.title: Color Settings ▸ Working CMYK (and Gray/Spot) has no effect; proof, print and CMYK export always use ISO Coated v2 while the UI says SWOP
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Color Settings ▸ Working Spaces; View ▸ Proof Setup ▸ Working CMYK; File ▸ Print (Photoshop Manages Colors)
findings.evidence: The #488 fix sends the chosen press through the proof options (store.ts:3592-3600, 3605-3613), but EngineClient.setProof whitelists only simulatePaperColor and simulateBlackInk (EngineClient.ts:500-510). `press` is therefore always undefined in proofPixel, isCmykGamutWarning and outOfGamutMask (EngineClient.ts:629-630, 673). The ICC path, workingCmykProfile() and fetchProofProfile() always load /profiles/ISOcoated_v2_300_eci.icc (store.ts:2576-2586). That file is used by Proof Colors, the print conversion (app.ts:4650), CMYK PSD export (app.ts:3491) and MCP convertToProfile (commands.ts:132-134). The default working CMYK is id 0, 'U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2' (colorManagement.ts:157). The Print dialog hard-codes 'Working CMYK — ISO Coated v2 300% (ECI)' (Dialogs.tsx:5413). workingGray and workingSpot have no consumers outside the dialog. No test asserts that the press reaches the display.
findings.repro: Edit ▸ Color Settings ▸ CMYK = 'U.S. Web Uncoated v2' (its readout shows 22% dot gain and 260% ink) ▸ OK. Then switch View ▸ Proof Setup to Working Cyan Plate and turn on Gamut Warning, or run Color Range ▸ Out of Gamut with the overlay off. The result is identical to Sheetfed Coated. Proof Colors with Working CMYK always shows the FOGRA39 proof.
findings.impact: Prepress users proof, gamut-check, print and export against a different press than the one the UI names. All six CMYK choices and the Gray/Spot choices are inert.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep `press` in EngineClient.setProof. Either select or bundle an ICC profile per working CMYK space and key refreshIccProof on workingCmyk, or relabel the choice to the one profile actually used. Remove or disable the Gray/Spot selectors until something reads them. Add an EngineClient test asserting that the press reaches the display path.
findings.verdict_reason: store.setProof and currentProofOptions add press = cmykWorkingSpace(workingCmyk) (store.ts:3599, 3612), and setColorPolicyPrefs re-pushes it on change (6891-6893). But EngineClient.setProof rebuilds proofOptions with only simulatePaperColor and simulateBlackInk (EngineClient.ts:500-507), so proofOptions.press is always undefined at 629, 630 and 673. proofPixel then falls back to SWOP (monet-color proof.ts:246). The ICC branch always fetches /profiles/ISOcoated_v2_300_eci.icc (store.ts:2576-2586). workingCmykProfile() feeds print (app.ts:4650), CMYK PSD (3491) and MCP (commands.ts:132). The Print dialog hard-codes the ISO Coated label (Dialogs.tsx:5413). workingGray and workingSpot are read only by the dialog's own selects (Dialogs.tsx:2877-2878).

findings.title: View ▸ Snap / Snap To is ignored by the Move tool; only marquee, ellipse and shape commits snap
findings.feature: View ▸ Snap, Snap To ▸ Guides/Grid/Document Bounds
findings.evidence: The Move drag computes mdx/mdy from the pointer and applies only the Smart Guides smartSnap against other layers (CanvasView.tsx:1893-1916). snapToGuides (CanvasView.tsx:3342-3353) is called only by marquee, ellipse and shape pointerdown/move/commit (1685, 1973, 2290, 2301, 2343). snapToGuides also snaps to guides that are hidden (it ignores showGuides and showExtras), while grid snapping requires the grid to be visible (3349). The e2e test snap-targets.spec.ts exercises only the __mv.snap helper, never a layer move.
findings.repro: New Guide (vertical at 100 px); View ▸ Snap on, Snap To ▸ Guides and Document Bounds on; select a layer; drag it with the Move tool so its left edge passes x=100 or the canvas edge: it does not snap.
findings.impact: The main use of guides and Snap To (aligning layers while moving them) does nothing even though the menu items are enabled. Hidden guides still pull marquee edges.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply snapToGuides-style snapping to the moving layer's bounds (edges and centres) in the Move-tool drag, before or alongside smartSnap. Gate guide snapping on showGuides && showExtras, as the grid already is.
findings.verdict_reason: The Move pointermove path (CanvasView.tsx:1884-1916) applies only smartSnap against other layers' bounds, and flushMove (1004-1015) passes dx/dy straight to move_layer_offset. snapToGuides/axisSnapTargets have no other callers (1685, 1973, 2290, 2301, 2343 and the __mv.snap hook in main.tsx:74-77). axisSnapTargets (snapTargets.ts) adds guide positions whenever targets.guides is set and never checks showGuides/showExtras, while grid snapping requires showGrid && showExtras (CanvasView.tsx:3349). snap-targets.spec.ts tests only the __mv.snap helper. Snapping does work for marquee and shapes, so Snap is not completely inert. Major is kept because moving layers is the main snapping workflow.

findings.title: File ▸ Print and Print One Copy likely do nothing in the macOS desktop app (iframe print() is a no-op in WKWebView)
findings.feature: File ▸ Print…, File ▸ Print One Copy, MCP print.oneCopy
findings.evidence: printPng prints by calling print() on a hidden iframe (print.ts:17-58). WKWebView only prints when its UI delegate implements the private printFrame callback, and wry 0.55.1 does not implement it (no printFrame in src/wkwebview). Tauri 2.11.2 works around this by overriding window.print for macOS through js_init_script (webview/plugin.rs:200-203, scripts/print.js), which is main-frame-only (plugin.rs js_init_script → for_main_frame_only: true), so the iframe's contentWindow.print is not overridden. Even that override would need `core:webview:allow-print`, which capabilities/default.json does not grant (core:webview:default excludes it). The e2e and unit tests replace the iframe's print() with a stub (e2e/print-settings.spec.ts:10-11, print.test.ts:46), so native printing is never exercised.
findings.repro: pnpm dev:vision on macOS, open any image, File ▸ Print One Copy (or File ▸ Print… ▸ Print). Expected: the macOS print sheet. Likely result: nothing appears, no error is shown, and MCP print.oneCopy reports 'Sent the document to the print dialog'. Confirm by running exactly this in the native build.
findings.impact: Printing, an advertised File-menu workflow with a full settings dialog, silently fails on the primary desktop platform.
findings.suggested_fix: Print natively. Either render the prepared PNG and page CSS in a dedicated hidden webview window and call Tauri's Webview::print there (granting core:webview:allow-print), or add a small native plugin that prints the image with NSPrintOperation. At minimum, detect the macOS no-op and report it instead of claiming success.
findings.verdict_reason: The code-level chain checks out. printPng calls printWindow.print() on an about:blank iframe (print.ts:14-58). wry 0.55.1 has no printFrame UI-delegate method: its only print path is WKWebView::print/printOperationWithPrintInfo (wkwebview/mod.rs:858-873). Tauri 2.11.2 adds scripts/print.js (window.print → plugin:webview|print) only through Builder::js_init_script, which sets for_main_frame_only: true (plugin.rs:370-374), so the iframe's print is not overridden. core:webview:default grants only get-all-webviews/position/size/toggle-devtools (reference.md), and capabilities/default.json does not add allow-print. Vision has no native print command (src-tauri/src). Both tests stub print(). The last step, that WebKit's subframe print() does nothing without the private UI delegate, is known WKWebView behaviour (the reason Tauri ships print.js) but cannot be proven by reading code. One native run of File ▸ Print One Copy settles it.

findings.title: Non-sRGB documents (Display P3, Adobe RGB, custom ICC) pay about 1 s of main-thread JS per full repaint (display LUT applied per pixel on every commit)
findings.feature: Color management display compensation; Proof Colors / Gamut Warning
findings.evidence: applyDisplayRect runs sampleDisplayLut or sampleProofLut per pixel in JS, allocating an array for every pixel (EngineClient.ts:592-645). blit() calls it over the full document (EngineClient.ts:682-707), and commit() calls blit() on every edit, undo, visibility toggle and live-preview frame (EngineClient.ts:855-869). Any tagged non-sRGB document keeps displayLut set (setDisplayProfile, EngineClient.ts:571-584), and iPhone HEIC files open as Display P3 (app.ts:7150-7154). Scratch benchmark of the same sampleDisplayLut over 6000×4000 pixels in Node: 928 ms per pass.
findings.repro: Open a 24 MP Display P3 or Adobe RGB photo, for example an iPhone HEIC. Paint a stroke, toggle a layer's visibility, or drag an adjustment dialog slider. Each commit or preview frame stalls for about 1 s (the same happens for any document with Proof Colors or Gamut Warning on).
findings.impact: Editing is sluggish for the most common photographic colour spaces, and live adjustment previews become about 1 fps.
findings.suggested_fix: Do the 3D-LUT pass in WASM (the engine already builds the LUT) or on the GPU, for example a WebGL shader or CSS color-space presentation. In JS at least, inline the trilinear sample without per-pixel allocations and repaint only the dirty rectangle.
findings.verdict_reason: setDisplayProfile keeps displayLut set for any assigned non-sRGB or custom-ICC document (EngineClient.ts:569-582). blit() copies the whole buffer and calls applyDisplayRect(0,0,w,h) (682-707). applyDisplayRect calls sampleDisplayLut per pixel, which allocates an out array and a closure per call (displayLut.ts:22-47), and destructures the result (EngineClient.ts:592-645). commit() calls blit() on every non-geometry commit (EngineClient.ts:823-839), and live previews go through commit. The HEIC path runs the embedded-profile policy (app.ts:7145-7157). A scratch Node benchmark of the same sampleDisplayLut over 6000×4000 took 1.19-1.51 s per pass on this machine. Brush dabs use blitRegion (dirty rect only), so the stall lands at stroke end, on toggles, undo and preview frames rather than on every dab.

findings.title: Guides cannot be dragged, moved or deleted individually; Lock Guides does nothing; guide edits are not undoable
findings.feature: View ▸ Lock Guides / Clear Guides / New Guide / New Guide Layout / Rulers
findings.evidence: lockguides toggles guidesLocked (App.tsx:3322), and nothing ever reads it (the only other references are store.ts:1093 and 1564). The rulers are pointerEvents:'none' SVGs (CanvasView.tsx:3252-3276), so a guide cannot be dragged out of them. The guide lines sit inside a non-interactive SVG (2940-2954). There is no move or delete path anywhere (no moveGuide or removeGuide). setGuides and clearGuides only mark the document dirty (store.ts:3547-3578). Guides are JS state outside the engine's DocSnap, so ⌘Z cannot restore them. New Guide does not turn guides visible (Dialogs.tsx:6720), unlike Guide Layout (6755) and From Shape (store.ts:3586).
findings.repro: Build a guide layout, then View ▸ Clear Guides, then ⌘Z: the guides are not restored (an earlier pixel edit is undone instead). Try to drag a guide from the ruler or move an existing one: impossible. Toggle Lock Guides: nothing changes.
findings.impact: A mistaken guide can only be removed by clearing all guides, and that cannot be undone. Lock Guides is a dead toggle. Photoshop records New Guide, Move Guide and Clear Guides as history states.
findings.suggested_fix: Record guide changes as history entries (push_history plus a JS guide snapshot per undo index, or keep guides in the engine's DocSnap). Add ruler drag-out and Move-tool guide dragging and deletion that honour guidesLocked, or disable Lock Guides until then.
findings.verdict_reason: guidesLocked is written by App.tsx:3322 and never read (store.ts:1093 and 1564 are its only other hits). The rulers and the guide SVG are pointerEvents:'none' (CanvasView.tsx:3252, 3266, 2940), and no move, remove or drag guide path exists. setGuides and clearGuides only markDirty and push the guides to e.set_guides (store.ts:2357-2367, 3547-3578). The engine keeps guides only for PSD export and not in DocSnap, and undo never reads them back. New Guide does not force showGuides (Dialogs.tsx New Guide OK) while Guide Layout does. Re-graded to minor: showGuides defaults to true; Lock Guides is inert but harmless because nothing can move a guide; and the lost state is guide metadata, not pixels. Missing ruler drag-out is a parity gap more than a regression.

findings.title: View ▸ Zoom In/Out, 100%, 200%, Print Size, the status-bar zoom field and the Navigator slider zoom about the image's top-left corner, not the view centre
findings.feature: View ▸ Zoom In (⌘+), Zoom Out (⌘-), 100% (⌘1), 200%, Print Size; zoom field; Navigator slider
findings.evidence: zoomBy calls setZoom(zoom*factor), which keeps panX and panY (store.ts:2818-2821, 10089-10091). Pan is the screen offset of the document origin (viewTransform.ts:26-28), so scaling pivots on the document's top-left. Callers: App.tsx:3242-3243, 3300, 3305, 3330, 1517, and Panels.tsx:2086. By contrast, setPaneZoom already centres through matchedView (store.ts:2846-2851), and the toolbar 100% button uses the centred requestZoom('actual') while the menu's 100% item does not (App.tsx:1446 vs 3330).
findings.repro: Open a large image, fit it, zoom into the lower-right area, then press ⌘+ or ⌘-, or type 300 into the zoom field: the view jumps toward the image's top-left instead of staying on what you were looking at.
findings.impact: The most frequently used view commands lose the user's place and force a pan after every step. The same command (100%) behaves differently from the menu and from the toolbar.
findings.suggested_fix: Route these callers through a centre-anchored helper, reusing matchedView/zoomAt with the viewport centre (and pixel-aspect ratio), like setPaneZoom.
findings.verdict_reason: zoomBy → setZoom(zoom*factor) with no pan (store.ts:10089-10091). setZoom changes pan only when pan is passed (2818-2821). Callers pass no pan: App.tsx:3242-3243 (zi/zo), 3300 (zoom200), 3305 (printsize), 3330 (actual), the zoom field at App.tsx:1517 and the Navigator slider at Panels.tsx:2086. No CanvasView effect re-anchors on a zoom change: its only setZoom calls are fit/fill/actual (570, 588, 597) and zoomAt for wheel and Zoom-tool clicks (1599, 2723). setPaneZoom centres through matchedView (2846-2851). The toolbar 100% goes through requestZoom('actual'), which centres the document (597), while the menu 100% does not. These are the most-used view commands, so major is kept.

findings.title: Slices, Count markers and Color Samplers are app-global, not per-document: they leak across tabs, and Save for Web slices another document
findings.feature: View ▸ Show ▸ Slices/Count/Color Samplers, View ▸ Clear Slices / Lock Slices
findings.evidence: When the active document changes, the per-document stash saves guides, notes, pixel-aspect ratio and so on, but not slices, countPoints or colorSamplers (store.ts:4626-4653). These live only in the global snapshot (store.ts:1116-1140). saveForWeb slices whatever store.state.slices holds (app.ts:5321-5323). clearSlices does not mark the document dirty and cannot be undone (store.ts:4337-4339).
findings.repro: Draw slices, Count markers or Color Samplers on document A, then switch to tab B: they are drawn over B, the Info panel reads B's pixels at A's sampler points, and File ▸ Save for Web on B exports B cut into A's slices.
findings.impact: Wrong exports and misleading measurements whenever more than one document is open.
findings.suggested_fix: Stash and restore slices, slicesLocked, countPoints and colorSamplers per document like guides and notes (and persist them in the project envelope). Make Clear Slices dirty the document and undoable.
findings.verdict_reason: captureActiveView stashes guides, notes and more but not slices, slicesLocked, countPoints or colorSamplers (store.ts:4625-4653). activateDoc's restore set() does not reset them either (6192-6215). No doc-change path clears them: the only resets are the explicit clear commands at 3704, 4250 and 4338. saveForWeb reads the global store.state.slices (app.ts:5321-5323), and clearSlices does not dirty the document or record history (4338). Re-graded to minor: the single-document common path works, and the leak is visible on screen because A's slices and samplers draw over B. No data loss.

findings.title: Color-policy 'Ask' prompts never appear in the desktop app: confirm() returns a Promise, so open and paste decisions are forced
findings.feature: Color Settings policies: Embedded / Missing / Paste profile = Ask
findings.evidence: tauri-plugin-dialog's init script replaces window.confirm with an async function that calls an unregistered command. The team documents this at app.ts:576-586 (#480) and routes Actions through plugin-dialog's ask(). The colour-policy prompts still call confirm() synchronously (app.ts:7379, 7398; store.ts:6645-6650). A Promise is truthy, so on desktop: embedded mismatch always preserves, missing-profile 'Ask' always assigns working RGB and never leaves untagged, paste mismatch always converts. No dialog is shown, and each call leaves an unhandled rejection.
findings.repro: Native app with the default 'Ask When Opening' policy: open a Display P3 PNG while the working RGB is Adobe RGB. No prompt appears and the profile is preserved. Set Missing = Ask and open an untagged PNG: it is always assigned working RGB.
findings.impact: Users cannot choose convert on open or leave a file untagged when the policy is Ask, the default embedded-profile policy. The e2e tests pass only in Chromium, where confirm() is synchronous.
findings.suggested_fix: Make applyOpenedImageProfilePolicy and prepareClipboardForPaste async and use @tauri-apps/plugin-dialog ask() on desktop, as confirmPlaybackPause does. The same pattern affects App.tsx:2158 and app.ts:8106.
findings.verdict_reason: tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1's init-iife.js sets window.confirm = async function(...) invoking plugin:dialog|confirm, and the plugin registers only open/save/message (lib.rs:198-202), so the call rejects. Vision registers the plugin (main.rs:327 monet_ui::dialog_plugin). app.ts:7379 and 7398 and store.ts:6645-6650 use the synchronous confirm() result, and a Promise is truthy, so embedded Ask always preserves, missing Ask always assigns, and paste Ask always converts. The team already works around this for Actions (app.ts:575-586). Minor is right: the forced answers match Photoshop's pre-selected defaults, and the default missing-profile policy is assign-working, not ask.

findings.title: 'Working RGB' is just the active document's profile: not persisted, and open-time conversions target whichever document was last active
findings.feature: Color Settings ▸ Working RGB; embedded/missing profile policies; New Document default
findings.evidence: Every open path reads `workingProfile = store.state.colorProfile` from the currently active document (app.ts:6950, 7070, 7115, 7143, 7171, 7234, 7250, 7289, 7325, 8025). Color Settings OK assigns the chosen working RGB to the active document (Dialogs.tsx:2849-2853); ColorPolicyPrefs deliberately has no workingRgb field (colorManagement.ts:124-125), so it is never persisted. New Document defaults to sRGB whenever any document is open (Dialogs.tsx:5753).
findings.repro: Set Embedded policy = Convert to Working RGB. With a Rec.2020 document active, open an Adobe RGB JPEG: it is converted to Rec.2020. Restart the app: Color Settings shows sRGB whatever was chosen before.
findings.impact: Pixel conversions on open depend on which tab happened to be active. Changing the working space reinterprets the open document, which Photoshop never does.
findings.suggested_fix: Store workingRgb (and optionally custom working ICC) in ColorPolicyPrefs and use it for policies and New Document. Stop assigning it to the active document from Color Settings.
findings.verdict_reason: Every open path captures workingProfile = store.state.colorProfile from the active document before opening (app.ts:6950, 7070, 7115, 7143, 7171, 7234, 7250, 7289, 7325, 8025), and convertToWorkingRgb converts to it (7360-7363). ColorPolicyPrefs has no workingRgb field (colorManagement.ts:124-127), and only the .csf file stores it. New Document defaults to 0 when documents are open (Dialogs.tsx:5753). This is a documented design choice (the dialog's own footnote), but tab-dependent conversion on open is a real wrong-result.

findings.title: Fit on Screen, Fill and Fit Layer ignore the pixel aspect ratio correction
findings.feature: View ▸ Fit on Screen / Fit Layer(s) / Zoom tool Fill; Pixel Aspect Ratio Correction
findings.evidence: The fitNonce and zoomCmd effects compute fitZoom/fillZoom(vp.w, vp.h, docW, docH) and centre using docW*z (CanvasView.tsx:584-599). fitLayer uses fitRectView without par (store.ts:10071-10081). The content transform, however, scales x by zoom*parX (CanvasView.tsx:343, 2787-2805).
findings.repro: View ▸ Pixel Aspect Ratio ▸ Anamorphic 2:1, then ⌘0: the image is twice the viewport width, cut off and off-centre.
findings.impact: Fit commands are wrong for any non-square pixel aspect ratio.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass docW*par into fitZoom/fillZoom and centre with the stretched width. Refit when the aspect ratio changes.
findings.verdict_reason: The fitNonce and zoomCmd effects compute fitZoom/fillZoom(vp, docW, docH) and centre with docW*z (CanvasView.tsx:584-599). fitLayer uses fitRectView without par (store.ts:10071-10081). The content transform stretches x by parX = pixelAspect when correction is on (CanvasView.tsx:341-343). setPaneZoom already passes par, which shows the omission elsewhere.

findings.title: Guides, notes and color samplers are not remapped by Image Rotation, Flip Canvas, Trim or Reveal All
findings.feature: Guides / Notes / Color Samplers after geometry edits
findings.evidence: runGeometryEdit remaps annotations only when given a scale or offset (app.ts:3496-3520). rotate90, rotate180 and rotateArbitrary pass none (3551-3553); trim and revealAll pass none (3538, 3546); flipH and flipV skip runGeometryEdit entirely (3549-3550).
findings.repro: Add a vertical guide at x=100 on a 1000×500 document, then Image ▸ Image Rotation ▸ 90° CW: the guide stays vertical at x=100 instead of becoming horizontal at y=100. Trim the top-left border: guides do not shift.
findings.impact: The guide layout no longer matches the content after common canvas operations.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend remapDocSpaceAnnotations with rotate and flip mappings (swap orientation for 90°) and pass trim and reveal-all offsets, which the engine can report.
findings.verdict_reason: runGeometryEdit remaps only when an annotations argument is given (app.ts:3496-3521). trim (3544-3546), revealAll (3538), rotate90, rotate180 and rotateArbitrary (3551-3553) pass none, and flipH/flipV bypass it entirely (3549-3550). remapDocSpaceAnnotations supports only scale and offset (store.ts:3560-3574).

findings.title: View toggles show no checkmarks (Proof Colors, Gamut Warning, Rulers, Snap, Lock Guides, Extras, Show ▸ *, Screen Mode, Proof Setup)
findings.feature: View menu state
findings.evidence: The checkedIds set passed to buildPhotoshopMenus contains only OpenType, imageassets and the image mode/depth ids (App.tsx:3506-3510). psMenus.ts:385 marks items checked only from that set. Only the injected pixel-aspect presets carry their own checkmark.
findings.repro: Toggle View ▸ Snap or Lock Guides and reopen the View menu: there is no indication whether it is on.
findings.impact: Several of these toggles have no other on-screen indicator (Snap, Lock Guides, Proof Setup choice).
findings.suggested_fix: Add the store booleans (proofOn, gamutWarningOn, showRulers, snapEnabled, snapGuides, snapGrid, snapDocBounds, guidesLocked, showExtras, show*, slicesLocked, pixelAspectCorrection, patternPreview), the screen mode id and the proof mode id to checkedIds.
findings.verdict_reason: checkedIds passed to buildPhotoshopMenus holds only OpenType keys, imageassets and imageModeCheckedIds (App.tsx:3506-3510). psMenus.ts:385 sets item.checked only from that set; the other checked sources are the injected pixel-aspect, measure-scale and Window items (psMenus.ts:254, 364, 461, 502). App.tsx has no view-state relabeling (proofOn, snapEnabled and guidesLocked appear only in the toggle actions).

findings.title: Color Range ▸ Out of Gamut selects different pixels depending on whether Proof Colors or Gamut Warning happens to be on
findings.feature: Select ▸ Color Range ▸ Out of Gamut
findings.evidence: outOfGamutMask uses the ICC LUT when one is installed and otherwise the SWOP heuristic (EngineClient.ts:664-676). The LUT is baked only while proofOn or gamutWarningOn (store.ts:2591, 2600). The doc comment claims the result is independent of the overlay.
findings.repro: Run Color Range ▸ Out of Gamut with Gamut Warning off, then again with it on: the selections differ (heuristic vs FOGRA39 ICC).
findings.impact: The selection is not reproducible and does not match what the overlay shows.
findings.suggested_fix: Bake or fetch the proof LUT on demand in outOfGamutSelect, independent of the view toggles.
findings.verdict_reason: outOfGamutMask uses iccProofLut when it is set and otherwise isCmykGamutWarning (EngineClient.ts:664-676). refreshIccProof installs the LUT only when want = (proofMode cmyk or custom) && (proofOn || gamutWarningOn), and otherwise sets it to null (store.ts:2587-2600). The doc comment's claim of independence from the overlay (EngineClient.ts:657-663) is therefore false.

findings.title: Rulers ignore Preferences ▸ Units & Rulers and zoom (fixed 50 px ticks; labels overlap when zoomed out)
findings.feature: View ▸ Rulers
findings.evidence: Rulers draw a tick every 50 document pixels and label every 100 pixels regardless of zoom or unit (CanvasView.tsx:3252-3276). The preferences pane labels the setting 'Rulers' and admits the on-canvas rulers still read pixels (Dialogs.tsx:1748-1750).
findings.repro: Set Units & Rulers = Inches and zoom a 6000 px image to 10%: the ruler shows overlapping pixel labels every 10 screen px.
findings.impact: The rulers are unreadable at low zoom and ignore the unit preference.
findings.suggested_fix: Choose the tick step from zoom (1/2/5×10ⁿ in the chosen unit via convertDocumentLength) and render only the visible range.
findings.verdict_reason: The ruler loops step dx/dy by 50 document pixels and label every 100 (CanvasView.tsx:3257-3262, 3270-3274), with no zoom-dependent step and no unit conversion. They iterate over the whole document, not the visible range. The Units & Rulers pane comment admits the rulers still read pixels (Dialogs.tsx:1748-1750).

findings.title: Extras (⌘H) does not hide Slices, Notes, Count, Color Samplers or Smart Guides
findings.feature: View ▸ Extras
findings.evidence: Grid, pixel grid, layer edges, guides, selection edges and target path are gated on showExtras (CanvasView.tsx:383-402, 661), but the slices, count, samplers and notes overlays are not (3140, 3190, 3203, 3220), and Smart Guides are not during a move (1897).
findings.repro: Place notes and color samplers, then press ⌘H: they stay visible.
findings.impact: ⌘H does not give a clean view of the image as Photoshop's does.
findings.suggested_fix: AND these overlays with showExtras.
findings.verdict_reason: The extras action only toggles showExtras (App.tsx:3246). Grid, pixel grid, layer edges, guides, selection edges and target path are ANDed with showExtras (CanvasView.tsx:384-386, 402, 661, 2978, 3018, 3038, 3085). showCount, showSamplers, showNotes, showSlices (346-353) and showSmartGuides (387) are not, and their overlays render on those flags alone (3140, 3190, 3203, 3220). Minor or polish.

findings.title: Color panel, pickers and Info CMYK/Lab readouts ignore the document profile and working CMYK
findings.feature: Color panel / Info panel readouts in managed documents
findings.evidence: The Info panel converts to Lab with an sRGB matrix (rgbToLab, monet-photo rgbLab.ts:39-48) and to CMYK with naive 1−max UCR (rgbToCmyk, rgbCmyk.ts:13-25), regardless of the document profile or working CMYK (Panels.tsx:3181-3187). The foreground/background swatches and the ColorPicker paint the raw numbers as CSS sRGB (Panels.tsx:1369-1376), while the canvas is display-compensated through the document profile (EngineClient.setDisplayProfile).
findings.repro: In an Adobe RGB or Display P3 document, eyedrop a saturated colour: the swatch looks different from the same colour on the canvas. The Info CMYK for mid-grey 128 reads 0/0/0/50, not a press separation.
findings.impact: Colour values and swatches are misleading in managed documents, and the CMYK readouts do not match the CMYK conversions Vision actually performs.
findings.suggested_fix: Route swatch previews through the same display LUT, derive Lab via the document profile, and derive CMYK via the working CMYK transform (the engine already exposes pick_cmyk and pick_lab paths).
findings.verdict_reason: For non-Lab and non-CMYK documents, the Info panel uses rgbToLab and rgbToCmyk on the picked RGB (Panels.tsx:3181-3187), with no document profile or working CMYK involved. The engine pick_lab/pick_cmyk run only in Lab and CMYK mode. The swatches use hsvToHex(fg/bg) as CSS (Panels.tsx:1370-1371), while the canvas is display-compensated through setDisplayProfile.

findings.title: Assign Profile and Convert to Profile are not macro-recordable
findings.feature: Actions recording of Edit ▸ Assign/Convert to Profile
findings.evidence: RECORDED_STORE_OPS includes the Image ▸ Mode conversions (convertGrayscale, setColorMode, setDepth) but not assignProfile or convertToProfile (app.ts:904-951). The dialogs call store methods directly (Dialogs.tsx:2932, 2984).
findings.repro: Record an action, run Edit ▸ Convert to Profile ▸ sRGB, stop recording: the action has no step.
findings.impact: 'Convert to sRGB' batch actions, a staple web-export macro, cannot be recorded.
findings.suggested_fix: Add assignProfile and convertToProfile to RECORDED_STORE_OPS. Custom ICC bytes need a serializable encoding, for example base64.
findings.verdict_reason: The RECORDED_STORE_OPS list (app.ts:904-951) includes convertGrayscale, setColorMode and setDepth but not assignProfile or convertToProfile. Only listed names are wrapped with recordedCall (app.ts:971-974). The dialogs call the store methods directly, and no other recording hook references either name.

findings.title: View ▸ New Guides From Shape uses the pixel selection, not the selected shape layer
findings.feature: View ▸ New Guides From Shape
findings.evidence: guidesFromShape reads engine.selection_bounds() and returns silently when nothing is selected (store.ts:3580-3587).
findings.repro: Draw a rectangle shape layer, deselect all, View ▸ New Guides From Shape: nothing happens.
findings.impact: The command does nothing in its named use case, with no feedback.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the active shape or vector layer's bounds (vector_item_bounds or active_layer_bounds), falling back to the selection.
findings.verdict_reason: guidesFromShape reads engine.selection_bounds() and returns silently when w or h is ≤ 0 (store.ts:3580-3583). It never looks at the active shape or vector layer's bounds.

findings.title: MCP view.setProof accepts any string and enables a no-op proof
findings.feature: MCP view.setProof
findings.evidence: setProofMode forwards `mode` unvalidated to store.setProof, which sets proofOn=true and proofMode=<anything> (commands.ts:956-966, store.ts:3605-3626). proofPixel's switch then falls through to identity.
findings.repro: MCP view.setProof { mode: "cmky" } returns 'Proof mode set to cmky'; Proof Colors is on but nothing is proofed.
findings.impact: The MCP client is told it succeeded when nothing was proofed.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate against the ProofMode ids, plus 'custom' only when a device profile is loaded, and throw otherwise.
findings.verdict_reason: setProofMode forwards mode unvalidated (commands.ts:960-966). store.setProof sets proofOn=true and proofMode=mode (store.ts:3615-3626). An unknown id matches no case in proofPixel's switch (proof.ts:245-275), so the pixels come back unchanged, and the command still returns 'Proof mode set to …'.

areas.coverage:
Code review only. I ran no tests, builds or suites and changed no files.

What I inventoried and traced:
- Window menu, built in psMenus.ts:451-517. Arrange has 13 commands. Workspace has 6 built-in workspaces plus Save, Reset Panels and Delete. There is the Contextual Task Bar toggle, 23 panel toggles and the open-document list.
- Help menu: About, System Info, Keyboard Shortcuts. I also read the native macOS app, Window and Help menus that mac-menu.ts builds.
- All 23 registered panels (App.tsx:3381-3405), from their UI entry through state/app.ts and store.ts, into the engine where it mattered: Layers, Color, Adjustments, Properties, History (with snapshots), Actions, Measurement Log, Info, Histogram (with scopes), Channels (alpha, spot and Quick Mask channels), Navigator, Second View, Animation (with the timeline), Notes, Swatches, Libraries, Brushes (which also holds the Brush Settings dynamics, Tool Presets and Brush Tips), Clone Source, Styles, Paths, Layer Comps, Character, Paragraph.
- Workspaces: built-ins, save/apply/reset/delete and storage in localStorage.
- CustomizeToolbar and ExtraTools.
- Contextual task bar and status bar.
- Document tabs and the name-based tab mapping.
- Window ▸ Arrange: Second View panel, Match View, and the float windows (FloatWindows.tsx, float.rs, capabilities/float.json).
- Edit ▸ Menus… hide pipeline and shortcut dispatch.
- Native popups: native-popup.tsx and monet-ui popup.rs, including the new-window hook, command registration and key forwarding.
- macOS native menu bridge (mac-menu.ts).
- Dock layout helpers: openPanel/closePanel, floats, LayerList keyboard navigation.
- Tauri dialog plugin behaviour, read from the local crate source: wry 0.55.1 WKUIDelegate and tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1 init script and command list.

I also grepped unit and e2e tests for each area.

Not reviewed in depth:
- float.tsx input replay line by line.
- dockable-core drop and split algorithms.
- Popup placement across multiple monitors.
- Every store method behind the less-used panel buttons: spot-channel engine ops, frame FX, timeline render.
- Runtime behaviour on WKWebView. The prompt() and confirm() conclusions come from the wry and tauri-plugin-dialog sources, not from running the app.
areas.parity_notes:
Photoshop items that Vision leaves out or folds into other surfaces. None of these are reported as bugs:
- **Panels not in Window:**
  - Merged into other panels:
    - Brush Settings (inside Brushes).
    - Tool Presets (inside Brushes).
    - Timeline (inside Animation).
  - Glyphs is a modal dialog (Type ▸ Panels ▸ Glyphs).
  - Gradients and Patterns exist only inside the Preset Manager.
  - Absent entirely:
    - 3D
    - Learn
    - Comments
    - Shapes
    - Device Preview
    - Modifier Keys
    - Discover
  - Photoshop's F5–F9 panel shortcuts are not bound.
- **Help menu:** only About, System Info and Keyboard Shortcuts. There is no user guide, online help, What's New or update check. On macOS, About is the stock NSApp panel, not Vision's About dialog.
- **Workspaces:**
  - The workspace captures panels, toolbar placement, the tool arrangement and custom shortcuts, but not the Edit ▸ Menus… hidden set. The ponytail comment at App.tsx:284 saying no menu-customization feature exists is now stale.
  - There is no 3D workspace.
  - 'Reset Panels' is used in place of 'Reset <Workspace>'.
- **History:** no non-linear history (deliberately absent) and no per-state thumbnails.
- **Other panels:**
  - Layer Comps: New Layer Comp has no options dialog.
  - Paths: saved paths cannot be renamed.
  - Channel Options has no Name field.
- **Window ▸ Arrange:** tiling and New Window are an in-dock 'Second View' panel, not OS windows. Float in Window, Float All and Cascade are real OS windows on desktop only.
- **Menus with no disabled placeholders:** psMenuData.ts has no Window or Help menu; both are generated in psMenus.ts, so they contain no disabled Photoshop placeholders.
- **Test-coverage notes:**
  - windowMenu.test.ts:66-75 asserts the counting that causes the close-background-tab bug.
  - The e2e workspace and prompt flows pass only because Chromium implements prompt().
  - No test covers Layers-panel keyboard navigation, undo after a snapshot restore, or History States edited key by key.

findings.title: Clicking a History snapshot replaces the document and wipes all undo history — one click irreversibly loses current work
findings.feature: History panel ▸ Snapshots (restore)
findings.evidence: Panels.tsx:2718 snapshot row onClick={() => store.restoreSnapshot(s.id)} (no confirm). store.ts:7302-7307 restoreSnapshot → revertActiveDoc(this.engine.buildProject(snap.bytes), …, { dirty: true }). revertActiveDoc swaps in a brand-new engine (store.ts:6052 d.engine = eng; the old engine is not kept) and clears history (6054 d.historyLabels = []; 6090 and 6117 history: []). It also calls fit() and resets layerColorLabels (6100). No snapshot of the pre-restore state is taken. e2e/history-snapshots.spec.ts only checks the restored composite, never undo afterwards.
findings.repro: Open an image; Autofirst snapshot exists by default. Make 20 edits. In History panel click the auto snapshot row (as Photoshop users do to compare), then try Edit ▸ Undo or click the last history state.
findings.impact: All edits since the snapshot are gone and cannot be undone. The History list is empty and Undo is disabled. In Photoshop, clicking a snapshot is a reversible navigation, so users click snapshot rows routinely.
findings.suggested_fix: Make restore an undoable history step on the existing engine: push_history('Snapshot') and then load the snapshot's layers into it. At minimum, auto-snapshot the current state before replacing it, or ask for confirmation. Add an e2e test that undoes a restore.
findings.verdict_reason: Panels.tsx:2715-2718: the snapshot row's onClick calls store.restoreSnapshot(s.id) with no confirm. store.ts:7302-7307 calls revertActiveDoc(buildProject(snap.bytes), ..., {dirty:true}), which swaps in the new engine (d.engine = eng), clears d.historyLabels and sets history: [] twice. Nothing snapshots the pre-restore state. autoFirstSnapshot defaults to true (store.ts:708) and is taken on open (store.ts:4868), so the row exists by default. The doc comment says the history reset is deliberate ('Like Revert, this resets the linear history'). Photoshop keeps the states after a snapshot click until the next edit, so the net effect is unrecoverable loss of every edit since the snapshot from a single click. I kept blocker for a Photoshop-class editor. If the team rates deliberate, labelled 'Restore' behaviour lower, the floor is major (cannot be undone).

findings.title: Save Workspace…, Delete Workspace…, Actions ▸ + Stop and the New Snapshot name prompt do nothing in the desktop app (window.prompt returns null in WKWebView)
findings.feature: Window ▸ Workspace ▸ Save/Delete; Actions panel Insert Stop; History New Snapshot…
findings.evidence: App.tsx:2665 savews and App.tsx:2683 delws get their names only from prompt(). Panels.tsx:2557 (Insert Stop) and Panels.tsx:2647 (New Snapshot, when 'Show New Snapshot Dialog by Default' is on) do the same and return when the result is null. wry-0.55.1 src/wkwebview/class/wry_web_view_ui_delegate.rs implements only runOpenPanel, requestMediaCapturePermission and createWebView. It has no runJavaScriptTextInputPanel, so WKWebView answers prompt() with null. The codebase already knows this: Panels.tsx:1802 says 'No prompt(): the desktop webview has none'. e2e/panel-views.spec.ts:142 and shortcut-sets.spec.ts:184 accept Chromium's prompt, which masks the bug (AGENTS: e2e does not drive WKWebView).
findings.repro: In the macOS app: Window ▸ Workspace ▸ Save Workspace… → nothing happens, no workspace is added. Delete Workspace… does the same. Actions panel ▸ expand an action ▸ '＋ Stop' → nothing is inserted.
findings.impact: User workspaces can be neither created nor deleted in the shipped desktop build. Insert Stop is dead, and New Snapshot silently does nothing when its dialog option is on.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace prompt() with an in-app Dialog plus Input for name entry. The Layer Comp Options dialog is a pattern to copy. For Delete Workspace, show a list or Select of the custom workspaces. Add a lint rule or test banning bare prompt() in src/.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:2665 (savews), App.tsx:2683 (delws), Panels.tsx:2557 (Insert Stop) and Panels.tsx:2647 (New Snapshot) are the only prompt() sites, and all of them return on null or empty. wry 0.55.1 (the version in Cargo.lock) has a WKUIDelegate that implements only windowWillClose, runOpenPanel, requestMediaCapturePermission and createWebView. It lacks runJavaScriptTextInputPanel, so WebKit treats prompt() as Cancel and returns null. tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1's init-iife.js overrides only alert and confirm, not prompt, and the app has no prompt polyfill. The codebase already acknowledges this at Panels.tsx:1802. The New Snapshot case is lower impact because showNewSnapshotDialog defaults to false (store.ts:709). The main harm: workspaces cannot be saved or deleted in the shipped build.

findings.title: Typing in the History panel's 'States' field trims the undo stack on every keystroke
findings.feature: History panel ▸ History States
findings.evidence: Panels.tsx:2683-2687 is a raw controlled <input type=number> with onChange={(e) => store.setHistoryStates(Number(e.currentTarget.value))}. store.ts:4351-4358 turns '' into 1 (Math.round(0)||MIN) and calls engine set_history_states right away. Engine raster/mod.rs:29284-29288 calls trim_undo_to_history_states() immediately, which is irreversible. The Preferences pane uses NumberField (Dialogs.tsx:2123), which commits only on Enter or blur. e2e/history-states.spec.ts:78 uses fill(), which sets the value atomically and never sees the intermediate states.
findings.repro: Make about 40 edits. In the History panel select the '50' in States and type 100: the first keystroke '1' sets the cap to 1. Backspacing the field to empty also clamps it to 1.
findings.impact: All but one undo state are permanently discarded while the user is just typing a larger number.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the monet NumberField here, which commits on Enter or blur, like Preferences ▸ Performance. Or commit onBlur/Enter only.
findings.verdict_reason: Panels.tsx:2683-2687 is a raw controlled number input whose onChange calls store.setHistoryStates(Number(value)) on every keystroke. store.ts:4351-4359 clamps with Math.round(n)||MIN, so an empty field becomes 1, then calls engine.set_history_states(v) immediately. Engine raster/mod.rs:29284-29288 calls trim_undo_to_history_states(), which drains undo entries (mod.rs:5729-5733) and cannot be reversed. Selecting '50' and typing '1' caps the history at 1 before the next digit arrives, and backspacing '50' to '5' trims to 5. Undo states are silently and permanently lost.

findings.title: Window ▸ <panel> closes a panel that is a background tab instead of bringing it forward (15 of 23 panels in the default layout)
findings.feature: Window menu panel toggles
findings.evidence: App.tsx:3491-3498 onOpenPanel calls dock.closePanel(id) whenever dockLayoutPanelIds(layout).includes(id). dockable.tsx:109-116 counts every tab in every stack, including inactive ones. In the Essentials seed (App.tsx:312-326), history, actions, paths, navigator, layercomps, properties, swatches, libraries, brushes, styles, adjustments, channels, info, notes and animation are all non-active tabs. A second click reopens the panel in the right dock's first stack (dockable-core.ts:355-357), not where it was. windowMenu.test.ts:66-75 asserts this counting.
findings.repro: Fresh workspace: Window ▸ History, or Window ▸ Paths or Window ▸ Navigator.
findings.impact: The panel the user asked to see disappears from the dock. Choosing it again puts it in a different group. On macOS there are no checkmarks to explain this (see the checkmarks finding).
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a panel as open only when it is the active tab of its group in an expanded dock or float. Otherwise call dock.openPanel(id), which already reveals an existing tab (openTabImmutable). Update windowMenu.test.ts to match.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:3491-3498 closes a panel whenever dockLayoutPanelIds(layout).includes(id) and it is not iconified. dockable.tsx:109-116 collects every tab of every stack, active or not. In the Essentials seed (App.tsx:312-326), 15 tabs are not the active tab of their stack (swatches, libraries, brushes, styles, adjustments, channels, info, notes, animation, properties, history, actions, paths, navigator, layercomps). A second choice goes through openTabImmutable, which for a missing tab adds it to the right dock's first panel column's first stack (dockable-core.ts:355-357), the Color group, not its original place. windowMenu.test.ts:60-78 asserts only the id collection and source strings, so this behaviour is codified. It is recoverable with a second click, but the common path does the opposite of what the user asked.

findings.title: Bare window.confirm() returns a Promise in the desktop app, so confirmations are silently skipped
findings.feature: Status bar 'Convert to RGB' (Photoshop preview); Actions ▸ + Stop 'Allow Continue'; also Save As PSD warning, profile prompts
findings.evidence: tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1 src/init-iife.js replaces window.confirm with an async invoke('plugin:dialog|confirm'). lib.rs:199-203 registers only open, save and message, so the call rejects and the Promise is truthy. app.ts:576-577 documents this (#480) and already routes Actions pauses and close prompts through plugin-dialog ask(). Still bare: App.tsx:2158 setRgbMode, where !confirm(...) is false and the conversion runs; Panels.tsx:2559-2560 allowContinue, which becomes a Promise; app.ts:8106 (Save As PSD/PSB lossy warning); app.ts:7379 and 7398 (embedded-profile choice on open); store.ts:6645-6648 (paste profile conversion).
findings.repro: Desktop app: open a CMYK or Lab PSD (read-only preview) and click 'Convert to RGB' in the status bar.
findings.impact: The conversion runs with no dialog, and the preserved non-RGB Photoshop source is dropped without the promised warning. Other sites skip the Save As PSD lossy-export warning and force the OK branch of the profile-mismatch prompts.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one shared async confirm helper that uses plugin-dialog ask() under Tauri, like confirmDiscard at app.ts:8392, and use it at every site. Add a test or lint that forbids bare confirm() and prompt() in src/.
findings.verdict_reason: tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.1 is registered through monet-ui (crates/monet-ui/src/dialog.rs:42). Its injected init-iife.js sets window.confirm = async () => invoke('plugin:dialog|confirm'), but lib.rs:199-203 and build.rs COMMANDS register only open, save and message. The call therefore returns a Promise that later rejects. That Promise is truthy, so !confirm(...) is false and confirm(...) counts as OK. Affected sites I read: App.tsx:2158 (Convert to RGB runs without a warning); app.ts:8106, which sits inside the isTauri() branch, so the PSD/PSB lossy warning is always skipped on desktop; app.ts:7379 and 7398 (profile prompts force the OK branch); store.ts:6645-6648 (paste always converts). app.ts:575-585 and 8387-8420 show the team already routes other sites through plugin-dialog ask() for exactly this reason (#480). One correction: the Insert Stop 'Allow Continue' confirm at Panels.tsx:2559 is never reached on desktop, because the prompt() before it returns null first (see the prompt finding).

findings.title: Native macOS menu bar drops every checkmark (Window panels/documents, Image ▸ Mode/depth, OpenType toggles, PAR, measurement scale)
findings.feature: macOS native menu bridge
findings.evidence: mac-menu.ts:27-30 MenuNode has no 'checked' field. nodeFromItem (44-51) ignores item.checked, and buildNode (158-163) creates plain MenuItem, never CheckMenuItem (grep finds no CheckMenuItem anywhere). On macOS the in-window menu is not drawn (primitives.tsx:397 'menus live in the global bar'), so App.tsx's checkedIds (3505-3510) and the Window panel/document checks (psMenus.ts:458-504) are never visible.
findings.repro: On macOS open Type ▸ OpenType ▸ Swash twice, or look at Image ▸ Mode or Window ▸ Layers.
findings.impact: There is no way to see toggle state from the menu. OpenType feature toggles have no other UI that shows their state. It also compounds the Window-menu close-instead-of-show problem.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry 'checked' through MenuNode and build CheckMenuItem for items that have it. Update check state with setChecked instead of a rebuild.
findings.verdict_reason: In mac-menu.ts:27-30, MenuNode has no checked field. nodeFromItem (44-51) drops item.checked, and buildNode (158-163) creates only MenuItem, Submenu and separators; the bridge has no CheckMenuItem. Vision's native/macMenu.ts is a thin wrapper around the shared bridge. On macOS, primitives.tsx:397 puts menus in the global bar, so none of the checked state computed in App.tsx (the checkedIds set and the Window panel and document checks) is ever visible.

findings.title: Hiding a command in Edit ▸ Menus… also kills its keyboard shortcut, and the dialog itself can be hidden with no way back
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Menus… / Keyboard Shortcuts
findings.evidence: App.tsx:3526-3534: shortcutCommands (dispatch and Edit ▸ Search) come from baseMenus, which pruneHidden has already filtered (psMenus.ts:147-165, 537-540). The Menus tab (Dialogs.tsx:2405-2415) lets every path be unchecked, including Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…, Edit ▸ Menus… and Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…. Separately, Edit ▸ Menus… maps to the same 'keyboardshortcuts' handler (psMenus.ts:80, App.tsx:2708). That handler calls open('keyboardShortcuts') without arg 'menus', so it opens on the Shortcuts tab (Dialogs.tsx:2184).
findings.repro: Edit ▸ Menus… → uncheck File ▸ Save → OK → press ⌘S: nothing happens. Or hide all three shortcut/menu entries: the dialog can no longer be reached, and neither can any hidden command.
findings.impact: Decluttering the menus disables core shortcuts like Save, a data-loss risk. Users can strand themselves until they clear localStorage 'mv.hiddenMenuCommands'.
findings.suggested_fix: Dispatch shortcuts from the unfiltered catalog, gated by enablement only. Make the Keyboard Shortcuts, Menus and Search entries unhideable. Open with arg 'menus' for Edit ▸ Menus….
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:3526-3534: shortcutCommands is built from baseMenus = buildMenus(hiddenMenuCommands, ...), which applies pruneHidden (psMenus.ts:147-165, 537-540). shortcutCommandsRef, which the keydown dispatcher uses at App.tsx:2306 and 2375, therefore lacks hidden commands. Only the editor uses the unfiltered catalog. The Menus tab (Dialogs.tsx:2405-2415) lets any path be unchecked. The only routes to the dialog are Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…, Edit ▸ Menus… and Help ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…, all through App.tsx:2708. I found no preferences reset or localStorage clear. Edit ▸ Menus… maps to 'keyboardshortcuts' (psMenus.ts:80), which calls open('keyboardShortcuts') without 'menus', so the dialog opens on the Shortcuts tab (Dialogs.tsx:2184). This is user-configured, so I kept minor.

findings.title: Brush Settings (Shape Dynamics, Scattering, Transfer) stop applying after New, Open or a tab switch while the panel still shows them
findings.feature: Brushes panel ▸ Shape Dynamics / Scattering / Transfer
findings.evidence: setBrushTransfer, setBrushShapeDynamics and setBrushScatter (brushDynamics.ts:53-56, 106-117, 160-165) push to the engine passed in, and only the Brushes panel sliders call them (Panels.tsx:3432-3443, 3474-3495). No other code calls set_brush_transfer, set_brush_shape_dynamics or set_brush_scatter. Each document has its own engine (store DocEntry.engine). store.pushBrush(), which runs on activate, does not re-send these. The ponytail note at brushDynamics.ts:50-52 acknowledges this.
findings.repro: Set Size Jitter to 100% and Scatter to 500%, open a second image or create a new document, then paint.
findings.impact: Strokes paint with no jitter or scatter while the panel shows the values. The result is wrong in any multi-document session.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-push the three current values inside store.pushBrush(), which already runs on New, Open and activate.
findings.verdict_reason: The only calls to setBrushTransfer, setBrushShapeDynamics and setBrushScatter are slider onChange handlers in Panels.tsx:3433-3512. The engine keeps the values on its own brush state (self.brush.*, raster/mod.rs:17111-17116), and each document has its own engine. store.pushBrush() re-sends set_brush, dynamics, shape, block and mode but never transfer, scatter or shape dynamics. The ponytail note at brushDynamics.ts:49-52 admits the gap. A second document's engine therefore paints with zero jitter and scatter while the panel shows the values.

findings.title: Layer Comps panel's 'Restore Last Document State' and ◆ marker leak across documents and apply another document's layer ids
findings.feature: Layer Comps panel
findings.evidence: Panels.tsx:3037-3038: applied and lastState are component state with no activeDocId reset. The ponytail comment claims 'resets on remount/document switch', but panels are not keyed per document (App.tsx:3402, 3748). apply() captures lastState only when applied < 0 (3082). restore() (3098-3103) sends lastState to store.applyLayerCompToEngine, which writes visibility, opacity, blend and offset by layer id to the current engine (store.ts:7204-7214).
findings.repro: Doc A: click a layer comp. Switch to doc B, which has layers with the same numeric ids. Click 'Restore Last Document State'.
findings.impact: Doc B's layers get doc A's visibility, opacity, blend and position. The ◆ marker points at the wrong comp. The change is undoable but surprising.
findings.suggested_fix: Reset applied and lastState on an activeDocId change, as LayersPanel does at Panels.tsx:469-475. Or keep them per document in the store.
findings.verdict_reason: Panels.tsx:3036-3037 keeps applied (useState) and lastState (useRef) with no activeDocId dependency. The panel is registered without a key at App.tsx:3402, so it stays mounted across document switches while visible; the comment's 'resets on ... document switch' is wrong unless the tab unmounts. restore() (3098-3103) sends lastState to store.applyLayerCompToEngine(engine.e, ...) on the current engine by layer id. The effect is undoable, hence minor.

findings.title: Arrow-key navigation in the Layers panel is dead (roving focus targets a non-focusable wrapper)
findings.feature: Layers panel keyboard access
findings.evidence: LayerList.rowEl returns the display:contents wrapper's firstElementChild (creative-layers.tsx:438-443). Vision's renderRow wraps LayerRow (role=option, tabIndex) in <div draggable data-mv-layer-drag> (Panels.tsx:867-869), so rowEl is that div. focusRow(...).focus() is a no-op, and activeId is never found because it compares against document.activeElement. rovingKeyDown (328-349) still calls preventDefault, so the keys are swallowed. No unit or e2e test uses arrow keys in Layers.
findings.repro: Tab to the selected layer row, then press ArrowDown or ArrowUp.
findings.impact: Keyboard users cannot move between layers in the listbox. Only the tab-stop row is reachable.
findings.suggested_fix: In rowEl, use el.querySelector('[role="option"]') instead of firstElementChild. Add a test with a renderRow that wraps its row.
findings.verdict_reason: creative-layers.tsx:438-443: under renderRow, rowEl returns the display:contents wrapper's firstElementChild.
