Vision's renderRow returns <div draggable data-mv-layer-drag> as that first child (Panels.tsx:866-869), which has no tabIndex, so focus() does nothing. The listbox keydown (470-477) compares rowEl(l.id) with document.activeElement (the inner role=option LayerRow), so activeId is never found and it falls back to tabStopId. rovingKeyDown (328-349) still calls preventDefault. Vision adds no arrow handling of its own; its only arrow code (Panels.tsx:693) is for sliders.

findings.title: Many panel actions are mouse-only span/div click targets (no role, tabIndex or key handler)
findings.feature: History, Paths, Layer Comps, Channels, Libraries, Styles, Animation panels
findings.evidence: History state rows (2740-2745) and snapshot rows with ✕ (2715-2728) are onClick divs and spans. The same holds for Paths rows and the Work Path 👁/✕ spans (2905-2922), Layer Comp rows and ⚙/⟳/✕ (3122-3131), the Channel Options ⚙ (1874) and Spot ⚙ (1916), the Quick Mask ⚙ (role=button but no tabIndex or key handler, 1833-1834), the Libraries img and × (3330-3333), the Styles × (3358), the Animation frame × (3743) and the timeline key × (3791).
findings.repro: Using only the keyboard, try to revert to a history state, load a saved path, apply a layer comp or delete a library asset.
findings.impact: Core panel workflows cannot be reached by keyboard or screen-reader users.
findings.suggested_fix: Render these as <button type=button> with aria-labels, as the Actions panel already does, or give them role and tabIndex plus Enter/Space handlers.
findings.verdict_reason: Code confirmed: History state rows and snapshot rows plus ✕ (Panels.tsx:2715-2745), Paths Work Path 👁/✕ and saved-path rows plus ✕ (2905-2922), Layer Comp rows and ⚙/⟳/✕ (3118-3126), Libraries img and × (3330-3333), and Quick Mask ⚙ (1833, role=button but no tabIndex or key handler) are all bare onClick divs or spans. The impact is partly overstated. History states can be reached step by step with the Undo/Redo Buttons or ⌘Z, and layer comps can be applied with the ◀/▶ Buttons (3109-3110). Loading a saved path, restoring a snapshot and deleting library assets or comps have no keyboard route.

findings.title: Paths panel: deleting a saved path or the Work Path is not undoable, and clicking a saved path overwrites an unsaved Work Path
findings.feature: Paths panel
findings.evidence: store.ts:7151-7154 deleteSavedPath → commitSavedPaths (markDirty and set only, no history). The doc comment at 7157 says 'Not undoable, like saving or deleting a path'; Photoshop records Delete Path. store.ts:7176-7178 deleteWorkPath clears penPath with no history. store.ts:7147-7150 loadSavedPath replaces penPath, penAnchors and penContours, and a single row click triggers it (Panels.tsx:2919). The ✕ controls are tiny spans with no confirmation.
findings.repro: Draw a work path (unsaved), then click a saved path row. The work path is gone and Undo does not bring it back. Or click ✕ on a saved or clipping path and press ⌘Z.
findings.impact: Vector work (including print clipping paths) can be lost with one click.
findings.suggested_fix: Route path save, delete and load through history. The engine or store snapshot of savedPaths and penPath can piggyback on push_history. At least keep the unsaved Work Path when a saved path is selected.
findings.verdict_reason: store.ts:7141-7154: commitSavedPaths only calls markDirty and set, and deleteSavedPath goes through it, so there is no engine history. The comment at 7157 says this is deliberate ('Not undoable, like saving or deleting a path'). deleteWorkPath (7176-7178) and loadSavedPath (7147-7150) just set store state. undo() (engine undo only) never restores penPath, savedPaths or penContours. One row click (Panels.tsx:2919) replaces an unsaved work path. The limitation is broader than the finding: pen path edits are not in history at all.

findings.title: Layers panel Delete/Duplicate (footer and context menu) ignore the multi-layer selection that Layer ▸ Delete and the lock cluster honour
findings.feature: Layers panel footer / context menu
findings.evidence: Panels.tsx:612 duplicateLayer(activeId), Panels.tsx:627 deleteLayer(activeId) and Panels.tsx:688 ctx-del act on the active layer only. Layer ▸ Delete deletes targetLayerIds() (App.tsx:2850, #243), and the panel's own lock buttons loop selectedIds (Panels.tsx:789-791).
findings.repro: Shift- or ⌘-click three layers, then click the panel's trash button.
findings.impact: Only one layer is deleted or duplicated, inconsistent with the menu and with Photoshop.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the same targetLayerIds() rule, ideally in one history step.
findings.verdict_reason: Panels.tsx:612 duplicateLayer(activeId), 627 deleteLayer(activeId) and 680 ctx-del deleteLayer(store.state.activeLayerId) act on one layer. App.tsx:2850 del loops over targetLayerIds() (#243). The panel's own lock controls loop over selectedIds (Panels.tsx:811, 825); the finding's cited lines 789-791 are the color filter, but the claim holds.

findings.title: Help ▸ About / System Info / Keyboard Shortcuts and Window ▸ Workspace Save/Reset/Delete are disabled on the Home screen
findings.feature: Help menu / Workspace on Home
findings.evidence: NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS (App.tsx:77) omits about, systeminfo, keyboardshortcuts, savews, resetws and delws. menuEnablement marks every other id false with no document (App.tsx:3433-3437), and stableMenuActions skips them too (3332-3336). About() is already engine-safe (Dialogs.tsx:2155-2156). On macOS the native Help aliases are derived from the same actions and are disabled too.
findings.repro: Close all documents, then open Help.
findings.impact: Help is entirely greyed out at first launch, and workspaces can't be reset before a document is open.
findings.suggested_fix: Add about, systeminfo, keyboardshortcuts, savews, resetws and delws to NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS.
findings.verdict_reason: NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS (App.tsx:77) is /^(new|openf|clearrecent|browse|search|colorsettings|pref[a-z]*|exportprefs|customizetoolbar)$/, so it excludes about, systeminfo, keyboardshortcuts, savews, resetws and delws. With no document, menuEnablement sets every other id to false (App.tsx:3439-3441, spread last), and stableMenuActions refuses to run them (3334). The Help menu has only those three items (psMenus.ts:519-527), so it is fully greyed out on Home. About is engine-safe (Dialogs.tsx:2155-2156 try/catch).

findings.title: macOS native menu bar is fully rebuilt (about 900 IPC item creations) whenever any enablement flag or a dirty '*' flips
findings.feature: macOS native menu sync
findings.evidence: menuSignature includes each item's enabled flag and label, and the Window document names carry the dirty '*' (mac-menu.ts:65-70; App.tsx:2142). syncMacMenu rebuilds whenever the signature changes (314-345), creating every Submenu and MenuItem with a separate IPC call (buildNode 158-163). psMenuData has 687 items, 58 submenus and 130 separators, plus the Window and injected items. menuEnablement flips on selectionActive, canUndo, canFade, canReselect, hasClipboard and similar (App.tsx:3438-3469).
findings.repro: On macOS, repeatedly make and drop a marquee selection (⌘D), or make the first edit after a save.
findings.impact: Each flip triggers a full NSMenu rebuild on the main thread. It is likely to cause hitches during common selection work, but I did not measure it.
findings.suggested_fix: Build once, keep item handles, and apply enabled, text and checked diffs with setEnabled, setText and setChecked. Rebuild only on real structural changes.
findings.verdict_reason: The mechanism is confirmed. menuSignature (mac-menu.ts:65-70) encodes the id, text and enabled flag of every node. syncMacMenu rebuilds the whole tree when the signature changes (mac-menu.ts:~310-340) with one Submenu.new or MenuItem.new per node through buildNode (158-163), then calls setAsAppMenu. menuEnablement depends on canUndo, canRedo, canFade, canReselect, hasClipboard, selectionActive and more (App.tsx:3443-3469), so a marquee create or deselect flips paste-into, clear, stroke and cropsel and triggers a full rebuild. The actual hitch cost is unmeasured, as the finding says; profiling a ⌘D loop on macOS would settle it.

findings.title: Library 'place' clips the graphic to any live selection and splits into two history steps
findings.feature: Libraries panel ▸ click asset to place
findings.evidence: library.insert runs store.addLayer() and then E().stamp_image(0,0,w,h,rgba) (app.ts:2226-2228). Engine stamp_image multiplies by self.sel.coverage(di) and skips uncovered pixels (raster/mod.rs:18619-18621), and pushes its own 'Paste' undo (18606).
findings.repro: Make a small marquee, then click a Libraries asset.
findings.impact: The new layer contains only the part of the graphic inside the selection, and Undo takes two steps. Photoshop places library graphics as a whole new layer regardless of selection.
findings.suggested_fix: Deselect temporarily, or add an engine op that creates the layer from RGBA ignoring the selection, as one history step.
findings.verdict_reason: app.ts:2218-2229: library.insert calls store.addLayer(), which runs e.add_layer plus commit, a step of its own, then E().stamp_image(0,0,w,h,rgba). Engine stamp_image (raster/mod.rs:18596-18637) calls push_layer_undo('Paste') and scales alpha by self.sel.coverage(di), skipping pixels outside the selection. The two calls are not wrapped in a history transaction.

findings.title: Floating panels are never clamped to the workspace; a float dragged or restored off-screen loses its only move handle
findings.feature: Dock floats
findings.evidence: onDragHeader sets x/y = start + delta with no bounds (dockable.tsx:377-385). normLayout keeps saved f.x and f.y as they are (dockable-core.ts:221-230), and mv.workspaceLast restores them on the next launch at any window size.
findings.repro: Drag a floating panel's header above the top edge, or float one at the far right, quit, and relaunch in a smaller window.
findings.impact: The panel is unreachable until the user runs Reset Panels or toggles it twice from the Window menu.
findings.suggested_fix: Clamp x and y in onDragHeader and in normLayout or on window resize, so that at least the header stays inside .monet-body.
findings.verdict_reason: dockable.tsx:378-386 sets x and y from start + delta with no bounds. normLayout (dockable-core.ts:222-230) keeps the persisted f.x and f.y. The float renders at left:f.x, top:f.y (dockable-views.tsx:591). onFloatKeyDown (579-586) handles only Escape, so there is no keyboard move. I found no clamp helper in monet-react or Vision. Recovery exists through Reset Panels or the Window menu toggle, so polish is right.

findings.title: Contextual Task Bar toggle has no checked state and is not persisted; the Histogram scope menu fakes checks with '✓ ' text
findings.feature: Window ▸ Contextual Task Bar; Histogram scope menu
findings.evidence: psMenus.ts:512 has no 'checked' on the toggletaskbar item. App.tsx:2013 useState(true) resets on every launch. Panels.tsx:1511-1515 builds labels as '✓ ' + label instead of using MenuItemDef.checked.
findings.repro: Hide the task bar and relaunch; the menu never shows its state.
findings.impact: Minor inconsistency with the rest of the menus.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the taskBarOpen state into checkedIds, persist it with the other mv.* preferences, and use checked on the scope items.
findings.verdict_reason: psMenus.ts:512 toggletaskbar has no checked field, and it is not in the checkedIds set App.tsx passes. App.tsx:2013 useState(true) is not persisted. Panels.tsx:1496-1500 scopeItem prefixes the label with '✓ ' instead of using MenuItemDef.checked. Given the macOS checkmark finding, the text prefix is actually the only form that shows up in the native bar, so the fix should land together with CheckMenuItem support.

areas.coverage:
Code review only; no builds or suites were run. To check the menu wiring and shortcut dispatch, I bundled the real psMenus.ts and keyboardShortcuts.ts with esbuild into a scratch script under the scratchpad (nothing in the repo was modified) and ran it against the live App.tsx action keys.

Inventory:
- **psMenuData.ts:** 687 leaf items. 610 carry a monetId (594 unique, 12 ids duplicated). 94 items show a shortcut.
- **After PATH_WIRING / LABEL_WIRING and first-wins dedupe:** 646 blueprint items are enabled with the full action table. 41 stay disabled placeholders: 34 have no id, `langindic` has no handler on purpose, and 6 lose to the first-wins dedupe (plus the `persp` case reported below).
- **About 55 injected items** (Export encoders, Window, Help, Text on Path, etc.).
- **App.tsx menuActions:** 670 keys, plus 26 OpenType tags spread in. All are reachable from a menu, so there are no dead handlers.
- **Shortcuts:** 90 distinct menu chords, 24 tool-letter groups and 13 tool-action shortcuts. I simulated every advertised menu chord through `collectShortcutCommands` and `shortcutCommandMap`. There are 2 mismatches: ⌘G (an intended alias) and ⇧⌘R (dead).
- **MCP:** 90 `@mcp` functions in commands.ts match the 90 tools in mcp.manifest.json name for name (checked by reading and diffing, not with `mcp:check`).
- **Recording:** about 150 names in RECORDED_STORE_OPS. About 80 menu handlers call store methods outside that list; most are view toggles, and the document-changing ones are listed in a finding.
- **Native macOS menu:** the shared bridge in monet-react mac-menu.ts. About 920 native nodes are built per rebuild. I checked the relevant tao 0.35.3, muda 0.19.2 and tauri-runtime-wry 2.11.2 sources in the cargo registry for how quit and accelerators behave.

Tracing went handler → store/app → engine only as far as needed to judge whether the wiring works. I did not check each feature's pixel correctness, colour-mode or bit-depth handling; those belong to the per-area reviewers.

Not verifiable by reading:
- Real WKWebView key-equivalent routing. The ⌘Q, ⌘W and ⌃⌘F findings rely on standard AppKit/WebKit behaviour and are marked medium confidence.
- The actual on-device cost of native menu rebuilds.
- Whether Windows/Linux builds are in the release.
areas.parity_notes:
Photoshop items shown disabled on purpose, not reported as bugs:
- 41 blueprint items stay disabled placeholders. 34 have no monetId, for example Browse in Bridge, Close and Go to Bridge, Invite to Edit and the other cloud/Bridge commands, and several Filter, Type and 3D entries.
- Type ▸ Language Options ▸ Indic Features (`langindic`) is a documented ponytail placeholder.
- 6 artboard-specific repeats lose to the first-wins dedupe (Fit Artboard on Screen, Artboard Guides, Clear Selected Artboard Guides, Canvas Guides variants). Only the Canvas Guides items are raised as a finding.

Contextual greying: Photoshop disables many commands by context, but Vision enables nearly everything once a document is open. Only 20 ids have runtime enablement: undo, redo, fade, reselect, the paste family, clear, stroke, crop-to-selection, transform again, the filter-mask pair and East Asian features. So Merge Down on the bottom layer, Ungroup on a non-group, Release Clipping, Apply/Delete Mask with no mask, Smart Object commands on non-smart layers and similar all look enabled and quietly do nothing (see store.mergeDown and store.ungroup at store.ts:7843 and 7909).

Shortcuts: ⌘G is deliberately shared by Layer ▸ New ▸ Group… and Group Layers (the later item wins). Tool tooltips hard-code their default letters ('Move (V)' and so on), so they go stale after a tool-shortcut rebind.

MCP: the surface is 90 tools against about 650 menu commands. There is no generic 'run menu command' tool, so most menu features (Levels/Curves, Image and Canvas Size, most layer and selection commands) reach agents only through script.run's `vision.*` ops.

Test gaps behind the findings above: no unit test checks that each advertised menu chord dispatches its own item (would have caught ⇧⌘R); the pasteboard tests never cover Paste enablement with an empty engine clipboard; and the ⌘Q guard is tested only against a mocked Tauri window. A stale comment in psMenus.test.ts (~line 136) still says Edit ▸ Toolbar… has no host action, although `customizetoolbar` is now wired.

findings.title: ⌘Q / app-menu Quit bypasses the unsaved-work guard, so unsaved edits are lost without a prompt
findings.feature: Native macOS menu ▸ Monet Vision ▸ Quit (⌘Q); unsaved-work guard
findings.evidence: packages/monet-ui/packages/monet-react/src/mac-menu.ts:187 installs PredefinedMenuItem 'Quit'. muda-0.19.2 predefined.rs:339 gives it ⌘Q and macos/mod.rs:994 maps it to `terminate:`. tao-0.35.3 platform_impl/macos/app_delegate.rs:131-135 handles only applicationWillTerminate → AppState::exit() → Event::LoopDestroyed. There is no applicationShouldTerminate handler, and tauri-runtime-wry-2.11.2 lib.rs:4192 maps LoopDestroyed straight to RunEvent::Exit, so no window CloseRequested is emitted. Vision's guard (apps/vision/src/state/app.ts:8356-8372) relies only on win.onCloseRequested; its comment claims Tauri fires it for ⌘Q. apps/vision/src-tauri/src/main.rs:406-413 run_return handles only RunEvent::Opened. The JS keydown map has no Mod+KeyQ, so ⌘Q always falls through to the native Quit. unsavedWorkGuard.test.ts only exercises a mocked window.
findings.repro: In the packaged macOS app, open an image, paint a stroke (document is now dirty), then press ⌘Q or choose Monet Vision ▸ Quit (or Dock ▸ Quit).
findings.impact: The app quits with no 'Unsaved Changes' prompt. Everything since the last recovery snapshot is lost: the default interval is 10 minutes (autoRecover.ts:8), and recovery is off in dev/debug builds.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the predefined Quit in the shared appSubmenu with a custom MenuItem (id app/quit) that runs the app's guard (confirmDiscardAll over store.dirtyDocNames()) and then calls exit, and bind Mod+KeyQ in the JS map to the same command. For Dock ▸ Quit and system logout, add a Rust-side applicationShouldTerminate hook (or handle RunEvent::ExitRequested and emit an event the webview answers). Add a native-harness check that ⌘Q with a dirty document prompts.
findings.verdict_reason: I followed the path end to end and found nothing that stops it. mac-menu.ts:187 installs PredefinedMenuItem 'Quit'. In muda-0.19.2 (the version in Vision's Cargo.lock) predefined.rs:339 gives it ⌘Q and macos/mod.rs:994 maps it to `terminate:`. tao-0.35.3 (also locked) never implements applicationShouldTerminate; a grep of its src returns nothing. It only has application_will_terminate → AppState::exit() (app_delegate.rs:131-135), which tauri-runtime-wry-2.11.2 lib.rs:4192 turns straight into RunEvent::Exit. No CloseRequested is emitted, so win.onCloseRequested in app.ts:8356-8372 never runs, even though its comment claims it covers ⌘Q. Vision's run_return (main.rs:406-413) handles only Opened. Nothing under apps/vision/src-tauri or packages/monet-ui/crates mentions NSApplication, ExitRequested or prevent_exit. The only KeyQ binding in JS is the tool key 'tool-q'. No unload hook saves recovery data; the default recovery interval is 10 minutes (autoRecover.ts:8). The only test is unsavedWorkGuard.test.ts, which uses a mocked window. Remaining gap: not reproduced on a packaged build, but the code is unambiguous.

findings.title: Cross-app Paste (Preview/Figma/Artisan → Vision) is unreachable until something has been copied inside Vision
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Paste / Paste in Place / Paste Into / Paste Outside, ⌘V, system pasteboard adoption
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/App.tsx:3448-3451 gates paste, pasteinplace, pasteinto and pasteoutside on `hasClipboard`, and a disabled item is dropped from both the menu and the shortcut map (psMenus.ts:220-222, keyboardShortcuts.ts:229). `hasClipboard` is `e.has_clipboard() || !!this.publishedPng?.length` (store.ts:2533), and publishedPng is set only by an in-app Copy or Cut (store.ts:6543-6548). The pasteboard is read only inside readyClipboardForPaste/adoptPasteboardImage (store.ts:6557-6576, 6656-6662), which run only after Paste is invoked. Nothing polls the pasteboard, and there is no DOM 'paste' listener. pasteboard.test.ts:61 stubs `has_clipboard` to true, so the 'adopts an image another app copied' test never covers the disabled state.
findings.repro: Launch Vision and open or create a document without copying anything in Vision. In Preview (or Artisan), copy an image. Back in Vision, press ⌘V or open Edit ▸ Paste.
findings.impact: Edit ▸ Paste and its Paste Special variants are greyed out and ⌘V does nothing, so this interop workflow is dead in a fresh session. It only starts working after the user copies something inside Vision.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep Paste enabled whenever a document is open, and let readyClipboardForPaste report 'nothing to paste' when both clipboards are empty. Alternatively, refresh `hasClipboard` from a cheap pasteboard probe on window focus. Add a test that Paste is enabled and runnable with an empty engine clipboard and a foreign image on the pasteboard.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:3448-3451 gates paste, pasteinplace, pasteinto and pasteoutside on hasClipboard. buildPhotoshopMenus removes the actions of disabled items (psMenus.ts:220-222), and collectShortcutCommands keeps only items that have an action (keyboardShortcuts.ts:229), so ⌘V is not in the dispatch map. hasClipboard is set only at store.ts:2533 (engine has_clipboard or publishedPng), and publishedPng is set only in publishClipboard (store.ts:6543-6548). The pasteboard is read only in adoptPasteboardImage, whose only callers are readyClipboardForPaste (Paste itself and the Vanishing Point paste at App.tsx:1643). There is no DOM paste listener or focus-time probe. On macOS, ⌘V then falls through to the native predefined Paste appended in mac-menu.ts:330, which sends paste: to the webview, where nothing listens. pasteboard.test.ts:61 stubs has_clipboard to true. Workaround: copy anything inside Vision first, then foreign images are adopted.

findings.title: Menu shortcuts, tool keys, digits and the macOS menu bar run commands on the document behind an open modal dialog
findings.feature: Global keydown dispatch and native macOS menu while a Dialog is open
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/App.tsx:2303 stops dispatch only when the target is an editable element, and only the Space branch checks `[aria-modal="true"]` (App.tsx:2362). Menu chords (2374-2376), tool letters and opacity digits otherwise go through. monet-react Dialog renders a header close button first (dialog.tsx:141-150, showClose defaults to true), and the focus trap focuses the first focusable element (overlay-core.tsx:151-156). Any Vision dialog without an autoFocus input, such as Canvas Size (Dialogs.tsx:10274-10320, no history transaction), therefore opens with focus on a non-editable button. historyTransactionActive (App.tsx:2345-2350) protects only live-preview dialogs. The native bar's `blocked` guard is also only historyTransactionActive (App.tsx:3575). DialogProvider.open replaces the current dialog (Dialogs.tsx:242-247).
findings.repro: With a saved (clean) document A and a second document B open, choose Image ▸ Canvas Size…, then press ⌘W. Document A closes behind the dialog. Enter a size and click Apply, and B's canvas is resized using A's dimensions. With a selection active, pressing ⌫ while the dialog is open clears pixels, ⌘Z undoes, digit keys change layer opacity and letters switch tools. On macOS the same happens from the menu bar, e.g. File ▸ Close or Image ▸ Mode.
findings.impact: A modal dialog can apply to the wrong document, or to a state that changed underneath it. Destructive edits land while the user thinks input is captured by the dialog. Photoshop blocks all of this while a modal is up.
findings.suggested_fix: In onKey (after the Escape/Enter handling) and in the native `blocked` callback, return early when a modal is open, e.g. `document.querySelector('.monet-dialog[aria-modal="true"]')`, or expose an `isModalOpen()` from DialogProvider. Keep the explicit exceptions (Vanishing Point/Liquify workspaces). Add a unit or e2e check that ⌘W and ⌫ are ignored while Canvas Size is open.
findings.verdict_reason: onKey is a window keydown listener (App.tsx:2503). It returns early only for editable targets (2303), Vanishing Point or Liquify sessions, and historyTransactionActive (2345-2350). Only the Space branch checks aria-modal (2362); menu chords dispatch at 2374-2376. The monet-react Dialog renders the header close button first (showClose defaults to true), and useFocusTrap with autoFocus=true focuses the first focusable element (overlay-core.tsx:151-156). The dialog does not stop keydown propagation; its only document listener handles Escape. Canvas Size (Dialogs.tsx:10274) has no autoFocus field and opens no transaction, so ⌘W, and ⌫ (Edit ▸ Clear, shortcut ⌫ at psMenuData.ts:591), both dispatch. The native bar's blocked callback checks only historyTransactionActive (App.tsx:3575). One repro detail is imprecise: CanvasSize re-reads ow/oh from store.state on every render, so after A closes, Apply resizes B from A's initial w/h values, anchored against B's dimensions. That is still the wrong document and the wrong size. Edits are undoable, which keeps this at major rather than blocker.

findings.title: Filter ▸ Lens Correction… shows ⇧⌘R, but the shortcut does nothing
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Lens Correction… (⇧⌘R) / File ▸ Automate ▸ Lens Correction…
findings.evidence: SHARED_ACTION_PATHS (apps/vision/src/ui/psMenus.ts:57-66) wires both File ▸ Automate ▸ Lens Correction… (no shortcut, psMenuData.ts:355-358) and Filter ▸ Lens Correction… (⇧⌘R, psMenuData.ts:3060-3064), and both get item id `lenscorrection`. collectShortcutCommands dedupes by item id across the whole bar (state/keyboardShortcuts.ts:229), so the File entry wins with defaultChord null and Mod+Shift+KeyR is never registered. Running every advertised menu chord through the real dispatcher confirmed it: '⇧⌘R Filter ▸ Lens Correction… dispatches: (nothing)'. The Keyboard Shortcuts editor also lists the command under the File path with no default.
findings.repro: Open a document and press ⇧⌘R.
findings.impact: A Photoshop-standard shortcut shown in the menu is dead. Users must go through the menu.
findings.suggested_fix: When dedupe hits a shared id, keep the first non-null default chord (or merge chords) in collectShortcutCommands. Alternatively, give the File ▸ Automate entry a distinct PATH_WIRING id. Add a unit test that every enabled menu item with a `shortcut` is the owner of its parsed chord in shortcutCommandMap, allowing only the documented ⌘G alias; that would have caught this.
findings.verdict_reason: Both entries are in SHARED_ACTION_PATHS (psMenus.ts:57-58), so both get an action. uniq() is scoped per submenu, so both keep the id 'lenscorrection' (psMenus.ts:374). collectShortcutCommands walks the menus in bar order (File before Filter) with a global `seen` set (keyboardShortcuts.ts:229). The File ▸ Automate entry (psMenuData.ts:355-358, no shortcut) registers first with defaultChord null, and the Filter entry carrying ⇧⌘R (psMenuData.ts:3063) is skipped. ⇧⌘R appears nowhere else in the blueprint. psMenus.test.ts:96 checks only that both paths are wired, not the chord.

findings.title: Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective is disabled even though its handler exists (first-wins dedupe)
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective; View ▸ Clear Canvas Guides / Show ▸ Canvas Guides
findings.evidence: The blueprint gives both Edit ▸ Perspective Warp and Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective monetId `persp` (psMenuData.ts:699-700, 743-744). buildPhotoshopMenus disables every repeat id unless its path is in SHARED_ACTION_PATHS (psMenus.ts:376-382), so the Transform submenu entry renders disabled. The handler `persp: () => open("perspective")` is registered (App.tsx:2759), and the sibling Transform ▸ Distort is enabled and opens the same dialog (App.tsx:2758). The same rule greys out View ▸ Clear Canvas Guides and Show ▸ Canvas Guides even though `clearguides`/`showguides` act on exactly those guides.
findings.repro: Open a document and choose Edit ▸ Transform.
findings.impact: In the core Transform submenu, 'Perspective' is greyed out while 'Distort' next to it works.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective' (and 'View ▸ Clear Canvas Guides' / 'View ▸ Show ▸ Canvas Guides') to SHARED_ACTION_PATHS, or wire them via PATH_WIRING. Extend psMenus.test's shared-path test.
findings.verdict_reason: Edit ▸ Perspective Warp (psMenuData.ts:699-700) and Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective (743-744) both have monetId 'persp'. The global `wired` set gives an action only to the first one unless the path is in SHARED_ACTION_PATHS (psMenus.ts:375), and neither path is listed there or in PATH_WIRING or LABEL_WIRING. The handler exists (App.tsx:2759), and Distort next to it opens the same dialog (2758). The same applies to View ▸ Show ▸ Canvas Guides (showguides, psMenuData.ts:3993) and View ▸ Clear Canvas Guides (clearguides, 4118). The Artboard variants are arguably right to be disabled.

findings.title: Many document-changing menu commands (and some MCP tools) are not recorded into Actions
findings.feature: Actions panel recording (rec / RECORDED_STORE_OPS) and MCP action.record
findings.evidence:
Only the proxied namespaces and the RECORDED_STORE_OPS list (apps/vision/src/state/app.ts:904-952) record. These handlers bypass both:
- Edit ▸ Clear (App.tsx:2734, `engine.e.clear_selection()`).
- Fill with Foreground/Background ⌥⌫/⌘⌫ (App.tsx:2736-2737 → fillWith 2116-2121 → `engine.e.fill_selection`, not the recorded `store.fillContents`).
- Convert to Profile (Dialogs.tsx:2984 and MCP doc.convertToProfile → `store.convertToProfile`).
- The Camera Raw Filter apply (`store.cameraRawDevelopTarget`).
- Layer ▸ Rasterize ▸ Layer / All Layers / Fill Content for non-type layers (`store.rasterizeFillLayer`, App.tsx:3019-3020).
- The Vector Mask commands (App.tsx:2986 and others), Make Work Path and Convert to Shape (App.tsx:3033-3034), and Combine Shapes (App.tsx:3044-3046).
- Select ▸ All Layers (2904), Quick Mask (2731), Auto-Align, Auto-Blend and Photomerge (2609-2611), and Merge to HDR Pro (2809, direct engine call).
- Delete Empty Layers, Flatten All Masks and Flatten All Layer Effects, Clear Guides, New Guides from Shape, and Layer Cleanup.
mcp/commands.ts:424 promises that 'every command Photoshop would record becomes a step — MCP tools included', but doc.convertToProfile, adj.cameraRawRecipe, layer.cleanup and layer.vectorMaskFromPath do not record.
findings.repro: Actions panel ▸ Begin Recording. Press ⌥⌫ (fill with foreground), then ⌫ with a selection, then Edit ▸ Convert to Profile… ▸ OK. Stop and inspect the steps.
findings.impact: Recorded actions silently miss steps, so replay or Batch gives different results from the recording. The MCP action.record documentation is inaccurate.
findings.suggested_fix: Route Fill FG/BG and Clear through the recorded store methods (fillContents, or a new recorded clearSelection). Add convertToProfile, cameraRawDevelopTarget, rasterizeFillLayer, the vector-mask and shape commands, selectAllLayers, toggleQuickMask and the Automate commands to RECORDED_STORE_OPS, with LIVE_STORE_OPS entries where needed. Extend actionRecording.test.ts with these ids.
findings.verdict_reason: RECORDED_STORE_OPS (app.ts:904-952) contains none of convertToProfile, cameraRawDevelopTarget, rasterizeFillLayer, the vector-mask ops, createWorkPath, convertToShape, combineShapes, selectAllLayers, toggleQuickMask, autoAlignLayers, autoBlendLayers, photomerge, clearGuides or cleanupLayers. A grep of src/state and src/mcp finds no other rec() path for them. Edit ▸ Clear calls engine.e.clear_selection directly (App.tsx:2734). Fill FG/BG go through fillWith, which calls engine.e.fill_selection (2116-2121), bypassing the recorded fillContents. Merge to HDR Pro calls the engine directly (2809). selectAllLayers is a plain set() (store.ts:7635). mcp/commands.ts:424 promises that 'every command Photoshop would record becomes a step — MCP tools included', which is inaccurate for these.

findings.title: NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS disables commands on the Home screen that do not need an open document
findings.feature: Home screen (#476) enablement
findings.evidence:
apps/vision/src/App.tsx:77 `/^(new|openf|clearrecent|browse|search|colorsettings|pref[a-z]*|exportprefs|customizetoolbar)$/`. App.tsx:3439-3441 and 3335 disable every other registered id when no document is open. Commands that disable but work without a document:
- Help ▸ About and Help ▸ System Info. About only guards engine.version in a try (Dialogs.tsx:2152-2156).
- Help and Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts… / Menus…, which read only the command catalog.
- Edit ▸ Presets ▸ Preset Manager.
- Window ▸ Workspace ▸ Save/Reset.
- File ▸ Automate ▸ Batch and Image Processor (BatchSource includes 'files'/'folder', app.ts:6268).
- Create Droplet and Script Events Manager.
- Load Files into Stack and Load Multiple DICOM Files (stackImages opens its first file as a new document, app.ts:7725-7743).
- Open as Smart Object, Video Frames to Layers, Scripts ▸ Browse…, and Type ▸ Font Preview Size.
The same DICOM load is allowed documentless over MCP (doc.loadDicomSeries).
findings.repro: Close all documents and open the Help or File ▸ Automate menus.
findings.impact: Photoshop allows these with no document open. Users on Home cannot read About or System Info, view shortcuts, or start a Batch. The menu and MCP disagree for DICOM loading.
findings.suggested_fix: Widen the allowlist (keyboardshortcuts, about, systeminfo, presetmanager, savews, resetws, delws, batch, imageprocessor, createdroplet, scripteventsmanager, loadfilesstack, loaddicom, opensmartobject, videoframes, opengif, scriptbrowse, fontpreview*). Better, declare per-command `needsDocument` next to menuActions so the list cannot drift.
findings.verdict_reason: The allowlist at App.tsx:77 is /^(new|openf|clearrecent|browse|search|colorsettings|pref[a-z]*|exportprefs|customizetoolbar)$/. Every other registered id is forced to false on Home (3439-3441). about, systeminfo and keyboardshortcuts (2706-2708), batch, createdroplet, scripteventsmanager, scriptbrowse and imageprocessor (2979-2984), presetmanager (2992), and loadfilesstack, loaddicom, opensmartobject and videoframes (2566-2581) are all excluded. The About dialog guards engine.version() in a try (Dialogs.tsx:2155), and stackImages opens its first file as a new document (app.ts:7735), so these work without an engine document. On macOS the native Help aliases are resolved against the enablement-filtered sourceBar, so they are disabled on Home too. The native About item still works on macOS.

findings.title: macOS native menu shows no checkmarks or Vision shortcuts, and advertises OS shortcuts that conflict with Vision's
findings.feature: Native macOS menu bar (the only menu bar on macOS)
findings.evidence: monet-react mac-menu.ts:49 builds MenuNode items with no `checked` field, and buildNode (158-163) creates plain MenuItems with no accelerator. Every checkmark (Image ▸ Mode colour mode and 8/16/32 Bits, Window ▸ panel checks, Type ▸ OpenType toggles, pixel-aspect and measurement-scale presets) and every Vision shortcut hint is therefore missing on macOS; primitives.tsx:397 confirms menus exist only in the global bar there. The synthesized OS items do carry accelerators (muda predefined.rs:317-339): Window ▸ Minimize ⌘M, where pressing ⌘M runs Curves; Enter Full Screen ⌃⌘F, where shortcutFromEvent folds Ctrl and Cmd into 'Mod' (keyboardShortcuts.ts:77) so ⌃⌘F opens Edit ▸ Search; and Close ⌘W. When the JS handler does not claim ⌘W (Home screen: App.tsx:2304-2309 never calls preventDefault; or focus in a text field: App.tsx:2303), the native CloseWindow closes the main window, and with no dirty documents the app exits.
findings.repro: On macOS, open Image ▸ Mode: no mode is checked. Open Window: Minimize shows ⌘M, but pressing ⌘M opens Curves. Press ⌃⌘F: Search opens instead of full screen. On Home, press ⌘W: the window closes and the app quits.
findings.impact: Mode, bit-depth and toggle states are invisible on the primary platform, all ~90 shortcuts are undiscoverable from the menu bar, and the shortcuts the bar does show are partly wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Carry `checked` into MenuNode and build CheckMenuItem for checked items. Set display-only accelerators, or append the shortcut text to the label if key equivalents must stay off. Drop the accelerators from the predefined items Vision rebinds (use custom items for Minimize, Full Screen and Close Window). Make Mod ignore Ctrl on macOS. Have the Home branch preventDefault ⌘W.
findings.verdict_reason: MenuNode (mac-menu.ts:26-29) has no checked or accelerator field, and buildNode (158-163) creates plain MenuItems, so checkmarks and shortcut hints are dropped on the native bar. The macOS titlebar renders no in-window menus (primitives.tsx:397). Window adds predefined Minimize, Fullscreen and CloseWindow (218-222), which muda gives ⌘M, ⌃⌘F and ⌘W (predefined.rs:317-333). Vision binds ⌘M to Curves, and shortcutFromEvent folds Ctrl and Meta into Mod (keyboardShortcuts.ts:77), so ⌃⌘F maps to Mod+KeyF, which is Search. On Home, onKey returns without preventDefault when the command is disabled (App.tsx:2304-2309), so the native ⌘W CloseWindow can close the window. Which side wins the ⌘M and ⌃⌘F conflicts at runtime depends on WKWebView key-equivalent routing, which I did not check on a device. The missing checkmarks and hints are certain.

findings.title: Hiding a command via Edit ▸ Menus… also disables its keyboard shortcut and removes it from Edit ▸ Search
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Menus… (hidden menu commands) vs shortcut dispatch
findings.evidence: buildPhotoshopMenus prunes hidden paths from the bar (psMenus.ts:537-540). App.tsx:3526-3533 builds the dispatch map (shortcutCommands) from that pruned `baseMenus`, and commandPalette.items (Search) comes from the same list. The editor's own contract says a hidden command 'still owns its chord' (Dialogs.tsx:2188-2191), so the chord stays reserved in conflict detection but is never dispatched.
findings.repro: Edit ▸ Menus… ▸ hide Edit ▸ Undo ▸ OK. Make an edit and press ⌘Z.
findings.impact: The chord is reserved but dead. Undo, Save and similar shortcuts silently stop working after the user tidies the menus, and the command also disappears from Search.
findings.suggested_fix: Build shortcutCommands and the Search list from the enablement-filtered menus with NO_HIDDEN (catalogMenus plus enablement), and use the hidden set only for the visible bar.
findings.verdict_reason: baseMenus is built with hiddenMenuCommands (App.tsx:3526-3528), and buildPhotoshopMenus prunes hidden paths (psMenus.ts:537-540). shortcutCommands comes from baseMenus (3531-3533) and feeds both the dispatch map (3541) and commandPalette.items for Search (3653). A hidden ⌘Z therefore never dispatches, while the editor still counts the chord as owned (Dialogs.tsx:2188-2191). The mechanism is certain. Whether it is a bug depends on intent: no test asserts either behaviour, and Photoshop keeps shortcuts working for hidden menu items, so I treat it as a defect.

findings.title: The whole native NSMenu (~920 items) is rebuilt on every enablement change, and old menu resources are never released
findings.feature: Native macOS menu sync
findings.evidence: menuSignature includes each item's enabled flag (mac-menu.ts:65-71). menuEnablement depends on selectionActive, canUndo, canRedo, canFade, canReselect, hasClipboard, activeIsText and others (App.tsx:3434-3470), so every select, deselect, first undo, fade window or text-layer switch changes `menus`. The sync effect (App.tsx:3574-3576) then rebuilds every Submenu and MenuItem through async Tauri IPC (mac-menu.ts:309-341). My count is ~921 nodes excluding Window and Help. Each MenuItem.new registers a Rust resource and a JS Channel (@tauri-apps/api menu/base.js newMenu), and nothing calls `close()` on the replaced tree.
findings.repro: On macOS, repeatedly make and drop a marquee selection (⌘A / ⌘D) and watch memory and the menu bar.
findings.impact: Hundreds of IPC round-trips per selection toggle, and resource-table growth for the whole session (possible jank or menu flicker). On-device magnitude is not measured.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the native tree and update only changed items with MenuItem.setEnabled/setText (look them up by id). Otherwise, `close()` the previous Menu before installing the new one.
findings.verdict_reason: menuSignature includes each node's enabled flag (mac-menu.ts:65-71), and menuTree sets enabled from item.disabled. menuEnablement depends on selectionActive, canUndo, canFade, hasClipboard and others (App.tsx:3434-3469), so a select or deselect changes the signature. syncMacMenu then rebuilds every node through MenuItem.new and Submenu.new, then setAsAppMenu (309-341). @tauri-apps/api 2.11.0 menu/base.js creates a new Channel per item and a Rust resource via plugin:menu|new, and mac-menu.ts never calls close() on the replaced tree. The rebuild-per-toggle and retained resources are confirmed. The jank and memory impact on a device is unmeasured, hence minor.

findings.title: Windows/Linux menus show macOS glyphs (⌘⌥⇧) for every shortcut the user has not changed
findings.feature: In-window menu bar on Windows/Linux; Keyboard Shortcuts dialog
findings.evidence: Blueprint labels are Mac glyphs ('⌘N', '⌥⌘W' in psMenuData.ts). applyShortcutOverrides reformats only items that carry an override (keyboardShortcuts.ts:258-270), and monet-react menu.tsx:289 renders `shortcut` verbatim. The in-window Windows menu is rendered from these labels (primitives.tsx:369-378). The Keyboard Shortcuts dialog formats with the default 'mac' platform (Dialogs.tsx:2424, 2443). Bundle targets are 'all' (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:28).
findings.repro: Run on Windows and open File: 'New… ⌘N'. Rebind one command, and that item alone shows 'Ctrl+…'.
findings.impact: The labels are wrong and inconsistent for non-Mac users. This only matters if Windows/Linux builds are in the release.
findings.suggested_fix: In applyShortcutOverrides, reformat every item's shortcut via parseShortcutLabel → formatShortcut(platform), not just overridden ones, and pass the platform to formatShortcut in the dialog.
findings.verdict_reason: applyShortcutOverrides returns an item unchanged unless it has an action and an override (keyboardShortcuts.ts:262), so blueprint labels such as '⌘N' pass through. App.tsx:3565 passes 'windows' only to that function. menu.tsx:289 renders item.shortcut verbatim, and monet-react does no glyph translation. The dialog calls formatShortcut(pending.chord) and formatShortcut(current(command)) with no platform argument (Dialogs.tsx:2424, 2443). This matters only if Windows/Linux builds ship; bundle.targets 'all' covers bundle formats on the build host, not cross-platform builds.

findings.title: MCP input checks: view.setProof accepts any mode and reports success; layer.vectorMaskFromPath op is unchecked; doc.new description is wrong
findings.feature: MCP view.setProof / layer.vectorMaskFromPath / doc.new
findings.evidence: apps/vision/src/mcp/commands.ts:960 setProofMode takes `mode: string` and hands it straight to store.setProof, which stores it and turns proofing on (store.ts:3605-3625). An unknown id returns 'Proof mode set to X' with no effective proof. The manifest has no enum, so clients cannot discover the valid ids (the menu ids are proofcmyk, proofacescg and so on). vectorMaskFromPath (commands.ts:919) passes any number as `op`, although the documented range is 0..3. doc.new's description says 'replacing the current one' (commands.ts:52), but store.newDocument adds a new tab (store.ts:4918).
findings.repro: Call view.setProof({mode:"cmky"}) via MCP.
findings.impact: Agents build on a false success and misread the document lifecycle.
findings.suggested_fix: Make `mode` a string-literal union (codegen emits an enum) or validate against the proof ids the View ▸ Proof Setup menu uses. Throw on op outside 0..3. Fix the doc.new description to say it opens a new tab. Run mcp:codegen afterwards.
findings.verdict_reason: setProofMode passes any string to store.setProof, which stores it, sets proofOn true (store.ts:3605-3625) and casts it to ProofMode (EngineClient.ts:501). An unknown id reports success. proofPixel switches on the mode, so an unknown id probably does nothing visible rather than break anything. One part is overstated: the manifest description does list the valid ids (cmyk, acescg, aces2065, hdr-pq, hdr-hlg), and those are mode ids, not menu ids. vectorMaskFromPath forwards any op. addVectorMaskFromPath treats an out-of-range op as a replace (store.ts:7326), yet MCP reports 'Folded … (op N)'. doc.new says 'replacing the current one', but newDocument calls addDoc and opens a new tab (store.ts:4918).

findings.title: Edit ▸ Menus… opens the dialog on the Keyboard Shortcuts tab instead of the Menus tab
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Menus… (⌥⇧⌘M)
findings.evidence: PATH_WIRING routes 'Edit ▸ Menus…' to `keyboardshortcuts` (psMenus.ts:80), whose handler is `open("keyboardShortcuts")` with no argument (App.tsx:2708). The dialog opens on the Menus tab only when `arg === "menus"` (Dialogs.tsx:2184), and no caller ever passes that.
findings.repro: Choose Edit ▸ Menus… or press ⌥⇧⌘M.
findings.impact: The user lands on the wrong tab (Photoshop opens on the Menus tab).
findings.suggested_fix: Give Menus… its own id (for example `menuscustomize: () => open("keyboardShortcuts", "menus")`) via PATH_WIRING, and update psMenusCustomize.test.ts.
findings.verdict_reason: PATH_WIRING maps 'Edit ▸ Menus…' to 'keyboardshortcuts' (psMenus.ts:80), and the handler is open("keyboardShortcuts") with no argument (App.tsx:2708). The dialog picks the Menus tab only when arg === "menus" (Dialogs.tsx:2184). ⌥⇧⌘M also reaches this handler: Menus… sits in the same Edit list as Keyboard Shortcuts…, so uniq() gives it the id 'keyboardshortcuts-2' and its chord is not deduped away.

findings.title: A disabled menu item shows its Photoshop default shortcut even after the user rebinds or unbinds it
findings.feature: Keyboard shortcut overrides in menu hints
findings.evidence: applyShortcutOverrides returns items unchanged when `!item.action` (keyboardShortcuts.ts:262), and items disabled by enablement have no action (psMenus.ts:220-222, 376-382).
findings.repro: Rebind Edit ▸ Undo to ⌥⌘U in Keyboard Shortcuts. With nothing left to undo, the greyed Undo item shows ⌘Z again. If ⌘Z was given to another command, both items show ⌘Z.
findings.impact: The menu displays shortcuts that are no longer bound.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply overrides to every leaf that has an id, whether or not it has an action.
findings.verdict_reason: applyShortcutOverrides skips any item without an action (keyboardShortcuts.ts:262), and items disabled by enablement or the first-wins rule have no action (psMenus.ts:220-222, 375-379). A greyed item therefore keeps its blueprint shortcut label. In practice only the in-window menu shows these labels (Windows/Linux), because the macOS native bar shows no shortcuts at all.

findings.title: Filter ▸ Last Filter and Image ▸ Transform Symmetry stay enabled but silently do nothing
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Last Filter (⌥⌘F), Image ▸ Transform Symmetry
findings.evidence: `lastfilter: () => repeatLastFilter()` (App.tsx:3117) calls `lastFilter?.()`, which is null until a filter has run (app.ts:1494). `transformsymmetry: () => store.beginPaintSymmetryTransform()` (App.tsx:2799) returns immediately when paintSymmetry === 0 (store.ts:9646). Neither has a menuEnablement entry (App.tsx:3442-3469).
findings.repro: In a fresh session press ⌥⌘F, or choose Image ▸ Transform Symmetry with Paint Symmetry Off.
findings.impact: Commands look available but give no feedback when they cannot run (Photoshop greys them out).
findings.suggested_fix: Publish `canRepeatFilter` and `paintSymmetry !== 0` into menuEnablement, the same way canFade and canTransformAgain are handled.
findings.verdict_reason: lastfilter calls repeatLastFilter (App.tsx:3117), which is `lastFilter?.()` (app.ts:1494) and does nothing until a filter has run. transformsymmetry (App.tsx:2799) returns immediately when paintSymmetry === 0 (store.ts:9646). Neither id has an entry in menuEnablement (App.tsx:3442-3468), so both stay enabled with no feedback.

areas.coverage:
Read-only review. No builds or tests were run, and nothing was edited.

Inventory:
- tauri.conf.json: identifier, version, productName, 5 icons, targets "all", CSP, asset scope, and 5 file-association groups covering 60 extensions.
- 2 capability files: default.json has 15 grants plus an fs:scope with 15 denies; float.json has 5 grants.
- build.rs, plus all 6 native Rust modules (main, c2pa_sign, droplet, float, heic, model_dl; 5,188 lines). For model_dl I read the command layer and only skimmed the transfer internals.
- 11 registered plugins exposing 22 plugin commands (c2pa 5, heic 2, models 6, float 6, droplet 1, atomicsave 1, drag 1), plus 8 app-level monet-ui commands.
- 17 frontend call sites of native plugins, each traced from the UI through app.ts to Rust.
- monet-mcp: transport, auth and exposure only. I counted the 90 MCP commands in commands.ts but did not review what each one does.
- The recovery timer, the unsaved-work guard, the ErrorBoundary and the boot path.
- The macOS menu bridge (monet-react mac-menu.ts) and the monet-ui popup and new-window hook.
- Release gates: check-model-licenses.mjs, verify-release-bundle.mjs, Vite's selective public-asset copy, and the CI packaged-smoke job.
- Docs: README, both AGENTS.md files, durable-save.md, c2pa-signing.md, mcp.md, MODELS.md and THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md.

I checked framework behaviour against the locked crate sources in ~/.cargo: tauri 2.11.2 (IPC ACL check, JSON parsing of request bodies, Channel arguments), tauri-utils 2.9.2, tao 0.35.3, muda 0.19.2 and tauri-plugin-drag 2.1.1. I also looked at the existing dist bundle for features that need a newer WebKit.

Not verified at runtime: WKWebView behaviour, the signing/notarization environment on the self-hosted runner, and actual memory use. The 4-bit/pixel memory estimates are worked out from the code, not measured. Engine pixel correctness and per-feature menu semantics belong to other reviewers.
areas.parity_notes:
Photoshop menu items without a monetId are shown disabled and were not reported as bugs.

Release, native and security points compared with a typical desktop release:
- No auto-updater (Tauri updater absent).
- No crash reporter or log files, and no telemetry. Privacy matches the docs: no analytics SDKs, no remote fonts or CDNs, the CSP limits network access to self, IPC, asset and dev localhost:1420, and the app works offline.
- No single-instance handling on Windows or Linux.
- macOSPrivateApi: true rules out the Mac App Store.
- HEIC open and export use macOS ImageIO only, but the HEIC file associations are registered on every OS.
- Model downloading is deliberately disabled; Install from Disk (Import) is the only provisioning path, and it is currently blocked (see the permission finding).
- The C2PA default signer is a documented dev key; TSA timestamping is opt-in.

Checked and found sound:
- float windows run under a least-privilege capability (no event emit), and each input is stamped with its own document id.
- the MCP token is 48 hex characters from the OS CSPRNG and the server binds to 127.0.0.1.
- the scripting worker hides network, eval and Worker globals, and CSP blocks it from reaching the MCP port.
- the model importer validates paths and refuses symlinks.
- the droplet applet quotes paths correctly.
- check:models and verify:bundle are both enforced by build:release.
- the JS @tauri-apps packages are on the same minor version as the Rust tauri 2.11.x.
- boot failures are shown to the user through BootError.

Doc inaccuracies:
- docs/durable-save.md and the root AGENTS.md say Vision's saves are power-loss durable; the atomicsave permission is never granted, so they are not.
- The README says "License: MIT", but there is no LICENSE file for Vision.

findings.title: Quit (Cmd+Q, app menu, Dock, logout) exits immediately and throws away unsaved documents without asking
findings.feature: App menu > Quit / unsaved-work guard (native macOS)
findings.evidence: mac-menu.ts:187 installs the built-in Tauri 'Quit' menu item. muda-0.19.2 macos/mod.rs:994 maps that item to NSApp terminate:. tao-0.35.3 app_delegate.rs:62-65 and 131-135 only implement applicationWillTerminate, which calls AppState::exit(). tao has no applicationShouldTerminate, so the quit cannot be vetoed. Vision's only guard is window.onCloseRequested (apps/vision/src/state/app.ts:8362-8372), which terminate: never triggers. main.rs:406-413 run_return also ignores exit requests. Nothing in the frontend intercepts Cmd+Q (psMenuData.ts, App.tsx). The native e2e only tests closing the window (native-webview-e2e.mjs:985).
findings.repro: Open an image, paint a stroke, then press Cmd+Q (or Monet Vision > Quit, or Dock > Quit). The app exits with no 'Unsaved Changes' prompt. Relaunch: edits made since the last 10-minute recovery tick are gone, and all edits are gone if recovery is off or it is a debug build.
findings.impact: Silent loss of all unsaved work in the most common way macOS users quit. The #54 guard only covers the window close button.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the built-in Quit with a custom 'Quit Monet Vision' item (Cmd+Q) that dispatches to JS. That handler should run the dirty check and offer Save / Don't Save / Cancel, not today's yes/no 'Quit without saving?', then call exit. Also handle RunEvent::ExitRequested in main.rs. Dock quit and logout still go through terminate:, which tao cannot veto, so write recovery snapshots shortly after each edit (debounced) instead of only on the 10-minute timer. Add a native e2e check for Cmd+Q.
findings.verdict_reason: mac-menu.ts:187 uses PredefinedMenuItem 'Quit'. muda-0.19.2 macos/mod.rs:994 maps it to sel!(terminate:). tao-0.35.3 app_delegate.rs:62-65,131-135 registers only applicationWillTerminate (AppState::exit) and has no applicationShouldTerminate. I grepped tao, tauri-2.11.2, tauri-runtime-wry-2.11.2 and muda for any terminate veto and found none. Vision's only guard is onCloseRequested (app.ts:8362-8372), and its comment wrongly claims it also covers Cmd+Q. main.rs:406-413 run_return handles only RunEvent::Opened. No frontend handler binds Cmd+Q (grep KeyQ finds only tool-q). The native e2e (native-webview-e2e.mjs:984-999) only presses the window's Close. Recovery is off in dev and debug builds (app.ts:8161-8163), and in release the default is a 10-minute tick (autoRecover.ts:8). Snapshots do survive a terminate, so the loss is the edits since the last tick. That is still silent data loss on the most common macOS quit path.

findings.title: Every c2pa, heic, models and atomicsave call is refused by Tauri's permission check in the native app
findings.feature: File > Export > Content Credentials (Signed); Preferences > Content Credentials; File Info credentials; HEIC/HEIF open (file association) and File > Export > HEIC; AI Models Install from Disk / verify / remove; durable (fsync) saves
findings.evidence:
Tauri refuses any plugin command that no capability grants (tauri-2.11.2 src/webview/mod.rs:1823-1851: 'Command plugin:x|y not allowed by ACL').

build.rs:5-16 only declares the in-app plugins droplet and float, and capabilities/default.json only grants droplet and float from Vision's own plugins. gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json has no entry for c2pa, heic, models or atomicsave.

The frontend still calls those plugins:
- plugin:c2pa|… at app.ts:4977, 5012, 5040, 5050 and contentCredentials.ts:116
- plugin:heic|… at app.ts:5149 and 7146
- plugin:models|… at modelDownload.ts:136/153 and modelSource.ts:57
- plugin:atomicsave|atomic_write at monet-react atomic-write.ts:53

tauriConfig.test.ts:24-27 records the same failure for droplet (#469). Galerie's build.rs declares its plugins correctly. None of these were ever granted: the original scaffold (89d53207) had a plain tauri_build::build(). No test drives these commands in WKWebView.
findings.repro:
In a packaged or dev native build, try any of these:
- Double-click a .heic photo in Finder (Vision is registered for .heic): the open fails with 'Command plugin:heic|decode_heic not allowed by ACL'.
- File > Export > Content Credentials (Signed): error.
- Preferences > Content Credentials: error.
- AI Models > Install from Disk: fails.
- Save anything: the console logs 'durable save unavailable' and the save falls back to write + rename without fsync.
findings.impact: Several advertised features never work in the shipped app. MODELS.md says Install from Disk is the only way to get optional models (DRUNet, MI-GAN, SD, colorizer…) into a release, so none can be installed. The 'every app is power-loss durable' guarantee (AGENTS.md, docs/durable-save.md) does not hold. The same missing atomicsave grant affects every Monet app.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare c2pa, heic and models in build.rs as in-app plugins that allow all their commands, and grant c2pa:default, heic:default and models:default in default.json. atomicsave comes from the monet-ui crate, so give it a permission set there, or declare it the same way in each app's build.rs, and grant it. Before granting atomicsave, make atomic_write enforce the fs:scope deny list; it currently writes to any destination, which would bypass the #10 deny list. Extend tauriConfig.test.ts to find every `plugin:<name>|` call in src/ and assert it is granted. Correct the durable-save docs.
findings.verdict_reason: tauri-2.11.2 webview/mod.rs:1818-1851 rejects any plugin:* command when resolve_access (authority.rs:439-471) finds no allowed entry. build.rs declares only droplet and float. capabilities/default.json and float.json grant none of c2pa, heic, models or atomicsave. gen/schemas/acl-manifests.json lists only core, dialog, drag, droplet, float and fs. No add_capability call exists anywhere. The plugins are named Builder::new("c2pa"/"heic"/"models"/"atomicsave") at c2pa_sign.rs:577, heic.rs:17, model_dl.rs:1345 and atomic_save.rs:120. The frontend invokes them at app.ts:4977/5012/5040/5050/5149/7146, contentCredentials.ts:116, modelDownload.ts:136/153, modelSource.ts:57 and atomic-write.ts:53. openHeic has no fallback (app.ts:7138-7160). git log -S atomicsave shows it was never granted. atomicWriteBytes silently falls back to plugin-fs write+rename, so saves still land, but without fsync. HEIC open/export, signed Content Credentials and model import are broken outright.

findings.title: Every save and every recovery snapshot turns the whole file into a JSON number array, costing gigabytes of transient memory
findings.feature: Save / Save As / Export / recovery snapshots (atomicWriteBytes durable path)
findings.evidence: durableNativeWrite calls invoke('plugin:atomicsave|atomic_write', { destination, bytes: Array.from(bytes) }) on every save. The attempt is repeated every time; the one-time flag only silences the warning (atomic-write.ts:50-67, 79). Tauri JSON-encodes non-binary arguments. In the native process, tauri-2.11.2 ipc/protocol.rs:521-528 parses the body into a serde_json::Value before the permission check runs; that is about 32 bytes per array element. The recovery timer sends every dirty document through the same path every N minutes (app.ts:8205-8210). The c2pa and heic plugins already avoid this by sending raw bytes.
findings.repro: Open a large layered PSD or project and Save As .psd or .mvision in the native app. The webview holds an array of about N numbers (about 8N bytes) plus a JSON string of about 3.6N characters; then the native process builds an N-element Value array (about 32N bytes). The call is then refused (see the permission finding) and the file is written again through plugin-fs. A 100 MB file means several GB of transient memory in both processes; files over about 550 MB exceed the JS string limit.
findings.impact: Long pauses on every save and every recovery tick. On large documents the WebContent or main process can be killed for memory, losing every open document.
findings.suggested_fix: Send the bytes as a raw body and put the destination in a percent-encoded header, as sign_content_credentials does. In Rust, take a Request and read InvokeBody::Raw. Do this together with the permission fix. Consider also skipping the durable attempt after the first refusal.
findings.verdict_reason: atomic-write.ts:53-56 sends bytes: Array.from(bytes). It is tried on every native save when no operations are injected (line 82); warnedNoPlugin only silences the log. tauri-2.11.2 ipc/protocol.rs:521-528 does serde_json::from_slice::<Value> on a JSON body before the permission check, so every save pays about 32 bytes per byte in the native process and then gets refused (see the permission finding). Recovery ticks route dirty documents through the same path (app.ts:8210). heic and c2pa already use raw bodies. One correction: the '~550 MB JS string limit' is V8's. WKWebView/JSC allows about 2^31 characters, while Windows WebView2 (V8, about 2^29) would fail at roughly 150 MB files. The core cost stands.

findings.title: Dragging a layer out to Finder always fails: the drag call is missing the required onEvent channel
findings.feature: Layers panel > drag a layer thumbnail to the desktop as a PNG (native)
findings.evidence: layerDragOut.ts:51-55 calls invoke('plugin:drag|start_drag', { item, image, options }). tauri-plugin-drag-2.1.1 src/commands.rs:112-119 declares on_event: Channel<CallbackResult> as a required argument, and the plugin's own JS always passes onEvent (api-iife.js startDrag). Tauri reads a Channel argument as a required string (ipc/channel.rs:300-307), and a missing key returns 'command start_drag missing required key onEvent' (ipc/command.rs:97-101). layerDragOut.test.ts:75-79 asserts the call without onEvent, so the unit test locks in the bug. No native e2e covers the drag.
findings.repro: In the native app, drag a layer thumbnail from the Layers panel onto the Desktop. A toast says 'Layer export failed: invalid args `onEvent` for command `start_drag`…' and no file appears.
findings.impact: The advertised drag-out feature (commit cbc8f450) never works on desktop. It works only in the browser build, which uses DataTransfer.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass onEvent: new Channel() from @tauri-apps/api/core (or use the plugin's startDrag helper), and update the unit test to expect onEvent.
findings.verdict_reason: layerDragOut.ts:51-55 invokes plugin:drag|start_drag with only item, image and options. tauri-plugin-drag-2.1.1 commands.rs:112-119 takes on_event: Channel<CallbackResult> as a non-optional argument. Tauri's Channel CommandArg (ipc/channel.rs:299-313) deserializes a required String, and CommandItem returns 'command start_drag missing required key onEvent' when the key is absent (ipc/command.rs:95-101). drag:default does grant allow-start-drag, so the argument error is what fails. The native path runs whenever isTauri() (layerDragOut.ts:17-24), and Panels.tsx:981-989 turns the rejection into an error toast. layerDragOut.test.ts:75-79 asserts the call without onEvent, which locks in the bug.

findings.title: The default project format .mvision has no file association, so saved projects will not open from Finder
findings.feature: Bundle file associations / Save As default
findings.evidence: fileAssociations (tauri.conf.json:26-129) registers only 'mvis' as the Monet Vision Document. Save As defaults to the .mvision project format: suggestedSaveName gives 'Untitled.mvision' (nativeIoPolicy.ts:113) and SAVE_FILTERS lists 'mvision' first (app.ts:7609-7615). Recovery snapshots are .mvision too. launchOpen.test.ts:88 checks a list that also omits mvision. svg, pdf and artisan open from File > Open but are not associated either.
findings.repro: Save a new document (default name Untitled.mvision), quit, then double-click it in Finder. macOS reports that no application is set to open it, and Open With does not list Monet Vision.
findings.impact: Users cannot reopen their own saved projects the normal way. It looks like the file is broken.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'mvision' (role Editor) to the Monet Vision Document association, and add it to the launchOpen.test.ts list. Decide whether svg, pdf and artisan should be associated too.
findings.verdict_reason: tauri.conf.json:29-123 associates 'mvis' but not 'mvision', and there is no custom Info.plist in src-tauri. suggestedSaveName defaults to 'Untitled.mvision' and turns unsupported or copy-only extensions into .mvision (nativeIoPolicy.ts:105-119). SAVE_FILTERS lists mvision first (app.ts:7612-7613), and recovery files are .mvision (autoRecover.ts:25). launchOpen.test.ts:88 checks a list that omits mvision. Workarounds still exist (File > Open, dragging onto the app), so major rather than blocker.

findings.title: WASM memory has no ceiling: closing a document does not free it, and an out-of-memory crash leaves unsaved work unsaveable
findings.feature: Engine memory (all documents share one wasm32 linear memory)
findings.evidence:
closeDoc drops the engine without freeing it (store.ts:6294: 'dropped engine is GC-reclaimed (no eager free)'; the same at store.ts:4871). Freeing then depends on wasm-bindgen's FinalizationRegistry, which only runs when the JS heap is under pressure, not the WASM heap.

All documents live in one wasm memory (EngineClient.ts:191-193), capped at 4 GiB on wasm32. The engine allows 80 MP documents (raster/mod.rs:1050), and 32-bit layers keep a pixels_f32 buffer (raster/mod.rs:182), about 1.6 GB per 80 MP layer.

The engine has no fallible allocations: 0 try_reserve calls against 132 large vec! allocations in raster/mod.rs. The app never handles WebAssembly.RuntimeError or a poisoned engine (grep of src/ finds nothing).

After an out-of-memory trap, wasm-bindgen leaves the Engine's borrow flag set, so every later call on it, including project serialization for Save and for recovery, throws.
findings.repro: Open and close several large 16/32-bit documents in one session, or convert an 80 MP document to 32-bit and add layers and history. When memory.grow fails, the engine aborts. Afterwards Save or Save As on the affected document throws.
findings.impact: Hard crash, or a document that can no longer be saved, in long or large-document sessions. That is data loss for any work since the last recovery snapshot.
findings.suggested_fix: Free engines when a document closes (after its references are cleared; a deferred free if needed). Estimate each document's footprint from size × depth × (layers + history) and refuse or warn before crossing a budget below 4 GiB. Catch WebAssembly.RuntimeError at the EngineClient boundary, mark that engine poisoned, and tell the user. Keep other documents saveable, and write recovery snapshots of the healthy documents right away.
findings.verdict_reason: The code claims hold. store.ts:6294 and 4871-4873 never free the Engine eagerly. raster/mod.rs has 0 try_reserve against 662 vec! allocations. MAX_PIXELS is 80 MP (raster/mod.rs:1050), and 32-bit layers carry pixels_f32 as well as the u16 pixels (raster/mod.rs:179-182), so a single 80 MP 32-bit layer is about 1.9 GB. src/ has no RuntimeError or poisoned-engine handling. One nuance: the generated pkg does register EngineFinalization = new FinalizationRegistry(ptr => __wbg_engine_free) (monet_render_engine.js:8020-8022). Closed engines are therefore freed eventually, on a JS GC whose timing is independent of wasm-heap pressure, rather than never, and linear memory never shrinks. Hitting wasm32's 4 GiB is realistic for large multi-layer or 32-bit sessions. A mid-call trap leaving the wasm-bindgen borrow flag set, so later calls on that Engine (including Save serialization) throw, is standard wasm-bindgen behavior. Medium confidence on how often it happens.

findings.title: The repo has no macOS signing, notarization or hardened-runtime setup, and no release pipeline
findings.feature: Bundle / distribution
findings.evidence:
The bundle section has no macOS block (no signingIdentity, entitlements, hardenedRuntime or minimumSystemVersion) and no Windows signing settings (certificateThumbprint or signCommand).

The only packaging job (.github/workflows/ci.yml:300-353) runs 'tauri build --ci' on a self-hosted runner and passes no APPLE_* signing or notarization variables. Its smoke check needs an external adapter and runner variables. MEMORY.md notes that CI has run nothing since about July.

The repo has no release or notarization docs (docs/ listing) and no updater.
findings.repro: Run 'pnpm --filter monet-vision exec tauri build' on a clean machine and download the DMG on another Mac. Gatekeeper blocks the unsigned, un-notarized app, and macOS 15+ removed the Control-click override.
findings.impact: Public macOS/Windows users cannot install the app without security overrides.
findings.suggested_fix: Put signing and notarization in the repo: bundle.macOS.signingIdentity (or APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY) plus APPLE_API_KEY/ISSUER notarization variables in a release workflow, and a Windows signCommand. Document the release steps. Decide whether to use the Tauri updater or document manual updates.
findings.verdict_reason: tauri.conf.json's bundle block (lines 26-131) has no macOS or Windows signing, entitlements or minimumSystemVersion. git grep finds no APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY, APPLE_API_KEY, notarization, signCommand or hardenedRuntime in the repo. ci.yml:300-330 runs 'tauri build --ci' without signing env. One nuance: the packaged-smoke contract pins a codesign Team ID and authority (verify-packaged-smoke-result.mjs:126-181; the adapter contract), so the team expects signed bundles, and signing may come from the self-hosted runner's environment outside the repo. Nothing anywhere notarizes or staples, so Gatekeeper will still block downloads.

findings.title: The shipped third-party notices leave out every Rust crate and npm dependency, and Vision has no LICENSE file
findings.feature: Licenses / NOTICE
findings.evidence:
THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md is described as 'the attribution NOTICE copied to dist/ and the Tauri bundle'. Its sections cover only openjpeg2-pure-rs, the ONNX models, the ICC profile, ORT and Lensfun (headings at lines 19-320).

It omits:
- the native binary's crates (tauri, wry, tao, c2pa, rustls/ring, ureq, serde…)
- the WASM engine's crates (image, psd, rawloader, moxcms, tiny-skia, rustybuzz, ttf-parser, i_overlay…)
- the JS dependencies (react, @tauri-apps/*, @jsquash/avif, yjs…)

verify-release-bundle.mjs:21 only checks the files that already exist. The README says 'License: MIT', but the repo root and apps/vision have no LICENSE file; only packages/monet-ui/LICENSE exists.
findings.repro: Build the release and look inside the .app bundle: no file credits the MIT/Apache/BSD/ISC code compiled into the binary and the WASM.
findings.impact: Non-compliance with the attribution terms of MIT, BSD and Apache-2.0 in a binary distribution. Legal risk for a public release.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate the notices at build time: cargo-about (or cargo-license) for src-tauri and packages/engine, and license-checker or rollup-plugin-license for the JS bundle. Ship the result next to THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md and make verify:bundle require it. Add a LICENSE file for Vision.
findings.verdict_reason: The THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md headings (lines 19-320) cover only openjpeg2-pure-rs, the ONNX models, the ICC profile, ORT and Lensfun. verify-release-bundle.mjs:21 only checks that the existing notice files exist. The repo has no cargo-about, license-checker or rollup-plugin-license wiring. The repo root and apps/vision have no LICENSE; only packages/monet-ui/LICENSE exists, while apps/vision/README.md:76-79 claims MIT. The app has no acknowledgements screen. MIT, BSD and Apache attribution for the compiled-in crates (tauri, c2pa, image, psd, etc.) and the JS dependencies is missing from the binary distribution.

findings.title: The c2pa commands run on the macOS main thread, so signing, manifest reads and TSA requests can freeze the app
findings.feature: Content Credentials sign / read / signer info / import
findings.evidence: sign_content_credentials (471), c2pa_read_manifest (538), c2pa_signer_info (547), c2pa_import_signer (558) and c2pa_clear_signer (570) are all declared as plain synchronous commands. heic.rs:505-509 and its guard test explain that such commands run on the macOS main thread and block the event loop. Signing hashes the full export and every parent or placed ingredient file. Import trial-signs up to 4 algorithms. With a TSA URL set, Builder::sign makes an HTTP round-trip (the http_ureq feature). This only becomes visible once the permission finding is fixed.
findings.repro: After fixing the permission problem, set a TSA URL that is slow or cannot be reached, then run File > Export > Content Credentials (Signed) on a large TIFF. The UI and all other IPC stop responding until the network call times out.
findings.impact: UI freezes or apparent hangs during signed export and credential reads.
findings.suggested_fix: Mark these commands #[tauri::command(async)] and add the same guard test heic.rs has.
findings.verdict_reason: c2pa_sign.rs:471, 538, 547, 558 and 570 are plain #[tauri::command] non-async fns, which run as Blocking on the main thread. heic.rs:505-509 documents this and guards heic's own commands with a test. One correction: the TSA round-trip only happens with an imported custom certificate (active_signer passes the TSA only on the custom path, c2pa_sign.rs:345-349). The dev signer has none, but it still hashes the full export and its ingredients on the main thread. This only matters once the permission problem is fixed.

findings.title: The C2PA dev private key is committed to the repo and embedded in the release binary, and every signed export uses it by default
findings.feature: Content Credentials default signer
findings.evidence: SIGN_KEY = include_bytes!("../certs/es256-key.pem") (c2pa_sign.rs:40-41). certs/es256-key.pem is tracked in git (git ls-files). active_signer falls back to it whenever the user has not imported a certificate (c2pa_sign.rs:353-355). The UI labels it as a self-signed dev signer (Dialogs.tsx:1672-1677).
findings.repro: Extract es256-key.pem from the repo or the app binary and sign any image. It validates as the same 'Monet Vision Dev Signer' identity that genuine Vision exports carry.
findings.impact: Default signed exports prove nothing about origin, since anyone holding the key can forge the same identity. Shipping a private key in a release is also a poor look.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate a per-install key in app data on first use, or disable Signed export in release builds until a certificate is imported. Remove the key from the release binary, for example by limiting it to test builds with #[cfg(test)].
findings.verdict_reason: c2pa_sign.rs:40-41 include_bytes! the key into the binary, and git ls-files shows certs/es256-key.pem is tracked. active_signer falls back to it at c2pa_sign.rs:353-355. The UI labels it 'Development — self-signed, not publicly trusted' (Dialogs.tsx:1673-1677), and the code comment admits it is not a trust anchor. Anyone can still forge the same default identity. Minor because it is disclosed.

findings.title: The local MCP control server is always on with no opt-out, and an unauthenticated probe lets websites detect it
findings.feature: MCP server (monet-mcp)
findings.evidence: main.rs:330-338 starts the server on every GUI launch, and no Preferences option exists to turn it off. GET /mcp answers without auth (lib.rs:262-267) and every response carries Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * (lib.rs:391-411), so any web page can fetch http://127.0.0.1:48211/mcp and see that the app is running. mcp.json holding the token is written with default permissions via std::fs::write (lib.rs:429). The token is also accepted in the query string and compared without constant-time equality (lib.rs:367-388). Anyone with the token can save or export to any path and build droplet apps (commands.ts:296-392).
findings.repro: While Vision runs, a web page calls fetch('http://127.0.0.1:48211/mcp') and reads {"server":"monet-mcp"}. On Linux with a home directory other users can read, another local user reads ~/.config/dev.monet.vision/mcp.json and drives the app.
findings.impact: A privacy leak (the running app can be fingerprinted), plus a cross-user control risk on permissive Linux setups. The user is never told that a control port is open.
findings.suggested_fix: Require auth on GET or drop the probe. Restrict CORS to no origin. Write mcp.json with 0600 permissions. Use constant-time comparison. Add a Preferences toggle for the MCP server, and consider making it off by default for release builds.
findings.verdict_reason: main.rs:330-338 starts monet_mcp for every non-CLI launch, and no Preferences toggle exists (the only 'MCP' in Dialogs.tsx is at line 11527, unrelated). lib.rs:265-269 answers GET /mcp without auth. cors() at lib.rs:397-411 sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *. authorized() at lib.rs:367-388 accepts ?token= and uses plain == comparison. write_connection_file (lib.rs:415-433) uses std::fs::write with default permissions. The server binds to 127.0.0.1 only, so the risk is fingerprinting plus local cross-user access.

findings.title: The fs:scope deny list misses other files that auto-execute or hold credentials
findings.feature: Capabilities / fs scope
findings.evidence:
The deny list (default.json:24-40, pinned by tauriConfig.test.ts:36-52) exists 'to stop a renderer compromise from owning the next shell/login' (#10). It still allows writes to:
- $HOME/.gitconfig (core.fsmonitor or hooksPath runs code on any git command)
- $HOME/.zlogin, .zlogout, .bash_login
- $HOME/.vimrc
- $HOME/Library/Preferences (for example Terminal startup commands)
- $HOME/.npmrc, .git-credentials, .cargo/credentials.toml
The grant is still fs:write-all with scope '**'.
findings.repro: Code-review only. A compromised renderer can call plugin-fs writeTextFile('~/.gitconfig', '[core]\n fsmonitor = <cmd>'), and the command runs on the user's next git status.
findings.impact: The #10 defense-in-depth goal is not met. The same write-to-code-execution path the list was meant to block remains open.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the missing entries. Better, narrow the write scope to the user's document folders plus files chosen in dialogs (paths from the dialog plugin are scoped automatically), rather than '**' minus a list that will never be complete.
findings.verdict_reason: The macOS/Linux repro fails. tauri-2.11.2 scope/fs.rs:198-219 sets require_literal_leading_dot=true on unix by default. tauri.conf.json has no plugins.fs override, and plugin-fs resolve_path (commands.rs:1537-1567) builds its scope with that default, so the '**' allow pattern cannot match any path with a leading-dot component. writeTextFile('~/.gitconfig') and every other listed dotfile (.zlogin, .vimrc, .npmrc, .git-credentials, .cargo/credentials.toml) are already refused on macOS and Linux; the existing dotfile deny entries there are redundant belt-and-braces. Still open: Windows, where the default is false so %USERPROFILE%\.gitconfig is writable, and macOS ~/Library/Preferences (no leading dot). The Preferences escalation (for example, Terminal startup commands via a direct plist write) is unverified because cfprefsd may overwrite it. Settling it needs a Windows or plist write test.
