findings.title: The ErrorBoundary replaces the UI with an error screen that offers no save or recovery
findings.feature: Crash handling (render errors)
findings.evidence: ErrorBoundary.tsx:35-46 renders BootError in place of the whole app and only logs the error. It does not call writeRecoverySnapshots() (app.ts:8178). The documents are still intact in engine memory, but the user has no way to save them and will usually quit, which then loses the work (see the Quit finding).
findings.repro: Trigger any render exception (a bug in any panel). The window turns into 'Monet Vision hit an unexpected error' with no action, and work since the last recovery tick is lost when the app is closed.
findings.impact: One UI bug turns into loss of up to 10 minutes of work, or all of it when recovery is off.
findings.suggested_fix: In componentDidCatch, run writeRecoverySnapshots() right away (it only needs the engine and fs, not React). Show 'Your documents were saved for recovery — Relaunch', and offer a retry that remounts App.
findings.verdict_reason: ErrorBoundary.tsx:35-46 only logs and renders BootError. It is the only boundary (main.tsx:95), so any render throw replaces the whole app. One mitigation: the recovery timer is started at module level (app.ts:8293), not from React, so snapshots keep being written after the error screen appears in release builds. The loss is therefore bounded by the last tick, as the finding says.

findings.title: On Windows and Linux a second launch reports the running session's recovery files as a crash and deletes them
findings.feature: Crash recovery / multi-instance (Windows, Linux)
findings.evidence: Vision has no single-instance plugin, so on Windows and Linux opening a file from Explorer or a file manager starts a new process. That process runs recoverLastSession (app.ts:8237-8277) against the shared appData/recovery folder. The running instance's live snapshots show up as 'from a session that ended unexpectedly', and restoreRecoveryFiles removes each one whether or not the user restores it (autoRecover.ts:57-76). The new process also rewrites mcp.json and takes over MCP clients. On macOS, LaunchServices sends the file to the running app instead, unless it was started with open -n.
findings.repro: On Windows, run Vision and edit a document until a recovery tick has written a snapshot. Double-click another PNG in Explorer. A second window asks to recover the first window's document; answer No. The first instance's snapshot is now deleted.
findings.impact: A false crash prompt, and the running session loses its crash protection.
findings.suggested_fix: Add tauri-plugin-single-instance and forward the new launch's file arguments to the running instance's open queue. Alternatively, put the process id in recovery file names or lock files so a live session's snapshots are never offered.
findings.verdict_reason: Cargo.toml and main.rs have no single-instance plugin. Every non-CLI process runs recoverLastSession at module load (app.ts:8293) against the shared appData/recovery folder, and restoreRecoveryFiles removes every file when restore=false (autoRecover.ts:57-76). The first instance's recoverySnapshots map still records the revision, so planRecovery will not rewrite that snapshot until the document changes again. The second process also takes the next MCP port and rewrites mcp.json.

findings.title: Saving over a symlinked document replaces the link, and the save drops the original file's attributes
findings.feature: Atomic save (both the native and plugin-fs paths)
findings.evidence: Both paths write a temp file and rename it over the destination path: atomic_save.rs:84-98 (fs::rename(&temp, &destination)) and atomic-write.ts:79-88. When the destination is a symlink, the link itself is replaced by a regular file and the real target keeps the old contents. Permissions, Finder tags and extended attributes, ACLs and hard links of the original are not carried over.
findings.repro: Create ~/Desktop/art.psd as a symlink to /Volumes/Work/art.psd. Open it, edit, and Save. /Volumes/Work/art.psd is unchanged and ~/Desktop/art.psd is now a separate file.
findings.impact: Edits land in the wrong file. Users who keep canonical files behind links, or share read-only permission setups, get silently diverging copies.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the destination with realpath before building the temp path, and rename over the resolved target. Copy mode and extended attributes from the existing file to the temp file before the rename (fcopyfile or clonefile metadata on macOS).
findings.verdict_reason: atomic_save.rs:86-98 builds the temp path as a sibling of the unresolved destination and calls fs::rename(temp, destination), which replaces the link itself. The fallback does the same: tauri-plugin-fs-2.5.1 rename (commands.rs:806-830) calls std::fs::rename on the resolved-but-not-canonicalized path; resolve_path only follows symlinks for the scope check (is_forbidden). Neither app.ts nor atomic-write.ts calls realpath or lstat. Mode and xattrs are not copied onto the temp file.

findings.title: Command-line jobs print nothing on Windows (GUI subsystem), yet droplets on Windows only work from the command line
findings.feature: Command line: --run-script / --play-action / droplet.json (Windows)
findings.evidence: main.rs:5 sets windows_subsystem = "windows" in release builds, so println!/eprintln! (main.rs:316, 374-379, 415) have no console. cmd.exe does not wait for GUI-subsystem programs, so exit codes are not visible either. droplet.rs:104 tells non-macOS users to 'run that with: monet-vision <droplet.json> <images…>'.
findings.repro: On Windows, run the release binary with --run-script test.js from cmd.exe. No log, usage text or errors appear, and %ERRORLEVEL% does not reflect the job's result.
findings.impact: The command-line automation documented for Windows cannot be scripted or diagnosed.
findings.suggested_fix: When a CLI job is detected, call AttachConsole(ATTACH_PARENT_PROCESS) before printing. Alternatively ship a small console-subsystem companion binary for command-line use.
findings.verdict_reason: main.rs:5 sets windows_subsystem="windows" in release. The CLI results go through println!/eprintln! (main.rs:316, 374-379, 415), and there is no AttachConsole or windows-sys usage. droplet.rs:103-105 tells non-macOS users to run 'monet-vision <droplet.json> <images…>'. The jobs still produce their output files, and stdout redirected to a file still works, so this is a diagnosability gap rather than a broken feature.

findings.title: No minimum macOS version is set (Tauri defaults to 10.13), but the bundle needs WebKit from Safari 15.4 or later
findings.feature: Bundle / OS support
findings.evidence: The config has no bundle.macOS.minimumSystemVersion, so Tauri writes LSMinimumSystemVersion 10.13. vite.config.ts builds for es2022, and the shipped main bundle uses structuredClone and Object.hasOwn (checked in dist/assets/main-*.js), both Safari 15.4+. Tauri 2 itself needs macOS 10.15 or later.
findings.repro: Install on macOS 10.15–12.2 with the system WebKit. The main module fails to parse, so not even BootError renders; the user sees an empty transparent window.
findings.impact: The app installs on systems where it cannot start, with no explanation.
findings.suggested_fix: Set bundle.macOS.minimumSystemVersion to the oldest OS the team tests (probably 13.0), and state the supported OS in the README.
findings.verdict_reason: tauri.conf.json has no bundle.macOS block. tauri-utils config.rs:691-693 defaults minimum_system_version to 10.13. vite.config.ts:127 targets es2022, and dist/assets/main-*.js contains structuredClone (2 hits) and Object.hasOwn (14). One correction: those are runtime APIs that throw when called, not parse errors, so the exact 'empty window, fails to parse' symptom is unproven, though es2022 syntax may also fail to parse on old WebKit. The substance holds: the app installs on OS versions it cannot run on.

findings.title: The version number is hard-coded in six places and nothing checks that they agree
findings.feature: Versioning / About box / C2PA claim generator
findings.evidence:
"0.1.0" appears in:
- package.json
- tauri.conf.json:4
- src-tauri/Cargo.toml:4
- mcp.config.json
- nativeIoPolicy.ts:11 (feeds the About dialog at Dialogs.tsx:2159 and the container stamp)
- c2pa_sign.rs:66 (the version in the MANIFEST_JSON claim generator)
No test compares them.
findings.repro: Bump tauri.conf.json to 0.2.0 for a release. The About box, saved project containers and signed C2PA manifests still say 0.1.0.
findings.impact: Wrong version in support reports and in provenance claims.
findings.suggested_fix: Take the version from one source. In Rust, use env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION") in c2pa_sign.rs. In the frontend, use getVersion() from @tauri-apps/api/app or a define from package.json. Add a test asserting package.json, tauri.conf.json and Cargo.toml match.
findings.verdict_reason: '0.1.0' is a literal in package.json:4, mcp.config.json:3, tauri.conf.json:4, Cargo.toml:4, nativeIoPolicy.ts:11 (VISION_CONTAINER_APP, feeding the About dialog at Dialogs.tsx:2159) and c2pa_sign.rs:66 (claim_generator_info). There is no getVersion, CARGO_PKG_VERSION or define. The '0.1.0' strings in tests are fixtures, not consistency checks.

findings.title: Filter > Browse Filters Online… does nothing in the native app
findings.feature: Filter > Browse Filters Online…
findings.evidence: The browsefilters handler calls window.open('https://exchange.adobe.com/…PHSP'). In the native app, monet-ui's new-window hook refuses every URL except its own popups (popup.rs:66-69), and no URL-opener plugin is installed (Dialogs.tsx:2518-2520 says the same). In the browser build it opens Adobe's Photoshop plug-in marketplace, whose plug-ins cannot run in Vision.
findings.repro: In the desktop app, choose Filter > Browse Filters Online…. Nothing happens.
findings.impact: An enabled menu item that does nothing, and one that sends browser users to an unrelated store.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the monetId so the item shows disabled, or add tauri-plugin-opener and point it at Vision's own documentation.
findings.verdict_reason: App.tsx:3107 calls window.open with the Adobe Exchange URL. monet-ui popup.rs on_new_window denies any URL that popup_label() does not recognize as a Monet popup, and denies everything off macOS. No opener plugin is in Cargo.toml or package.json, and Dialogs.tsx:2517-2518 notes the same limitation. The item is enabled but does nothing in the desktop app.

findings.title: Enabled Preferences items open empty panes (Scratch Disks, Plug-Ins, Technology Previews, Product Improvement)
findings.feature: Edit > Preferences submenu
findings.evidence: psMenuData.ts:888, 893, 895 and 896 give these items monetIds, so they are enabled. They have no entry in PREF_PANES (Dialogs.tsx:2048-2061), so they show 'No configurable options for this pane in this build.'
findings.repro: Choose Edit > Preferences > Scratch Disks…. The pane is empty.
findings.impact: Placeholders presented as working features. Scratch Disks in particular suggests a memory limit that does not exist (see the WASM memory finding).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the monetIds so these items show disabled, or give Product Improvement a one-line 'No telemetry is collected' statement and Scratch Disks a note on memory limits.
findings.verdict_reason: psMenuData.ts:888, 893, 895 and 896 carry monetIds, and App.tsx:2718-2726 routes them to open('preferences', …). None of these four is in PREF_PANES (Dialogs.tsx:2048-2061) or PREF_INLINE_PANES (Dialogs.tsx:2065), so Dialogs.tsx:2141-2142 renders 'No configurable options for this pane in this build.'

findings.title: A release panic aborts the app instantly, and nothing records a log
findings.feature: Native crash and log handling
findings.evidence: The release profile uses panic = "abort" (Cargo.toml:44). There is no panic hook, no log plugin and no log file, and all native diagnostics are eprintln!, which goes nowhere for apps launched from Finder. Devtools are off in release. c2pa_read_manifest parses untrusted user files (contentCredentials.ts:116), so any panic inside c2pa-rs kills the whole process along with every unsaved document.
findings.repro: Code-review only. Any Rust panic in a command, for example on a malformed image with an embedded manifest, ends the process with no dialog and no log.
findings.impact: Instant loss of unsaved work on a native panic, and no information to diagnose user reports.
findings.suggested_fix: Install a panic hook that writes to a log file in app data, and add tauri-plugin-log with a file target. Consider panic = "unwind" for the Tauri binary, so async command panics become errors instead of aborts; confirm the LTO reason in the Cargo.toml comment still holds.
findings.verdict_reason: Cargo.toml:44 sets panic = "abort" in the release profile. There is no std::panic::set_hook and no tauri-plugin-log, and diagnostics are eprintln!, which Finder launches discard. I regraded this from polish to minor: it is not cosmetic, since any native panic kills every open document with no dialog and leaves no diagnostic trail for support. The risk is conditional on a panic actually occurring. Note that panic=unwind would only help async commands; a panic inside a sync command or an Obj-C callback still aborts.

findings.title: About 1,000 lines of disabled download code still ship in the binary
findings.feature: Model provisioning
findings.evidence: download_model returns Err before reading any input (model_dl.rs:1177-1186) and is marked #[allow(unreachable_code)]. The code after it, plus download_to, redirect handling and the https_only client (about lines 216-262 and 1012-1160), is 'retained for its unit tests'. The cancel_download command still ships, and modelDownload.ts:48-58 keeps a matching unreachable JS path.
findings.repro: n/a
findings.impact: Dead code and extra attack surface in the release binary, and it confuses the no-download policy.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the transfer code under #[cfg(test)] or delete it, drop download_model and cancel_download from the registered commands, and remove the dead JS.
findings.verdict_reason: model_dl.rs:1165-1186 returns Err before touching any input, under #[allow(unreachable_code)], yet download_model and cancel_download are still registered (model_dl.rs:1346-1353). modelDownload.ts:48-58 keeps a matching unreachable path after an unconditional throw. The 'extra attack surface' part is overstated: the early return means the renderer cannot reach the transfer code. It is dead weight and a source of confusion rather than a live risk.

areas.coverage:
Known issues: `gh issue list --state open` returns no open issues for Legoless/monet-core, so there were no open issues to classify. Instead I reviewed the closed ones:
- 503 closed issues in total (498 completed, 5 not planned). 94 were closed in the last 30 days, 74 of them Vision-area, 2026-09-04 to 09-20. I read the closing comments of all 94 and pulled out every stated caveat.
- Recent bug fixes #484–#503: confirmed each fix is present in code and has a regression test that cites its number (CanvasView.test.ts, projectEnvelope.ts:598, app.ts:6319/7639, mac-menu.ts:207, dockable-core.ts:335, perDocumentTools.test.ts and others).
- The 3 "not planned" bugs are duplicates of fixed issues. #117 points to #224, fixed at monet-photo xmp.ts:931-934. #173 points to #101, fixed in store.setGlobalLight (store.ts:8590-8605). #210 is outside Vision.
- #488 was closed, but most of its defect still reproduces in the shipped path (finding 2).

Parity ledgers:
- Read docs/plans/README.md, 08-open-items.md, the "Known limits" in 11-universal-container.md, the Vision README and AGENTS.md, and the docs/issue-proofs README.
- Grepped apps/vision/src, apps/vision/src-tauri/src and packages/engine/src. Results: 1 TODO or FIXME (engine vector/render.rs:3314), 0 "not implemented" or unimplemented!, 42 user-facing unsupported/not-available messages, and 249 deliberate-shortcut comments, all read for user-visible ceilings.
- Menu inventory from psMenuData.ts: 687 leaf items, 610 with a monetId, 77 without. About 50 of those 77 are wired by LABEL_WIRING and PATH_WIRING in psMenus.ts.
- Listed every App.tsx menu action that opens a dialog under a different name, and every "…" item that runs without a dialog.

Not done: no builds or tests were run (code reading only). I did not re-verify the roughly 400 issues closed in August beyond sampling the critical ones (#24, #237). PSD export of pattern-overlay effects was not traced.

Process risk, not a code finding: the closing comments on every issue since 5 Sep say GitHub Actions jobs exit with 0 steps because of an account billing block. All verification is local, and CI is not a release gate.
areas.parity_notes:
Placeholders that are correctly disabled (no monetId and no wiring):
- File ▸ Browse in Bridge and Close and Go to Bridge, Invite to Edit, Share, Share for Review, Import ▸ WIA Support.
- Edit ▸ Adobe PDF Presets, Edit ▸ Remote Connections.

Of the 77 blueprint items without a monetId, the rest (OpenType features and Stylistic Sets 1–20, Font Preview Size, East Asian, Photomerge, Sky, Check Spelling, Create Droplet, Script Events Manager, DICOM and so on) are wired through LABEL_WIRING and PATH_WIRING.

Partial implementations presented as working. Each is disclosed somewhere in the code or a closing comment, but none is a full Photoshop equivalent:
- **Merge to HDR Pro…:** has no dialog. It merges the document's visible layers with fitted exposures and hardcoded ghost removal (App.tsx:2804-2809).
- **Photomerge, Auto-Align, Auto-Blend:** run immediately on layers, with no dialogs.
- **Smart Object ▸ Stack Mode:** produces a merged layer, not a re-editable smart stack.
- **Save for Web GIF:** has no Colors, Dither or Lossy controls (app.ts:5278).
- **Image Processor copyright:** only JPEG and PNG receive it (disclosed in the dialog).
- **Content-Aware Fill:** Edit ▸ Fill ▸ Content-Aware and path fill still use the diffusion fill (#430).
- **Vanishing Point:** planes are not saved with the document. There is no Measure, Render Grids or 3D/DXF export (#447).
- **Clone Source:** slots are session-only. There is no Clipped, Auto Hide, Invert or Offset (#427).
- **32-bit float:** Photo Filter, Channel Mixer, Vibrance, and the noise and distort filters still refuse (#434).

Documentation:
