The parity gaps listed in my memory ledger as still open on 2026-07-20 (LaMa tier, waveform, BPC) are now in the code: LaMa at app.ts:2004-2024, the waveform in Panels and MCP, and BPC per plans/08 §4.

findings.title: Layer Style patterns are not saved in the document; 'Defined' follows whatever pattern is active in the app
findings.feature: Layer ▸ Layer Style ▸ Pattern Overlay / Bevel Texture / Stroke (pattern fill)
findings.evidence: mod.rs:3452-3461: style_patterns is pushed from the app-level TS library and the comment says 'the document carries the id, not the pixels … reopening it where that pattern is absent renders the checker'. Neither the engine's defined-pattern slot (self.pattern, set at mod.rs:19728-19744) nor style_patterns is written by any serializer. projectEnvelope.ts has no pattern field (grep count 0). store.ts:9905 says the Patterns library is 'localStorage only, so patterns do not travel with a project'. effects.ts:62-65 keeps 'Defined' (kind 3) as a live option that samples the single global slot. store.selectPattern (store.ts:9842-9848) repoints that slot with no history entry and no dirty flag, and definePattern (store.ts:9833-9836) says the same. On reopen, store.ts:2946 fills an empty slot with whichever preset is active at that moment. Library tiles are keyed by a hash of the pattern name (effects.ts:77), so renaming or deleting a preset orphans the style (Dialogs.tsx:12180-12187 shows '(missing pattern)').
findings.repro: 1) Define two patterns A and B. 2) On a layer, add a Pattern Overlay with Pattern = Defined while A is active. 3) Pick B in the Patterns panel or Edit ▸ Fill: the existing overlay re-renders as B, with no history step and no unsaved marker. 4) Alternatively save as .mvision, relaunch or open on another machine, and reopen: the overlay renders the checker, or whichever pattern happens to be active. A library pattern that is renamed or deleted, or a file sent to another user, renders the checker as well.
findings.impact: A saved document is not self-contained. Its appearance, and every export or print of it, silently changes after reopening or after an unrelated pattern pick. Photoshop embeds these patterns in the document. No test covers a reopen.
findings.suggested_fix: Store the tile pixels (or a per-document pattern table) with the document, in MVSN or the project envelope, and give the engine a per-document style-pattern table populated on load. Convert a 'Defined' pick into a document-owned tile id when the effect is applied, so a later Patterns-panel pick cannot change it. Add an e2e test: apply the overlay, save, clear the library, reopen, compare pixels.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed. The engine field style_patterns (mod.rs:3452-3461) carries a ponytail note that says a document stores only the pattern id. save_project (mod.rs:30790ff) writes self.contours, saved_sels, spot_channels and other fields, but never self.pattern or style_patterns. projectEnvelope.ts has no pattern field, and the library lives only in localStorage (store.ts:9905-9908). selectPattern (store.ts:9842-9848) calls e.set_pattern, which clears fx_cache and recomposites (mod.rs:19733-19745), with no history entry and no dirty flag. Its caller is the PatternPicker swatch (Dialogs.tsx:5688), which the Fill dialog also uses, so repro step 3 holds for an effect set to 'Defined' (kind 3). The Layer Style picker offers 'Defined' next to library ids (Dialogs.tsx:12170-12190). One refinement: with a library-id pattern, reopening on the same machine renders correctly because localStorage persists. The loss affects 'Defined' after a relaunch, since the active slot starts empty (store.ts:9910-9912), a file opened on another machine, and a renamed or deleted preset, which is keyed by an FNV hash of the name (effects.ts:77-84). Major is the right grade: the saved document is not self-contained, and a shared file silently changes appearance.

findings.title: Color Settings ▸ Working Spaces CMYK, Gray and Spot have no effect on the shipped proof or export (closed #488 still reproduces)
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Color Settings ▸ Working Spaces; View ▸ Proof Colors / Gamut Warning; File ▸ Export ▸ Export CMYK PSD
findings.evidence: store.ts:2576-2586: workingCmykProfile() always fetches /profiles/ISOcoated_v2_300_eci.icc, whatever colorPolicyPrefs.workingCmyk is. That profile is what the CMYK PSD writer uses (app.ts:3490-3492), and it is bundled at public/profiles. The default proof mode is 'cmyk' (store.ts:1569), so refreshIccProof installs the ICC LUT, and EngineClient.applyDisplayRect (EngineClient.ts:596-620) and outOfGamutMask (:661-676) take the ICC branch. The #488 fix (commit 3d17c76b) only passed `press` into the 'profile-free heuristics (no press profile available)' fallback, and its message says 'The ICC-based proof path is unchanged'. workingGray and workingSpot have no consumer outside the dialog and colorManagement.ts. The dialog still echoes the chosen press numbers (Dialogs.tsx:2876-2881). The default label is 'U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2' (colorManagement.ts:25), but separations and the embedded profile are ISOcoated v2.
findings.repro: 1) Edit ▸ Color Settings. Set CMYK to 'U.S. Web Uncoated v2'. The readout shows 22% dot gain and 260% total ink. 2) View ▸ Proof Colors or Gamut Warning: no change compared with SWOP, because the ICC proof comes from ISOcoated_v2. 3) Export CMYK PSD: the plates and embedded ICC are ISOcoated_v2 under every choice. 4) Change Gray or Spot: nothing reads them.
findings.impact: Enabled color-management controls give a prepress user wrong output while the dialog claims otherwise. The closed issue suggests the gap is fixed, but it is not. The only regression test is a proofPixel unit test on the fallback path.
findings.suggested_fix: Simplest honest fix: disable Gray and Spot, and disable the CMYK picker or relabel it as 'ISO Coated v2 (bundled)', with a note, until more press profiles ship. Proper fix: bundle one ICC per offered CMYK space and select it by id in workingCmykProfile() (add workingCmyk to the refreshIccProof cache key). Apply the Gray working dot gain in Image ▸ Mode ▸ Grayscale. Reopen #488 and add an e2e test asserting that two working spaces give different proof pixels in the ICC branch.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed. workingCmykProfile() and fetchProofProfile() (store.ts:2576-2587) always fetch /profiles/ISOcoated_v2_300_eci.icc, and it is the only profile in public/profiles. refreshIccProof's cache key (store.ts:2595-2597) does not include workingCmyk. The default proofMode is 'cmyk' (store.ts:1569). In EngineClient.applyDisplayRect (EngineClient.ts:611-627) the ICC branch uses sampleProofLut only, and `press` is read only in the 'profile-free heuristics' else branch. outOfGamutMask (EngineClient.ts:661-676) is the same. The #488 handler in setColorPolicyPrefs (store.ts:6891-6894) re-pushes setProof options, which the ICC branch ignores. cmykPsdBytes (app.ts:3490-3492) and the other CMYK export paths (Dialogs.tsx:5390, app.ts:4650, mcp/commands.ts:132) all take the same fixed profile. workingGray and workingSpot are read only by the dialog and by normalize/presets in monet-color. The message of commit 3d17c76b says the ICC path is unchanged, and gh reports #488 as CLOSED. The default label 'U.S. Web Coated (SWOP) v2' (monet-color colorManagement.ts:25) does not match the embedded ISOcoated v2 profile.

findings.title: On the Home screen (no document open) every command outside a narrow list is disabled, including Help ▸ About, Keyboard Shortcuts, Batch, Image Processor and file-creating commands
findings.feature: Home start screen (#476): menu enablement
findings.evidence: App.tsx:77 `NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS = /^(new|openf|clearrecent|browse|search|colorsettings|pref[a-z]*|exportprefs|customizetoolbar)$/`. App.tsx:3440-3467 sets every other id to false ('last, so no per-command flag can re-enable'), and psMenus.ts:216-221 drops disabled actions. The dispatcher (App.tsx:3335) also refuses them. Among the refused commands, these open or create their own document or need none: opensmartobject (app.ts:7413), opengif, loadfilesstack and loaddicom (stackImages opens a new document first, app.ts:7735), videoframes, scriptbrowse, script, batch, imageprocessor, presetmanager, and Help's about/systeminfo/keyboardshortcuts (About guards engine.version() in a try, Dialogs.tsx:2156). The comment at App.tsx:74-76 says the list is 'the ones that create/open one, and preferences'. No test covers the Home enable set (appCommands.test.ts:20 only mentions it).
findings.repro: Launch Vision. The Home screen appears. Open Help: About Monet Vision… and Keyboard Shortcuts… are greyed out. So are File ▸ Automate ▸ Batch…, File ▸ Scripts ▸ Image Processor…, Load Files into Stack…, Load Multiple DICOM Files…, File ▸ Open as Smart Object…, File ▸ Import ▸ Open GIF as Animation…, Video Frames to Layers…, and Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts/Menus…
findings.impact: At launch the user has to create a throwaway document before they can batch-process, stack files, open DICOM or GIF animations, or even open About. Photoshop allows all of these with no document open.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the document-independent ids to NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS (about, systeminfo, keyboardshortcuts, presetmanager, opensmartobject, opengif, loadfilesstack, loaddicom, videoframes, scriptbrowse, script, batch, imageprocessor, createdroplet, scripteventsmanager, loaddroplet). Add a unit test that pins the Home-enabled set.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed. NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS (App.tsx:77) excludes about, systeminfo, keyboardshortcuts, batch, imageprocessor, opensmartobject, opengif, loadfilesstack, loaddicom, videoframes, script, scriptbrowse and presetmanager (handlers at App.tsx:2566-2992). The enablement map sets them all to false last (App.tsx:3440-3467). buildMenus filters out actions set to false (psMenus.ts:219-221), and the dispatcher wrapper refuses them too (App.tsx:3335). The refused commands really are document-independent. openAsSmartObject (app.ts:7413) routes through routeOpen, which opens a document. stackImages (app.ts:7735) opens the first file as a new document before importing the rest. importVideoFramesToLayers builds its own items. About wraps engine.version() in a try (Dialogs.tsx:2156). The Home screen renders when no document is open (App.tsx:3745). No test pins the Home-enabled set (grep finds NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS only in App.tsx). This is a UX gap with a workaround (create a document first), so minor is right.

findings.title: The default project format .mvision is not registered as a file association in the bundle
findings.feature: File ▸ Save / Save As (default project format), Finder double-click
findings.evidence: nativeIoPolicy.ts:105-113 makes `${stem}.mvision` and 'Untitled.mvision' the suggested save name. SAVE_FILTERS lists 'Monet Vision Project' (mvision) first (app.ts:7613-7614), and the app's own recovery and smart-contents files are .mvision (app.ts:2797, 8154). bundle.fileAssociations (tauri.conf.json:29-127) registers image formats, psd/psb/xcf, RAW, mvis and the other apps' containers, but not mvision or artisan. `git log` shows mvision was never associated.
findings.repro: Save a document with the default name (Untitled.mvision) and double-click it in Finder. macOS does not know it belongs to Monet Vision: the file has a generic icon and no default app.
findings.impact: The app's own default save format cannot be reopened from the OS. Users must go through File ▸ Open or Open With.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an association entry for ["mvision"] (role Editor, a document icon) and optionally ["artisan"]. Or switch the default project extension to the already-associated .mvis.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed. Parsing tauri.conf.json bundle.fileAssociations gives these extension groups: images, psd/psb/xcf, RAW, ['mvis'] as Editor, and the other apps' containers as Viewer. Neither mvision nor artisan is present, and there is no platform-specific conf or Info.plist override in src-tauri/. withProjectExtension/suggestedSaveName (nativeIoPolicy.ts:105-113) default to Untitled.mvision. SAVE_FILTERS lists 'Monet Vision Project' (mvision) first (app.ts:7613-7614). `git log -S'"mvision"'` on tauri.conf.json returns nothing, so it was never associated. Opening through File ▸ Open still works, so minor is right.

findings.title: Filter ▸ Browse Filters Online… does nothing in the desktop app
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Browse Filters Online…
findings.evidence: App.tsx:3107 `browsefilters: () => window.open("https://exchange.adobe.com/apps/browse/cc?product=PHSP", "_blank", "noopener")`. Vision sets no Tauri on_new_window handler (none in src-tauri/src) and installs no opener or shell plugin (Cargo.toml:17-20). In wry 0.55.1 on macOS, createWebViewWithConfiguration returns None when new_window_req_handler is None (wry_web_view_ui_delegate.rs:148-258), so the request is dropped. Dialogs.tsx:2517-2519 already notes 'no opener plugin is installed'. It is the only window.open in the app.
findings.repro: In the native app choose Filter ▸ Browse Filters Online…: nothing happens. In the browser build it opens Adobe Exchange, which lists Photoshop-only plug-ins that Vision cannot load.
findings.impact: An enabled menu item that does nothing. Even where it works, it sends users to plug-ins that are incompatible with Vision.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the monetId so the item becomes a disabled placeholder, or add tauri-plugin-opener and point it at a Vision-relevant page.
findings.verdict_reason: The conclusion is confirmed, but the stated mechanism needs a correction. Vision's main window is built with monet_ui::MonetWindow::builder (src-tauri/src/main.rs:389-401), and that builder does install an on_new_window handler (monet-ui/src/lib.rs:522-523, added in the recent popup commit 187fc6bb). The handler, popup::on_new_window (popup.rs:57-66), returns NewWindowResponse::Deny for any URL that is not about:blank#monet-popup-<id>. So window.open('https://exchange.adobe.com/…') (App.tsx:3107) is still dropped. No opener or shell plugin is in Cargo.toml, and Dialogs.tsx:2517-2518 confirms that no opener plugin is installed. It remains an enabled item that does nothing, and it points to Photoshop-only plug-ins.

findings.title: Several menu commands open another command's dialog: Transform Distort/Perspective, Matting ▸ Color Decontaminate, Modify ▸ Contract
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Distort / Perspective; Layer ▸ Matting ▸ Color Decontaminate; Select ▸ Modify ▸ Contract…
findings.evidence: App.tsx:2758-2759: `xfdistort: () => open("perspective")` and `persp: () => open("perspective")`, and Edit ▸ Perspective Warp also uses monetId 'persp' (psMenuData.ts:697-700, 742-745). All three open the same numeric 'Perspective Warp' dialog with eight percent-of-canvas corner sliders (Dialogs.tsx:8311-8332); there are no on-canvas handles, and Free Transform has no corner distort (CanvasView.tsx:3777-3781). App.tsx:2769: `colordecontaminate: () => open("defringe")` opens the Defringe dialog. App.tsx:3090-3091: Expand… and Contract… both open ExpandContract, titled 'Expand / Contract Selection', where Expand is the primary button (Dialogs.tsx:5906-5913).
findings.repro: 1) Edit ▸ Transform ▸ Perspective: the dialog is titled 'Perspective Warp' and moves corners freely, with no mirrored perspective constraint. Distort gives the identical dialog. 2) Layer ▸ Matting ▸ Color Decontaminate opens a 'Defringe' dialog. 3) Select ▸ Modify ▸ Contract… opens a dialog whose highlighted primary button is Expand.
findings.impact: Three different Photoshop commands behave identically, and dialog titles do not match the chosen command, so users can apply the wrong operation.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the mode as the dialog arg (open("perspective", "distort" | "perspective"), and constrain opposite corners for Perspective; open("expandContract", "contract") with the matching primary button and title). Give Color Decontaminate its own mask-driven op, or remove its monetId until one exists.
findings.verdict_reason: The facts are confirmed, but the impact is overstated. xfdistort and persp both call open('perspective') (App.tsx:2758-2759), and Edit ▸ Perspective Warp also uses monetId 'persp' (psMenuData.ts:700, 744). The dialog is the free-corner 'Perspective Warp' (Dialogs.tsx:8311-8332), and Free Transform has no distort (CanvasView.tsx:3777-3781). colordecontaminate opens 'defringe' (App.tsx:2769). expand and contract both open ExpandContract (App.tsx:3090-3091), where Expand is the primary button (Dialogs.tsx:5910-5913). Mitigations: routing Distort to a free-corner pin is the correct capability and is documented as such (App.tsx:2756-2757). The free-corner dialog can produce any perspective result, only without the mirrored constraint. The Contract dialog has an explicitly labelled Contract button, and neither the monet-react Dialog nor Vision maps Enter to the primary button (no Enter handler in dialog.tsx), so users are unlikely to apply the wrong operation by accident. What remains is a title mismatch plus Color Decontaminate reusing the Defringe algorithm, so this is polish or a parity note, not wrong output.

findings.title: Edit ▸ Fill with Contents = Content-Aware silently ignores Mode, Opacity and Preserve Transparency
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Fill… (Content-Aware)
findings.evidence: Dialogs.tsx:5930 `if (contents === "contentAware") contentAwareFill(); // ignores Preserve Transparency`. The Mode Select, Opacity Slider and Preserve Transparency Checkbox (Dialogs.tsx:5956-5966) stay enabled for Content-Aware. contentAwareFill() takes no arguments (app.ts:1675-1676). The #430 closing note also says this path still uses the diffusion fill, not the new exemplar workspace.
findings.repro: Make a selection. Edit ▸ Fill… → Content-Aware, Mode Multiply, Opacity 30%, Preserve Transparency on → OK. The result is a 100% Normal fill that also fills transparent pixels.
findings.impact: Visible controls are silently ignored, so the result differs from what the user set up, and the fill is lower quality than Edit ▸ Content-Aware Fill.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable Mode, Opacity and Preserve Transparency while Content-Aware is selected, or route through contentAwareFillWith and then blend by mode/opacity with a restore_locked_transparency pass. Consider using the workspace's exemplar synthesis here too.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed. In FillContents.apply (Dialogs.tsx:5929-5932), the content-aware case calls contentAwareFill() with no arguments, and the code comments that it ignores Preserve Transparency. contentAwareFill (app.ts:1675-1677) calls E().content_aware_fill() and records ['contentAwareFill', []], so mode, opacity and preserve never reach the engine. The Mode Select, Opacity Slider and Preserve Checkbox (Dialogs.tsx:5956-5966) render with no dependence on contents, so they stay enabled for Content-Aware.

findings.title: Recorded 'Apply Style' action steps store the Styles panel index, so replay applies a different style after the list changes
findings.feature: Actions recording of Styles panel ▸ Apply Style
findings.evidence: app.ts:926-929 lists 'applyStylePreset' in RECORDED_STORE_OPS with the comment 'the Styles panel records the preset INDEX, so replay follows the playing machine's preset list'. store.applyStylePreset(i) (store.ts:8767-8780) reads this.snap.stylePresets[i]. This is the same position-derived-id class that #494 fixed for droplets and Script Events.
findings.repro: Record an action that clicks the 3rd style in the Styles panel. Delete or reorder the 1st style, or play the action on another machine or on a .atn round-trip. Playback applies whatever style is now 3rd, or silently does nothing if there is none.
findings.impact: Macros silently apply the wrong layer style, with no error.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the style by name (or embed the style payload), as #494 did for action references. Refuse with a named error when the style is missing.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed. RECORDED_STORE_OPS includes 'applyStylePreset', with a ponytail comment admitting that it records the preset INDEX (app.ts:926-929). store.applyStylePreset(i) (store.ts:8767-8780) reads this.snap.stylePresets[i] and returns silently when it is missing. The Styles library can change under a recorded step through addStylePreset, removeStylePreset (store.ts:8750-8756), renameStylePreset (store.ts:4074) and importStylePresets. Replay can therefore apply a different style, or do nothing, with no error.

findings.title: A Vanishing Point paste/float on a 16-bit document is written back at 8-bit precision
findings.feature: Filter ▸ Vanishing Point (float stamping)
findings.evidence: store.ts:3362-3364 comment: 'stamp_image is 8-bit in, so a float on a 16-bit document is quantized (and 32-bit refuses it)'. commitVanishingPointFloat passes 8-bit RGBA from warpQuadToQuad to s.engine.stamp_image. The #447 closing comment lists this as an open follow-up.
findings.repro: Open a 16-bit smooth gradient image. Filter ▸ Vanishing Point, create a plane, paste or float a region onto it, OK. Inspect the stamped area: its values fall on 257-step (8-bit) levels and show banding next to untouched 16-bit pixels.
findings.impact: A 16-bit document is quietly degraded to 8-bit precision inside the stamped area.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a u16 stamp (and warp) path in the engine and feed it from a 16-bit source capture. Until then, show the same 'Convert to 8-bit' refusal already used on 32-bit.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed. commitVanishingPointFloat passes warpQuadToQuad's 8-bit rgba to s.engine.stamp_image (store.ts:3362-3364, with a ponytail comment). Engine stamp_image (mod.rs:18596-18636) takes &[u8], builds its source as rgba/255.0, and writes the result through composite_over(...).to_u16. Opaque stamped pixels therefore land on 8-bit levels in a u16 layer. Accepting this depends on the float source also being an 8-bit capture, which the Uint8Array rgba field indicates.

findings.title: The shared engine renders vector image items only if they are base64 PNG; JPEG/WebP/GIF images from Artisan documents open blank in Vision
findings.feature: File ▸ Open / Place of Monet Artisan documents (kind-3 vector layer)
findings.evidence: render.rs:3312-3337: render_image says 'Non-PNG / non-data-URL hrefs render as nothing (TODO)' and only calls sk::Pixmap::decode_png. Artisan creates image items with the clipboard's MIME type (commands.ts:170-172, bytesToDataURL(bytes, raster)) and accepts data:image/(png|jpe?g|gif|webp|avif|bmp) on SVG import (artisan io/compatibility.ts:225-228). Vision opens .artisan scenes through the same engine (store.ts:5042-5046, eng.set_document).
findings.repro: In Artisan, paste a JPEG from the clipboard (or import an SVG that embeds a data:image/jpeg) and save. Open that file in Vision: the image area is empty and no error is shown.
findings.impact: Silent loss of content when moving documents between apps. Not confirmed with a real saved file (Artisan's save path was not traced).
findings.suggested_fix: Decode JPEG, WebP and GIF in render_image (the image crate is already an engine dependency), or have the engine report the dropped item.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed at code level. render_image (vector/render.rs:3313-3337) returns early unless the href is base64 that decodes with sk::Pixmap::decode_png, and its doc comment says non-PNG renders nothing (TODO). Vision's buildArtisan (store.ts:5042-5046) hands the scene to eng.set_document, so the engine rasterizes kind-3 layers. Artisan draws image items as DOM SVG (render/item-node.tsx:600ff), so JPEG shows correctly in Artisan itself. Artisan's SVG import creates image items with the href unchanged (io/import/svg.ts:1002) and accepts data:image/jpeg, webp and gif (io/compatibility.ts:227). No transcoding was found in the linked-assets or save paths. The clipboard-JPEG repro is weaker, because WebKit's async clipboard may expose only image/png. The SVG-embedded JPEG path is the reliable repro. The engine's image crate already has the jpeg, webp and gif features, but it is optional (Cargo.toml:40). Not proven end to end with a real saved file.

findings.title: Preferences dialog section list cannot be reached by keyboard
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Preferences (section sidebar)
findings.evidence: Dialogs.tsx:2082-2089 renders each of the 20 PREF_SECTIONS as a plain <div onClick={() => setSec(s)}>, with no role, tabIndex, keyboard handler or aria-selected.
findings.repro: Open Edit ▸ Preferences ▸ General and press Tab or the arrow keys. Focus never reaches the section list, so Performance, Cursors, Camera Raw and the other panes can only be reached by mouse or by picking the specific Preferences menu item.
findings.impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot move between preference panes inside the dialog.
findings.suggested_fix: Render the list as role="tablist" with role="tab" buttons (tabIndex, aria-selected, arrow-key handling), or reuse the shared Monet tabs component.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed. PREF_SECTIONS (20 entries, Dialogs.tsx:1552) render as plain <div onClick={() => setSec(s)}> with no role, tabIndex, key handler or aria-selected (Dialogs.tsx:2082-2088). The impact is partly mitigated: psMenuData has 18 distinct pref* menu ids, and they are reachable from the keyboard-accessible menu bar. Inside the dialog itself, keyboard users still cannot switch panes.

findings.title: The Statistics and Smart Object Stack Mode dialogs still say 'Dimmed modes are not available yet' although every mode is enabled
findings.feature: File ▸ Scripts ▸ Statistics…, Layer ▸ Smart Objects ▸ Stack Mode
findings.evidence: stackModes.ts:35 `ENGINE_STAT_MODES = 11`, so statModeReady() is true for all 11 modes and none are dimmed. The copy at Dialogs.tsx:3736-3737 and 3761-3762 still says 'Dimmed modes are not available yet'. The comment at stackModes.ts:28-34 still says the engine only implements modes 0..6.
findings.repro: Open File ▸ Scripts ▸ Statistics…: every Stack Mode option is enabled, but the footer says dimmed modes are unavailable.
findings.impact: Stale copy suggests missing functionality.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 'Dimmed modes…' sentence from both dialogs (keep 'the stack is merged rather than re-editable') and update the stale comment in stackModes.ts.
findings.verdict_reason: Confirmed. ENGINE_STAT_MODES = 11 (ui/stackModes.ts:35), so statModeReady() is true for modes 0-10 and nothing is dimmed. The ponytail comment above it (stackModes.ts:28-34) still says the engine implements only 0..6. Both dialogs still contain the text 'Dimmed modes are not available yet' (around Dialogs.tsx:3737 and 3761). This is stale copy only.

areas.coverage:
Area: collaboration, notes, animation, and misc interop in Monet Vision (apps/vision plus packages/engine). This was a read-only code review. I ran no builds or suites.

Inventory (35 features in scope):
- 25 menu commands with a monetId:
  - File/Export: gif, rendervideo, opengif, videoframes, importnotes
  - Image ▸ Analysis: setmeasurescale, selectdatapoints, recordmeasurements, rulertool, counttool, colorsamplertool, notetool, placescalemarker
  - View ▸ Show: showcount, shownotes
  - Help: about, systeminfo, keyboardshortcuts
  - Edit clipboard family: cut, copy, copymerged, paste, pasteinplace, pasteinto, pasteoutside
- 4 panels: Animation (including the keyframe Timeline section, about 18 controls), Notes, Libraries, Measurement Log.
- 4 tools: note, count, ruler, colorsampler.
- 6 cross-cutting paths: Home recent-files screen, layer drag-out (src/native/layerDragOut.ts + tauri-plugin-drag), .artisan open (parseArtisanScene/buildArtisan), GIF open through File ▸ Open, OS pasteboard read/write (store.ts writePasteboardPng/readPasteboardImage/adoptPasteboardImage), and realtime collab (src/collab, EngineClient stroke capture/replay, CollabCursors).

Traced UI → handler → app.ts/store.ts → engine for each. Engine functions checked:
- add_frame, bake_frame, tween_frames, import_gif, frames_apply_adjustment, set_frame_delay, frames_to/from_layers, reverse/clear_frames, frame_thumb, export_gif, doc_snap, push_stack_undo, import_image, stamp_image, set_brush/set_brush_mode.

Also read:
- The Tauri config: main.rs, capabilities, CSP.
- Dependency sources: tauri-plugin-drag 2.1.1 commands.rs, Tauri 2.11.2 ipc/channel.rs + command.rs, wry 0.55.1 wkwebview/navigation.rs.

Tests grepped:
- e2e: anim-video, notes, collaboration-two-client, layer-drag-out, home.
- unit: layerDragOut, toolRecording, artisanOpen, timeline, libraries, measurementLog, helpMenu.

Not verified (no runtime):
- What WKWebView actually does with `<a download>` and with clipboard read/write outside a user gesture.
- Real OOM thresholds.
- Internals of the monet-collab package.
- Artisan's side of the pasteboard handoff.
areas.parity_notes:
- **Disabled Photoshop placeholders (no monetId), correctly shown disabled, not reported as bugs:**
  - Layer ▸ Video Layers submenu: New Video Layer from File, New Blank Video Layer, Insert/Duplicate/Delete Frame, Show Altered Video, Restore Frame, Restore All Frames, Reload Frame.
  - File ▸ Export ▸ Export Video (codec)…. The `vid` action exists but nothing reaches it.
  - Layer ▸ Smart Objects ▸ Relink to Library Graphic….
  - View ▸ Show ▸ Mesh / Edit Pins.
- **Missing relative to Photoshop:**
  - No onboarding, tutorials or sample content. Home offers only New/Open/Recent.
  - The Help menu has only About, System Info and Keyboard Shortcuts: no user docs, "What's New" or update check.
  - Timeline Tween always inserts 4 in-betweens on the last two frames. There is no frame selection or tween dialog, no frame-disposal or optimisation settings, and Render Video ignores per-frame delays (uniform fps).
  - Video Frames to Layers has no Photoshop-style range / every-N-frames / "Make Frame Animation" dialog.
  - Count tool has no count groups, colour or size options. Measurement Log records only ruler length/angle and count.
  - Notes, count markers and samplers are not written to or read from PSD.
- **Features with no MCP command:** none of the animation/timeline, notes, count/measurement, libraries or clipboard features have an @mcp wrapper in src/mcp/commands.ts. Only script.run can reach some of them (addFrame).
- **Collaboration:** not exposed to desktop users. It is enabled only by ?room= or VITE_COLLAB=1 in browser/dev builds, and the desktop CSP blocks its socket anyway.
- **Artisan interop looks sound:** .artisan opens as one kind-3 vector layer through the shared engine, validated and unit-tested. Vision→other apps publishes PNG only; there is no private Monet flavour, so cross-app pastes are 8-bit.

findings.title: Every saveBytes export goes through <a download>, which the macOS Tauri webview cancels; animated GIF, Render Video and Measurement Log export likely write nothing in the desktop app
findings.feature: File ▸ Export ▸ Export Animated GIF; File ▸ Export ▸ Render Video…; Animation panel Export GIF; Measurement Log ▸ Export (and every other saveBytes caller: 63 non-test call sites)
findings.evidence:
app.ts:3605-3627: saveBytes → downloadBytes only builds a blob URL and clicks an <a download> anchor. It has no isTauri branch and no native save dialog. Callers:
- exportGIF app.ts:1921-1923
- exportVideo app.ts:1984-1990
- MeasurementLogPanel exportLog Panels.tsx:2379-2383

src-tauri/src/main.rs:321-360 registers no on_download handler. The monet-ui window builder (packages/monet-ui/crates/monet-ui/src/lib.rs:508-527) registers none either. In wry 0.55.1 (the version in Cargo.lock), wkwebview/navigation.rs:67-74 does this: when a navigation has shouldPerformDownload and has_download_handler is false, it calls WKNavigationActionPolicy::Cancel. docs/issue-proofs/pages/378.html:173 already flags the same doubt for Artisan's shell.
findings.repro:
1. pnpm dev:vision.
2. Open an image and add 2 frames in the Animation panel.
3. Choose File ▸ Export ▸ Export Animated GIF (or Render Video…, or Measurement Log ▸ Export).
4. Expected: a file is written or a save dialog appears. Likely actual: nothing happens and no error is shown.
findings.impact: The core animation outputs (GIF and video) and the measurement log can never leave the desktop app. The Chromium e2e 'desktop' project cannot catch this: it drives Chromium, where <a download> works. The same path probably breaks Quick Export PNG/JPG and every other saveBytes export outside this area.
findings.suggested_fix: One fix in saveBytes covers all 63 callers: under isTauri(), call plugin-dialog save({defaultPath: filename}) and then atomicWriteBytes(path, bytes), which docs/durable-save.md already requires. Keep downloadBytes for the browser. Add a test:e2e:native check that exports a GIF.
findings.verdict_reason: I followed the code path end to end. saveBytes (app.ts:3605-3609) always calls downloadBytes (3614-3628), which only clicks a blob <a download>. saveBytes has had no isTauri branch since the first scaffold (89d53207). Nothing registers a download handler: Vision's main.rs builder (321-360) and the monet-ui window builder (lib.rs:508-527, which sets only on_new_window and on_page_load) have none, and tauri-2.11.2 webview/mod.rs defaults download_handler to None. In wry 0.55.1, wkwebview/mod.rs:570 sets has_download_handler = download_started_handler.is_some(), and navigation.rs:67-74 returns WKNavigationActionPolicy::Cancel when shouldPerformDownload is true and no handler exists. WebKit sets shouldPerformDownload for an anchor that has a download attribute. The problem is wider than this area: Quick Export PNG (App.tsx:2586), Export As (app.ts:4798-4829), PSD/TIFF/WebP/PDF and about 60 other callers all use saveBytes. No test drives this path in the real app: scripts/native-webview-e2e.mjs checks export only through MCP doc.exportPngBase64, and the Chromium e2e run can't see it. I did not drive the webview at runtime. The one remaining assumption is WebKit's documented shouldPerformDownload behaviour. Blocker, because every desktop export path is affected.

findings.title: Native layer drag-out always fails: the raw invoke of plugin:drag|start_drag omits the required onEvent channel
findings.feature: Layers panel ▸ drag a layer thumbnail out to Finder/other apps as PNG
findings.evidence:
layerDragOut.ts:52-56 calls invoke("plugin:drag|start_drag", { item: [path], image, options: { mode: "copy" } }) with no onEvent.

The plugin's command (tauri-plugin-drag-2.1.1/src/commands.rs start_drag) takes `on_event: Channel<CallbackResult>`, which is not an Option. Tauri 2.11.2's Channel::from_command (ipc/channel.rs:300-315) deserializes a String from the payload, and a missing key errors with "command {} missing required key {}" (ipc/command.rs:100).

The unit test (layerDragOut.test.ts:72-76) mocks invoke and asserts exactly this incomplete argument set. e2e/layer-drag-out.spec.ts covers only the browser DataTransfer branch.
findings.repro: In the desktop app, drag a pixel layer's thumbnail from the Layers panel toward Finder.
findings.impact: The onDragStart handler has already called preventDefault(). The invoke is rejected, the staged file is swept, and the user gets a 'Layer export failed: invalid args onEvent…' toast. The advertised desktop drag-out never works.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass a channel: `import { Channel } from "@tauri-apps/api/core"; … onEvent: new Channel()` (as the official @crabnebula/tauri-plugin-drag startDrag does). Update the unit test to assert onEvent is present.
findings.verdict_reason: layerDragOut.ts:52-56 invokes with only item, image and options. The start_drag command in tauri-plugin-drag-2.1.1 (commands.rs) takes `on_event: Channel<CallbackResult>`, which is not an Option. Tauri 2.11.2's Channel::from_command (ipc/channel.rs:300-315) deserializes the key, and a missing key returns "command start_drag missing required key onEvent" (ipc/command.rs:98-101). The caller (Panels.tsx:981-989) has already called preventDefault and shows the rejection in a 'Layer export failed' toast. The unit test (layerDragOut.test.ts:72-76) asserts exactly this incomplete payload, so the test locks the bug in. The plugin permission is granted (capabilities/default.json has drag:default), so the missing key is the only reason it fails.

findings.title: Recorded or collaborative strokes from retouch tools replay as plain foreground-colour paint
findings.feature: Actions ▸ Allow Tool Recording (paintStroke replay); realtime collab stroke channel
findings.evidence:
Stroke capture starts for every brush-family tool. CanvasView.tsx:1256-1299 routes adjustmentbrush/brush/pencil/erase/dodge/burn/patternstamp/colorreplace/sponge/blur/sharpen/backgrounderaser/mixerbrush/historybrush/smudge into the same case, which calls engine.strokeCaptureBegin().

The capture (EngineClient.ts:216-221) records only lastBrush, which is set in store.ts:2918 as [size, hardness, flow, opacity, spacing, r, g, b, a, erase]. It does not record the tool mode (set via set_brush_mode, store.ts:2923-2924) or the dodge/blur/sponge/mixer options.

On replay, applyStroke (EngineClient.ts:266-289) calls only e.set_brush(...). The engine's set_brush (packages/engine/src/raster/mod.rs:17082-17083) resets `self.brush.mode = if erase {1} else {0}`, so a Dodge/Burn/Smudge/Blur/Sharpen/Sponge/Mixer/History stroke replays as a mode-0 paint stroke in the foreground colour.

The replay is used by the paintStroke op (app.ts:2291-2294) behind Allow Tool Recording (app.ts:781-783) and by the collab channel. src/collab/index.ts:11-14 and docs/realtime-collaboration.md claim these tools 'simply don't capture', which is false.
findings.repro:
1. Actions panel: turn on Allow Tool Recording and start recording.
2. Pick the Dodge tool and drag across the image. Stop recording.
3. Undo, then play the action.
4. Expected: a lightening stroke. Actual: a stroke painted in the foreground colour.
findings.impact: Actions that include retouch-tool gestures damage the image on playback. With collab on, peers' canvases diverge.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture the stroke's brush mode (and the mode's option set) in StrokeOp, and have applyStroke call set_brush_mode after set_brush. Alternatively, call strokeCaptureBegin only for brush/pencil/erase, as documented. Add a toolRecording test that records a dodge stroke.
findings.verdict_reason: CanvasView.tsx:1257-1297 calls engine.strokeCaptureBegin() for every tool in the brush family, including dodge, burn, smudge, blur, sponge, mixer and history. strokeCaptureBegin (EngineClient.ts:216-222) does not filter by tool. It snapshots only lastBrush, which store.pushBrush sets to [size, hardness, flow, opacity, spacing, r, g, b, a, erase] with r,g,b from the foreground colour (store.ts:2918-2921). The mode is set separately through set_brush_mode (2922-2923) and is not captured. On replay, applyStroke (EngineClient.ts:266-289) calls only e.set_brush, and the engine's set_brush (mod.rs:17075-17084) resets brush.mode to 0 or 1. So a Dodge stroke replays as a mode-0 paint stroke in the foreground colour. Allow Tool Recording feeds this path (app.ts:781-782 recordTool paintStroke, then 2291-2292 replayStroke), and recordTool (789) has no tool filter either. The comment in collab/index.ts:11-14 that these tools 'simply don't capture' is false.

findings.title: Every stack-undo snapshot clones all animation frames, with no frame memory budget: building or editing a moderate animation can exhaust WASM memory
findings.feature: Animation panel (+ Frame, Tween, From Layers, Render → Frames, imported GIFs)
findings.evidence:
doc_snap (mod.rs:5505-5525) copies `frames: self.frames.clone()` (full RGBA8 canvas buffers) into every Snap::Stack. push_stack_undo (mod.rs:5692-5697) is used at 159 call sites, including add_layer (9337), and history keeps UNDO_CAP = 50 (mod.rs:989).

add_frame (28789-28796) pushes a stack snapshot of all previous frames before appending, so adding N frames one by one stores N(N-1)/2 frame copies. Worked example at 1920×1080 (8.3 MB per frame), 30 frames: 435 copies ≈ 3.6 GB in history, plus 30 layer snapshots.

Only import_gif has a budget (MAX_GIF_BYTES 256 MB, 28851-28877). add_frame, bake_frame and tween_frames have none, and store.timelineRender (store.ts:3873-3897) can bake up to 60 fps × 60 s = 3600 frames. After loading a 256 MB-frame GIF, each later New Layer or blend-mode change clones another 256 MB.
findings.repro:
1. Open or create a 1920×1080 document.
2. Click Animation ▸ + Frame about 30 times, with small edits in between.
3. Or open a large animated GIF and add about 15 layers.
Memory grows quadratically until a wasm allocation traps.
findings.impact: On a wasm32 allocation failure the engine traps. The active document's Engine is left in a poisoned borrow state, and save and autosave of it fail. Work since the last recovery snapshot is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Store frames as Vec<Rc<[u8]>> or Arc so snapshots share frame buffers (copy-on-write). Or keep frames out of DocSnap, with a dedicated frames snapshot pushed only by frame ops. Add a total-frame-bytes budget, like MAX_GIF_BYTES, to add_frame/bake_frame/tween_frames, with a user-visible refusal.
findings.verdict_reason: Frames are Vec<Vec<u8>> (mod.rs:915/3398). doc_snap deep-copies them on every stack snapshot with `frames: self.frames.clone()` (5523). push_stack_undo (5692-5697) always uses doc_snap. push_undo trims history by count only (trim_undo_to_history_states, 5729-5734, UNDO_CAP 50) and has no byte budget. add_frame (28789-28795) pushes a stack snapshot before appending, so adding frames one at a time stores copies quadratically, and the reviewer's arithmetic holds. bake_frame and tween_frames have no size budget; only import_gif has MAX_GIF_BYTES (28852). timelineRender (store.ts:3873-3897) can bake up to 60 fps × 60 s = 3600 full-size frames without any budget. I did not drive an actual OOM trap. One detail is overstated: a blend-mode change probably uses a property snapshot rather than a stack snapshot. New Layer does clone all frames.

findings.title: Video Frames to Layers pushes a full-document undo snapshot per frame: ordinary 720p/1080p clips run out of memory; the 48-frame cap is silent and there are no tests
findings.feature: File ▸ Import ▸ Video Frames to Layers…
findings.evidence:
importVideoFramesToLayers (app.ts:7841-7880) samples min(48, dur×8) frames and calls stackImages (7725-7744). For each frame after the first, stackImages calls E().importImage, and import_image (mod.rs:29356-29381) calls add_layer → push_stack_undo('New Layer') → doc_snap, which clones every existing 16-bit layer (Layer.pixels: Vec<u16>, mod.rs:179).

A 48-frame 1080p clip stores 1128 layer copies × 16.6 MB ≈ 18.7 GB in history, and 720p ≈ 8.3 GB. Both are far past the wasm32 4 GB ceiling.

Other problems:
- No options dialog.
- The new document is named 'Frame 1', because the first frame goes through routeOpen with that name.
- seekVideo (7829-7835) has no timeout or error path, so a stalled seek hangs silently.
- grep finds no unit or e2e test that references importVideoFramesToLayers.
findings.repro: Import a 6-second 1080p .mp4 with File ▸ Import ▸ Video Frames to Layers.
findings.impact: A likely engine trap/OOM partway through building a new document. Shorter clips succeed, but the sampling is silently truncated.
findings.suggested_fix: Build the stack without per-layer history. Either add frames through a non-undo layer insert, or clear or collapse history after building the fresh document. Check a total-bytes budget before decoding. Name the document after the video file, and add a seek timeout plus a minimal e2e test with a tiny fixture video.
findings.verdict_reason: importVideoFramesToLayers (app.ts:7841-7880) samples min(48, dur×8) frames and passes them to stackImages (7725-7744). stackImages calls E().importImage for every frame after the first. import_image (mod.rs:29356-29381) calls add_layer, and add_layer (9336-9337) calls push_stack_undo('New Layer'), which snapshots every existing layer. Layer.pixels is Vec<u16> (mod.rs:179), so a 1080p layer is about 16.6 MB. With 47 snapshots holding 1+2+…+47 layers, the reviewer's figure of about 18.7 GB is right, and it is far past the wasm32 limit. History is trimmed by count only. The only budget in the stack path is readStackPaths' encoded-bytes cap, and the video path bypasses it. seekVideo (7829-7835) has no timeout or error handler. A grep finds importVideoFramesToLayers only in App.tsx, psMenuData.ts and app.ts, with no tests. I did not reproduce the OOM at runtime.

findings.title: Timeline keyframes are app-global session state keyed by per-engine layer ids: they are not saved, not per document, and Render → Frames on another tab animates unrelated layers
findings.feature: Animation panel ▸ Timeline (◆ Key active layer, Render → Frames)
findings.evidence:
`timeline` is a top-level snapshot field (store.ts:940, default 1446). It is not a DocEntry field:
- addDoc (4755-4860) and activateDoc (6177-6224) never swap or reset it.
- docDocumentMeta (4466-4500) never serializes it.
- timelineAddKey (3853-3860) does not markDirty.

Keys store raw layerId values. Layer ids are a per-Engine counter, which is why layerColorLabels/duotone are kept per document ('ids are per engine', 6204 and 6216).

timelineRender (3873-3897) runs on whatever document is active. It calls e.clear_frames() and then drives set_layer_opacity/offset on those ids.
findings.repro:
1. In doc A, key layer 'Layer 1' at 0 s and 2 s with different opacity.
2. Open doc B, which has its own frames.
3. Click Render → Frames.
B's frames are replaced, and whichever B layer shares A's numeric id gets animated. Separately: save doc A as .mvision and reopen it; the keyframes are gone.
findings.impact: Wrong output on the second document, and authored keyframes are silently lost on save/reopen. The only protection is the undo entry that clear_frames happens to push.
findings.suggested_fix: Move `timeline` into DocEntry: capture it in captureActiveView, restore it in activateDoc, reset it in addDoc. Add it to docDocumentMeta/project metadata, and mark the document dirty on key edits.
findings.verdict_reason: `timeline` is referenced only in store.ts: the snapshot field (940), the default (1446) and the timeline* methods (3853-3897). Panels.tsx is the only other file that reads it. It does not appear in activateDoc's per-document restore block (6198-6225), which does swap notes, guides, layerColorLabels and duotone and says 'ids are per engine'. It also does not appear in document metadata or persistence. timelineAddKey (3853-3860) stores the raw activeLayerId and does not markDirty. timelineRender runs against whatever engine is active: it calls clear_frames and then drives set_layer_opacity/set_layer_offset on those ids. So switching tabs applies A's keys to B's layer ids, and the keys are lost on save and reopen.

findings.title: A failed pasteboard publish is still recorded as published, so a later Paste can adopt an older or foreign image instead of what was just copied; Edit ▸ Paste stays disabled for a foreign-only clipboard
findings.feature: Edit ▸ Copy / Paste interop with other apps (Artisan, Preview, Figma)
findings.evidence:
publishClipboard (store.ts:6543-6548) sets `this.publishedPng = png` and then fires `void writePasteboardPng(png)`. The write returns false on refusal (1902-1912), but publishedPng is kept either way.

adoptPasteboardImage (6557-6576) treats any pasteboard image whose bytes differ from publishedPng as foreign and overwrites the engine clipboard with it. When the write was refused, the pasteboard still holds the previous content (an earlier Vision copy or a screenshot). WebKit's clipboard API requires a user gesture, and a native menu-bar click arrives over IPC without one.

Separately, menuEnablement paste (App.tsx:3448) is gated on the internal hasClipboard (store.ts:2533), so Edit ▸ Paste is greyed out when only another app has copied. ⌘V still works because shortcut commands come from catalogMenus with no enablement (App.tsx:3538-3541).
findings.repro:
1. Take a screenshot to the clipboard.
2. In Vision, make a selection and choose Edit ▸ Copy from the macOS menu bar.
3. Press ⌘V.
The screenshot may be pasted instead of the selection.
findings.impact: The wrong pixels are pasted with no warning. Menu Paste and ⌘V also behave inconsistently.
findings.suggested_fix: Await writePasteboardPng and set publishedPng only when it returns true. On failure, clear publishedPng and skip adoption for the next paste (the internal clipboard wins), or publish through a native NSPasteboard command. Enable paste when hasDocument, and let paste() report 'nothing to paste'.
findings.verdict_reason: The logic is as described. publishClipboard (store.ts:6543-6548) sets publishedPng before the write, then calls `void writePasteboardPng`, which returns false when refused (1902-1912). adoptPasteboardImage (6557-6576) adopts any bytes that differ from publishedPng. The native menu items carry no accelerators (mac-menu.ts header) and are dispatched over IPC, so a menu-bar Copy runs without a user gesture, and WebKit rejects clipboard.write in that case. A keyboard ⌘C runs inside keydown, has a gesture and works. That makes the failure specific to menu-bar Copy. The wrong paste also requires the user to accept WebKit's DOM-paste prompt on ⌘V. The result is visible and undoable, so I downgrade it to minor. Paste enablement is `hasDocument && hasClipboard` (App.tsx:3448), and hasClipboard is `e.has_clipboard() || publishedPng` (store.ts:2533), so menu Paste is greyed out for a clipboard that only another app has written. ⌘V still works, but the reason differs from the finding's: shortcutCommands is built from baseMenus, not catalogMenus, and collectShortcutCommands (keyboardShortcuts.ts:220-244) ignores `disabled`.

findings.title: Count markers, the ruler line and colour samplers are app-global, not per document: they leak across tabs, are never saved, and are not remapped by Image Size/Crop
findings.feature: Count tool, Ruler tool, Color Sampler, Record Measurements
findings.evidence:
countPoints, rulerLine and colorSamplers are top-level snapshot fields (store.ts:1115-1121, defaults 1582-1585). They are absent from DocEntry, captureActiveView (4629-4657), activateDoc (6190-6218) and docDocumentMeta.

remapDocSpaceAnnotations (3560-3574) remaps notes and samplers but not countPoints or rulerLine. recordMeasurement (4283-4295) logs countPoints.length whichever document is active.

Also, Count tool Alt-click removes the LAST marker regardless of where you click (CanvasView.tsx:1558-1563 → store.removeLastCountPoint 3698-3701), while the status hint says 'Alt-click to remove'.
findings.repro:
1. Place 12 count markers on doc A.
2. Switch to doc B. The markers draw on B, and Record Measurements logs count 12 for B.
3. Save A as .mvision and reopen it. The markers are gone.
findings.impact: Wrong analysis results with multiple documents open, and measurement markup is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Move these fields into DocEntry and save/restore them the way notes and guides are. Include countPoints in remapDocSpaceAnnotations and persist it in project metadata. Hit-test the nearest marker for Alt-click.
findings.verdict_reason: In store.ts, rulerLine, countPoints and colorSamplers appear only at the declaration (1115-1121), the defaults (1582-1585), their setters (3691-3725), clearColorSamplers (4250), remapDocSpaceAnnotations (3571, samplers only) and recordMeasurement (4284-4292). None of them is in the activateDoc restore block. remapDocSpaceAnnotations (3560-3574) remaps notes, guides and samplers, but not countPoints or rulerLine. The Count tool's Alt-click handler (CanvasView.tsx:1558-1563) calls removeLastCountPoint, while the hint text at App.tsx:1461 says 'Alt-click to remove'.

findings.title: Libraries keeps only a ≤256 px thumbnail, so placing a graphic inserts a tiny, selection-clipped copy at 0,0 in two undo steps
findings.feature: Window ▸ Libraries panel (+ Capture, click to place)
findings.evidence:
LIB_MAX_DIM = 256 (app.ts:2191). capture() downscales the whole composite to fit 256 px before storing it (2195-2205).

insert() (2218-2230) does the following:
- Decodes that thumbnail.
- Calls store.addLayer(), which is one undo step.
- Calls E().stamp_image(0,0,…), a second step labelled 'Paste'. stamp_image (mod.rs:18596-18626) masks every pixel by self.sel.coverage, so an active selection clips the placed graphic.
- In a 32-bit float document, stamp_image refuses, but the empty 'Layer N' has already been added.
findings.repro:
1. Capture a 4000×3000 photo into Libraries.
2. Click the asset in another document that has an active selection.
findings.impact: The 'reusable graphic' comes back as a 256 px, partially masked copy at top-left. Users will read this as a broken feature.
findings.suggested_fix: Store full-resolution assets in IndexedDB or on disk, keeping the thumbnail for the grid only. Place centred via a single engine op that ignores the selection, in one history step. Check the refusal before adding the layer.
findings.verdict_reason: LIB_MAX_DIM = 256 (app.ts:2191), and capture() downsizes to it before storing (2195-2205). The comment makes clear this is a deliberate localStorage trade-off. insert() (2218-2230) calls store.addLayer() and then E().stamp_image(0,0,…). stamp_image (mod.rs:18596-18626) pushes its own 'Paste' layer undo and multiplies by self.sel.coverage, so an active selection clips the graphic. It also refuses through reject_legacy_float_edit after the layer has already been added. Everything in the finding is as described.

findings.title: With no document open, Help ▸ About/System Info/Keyboard Shortcuts, Open GIF as Animation and Video Frames to Layers are disabled
findings.feature: Home start screen menus
findings.evidence:
NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS = /^(new|openf|clearrecent|browse|search|colorsettings|pref[a-z]*|exportprefs|customizetoolbar)$/ (App.tsx:77).

Every other command is disabled when documents are empty: stableMenuActions refuses it (3333-3336), and menuEnablement spreads `documentless` last (3437-3442, 3467). The Help entries use act() (psMenus.ts:519-527), so they come out disabled.

about/systeminfo/keyboardshortcuts need no engine: About only reads engine.version() inside a try, Dialogs.tsx:2152-2156. opengif and videoframes create new documents.
findings.repro: Cold-launch the app to the Home screen, then open the Help menu.
findings.impact: Users can't see the version or edit shortcuts from the start screen. Two open-style imports are unavailable exactly when they are most useful.
findings.suggested_fix: Add about|systeminfo|keyboardshortcuts|opengif|videoframes (and other document-creating imports) to NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS.
findings.verdict_reason: NO_DOCUMENT_COMMANDS (App.tsx:77) does not include about, systeminfo, keyboardshortcuts, opengif or videoframes. stableMenuActions (3333-3336) drops any other command when no document is open, and the Home-screen keydown path (2304-2308) runs through the same wrappers. So System Info, Keyboard Shortcuts, Open GIF and Video Frames to Layers do nothing from Home. One mitigation: on macOS the app menu adds a native PredefinedMenuItem About (mac-menu.ts:172), which shows the bundle version regardless. The in-app Help ▸ About still stays disabled.

findings.title: Render Video adds an unsynced 'Add Frame' history entry to frame-less documents, and Cancel does not stop an in-flight render
findings.feature: File ▸ Export ▸ Render Video…
findings.evidence:
recordVideo (app.ts:1946-1982) runs `if (count === 0) { E().add_frame(); count = 1; }` (1952). add_frame pushes a stack undo (mod.rs:28789-28796) and mutates document frames, but nothing calls engine.commit(): no dirty flag, no History/Animation panel resync.

RenderVideoDialog (Dialogs.tsx:10816-10839) keeps Cancel enabled while busy. Cancel only calls close(), so the real-time MediaRecorder loop keeps running and saveBytes fires after the dialog is gone.
findings.repro: On a document with no frames, choose Render Video… ▸ Render and then check History. Or, with 200 frames, click Render and then Cancel.
findings.impact: A hidden history step and document change from an export command, plus an export the user tried to cancel.
findings.suggested_fix: Export a transient composite instead of mutating frames when there are none (as export_gif already does). Add an AbortSignal to recordVideo and wire it to Cancel.
findings.verdict_reason: recordVideo (app.ts:1952) calls `E().add_frame()` when frame_count is 0. add_frame pushes stack undo (mod.rs:28789-28795), and neither recordVideo nor exportVideo (1984-1990) calls engine.commit. In RenderVideoDialog (Dialogs.tsx:10816-10841), Cancel stays enabled while busy and only calls close(). The render() promise and its real-time MediaRecorder loop keep running and still reach saveBytes.

findings.title: Place Scale Marker discards the user's selection and lands as 4–5 separate history steps
findings.feature: Image ▸ Analysis ▸ Place Scale Marker…
findings.evidence:
placeScaleMarker (app.ts:7886-7901) makes separate history entries:
- store.addLayer() → New Layer
- E().select_rect(...) → selection undo
- fill_selection → Fill
- E().select_none() (7896) → Deselect
- optionally text.create → a fifth entry

The prior selection is never saved or restored, and the function is not rec()-wrapped.
findings.repro:
1. Make a selection.
2. Run Place Scale Marker.
The selection is gone, and undoing the command takes 4–5 presses.
findings.impact: Silent loss of the working selection and a noisy history.
findings.suggested_fix: Save the selection mask as skyReplacement does (app.ts:7906-7931) and restore it. Group the steps in one history transaction, and wrap the command in rec().
findings.verdict_reason: placeScaleMarker (app.ts:7886-7901) calls store.addLayer, then set_layer_name (engine pushes 'Rename Layer', mod.rs:16562), select_rect ('Marquee' sel undo), fill_selection, select_none ('Deselect'), and optionally text.create. That is 5-6 entries, one more than the finding claims. It never saves or restores the prior selection, unlike skyReplacement (7906-7931). It is not rec()-wrapped: the dialog calls it directly (Dialogs.tsx:4978).

findings.title: The Animation panel re-encodes every frame thumbnail, and onion skin re-encodes a full-resolution PNG, on every document edit
findings.feature: Animation panel frame strip; Onion Skin
findings.evidence:
AnimationPanel calls anim.thumbUrl(i) inline for every frame on every render (Panels.tsx:3731-3733). engine.frameThumbUrl (EngineClient.ts:912-923) creates a canvas and calls toDataURL each time. The panel is re-rendered through Editor's unmemoized `panels` map (App.tsx:3381-3397) whenever `layers` changes, i.e. on every commit.

The onion skin useMemo (CanvasView.tsx:444-450) deliberately invalidates on historyIndex. It calls frameThumbUrl(last, docW, docH), a full-document PNG encode, after every brush stroke.
findings.repro:
1. Open a 300-frame GIF with the Animation panel visible, or turn on Onion Skin on a 24 MP document.
2. Paint strokes.
findings.impact: A stall after every stroke that grows with frame count or document size.
findings.suggested_fix: Cache thumbnails per frame and invalidate them on frame-op revisions only. Draw the onion skin from a canvas/ImageData blit instead of a data URL, and invalidate it only when frames change.
findings.verdict_reason: AnimationPanel calls anim.thumbUrl(i) inline for every frame (Panels.tsx:3731-3733). frameThumbUrl (EngineClient.ts:912-923) builds a canvas and calls toDataURL on each call, with no caching. Editor subscribes to `layers` and rebuilds the unmemoized panels map (App.tsx:3381-3397), and dockable-views calls meta.render(). The onion skin useMemo (CanvasView.tsx:444-450) invalidates on historyIndex and encodes the frame at full document size. That onion-skin cost is an acknowledged `ponytail:` trade-off in the code comment, but it is still real. Perf only, so it stays minor.

findings.title: Notes ▸ Clear All deletes every note immediately, with no confirmation and no undo
findings.feature: Note tool options bar ▸ Clear All
findings.evidence: The options-bar button calls store.clearNotes() directly (App.tsx:1405-1407). clearNotes → commitNoteState (store.ts:3733-3736, 3810-3813) only marks the document dirty and sets state. Note edits never enter engine history, so Edit ▸ Undo cannot bring them back.
findings.repro: Add several notes with text, then click Clear All.
findings.impact: Irrecoverable loss of annotation text (up to 1000 notes × 20k characters each) from a single click.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm before clearing, as Photoshop does. Alternatively, keep a one-level restore or put note edits into history.
findings.verdict_reason: The Clear All button calls store.clearNotes() directly (App.tsx:1406). clearNotes, through commitNoteState (store.ts:3733-3736, 3810-3813), only marks the document dirty and sets state. There is no engine history entry and no confirm prompt. The only recovery is Revert or closing without saving, if the notes had been saved before.

findings.title: Realtime collaboration is a dev/web-only prototype: no auth token, blocked by the desktop CSP, remote strokes land on the local undo stack, and its docs are out of date
findings.feature: Realtime collaboration (src/collab, ?room= / VITE_COLLAB=1)
findings.evidence:
startCollab (collab/index.ts:47-67) defaults to room 'vision-demo' and ws://localhost:1234 (plaintext), and never passes CollabOptions.token, although scripts/collab-server.mjs supports COLLAB_TOKEN. Anyone who knows the room name can inject strokes.

The Tauri CSP connect-src (src-tauri/tauri.conf.json:17) has no ws://localhost:1234, so a VITE_COLLAB=1 desktop build boots the collab canvas but cannot connect.

Replay behaviour in applyStroke (EngineClient.ts:266-289):
- It paints under the LOCAL selection, because engine dabs apply self.sel coverage.
- It never calls engine.commit(), so the document is not marked dirty and closing can drop remote strokes without a prompt.
- It pushes local undo, so ⌘Z reverts a peer's stroke on this client only; the e2e spec asserts undo_depth +1.

docs/realtime-collaboration.md says capture is 'gated to brush/erase in CanvasView' and that 'runtime two-client validation … is still to be done'. Both are contradicted by CanvasView.tsx:1256-1299 and e2e/collaboration-two-client.spec.ts. yjs/y-websocket are statically imported (app.ts:8, CanvasView.tsx:10), so they ship in the release bundle even though the feature is unreachable.
findings.repro: Run the web build with ?room=vision-demo while a collab server is running, and join from a second browser.
findings.impact: Not reachable by desktop users today, but not release-ready if it is ever exposed: canvases diverge and anyone can join a room.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep it out of release builds (dynamic import behind the flag). Before exposing it: require a token, use wss, replay with an empty selection and without local undo, commit or mark dirty, and correct the doc.
findings.verdict_reason: startCollab (collab/index.ts:47-67) uses the default room 'vision-demo' and ws://localhost:1234, and passes no token, although CollabSession supports one (monet-collab session.ts:23-24,54). The CSP connect-src (tauri.conf.json:17) allows only ws://localhost:1420. applyStroke calls stroke_begin/stroke_end, which push local undo; the e2e test asserts undo_depth +1 (collaboration-two-client.spec.ts:65-68). docs/realtime-collaboration.md:73 claims capture is 'gated to brush/erase', which contradicts CanvasView. app.ts:8 statically imports ../collab, so monet-collab and yjs ship in the bundle. A desktop user can't reach any of this unless the app is built with VITE_COLLAB=1, so minor is right.

findings.title: Frame, library and keyframe delete controls are clickable spans with no keyboard access or accessible name
findings.feature: Animation panel frame ×, Timeline keyframe ×, Libraries asset ×
findings.evidence: The following delete controls are all with only a title attribute: - Panels.tsx:3739 (delete frame) - 3782 (delete keyframe) - 3334 (remove library asset) They have no role=button, no tabIndex and no key handler. Library assets are also placed via onClick on an (3332).
findings.repro: Tab through the Animation or Libraries panel with the keyboard.
findings.impact: These actions can't be reached from the keyboard or by screen readers.
findings.suggested_fix: Use <button type="button" aria-label="Delete frame N">, as the Swatches/Styles tiles already do.
findings.verdict_reason: Panels.tsx:3739 (delete frame), 3782 (delete keyframe) and 3333 (remove library asset) are all <span onClick> with only a title attribute. None has a role, a tabIndex or a key handler.

findings.title: About shows no licences or acknowledgements, although the bundle ships third-party and CC-BY-SA notices
findings.feature: Help ▸ About Monet Vision…
findings.evidence: About (Dialogs.tsx:2151-2178) lists only Version, Engine and Platform. public/ ships THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md, LICENSE-APACHE-2.0, LICENSE-LENSFUN, NOTICE-LENSFUN.md, lensfun-attribution.json and licenses/, but nothing in src references them (grep finds no matches). The Help menu (psMenus.ts:519-527) has no documentation link either.
findings.repro: Open Help ▸ About Monet Vision….
findings.impact: Attribution-required notices (Lensfun CC-BY-SA, the model licences) are not visible to users.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an 'Acknowledgements / Licenses' link in About that opens THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md, and consider a Help link to user documentation.
findings.verdict_reason: About (Dialogs.tsx:2151-2178) lists only Version, Engine and Platform. public/ ships THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.md, LICENSE-LENSFUN, NOTICE-LENSFUN.md, lensfun-attribution.json and licenses/, but no src file links to these (a grep finds only a model-licence textPath in modelRegistry.ts). The notices do ship inside the bundle, so polish is a reasonable grade.
